scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
scholarships.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)

applicant_utility.summary: This is not one scholarship but around two hundred separate Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters, each run by its own university consortium with its own deadline, its own document list and its own scholarship quota, so the real work is shortlisting programmes from the EACEA catalogue in early autumn and then tracking each consortium's site rather than waiting for an EU-wide call. The money itself is fixed centrally at EUR 1 400 per month for the whole programme, which works out to roughly EUR 16 800 for a 12-month master, EUR 25 200 for 18 months and EUR 33 600 for 24 months, plus up to EUR 60 000 in special-needs top-up where applicable. Because that single monthly rate has to absorb travel, visa, installation and subsistence, the arrival month is the tightest part of the budget, and scholarship-funded places are only awarded to the best-ranked applicants even though unfunded places in the same programme are open to anyone who meets the entry requirements.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor's students and recent graduates who want a multi-country master's in a niche interdisciplinary field and can commit to full-time study in at least two countries that are not their own.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist from the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, then open each consortium's own site and confirm it actually awards EU scholarships for the intake you are targeting; EACEA warns that some listed masters carry the Erasmus Mundus name while nearing the end of their funding period.

Build a deadline tracker per programme. Most consortia open applications in October and close between December and January for the following academic year, and the scholarship round often closes earlier than the self-funded round.
Get your expected graduation date confirmed in writing by your registrar if you are still studying, since you must graduate before the programme starts.

Check your degree's recognition early: a bachelor-equivalent qualification must be officially recognised in the degree-awarding country, so unusual or newly established credentials need checking with the consortium before you apply.
Confirm you have never held an EMJM scholarship before, because a previous award permanently bars a second one.
Save two to three months of living costs before departure, since the first monthly payment lands only after you have paid for flights, the visa appointment, a rental deposit and your first groceries.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that no longer funds scholarships; the application can succeed academically while carrying no money, so the offer is effectively unfundable.
Missing the consortium's own deadline rather than a central one, because the Commission sets none and several runs close earlier for scholarship-track applicants.

A generic motivation letter. Selection is run by the consortium alone and is holistic rather than grade-driven, so failure to reference the specific mobility track, partner universities and research themes of that programme is the most common way to lose a place.
Part-time or reduced-load enrolment, since the scholarship can only be awarded in full to full-time students.

The nationality quota: consortia should keep any single nationality at no more than 10% of their scholarships, so applicants from heavily represented countries face a real ceiling regardless of merit.
Incomplete credential certification, where transcripts and diplomas are not translated, notarised or legalised in the exact form the consortium demands.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The scholarship covers travel, visa, installation and subsistence within the EUR 1 400 monthly rate, but applicants still fund pre-departure credential translation and legalisation, any test fees, personal and health insurance, replacement of lost documents, and the gap between arriving abroad and the first monthly payment.
document_audit: The Commission publishes no central student document list, so the only safe source is each consortium's own application page; expect transcripts, degree certificate, CV, motivation letter, references and proof of language proficiency, but confirm the exact set per programme.

Language proof is governed by a jointly agreed consortium language policy rather than an EU-wide rule, so check whether the programme accepts a medium-of-instruction certificate before paying for IELTS or TOEFL.
Scholarship-track applications frequently require extra items that self-funded applicants do not submit, such as a separate scholarship statement or declaration of intent to take up the funded place.
With no central portal there is no central checklist to fall back on, so every additional programme you apply to means rebuilding the file from that consortium's own instructions.
alerts: There is no single deadline to watch. Tracking only the brand name 'Erasmus Mundus' rather than individual programme sites is the single most reliable way to miss every window.
EACEA warns explicitly that numerous frauds target Erasmus Mundus applicants and that EU scholarships are not granted for a fee; no application or selection fee should ever be paid.
The scholarship is tied to full-time enrolment for the full programme duration, so it is incompatible with part-time study or a work-heavy schedule.

Additional regional scholarships funded through NDICI and IPA III can change the number of funded places available for applicants from targeted world regions, so odds vary by programme in a way the headline catalogue does not show.
Some catalogued masters are approaching the end of their EU funding or hold only temporary use of the name, so being listed is not proof that a scholarship is on offer this cycle.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the consortium's own online portal, then its selection committee ranks all applicants and offers the limited scholarship places to the best-ranked ones alongside unfunded offers, so the scholarship decision and the admission decision arrive together.

scholarships.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level, integrated transnational study programmes at master's level designed and delivered by international partnerships of higher education institutions. An EMJM involves at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, and includes periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence. Each edition runs 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits) and awards either a joint degree or multiple degrees. A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year, and students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme.

scholarships.title: DAAD Scholarship
scholarships.name: DAAD Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Mostly Master's/PhD (a few UG-eligible programmes exist but are rare)
scholarships.degree_levels: Mostly Master's/PhD (a few UG-eligible programmes exist but are rare)

applicant_utility.summary: DAAD is a database rather than one scholarship, so your first job is finding the programme that matches your level and subject and then reading that Call's own deadline and document list. Expect EUR 992 a month as a master's student, EUR 1,400 as a doctoral candidate or postdoc, a lump-sum travel allowance and in many programmes DAAD-arranged health insurance - but plan for tuition yourself, because DAAD does not pay university fees and places like Baden-Württemberg (EUR 1,500 per semester) or TUM (EUR 4,000-6,000 per semester) charge them. Winning the scholarship is still not admission: you must secure your own place at a German university or the award is forfeited.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-directed graduates and doctoral candidates with strong grades and a convincing project story who can manage several separate application calendars at once.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist programmes in the DAAD scholarship database by level, subject and country, and read each Call's 'Application procedure' and 'Application documents' tabs before drafting
Check two language requirements: what the scholarship asks for (proof of the language of instruction) and separately what your chosen university's admission requires (often C1)
For research or a doctorate, secure a German supervisor first and get the informal letter confirming supervision, a workplace and the working language
Send your shortlist and timing plan to the DAAD Information Centre in Dhaka - it is the official local contact point for Bangladesh
If you have been in Germany, count your months: more than 15 months by the closing date normally makes you ineligible
common_rejection_risks: Assuming one DAAD deadline - each programme closes on its own date and several are annual
Missing the language-of-instruction proof, or submitting a certificate older than 3 years
Holding a full Erasmus grant or another German state-agency scholarship, which blocks simultaneous DAAD funding
A weak research proposal or motivation letter: the committees score project preparation, feasibility and consistency of the schedule explicitly
Budgeting only for the stipend and then discovering the chosen university charges tuition
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: University tuition fees where charged (non-EU/EEA international students in Baden-Württemberg: EUR 1,500 per semester; TUM master's: EUR 4,000-6,000 per semester from winter semester 2024/2025; private universities and non-consecutive programmes can charge more), plus the gap between the stipend and high city rents that the DAAD FAQ itself warns about.
document_audit: Certificates and transcripts do not need to be certified at application - only after a positive selection decision - but keep originals retrievable
Documents in other languages must be translated into German or English; the translation need not be certified and you may translate yourself
The research proposal has a 10-page maximum and the time plan must be uploaded as a separate file
If AI tools are used in preparing the application, the DAAD requires an explicit note in the documents ('Produced with the aid of the tool used')
alerts: A full DAAD scholarship is not compatible with Erasmus funding
Scholarship without admission means the funding is forfeited, so apply to several universities early

Health insurance is compulsory from day one; the DAAD-arranged insurance excludes pre-existing conditions such as HIV, multiple sclerosis, haemophilia, cancer including leukaemia and chronic kidney disease, and births within 8 months of cover
Any part-time income above EUR 603 gross per month, or a second scholarship, is deducted from the DAAD payment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Select the programme in the database, apply inside its window (usually via the DAAD portal with all listed documents), wait on the independent selection committee decision, then arrange university admission and insurance separately.

Applications are submitted to the specific programme rather than to a single central DAAD form, and each programme sets its own eligibility, deadline and award conditions. scholarships.description: The Global Korea Scholarship is the Republic of Korea's representative government-invited scholarship programme, administered by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED), which invites outstanding students from around the world to study at Korean universities. It funds Korean language training plus associate degree, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programmes across more than 80 GKS universities, and also runs an exchange students programme and Korea-Japan exchange programmes. Applicants apply either through their Korean embassy (Embassy Track) or directly to a GKS university (University Track), and the scholarship covers airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances.

applicant_utility.summary: MEXT is seven scholarships in one: your money, age limit and examinations all change with the type you pick - research students get 143,000-145,000 yen a month with exemption of tuition and round-trip airfare, while undergraduates get 117,000 yen. Age rules are strict and unforgiving: under 25 for undergraduate, under 35 for research and teacher training. Since the Bangladeshi cycle runs through the Embassy of Japan and its notice page could not be reached today, confirm the current dates directly with the embassy rather than trusting any aggregator.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent high school graduates under 25 (undergraduate) and graduates under 35 with a Japanese supervisor secured for research-level study.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify which of the seven types applies to you - the stipend, age rule and examination subjects differ by type
Check the age cut-off against your birthday: undergraduates must be under 25 and research students under 35
Prepare for the embassy-recommendation examinations: Japanese and English for research/teacher training; Japanese, English, mathematics and science for undergraduates
Secure a graduate school admission path before relying on the scholarship - the award follows university admission
common_rejection_risks: Applying for the wrong type after your birthday has passed the age cut-off
Assuming the undergraduate stipend applies at graduate level (or the reverse)
Missing the embassy-recommendation examination or language requirement for your type
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs above the monthly scholarship, university admission fees not covered by the exemption, and personal expenses; the official page does not publish figures for those.
document_audit: Teacher-training applicants need five years of active teaching experience at primary, secondary or teacher-training college level - college and university teachers currently in service are excluded
Japanese studies applicants must remain enrolled at their home institution abroad while studying in Japan
alerts: The Bangladesh embassy notice page (bd.emb-japan.go.jp) blocked automated access on 10 October 2026 - verify the current deadline there directly
Scholars must not be enrolled in or have graduated from a Japanese university before applying through the undergraduate route
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Choose the type that matches your academic stage, apply through the Embassy of Japan or a Japanese university depending on the route, sit or satisfy the language and subject requirements, then finalise university admission before the scholarship is granted.

scholarships.description: The Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship is MEXT's scholarship programme for international students, offered in seven types: Research students, Teacher training students, Undergraduate students, Japanese studies students, College of technology students, Specialized training college students and Young Leaders Program students. There are two application routes: a recommendation from a Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission, or a recommendation from a Japanese university. The scholarship pays a monthly stipend, exempts tuition and provides a round-trip travel allowance (airfare), and in most tracks includes Japanese language training before or during study.
scholarships.duration: Research Students: 2 years for regular course (6 months preparatory education added if needed). Undergraduate: 5 years including Japanese language training (7 years for medicine/dentistry/pharmacy/veterinary science). Standard: Master's 2 years, Doctoral 3 years (4 years for some fields).

applicant_utility.summary: MOPGA 2027 is a 12-month, non-renewable postdoctoral fellowship paying EUR 2,500 per month plus a EUR 500 settling-in allowance and full health coverage, for foreign-nationality researchers who defended their PhD between December 2021 and December 2026 and will run a climate, energy or One Health project at a French host laboratory. You apply through Campus France's SMApply platform by 15 December 2026, and the host laboratory must supply a director-co-signed support letter before you submit - it is the single document most applications underestimate. Budget for your own relocation: the programme explicitly does not cover international travel, and the host laboratory receives no funding from it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers within five years of their PhD with a well-defined environmental or climate project and a French collaborator already in their network.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your thesis defence date falls inside December 2021 - December 2026 inclusive, and gather the official defence certificate if the diploma is not yet issued
Line up the supervisor support letter co-signed by the laboratory director (or the director's separate commitment letter) well before mid-December
Draft every project section to its character limit (2,000 characters; 4,500 for methodology and timeline) and stress the innovative/advanced-technology angle
Trim your CV to 4 pages with a publication list and ask your supervisor for a 2-page CV
Verify you are not professionally active in France and have never held a MOPGA fellowship before starting the form
common_rejection_risks: A project outside the five themes - pure medicine or human-health proposals without an environmental or animal-health dimension are ineligible
A missing, unsigned or generic host-laboratory letter; the lab must confirm the scientific environment and resources
A proposal that reads as incremental rather than innovative, since advanced-technology approaches are explicitly favoured
Overrunning the per-section character limits and losing substance to truncation
Emailing the application instead of using SMApply - email submissions are not considered
Holding or planning a French employment contract or other French government individual funding, which cannot be combined with the fellowship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel to France (unless the host lab helps), any laboratory-side research costs since the programme funds no lab expenses, visa and residence-permit fees, and accommodation and daily costs beyond the EUR 2,500 monthly allowance.
document_audit: Your CV is capped at 4 pages and must include the publication list; the supervisor CV is capped at 2 pages - both limits are hard
If the PhD diploma is not yet issued, an official defence certificate, proof of thesis submission or similar institutional document is acceptable
The support letter must be co-signed by the laboratory director or paired with the director's own letter of commitment
Recommendation letters: between 1 and 3, so decide deliberately rather than padding the file
A passport or national identity document copy is mandatory - check validity early
alerts: Deadline is fixed at 15 December 2026 for a call that opened 15 September 2026 - there is no late window
The PhD-defence eligibility window is inclusive and strict (December 2021 - December 2026); maternity-leave extensions must be documented in the file
French nationals are excluded and you must not be professionally active in France when you apply
The fellowship lasts exactly 12 months with no renewal - plan your next funding step before you arrive, since results only land May-June 2027 and the stay starts September-December 2027
The fellowship pays living expenses only; host laboratories receive nothing, so agree who covers research costs directly with the lab
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One SMApply submission with host-lab documents attached; MESRE-appointed scientific experts review the dossier, a scientific committee makes the final selection, and results are notified by email in May-June 2027.

scholarships.title: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship
scholarships.name: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Undergraduate, Graduate, Japanese Language Institute, College of Technology, Specialized Training College
scholarships.degree_levels: Undergraduate, Graduate, Japanese Language Institute, College of Technology, Specialized Training College

important_advice_for_students: Do not apply directly to JASSO. JASSO states the method of application is 'Please ask the staff at the educational institution in which you are enrolled'. Nothing you submit to JASSO will be considered.

Check first whether your institution can even recommend candidates. JASSO warns that the recommendation quota depends on the number of enrolled international students and that depending on the institution you may not be able to apply.
Budget on the stipend alone. This is 48,000 yen (or 30,000 yen at a Japanese language institute) per month. Tuition and enrollment fees are yours.

Pass the income test before anything else: your allowance excluding enrollment fee and tuition fee must not exceed an average of 90,000 yen per month, and any financial supporter in Japan must earn under 5 million yen a year.

Check that you are not on the grant of a Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship or any foreign government scholarship, and that you are not already on JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program - all three are explicit disqualifiers.
Get your language evidence ready early: JLPT N2+, EJU Japanese 200+, or CEFR B2+. These tests are scheduled and booked months ahead.
Note that the published English page does not give the GPA number; the Japanese page specifies a grade point average of 2.30 or above and expects it to be maintained during the award.

referee_tracking.role: None - no referee, reference or recommendation letter is required by the published JASSO programme page
referee_tracking.instructions: The published page describes no referee process at all. Selection is by institutional recommendation, and any referee requirement would sit inside the institution's own application guidelines (å‹Ÿé›†è¦é …), which JASSO does not publish. Confirm with your institution's international students office before assuming no reference is needed.

post_award_requirements: Sign the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office of the enrolled institution (monthly enrolment confirmation).
Cooperate with JASSO's career path survey, conducted through the enrolled institution or by other methods.
Maintain the published grade standard during the scholarship period (Japanese page: grade point average of 2.30 or above, expected to be maintained).
The award is paid monthly, so loss of enrolment status or missing the monthly signature stops payment.
questions_to_ask_host: Does my institution recommend candidates for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship this year, and what is my quota?
What is the internal deadline and the internal selection criteria in your application guidelines (å‹Ÿé›†è¦é …)? JASSO publishes none.
Which documents do I need for the institutional recommendation, and in what format, size and language must they be submitted?
Is tuition and the enrollment fee payable by me in full, and does the university offer a separate fee-reduction scheme I can stack?
Which English or Japanese proficiency evidence do you accept as satisfying the JLPT N2 / EJU 200 / CEFR B2 condition, and how recent must it be?
Which scholarship period can I be recommended for - the April-start 12 months or the October-start 6 months?
common_rejection_risks: Applying to JASSO directly instead of through the enrolled institution - there is no direct route.
Being at an institution with no recommendation quota, or missing the institution's internal deadline.
Allowance above the 90,000 yen per month average, or a supporter in Japan earning 5 million yen or more.
Already holding a Monbukagakusho or foreign government scholarship, or JASSO Student Exchange Support.
Not meeting the published language condition (JLPT N2 / EJU Japanese 200 / CEFR B2).
Falling below the grade point average threshold, or being unlikely to maintain it during the award.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees at the enrolled institution - not covered.
Enrollment fee - not covered.
Airfare to Japan and any relocation cost - not mentioned anywhere on the published page, so treat as not covered.
Books, materials and living costs beyond the 48,000 yen (or 30,000 yen) monthly stipend.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your institution actually recommends candidates for this scholarship this year - JASSO states the quota depends on the number of international students enrolled and that 'depending on your educational institution, you may not be able to apply'.
Confirm you hold residence status 'Student' (留学) and are not a grantee of the MEXT Scholarship or a foreign government scholarship.
Check your previous year's GPA is 2.30 or above and that you can maintain it during the grant period (the Japanese programme page sets this at 2.30 for all levels).
If you are not exempt by level, confirm JLPT N2+, EJU Japanese 200+ or a JASSO-recognised Japanese level, or CEFR B2+ in English.
Add up all allowance you receive excluding enrolment fee and tuition fee - it must not average more than JPY 90,000 per month.
If a financial supporter resides in Japan, confirm their annual income is under JPY 5,000,000.

List every other scholarship and support you hold and check none is restricted from concurrent receipt with the Honors Scholarships, and that you are not under JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program.
Agree in advance to the monthly enrolment-confirmation signature and to JASSO's career path survey.
Get the bank's account details ready for the 振込口座届 you will submit through the JASSO payment system once selected.
document_audit: JASSO publishes no document list and no format rules for this programme - no file size, file type, translation or date-of-issue rule exists on the official page. The binding document rules are in your institution's application guidelines (募集要項).

Ask the institution in writing for: the required documents, accepted file formats and sizes, whether a certified translation is accepted for documents not in Japanese, and how recent each document must be.

The published evidence items you will need to produce are: proof of enrolment as a full-time regular student, your previous year's grade report showing GPA 2.30 or above, a JLPT certificate / EJU score report or CEFR B2+ English evidence, and evidence of allowance received and of any financial supporter's income.
Monthly signature is the one published signature rule: you must sign the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office.

After selection, the bank account details form (振込口座届) is submitted through the JASSO scholarship payment system; the log-in ID and password come from the institution's staff, so request them at selection, not before.
submission_workflow: 1. Ask the staff at your enrolled educational institution whether they recommend candidates for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship and what the quota is.
2. Obtain the institution's application guidelines and their internal deadline - JASSO publishes none.
3. Prepare the evidence listed in the document audit and submit to the institution's international students office by its internal deadline.
4. The institution selects and recommends candidates to JASSO. You submit nothing to JASSO directly.
5. If selected, the institution issues you a log-in ID and password for the JASSO scholarship payment system (留学生給与等給付システム).
6. Submit the bank account details form (振込口座届) at https://www.sas.jasso.go.jp/abr/ following the current edition manual.
7. Sign the enrolment-confirmation sheet every month at the international students' office so that payment continues.

applicant_utility.summary: Erasmus+ pays you a monthly grant that depends on the country group you are moving to - anywhere between 225 and 674 EUR per month under the Guide's ranges, with the exact figure set by the National Agency and your institution - and exempts you from the receiving institution's tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library access fees. The grant is explicitly a contribution to travel and daily living costs, not a wage: housing deposits, flights and daily life above that contribution are yours to fund. Your application never goes to Brussels; your own university's international or Erasmus+ office applies for the funding on your behalf and also decides your selection.

scholarships.description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is open to short-cycle, Bachelor's and Master's students and to doctoral candidates registered at a participating higher education institution and enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree. There is no central application form: students apply through the international or Erasmus+ office of their own institution, which selects applicants fairly and transparently. The grant contributes to travel and daily living costs with amounts varying by destination and demand, and Erasmus+ students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library fees at the receiving institution. Mobilities run from 2 to 12 months for long-term study, or 5 to 30 days for short-term blended mobility, with up to 12 months in total per study cycle.

Maximum total duration is 12 months within one study cycle, with more than one exchange possible within that limit. For one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture, up to 24 months.

important_advice_for_students: You cannot apply to the European Commission. MSCA Doctoral Networks money goes to a consortium; you get a job as a recruited researcher inside a funded project.
Your real entry point is a funded project vacancy. Search the EURAXESS jobs list, which is updated daily, and apply directly to the institution or project.

Test your mobility eligibility first. If you have lived or worked/studied in the recruiting country for more than 12 months in the past 36 months, you are ineligible. This is the most common hard fail.
You must not already hold a PhD at the recruitment date.

Check the funding type before you commit. Standard, Industrial Doctorate and Joint Doctorate carry different rules - Industrial Doctorates require at least 50% of your time outside academia and mandatory joint supervision; Joint Doctorates run up to 48 months and lead to a joint or multiple degree.
Read the individual vacancy advertisement, not just the MSCA name. Conditions, salary and start date are set by the recruiting organisation and vary by country.

Overall indicative budget for the 2026 call is 593.03 million - that is the call total, not your fellowship. No per-fellowship salary figure is published on the MSCA pages read, so do not assume a number.

referee_tracking.instructions: MSCA does not publish a referee or reference-letter requirement for doctoral candidates. Selection is an open, transparent and merit-based process run by each funded network, so referees, if any, are set by the individual vacancy advertisement and the host institution's own process. Check the vacancy text.

post_award_requirements: Enrolment in the doctoral programme is a condition of the fellowship and must continue during the project.
Comply with the mobility rule throughout the fellowship.
For Industrial Doctorates, spend at least 50% of time outside academia.
Participate in network training, research and networking activities and follow the network's supervisory board arrangements.
Work to a career development plan agreed jointly with the supervisor, covering training, teaching, publication planning and conference participation.
Report on green / sustainable practices adopted by the project.
Abide by the grant agreement signed with the European Research Executive Agency and by the beneficiary's own employment contract.
questions_to_ask_host: Is the doctoral programme enrolment fee-free for employed researchers, or do I pay tuition to the host institution?
What is the gross and net monthly salary under national law, and which MSCA allowances (living, mobility, family, long-term leave, special needs) apply to my case?
Which country coefficients apply to my host country and family situation?
What is the exact employment start date, contract type and duration, and is the contract with the host institution or a partner?
Which secondment opportunities are paid, and how much funding is left for them?
What are the selection criteria, the assessment timeline, and does the process include an interview?
Which documents do you need, in which format, and by what internal deadline - which is earlier than the MSCA project start?
Is a reference letter or referee report required, and who contacts referees?
common_rejection_risks: Failing the mobility rule (more than 12 months in the recruiting country in the 36 months before recruitment).
Already holding a doctoral degree at the recruitment date.
Not enrolled in a doctoral programme leading to a degree in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
For consortium applicants: fewer than three independent legal entities in three different EU Member/Associated Countries, or none in an EU Member State.
For Joint Doctorates: fewer than three entities entitled to award doctoral degrees, or no degree-awarding institution in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
For Industrial Doctorates: an individual research plan that does not reach 50% time outside academia.
Resubmitting a proposal that scored below 80% the previous year - a resubmission restriction applies.
Late submission - the Electronic Submission Service will not accept a proposal after 17.00 CET on 24 November 2026.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Doctoral enrolment or tuition fees at the enrolling institution, if charged - the MSCA pages read do not state that these are covered; confirm with the host.
Visa, residence permit and relocation costs - not published as covered by MSCA.
Any salary component not covered by the living, mobility, family, long-term leave or special needs allowances.
Costs during secondments beyond the funded period, and personal costs not permitted under the grant.
document_audit: At EU level the published documents are for organisations, not individual candidates: guide for applicants, MSCA Work Programme and general annexes, proposal template and instructions, MSCA-specific evaluation forms, and the Horizon Online Manual.

No file size limits, accepted file types, translation rules or date-of-issue rules for individual candidates are published on the MSCA pages read; these are set by each vacancy advertisement and by the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal upload rules.
For the organisational route, the Electronic Submission Service is the only accepted submission system - proposals sent by email are not admissible.

alerts.message: Read the call page and the guide for applicants as soon as the call opens; consortium formation takes longer than applicants expect.
Hard submission deadline for proposals. Submit early; you can update, download or withdraw only up until the deadline.
If you are a doctoral candidate, monitor the EURAXESS list of MSCA-funded vacancies, which is updated daily.
Re-run the mobility check against your actual travel history in the past 36 months.

application_readiness_checklist: You cannot apply to the European Commission. The 24 November 2026 deadline belongs to consortium proposals; you apply to institutions advertising funded vacancies on EURAXESS.
Check you do not already hold a doctoral degree at the recruitment date - this is an absolute disqualifier.
Check the mobility rule: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in the recruiting organisation's country in the 36 months before your recruitment date.
Confirm the advertised position states that you will be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project.
For an Industrial Doctorate, confirm the position commits you to at least 50% of your time outside academia and joint supervision.
For a Joint Doctorate, confirm the advertised programme is a joint doctoral programme with joint supervision and a joint or multiple degree.
Prepare to be recruited as an employee: you will need identity, nationality, address, bank and tax-residence documents under the host country's employment law.
Use EURAXESS early for visa, pension and tax advice - MSCA publishes no arrival rules and the host country sets them.
submission_workflow: 1. Search the EURAXESS vacancy list for MSCA-funded doctoral positions (the MSCA filter covers EU-funded and MSCA-funded posts, updated daily).
2. Check the mobility rule for each advertised country before applying - a country you have lived in for over 12 months in the last 36 months will disqualify you.
3. Read the full requirement list published in the vacancy; it is set by the advertising institution, not by the EU.
4. Prepare the documents the vacancy asks for, using EURAXESS guidance for visa, pension, taxation and qualification-recognition issues.
5. Apply directly to the institution or project - you submit nothing to EURAXESS and nothing to the European Commission.
6. If shortlisted, expect an interview and reference checks by the host; agree your start date, salary and any secondment plan in writing before signing.
7. On appointment, the host enrols you in the doctoral programme and employs you, then claims the MSCA allowances through the beneficiary's reporting.

scholarships.description: France Excellence-Major is a French government scholarship run by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs that supports the best non-French baccalaureat holders from the network of French schools abroad to continue their higher education in France. Around 800 foreign students are supported at any one time over five years of study, and about 200 new holders join each year. Applications require pre-selection by the head of the French school abroad and online entry on the dedicated Cascade application, followed by assessment by the French embassy's cultural cooperation service and a selection commission convened by AEFE each May. Selection weighs school results, a coherent orientation project, involvement in school life and extracurricular activity, and motivation for demanding French higher education. Holders receive a family-need-rated monthly allowance of EUR 280 or EUR 860, complementary health cover, and, at the higher rates, round-trip travel and CROUS housing.

application_readiness_checklist: Check the 90-day Germany residence rule across the 18 months before you would submit
Confirm your career stage: within four years of the doctorate for postdocs, within twelve years for experienced researchers
Confirm you are not a German national or educational resident, or that you meet the long-term foreign residence test
Secure a host at a German university or research institution who will sign a mentoring agreement and confirm research facilities
Confirm the host is not your doctoral supervisor, your long-term postdoc mentor, or a close relative or partner
Request your two expert reviews early and send reviewers their secure upload links, since you cannot submit until they have uploaded
Prepare a CV of no more than two pages and a research outline of no more than five pages
Use the provided sample formats for the complete publication list and the key publication list
Submit well before the 800-application cap, since the round closes automatically at capacity
Check the call opening dates (15 March, 15 July, 15 November) and plan your fellowship start date
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the 800-application cap has closed the round, which currently happens quickly
Breaching the 90-day-in-18-months Germany residence rule
Missing the career-stage window, where a doctorate older than four years rules out postdoc funding
Formally rejected for incomplete documents or for diverging substantially from the publication list specifications
Choosing a doctoral supervisor or long-term postdoctoral mentor as host, which is generally rejected for lack of further independent academic development
Submitting before the two expert reviews have been uploaded by the reviewers
Missing the German language certificate where German is required for the research
Previously having received direct Humboldt Foundation sponsorship, which bars reapplication to this programme
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Germany beyond the monthly fellowship and family allowances
Tuition or enrolment fees, which this fellowship does not fund
Return travel if the home institution already covers it, or amounts above a single lump sum
Family travel, which is paid only in exceptional circumstances
Costs of research stays outside Germany beyond the 25% guidance, and any earnings there are usually deducted
document_audit: Confirm the CV is two pages maximum and the research outline is five pages maximum
Confirm the complete publication list and key publication list follow the provided sample formats exactly
Confirm key publications are uploaded, with translations or summaries where not in German or English
Confirm the mentoring agreement and research facilities confirmation are in place before submission
Confirm expert reviews are no more than 12 months old at the time of application
Confirm the doctoral certificate or expected-completion confirmation is uploaded

alerts.message: The current call is closed at capacity. The next call opens 15 November 2026; if you cannot submit in time, work started then counts as received on the portal closure date provided you submit no more than 14 days after the next call opens.
Expect roughly one in four to five applications to be approved, so apply with a strong publication record and a clearly original project.
Applications involving returning to the doctoral supervisor or a longer postdoctoral mentor are generally rejected, so seek a genuinely new academic environment.
Time outside Germany should usually stay under 25% of the funding period, and earnings from the host country are reported and usually deducted.

submission_workflow: Verify your career stage and the 90-day/18-month Germany residence rule
Choose an academic host in Germany and agree the mentoring agreement and facilities confirmation
Contact your two expert reviewers and send them their secure upload links
Prepare the two-page CV, five-page research outline, publication lists and key publications
Upload a German language certificate if required for your research
Wait for the expert reviews to be uploaded, then submit the application through the online portal
Monitor the portal status, since the application is only forwarded once the host has submitted their documents
Await the formal eligibility and completeness checks and, if shortlisted, the peer review and selection committee stage
Arrange the pre-stay language course and the fellowship start, two to twelve months after the selection meeting

scholarships.deadline: Three calls annually: March 15, July 15, November 15 (2026 schedule)
scholarships.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
scholarships.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.
scholarships.application_period: Three selection rounds per year (March, July, November)
scholarships.official_source: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (German Federal Foreign Office)
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).

scholarships.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.

scholarships.title: JASSO Student Exchange Support Program
scholarships.name: JASSO Student Exchange Support Program

application_readiness_checklist: Understand the route first: you cannot apply to JASSO yourself - your Japanese host school submits the application
Find a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology or professional training college that has an exchange agreement with your home institution
Check your nationality: you must be from a country with diplomatic relations with Japan; Taiwan and Palestine are expressly accepted
Check the 80,000 JPY cap - if your other scholarships for study in Japan total more than 80,000 JPY per month, you are ineligible
Confirm you do not have the financial means to study in Japan, which is an eligibility condition rather than a partial-need test
Confirm your home-country record is strong: eligibility requires "excellent academic and personal records at your home school"
Confirm you will return to complete your studies at your home school after the period in Japan
Check you are eligible for the Student Visa, or note that for 90 days or less the Japanese school arranges the status of residence
Ask your home school about its own selection method, since JASSO says it "is different from each school and each program"
Agree the start date with the Japanese school, because you must start during the school's designated period
important_advice_for_students: Do not look for a JASSO application form or deadline - JASSO publishes neither, and applications come only from Japanese schools
Do not treat this as a full scholarship: 80,000 JPY per month is the only published benefit, and JASSO says nothing about tuition, travel, accommodation or insurance
Plan the length of your stay carefully - anything from 8 days to one year is eligible, and the monthly rate is the same, so a short stay gives a small total award
Do not combine it with another Japanese scholarship paying more than 80,000 JPY per month; the sum matters, not the number of scholarships
The fastest route is through your home school's exchange office, because the selection method is institution-specific and JASSO repeatedly redirects students there
If you are applying for 90 days or less, the Japanese school handles the status of residence, which simplifies your visa position
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to JASSO instead of through a Japanese school, which is impossible
Applying without a student exchange agreement or other student exchange arrangement in place
Coming from a country without diplomatic relations with Japan
Receiving more than 80,000 JPY per month in total from other scholarships for study in Japan
Having the financial means to study in Japan, which makes you ineligible
Weak academic or personal records at the home school
Not intending to return to complete studies at the home school
Starting the programme outside the Japanese school's designated period
Missing the school's own internal selection timetable, which JASSO does not publish
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition at the Japanese school, if any is charged - JASSO publishes no tuition coverage
Living costs beyond the 80,000 JPY monthly stipend; JASSO publishes no living-cost calculation
Round-trip travel to and from Japan - no travel component is published
Health insurance - no insurance component is published
Books, materials and personal expenses
Any costs arising from a programme longer than one year
document_audit: Documents are submitted by the Japanese school to JASSO, not by the student
JASSO screens "the application documents submitted by Japanese school" but publishes no document list
The home school will tell you what is required, since "the selection method of scholarship recipients is different from each school and each program"
No published file size limit, accepted file type, translation, certification, date or signature rule
Expect to evidence: exchange agreement or arrangement, financial need, academic and personal records, visa eligibility, and total monthly scholarship income from other sources

alerts.message: There is no JASSO deadline to track; the operative dates are your home school's selection process and the Japanese school's designated programme period.
If your other Japanese scholarships total more than 80,000 JPY per month, you become ineligible for this one.

alerts.trigger: If your stay is 90 days or less
alerts.message: The Japanese school arranges your status of residence.

Confirm eligibility against all seven published conditions, including the 80,000 JPY cap and the financial-need condition
Confirm Student Visa eligibility
Ask the Japanese school to submit the application and documents to JASSO
Await JASSO's notification to the Japanese school
Begin the programme during the school's designated period
Return home to complete your studies at your home institution
post_award_requirements: Start the study-in-Japan programme during the Japanese school's designated period
Stay within the 8-days-to-one-year funded period
Do not accept other scholarships for study in Japan totalling more than 80,000 JPY per month
Complete studies at the home school after the period of study in Japan
Remain within the exchange agreement or arrangement for the whole funded period

scholarships.title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) Non-degree Exchange Program
scholarships.name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) Non-degree Exchange Program

important_advice_for_students: Do not confuse this with the GKS Degree Program. The exchange programme is 4 months, pays KRW 630,000 per month plus round-trip economy airfare, accommodation, settlement and insurance - it does NOT list tuition, and the quota (~500) and route are completely different.

Your real task is institutional. You cannot apply to NIIED. Your home university must have an agreement with a NIIED-affiliated Korean university that has been selected to run the programme, and the Korean university must recommend you.
Check you are applying to only one Korean university at a time. Multiple simultaneous applications are disallowed.
You must be in a degree exchange programme. A Korean language course placement does not qualify.
You need 80% overall academic performance at your home university. Have your transcript ready with that figure provable.

If you have ever held a Korean government scholarship, you are ineligible. If you currently study in Korea, you are ineligible. If you hold Korean citizenship, including dual citizenship, you are ineligible.
There is no published extension: recipients who have completed one semester (4 months) cannot apply for a scholarship extension.
Budget on KRW 630,000 per month. Study in Korea notes the monthly allowance may vary based on stay and semester end date, so the final month can differ.

referee_tracking.instructions: NIIED's published selection procedure is 'NIIED reviews and selects scholarship applicants recommended by the selected universities' - it names no referee, transcript assessor or interview panel. Any reference or recommendation letter required is set by your home university and the participating Korean university, not by NIIED. Ask both before nominating.

post_award_requirements: Complete the published support period of 4 months (1 semester) at the participating university.
Stay within the degree exchange programme you were nominated for.
Return to your home university at the end of the exchange - the award is round-trip airfare and a single 4-month period; no continuation or second placement is published.
Any reporting to the participating university or NIIED is set by that institution; NIIED publishes no post-award reporting rule on the pages read.
questions_to_ask_host: Is my university on NIIED's published list of universities operating the GKS Exchange Students Program this year?
What is the internal nomination deadline at my home university, and how far ahead of that do you need my documents?
Am I exempt from tuition at the host as an exchange student, and is any tuition charged to me or to the GKS grant? NIIED does not list tuition as covered.
What exactly does 'accommodation' cover - dormitory place, and any dormitory fee not covered by the grant?
How is the KRW 630,000 monthly allowance adjusted at the start and end of the semester, given the published note that it varies with stay and semester end date?
Is airfare booked centrally or do I book and claim? Which economy routing and fare rules apply?
What documents, in which language and format, do you need for nomination, and does the home university require translation or notarisation?
common_rejection_risks: Previous receipt of a Korean government scholarship.
Holding Korean citizenship, including as a dual national.
Currently studying in Korea.
Placement in a Korean-language-only course rather than a degree exchange programme.
Overall academic performance below 80% at the home university.
No agreement between the home university and a participating Korean university, or the Korean university is not on NIIED's selected list.
Applying to more than one Korean university at the same time.
Applying for an extension after having already completed one semester.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, if the host charges them to exchange students - tuition is not a published GKS exchange benefit.
Any portion of airfare above the actual economy-class round-trip cost, and baggage or seat fees.
Living costs beyond KRW 630,000 per month, and any semester-end reduction in that allowance.
Books, materials, and personal expenses.
Visa, residence permit and any dormitory deposit not covered by the accommodation benefit.
document_audit: NIIED's English programme page and the Study in Korea GKS Exchange Students Program section publish no document list, no file-size limit, no accepted file types, no translation rule and no date rule. documents and document_format_rules are therefore deliberately empty.
The requirement list is set by the participating Korean university and the home university; obtain it in writing before assembling anything.

Minimum evidence you will need and that the published conditions already key on: proof of enrolment at the home university, proof of the university agreement, a transcript evidencing 80% or above overall academic performance, and proof of nationality.

alerts.trigger: Before applying to any Korean university
alerts.message: Confirm the university appears on NIIED's published list of universities operating the GKS Exchange Students Program. Only those universities can nominate you.
Apply through one Korean university only. Simultaneous applications are disallowed.
Confirm in writing whether tuition is payable, since tuition is not a published benefit of this programme.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your Korean university appears in NIIED's published participating-university list for the current year (the current list is the 2026 file) - only those universities can nominate anyone for this programme.
Confirm your home university holds an agreement with that specific participating Korean university. Without the agreement there is no route at all.
Confirm you will be placed in a degree exchange programme. A Korean-language-only placement is explicitly excluded.
Confirm your overall academic performance at the home university is 80% or above.
Confirm you have never received a scholarship from the Korean government, that you do not hold Korean citizenship (including as a dual national), and that you are not currently studying in Korea.
Choose exactly one Korean university - applying to more than one at the same time is disqualifying.
Check you have not already completed a one-semester (4-month) scholarship period under this programme; if you have, an extension is impossible.

Budget for what the scholarship does not pay: tuition at the host if charged to exchange students, and anything beyond the standard KRW 630,000 monthly allowance and the actual round-trip economy fare.
Plan for a four-month stay only, and arrange your own academic credit transfer with your home university before you go.
submission_workflow: 1. Obtain NIIED's participating-university list for the current year from the Study in Korea GKS Exchange section and pick one university that has an agreement with your home university.
2. Apply to your home university for the exchange place, using its exchange-application process for students nominated under that bilateral agreement.
3. Meet your home university's internal deadline - this is the only deadline that exists; NIIED publishes none.
4. Submit to your home university the academic evidence it requires, including proof of 80% or above overall academic performance, for onward nomination.
5. The participating Korean university selects you from the nominations and forwards its recommendation to NIIED.
6. NIIED reviews the recommendations and announces the scholarship selection; keep an eye on your home and host university for the notification, since NIIED publishes no results date.

7. After selection, confirm with the participating university what the accommodation, settlement and insurance components mean in practice, and book travel against the actual round-trip economy fare only.

scholarships.description: Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term awards administered by Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade for people from developing countries, particularly in the Indo-Pacific, to study full time at participating Australian universities and TAFE institutions. Benefits generally include full tuition fees, return airfare, an establishment allowance, a fortnightly living-expense contribution, health cover and the Introductory Academic Program. Applicants must sign a contract with the Commonwealth and leave Australia for two years after completing the award or repay the cost.

applicant_utility.summary: This row is a duplicate label problem rather than a live scholarship: the Netherlands Fellowship Programme (and the Orange Knowledge Programme that succeeded it) no longer run - the official Study in NL hub confirms OKP ended in 2024 and lists only MSP, Erasmus+ and the NL Scholarship as Nuffic-administered awards. If your degree is not sponsored under one of those, OTS-style support is arranged directly with individual Dutch universities, without any central Nuffic page, deadline or amount. Treat any site advertising 'NFP/OTS 2027' with suspicion and go to the university's own funding page instead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students assessing current Dutch options rather than this legacy label - realistically the NL Scholarship (Holland Scholarship), Erasmus+ or a university bursary.

As of 2026-10-04 the Study in NL scholarship hub no longer lists a dedicated OTS page, so amounts and deadlines must be obtained from the participating institution or Neso office. This row must not be merged with the Netherlands Fellowship Programme (NFP), which is a separate Nuffic programme.

scholarships.description: The Swedish Institute, a Swedish government agency, awards fully funded scholarships for master's studies in Sweden to global professionals from 34 eligible countries. The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals covers full tuition fees, a monthly living-expense allowance of SEK 12,000 and a one-time travel grant, and runs once a year for master's studies starting in the autumn semester. The Swedish Institute also runs the Pioneering Women in STEM scholarship, awarded through the same single application. The 2026/2027 call closed on 25 February 2026 and recipients were announced on 23 April 2026; the next call is expected to be published on si.se in mid-November 2026.

scholarships.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program is administered by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) for outstanding foreign students, and is distinct from the MOFA Taiwan Scholarship and the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship. It pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 each semester and a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 for bachelor's students and NTD 20,000 for master's and doctoral students. Applications go to the Taiwan Representative Office responsible for the applicant's country and a separate application to a Taiwanese university is also required. The 2026 round ran from 1 February to 31 March 2026 and has closed; the next round falls in early 2027.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a monthly grant for living and studying costs, not a full scholarship: it is paid only for the months actually in Italy, and nine-month grants run 1 November to 31 July, so plan your own funds around the rest of the year. Applications are free and go only through the official Study in Italy platform - never pay an agent - and you may list up to three course options of the same type. The A.Y. 2026-2027 round has already closed with the final ranking published on 3 June 2026, and the portal had not yet announced the next call as of 10 October 2026, so use the interval to line up your CEFR-language certificate and supervisor contacts.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-motivated graduates and PhD applicants who can top up the Italian living grant with their own funds and apply separately for university admission.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on the eligible countries list in the Call - if it is not, you cannot apply at all
Choose up to three course options, all of the same type, at institutions listed on the Universitaly portal
Start the separate university enrolment process early: the grant application does not enrol you

Prepare your language certificate from an official body with an explicit CEFR level (Duolingo only works for English), and be ready to supplement it by 14:00 Italian time on 1 July if you make the ranking
Keep the motivation letter under 500 words and upload everything as PDF files under 2 MB
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 July 14:00 Italian time supplementary-documents deadline, after which the application cannot be evaluated
Proposing an online study programme, which is expressly ineligible
Uploading translated or legalized paperwork that was never required, wasting time and stalling the real gaps (qualification, transcript, language certificate)
Assuming the MAECI grant also secures university admission - it does not
Mixing course types across the three options, which the platform disallows
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the monthly grant: accommodation outside the 1 November - 31 July window, travel to Italy, enrolment taxes or tuition the institution charges, and general living costs.
document_audit: PhD applicants must upload the admission letter; until it exists, the supervisor's invitation letter substitutes, but pre-admission letters are never accepted
Renewal applicants need a certificate or hand-signed self-declaration of university credits (CFU) obtained with marks
No translations or legalizations are needed - original scans in PDF only, merged where necessary, each file under 2 MB
Supplementary documents - including language certificates - cannot be submitted for intensive language courses or renewals, so those must be complete at submission
alerts: The next Call is not yet published; the grant amount itself is fixed only in each Call, which is why no figure appears here
Only applications submitted through the Study in Italy website are accepted - other channels are not
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Wait for the Call on studyinitaly.esteri.it, apply free of charge on the platform with up to three same-type course options, upload the PDF document set before the deadline, supplement by 1 July 14:00 Italian time if ranked, then await the ranking published by the Italian Diplomatic representation.

scholarships.description: The Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation awards scholarships to foreign students and Italian citizens resident abroad (IRE) under Italian law 288/55, to foster cultural, scientific and technological cooperation and to promote Italian language and culture. Scholarships are available only for academic courses taught on Italian territory, and the call sets out separate categories for degree study, research grants and shorter language or training courses. For academic year 2026-2027 applications were accepted exclusively through the Study in Italy portal and had to be received by 2 p.m. CET on 26 March 2026, so that cycle is closed. The ministry publishes the annual call, the English version and a list of eligible countries as PDF documents for each academic year.

scholarships.title: Pearson International Scholarship (University of Toronto)
scholarships.name: Pearson International Scholarship (University of Toronto)

applicant_utility.summary: Pearson is one of the few true full rides - it pays tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years - but you cannot apply yourself: a current secondary school must nominate you through its own participating portal account, one student per year, by noon EST on 9 October 2026. With that nomination door now closed for the 2027 cycle, the only steps still salvageable are the OUAC admission application by 16 October 2026 and the Pearson application form with supporting documents by 6 November 2026, if you were already nominated. Ignore anyone offering agent services: the official page states that offices and agents have nothing to do with the process.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year international secondary students with an exceptional record of academics, creativity, leadership and community commitment who can get nominated by their own current school.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm whether your school is a participating school on the Pearson portal and, if nomination is still open, that it can nominate you by the noon EST deadline
If nominated: submit the OUAC admission application by 16 October 2026 and include the University of Toronto
Complete the Pearson scholarship application form and upload supporting documents by 6 November 2026
Choose one intended program of study carefully - the award is restricted to the first-entry undergraduate program selected on the application form
Track notifications from end January 2027 onward: nominations, offers, acceptances and wait lists, all resolved by end of April 2027
common_rejection_risks: Assuming self-application is possible - nomination by your current secondary school is the only route published
Missing the staggered deadlines: nomination (9 October), OUAC admission (16 October), Pearson application and documents (6 November)
Applying through an agent: the page warns offices and agents have nothing to do with the process and the university bears no responsibility for errors by third parties
Being ineligible on status: already enrolled in post-secondary, or starting post-secondary in January 2027
Losing the scholarship later by not maintaining full-time enrollment and satisfactory academic standing
