scholarships.title: Australia Awards Fellowships
scholarships.name: Australia Awards Fellowships

important_advice_for_students: You cannot apply for this as an individual, and you are very unlikely to be the right applicant. The applicant must be an Australian legal entity with a current ABN; students apply only as the nominated Fellow inside someone else's application.

Your realistic route is: be employed by an Overseas Counterpart Organisation in an eligible country that already has or can build a partnership with an Australian organisation, and be nominated as a senior official or mid-career professional.

Check the eligible country list first. The programme is limited to listed ODA-eligible countries in the Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and the Middle East, Africa, the Caribbean and (Europe) Ukraine.

The hard personal disqualifiers are worth checking early: any Australian citizenship including dual citizenship, any Australian permanent residency or an application for it, being current serving military personnel, and being married or engaged to (or in a de facto relationship with) anyone who holds or is eligible to hold Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency.

Budget carefully. The published figure is 'up to $34,500 per Fellow' and the Australian Host Organisation must add an in-kind and/or financial co-contribution. Treat $34,500 as a ceiling, not an entitlement.
DFAT funds only the individual Fellow. Family members are not funded and no visa support letters are issued for them - if you need family to travel, that cost is not covered.

English ability is a real requirement, not a formality: the Fellow must have 'an adequate level of English language ability to be able to fully participate in the program, including an ability to complete the Fellow's Completion Survey at the conclusion of their Fellowship'.
Watch the calendar. Round 21 closed on 16 January 2026 and Round 22 is expected to open only in the final quarter of 2026, so this is not a programme to start assembling in December.
If your OCO is an international branch of the Australian organisation, or sits under the same overarching international organisation, it does not qualify.

referee_tracking.role: No individual Fellow referee or reference process is published
referee_tracking.instructions: DFAT publishes no referee requirement for the Fellow. Selection happens at application level, assessed by DFAT against the mandatory Application Compliance Criteria, and the Fellow is vetted by the Australian Host Organisation against the published general eligibility requirements. Any reference or supporting statement is an Australian Host Organisation requirement under the round guidelines, not a DFAT-published Fellow requirement.

post_award_requirements: Participate in the nominated Fellowship activities for the full duration proposed by the Australian Host Organisation, except in exceptional circumstances approved by the GSU and DFAT.
Travel without family members - DFAT funds and provides visa support letters for the individual Fellow only.
Complete the Fellow's Completion Survey at the conclusion of the Fellowship (the English requirement is written around this).
Deliver the in-partner country component focused on implementation and exchange of expertise, skills and knowledge; the in-partner country duration may not exceed the in-Australia duration.
Follow the Australia Awards Fellowships Pre-Departure Guide, which DFAT publishes for each round.
Deliver the minimum two weeks in Australia as planned - the design of the placement is assessed on that basis.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the Australian Organisation's co-contribution in cash and in kind, and how is it valued?
How much of the up-to-$34,500 will actually be available for me, and what does the budget table for the round allow me to spend it on?
Is airfare, accommodation, per diems and visa costs inside the grant or additional? The DFAT page does not break this down.
Do I pay any fees to the host institution, and are there tuition or course costs for the study/training components?
What are the internal nomination deadlines, and who in my OCO signs the application?
What are the exact document requirements, file formats and page limits set out in the round guidelines?
Does the Fellowship include any onward in-partner country funding, and is that funded by DFAT or by my OCO?
What happens if my circumstances change mid-Fellowship - who do I notify, and what does the GSU approval process require?
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an individual, or as an OCO rather than an Australian ABN-holding entity.
An OCO that is an international arm/branch of the Australian organisation or sits under the same overarching international body.
An OCO in a country not on the eligible list.
Failing any mandatory compliance criterion - these are stated as pass/fail gates to reach assessment.
No co-contribution from the Australian Organisation, or no in-partner country activity.
Less than two weeks in Australia, total duration outside 2-52 weeks, or in-Australia duration not longer than in-partner country duration.
Exceeding six applications as the Australian Organisation, or proposing more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows.

A nominated Fellow with Australian citizenship, Australian permanent residency, an application for either, or a partner who holds or is eligible to hold Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency.
A nominated Fellow who is current serving military personnel, or who cannot travel without family members.
Insufficient English to participate fully, including completing the Completion Survey.
An applicant on the National Redress Scheme or a proscribed list.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Family travel and related costs - DFAT funds only the individual Fellow.
Any cost above the up-to-$34,500 per Fellow ceiling.
Whatever the Australian Host Organisation does not cover from its required co-contribution.
Personal expenses, and any costs of extending the placement beyond the approved duration.
document_audit: DFAT publishes no document list, file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule or date-of-issue rule on this page. document_format_rules is therefore deliberately empty.

The binding format source is the current round guidelines - DFAT has published 'Australia Awards Fellowships guidelines round 21' and round 20 guidelines and round 20 budget tables as DOCX and PDF. Get the guidelines for the round you are applying to and work from its document checklist.

Compliance items to have ready: current ABN of the Australian Organisation; confirmation the submitting officer is an employee; the Organisation's application count to date; confirmation of non-listing on the National Redress Scheme and the four proscribed lists; the OCO's country of operation and residence; a per-Fellow eligibility checklist (age, citizenship, residency status, service status, partner status).

alerts.message: Round 22 is expected to open. Watch the Australia Awards site and the DFAT page for the published opening date and closing deadline.
Attend the Industry Information Session - Round 21's was held in the week after opening and is where DFAT walks through the compliance criteria.
Re-run the mandatory Application Compliance Criteria list. Failing any one of them means the application does not reach assessment.
Check the spouse/partner restriction and the Australian citizenship / permanent residency restriction. Both are absolute disqualifiers.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are applying through an Australian legal entity with a current ABN - individuals and OCOs cannot apply, and the submitting officer must be an employee of that entity.

Confirm your country of citizenship and your country of residence both appear in DFAT's published eligible-country list; citizenship and residence may be different countries but both must be eligible.
Confirm you have held no Australian permanent resident status and are not applying for it.
Confirm you are not current serving military personnel.

Confirm you are not married, engaged or in a de facto relationship with anyone who holds or is eligible to hold Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency - this is a hard exclusion and is widely missed.
Confirm you can obtain a visa satisfying Department of Home Affairs requirements for the whole Fellowship.
Confirm you have been working in your country of citizenship or residency, in a field relevant to the Fellowship, before the proposed start date.
Confirm you can travel without family members and can be away for 2 to 52 weeks.
Confirm your English is good enough to take part fully and to complete the Fellow's Completion Survey at the end.
Have the Australian Host Organisation's co-contribution (cash and/or in kind) agreed and quantified before drafting.
Build the Fellowship so that at least two weeks sit in Australia, the in-Australia block is longer than the in-partner country block, and the total stays within 52 weeks.
Align the proposal to exactly one of the six development priority areas and say so explicitly.
Check the Australian organisation is not listed on the National Redress Scheme and is not on the ADB, World Bank, terrorist-organisation or Consolidated List proscribed lists.
Confirm the Australian organisation is within its six-application cap and that the proposal is within the 15 DFAT-funded Fellow cap.
Download the current round's guidelines and budget table and use their exact templates - format failure means no assessment at all.
submission_workflow: 1. Choose the one development priority area your Fellowship aligns with and settle the eligible-country question for the OCO.
2. Agree the Fellowship shape with the Australian Host Organisation: total 2-52 weeks, minimum two weeks in Australia, in-partner country activity included and shorter than the Australian block.
3. Agree and value the Australian Host Organisation's co-contribution in cash and in kind.
4. Download the current round's guidelines and budget table from the DFAT round resources and build the application in the specified format.
5. Run the mandatory compliance criteria against your draft - all of them, because one failure removes the application from assessment.
6. Have the submitting officer, who must be an employee of the Australian Organisation, lodge the application with DFAT before the published round closing date and time zone.
7. After DFAT selects the Australian Host Organisation, the host confirms the individual Fellow's eligibility and arrangements, and DFAT issues the visa support letter for the Fellow only.
8. Follow the DFAT Pre-departure Guide once the Fellowship is confirmed.

scholarships.description: Australia Awards Fellowships is a DFAT competitive grants programme in which an Australian organisation - never an individual - applies for funding to host a Fellow nominated by an overseas counterpart organisation in an eligible developing country. The grant is up to $34,500 per Fellow for a single Fellowship of 2 to 52 weeks, and the Australian Host Organisation must add a mandatory cash and/or in-kind co-contribution; DFAT publishes no tuition component, no living-cost rate and no separate airfare figure. Every application must first clear a mandatory compliance gate - correct format, current ABN, no more than six applications per organisation, no more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows, at least two weeks in Australia, in-partner country activity, and alignment with one of six development priority areas - or it is never assessed. The Fellow must travel without family, cannot hold or be seeking Australian permanent residency, and must be a citizen of and resident in one of DFAT's listed eligible countries; Round 21 closed on 16 January 2026 and Round 22 is expected to open in the final quarter of 2026 with no date published.
scholarships.duration: 2 to 52 weeks per Fellowship. The Fellowship commences in Australia and is followed by in-partner country activities focused on implementation and exchange of expertise. The duration of the in-partner country activities must not exceed the duration of the activities in Australia. The mandatory compliance criteria add that at least two weeks must be delivered in Australia and that the total cannot exceed 52 weeks, counting in-Australia, online and in-partner country activity together.

Mandatory compliance gate: the application must satisfy every published Application Compliance Criterion or it does not progress to the assessment stage - specified format; legal Australian entity with a current ABN; applicant not an individual or OCO; submitting officer an employee of the Australian Organisation; no more than six applications by the organisation; no more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows in one application; eligible countries only; a co-contribution from the Australian Organisation included; in-partner country activity included; alignment with one development priority area; a minimum of two weeks in Australia; total duration of 2 to 52 weeks; in-Australia duration longer than in-partner duration; OCO from an eligible ODA-listed country and not an arm/branch or sister body of the Australian organisation; not listed in the National Redress Scheme; not on the ADB, World Bank, terrorist-organisation or Consolidated List proscribed lists

important_advice_for_students: There is no Commonwealth application and no Commonwealth deadline. Everything - application, selection, deadline, documents, English test - is set by the university, and it must publish that in its RTP scholarship policy. Read the policy before you spend anything on applications.

As an international student you are eligible, but your university may only spend up to 10% of its RTP funding per grant year on international students. Ask the postgraduate research office directly whether any RTP places are available to internationals before you invest in a research proposal.

Check the exact combination you are being offered. A university may give you a fees offset only, stipend only, allowance only, or a combination, and the fee offset amount varies by university and research area. The offer letter must state the estimated value of each component.

Budget on the range, not a number. The stipend must be at least the base full-time rate and no more than the maximum: for 2027 that is AUD 35,550 to AUD 55,537 per year; 2026 was AUD 34,315 to AUD 53,608. Part-time is 50% of whatever the university offers and is taxable, whereas full-time stipends are tax exempt if you meet the ATO criteria.
If you are an international student, ask whether an OSHC allowance is included. It is listed as a valid allowance use, but it is not automatic.

Do not assume a scholarship you must not combine still blocks you. The old rule barring other income related to the course of study above 75% of the stipend was removed on 3 December 2025. But if you already hold a Commonwealth award for HDR tuition fees, that bars an RTP fees offset - so check before you accept a second offer.

Plan your period of support carefully. It is counted from your HDR commencement date, including any time done at a previous university, and it is not reset if you transfer. Support cannot be extended beyond the maximum (4 years FT doctorate, 8 years PT doctorate, 2 years FT masters, 4 years PT masters).
Check whether your provider restricts paid work. The provider must publish the circumstances in which it will not let you work outside your HDR, including any hours cap.
You will have to acknowledge the Commonwealth in publications, and add the RTP DOI to your ORCID profile if you have one.

referee_tracking.role: Referee reports - at the provider's discretion, not a Commonwealth requirement
referee_tracking.instructions: The Commonwealth Guidelines do not name a required number of referees. FAQ 4 and FAQ 8 both state only that 'in determining its selection process for RTP scholarship, a university may consider previous study, relevant work experience, research publications, referee reports, and other factors'. The number of referees, who may be contacted, and the form of the report are set in the university's RTP scholarship policy and its HDR admission requirements. Check both, and contact referees early - academic referees can be slow.

post_award_requirements: Acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in research publications using the required wording: 'This research was supported by the Commonwealth through an Australian Government Research Training Program Scholarship [DOI: https://doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220] .' This applies to recipients of an RTP fees offset, stipend or allowance.
Include the RTP DOI in your ORCID profile if you already have one (the Funding section is described as appropriate). There is no requirement to create an ORCID profile if you do not have one.
Meet the provider's rules on work outside your HDR, which the provider must publish in its RTP scholarship policy.
Follow the provider's published suspension process; the provider must publish how suspensions operate.

Accept the provider's conditions on paid recreation leave, personal leave, additional personal leave, parental leave, partner leave and family and domestic violence leave, and note which of these extend the period of support.
Maintain enrolment and progress in the HDR; the provider administers the scholarship.
questions_to_ask_host: Do you offer RTP to international students this year, and how many places are left under your 10% cap?
Which combination will I receive - fees offset, stipend, allowances - and what is the estimated value of each, as stated in my offer letter?
What stipend rate will I be paid, and is it the base rate or above? Will the rate be re-indexed each 1 January?
Will the award be full-time or part-time, and does a part-time load halve the stipend?
Is an OSHC allowance included for me and my dependants, and is a relocation allowance available?
What is your internal closing date, and what documents, formats and referee reports do you require?
What English language or IELTS requirement applies to international applicants in your RTP process?
What restrictions do you place on paid work, and do I need approval before taking any work?
What is your policy on suspending the scholarship, and on transferring to another university without resetting my period of support?
How does the RTP industry internship weighting work for my research doctorate, and what is the deadline for the written internship agreement?
common_rejection_risks: Missing the university's internal deadline - the Commonwealth publishes none, so all timing risk sits with the provider.
Applying for a coursework degree (bachelor or masters coursework) instead of a research degree.
Applying for an HDR at an overseas university rather than an eligible Australian provider.
The provider having no international-student RTP places available under its 10% cap.
Holding another Commonwealth award or scholarship for HDR tuition fees, which bars an RTP fees offset.

Missing the provider's additional selection criteria - first class honours is not required by the Guidelines, but marks, discipline, first-time-research status and on-campus study are all things providers publish as priorities.
Failing the provider's English language or IELTS requirement.
Assuming the maximum stipend rate. The provider sets a rate within the base-to-maximum band.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any part of the HDR tuition fee not covered by the fees offset - the offset must fully cover applicable HDR fees, but the student must check the estimated value in the offer letter because it varies by university and research area.
Living costs above the stipend actually offered. The stipend is a band, not a fixed amount.

Everything not covered by an allowance: the published allowance examples are relocation, thesis printing, academic publication and OSHC. Books, equipment, conference travel and living-cost shortfalls are not named as covered.
Living costs for dependants beyond any OSHC allowance.
For part-time students, the difference between 100% and 50% of the full-time rate, and the tax payable on the part-time stipend.
Unpaid research-related costs if the provider offers fees offset only with no stipend and no allowances.
document_audit: The Commonwealth publishes no RTP document list for students. Required documents are those of the university's RTP scholarship application process and its HDR admission requirements, published in the university's RTP scholarship policy.
No file size limits, accepted file types, translation rules, date-of-issue rules or signature rules are published centrally. document_format_rules is therefore deliberately empty.

What is certain from the published sources: referee reports may be required (the provider's discretion); the offer letter must state the estimated value of each type of support; if an industry internship weighting is being claimed, the written agreement between student, provider and research end-user must be in place within the published 18-month (full-time) or 36-month (part-time) window.

For international students, the Australian visa application's funding section is a separate Department of Home Affairs matter; both the Department of Home Affairs and the university's postgraduate research office may assist.

alerts.message: New base and maximum RTP stipend rates for the following year are announced (effective 1 January). The new rates apply to all RTP stipend payments made in that year, not only to new recipients.
Open the chosen university's RTP scholarship policy. The Commonwealth application, selection criteria, deadline, documents and English requirement are all in that document.
Check the offer letter lists the estimated value of each support type, and check you are not in receipt of another Commonwealth award for HDR tuition fees.
Track your period of support from the HDR commencement date. It is not reset by a transfer and cannot be extended beyond the maximum.
Include the required acknowledgement sentence and the RTP DOI 10.82133/C42F-K220, and add it to your ORCID profile if you have one.

application_readiness_checklist: Pick your provider from the Department's published list of higher education providers eligible for research block grants - an ineligible provider cannot offer an RTP scholarship.
Go to that provider, not to the Department of Education. There is no Department application route and no national deadline; applications are the provider's own.
Confirm your proposed degree is a research doctorate or research masters, not a coursework degree.
Ask the provider exactly which components it will include - fees offset, stipend, ancillary allowances - because the scheme is 'one or more of' and providers differ.
Ask for the stipend rate you would get and whether it is the base rate or the maximum rate for your award.
Check the period of support against your intended load: 3-4 years full-time for a research doctorate (6-8 part-time), up to 2 years full-time for a research masters (up to 4 part-time).

Budget for the fact that leave does not extend your funding: paid recreation leave and approved personal leave do not add to the period of support, and only approved suspension and additional approved paid parental, partner, personal, family and domestic violence leave do.
You may apply to multiple providers, but each runs its own independent selection - there is no advantage in holding offers from two providers and no national ranking.
If you already have an ORCID profile, be ready to add the RTP DOI (doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220) to it; you are not required to create one.
Plan to acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in any output from the project, using the published wording with the RTP DOI.

If you might do an industry internship, note the published eligibility: at least 3 months and 60 full-time-equivalent days, written agreement within 18 months of commencement full-time or 36 months part-time.
submission_workflow: 1. Read the RTP FAQs for students on the Department page first, especially FAQs 3, 5 and 28-30, so you are not surprised by scheme-level rules.
2. Choose an eligible provider from the Department's published list of HEPs eligible for research block grants.
3. Contact that provider's HDR or scholarships office directly about RTP scholarship applications - this is the only application route that exists.
4. Obtain that provider's application form, document list, format rules, deadline and selection criteria; none of these come from the Department.
5. Submit the application to the provider by its deadline, and repeat for any other provider you choose to approach.
6. If shortlisted, expect the provider's own assessment process and offer; check the component mix, stipend rate, student load and period of support in writing before accepting.
7. After accepting, meet the acknowledgement obligation: use the published wording with the RTP DOI in outputs, and add the DOI to your ORCID profile if you have one.

scholarships.description: The Research Training Program is Australian Government funding that flows to eligible universities as block grants, which those universities then use to offer scholarships to students doing a research doctorate or research masters. A scholarship may comprise one or more of three published components - a tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs, and allowances for the ancillary costs of a higher degree by research - and it is the university, not the Department, that decides the mix, applies, selects and sets the deadline. Stipend rates are indexed annually and published as a base and a maximum (2027: $35,550 base, $55,537 maximum), so the amount you receive depends on your provider and your stipend level rather than on a national figure. Support runs 3 to 4 years full-time for a research doctorate, or up to 2 years full-time for a research masters, and from 3 December 2025 recipients must acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution using the RTP's own DOI and add it to any ORCID profile they hold.
scholarships.duration: Research doctorate: a minimum of 3 years and up to a maximum of 4 years at the discretion of the higher education provider for a full-time student load, and a minimum of 6 years up to a maximum of 8 years for a part-time student load. Research masters: up to 2 years full-time and up to 4 years part-time. A student's period of support is not increased for periods of paid recreation leave or personal leave approved by the provider; it is increased by the length of any approved RTP suspension, or any additional approved paid personal leave, paid parental leave, paid partner leave, or paid family and domestic violence leave.

scholarships.selection_notes:
No selection criteria are published by the Department of Education. Each HEP runs its own application and selection process and publishes its own criteria; the Department page contains no ranking, weighting, pass mark or assessment panel.
The published scheme-level constraints that shape any selection are: the degree must be a research doctorate or research masters; the provider must be eligible for research block grants; the period of support must sit inside the published band for the degree and student load; and the scholarship may comprise one or more of the three published components.
Published incentive rule that affects provider behaviour: an additional weighting of 2.0 within the RTP funding allocation formula is applied to each research doctorate student reported from 2022 as completing their course having undertaken an eligible industry internship.
Published allocation rule that affects how generous a provider can be: 2026 RTP grant amounts are allocated on a formula reflecting each provider's relative performance in attracting research income and supporting students to complete HDRs.

scholarships.title: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program
scholarships.name: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program

important_advice_for_students: This is a leadership and public-service award, not an academic scholarship. The published criteria are five years of professional experience, leadership, public service and limited U.S. exposure. A strong transcript will not compensate for thin professional or civic record.
'Limited experience in the United States' is the requirement most applicants misread as a strength. Substantial prior U.S. study or work disqualifies you.

You cannot apply directly. The route is your Binational Fulbright Commission or the U.S. Embassy, which run their own country process on their own deadline. Treat the national post as your employer in this process and keep them engaged.
The transcript rule is precise: official, valid, in English, and listing courses and grades. A certificate or a transcript without grades does not comply.
The essay has a published bar rather than a scoring scale - it must thoroughly address the prompt. Thin essays are the most likely avoidable rejection at the national stage.
One of your two referees must be your current employer. Do not assume two academic referees will do.
Budget around a ten-month non-degree year with a Professional Affiliation placement, and expect to be in the United States from late August or September.

There is no published appeals route. The national selection, the U.S. review committees and the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board are sequential and final, so the only leverage you have is the quality of the national application.

referee_tracking.instructions: The published rule is that two letters of recommendation are required in English and that one must be from the applicant's current employer. This is a hard content requirement, not a suggestion. Request it with enough lead time for a referee writing in English, and give the employer a specific account of your public service and leadership, since those are the published merit signals the letter is being read against.

referee_tracking.role: Second referee - one further letter of recommendation, in English
referee_tracking.instructions: The published rule requires two letters in total, one of which must be the current employer, so the second may be academic, professional, civic or from a previous employer, provided it is in English. Choose the referee whose view of your leadership qualities and record of public service is strongest, since those are the published selection signals, and brief them on the programme's criteria.

post_award_requirements: Take up the place in the United States for the ten-month Fellowship Period, starting between August and September in the year of selection.

Participate in both published components: academic enrichment at the host university, taken without the expectation of meeting degree or diploma requirements, and the six-week Professional Affiliation placement with a host organisation.
Note that the fellowship is non-degree: no degree or diploma is conferred, so any academic credit is subject to the host's own policy and is not guaranteed by the programme.
Observe the terms of your national post's nomination, since that is the route through which the fellowship was awarded.
Participate in the programme's community components, including the Global Policy Dialogues and the annual Global Leadership Forum, which the programme publishes as key components.
Maintain eligibility conditions that the programme publishes for Fellows, and meet any conditions your national post or the Institute of International Education sets at award stage.
questions_to_ask_host: Is my country on the eligible list for this cycle, and does my Binational Fulbright Commission or Embassy have a country-specific quota?
What is the internal deadline my post has set, and is there an earlier internal shortlisting deadline before the national nomination?
Which of the four Impact Areas and which Field of Study is my post recruiting against this year?
What does my post weigh most - the essay, the professional experience and public service record, or the academic transcript?
Is there a second-round interview or assessment at national level, and who conducts it?
How many candidates does my country nominate, and how does that change if my post is selective?
What is the Professional Affiliation placement process, and can the host organisation influence the placement?
What is the fellowship's commencement and completion timetable, and how does the Professional Affiliation placement fit inside the ten months?
What does the fellowship cover exactly for my host - health insurance, travel, books, and any costs the programme does not name?
common_rejection_risks: Not a citizen of an eligible country.
No undergraduate degree.
Fewer than five years of full-time professional experience, or part-time experience only.
More than three years of prior US residence or activity without the required four years back home at professional level.
Incomplete answers to questions, or essay responses in English that do not thoroughly address the prompt.
Only one letter of recommendation, or missing the letter from the current employer, or letters not in English.
Non-official, invalid, or incomplete transcripts, or transcripts not in English, or missing diploma where the transcript does not show proof of the degree.
Missing the post's internal deadline so the post cannot nominate you before its mid-September submission to Washington.
Expecting a degree or expecting to choose the host university - the programme is explicitly non-degree with assigned placement.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All dependant costs - no additional maintenance allowance is provided for dependants.
Proof of financial support for accompanying family members.
Dependant health insurance meeting U.S. State Department requirements.
Child care for dependants.
Dependant travel to and from the U.S.

Anything you commit to at home that conflicts with a rigorous ten-month schedule with considerable time away from the host campus.
document_audit: Complete answers to every question on the post's application form.
Essay responses in English that thoroughly address each prompt.
Two letters of recommendation, both in English, one from the applicant's current employer.
Official transcripts in English, official and valid, listing courses taken and grades received.
Diploma only if the transcript does not show proof that the degree was obtained.

No file-size limit, accepted file type or upload portal rule is published by the programme; the application is the post's own system, so confirm the technical rules with the post before you assemble files.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your country first. Citizenship of an eligible country is the first published requirement, eligibility is country-by-country, and the programme publishes a country eligibility list and a 'Check Eligibility' tool. Everything else is wasted effort if you are not on that list.

Confirm the six published requirements: eligible-country citizenship, an undergraduate degree, at least five years of full-time professional experience, demonstrated leadership and a record of public service, limited experience in the United States, and demonstrated English language ability.
Count your professional experience properly - five years of full-time is the floor, and the public-service and leadership evidence is assessed alongside it.
Think carefully about your U.S. exposure. The published requirement is limited experience in the United States, and long prior U.S. study or work is a disqualifier, not a strength.

Contact your Binational Fulbright Commission or the U.S. Embassy's Public Affairs Section immediately. There is no central deadline and no direct application; the post sets the internal deadline and it varies by country.
Arrange two English letters of recommendation early, and make sure one is from your current employer. That is a published hard requirement, not a preference.
Order official English transcripts that list courses taken and grades received. If the transcript does not show the degree, you must also upload the diploma.
Write the essay in English and address the prompt thoroughly. The published requirement is that essay responses 'thoroughly address the prompt', alongside complete answers to all questions.

Check the four Impact Areas and their Fields of Study before you invest in the essay, because your national post will be assessing fit against the programme's structure: Human & Institutional Capacity; Rights & Freedoms; Sustainable Lands; Thriving Communities.
Plan for ten months, not a degree. There is no degree or diploma at the end, so if you need a credential this is the wrong programme.
Do not wait on the central programme office for news. The status is communicated to you by your Embassy or Commission after the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board approves.
submission_workflow: 1. Use the published country eligibility list and the 'Check Eligibility' tool to confirm you are a citizen of an eligible country.

2. Verify the six published eligibility requirements: undergraduate degree, at least five years of full-time professional experience, leadership and public service, limited U.S. experience, and English language ability.

3. Identify your Field of Study within one of the four Impact Areas - Human & Institutional Capacity, Rights & Freedoms, Sustainable Lands, Thriving Communities - and note the specific field, because your national post will be working to that structure.
4. Contact your Binational Fulbright Commission or the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy for the application pack and the internal deadline, which varies by country.
5. Order official English transcripts that list courses taken and grades received, and add a diploma only if the transcript does not show the degree.
6. Request two English letters of recommendation, ensuring one is from your current employer.
7. Draft the essay in English so that it thoroughly addresses the prompt, and complete every question in the application.
8. Submit to the national post by that country's deadline. There is no central deadline and no direct submission to the programme.
9. If nominated, the file goes to independent review committees in the United States, and final approval is made by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board.
10. Wait for status from your Embassy or Commission, which will inform you after the Board's approval.

Humphrey Fellowship Program is a U.S. Department of State fellowship, administered by the Institute of International Education, for mid-career professionals from eligible countries. It is a non-degree program: fellows may take academic coursework at a U.S. host university but do not earn a degree. The package covers host-university tuition and fees, a maintenance allowance with a one-time settling-in allowance, accident and sickness insurance, a book allowance, a one-time computer subsidy, international and programme-event air travel, and a professional development allowance. Applications go through each applicant's Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section, so deadlines vary by country and nominations must reach IIE by mid-September.

Indicating a financial need greater than Clark can offer. The admissions process is need-aware and the application may be denied on that basis.
Missing the CSS Profile deadline - the CSS Profile must be filed by the admissions deadline, so a late filing forfeits need-based consideration entirely.

Forgetting the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form, which all international students must complete and which only becomes available after applying.
Submitting only two years of educational data. Clark cannot review an application with only two years of credentials, and 6-3-3 systems need an extra middle school year.
Sending the Duolingo English Test score as a screenshot or scan - it must come directly from the Duolingo portal.
Non-English documents with no certified translation.
Missing an optional-looking deadline that is not optional, such as senior-year records that do not yet exist in your system.
Assuming a Presidential Scholarship means the whole cost - even that award leaves approximately USD 12,000-15,000 per year payable by the recipient.
Assuming a private scholarship will be added on top of Clark's package - it must be declared and is counted within it, and an undeclared external award can change your package.
Early Decision applicants who are admitted but then enrol elsewhere, breaching a binding agreement.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide your round first, because it is the biggest scholarship lever Clark publishes: Early Decision is binding but comes with scholarship decisions before Thanksgiving, more scholarship funding and a higher admission rate; Early Action and Regular Decision are non-binding.
Get the FAFSA done - it is on the published application checklist and it is what establishes need.

If you are an international aid applicant, complete the separate Clark University International Student Aid Application as well. This is a published, distinct requirement and it is the step international applicants most often miss.
If English is not your native language, book the official TOEFL, Duolingo or IELTS test early enough to have the report in hand - an official score report is required.

Book the interview. It is officially optional, but Clark states it is especially important for applicants who do not speak English as a native language, and it is the most credible differentiator available to you.
Line up one teacher recommendation and a counselor recommendation - both are on the published checklist.

Model the real cost, not the headline. Even the Presidential Scholarship leaves you responsible for approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year, and international students are published as typically paying around $40,000 per year after aid against roughly $85,000 total cost of attendance.
Compare the two official Clark pages that publish the average aid package before you rely on either number - they disagree, and neither states a year or population.
Be clear on what you are applying for: this is an institutional portfolio, not one scholarship, so ask which named award you would be considered for and what its individual conditions are.
If you are a transfer applicant, note the rolling windows (1 February - 1 June for fall start, 1 September - 1 November for spring start) and the roughly 4-week rolling notification.
important_advice_for_students: There is no scholarship application. Every dollar of merit aid is decided inside the admissions process, so the strength of your admission file and your round choice are the scholarship strategy.
Early Decision is the only round with a published scholarship benefit. If Clark is genuinely your first choice, the binding commitment is buying you a materially better funding position.
Do not read 'full tuition, housing and meals' as fully funded. Clark itself says the Presidential Scholarship recipient is still responsible for approximately $12,000-$15,000 a year.

International applicants: the International Student Aid Application is a separate published requirement on top of the FAFSA, and English proficiency evidence is mandatory unless English is your native language.

Sit the interview even though it is optional. Clark flags it as especially important for non-native English speakers, and Clark assesses English proficiency holistically rather than by a published minimum.

Be sceptical of single figures. Clark publishes two different average aid-package numbers on two official pages, and international cost figures that do not reconcile with the total cost of attendance. Read the Cost of Attendance page and the Office of Financial Assistance page together.
document_audit: The published application checklist is: Common Application or Coalition Application with Scoir; transcript(s); optional interview; counselor recommendation; one teacher recommendation; FAFSA application. Treat that as the minimum set.
Add the Clark University International Student Aid Application if you are an international applicant seeking aid - it is published as required, and it is not on the general checklist.

Add an official TOEFL, Duolingo or IELTS score report if English is not your native language. 'Official' is the only format word Clark publishes for it, so use an official report rather than a home-printed score sheet.

Transfer applicants must use the Transfer Common App or the Clark Transfer App, not the first-year application, and Clark flags additional transfer requirements on a separate page - get those from the transfer applicant guidance rather than assuming they mirror the first-year list.

No file size, file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published. Format rules come from the Common Application, Coalition Application, Scoir, Transfer Common App and Clark Transfer App platforms, and from Clark's own admissions and financial-aid systems. Ask Financial Aid for the current rules rather than assuming.

submission_workflow: 1. Choose your round and note its deadline: 1 November for Early Decision I and Early Action, 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision, or the rolling transfer window for your intended semester.
2. File the FAFSA, and add the Clark University International Student Aid Application if you are an international aid applicant.
3. Request an official TOEFL, Duolingo or IELTS score report if English is not your native language.
4. Ask your counselor for a recommendation and one teacher for a recommendation, and agree dates with both.
5. Submit the Common Application, or the Coalition Application with Scoir. Transfer applicants use the Transfer Common App or the Clark Transfer App.
6. Upload transcript(s) and complete the essay and activities sections.
7. Sit the interview - optional, but strongly encouraged and specifically flagged as important for non-native English speakers.
8. Submit before your round deadline. There is no separate scholarship submission at any point.
9. Review the award letter against the published Cost of Attendance, Merit-Based Aid and Need-Based Aid pages before accepting, and confirm in writing any condition not stated on the pages.
post_award_requirements: Confirm in writing the academic standing required to keep the award. Clark publishes no threshold, so this must come from Financial Aid in writing at award stage.

Confirm the renewal or continuation position. Only the Presidential Scholarship has a published term - four years of undergraduate study - and no renewal or extension condition is published for any award.

Confirm the year-by-year amounts, because the published average aid-package figures differ between two official Clark pages and the top award still leaves roughly $12,000-$15,000 a year to the recipient.
If you received Early Decision, note that you are bound to enrol at Clark and had to withdraw your other applications.

If you are an international student, maintain the immigration status required for your programme and meet any separate terms of the Clark University International Student Aid Application - neither is published on the pages read.
Re-check the total cost of attendance at each renewal point: Clark publishes no tuition-increase protection, so treat the four-year published figures as current-year figures, not guarantees.
questions_to_ask_host: Which named scholarship would I be considered for, and what are that award's individual conditions, amount and renewal terms?
Is the award I am being offered a gift or a loan, and does it have an academic threshold, a conduct condition, or a repayment trigger?
For the Presidential Scholarship, how is the approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year of remaining cost calculated, and what does it cover?
How do Clark's named scholarships stack with need-based aid, and can a merit award be reduced if my need changes in a later year?
What is the current academic standing required to retain my award, and what happens if I fall below it for one semester?
For international students, does the Clark University International Student Aid Application cover the full four years, and what happens to my award if my family's financial situation changes?
Is there any award for international students comparable to the Davis United World College Scholars Program, and what is its cap?
If I am offered Early Decision funding, does the binding commitment change if my aid package changes before enrolment?

scholarships.description: This record covers Clark University's institutional undergraduate scholarship portfolio rather than a single named award. The headline award is the Presidential Scholarship, which covers the full cost of tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for the four years of undergraduate study, with recipients still responsible for additional costs of roughly $12,000 to $15,000 per year; a second named award, the Davis United World College Scholars Program, is a need-based grant of up to $15,000 per year. There is no separate scholarship application: scholarships are decided inside the admissions process, bundled with the admission decision and made more generous in the binding Early Decision rounds, which publish decisions before Thanksgiving alongside more scholarship funding and a higher admission rate. Underneath the named awards sit institutional need-based aid that Clark reports as reaching 99% of first-year students with 98% of aid in the form of non-repayable grants, while international students are reported as typically paying around $40,000 per year after aid against a total cost of attendance of approximately $85,000.

scholarships.description: The Clarendon Fund offers over 200 new fully-funded scholarships each year to outstanding graduate scholars at the University of Oxford, covering course fees in full and paying a grant for living expenses. There is no separate scholarship application: candidates are considered automatically if they apply for a new full-time or part-time Master's or DPhil by the December or January admissions deadline for their course, and departments nominate to their division for divisional ranking. Selection criteria are academic record, future potential and aptitude, and student motivation, and successful candidates are usually notified by the end of April.
scholarships.duration: Normally the scholar's period of fee liability; at the discretion of the academic divisions some awards extend beyond it with only the living grant paid in the extra period

applicant_utility.summary: Reach Oxford covers course fees, a living-costs grant and one return air fare per year for three or four years, but only around two to three awards exist annually, so treat it as a small lottery layered on top of a successful UCAS application. Oxford cannot consider you without an offer, so admissions come first and the scholarship step follows in January. selection weighs highest academic ability together with financial need, social commitment and demonstrable inability to study a degree at home, so every criterion needs documentary evidence rather than assertion.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Highest-ability students from DAC-listed low-income countries who hold or expect an Oxford offer outside medicine and genuinely cannot complete a degree at home.

applicant_utility.summary: This studentship pays full PhD fees plus a GBP 23,805 annual stipend for four years, but you never apply for it directly - your department nominates you from your PhD admission application, so the admissions file is the scholarship application. The decisive date is your department's first funding deadline for 2027/28 entry: complete applications with both references in by 3 December 2026 or 13 January 2027 are guaranteed consideration, while later candidates only compete for unawarded funds at the 27 May 2027 round. Apply as soon as the cycle opens in October 2026, because competition is intense and a late file can lose funding consideration entirely.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving graduates with a sharp research proposal that matches an LSE department's expertise, including international applicants who need full fees and living support.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your department's exact funding deadline on its programme page (some set 3 December 2026, others use 13 January 2027)

Nominate two referees early and chase them; the application is not considered until both references arrive
Book IELTS Academic or TOEFL early - Research-level scores for most MPhil/PhD programmes, higher in some departments, and tests must be under two years old at 1 October 2027
Submit as early in the cycle as possible once applications open in October 2026
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete application at the departmental funding deadline - usually a missing reference or transcript - which kills funding eligibility even if the academic place survives
A research topic with no matching supervisor or research group in the department
Missing the first funding panel and expecting an initial LSE PhD Studentship from the second round
Because there is no separate application, a thin admissions file leaves nothing else to rescue the funding case
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The studentship publishes full fees plus the GBP 23,805 stipend only; visa fees, the immigration health surcharge, flights to London, and any living or accommodation costs above the stipend remain self-funded.

Add GRE/GMAT only where the programme requires it - LSE warns selectors will not read extra documents
Some departments set their own proposal format or word count, so check the departmental guidance before finalising

ESRC DTP consideration requires applying by your department's first funding panel deadline (3 December or 13 January 2027)

scholarships.title: LSE Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.name: LSE Excellence Scholarship

common_rejection_risks: Applying to a PGT programme at a department that is not on the published list of twelve. This is the most common hard fail and it is structural: the list names exactly Accounting, Anthropology, Gender Studies, Geography and Environment, Health Policy, International Development, International History, LSE Law School, Mathematics, Media and Communications, School of Public Policy, Sociology and Statistics.
Applying to an executive education programme - explicitly not eligible.
Applying to a double degree where the first year of study is at another institution - explicitly not eligible.

Missing the admission cycle rather than the scholarship deadline. Because there is no scholarship deadline, students often apply to the scholarship too late in the cycle. The award runs out: awards are made 'until all awards are allocated'.
Assuming a financial support application is needed and delaying to meet the (irrelevant) Graduate Financial Support Application deadline.
Assuming need is considered. This is a merit award identified from the admission application, and LSE states financial information is not considered as part of the admission application.
Applying for the 2026 entry cycle when the published page is for students joining LSE in 2026 and LSE states applications have closed for 2026 entry.
Assuming Â£20,000 covers fees or living costs in full - it is a fixed total value and LSE does not publish it as a full-fee waiver.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything above the Â£20,000 total value (Â£10,000 per year on two-year programmes).
Living costs beyond whatever portion of the award is applied to them - LSE does not publish the split between fees and living costs.
Travel to and from London, and any airfare, visa or settlement costs - no travel component is published.
Books, equipment and other study costs.
Costs of any preceding or subsequent study elsewhere.

alerts.message: Check your target programme is offered by one of the twelve eligible LSE departments. The scholarship cannot be considered outside that list.
Apply for admission early in the cycle. Awards are made on a rolling basis until the pool is exhausted, so a strong application submitted late can lose to a strong application submitted early.
Do not invest in a financial support application for this scholarship - none is required, and financial information plays no part in the admission decision.

alerts.trigger: If you are on a double degree
alerts.message: Only eligible if your first year of study is at LSE.

For LSE's separate graduate scholarships only successful applicants are contacted, and no response by the end of July means the application was unsuccessful. No individual feedback is provided on any application.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your target programme's department against the published list of thirteen. If it is not on that list - for example if you are considering the European Institute, Geography's other programmes, or anything outside the named departments - this scholarship is not available to you.
Check the programme type. Executive education programmes are expressly excluded, and a double degree programme only qualifies if your first year of study is at LSE.
Do not look for a scholarship application. There is none. Your LSE postgraduate admission application is the entire submission, and LSE publishes that no financial support application is required.

Apply early within the cycle. Awards are made on a rolling basis until all awards are allocated, so the pool of competing applicants grows as the cycle proceeds and the same academic file carries a weaker position at the end.
Target entry in the 2026 cohort if you are following this record; LSE publishes the award for 2026 joiners only and does not state that it will repeat.

Strengthen the two things actually judged: outstanding academic ability and strong potential to thrive in the chosen programme. Both are read off the admission application, so your academic record, references and statements carry the scholarship weight.
Budget realistically. £20,000 total is not a full-fee award, LSE publishes no breakdown of what it pays for, and no travel, visa or arrival funding is published.
Ask LSE for the academic progress condition in writing before you accept. None is published, and it governs whether you keep the second £10,000 on a two-year programme.
If you also want LSE's other scholarships, use the separate published 'How to apply for a scholarship' route - it does not apply to this award, and mixing the two up will cost you time.
important_advice_for_students: This is an admissions award, not a funding application. Everything you do to be admitted is what wins it, and there is no scholarship essay to write.
Timing is a real advantage. Because awards are allocated on a rolling basis until the pool runs out, applying early is worth more than an identical file applying late.
Check the department list first. It is the cheapest way to find out whether you are eligible at all, and it is easy to assume any LSE master's qualifies.
Do not model this as a fee waiver. LSE publishes a total value with no breakdown, and £20,000 does not cover LSE fees plus London living costs.
A double degree only counts if year one is at LSE. If year one is at the partner institution, you are not eligible for the award even though you are on a double degree.
Executive education is excluded outright - if you are considering an LSE executive programme, this scholarship is irrelevant to you.

Do not prepare documents for LSE's general scholarship process. The published 'How to apply for a scholarship' page applies to LSE's other scholarships, and by LSE's own wording here it is not the route for this award.

No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published for the scholarship. Anything you encounter is an admission-document rule, so get the current admission document rules from the programme page rather than from funding pages.
One thing to confirm in writing: whether any academic progress or attendance condition attaches to the award, and how the second £10,000 is released on a two-year programme. LSE publishes neither.

3. Submit the standard LSE postgraduate admission materials for the programme. No financial support application is required or accepted for this scholarship.
4. Do not submit anything to LSE's general scholarship process - it does not apply to this award.
5. Be aware that awards are made on a rolling basis during the application cycle until all awards are allocated, so there is no single results date for the scholarship.
6. If selected, accept the place and then confirm in writing the academic progress condition, the payment schedule, and how the second £10,000 is released on a two-year programme.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are in the first or second year of your PhD at the time of application - third year and later is ineligible

Confirm your eligibility category: Canadian student at a Canadian university, Canadian student at a university outside Canada, or international student at a Canadian university. International students outside Canada or at non-Canadian universities are ineligible

Check that your field is broadly humanities or social sciences and that your research maps to at least one of the four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment
Submit the eligibility verification form by 2 October 2026 - you cannot access the full application until the Foundation confirms you
Secure exactly three referees: your PhD supervisor, another academic referee, and one outside academia. No family members, and no more or fewer than three
Choose a supervisor or former supervisor if your thesis supervisor has not been chosen or does not know you well, and explain it in the 'Special Circumstances' section
Brief your referees early: they must complete their reference material inside the application file by 30 October 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET, and letters cannot be sent to the Foundation directly
Verify before you submit that the reference letters are attached to your file - the Foundation will not accept an application without them
Submit the complete application by 6 November 2026 at 5 p.m. ET and keep the confirmation e-mail
Prepare to be interviewed in French or English, in person in Montreal, with travel costs covered
important_advice_for_students: Do this in order: the eligibility form comes first and the full application is only unlocked after the Foundation confirms you, so missing 2 October closes the door for the whole cycle
Do not plan on tuition being covered - the published benefits are a stipend of up to $50,000 per year and a research and travel allowance of up to $20,000 per year, and nothing else

Do not worry about the amount if you plan to study abroad: the Foundation states the amount is the same wherever you study, though it does convert foreign external funding into Canadian dollars when assessing value
Do use the fourth language rule: you need effective communication in French or English, not both
Keep letters to three to four pages - there is no word limit but the Foundation's own guidance is that a letter should not exceed that, and quality trumps quantity
If you are writing in French, you get 20% more room on any page limit
Part-time work up to 20 hours per week is explicitly allowed and does not reduce the award, including RA, TA and lecturer roles

If you need a parental, medical, personal or professional leave, you can suspend the Scholarship for up to one year, but know that payments pause until you re-enrol full-time and that there is no paid parental leave
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 2 October eligibility verification deadline, which makes the whole application impossible
Being in the third or later year of the PhD at the time of application
Being an international student who resides outside Canada or is enrolled at a non-Canadian university
A field outside the broad humanities and social sciences, or research not aligned with any of the four themes

Using more or fewer than exactly three referees, or a family member as a referee
Submitting reference letters directly to the Foundation instead of through the application file
A proposal that is strong academically but not clearly linked to a Foundation theme, since theme alignment is an explicit assessment criterion
A letter from a referee chosen mainly for convenience rather than one who can speak to academic leadership and community contribution

Living costs above the up-to-$50,000 annual stipend; no living-cost breakdown is published
Health insurance and mandatory student fees

referee_tracking.instructions: One letter from your PhD supervisor. If your supervisor has not yet been chosen or does not know you well, you may ask a former supervisor or another professor, and the Foundation strongly recommends explaining this in the 'Special Circumstances' section of your application.

One letter from another academic referee. The Foundation defines this as "anyone who can vouch for your academic progress... someone who knows you as a student, academic, or researcher." Choose someone who can demonstrate your academic leadership in your research area and your contribution to graduate students and the community.

One letter from outside academia: "someone who knows you outside of academia and can speak to your character, commitment or commitment and engagement in non-academic settings." Family members cannot act as referees. Referees may live outside Canada.

Exactly three referees, no more and no less. Reference letters cannot be sent directly to the Foundation; they must be completed through the specific mechanism provided inside the application file. Deadline for references to be received: 30 October 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET. The application cannot be submitted if the reference letters are not attached to the file. Referees may respond in either French or English.

scholarships.selection_notes: UBC states there are no exceptions to the eligibility criteria. Applicants are assessed on demonstrated leadership qualities, exceptional contributions to their communities, and outstanding academic performance (all As or equivalent standard). Applicants may be invited to a video interview to share more about themselves and reflect on past educational and leadership experiences beyond the written application. You do not select which award you wish to receive; the team automatically considers you for the awards you are eligible for. applicant_utility.summary: Worth CAD $45,000 per year ($180,000 over four years), this is York's flagship entrance award for international high school students entering Fall 2027. You cannot apply directly: you must first apply to York admissions, then use your York reference number in the scholarship portal by January 27, 2027, and your school must nominate you by February 4, 2027. Plan backwards from those dates, because only two students per school can be nominated each year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-tier international high school students with roughly 80%+ average who can document sustained volunteering and extracurricular leadership and who can persuade their school to use one of its two nomination slots on them
application_readiness_checklist: Submit your York undergraduate application as early as possible; the scholarship portal needs the York reference number it generates, and late admission applications compress the whole timeline
Secure your school's nomination before January: only two students per school per year are accepted, so confirm early in the fall with your guidance counsellor
Draft the 500-word personal statement around concrete professional goals, leadership evidence and community impact, not generic ambition
Assemble a tight record of volunteer work and extracurriculars (max 3) and awards (max 3), with dates and roles
Prepare the financial profile: an honest estimate of total funding available for your 3-4 years, since York uses need context alongside merit
Brief your nominator in writing on the February 4, 2027 deadline and the letter requirements (signed, on school letterhead)
common_rejection_risks: Losing the school nomination race: two slots per school per year often go to the highest-profile students, so asking in April or later can mean you never get one
Nominator misses the February 4, 2027 deadline; York only emails the nomination link after you submit your own application, so any delay on your side cascades
Final admission average below the 80% minimum, including translation/conversion surprises for non-Ontario curricula
A personal statement that lists achievements without evidence of leadership and community commitment, which is what the selection criteria actually reward
Applying to York admission too late in the cycle, leaving no time to complete the scholarship portal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The official terms publish only the $45,000/year value and do not itemize covered expenses, so budget separately for residence and meal plans, University Health Insurance Plan, flights, visa costs and personal spending; the 4-year housing guarantee from York does not remove those housing bills
document_audit: The reference letter must be signed and printed on the school's official letterhead; a generic counsellor email is not the same document
Only 3 extracurriculars and 3 awards can be listed, so choose those with verifiable impact rather than padding the total
The financial profile asks for estimated total funding for the full degree, not family income documents, so prepare the figures in advance
alerts: PISE cannot be combined with York's automatic entrance scholarships: if you win PISE you receive the higher-value award instead, so do not count on stacking $37,500 of entrance scholarships on top
The portal opens November 1, 2026 and closes January 27, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST; the separate February 4 deadline covers only the nominator's submission
Students admitted to Computer Science, Cybersecurity or Engineering face extra restrictions on the automatic entrance scholarship, which makes PISE the more relevant award in those programs
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application first, scholarship portal second, nominator third: York releases the nomination link to your school official only after your own application is in, so your submission date gates everyone else's

applicant_utility.summary: The Emile Boutmy scholarship is Sciences Po's flagship tuition-fee award for non-EU students: EUR 9,500 a year at Bachelor's level (or a full fee exemption) and EUR 18,500 a year for each of the two Master's years. There is no separate form - you declare it in the 'Financial information' section of your Sciences Po application, so the scholarship decision comes only after an admission decision. Treat it as a fee discount to stack with external funding such as Eiffel or French government scholarships, not as a full ride, because living costs are not covered.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU nationals with strong secondary or undergraduate records, no EU household tax residence, applying to the Undergraduate College or a two-year Master's who can fund Paris living costs themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your parents' tax residence sits outside the EU before relying on eligibility - Sciences Po looks at the parents' tax residence, not yours
Tick the Emile Boutmy box in the 'Financial information' section before submitting; it cannot be added after admission or during your studies
Book any required language test early (results can take up to three months) so scores are attached by the deadline; for the 2027 intake the test must be dated on or after 1 January 2025
Check your programme is eligible - journalism programmes, one-year Master's, the PhD, most dual degrees and exchange routes are excluded
Budget the EUR 150 graduate application fee, which is non-refundable even for an incomplete or unsuccessful application
common_rejection_risks: Declaring the scholarship after submitting the application or after being admitted - neither is possible
A missing language test by the deadline: the file is not complete and is not reviewed
Assuming your own EU residence counts - a parent taxed inside the EU disqualifies the application
Swiss, Norwegian, Quebec Master's or dual-EU-citizenship candidates applying despite the exclusion
Enrolling in a dual degree directly in the third year, which cancels a Bachelor's award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Paris or on the regional campuses, flights, health cover and the EUR 150 graduate application fee (waivers only for CROUS holders, applicants with disabilities, Mastercard Foundation-eligible candidates and refugees) are not funded by this scholarship.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply in the first round and get a complete file in before 15 January if you want to be considered for all funding
Register in the BSE application system early, since you need the account to start
Prepare a mathematics-heavy statement of purpose that explains your recent mathematical background through courses, research or practical applications
Brief your two referees in advance - letters from professors are strongly preferred, and BSE contacts referees by email after you submit
Arrange the EUR 100 application fee (credit card or Flywire) as part of your submission
Have your language score ready (TOEFL 90, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 120 or Cambridge 180), or wait until you can provide it
Add a GRE score if you are applying to the PhD Economics Track
common_rejection_risks: Missing 15 January, which limits you to whatever funding is left
An incomplete application because one or both reference letters were never uploaded - the application is not considered complete until both arrive
A weak quantitative background, which BSE calls a key admission criterion alongside academic record and reference letter
Missing the mathematics explanation in the statement of purpose, which BSE calls essential
Applying without a language certificate
Assuming admission guarantees funding - fulfilment of application requirements does not guarantee admission, and aid is merit-based
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Barcelona, which no published award states it covers
Travel and health insurance
Any portion of tuition not covered by a named scholarship or waiver
document_audit: Undergraduate diploma or degree-completion certification, or the signed declaration plus provisional transcript
Official final undergraduate transcript
Sworn translation if not in English, Spanish, Catalan, French, Italian or Portuguese
CV of no more than 2 pages
Statement of purpose
English language certificate at the published level
Passport copy
Both signed reference letters uploaded by the referees themselves

scholarships.name: IE University Master's Awards and Scholarships

application_readiness_checklist: Submit the IE University admission application for your master's programme first â€” the financial aid application cannot be submitted before it and is not evaluated until you are admitted.
Log in to my.ie.edu/applymasfaid with the same email and password as your admission application.
Choose up to three awards or scholarships, but expect to be offered only the single highest-value one.
Write the short essay: your financial situation, how you plan to cover all costs of the programme, and why you are a standout candidate for the specific award you are applying to.
Gather financial documentation: last three pay slips and your most recent income tax declaration, in English or Spanish.
If you are not working, have your parents or tutors submit their own financial documentation; your file is not reviewed until it arrives.
If you marked yourself financially dependent, chase your tutor(s) â€” their accreditation must be received before review.
Press SUBMIT and keep the platform confirmation.
Finish your programme enrolment process once you receive an offer.
important_advice_for_students: Apply early. Funds are allocated on a rolling basis, so there is no benefit to waiting until the programme start date, which is the published deadline.

Do not budget for the place reservation fee being covered by aid â€” IE University states the award is applied to outstanding tuition fees and cannot pay the reservation fee. The 150â‚¬ application fee is also not waivable.

Do not assume the award covers your living costs. Most of these awards are partial tuition coverage; only a limited set of IE Foundation, partner and donor full awards reach 100% of tuition and living costs.
The award is not portable: if you change programme or intake you must submit a whole new financial aid application.
The IE Financial Aid Committee will not reconsider a disappointing outcome unless you can show significant and unexpected changes in your financial situation, and only by the programme start date.
If you also hold a Direct Award, you may still apply for additional financial aid.

Have a backup plan: IE University points you to interest-free tuition payment plans, employer funding and private loans, and notes loan eligibility can depend on your country of citizenship or residence.
common_rejection_risks: Applying for financial aid before submitting the admission application.
Applying before being admitted â€” the application is not evaluated until admission is granted.
Incomplete file: missing pay slips, missing tax declaration, or documentation not in English or Spanish.
Financially dependent candidates whose parent or tutor never completes their accreditation, so the file is never reviewed.
Forgetting to press SUBMIT after uploading documents.
Missing the programme start date deadline; all applications must be submitted prior to the start of the program.
Essay that does not address your financial situation, how you will cover programme costs, and why you fit the specific award.
Expecting two awards when you applied for three â€” only the highest-value offer is made.
Forgetting an award-specific essay required by a partner scholarship in the 'Additional Documentation' section.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The place reservation fee â€” explicitly not payable from financial aid.
The 150â‚¬ application fee â€” IE University does not waive it.
Living costs in Madrid or Segovia for the majority of awards (only certain IE Foundation, partner and donor full awards reach 100% of tuition and living costs).
Travel costs, visa, and any expenses beyond outstanding tuition fees.
The balance of tuition fees for any award that covers 10% to 40%.
A one-time non-refundable 400â‚¬ administrative fee if tuition payments are spread over more than three consecutive months via a payment plan.
document_audit: Short essay â€” mandatory for every financial aid application.
Last three pay slips â€” attach to the application.
Most recent income tax declaration â€” must be in English or Spanish.
Parents' or tutors' financial documentation â€” required if you are not working; their information must arrive before your file is reviewed.
Tutor accreditation of economic situation â€” required if you marked yourself financially-dependent.
Scholarship-specific essay â€” place in the 'Additional Documentation' section of the IE Financial Aid Application if the individual award description requires it.
Language check: pay slips and tax declaration must be in English or Spanish, not any other language.
Completeness check: IE verifies the application is complete after submission and may request further information or documentation, so confirm every upload is registered on the platform.

submission_workflow: Apply for admission to the master's programme.
