Select up to three awards or scholarships.
Write and upload the essay and all financial documentation.
Add any award-specific essay in the 'Additional Documentation' section.
Press SUBMIT and save the platform confirmation.
Ensure parents/tutors complete their accreditation if applicable.
Monitor the platform for status and requests for further information.
On decision, read the terms and conditions in the email and complete enrolment.
post_award_requirements: Formally finish the enrolment process in the programme to secure the award.
Read and comply with the terms and conditions included in the decision email.
Note that awards are not transferable between programs and intakes, so any programme change forfeits the award.

application_readiness_checklist: Pick your route before you start: a Talent/Need-based Scholarship (talent + financial need, 50-85% of tuition) OR one Excellence Award (talent only, 10-50% of MSc tuition). You cannot hold both, and Esade states each is incompatible with other Esade prizes and awards.
Apply for admission to the Esade MSc or MBA, and submit the financial aid application at the same time â€” funds are limited and Esade urges early application.
Get an above-average Admissions Test score. Esade states this is expected for need-based scholarships.
Collect supporting economic documents for your family household's financial circumstances â€” this is the core evidence for a need-based award.
For a Geographical Area Excellence Award, prepare a maximum of two documents evidencing academic prizes, awards or recognition â€” and no more.
For a programme-specific award, write the required essay (marketing goals, entrepreneurial experience, or leadership views).
For a Full Time MBA Excellence Award, log into the Esade Admissions Portal and open the Award Information section to start the award application.
Diary the deadlines: Excellence Award applications close July 15, 2026 for the 2026 intake; the FundaciÃ³ Princesa de Girona Scholarship closes June 15.
Budget separately: the â‚¬150 application fee, the â‚¬100 MBA Student Association Fee, and for the MBA the â‚¬8,000 Reservation and â‚¬8,000 Commitment Fees are not covered.
Line up housing and living-cost cover separately â€” Lodging Grants are only for students living outside Barcelona province, and Living Grants are a different instrument.
important_advice_for_students: Do not assume this is a full scholarship. The published figures are 50% to 85% of tuition for need-based awards and 10% to 50% for Excellence Awards, and the Scholarship Program's own statistic is that 84% of recipients' tuition fees are covered.
Room and board is not part of these tuition scholarships. Apply separately for Esade Lodging Grants (only if you live outside Barcelona province) and Esade Living Grants.

The most common disqualifier is stacking: a need-based scholarship cannot be combined with other Esade prizes or awards, and the same applies to Excellence Awards. Also, you may apply for only one Excellence Award.
Apply with your programme application, not afterwards. Esade states the number of scholarships is limited and urges applicants to apply when they first apply for a place.
Your admissions test score is doing real work. Esade expects an above-average Admissions Test score, and the Geographical Area awards give special consideration to above-average GMAT/GRE scores.
Watch the year labels. The fee tables are for 2027-2028 while the Excellence Award deadline is stated for the 2026 intake â€” confirm which intake a deadline refers to before you rely on it.

For the Full Time MBA, the money moves fast: pay the non-refundable â‚¬8,000 Reservation Fee within 2 to 4 weeks of admission, and the â‚¬8,000 Commitment Fee by June 15, 2026, or you lose the place regardless of any award.

Check award-specific conditions. Dedicated Talent Scholarships can be restricted by the partner company to a particular programme or student profile, and FundaciÃ³ Princesa de Girona Scholarships are only for Spanish citizens or residents.
Esade's Income Share Agreement can be combined with scholarships or awards if you still need to cover the remaining tuition.
common_rejection_risks: Applying for financial aid after admission rather than with the initial programme application, when places are already allocated.
A below-average Admissions Test score.
Missing or incomplete supporting economic documentation for the family household's circumstances.
Applying for more than one Excellence Award â€” each candidate can apply for one award.
Stacking a need-based scholarship or Excellence Award with another Esade prize or award, which Esade states is not permitted.
Missing the July 15, 2026 Excellence Award deadline for the 2026 intake, or the June 15 FundaciÃ³ Princesa de Girona deadline.
Applying for a Geographical Area award with more than two supporting documents.
Applying for a FundaciÃ³ Princesa de Girona Scholarship without Spanish citizenship or residence.
Applying to an award tied to a different programme (for example the Global Marketing Award without applying to the MSc in Marketing Management).
Failing to pay the Full Time MBA Reservation Fee in the 2 to 4 week window, or the Commitment Fee by June 15, 2026.
Not completing enrolment after receiving the award, which is required to secure it.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Room and board â€” not covered by the tuition scholarships; requires a separate Lodging or Living Grant, and Lodging Grants are limited to students living outside Barcelona province.
Transportation and general living expenses â€” requires a separate Esade Living Grant.
The â‚¬150 application fee.
The â‚¬100 MBA Student Association Fee (Full Time MBA).
The non-refundable â‚¬8,000 Reservation Fee and â‚¬8,000 Commitment Fee for the Full Time MBA.

Programme application documents â€” for the Full Time MBA, Excellence Award evaluation is based on the documents supplied for admission, so your admission file is your award file.

Award-specific essay â€” Global Marketing Award (short- and long-term marketing goals), MSc for Entrepreneurs Award (previous entrepreneurial experience), MSc for Global Leaders Award (views on effective leadership and how the programme supports career development).

Publication check: Esade publishes no file type, size limit, signature, date or translation rules for these documents on the pages read. Confirm the accepted formats inside the Admissions Portal Award Information section before uploading.

scholarships.description: Esade's Scholarship Program funds academically excellent students with limited financial resources. MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships (published as Esade Need-based Scholarships) cover 50% to 85% of the programme tuition fee and are assessed on talent and financial need. Esade also runs Excellence Awards, which are talent-only, range from 10% to 50% of MSc tuition, and are limited to one award per candidate. scholarships.description: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore, jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member, with research conducted at an A*STAR Research Institute. Support published for up to 4 years comprises full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment. Monthly allowance is a published matrix by track and residency status: AGS (STEM) $4,500 for Singapore Citizens, $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents and $3,600 for International Students; AGS (Specialised Tracks: Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) $6,200, $5,600 and $5,000 respectively.

scholarships.selection_notes: Referees can be academic referees from universities or supervisors/PIs whom you have worked with. There will be at least 2 rounds of interviews involving the senior management of the Biomedical Research Council or Science & Engineering Research Council, and researchers from A*STAR's Research Entities. The nomination of supervisor(s) has to be approved by A*STAR; in most cases the main and co-supervisors should hold at least the designation of Principal Investigator or Principal Scientist at an A*STAR RI. Final approval of the PhD supervisor(s), research project and university for successful applicants is subject to A*STAR's approval. A*STAR makes a holistic assessment of each application and takes into consideration factors such as achievements in science/maths related competitions and CCAs; prior research experience helps but is not mandatory. The application process typically takes about 5 months from submission of a complete application to notification of results.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Final-semester undergraduates and Master's students at, or on track to graduate from, a Singapore autonomous university, and mid-PhD students already enrolled in a Singapore autonomous university, who want to do a research-intensive PhD at an A*STAR Research Institute. International students without Singapore Permanent Residence should be comfortable with a 3-year service commitment in a Singapore-based company.
scholarships.notes: Bond-free for Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents. Foreigners who are non-SPRs must serve a 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies, without commitment to any specific organisation; Singapore-based companies refer to local companies and international companies that have a base in Singapore and which is registered with the Accounting & Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA). The area of work should preferably be in Biomedical Sciences, Physical Sciences, Engineering or Computing and Information Sciences. Not deferrable within the 4-year funding period without approval: if you need more time to complete your PhD you will have to seek approval from A*STAR's management for your PhD extension. A*STAR does not pay for consumables or research fees; fees involved in the lab should be borne by the university. All scholars need to seek A*STAR's written permission before changing your course of study/research project. Mid-term applicants receive the same terms of support as full-term AGS awardees from the point of the award, with retrospective payment for all tuition fees and/or any compulsory fees from Year 1 of study onward. All rates/allowances are subject to adjustments by A*STAR from time to time. A pre-application Master's degree is not required.

scholarships.description: The President's Graduate Fellowship is awarded by the NUS Graduate School to PhD candidates who show exceptional promise or accomplishment in research, and a number of PhD research students are selected each semester by the University. It is open to Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents and all international students, covers a full waiver of tuition fees at the University and pays a monthly stipend of SGD 3,900 for international students, SGD 4,400 for Permanent Residents and SGD 4,800 for Singapore Citizens, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens. International students additionally receive a one-off settling allowance of S$1,000 and a one-off air travel allowance of up to S$750, and from the AY2023/24 intake recipients are eligible for the NUSGS Research Incentive Award. The Fellowship is tenable for one year in the first instance, renewable each semester, with a maximum period of four years, and is awarded by faculty/department nomination only.

scholarships.description: The NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship is a University-level scholarship offered by the National University of Singapore to support exceptional students from all countries except Singapore who apply as freshmen to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS. Candidates are considered and shortlisted through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS, and selection interviews are held from January to July with outcomes notified by mid-July. Benefits comprise 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, an S$5,800 annual living allowance, an S$5,000 annual accommodation allowance and a S$1,750 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment. The award is renewed each semester provided the holder maintains a GPA of at least 3.5 (or top 80% of cohort for Dentistry, Law and Medicine) and good conduct.
scholarships.duration: The scholarship is tenable for the normal candidature period and can be transferred across programmes; renewed every semester provided the GPA and conduct conditions are met.

scholarships.description: The Nanyang Global Scholarship is awarded by Nanyang Technological University to outstanding freshmen pursuing undergraduate programmes, recognising students with outstanding academic results, strong leadership abilities and very good co-curricular records. It is open to all nationalities and covers the years of study at NTU for successful awardees reading a full-time undergraduate degree programme. Benefits include full coverage of subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant, a living allowance of S$6,500 per academic year, an accommodation allowance of up to S$2,000 per academic year for NTU hostel residents, a travel grant of up to S$8,000 for an overseas programme for new cohorts from AY2025, a one-off computer allowance of S$2,000, and enrolment into NTU Honours College. application_readiness_checklist: Be on a full-time PhD at NTU. NPGS is not available for Master's programmes.
Have, or be on track for, an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent â€” if your degree is unfinished, get written confirmation from your university now, because this is a hard gate.
Line up a supervisor before you submit. It is highly recommended; if you cannot, NTU will appoint one based on your research interests, but you lose control of that match.
Assemble resume, educational certificates and transcripts, test scores and recommendation letters per the Research Programmes Admission Guide 'How to Apply â€“ Supporting Documents' list.
Check every test score's date: scores must be within 5 years or less from the date of your application.
If your prior study was in English and you want a test waiver, request a medium-of-instruction letter from your home university.
Apply in the October/November to December window and tick interest in the 'NTU Scholarship' in the application â€” there is no separate scholarship form.
Plan for the final interview at university level; outcomes land roughly 3 to 6 weeks after it.
Have a Singapore bank account ready and update your details in GSLink by the 15th of the semester commencement month.
important_advice_for_students: There is no bond. NTU states plainly that there is no bond attached to the scholarship, so you are not locked into returning to your home country.
Do not read 'priority will be given for campus accommodation' as free housing. It is a queue preference; you still need to budget for rent, and priority does not guarantee a place.
Budget in Singapore dollars and by citizenship tier. Your stipend is S$5,300 (Citizen), S$4,800 (PR) or S$4,300 (International), and only Citizens get the CPF contribution on top.
Renewal is not automatic in name: it is renewable 'subject to good progress', up to 4 years, and the school also weighs availability of research funding. Keep your progress reports clean.
As an International Student you will be required to do teaching or laboratory supervision under the Graduate Assistantship Programme. Factor that workload into your research time.
NTU reserves the right to vary the stipend at any time and states that coverage and award terms are subject to change â€” do not build a fixed budget on today's figure.
If you are an existing student on a higher stipend rate, NTU says your stipend remains the same; the revised rates apply from January 2026.
The conference allowance is capped and runs on a financial-year basis (April to March), so plan conference travel against the S$5,000 cap and the April-to-March window.
You do not need a separate scholarship application. The single most common administrative mistake is simply forgetting to indicate the 'NTU Scholarship' in the programme application.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a Master's programme â€” NPGS is only for PhD.
Not holding, and not being able to evidence being on track for, an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent.
Failing to supply the official university documentation confirming on-track status when the undergraduate degree is incomplete.
Missing the October/November to December application window, or submitting before the period for the academic year is announced.
Submitting an incomplete application â€” consideration happens on submission of a complete application within the period.
Forgetting to indicate interest in the 'NTU Scholarship' in the programme application.
Submitting GRE/GMAT scores older than 5 years from the application date.
Requesting a test waiver without the home university medium-of-instruction letter.
Not attending or not preparing for the final interview at university level.
Failing to update GSLink bank details by the 15th of the semester commencement month, which delays stipend payment.
Applying for the wrong NTU entity â€” NIE runs a separately announced application period.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation and rent â€” the award gives only priority for campus accommodation; it does not pay for housing.
Airfare to Singapore and any relocation cost â€” no travel or relocation allowance is published.
Anything beyond the S$5,000 per financial year Overseas Conference Allowance cap.
Personal, medical and day-to-day living costs above what the monthly stipend and the book, IT and thesis allowances cover.
Costs arising if the award is not renewed: renewal is subject to good progress and to the school's determination and availability of research funding, so plan for an unpaid final period.
document_audit: Resume â€” required.
Educational Certificates and Transcripts â€” required.
Test Scores (GRE, IELTS etc.) â€” required unless waived; test dates must be within 5 years or less from the date of your application.
Recommendation Letters â€” required.

On-track-to-graduate documentation from your awarding university â€” required only if the undergraduate degree is not yet complete, and it must be official documentation confirming an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent.
Medium-of-instruction letter from your home University â€” required only if you are seeking a GRE/IELTS waiver on the basis that your studies were taught in English.
Date audit: every test score must be within 5 years of the application date; expired scores are a published rejection ground.

scholarships.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) is a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme offered by Nanyang Technological University to encourage outstanding graduates or final-year students to take their first step towards a leading research career by studying full-time for a PhD at NTU. It is described as the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President, recognising PhD students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities. Open to all nationalities, it requires an Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level, or official documentation confirming the candidate is on track to achieve it. Monthly stipends revised with effect from January 2026 are S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents and S$4,300 for international students, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens. The award also covers the annual tuition fee and provides an overseas conference allowance of up to S$5,000 per financial year, an annual book allowance of S$500, a one-off IT allowance of S$1,500, a one-off thesis allowance of S$600 and priority for campus accommodation. There is no bond attached to the scholarship, though international students must perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties under the Graduate Assistantship Programme.
scholarships.duration: The award is tenable for one year in the first instance and is renewable subject to good progress. The maximum period of the Scholarship is 4 years for PhD candidates, as determined by school as well as availability of research funding in each case.
scholarships.application_period: The application period is announced by NTU in due course for each Academic Year. Successful candidates are informed of the outcome together with the offer of admissions via email.

applicant_utility.summary: This is SMU's flagship donor-funded freshman scholarship: four years of subsidised tuition fees waived, S$5,000 a year for living costs, a S$16,000 grant for overseas exchange, study missions, community service or case competitions, and a one-off S$1,800 computer allowance. You cannot apply for it separately - you compete for it by marking the Scholarship section of your SMU admission application and submitting the personal essay, and only up to 60 are funded. If you are not Singaporean, accepting it means signing the MOE Tuition Grant and committing to three years of work at a Singapore-based company after graduation. The last published round closed on 19 March 2026 and the next cycle's dates had not been posted as at 10 October 2026, so start preparing documents and test scores now.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-calibre school leavers of any nationality with a strong academic record plus a deep co-curricular and community service portfolio who want a full ride at SMU and accept the three-year Singapore work obligation
application_readiness_checklist: Register for and sit an accepted standardised test (IELTS/TOEFL/SAT/ACT/PTE Academic/C1 Advanced/AST) months early - IELTS/TOEFL scores are only valid for 2 years and official scores must be sent electronically to SMU (TOEFL code 9014, SAT 2861, ACT 5284)
Have your school attest predicted scores - self-declared predicted scores are not accepted
Nominate your tutor or principal referee early in the Scholarship section so they can submit the online recommendation before the closing date
Draft the scholarship personal essay around concrete leadership, communication and community service evidence, since shortlisting weighs the non-academic record heavily
Upload your passport particulars page (and Student Pass if applicable), high school results and test scores via Applicant's Self Service, and pay the S$15 application fee
Prepare for a panel interview: shortlisted applicants are invited to SMU, and applicants not residing in Singapore are interviewed by Zoom for the listed non-law programmes
common_rejection_risks: A thin non-academic record - shortlisting explicitly weighs academic qualifications AND the strength of co-curricular/community service records
Missing the scholarship essay or the Scholarship section of the application form, since everything rides on the admission application
Official test scores never arriving because the applicant uploaded a copy but did not have the testing agency send them electronically
Late referee submission when the optional recommendation was not actually filed in time to support the application
Failing to plan the required second major / double degree structure, which is a condition of the award rather than an afterthought
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The S$15 application fee and standardised test fees (borne by the applicant), plus personal spending beyond the S$5,000 annual living allowance and any overseas programme costs not met by the S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant

alerts: Non-Singaporeans (including Permanent Residents) sign a 3-year MOE Tuition Grant obligation - do not accept if you plan to build your career outside Singapore

scholarships.description: The Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme is one of Singapore Management University's most prestigious undergraduate scholarships, made possible by a gift from the Lee Foundation, with up to 60 scholarships funded. It is open to full-time SMU first-year undergraduates of any nationality taking a single or double degree programme, and requires a second major or an equivalent breadth requirement, demonstrated leadership and communications skills, and a substantial record of co-curricular activity or community service. Benefits comprise a waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms for up to four years, a S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant funding overseas exchange, community service or competitions, a S$5,000 annual living allowance, a S$1,800 one-time computer allowance, and development opportunities from SMU's Student Success Centre. Applicants are considered through the Scholarship section of the standard admission application, with no separate scholarship form. The scholarship is bond-free, but non-Singaporean scholars must sign a Ministry of Education Tuition Grant agreement obliging them to work for Singapore-based companies for three years after graduation.

scholarships.name: QUAD STEM Scholarship Scheme (ICCR)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-ride for a four-year B.Tech at eight named Indian institutes, but it is rationed by country: 50 slots are split across 32 countries, with most getting exactly one. Your country's Mission, not ICCR, picks the recipient, and admission is decided separately by the institute you list, so both gates must open. Money-wise, expect INR 18,000 a month plus INR 6,500 or 5,500 of house rent allowance, a return economy airfare booked by the Mission, and tuition paid straight to the institute. The things that actually sink candidates are mundane: a passport that is not valid for two years from 1 July 2026, a second registration on the portal, or missing the 7-day window to accept an offer.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent school leavers from the 32 listed QUAD countries with strong Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry results at Standard XII who want a fully funded engineering degree abroad.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your country's slot allocation first - if it holds a single slot, plan to apply in the very first days of the window
Verify passport validity covers at least two years from 1 July 2026, and renew before registering if it does not
Rank your five institute/course choices carefully, because neither the course nor the university can be changed after the award
Confirm you studied Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry at Standard XII, since science and engineering UG entry requires it
Draft the mandatory 500-word English essay on one of the topics listed on the A2A Portal, and upload any TOEFL or IELTS certificate you hold
Register on the Study in India (SII) Portal as soon as an offer arrives, since the unique ID is needed for the visa
common_rejection_risks: Registering twice on the A2A Portal in the same academic year, which cancels every application you submitted
Missing the 7-day deadline to accept or reject the offer, or failing to upload the Medical Fitness Certificate in time, both of which cancel the award
Any mismatch between portal data and documentary evidence, which results in cancellation of the application
Falsifying a date of birth, which leads to automatic rejection and, if found after joining, repayment of every expense plus a forgery complaint
Applying for a B.Tech at an IIT, where foreign students are not admitted under this programme, or for a Medical, Law or Integrated course
Assuming that admission by an institute guarantees the scholarship - the Mission selects only within its slot count
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Hostel or private accommodation charges, mess charges, security deposit and caution money, fees for obtaining certificates, immigration registration fees or penalties, and any other charge outside the scholarship norms. ICCR also advises carrying self-financial support of around USD 1,500, because completing the formalities to release allowances takes two to three months.
document_audit: The photograph must have a white background and both ears visible to the portal's specifications, which is a common silent rejection
Mark sheets, birth certificate, school leaving certificate and nationality certificate must be in English and produced in original for verification at admission
The Medical Fitness Certificate must come from a reputed hospital or laboratory on the prescribed format; the Mission may accept or reject it without giving reasons
Air tickets are booked by the Indian Mission - never book your own, as there is no reimbursement
alerts: The 2026-27 round is closed and the portal confirms registration is shut; the scheme is notified only up to AY 2027-28, so watch the portal and your Indian Mission rather than relying on third-party aggregators
You must leave India after receiving your provisional marksheets and before your Residential Permit expires - the scholarship is not a migration route
Working in India while studying on this scholarship is not permitted
Stipend and HRA are paid only after you open a State Bank of India account and register it with ICCR, and allowances are suspended if you fail a year or do not submit semester progress reports
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the A2A Portal, submit one application with up to five institute choices and the mandatory essay, let the institutes scrutinise and post provisional admission, then await the Indian Mission's offer - accept within 7 days with a medical fitness certificate, complete SII and visa formalities, and let the Mission book the air ticket.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the widest-reaching ICCR scheme - 116 slots across 23 countries at undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral level, in both STEM and Non-STEM subjects - but it is also the one most people misread on airfare. Only Mexico and Turkmenistan get a ticket, so if your country is one of the other 21 you must fund your own flight. The money itself is level-banded: INR 18,000 a month at UG, 20,000 at PG and 22,000 at Ph.D., with house rent allowance of 6,500 or 5,500 (12,500 at doctoral level), annual contingency and a one-off thesis grant, and tuition paid straight to your university. Because slots are tiny per country, the practical discipline is to file one perfect application in the opening days rather than several.

common_rejection_risks: Submitting a second registration on the A2A Portal in the same academic year, which voids every application
Applying for a Medical, Para-medical, Law or Integrated course, all of which are explicitly excluded
Age breach on 1 July 2026 - 35 maximum for UG, PG, certificate and diploma, 40 for Ph.D., with no exceptions at those levels
A mismatch between portal entries and documentary evidence, which cancels the application outright
Assuming admission by a university secures the scholarship; the Mission selects only within its slot allocation
Missing the 7-day acceptance window or the medical fitness upload deadline after an offer is issued
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Return airfare for nationals of the 21 countries without an airfare provision, plus hostel or private accommodation charges, mess charges, security deposit and caution money, certificate fees, immigration registration fees and penalties, and any AIU equivalence certificate fee. ICCR advises carrying around USD 1,500 because it takes two to three months for allowances to start flowing.

scholarships.name: UGC Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) and Research Associateship (RA) for Foreign Nationals

application_readiness_checklist: Sit UGC-NET (or the UGC-CSIR joint test) and qualify in the Junior Research Fellowship category â€” this is the only entry route UGC publishes.
Confirm you qualified under the JRF category, not the 'Assistant Professor + Ph.D.' category or the 'Ph.D. only' category; neither carries the fellowship.
Secure an M.Phil. or Ph.D. research place at a University, Institution or College.

Work with your institution's research/admissions office immediately: UGC says the M.Phil/PhD registration is made by the institution, and it must happen within two years of your result or award letter.

Check which contingency you are eligible for â€” Contingency A if you are in Humanities or Social Sciences (including Languages), Contingency B if you are in Science. The rates differ and are not interchangeable.
Budget against Rs. 37,000 per month for the first 2 years, then Rs. 42,000 per month, knowing the tenure ends at 5 years or thesis submission, whichever comes first.
Do not assume tuition is paid: UGC publishes the fellowship and contingency only, with no tuition-fee statement.
important_advice_for_students: There is no separate fellowship application form at UGC. The only thing you apply for is the qualifying test. The fellowship follows from the result plus an institutional registration.

The two-year clock is the real deadline and the institution holds it, not you. UGC says registration for the M.Phil/PhD is made by the University/Institution/College within two years of the declaration of result, issue of the award letter, or joining the fellowship. Chase your institution in writing.

Your qualifying category is worth as much as your score. NTA is explicit that the 'appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to Ph.D.' category does not carry the JRF award, and 'admission to Ph.D. only' does not carry either.
Do not budget the fellowship as covering tuition. UGC's published financial assistance is the monthly fellowship plus a contingency allowance, with no mention of fee payment.

Note the two-tier contingency. Humanities and Social Sciences scholars get Contingency A (Rs. 10,000 pa as JRF, Rs. 20,500 pa as SRF); Science scholars get Contingency B (Rs. 12,000 pa as JRF, Rs. 25,000 pa as SRF). Science scholars receive more.
Plan for the step-up at 2 years: your rate rises from Rs. 37,000 to Rs. 42,000 and your contingency also steps up, so year three onwards is better than years one and two.

If you are a foreign national, resolve your eligibility before anything else. NTA frames UGC-NET as determining 'the eligibility of Indian nationals' for the JRF award, and the UGC scheme page publishes no foreign-national provision. Do not assume you can sit the test and claim the fellowship.
common_rejection_risks: Qualifying under 'appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to Ph.D.' or 'admission to Ph.D. only' rather than the JRF category.
Never sitting, or not passing, NET-JRF or the UGC-CSIR joint test.
The host institution failing to lodge the M.Phil/PhD registration within the two-year stipulated period.
Joining the fellowship without a confirmed M.Phil. or Ph.D. registration.
Expecting the fellowship to pay tuition fees, which UGC does not state it covers.
Applying for the wrong contingency band by misidentifying the discipline as Science versus Humanities/Social Sciences.
Assuming a Research Associateship is a separate UGC scheme that can be applied for directly â€” UGC's Student Corner lists only two fellowships and does not publish an RA scheme page.
Missing the UGC-NET cycle dates, which are set by NTA rather than by the fellowship page.
estimated_uncovered_costs: M.Phil./Ph.D. tuition and programme fees â€” no tuition payment or waiver is published under this scheme.
Living costs beyond the monthly fellowship of Rs. 37,000 (first 2 years) or Rs. 42,000 (thereafter).
Travel, relocation and fieldwork costs â€” no travel allowance is published.
Medical insurance and health cover â€” not published as covered.
Costs after the fellowship ends: tenure is 5 years or thesis submission, whichever is earlier, and no extension is published.
document_audit: UGC publishes no document list for this scheme on the scheme page, so documents is recorded as empty rather than filled from assumption.
UGC publishes no file format, size, translation or signature rules, so document_format_rules is an empty list.

Practical note: the documents that matter procedurally are your UGC-NET result and award letter, because UGC's two-year registration clock is measured from the date of declaration of result, the date of issue of the award letter, or the date of joining the fellowship. Keep certified copies of all three dates.
Get your institution's written confirmation that the M.Phil/PhD registration has been made and the date it was made â€” that is the only evidence that satisfies UGC's two-year condition.

alerts.message: Check which category you qualified in. Only the JRF category carries the fellowship.

alerts.trigger: Your result or award letter is dated

alerts.message: You are inside the risk window. Escalate to the institution's research office or the UGC contact before the two years elapse.
Your rate steps from Rs. 37,000 to Rs. 42,000 per month and your contingency steps up too.
NTA describes UGC-NET as determining the eligibility of Indian nationals for the JRF award. Confirm your eligibility in writing with UGC before investing time in the application.
The fellowship ends at 5 years or thesis submission, whichever is earlier. Plan the end date.

submission_workflow: Register for and sit the UGC-NET examination through the National Testing Agency portal (https://ugcnet.nta.nic.in/), or the UGC-CSIR joint test.
Await the result and confirm you qualified in the Junior Research Fellowship category.
Secure an M.Phil. or Ph.D. research admission at a University, Institution or College.
Ask that institution to register you for the M.Phil/PhD, and obtain written confirmation of the registration date.
Complete registration within two years of the declaration of result, the issue of the award letter, or joining the fellowship.
Join the fellowship as Junior Research Fellow at Rs. 37,000 per month, with the contingency applicable to your discipline.
After 2 years, move to Senior Research Fellow at Rs. 42,000 per month with the higher contingency rate.
Submit the thesis within the 5-year tenure.
post_award_requirements: Remain registered for the M.Phil. or Ph.D. programme that the fellowship is attached to.
Complete the thesis within the tenure of 5 years or on submission of the thesis, whichever is earlier.
Report through the host institution; UGC publishes no separate reporting obligation for the fellow.
No return-home obligation is published for this scheme.
questions_to_ask_host: Has my M.Phil./Ph.D. registration been formally made by the institution, and on what date?
Does your institution treat the UGC-NET qualifying category as sufficient, or do you impose additional conditions?
Which contingency band will be applied to me â€” Contingency A (Humanities and Social Sciences) or Contingency B (Science)?
Are programme tuition fees payable separately, and does the institution waive them for JRF holders?
How is the fellowship disbursed, and through what account and documentation?
What happens if I change discipline or institution mid-fellowship â€” does the contingency band or the rate change?
Is a Research Associateship available after the Ph.D. through your institution, and on what terms?

scholarships.title: Netaji Subhas-ICAR International Fellowship (NS-ICAR IF)
scholarships.name: Netaji Subhas-ICAR International Fellowship (NS-ICAR IF)
official_source_urls: https://www.icar.gov.in (unreachable: webfetch transport error; browser ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID)

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your Master's is in agriculture/allied sciences with OGPA 6.60/10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent â€” this is a hard numeric gate.
Check the age gate against the last date for receipt of applications: 35 for fresh candidates, 40 for in-service candidates.
Check the freshness gate: as a fresh candidate your Master's must have been completed not more than two years before the specified date in the year of admission.
As an in-service candidate from India, confirm you are employed in the ICAR-AU system and that you can get deputation approval from your Director/Vice-Chancellor.
Choose a research topic inside the Council's identified priority areas â€” they are published one year in advance and a proposal outside them is not eligible.
Pick a host from the published lists: identified overseas institutions for Indian candidates, identified Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system for overseas candidates.
Apply to the host yourself and get the acceptance letter â€” ICAR makes you obtain it 'at their own level' and you must have it in hand at interview.
Write the research plan and give it a title; the form asks for discipline, degree programme, session and year of admission, prescribed duration, proposed area of study and the host's contact person.
Nominate two referees with email addresses â€” one your current supervisor (if employed) and one an expert in your area. ICAR will contact them directly.

Assemble the certified pieces early, because they take longest: the doctor's physical fitness certificate with seal, and â€” for overseas applicants â€” the Indian Diplomatic Mission certificates with office seal.
Attach copies of your academic documents, a recent photograph, supporting documents for achievements, and copies of research papers for publications above NAAS 4.0.
If you are an Indian candidate, have your Aadhar number ready â€” it is mandatory to receive the fellowships.
Email the whole pack to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with the subject exactly as "Application for NSIF: [your name] and [contact number]" by the deadline.
Plan your financial buffer: host fees, medical insurance and medical fitness come out of your own pocket or out of the fellowship.
important_advice_for_students: This is not full funding. ICAR states plainly that 'All fees chargeable by the host institution where the fellow is enrolled will be paid by the fellow himself out of the fellowship grant or from his/her own resources', and that all other costs including medical insurance come from the fellowship or your own resources. Model the host tuition fee before you commit.

You get the air ticket, and it is genuinely generous: a to-and-fro economy class ticket provided by the Council for both Indian and overseas candidates. But for Indian candidates, getting to the departure airport in India and from the arrival airport to the overseas university is on you or your sponsor.
For overseas fellows in India, the Council also reimburses economy-class travel from the port of arrival to your university and back â€” worth claiming.

Budget for three years and no more. The tenure 'will not be extended in any case'. If you are slow, you finish on your own money, and if you are two years past the prescribed programme duration the Council may recover the fellowship paid.

The stakes on conduct are high. Unsatisfactory performance or conduct probation terminates the fellowship immediately and makes you pay for the rest of the programme. Indian Fellows who do not return to India face recovery of the entire amount paid plus 10% overhead, and the Indian Embassy in the host country may be informed.

Do not move or change your research direction. You must sign an undertaking that you will neither change the place of work nor deviate from the broad research area, and progress is certified every six months by your advisor.

If you are an overseas fellow and your work needs Indian field trials, you may spend up to one-and-a-half-year in India and you keep the same fellowship rate during that time â€” but interim trips beyond that need your Advisor's consent and prior ICAR approval, and ICAR funds no travel for them.

Prepare for the money mechanics. The first six months are released only after ICAR receives your acceptance and your host's admission letter, and the first installment to an Indian fellow is paid in Indian Rupees only.

Indian fellows must put up an irrevocable US$ 10,000 bank guarantee in favour of the Secretary, ICAR for the whole programme. Foreign national fellows instead have Rs. 2,00,000 recovered from their grant (Rs. 1,00,000 each from the first two installments), refunded at final release. These are different mechanisms â€” know which applies to you.
The interview may not be a video call you choose. The Committee can use teleconferencing, and overseas candidates may be interviewed by Council-identified experts based in their home country.

ICAR shares in your IP. The Council takes an appropriate share on patents and knowledge generated under its IP Management bulletin, and any other IP agreement you sign must be shared with ICAR. Acknowledge ICAR support in all publications.

Note the 30-fellowship cap: allocation between Indian and overseas candidates depends on the availability of good candidates in the priority areas, so a strong topic matters as much as a strong record.
common_rejection_risks: Master's degree below OGPA 6.60/10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent.
Over the age limit on the last date prescribed for receipt of applications (35 fresh, 40 in-service).
As a fresh candidate, having completed the qualifying degree more than two years before the specified date in the year of admission.
As an in-service candidate from India, not being employed in the ICAR-AU system.
Proposed research outside the Council's identified priority areas.
No acceptance letter from the host â€” you must have one, and you must produce it at the interview.
Naming a host that is not on the identified list, or a host without the required research and teaching capability and faculty/infrastructure strength.
Only one referee, or two referees who do not meet the published composition (current supervisor plus an expert in the area).
Missing, unsealed or unsigned certificates â€” the physical fitness certificate needs a doctor's seal, and overseas applicants' certificates need the Indian Diplomatic Mission's office seal.
Missing the Certificate from the Candidate including the return-home undertaking.
Missing supporting documents: academic document copies, recent photograph, achievement documents, or copies of research papers for NAAS-above-4.0 publications.
An in-service candidate who cannot produce deputation approval, or an Indian in-service candidate who will not execute the three-year service bond.
No Aadhar number for an Indian candidate, which ICAR states is mandatory to receive the fellowships.
A wrong or missing email subject line â€” ICAR specifies "Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number".
Missing the deadline. For the 2026 cycle the last date was September 25, 2026.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All host institution fees where the fellow is enrolled â€” explicitly the fellow's own responsibility, out of the grant or own resources.
Medical insurance â€” explicitly excluded; the fellow meets it from the fellowship or own resources.
The medical fitness test â€” at the fellow's own cost.
For Indian candidates going abroad: travel from residence/work to the port of departure in India, and from the port of arrival to the destination University overseas.
Interim visits to India by overseas fellows â€” ICAR provides no financial support on travelling for the purpose.
Completion costs if the Ph.D. is not finished within the three-year tenure, or recovery of the fellowship paid if it is not finished two years beyond the prescribed programme duration.
For Indian fellows: the working capital tied up in the US$ 10,000 irrevocable bank guarantee held for the whole programme.
For foreign national fellows: Rs. 2,00,000 withheld from the grant until final release.
Books, equipment, fieldwork and consumables beyond the annual contingent and preparatory lump sum of US$ 1,000 (Indian fellows abroad) or INR 25,000 (overseas fellows in India).
document_audit: Completed application form in the prescribed ICAR proforma, signed with date and place.
Recent photograph of the applicant â€” a stated form item.
Copies of documents for every academic qualification from the graduate degree onwards, showing university/institution, degree, year, subjects and marks/grades/OGPA.
Supporting documents for professional work experience and achievements: awards/honours/scholarships (Gold Medal, Best Thesis, NTS, JRF), NET, ARS, research/teaching experience.

Publications above NAAS 4.0 only, in the prescribed four-column format (authors and title, name of journal, journal ID, NAAS score against the NAAS list of Science journals 2025), with copies of the research papers attached.
Acceptance letter for admission from the Host University â€” copy to be attached.
Copy of the research plan â€” YES/NO indicated and the copy attached.
Deputation permission from the parent organisation for in-service candidates.
Certificate from the Candidate: truth declaration, agreement to the guidelines/terms and conditions, and the undertaking to complete the Ph.D. and return to their country. Signed.

Certificate from the Indian Diplomatic Representative (overseas applicants only): permanent domicile certification, the return-to-country-of-domicile undertaking, and certification that the entries were checked against original documents and the application is complete, with scanned copies of relevant certificates enclosed. Must carry signature, name, designation, OFFICE SEAL, address, date and place.

Certificate of Physical Fitness by an authorized Medical Doctor: medical history, physical examination, lungs, summary, the doctor's view on ability to carry a full course of study involving long hours of work, health rating (EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR), vaccination record and general remarks. Must carry signature, address, date and DOCTOR's SEAL.

Certificate of Proficiency in English (overseas applicants only): whether the applicant is proficient/not proficient in written/spoken English and/or has/has not passed the English Proficiency Test, naming the conducting authority, under the SEAL of the Indian Diplomatic Mission.
Referee comment forms, one per referee, in the prescribed FORMAT: referee's name, designation, affiliation, contact phone, email; the three declarations; signature and date.
Passport details (number, date of issue, place of issue, date of expiry) and, for Indian candidates, the Aadhar number.
Fresh/in-service tick, with the Master's completion year for fresh candidates or the employer's name, address, head of organization and position held for in-service candidates.

Health advisory to action on: those planning to study in India are strongly advised to get vaccinated against typhoid/cholera before coming to India; those proceeding for overseas studies may get appropriate vaccination as per the host country's requirements.
Publication check: ICAR's document publishes no file size limit, accepted file extension or translation rule, so those remain to be confirmed with the ADG (HRD) at ICAR before you send.

referee_tracking.instructions: One of the two referees should preferably be the applicant's supervisor in the current occupation (if employed). The applicant supplies the referee's name, address, contact phone number and e-mail address; the Council may contact the referees directly to obtain comments in the prescribed format. The referee completes the 'FORMAT FOR REFEREE COMMENTS ON THE SUITABILITY OF CANDIDATE FOR NETAJI SUBHAS-ICAR INTERNATIONAL FELLOWSHIP', which asks them to state whether they are well acquainted with the applicant's work and achievements, whether they are satisfied the applicant has the sincerity, zeal and capacity to complete the Ph.D. programme applied for with funding support under the fellowship, and whether they would recommend the applicant without hesitation â€” then signs and dates it.

referee_tracking.role: Referee 2 â€” expert in the area
referee_tracking.instructions: The second referee should be an expert in the area and well acquainted with the candidate's work. The applicant supplies the name, address, contact phone number and e-mail address, and ICAR may contact this referee directly using the prescribed referee comment format, with signature and date.

Not a referee in the assessment sense, but the host's advisor/supervisor/head of institution certifies every academic progress report that the fellow submits to the Council, and those certified reports are the condition for each subsequent release of the fellowship.

A certifying authority rather than an academic referee. The mission certifies that the applicant is permanently domiciled in the named country and will return to the country of domicile on completion of studies in the host country; certifies that the entries in the application form, particulars about examinations passed, marks obtained, subjects studied and syllabi covered have been checked with original documents and that the application is complete in all respects; and confirms the applicant has enclosed scanned copies of relevant certificates, diplomas or degrees. Requires signature, name, designation, office seal, address, date and place.

Completes the Certificate of Physical Fitness, including medical history, physical examination, lungs, summary, an explicit statement on whether the applicant is or is not physically able to carry on a full course of study involving long hours of work in a college/university/institution in India or abroad, a health rating, the small pox vaccination record, and whether there is evidence of communicable disease, fatigue or physical defects. Requires signature, address, date and doctor's seal.

questions_to_ask_host: Is my proposed Ph.D. programme and research area covered by the Council's identified priority areas for this cycle?

What are the host's admission and course requirements, and what is its own admission deadline relative to ICAR's September 25 deadline?
What English proficiency evidence does the host require, and does it align with the Indian Diplomatic Mission certificate ICAR asks for?
How will my advisor certify the six-monthly progress reports, and what evidence of progress does the host require?
What is the host's policy on the maximum period I may spend on research experiments and data collection at the host or in India?
Who is the contact person at the host that ICAR will approach, and how quickly can the host issue my acceptance letter?
What is the prescribed duration of the Ph.D. programme, since ICAR uses it to judge whether I am two years overdue?
If I am an overseas fellow needing Indian field trials, how would a one-and-a-half-year stay at an Indian SAU or institute be arranged, and who verifies my absence?

scholarships.name: IIT Kanpur Institute Fellowship (for International Students)

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are not an Indian citizen by birth or naturalization and do not hold an OCI/PIO card â€” otherwise this route does not apply to you.
Register on the Study in India (SII) portal. IIT Kanpur calls this mandatory and says it is also linked to issuance of your study visa, so do it before anything else.

Pick one funding route and meet its own condition: ICCR, Study in India, AARDO (AARDO member country, MTech only), India Bhutan Friendship (Bhutanese, MTech), ASEAN-DIA (currently on hold), or the Institute Fellowship (no other funding).
Match your degree to a published programme and department, and check that department's eligibility minimum â€” the published figures are absolute minimums and departments may add more.

Assemble: passport/citizenship card, applicant photo, applicant signature, proof of date of birth, qualifying degree certificate (original/provisional), GATE score card if you have one, and the mark/grade sheet of the qualifying degree as a single PDF file.
Add the NOC only if you are a sponsored, part-time or external candidate.
Apply in the right window: Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April, or Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD only.
Submit through Pingala, or use the Foreign National email route with IIT Kanpur's offline sample form if the portal has closed.
Do not pay the application fee â€” it is waived for the Foreign National category, and you are asked to ignore the Pingala payment prompt after submitting.
Do not let a missing GATE score stop you â€” the GATE requirement is waived for the Foreign National category.
Be ready for a video-conferencing interview if shortlisted, and accept that departmental committees make the final admission decision.
important_advice_for_students: Do not read 'Institute Fellowship at par with Indian students' as full funding. Foreign students pay a published fee structure on top: USD 250 to USD 4,000 in tuition depending on programme and SAARC status, plus INR 17,495 hostel fee. Budget for that.

The single exception on tuition is the AARDO Fellowship, which waives tuition and gives free accommodation plus airfare to and from New Delhi â€” but it is for MTech only and for AARDO member countries in Asia and Africa.
The cheapest route to a scholarship may be Study in India: apply there, sit the PRAGATII exam, and meritorious students are selected for up to USD 3,200 covering tuition, accommodation and mess.
If you already hold another scholarship, you lose the Institute Fellowship â€” it is explicitly limited to students who receive no other funding. Do not count on both.
The Study in India registration is not paperwork you can defer. IIT Kanpur links it to your study visa, so a missing registration can block your visa and therefore your admission.

Two real advantages: the application fee is waived and the GATE requirement is waived for the Foreign National category. Do not let a missing GATE score stop you, and do not attempt to pay a fee you do not owe.

Watch the two-stage assistantship structure if you are a PhD candidate: Rs. 37,000/- per month for the first two years, then Rs. 42,000/- for another three years. The rate steps up, so your later years are better funded.

If you want the assistantship, you must be a regular candidate. M Tech/MS (By Research) in Cybersecurity is explicitly for sponsored/part-time/external candidates and carries no financial assistantship.

Be practical about the assistantship duty: MTech, MDes and MS (By Research) assistants are assigned 8 hours of work per week, and the institute states you are expected to carry out the assigned duties during the programme.

The email route for foreign nationals has its own, later deadline than the portal. For 2026-27 the portal closed April 15 at 02:00 PM but foreign nationals could still email until April 30, 2026 â€” do not assume the portal and email deadlines coincide.
Applications to ICCR are usually April-June, which is a different calendar from IIT Kanpur's own windows. If you are routing through ICCR, you are managing two deadlines.
ASEAN-DIA is on hold. If that was your plan, it is not available right now, and the ASEAN portal is a different route hosted at IIT Delhi.
Departments can set requirements above the published minimums, so treat the eligibility table as a floor and confirm with your target department before you invest effort.
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an Indian citizen or OCI/PIO card holder through the foreign-national route, where those candidates are not treated as foreign nationals.
Missing the mandatory Study in India registration, which is also linked to study visa issuance.
Applying outside the published windows (Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April; Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD).
Missing the Foreign National email deadline because you assumed it matched the Pingala portal closure date.
Splitting the qualifying mark/grade sheet into multiple files when it must be a single PDF file.
Applying for the assistantship while sponsored, part-time or external â€” assistantship is limited to regular students.
Applying for M Tech/MS (By Research) in Cybersecurity as a regular candidate â€” it is sponsored/part-time/external only and carries no assistantship.
Counting on the Institute Fellowship while also holding another scholarship â€” it is limited to students with no other funding.
Relying on the ASEAN-DIA fellowship, which is published as currently on hold.
Applying for the India Bhutan Friendship Scholarship as a non-Bhutanese student, or for AARDO from a non-member country.
Being below the department's actual requirement, where the department has set a bar above the published absolute minimum.
Failing to prepare for, or attend, the video-conferencing interview that decides the final selection of shortlisted FN candidates.
Attempting to pay the waived application fee on the Pingala Portal after submission.
Not sending the required testimonials with the emailed Foreign National application.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees for every route other than the AARDO Fellowship: USD 250 (PhD SAARC), USD 500 (PhD Non-SAARC), USD 500 (MTech SAARC), USD 750 (MTech Non-SAARC), USD 2,000 (MBA SAARC) or USD 4,000 (MBA Non-SAARC).
The hostel fee of INR 17,495 in every row of the fee structure table, except under the AARDO Fellowship which includes free accommodation.
Books, equipment, travel and everyday living costs beyond the monthly fellowship or assistantship and the annual scheme-specific items.
The gap between the India Bhutan Friendship Scholarship's 'fully funded' description and any cost not named in it â€” IIT Kanpur publishes no itemised coverage for that scholarship.
Any cost attached to the Study in India route above the capped USD 3,200 scholarship.
Travel to and from India for everyone except AARDO beneficiaries, for whom airfare to and from New Delhi is published.
Medical insurance and other personal costs â€” not published as covered by any of these schemes.
document_audit: Passport/Citizenship Card â€” required; this is also how the foreign-national status is evidenced.
Applicant Photo â€” required.
Applicant Signature â€” required, i.e. a signature specimen is a submitted item, not merely a field.
Proof of Date of Birth â€” required.
Qualifying Degree Certificate (Original/Provisional) â€” required.
GATE Score Card, if available â€” optional as a document, but note the GATE qualification requirement itself is waived for the Foreign National category.
Mark/Grade sheet of Qualifying Degree â€” must be a single PDF file.
NOC â€” only for Sponsored/Part Time/External Candidates; do not submit it otherwise.
Foreign National email route: the complete application together with the required testimonials, optionally using IIT Kanpur's published offline sample application form (Application-Form-offline.doc).
Study in India registration confirmation â€” mandatory for all foreign students and linked to study visa issuance.

Publication check: IIT Kanpur publishes no file size limits, accepted file extensions, signature format or translation rules on these pages. Only the 'single PDF file' rule for the mark/grade sheet and the official offline .doc sample form are stated. Confirm remaining upload rules inside the Pingala portal.

alerts.trigger: Before you start anything else, if you are a foreign national
alerts.message: Register on the Study in India portal. IIT Kanpur states it is mandatory for all foreign students and that it is linked to your study visa.
The Autumn window opens on 20 March for M.Tech., M.B.A., M.Des. and Ph.D. Prepare the single-PDF mark sheet before the window.
The Autumn window closes and the Pingala portal becomes inaccessible after 02:00 PM. Foreign nationals then rely on the separate email route with the offline sample form.
For the 2026-27 cycle this was the Foreign National email deadline (admissions_ir@iitk.ac.in, cc admissiondesk@iitk.ac.in).
The Spring Ph.D. window opens and runs to 31 October. Ph.D. only â€” no MTech in the Spring intake.
Expect a video-conferencing interview, and remember the competent committees of the departments make the final admission decision.
Ignore the application-fee payment prompt â€” the fee is waived for the Foreign National category.

alerts.message: The AARDO Fellowship is the strongest published package â€” tuition waiver, free accommodation, an Indian-par stipend and airfare to New Delhi â€” but it is MTech only.

submission_workflow: Confirm foreign-national status (not an Indian citizen by birth or naturalization; no OCI/PIO card).
Register on the Study in India portal and keep the confirmation, since it is linked to your study visa.
Select the funding route that fits your circumstances and complete that scheme's own conditions.
Check your target programme and department's eligibility minimums, including any departmental requirement above the published floor.

Prepare the document set: passport/citizenship card, photo, signature, proof of date of birth, qualifying degree certificate, GATE score card if available, and the mark/grade sheet as a single PDF; add the NOC only if sponsored, part-time or external.
Apply within the correct window â€” Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April, or Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD.

Submit through Pingala for M.Des / MS (By Research) / PhD, or email the complete application with the required testimonials to admissions_ir@iitk.ac.in (cc admissiondesk@iitk.ac.in) as a Foreign National candidate.
Do not pay the application fee; skip the GATE requirement.
Prepare for the video-conferencing interview if shortlisted.
On admission, separately apply to the external scheme you are using, on that scheme's own portal and calendar (ICCR is usually April-June).
Register for and complete the assistantship or Institute Fellowship award formalities once admitted.
post_award_requirements: Keep the Study in India registration current, since it is linked to study visa issuance.

For Institute Assistantship holders: carry out the assigned duties during the programme â€” 8 hours of work per week for MTech, MDes and MS (By Research) assistants â€” and remain a regular (non-sponsored/non-part-time/non-external) student.
Pay the published tuition and hostel fee charges unless covered by a scheme that expressly waives them (only the AARDO Fellowship is published as waiving tuition).
Do not combine the Institute Fellowship with other funding; if other funding arrives, the Institute Fellowship does not apply.
No return-home, deferral, renewal or clinical obligation is published by IIT Kanpur for these schemes.
questions_to_ask_host: What are the specific eligibility requirements my department applies on top of the published absolute minimum?
Does my department require a GATE score despite the Foreign National waiver, and will the waiver be honoured for my programme?
Is the assistantship or Institute Fellowship available to me given my candidate category, and at what monthly rate for my programme and year?
What is the exact total fee I will owe, in USD and INR, for my programme and my SAARC or non-SAARC status, and when is it payable?
Is campus hostel accommodation guaranteed at INR 17,495, or is it first-come first-served?
What is my department's real interview process, and how long should I allow for the video-conferencing shortlist?
Which funding scheme do you recommend for my nationality, and does IIT Kanpur have any fee concession for me beyond the published table?
How do I combine the Institute Fellowship with an ICCR or Study in India scholarship, given the 'no other funding' condition?
What is the latest date by which I must have completed my Study in India registration to avoid any delay to my study visa?
Who at the admissions office confirms my admission, and what is the process for converting my offer into enrolment?

scholarships.title: Fellowship for International Research Scholars in Technology at IIT Hyderabad (FIRST@IITH)
scholarships.name: Fellowship for International Research Scholars in Technology at IIT Hyderabad (FIRST@IITH)

applicant_utility.summary: This is an e-mail application, not a portal one: the form, testimonials and a single reference letter must reach ia.ir@iith.ac.in before 17:00 IST on 31 October 2026, with the exact subject line for the January 2027 intake. The academic filter is unusually explicit - a master's in engineering or technology with CGPA 8.5/10 or equivalent, and both bachelor's and master's from foreign universities - so OCI/NRI holders and Indian-qualified students cannot use this route. The stipend is 60,000 INR per month with 1,00,000 INR per year contingency, described by IITH as full financial support for the PhD, but the published package itemises only those two components, so confirm fee treatment in writing when you correspond.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-OCI international master's graduates in engineering or technology with a strong CGPA and both degrees from foreign universities who want a funded PhD in India.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm both your bachelor's and master's degrees are from foreign universities and that you hold neither OCI nor NRI status

Download the current January 2027 application form from the IITH International Relations site rather than reusing an old PDF
Ask your referee for the single reference letter early and make sure the subject line in your e-mail matches the prescribed wording exactly

common_rejection_risks: Holding OCI or NRI status, which excludes the applicant regardless of qualifications
One of the two degrees earned at an Indian university
A CGPA below 8.5 on the 10-point scale or an unconverted equivalent

alerts: The January 2027 call was published on 1 October 2026 and closes 31 October 2026 - a four-week window, so start immediately
No application fee is charged, which makes this one of the lowest-cost international PhD applications available
IITH runs a separate self-financing PhD route for foreign nationals for the same January 2027 intake - do not confuse the two and pay fees you need not pay
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Download the form, complete it with testimonials and one reference letter, e-mail to ia.ir@iith.ac.in with the prescribed subject line before 31 October 2026, 17:00 IST.

scholarships.title: KIIT University India Scholarships Programme (KUISP)
scholarships.name: KIIT University India Scholarships Programme (KUISP)

applicant_utility.summary: KUISP is a tuition-fee-only award: KIIT waives 50-100% of tuition for foreign nationals, but you still pay for hostel, food, airfare, visa and insurance. The scheme is capped at 100 scholarships worldwide with only two full waivers per country, so it is competitive even though the application is free. It is offered across listed humanities, social science, media, law, management and engineering/PhD schools rather than KIIT's full course list, and KIIT publishes no closing date, so apply as early as possible once the portal opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funded-at-heart international applicants who can cover accommodation, food and travel themselves but need tuition relief, especially those from countries with a large applicant pool and strong school grades.
application_readiness_checklist: Check that your intended programme sits in a school named in the KUISP annexure (language, social/financial/human sciences, mass communication, film and media, or the listed PhD specialisations) before starting an application
Register on international.kiit.ac.in, verify the email link from kiit.global@kiit.ac.in, and complete every stage of the form to get an application number
Scan your passport, school leaving certificate, and full secondary/higher-secondary transcripts plus bachelor's and (for PhD) master's transcripts
Obtain recommendation letters and, for doctorate, a 250-word letter of interest
Get every non-English document officially translated into English
Budget roughly USD 500 one-time registration plus about USD 2,000 per year for AC three-sharing hostel and four daily meals, which the leaflet states students pay themselves
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a programme outside the KUISP-eligible schools, such as B.Tech, MBBS, BDS or B.Arch, which are not covered by the scheme
Losing out on a per-country slot because only two full and ten half waivers exist per country inside a worldwide cap of 100 scholarships
Submitting incomplete transcripts that stop at the last degree instead of tracing secondary education
Assuming a mission recommendation substitutes for a complete portal application, or waiting for a mission route that has already closed
PhD part-time applicants who are not actually employed full time, which contradicts the published part-time criterion
Missing English translations of certificates from a non-English-medium school
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The KUISP leaflet states the scholarship does not cover airfare tickets, visa fees, medical insurance, stipends, personal living expenses or a laptop. Students additionally pay a one-time registration fee of USD 500 and an annual fee of USD 2,000 covering AC three-sharing hostel accommodation and four meals a day (vegetarian plus non-vegetarian).
document_audit: The passport must be valid for the whole study period, and a scanned copy is mandatory
The school leaving certificate is requested separately from transcripts
Proof of English proficiency is 'if any', so do not wait for an IELTS result, but translated transcripts are effectively compulsory for non-English schools
Doctorate applicants need either recommendation letters or a 250-word letter of interest, a stricter limit than most KIIT PhD routes
Awards/honours certificates are optional but are the only published way to evidence merit beyond grades
alerts: KIIT's own site states admissions for 2026-27 are open but publishes no KUISP closing date; treat the window as short and apply on day one
The previous KUISP cycle ran 1 March to 30 August with missions recommending by 30 September, so an early-year portal registration matches the historic pattern

A separate scheme, the KIIT International Semester Scholarship Programme, also exists for one to two semesters with publication fees of USD 500 plus USD 1,250 per semester - do not confuse it with KUISP

Earlier KUISP leaflets excluded SAARC countries and KIIT's fee schedule still prices SAARC applicants separately at USD 8,000 per annum, so confirm whether your nationality falls inside the current round
KIIT explicitly warns that the quantum, eligibility and duration of the scholarship can change, so verify against the latest notification before committing
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the KIIT International Admissions Portal, verify your email, complete the programme, personal, address, qualification and upload sections, submit the declaration to receive an application number, then wait for the offer letter in your student dashboard.

Domestic first-years should target the November 1 Early Action I date, while international applicants face one November 30 deadline, roughly 40 seats worldwide, and a $2,200 deposit after admission.

Admitted students average a 3.65 high school GPA and qualify for federal Pell Grants, and Berea is academically competitive with an average ACT of about 25 and more than half of first-year students ranked in the top fifth of their high school class. Housing, food and fees remain payable for current cohorts, but from Fall 2027 the College's Financial Freedom Pledge guarantees 100% of tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies without loans for all students until graduation. Endowment earnings provide 74% of the College's operating budget, state and federal aid 19% and donors the remaining 7%.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are not a U.S. citizen and do not hold dual U.S./other-country citizenship â€” dual citizenship disqualifies you outright.
