important_advice_for_students: There is no separate application and no nomination. The entire published FAQ answer to "How do I apply?" is "Simply apply to Duke University." If you were counting on a separate Karsh form or a nomination, neither exists.

The financial aid interest box is the single most consequential checkbox in your application. Duke states that international applicants admitted with "no financial aid interest" are ineligible to apply for financial aid for any year of undergraduate study â€” that decision is effectively irreversible.
You are pooled separately. International applicants who indicate interest in financial aid are considered in a separate admission pool, so applying with aid interest changes who reads your file.

Missing the CSS Profile deadline does not destroy eligibility, but it delays the aid estimate. Duke says total eligibility will not change and it keeps processing applications as they arrive â€” but your aid award may arrive after your admission letter rather than with it.
Late documents are the real risk, not the deadline. If the College Board requests foreign tax forms or employer statements and you are slow, your award slips.

Get the translations right the first time. Duke requires official English translations, both the original and the translated copy, and the currency conversion into US dollars as part of the translation.
Airfare and visa costs are not in this award. Duke's published cost of attendance includes only domestic transportation of $582, varying by home address. Budget your own flights, visa and SEVIS fee.

Renewal is favourable for international students. Duke issues four-year aid awards to international applicants and automatically renews them for subsequent years â€” but you still submit a new aid application each year with updated income and asset information.

If next year's cost of attendance rises, your grant aid rises with it. Duke states that where you qualified for need-based grant aid and the 2026-27 cost of attendance is higher than the current year, it will increase your grant aid to cover the difference.
Plan around the June funding step and the arrival session. Aid steps arrive by email in June once you enrol, and you must attend a financial aid session on arrival before aid is applied.
The award includes three summers of funding for research and unpaid internships. That is a genuine extra: use it for unpaid opportunities you could not otherwise afford.
common_rejection_risks: Holding dual U.S./other-country citizenship.
Already holding a B.A. or B.S. degree.
Failing to demonstrate financial need â€” international applicants must have demonstrated need to be eligible.
Leaving the financial aid interest box unticked, or failing to have it changed through the Office of Undergraduate Admissions.
Being admitted in the "no financial aid interest" pool, which makes the applicant ineligible for aid in every year.
Missing the CSS Profile deadline (November 3 Early Decision, February 1 Regular Decision) and receiving a delayed aid estimate.
Not completing the CSS Profile at all, which removes you from institutional aid consideration.
Not completing both parents' CSS Profiles where both parents contribute, leaving Duke unable to calculate the Expected Family Contribution.
Being slow to respond to a College Board request for foreign tax forms or employer income statements.
Submitting translations that are not official, or omitting the original-language copy, or omitting the currency conversion into US dollars.
Skipping the FAFSA when required â€” only students who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents may skip it.
Failing to attend the mandatory financial aid session on arrival at Duke.
Failing to submit a new aid application in later years, or leaving income and asset information out of date.
estimated_uncovered_costs: International airfare to the United States â€” Duke's cost of attendance lists only domestic transportation of $582, varying by home address.
US visa application fee, immigration paperwork and the I-901 SEVIS fee â€” none is published as covered.
Anything above your demonstrated financial need: the award is explicitly need-based and is sized to demonstrated need, so a change in your family's circumstances could leave a gap.

Books, course materials and supplies beyond the demonstrated-need calculation if your circumstances change after award â€” Duke requires a new aid application each year with updated income and asset information.

Expenses incurred by current students that Duke's cost of attendance does not itemise, such as travel home or non-Duke study-abroad costs.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply to Harvard College and indicate interest in financial aid in the same submission â€” Harvard wants you to know you can afford to come the moment you are admitted.
Pick your plan: Restrictive Early Action / QuestBridge Match (November 1), Regular Decision (February 1), or Transfer (March 1). The CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC all share that date.
Register for the CSS Profile and list Harvard with code 3434.
Decide the parent-profile structure: one profile if your parents are married or live together; one each if they are separated or divorced.
Prepare both parents' 2025 income tax document with every page and schedule, or a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus employer letters if they do not file.
Prepare your own 2025 income tax document (signed) or a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus any W-2 Forms.
Translate any non-English document into English yourself if needed â€” Harvard says an official translation is not required and students usually write the translation on the document.

Handle the CSS Profile fee problem early if it applies to you: if you cannot afford it or the College Board cannot process payment from your country, use Harvard's alternate application for financial aid instructions.
Skip the FAFSA if you are not a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or other eligible non-citizen.
Complete the CSS Profile before you try to open IDOC â€” Harvard states you cannot access IDOC until the CSS Profile is done.
Upload everything through IDOC. Do not email documents to Harvard under any circumstances.
Add business, trust or estate documents, and a letter on unusual circumstances, if they apply to you.
Note the aid decision timing: mid-December for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match, around April 1 for Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision.
important_advice_for_students: Applying for aid does not hurt your admission chances. Harvard states need-blind admissions explicitly: your financial need and your aid application will never affect your chance of being admitted. There is no reason to apply without indicating aid.
You get exactly the same aid as an American student. Harvard states this twice and in strong terms. Do not assume international status reduces the package.
Aid is 100% need-based with no merit component and no preferential policies. There is nothing to win with extra talents or activities at the aid stage.

Budget for the student contribution, not just the scholarship. Harvard's aid includes a standard expected contribution from your own earnings, usually met by working around 10 to 12 hours a week. Harvard also publishes an average parent contribution of $13K.

You are not required to take any loan. Harvard states loans are never required and that most students graduate debt-free, even though the Harvard Student Loan is open to international students on the same terms as everyone else.

Airfare is the gap to plan for. Harvard's cost of attendance lists only $0-$5,000 for transportation and mentions an unquantified additional travel allowance for aid-eligible students. Confirm the actual treatment of international airfare with the Financial Aid Office before you commit.

Health insurance is a separate required cost: $4,954 for 2026-27 unless you are covered under your family's health plan. Harvard lists this as an addition to the total billed and unbilled costs, so check whether it sits inside your demonstrated need.

You cannot substitute an outside scholarship for Harvard's money. Outside awards first replace the term-time job expectation and then replace an equal amount of Harvard scholarship â€” they never reduce the parent contribution. Win external awards only as much as your need.
Report outside awards or you risk an aid reduction later. They must be reported and applied toward college expenses.

Late is fine, late is slower. Harvard will accept a late application, and a late tax filing does not affect eligibility â€” it only pushes back your decision. That is a genuine benefit of Harvard's process.

Do not send draft or estimated taxes. Harvard requires the actual return as filed with the government. Estimates on the CSS Profile itself are fine, because Harvard updates the profile when the real return reaches IDOC.
A single missing schedule can cost you time. Harvard flags sending one or two pages and omitting schedules like Schedule 1, Schedule A and Schedule B as a common mistake.
If you have an unusual circumstance, say so in writing. Harvard reviews complex cases individually but will not compensate for parents withdrawing support or for large consumer debts.

Watch your College Board account, not Harvard's portal, until admissions decisions are made. Harvard does not track financial aid materials until after decisions, but will notify you if something is missing after admission.
common_rejection_risks: Not indicating financial aid interest on the admission application.
Missing the applicable CSS Profile, FAFSA or IDOC deadline (November 1 Restrictive Early Action/QuestBridge, February 1 Regular Decision, March 1 Transfer).
Trying to access IDOC before completing the CSS Profile.
Sending draft or estimated tax returns instead of the actual return as filed.
Sending only part of a tax return and omitting the schedules.
Emailing documents instead of using IDOC â€” Harvard states explicitly that email is not secure and it will not be accepted.
Parents who do not file tax returns submitting nothing, or neither a Tax Non-Filer Statement nor alternative income documentation.
Failing to translate non-English documents.
Not adding Harvard's CSS Profile code (3434) or FAFSA code (E00468), so Harvard never receives the form.
Failing to report outside awards.
Canadian students submitting the wrong forms â€” Harvard specifies the T-1 General Form for the personal return and the T-2 Corporate Return for the corporate return.
Relying on the FAFSA's 20-school limit and leaving Harvard off the list without adding it back once admitted.
A student contribution shortfall: if you cannot save enough to meet your expected contribution, the Harvard Loan may be needed, and Harvard Grant eligibility is required to use it.
Expecting Harvard to cover a gap created by parents withdrawing support or by family consumer debt â€” Harvard rules both out.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The parent contribution, determined from family income, assets and circumstances. Zero for families with annual income below $100,000; families with significant assets are asked to pay more.
The student contribution, a standard expected contribution from your own earnings, usually met by working around 10 to 12 hours per week.
Health insurance of $4,954 for 2026-27, required unless you are covered under your family's health plan, and published as a cost in addition to the total billed and unbilled costs.
International airfare and visa costs, where the additional travel allowance for aid-eligible students does not reach them â€” Harvard publishes no itemised international travel figure.
Any cost above demonstrated financial need.
Expenses arising from parents withdrawing financial support or from family consumer debt, which Harvard explicitly will not cover with additional aid.
Money borrowed by parents to meet the parent contribution, if the family chooses not to fund it from savings or current income.
Term-time work earnings used to meet the student contribution, offset by outside awards if you hold any.
document_audit: CSS Profile for the relevant school year, listing Harvard with code 3434 â€” required for all applicants regardless of citizenship; one profile if parents are married or live together, one each if separated or divorced.

Parents' 2025 income tax document for both parents â€” for international students, whatever documentation of income and taxes paid is submitted to their national government, which may be two separate documents. All pages and schedules required.
Tax Non-Filer Statement (Harvard's or IDOC's version, both acceptable) where a filer is missing, plus a wage statement, salary certificate, or employer letter stating annual income.
Student's 2025 income tax document, signed, or a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus copies of any W-2 Forms received.
Business/Farm Supplement form for each business and/or farm a parent has an interest in, plus the 2025 business tax return and K-1 statements (US: 1065, 1120-S, 1120).
Full Trust Tax Return plus a letter explaining the contents, value and accessibility of the trust or estate.
A letter about unusual expenses or special circumstances, submitted with the rest of the documents.
FAFSA with Harvard's code E00468 â€” required only for U.S. citizens, permanent residents and other eligible non-citizens.
Canadian specifics: T-1 General Form for the personal tax document; T-2 Corporate Return for the corporate return.

Routing check: all documents go through the College Board IDOC Service. Harvard states email is not a secure method and documents sent by email will not be accepted. Extra documents should be submitted as an 'institution specific required document' or 'other document'.

Translation check: non-English documents must be translated into English. Harvard states an official translation is not required and that students usually write the translation on the document themselves.
Completeness check: IDOC's own list is explicitly not definitive â€” use Harvard's list as the checklist. Omitting a schedule is a published common mistake. Do not send state tax returns.
Publication check: Harvard publishes no file size limits or accepted file extensions beyond the IDOC upload and the translation rules recorded here.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you come from an eligible country â€” one of Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, the Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania or Uganda. If you are in Canada, Portugal or the USA you must be originally from one of those countries.
Confirm you are not planning to study in the United Kingdom or Russia. Those destinations are excluded outright.
Confirm you are entering the first year of your programme. If you have already enrolled or started, you are not eligible and there is no exception to find.
Confirm your programme is full-time. Part-time and short-term courses are not considered at all.
Secure admission to a reputable postgraduate institution. If it is local, regional or distance learning, be ready to evidence that course quality is maintained.
Build your other funding first. The AKF explicitly says to treat the ISP as a resource of last resort and to secure multiple sources so you can request a smaller amount.
Write out a multi-source funding plan that covers every year of study â€” this is a named eligibility criterion, not a formality.
Assemble evidence of leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Line up a guarantor who will co-sign the award agreement. This is a hard condition of the award.
Use the eligibility tool on the AKDN International Scholarships page to verify eligibility and get your local team contact.
Apply through the AKF contact in your country â€” there is no central portal.
Price the award honestly: 50 percent must be repaid plus a service charge, so model the loan half before you accept.
important_advice_for_students: This is not a gift. Half of every AKF ISP award is a loan you repay, with a service charge on top. Repayment starts six months after you graduate, terminate your studies, or lose support for falling below academic standards.
You need a guarantor. Someone has to co-sign the award agreement. Do not apply without one lined up.

The AKF wants you to arrive with other funding. It says plainly to consider the ISP "a resource of last resort" and to secure multiple sources to reduce what you request. Applying with a thin funding plan is itself an eligibility failure.
If you are a PhD applicant, understand the cliff. You get two years and then you are "expected to find funding from alternative sources". Only Master's students get the full duration of the course.
Your country of origin and your destination country both matter. You must be from a listed country, and you cannot study in the UK or Russia even if your country is eligible.
First year only. Already enrolled means already ineligible. Do not accept an offer and then apply.
Age matters as a preference, not a rule: preference is given to young professionals under 30. If you are over 30, you are not barred, but you are competing against a stated preference.

Distance learning is allowed but conditional. Local, regional and distance-learning programmes are fundable "only if the quality of the course is maintained", so expect to be asked to justify quality.
The award does not pay for your flight, your clothes, your furniture or your family. Those four exclusions are stated explicitly, so budget them yourself.
You must keep demonstrating need and academic standing for the whole programme. Improving your finances is not neutral â€” ongoing financial need is part of maintaining the award.
Timing: the 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next opens in early 2027. There is no published day-level deadline, so watch the AKDN page and your local AKF contact rather than a calendar date.
Use the AKF's own list of alternative scholarships. The Foundation publishes a long 'starter' list of other scholarships and assistance programmes precisely because it expects you to fund the rest.
common_rejection_risks: Having already enrolled in, or commenced, postgraduate study.
Applying to a part-time programme or a short-term course.
Planning to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.
Applying from a country not on the list, without being originally from a listed country.
Having no admission to a reputable postgraduate institution.
Demonstrating no genuine financial need.
Presenting no multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study.
Being unable to name a guarantor to co-sign the award agreement.
Applying to a low-quality local, regional or distance-learning programme without being able to demonstrate that quality is maintained.
Being over 30 â€” not a hard bar, but the AKF states a preference for young professionals under 30.
Applying to a PhD without funding secured for years three onward.
Expecting the award to cover airfare, clothing, furniture or family living expenses.
Falling below the academic standards expected of ISP students during the programme, which withdraws support and starts the repayment clock.
estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel costs â€” explicitly not covered.
Clothing â€” explicitly not covered.
Furniture â€” explicitly not covered.
Living expenses for family members â€” explicitly not covered.
Repayment of 50 percent of the award amount, plus the service charge on the loan component, beginning six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support.
For PhD students: all funding from year three onward, since the award covers only the first two years.
Any other costs arising from the multi-source funding plan you were required to build â€” the AKF expects you to cover the balance yourself.
Costs of the guarantor arrangement, if any, which the AKF requires but does not describe.
document_audit: The Aga Khan Foundation does not publish a document list for the AKF ISP on its official page. documents is therefore recorded as an empty list rather than filled from assumption.

Evidence you will need in substance, from the published eligibility criteria: academic records; a Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience; documentation of genuine financial need; a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan covering all years of study; admission to the postgraduate institution; first-year status; and evidence of leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Guarantor arrangement: a guarantor is required to co-sign the award agreement. The AKF does not publish the guarantor's documentation requirements, financial thresholds or eligibility.

Publication check: no file size limits, accepted file extensions, translation or certification rules are published for this programme. Confirm the actual document requirements with the AKF contact in your country, since the process runs through them.

submission_workflow: Verify country eligibility: from a listed country, or originally from a listed country if applying from Canada, Portugal or the USA.
Verify destination eligibility: not the United Kingdom, not Russia.
Verify programme type: full-time, first year, Master's preferred over PhD, not a short-term course.
Secure admission to a reputable postgraduate institution, and evidence course quality if it is local, regional or distance learning.
Build and document a multi-source funding plan covering every year of study, and secure the non-ISP portion of that funding.
Document genuine financial need.
Gather evidence of leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Use the eligibility tool to confirm eligibility and obtain your local AKF team's contact details.
Submit the application through the AKF contact in your country.
Secure a guarantor who will co-sign the award agreement.
On award, sign the half-grant, half-loan agreement, note the service charge and the six-month repayment trigger, and maintain good academic standing and demonstrated ongoing need throughout.
post_award_requirements: "In order to maintain an AKF ISP award, you need to demonstrate good academic standing, as well as ongoing financial need, during the course of your postgraduate programme."
Maintain the academic standards expected of ISP students; failure results in withdrawal of support.
Co-sign the award agreement, which a guarantor must also sign.
Repay 50 percent of the award amount plus the service charge on the loan component, starting six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support.
PhD students must find alternative funding from alternative sources after the first two years.
Keep the multi-source funding plan in place for all years of the programme.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the total award amount available to me, and what exactly is the split between the grant and the loan component?
What is the service charge on the loan component, and what is the total I would repay over what period?
Who can serve as my guarantor, and what do they need to show to qualify?
How is my requested amount calculated, and how much does each additional funding source I secure reduce what I can ask for?
How is 'genuine financial need' assessed for applicants from a country where income data is hard to document?
What evidence do you need to show that a local, regional or distance-learning course maintains quality?
Is there a hard age cut-off, or is the under-30 preference applied strictly?
What are the actual document requirements and formats, since the published page does not list them?
What happens to the award if I change programme, institution or mode of study during the course?
Are there any reporting requirements during the award period beyond demonstrating academic standing and ongoing need?
For a PhD applicant, does the AKF help identify alternative funding for years three onward, or is that entirely on me?

scholarships.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP), established in 1969 by Prince Karim Aga Khan IV, is an opportunity for outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing their studies to pursue postgraduate education. It has supported more than 1,500 students. Awards are structured as half grant and half loan, so 50 percent of the award must be repaid, and they cover tuition and student living expenses. Priority goes to Master's programmes; PhD students receive funding for the first two years only. The 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next cycle opens in early 2027.
scholarships.duration: Master's scholarships are granted for the entire duration of the degree course; PhD scholarships are awarded for the first two years
scholarships.application_period: The 2026-2027 cycle is closed. The next cycle opens in early 2027; the programme is run through a global, annual and competitive application process, with applications handled by contacts in countries where AKF ISP is available.

eligibility: have excellent academic records;
hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience;
demonstrate genuine financial need;
demonstrate a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study;
be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution;
be starting the first year of the programme; and
have strong leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Note: preference is given to young professionals under 30 years of age.

The programme is available in Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, and Uganda. In countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA, applications are accepted from those who are originally from one of the countries listed above. At this time, AKF ISP is not available to students who wish to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold a bachelor's degree and are proficient in English, the two published requirements common to both programs

Bank three years (master's) or five years (certificate) of full-time relevant peace or development experience and evidence it against the Rotary Peace Fellowships Relevant Experience Eligibility Guide
Check the three-year gap rule: your most recent completed undergraduate or graduate degree must be at least three years before your intended fellowship start date
Check the three-year post-Rotary rule if you previously held a Rotary Peace Fellowship (certificate or master's) or a Global Grant Scholarship
Confirm you are not an active Rotary member, not a Rotaract member who is also a Rotary member, and not an employee of a Rotary club, district, Rotary International or other Rotary entity
Confirm no close relative (spouse, child, grandchild, spouse of a lineal descendant, parent, grandparent) falls into the excluded Rotary categories
If you resigned from Rotary, confirm more than 36 months have passed
If you are enrolled in, or will be enrolled in, an undergraduate or graduate programme this academic year, you are not eligible
Confirm your chosen Rotary Peace Center is not in your home country if you are applying to the master's program
For a certificate application, confirm you meet the regional criterion for Makerere (Africa), Bahçeşehir (Middle East/North Africa) or Symbiosis (Asia)
Request university transcripts now if you are applying to the master's program
Book IELTS or TOEFL if your program requires an English language proficiency test score
Identify academic and/or professional referees who will submit recommendations
Use the Rotary Club Finder to contact a local Rotary or Rotaract club; many districts have a District Rotary Peace Fellowship Subcommittee Chair who can mentor the application
Research the curriculum and programs at each Rotary Peace Center and, for the master's program, decide your ranked pair
important_advice_for_students: Submit original and authentic content based on your personal experience, knowledge and motivation. Rotary states that use of generative AI content is highly discouraged and that plagiarism will disqualify an application
A club or district recommendation is optional but strongly encouraged; it is not a requirement and its absence will not disqualify you
Do not apply to more than you can genuinely complete: all applications are considered final upon submission

Do not stop at the Rotary stage. Being selected for the fellowship does not mean you have been admitted to the university, and you must apply separately for admission to the university where your Peace Center is located
For the master's program you will be asked to rank two Rotary Peace Centers; research the curriculum at each before you rank them

For the certificate program, come with a social change initiative to promote peace and development within the program region; the feasibility and impact of that initiative is a published selection criterion
All materials must be in English, so budget for certified translation of anything not already in English
Do not wait for a Rotary club to appear: build the peace and development experience and the leadership evidence first, since that is what the published selection criteria weigh
common_rejection_risks: Screened out at the first stage for failing a published eligibility requirement, including English proficiency or the bachelor's degree
Active Rotary membership, Rotaract-plus-Rotary dual membership, or employment by a Rotary club, district, Rotary International or other Rotary entity
A spouse, child, grandchild, spouse of a lineal descendant, parent or grandparent in an excluded Rotary category
Resignation from Rotary within the previous 36 months
Fewer than three years between the most recent completed degree and the intended start date
Still enrolled in, or about to enrol in, an undergraduate or graduate programme in the coming academic year
Less than three years since completing a Rotary Peace Fellowship (certificate or master's) or a Global Grant Scholarship
Applying for doctoral study, which Rotary states the fellowships may not be used for
Recommenders not entered before submission, leaving the application with missing or unverified recommendations
Plagiarism, or reliance on generative AI content, which Rotary says will disqualify an application
Certificate applicants who do not meet the published regional criterion for their chosen center
estimated_uncovered_costs: No published not-covered list exists on the official Rotary pages. Rotary states only that the fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses, so costs outside those four categories are not established either way
Visa application and issuance fees are not mentioned in the published coverage list
Personal belongings, laptop and electronics costs are not mentioned in the published coverage list
Any costs arising from a change of Rotary Peace Center after the November notification are not addressed in the published coverage list
Confirm directly with Rotary which additional expenses, if any, remain the fellow's responsibility before accepting
document_audit: Resume - required; all materials must be in English

scholarships.description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship is funded by The Rotary Foundation and awards up to 170 fellowships a year for leaders with work experience in peace and development to study at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers. Each year up to 50 fellowships fund master's degrees and up to 120 fund professional development certificate studies at partner universities. Fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses. Master's programmes run 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study, while the certificate programme is a one-year blended learning course for working professionals that includes field studies and a social change initiative. Fellowships cannot be used for doctoral study. Applications open in February and the global deadline is 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.

applicant_utility.summary: €6,500 a year for two years plus a full tuition fee waiver for international students matriculating in the first year of a Bologna Laurea Magistrale, leaving only €157.04 of regional tax, stamp duty and insurance to pay. Ranking is decided by GRE General Test scores alone, so your GRE is effectively the entire competition: below 290 in Verbal plus Quantitative or 3.0 in Analytical Writing you are excluded no matter how strong your transcript is. Because the ISEE band is €16,000-€35,000 this is a needs-linked as well as a merit award, and the financial documentation runs through ER.GO rather than the scholarship portal.

scholarships.description: The University of Bologna awards 30 International Talents @unibo study grants each year to international students who matriculate for the first time in the first year of a Second Cycle (Laurea Magistrale) degree programme. Each grant is worth EUR 6,500 gross per academic year and is awarded for two academic years, and successful applicants also receive a full tuition fee waiver, paying only EUR 157.04 in regional taxes, stamp duty and insurance premium. Selection is based on GRE General Test scores, with minimum scores of 290 in the combined Verbal and Quantitative Reasoning sections and 3.0 in Analytical Writing, together with a family economic situation within an ISEE band of EUR 16,000 to EUR 35,000. scholarships.description: The University of Padua awards up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships each year to the most deserving international candidate on each degree programme delivered entirely in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus full exemption from student fees, leaving only the regional right-to-education tax and the revenue stamp payable. There is no separate scholarship application: applying to an eligible English-taught degree programme by its admission deadline makes the candidate eligible automatically. Selection is made by the Teaching Committee of each degree programme on academic excellence and the quality of the candidate's prior academic record, with the youngest candidate preferred in a tie.

applicant_utility.summary: A €7,200 annual scholarship for non-EU citizens living abroad, rising to €8,500 for women on STEM programmes, awarded through the admission ranking of the relevant call rather than through any scholarship form, and paired with a tuition exemption for that year. The money is conditional from the start: the second instalment depends on earning at least half your first-year credits in the January and February exam sessions, or 42 credits by 10 August, and the University re-checks every September whether you keep the award. Because there is no separate application, applying to the right non-EU admission call is the entire game.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU citizens living abroad with a strong admission application to a Trento two-year or single-cycle degree programme, particularly women applying to STEM programmes where the award is larger.

Plan your first-year exam schedule around the January and February sessions, since the second instalment depends on credits earned there
Understand that failing the credit test can leave you repaying part of the award and paying fees at the applicable rate

Failing to earn at least half of the first-year credits in the January and February sessions and not reaching 42 credits by 10 August
Losing credits by the 10 August check, so the September verification does not confirm you for the next academic year
Applying as an Erasmus Mobility or visiting student, or to a Master of Arts, all of which are excluded
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Rovere or Trento beyond the scholarship, plus flights and any regional fees not swept into the tuition exemption.
document_audit: There is no scholarship file of its own, so every document you submit in the admission call serves double duty
The gender-based STEM uplift means two applicants with identical profiles can receive different amounts, so check your programme's STEM status rather than assuming the lower figure
alerts: The University states that it checks credits earned by 10 August and confirms or refuses the scholarship for the following academic year in September, so every autumn is a re-qualification

The number of scholarships is described only as limited, so do not treat admission as a guarantee of funding
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply in the non-EU citizen admission call for your programme, watch the admission ranking, then honour the credit milestones: the first instalment by December of the first year, the second by May or, failing that, by October once the 42-credit fallback is met.

The scholarship is worth EUR 7,200 per year, or EUR 8,500 per year for female students enrolled in STEM programmes, and scholarship holders are also exempted from paying tuition fees for that year. It is paid in two instalments, the second conditional on earning at least half of the credits required by the course in the January and February exam sessions. The award lasts a maximum of two years on a master's programme and three years on an undergraduate programme.

scholarships.description: The Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) is a merit award from the University of Milano-Bicocca for international students who hold a foreign qualification, are not resident in Italy and are admitted to one of the University's English-taught degree programmes. Around 100 scholarships are awarded each year, with five dedicated to each eligible English-taught course, mainly at Master's level. Each scholarship is worth EUR 10,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from tuition fees, and is renewable for a maximum of three years on Bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes and two years on Master's degree programmes. No separate application is needed: applying to an eligible programme makes the candidate automatically part of the selection, and applicants are not required to submit any further form.

scholarships.description: Talents 4 UniTo is the University of Turin's programme of 40 two-year scholarships for talented international students enrolling for the first time in a postgraduate degree without a restricted number of places taught in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 20,000 gross in total (EUR 10,000 per academic year) and holders are exempt from university tuition fees, except for the first instalment due for enrolment in each academic year. Candidates are international students who hold a qualification obtained outside the Italian system valid for admission to a postgraduate degree, do not hold Italian citizenship and are not resident in Italy. There is no separate application form: applicants are included automatically if they apply on apply.unito.it for up to two eligible programmes during the published window. Selection is carried out per programme by an Evaluation Teaching Committee on a 50-point scale with a 36-point eligibility threshold, and two scholarships are awarded per programme.

applicant_utility.summary: Three two-year UNHCR-supported scholarships for refugee students resident in 13 listed African and Asian countries, worth €7,000 a year plus exemption from essentially all enrolment charges, university accommodation and a broad package of health, permit and settlement support. Applications go through the single UNICORE portal at universitycorridors.unhcr.it by 17 April 2026 at noon Italian time, and selection has two distinct gates: a documentation and CV score that must reach 25 out of 40 just to reach the interview, and then an interview that must push you to 40 out of 80 overall. Note the trap that you must not be pre-enrolled on Universitaly at any other Italian university, which rules out hedging across corridors.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Refugee students resident in one of the 13 corridor countries who hold a bachelor's degree awarded between January 2021 and April 2026 with a GPA of 3.0 or an average of at least 24/30, and have never studied at UniTo or a UNICORE partner.

Check your degree date falls between 01 January 2021 and 17 April 2026

Verify you are not pre-enrolled on Universitaly at another Italian university, which disqualifies you
Collect the Refugee Identity card or Proof of Registration and the stamped, signed transcript with an official translation into English or Italian
common_rejection_risks: Residing in a country not on the 13-country list, which is a hard eligibility bar
A qualification awarded outside the 01/01/2021 to 17/04/2026 window
A GPA below 3.0 or an average below 24/30 after conversion
Never having been enrolled at UNITO or another UNICORE partner university - a second corridor entry is barred
Being pre-enrolled on Universitaly at another Italian university
Documents submitted in a format other than PDF or not legible, which is an explicit exclusion ground
Submitting an incomplete application, sending it by email, using multiple email addresses, or trying to modify it after submission
Missing the 10 July 2026 acceptance deadline, or failing to complete matriculation, visa and permit steps in time
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights to Italy and any costs before arrival other than the €100 first-necessity payment; the scholarship is not compatible with any other scholarship from public or private institutions.
document_audit: Everything must be PDF and legible; the transcript needs the stamp and signature of the issuing institution
Once submitted, the application cannot be modified, so assemble the file completely before you press send
Bring the Ration Card Number or Refugee Identity Card to the online interview, since it is checked
You will need an Italian bank account with an IBAN held or co-held by you, plus a signed financial contract, before the first €3,000 instalment is released
alerts: Only eligible applications proceed to the selection stages, and failing the degree-programme admission step automatically excludes you from the scholarship selection
The tie-break favours female candidates and younger candidates, so a marginally tied position can still resolve favourably
Results appear on the University portal from 22 June 2026 with no personal notification

The corridor is jointly run by UniTo, UNHCR, MAECI, Unione Pastorale Migranti, Camminare Insieme and the Commissione Sinodale per la Diaconia, so services come from several organisations rather than the university alone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply at universitycorridors.unhcr.it by 17 April 2026 at noon Italian time with all documents in legible PDF, complete the qualification evaluation and UNHCR status check, attend the online interview with your ration card or refugee ID, then check the University portal from 22 June 2026 and accept by 10 July 2026 before matriculating, obtaining the visa and arriving in Italy.

scholarships.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan), funds international students for degree programmes or a pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program at Mandarin-teaching institutions affiliated with MOE-accredited universities. Recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes or NT$28,000 for the LEP, plus one-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan, and must cover all other expenses themselves. The award period is one year for the LEP, up to four years for undergraduate and doctoral study and two years for a master's, with a five-year total cap. Applications are accepted from 1 February to 31 March each year, and the programme is open to students of any country except mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, in principle prioritising Taiwan's diplomatic partners.
scholarships.duration: Pre-degree LEP: one year. Degree programmes: undergraduate maximum four years, master's maximum two years, doctoral maximum four years. Award periods must be continuous with no breaks and cannot exceed five years in total.
scholarships.application_period: Annual window from 1 February to 31 March, applying to the Taiwan Scholarship cycle for the following academic year. The February-March 2026 window has closed; the next is expected 1 February to 31 March 2027.
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan)
eligibility: Is a high school graduate or above with an excellent academic record, of good moral character and has no criminal record.
Is not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan).
Is not an overseas compatriot student.
Has never attended an educational institution in Taiwan at the same level of degree or LEP that he/she intends to apply for.
Is not an exchange student through any cooperation agreement between a foreign university/college and an educational institute in Taiwan while receiving the Scholarship.
Has not previously had a Scholarship revoked by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.
In principle, holds citizenship of a country that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan; special consideration may be given to students from other countries.
The programme is not applicable to students from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: High school graduates or above with an excellent academic record and good moral character, who are not nationals of the Republic of China (Taiwan), are not overseas compatriot students, and have never studied in Taiwan at the same level they are applying for. In principle granted to students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, with special consideration possible for students from other countries. Not applicable to students from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau.
benefits: NT$33,000 per month stipend for degree programmes.
NT$28,000 per month stipend for the pre-degree LEP.
One-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan.
Possible university-level tuition and miscellaneous fee reductions, at each institution's discretion.
coverage: Monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes.
Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for the pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program (LEP).
One-way economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan.
Recipients are responsible for all other expenses during their stay in Taiwan; MOFA will in principle not provide any other subsidies.
Universities and colleges may offer reduced tuition and miscellaneous fees, but this is discretionary and not guaranteed.
requirements: High school graduate or above with an excellent academic record and good moral character.
No criminal record.
Not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and not an overseas compatriot student.
No prior study in Taiwan at the level being applied for.
Not simultaneously an exchange student under a university cooperation agreement while holding the Scholarship.
No previous Scholarship revocation by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.

MOFA Taiwan Scholarship Terms of Agreement
Plane Ticket Application Form for MOFA Scholarship Recipients
Health certificate meeting the required items (Form B)
required_documents: MOFA Taiwan Scholarship Application Form (published by MOFA)
MOFA Taiwan Scholarship Terms of Agreement
Plane Ticket Application Form for MOFA Scholarship Recipients
Health certificate meeting the required items (Form B)
application_method: Consult the Taiwan Scholarships and Huayu Enrichment Scholarships website, which the MOFA guidelines page names as the source of further information.
Submit the application within the 1 February to 31 March window for the relevant cycle.
scholarships.selection_notes: The Scholarship is in principle granted to students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan; special consideration may also be given to students from other countries. Selection follows the programme guidelines published by MOFA and administered for applicants through the Taiwan Scholarships portal.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
scholarships.best_fit: Students from Taiwan's diplomatic partners (and, with special consideration, other countries) seeking a funded degree or a pre-degree Mandarin year in Taiwan who can satisfy the good-character and academic-record requirements and who are not from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau.
scholarships.notes: The MOFA stipend is a living allowance, not a tuition waiver: the guidelines state that recipients are responsible for all expenses during their stay in Taiwan and that MOFA will in principle not provide any other subsidies. Tuition reduction is only discretionary ('Universities and colleges may offer Scholarship recipients reduced tuition and miscellaneous fees'). The MOFA guidelines page points to a separate Taiwan Scholarships and Huayu Enrichment Scholarships website for full application detail; that deep URL was not captured on the page as read.

scholarships.title: Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (HES), Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)
scholarships.name: Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (HES), Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)
scholarships.deadline: Applicants must apply to the authorized overseas office for their country of nationality 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'. MOE publishes no single fixed date, so no ISO deadline date can be recorded.
scholarships.description: The Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship to encourage international students to study Mandarin Chinese in Taiwan. The award funds a 2-month summer course or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course, and pays a monthly stipend of NT$28,000. Applicants must be foreign nationals aged 18 or over with an excellent academic record and good moral character, must already have applied to a Chinese language centre, and must submit their documents to the ROC overseas office for their country of nationality. MOE publishes no single deadline date, noting only that applications are made 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'.
scholarships.duration: A 2-month summer course, or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, with the deadline set by each applicant's own ROC overseas mission or representative office, which MOE says is 'usually in January or February each year'. The round for the current cycle has closed as of 2026-10-04; the next nominations are expected in January or February 2027.
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education (MOE), Republic of China (Taiwan)
eligibility: A foreign person (not an ROC passport holder and not an overseas compatriot student).
At least 18 years old.
Has graduated from secondary school or has studied at post-secondary level.
Has an excellent academic record.
Is of good moral character.
Excluded: a person currently studying Chinese in Taiwan, or who has previously undertaken a degree programme in Taiwan.
Excluded: a person who has previously received a Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, a TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship, or a Taiwan Scholarship.
Excluded: an exchange student currently studying or researching in Taiwan under an academic cooperation agreement between a Taiwan university/college and an overseas institution.
Excluded: a person currently studying or researching in Taiwan who is receiving a scholarship or financial assistance from any Taiwan government agency or any educational institution in Taiwan.

Exception: the graduation and academic records of a foreign national recommended or selected by a foreign government, institution or educational institution under an education cooperation agreement are not subject to the preceding exclusion.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Foreign nationals aged 18 or over who have graduated from secondary school or studied at post-secondary level, with an excellent academic record and good moral character. Excluded are overseas compatriot students and ROC passport holders, people currently studying Chinese in Taiwan or who previously completed a degree programme in Taiwan, people who previously received an HES, TUSA Global Ambassador Scholarship or Taiwan Scholarship, exchange students in Taiwan under a cooperation agreement, and people already studying or researching in Taiwan while holding another Taiwanese scholarship or financial aid.
benefits: Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for the duration of the awarded course (2-month summer course, or 3, 6, 9 or 12 months).
coverage: Monthly stipend of NT$28,000.
No tuition, accommodation, airfare or insurance coverage is stated on the MOE HES page.
requirements: Meet the five published eligibility conditions and avoid all five published exclusions.
Be at least 18 years old.
Have graduated from secondary school or studied at post-secondary level with an excellent academic record.
Be of good moral character.
Have already applied to a Chinese language center, and supply proof of that application.
Submit all five required document types listed by MOE.
Apply before the deadline set by the relevant ROC overseas mission.
documents: Application form
A photocopy of the applicant's passport, or other documentation adequate proof of nationality
A photocopy of proof of the applicant's highest education level and photocopies of related transcripts
A photocopy of documentary proof that the applicant has already applied to a Chinese language center (for example, a photocopy of the application-for-admission form)

required_documents: Application form
A photocopy of the applicant's passport, or other documentation adequate proof of nationality
A photocopy of proof of the applicant's highest education level and photocopies of related transcripts
A photocopy of documentary proof that the applicant has already applied to a Chinese language center (for example, a photocopy of the application-for-admission form)

application_method: Submit the required documents and apply to the authorized overseas office in the applicant's country of nationality, or to the authorized overseas office with jurisdiction over Taiwan-related matters in that country.
Alternatively, where another method is required to facilitate the implementation of a policy, applications are not subject to being made this way.
Also apply separately to the chosen Mandarin Chinese language training center, and submit proof of that application as part of the package.
scholarships.selection_notes: The scholarships are awarded through Republic of China (Taiwan) embassies and overseas missions (Representative Offices) on the basis of merit, using the guidelines each office issues for its own jurisdiction.
scholarships.program_type: Government non-degree language scholarship (Ministry of Education Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, awarded through ROC overseas missions on merit)
scholarships.best_fit: Adults aged 18 or over, from any country other than Taiwan, who want to study Mandarin at a Taiwanese university-affiliated language centre and can apply to that centre separately; the 2-month summer course suits short-stay learners and the 3-12 month awards suit longer immersion.
scholarships.notes: Important provenance issue: the stored official_source_url for this record (https://english.moe.gov.tw/cp-24-16833-23C09-1.html) is MOE's Taiwan Scholarship Program page, a different award (tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 or NTD 20,000). It does not document HES. The live HES page is https://english.moe.gov.tw/cp-24-24284-3ea37-1.html, recorded in research_notes.url_observed. Do not merge HES money figures with Taiwan Scholarship figures. An older MOE 'Study in Taiwan' brochure states an HES stipend of NTD 25,000, whereas the current MOE HES page states NTD 28,000; the current page is authoritative.

scholarships.title: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) - Ph.D. Scholarship and Stipend, Academia Sinica
scholarships.name: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) - Ph.D. Scholarship and Stipend, Academia Sinica
scholarships.deadline: The TIGP Admission Office receives online applications 'from November 1st to February 1st every year' (GMT+8). The most recent cycle, for fall 2026 entry, closed at 1 February 2026 and admissions results were announced on 20 July 2026. No application announcement for the next cycle had been posted as of 2026-10-04, so no exact calendar date is recorded.
scholarships.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP), administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes and pays a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for one further year for students who perform well. Academia Sinica also subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, but students still pay the domestic tuition rate, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder. Applications are submitted online between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8) with no application fee, and admission results are usually announced in late June or early July for enrolment the following fall.
scholarships.duration: PhD programme of three years. The stipend is paid for the first year and, for students who perform well, extended for one more year; after the scholarship/stipend allowance period, further financial support depends on the individual thesis advisor.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, 1 November to 1 February (GMT+8). TIGP posts a 'TIGP Application Announcement' each November (the 2026 one was published 2025-11-01). Admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and admitted applicants enrol in the following fall semester.
scholarships.official_source: Academia Sinica (Taiwan International Graduate Program), in collaboration with partner universities
eligibility: International applicant seeking admission to one of the fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes.
Must satisfy the general and programme-specific admission requirements published on the TIGP site for the chosen programme.
Must not already hold the degree level to which they are applying, per TIGP's general admission requirements.
No application fee is required.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: International applicants seeking admission to one of TIGP's fourteen English-taught PhD programmes. Admission is competitive and per-programme; applicants must hold a qualifying degree by enrolment and are advised to contact the TIGP Admission Office. No application fee is charged. Academic integrity is a core value of the programme and breaches can affect grades, stipend and academic standing.
benefits: Tax-free monthly stipend of NT$40,000 (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year.
Stipend extended for one additional year for students who perform well.
International tuition surcharge fully subsidised for five consecutive years, leaving students at the domestic tuition rate.
Eligibility to apply separately for the Presidential Fellowship, Research Performance Fellowship, Rising Star Fellowship, PhD Supplemental Stipend Program and Travel Grants.
coverage: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year.
Stipend extended for one further year for students who perform well.
Academia Sinica subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, so international students pay the same tuition as domestic students.
Separate TIGP awards available on top: Presidential Fellowship, Research Performance Fellowship, Rising Star Fellowship, PhD Supplemental Stipend Program and Travel Grants.
No travel, accommodation or insurance provision is stated in the core TIGP scholarship/stipend description; accommodation is budgeted separately by the programme.
requirements: Apply online through the TIGP application system between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8).
Meet the general admission requirements and the specific requirements of the chosen Ph.D. programme.
Select a thesis advisor before the end of the first year of study.
Uphold the academic integrity standards of Academia Sinica and the partner university.
Confirm tuition arrangements with the programme secretary, since the domestic tuition rate varies by partner university.
documents: Online application submitted through the TIGP online application system (no application fee).
Academic records for the qualification stated in the online application.
Documents specified by the individual PhD programme's own admissions page.
required_documents: Online application submitted through the TIGP online application system (no application fee).
Academic records for the qualification stated in the online application.
Documents specified by the individual PhD programme's own admissions page.
scholarships.english_requirement: The fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes are taught in English. No mandatory English test score is stated on the TIGP scholarship, tuition or admissions pages read on 2026-10-04.
application_method: Submit the application online through the TIGP online application system at https://tigp.apps.sinica.edu.tw/index.php between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8).
Choose one of the fourteen Ph.D. programmes and meet that programme's own admission requirements.
No application fee is required.
Contact the TIGP Admission Office (tigp@as.edu.tw) with programme or application questions.
scholarships.selection_notes: Admission is decided per Ph.D. programme. TIGP states that admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and each programme publishes its own admission criteria and evaluation. A research proposal and interview requirements are set at programme level.
scholarships.program_type: Research-based doctoral scholarship programme administered by a research institute (Academia Sinica) with partner universities
scholarships.best_fit: International master's holders seeking a funded, English-taught research PhD in Taiwan across the natural sciences, life sciences, medicine, geoscience, interdisciplinary neuroscience, AI and East Asian studies, who are willing to pay domestic-rate tuition themselves.
scholarships.notes: TIGP is not free tuition. Academia Sinica subsidises the international fee differential for five consecutive years, so students still pay domestic tuition, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester thereafter. Budgeted living costs given on the official site are approximately NT$5,000-14,000 per month for accommodation, NT$6,000-10,000 for food and NT$1,000-3,000 for study and personal requirements, so the NT$40,000 stipend is broadly adequate but not surplus. After the stipend period, support depends on the thesis advisor. TIGP also runs a separate Taiwan International Internship Program (TIIP), which is not part of this award.

scholarships.title: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)
scholarships.name: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)
scholarships.deadline: There is no single INTENSE deadline. Each participating university sets its own application window and nomination deadline per intake, and the two intakes do not coincide. Windows published by partner universities for 2027 Spring include 10 September to 12 October 2026 (NCHU), 1 to 22 October 2026 (NCU) and 21 September to 23 October 2026 (KMU), all GMT+8; for 2027 Fall, NTUT publishes a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027. Applications for several 2027 Spring intakes are open as of 2026-10-04.
scholarships.description: The International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) is a Ministry of Education initiative, run with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies to recruit international students into industry-linked degree programmes in key fields such as STEM, finance and semiconductors. Admitted students receive full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support and a monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 paid by the partner company, plus paid internships, in exchange for an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation. Applications are made to individual participating universities, which publish their own deadlines for each Spring and Fall intake, so there is no single programme-wide application date.
scholarships.duration: Typically a two-year degree programme of study plus internship, followed by employment in Taiwan.
scholarships.application_period: Two intakes a year. Spring intake first round runs from early October to late December and second round from early April to late June; the Fall intake mirrors those two rounds. Each participating university publishes its own exact dates, so no single application period applies.
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education (MOE), Republic of China (Taiwan), with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies
eligibility: Must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Must apply to a specific approved INTENSE programme at a participating university, in one of the key industry fields (commonly STEM, finance and semiconductors).
English-taught programmes: CEFR B1 English proficiency required at admission, and TOCFL Level A2 (Listening and Reading) by the end of the first semester of the second academic year.
Chinese-taught programmes: TOCFL Level B1 (Listening and Reading) required.
Some programmes restrict eligible nationalities, for example Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand; others accept students of all nationalities.
Must satisfy the participating university's own programme requirements, including academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: International students who meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan and who are recruited by a participating university for an approved INTENSE programme in a key industry field. Nationality targets differ by programme and university, with Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand commonly named, and some programmes open to students of all nationalities. English-taught programmes require CEFR B1 English at admission; Chinese-taught programmes require TOCFL Level B1.
benefits: Full tuition and credit waiver for up to two years.
One-way flight ticket to Taiwan plus initial administrative expense support.
Monthly stipend of at least NT$10,000 for up to two years, paid by the partner company.
Paid summer internships, with allowances not lower than the minimum wage under a bilingual contract.
Priority employment in Taiwan after graduation with a partner company.
coverage: Full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, with universities responsible for tuition subsidies.
One-way airfare to Taiwan.
Initial administrative expense support.
Monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 for up to two years, sponsored by the partner company.
Internship allowances not lower than the Taiwan minimum wage, under a bilingual internship contract.
Priority hiring with partner companies after graduation, at salaries not lower than average.
requirements: Meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Meet the participating university's programme-specific academic and language requirements.
Maintain grades in the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points, or equivalent to Grade A.
Accept the mandatory internship stage and the employment obligation in Taiwan.
For students already studying in Taiwan at junior or senior undergraduate level, academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct grade of at least 80 or Grade A.
documents: Official transcript of the highest level of degree completed, in Chinese or English (or a certified translation if in neither language)
Proof of language proficiency appropriate to the programme language (CEFR B1 English, or TOCFL as specified)
Passport and, where applicable, Certificate of Entry/Exit Dates from the National Immigration Agency
Future career plan
Two letters of recommendation
Passport-size photograph
Self-check for eligibility verification and declaration for international students
Any additional documents required by the individual INTENSE programme
required_documents: Official transcript of the highest level of degree completed, in Chinese or English (or a certified translation if in neither language)
Proof of language proficiency appropriate to the programme language (CEFR B1 English, or TOCFL as specified)
Passport and, where applicable, Certificate of Entry/Exit Dates from the National Immigration Agency
Future career plan
Two letters of recommendation
Passport-size photograph
Self-check for eligibility verification and declaration for international students
Any additional documents required by the individual INTENSE programme
scholarships.english_requirement: English-taught programmes require CEFR B1 English proficiency at admission, plus TOCFL Level A2 (Listening and Reading) by the end of the first semester of the second academic year. Chinese-taught programmes require TOCFL Level B1 (Listening and Reading).
application_method: Apply directly to the participating university running the specific INTENSE programme through that university's online application portal.
Meet the programme's language and academic requirements; the university handles tuition subsidy, Chinese proficiency verification and employment tracking.
Some programmes run a student nomination step before the national application deadline.
scholarships.selection_notes: The university's proposal must pass joint review by the Ministry of Education and the relevant ministries before the programme can run, and participating universities must sign contracts with companies to provide student living allowances and internships. Admission is therefore per programme and per intake, with results typically announced in the middle of the year for a September start and in mid-January for a February start.
scholarships.program_type: Industry-academia collaboration degree programme (MOE specialised class) with a compulsory employment obligation in Taiwan after graduation
scholarships.best_fit: International students from Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand who hold a qualifying degree, meet CEFR B1 English or TOCFL B1 Chinese, and are willing to accept a two-year study-and-internship pathway tied to an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation.
scholarships.notes: This is a multi-university national programme, so benefits and deadlines are not uniform. Published packages differ by university: one partner advertises full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket, initial administrative expense support and an NT$10,000 monthly industry-sponsored stipend, while another caps tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy at NT$50,000 per semester for up to two years and lists partner-company stipends between NT$10,000 and NT$15,000 depending on the job and Chinese-proficiency requirement. The scheme carries an employment obligation: the stipend duration matches the work-obligation duration and repayment may be requested if the contract is violated. The stored official_source_url and application_link both point to NTU's Overseas Compatriot and Mainland Chinese Students Advising Division, which does not host this programme.

scholarships.title: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
scholarships.name: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: The published application period on NTU's International Student Services scholarships page is April 23, 2026 - May 15, 2026, submitted through the International Degree Current Student System. The 2026 window has closed; the same window is expected for the next cycle.
scholarships.description: The NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship supports current international graduate students at National Taiwan University through a matching-fund structure: NTU waives the student's tuition, while the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor pays a monthly research-assistant salary, with published minimums of TWD 6,000 per month for two years for master's students and TWD 8,000 per month for three years for PhD students, before tax. Applicants must first secure a professor willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form, and must pass an annual review to keep the award. The published application period is 23 April to 15 May, through NTU's International Degree Current Student System, and roughly half of applicants are awarded.
scholarships.duration: Minimum monthly support for two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to passing an annual review.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, with a published application period of 23 April to 15 May for existing international degree students at NTU, applying through the International Degree Current Student System.
scholarships.official_source: National Taiwan University (NTU), Office of International Affairs
eligibility: Must be a current international graduate student at NTU.
Overseas Chinese students and Mainland Chinese students are excluded.
Must have a thesis or dissertation supervisor willing to sponsor the award and sign the university's word form.
Must pass the annual review to continue receiving the scholarship.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Current international (non-overseas-Chinese, non-Mainland-Chinese) graduate students already enrolled at NTU. Because the award is a matching fund, a graduate student also needs a thesis or dissertation supervisor who is willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form; scholars must pass an annual review to keep the award.
benefits: NTU tuition waiver.
Supervisor-paid monthly research-assistant salary, minimum TWD 6,000 per month for master's students (two years) and TWD 8,000 per month for PhD students (three years), before tax.
Renewal for up to two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to annual review.
coverage: Tuition waiver from the university.
Monthly payment from the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor as a research-assistant salary.
Published minimum monthly payment: TWD 6,000 per month for master's students for two years, and TWD 8,000 per month for PhD students for three years, before tax.
requirements: Be a current international graduate student at NTU (overseas Chinese and Mainland Chinese students are excluded).
Secure a sponsoring thesis or dissertation supervisor who will sign the word form and pay the research-assistant salary.
Submit past years' transcripts or an Advisor Evaluation Form.
Submit a recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship and a curriculum vitae.
Pass the annual review to retain the award.
documents: Past years' transcripts, or an Advisor Evaluation Form for graduate students who do not have transcripts
Recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship
Curriculum vitae
Any other documents that strengthen the application, such as award records, proof of outstanding performance or publications
A signed word form from the sponsoring professor
required_documents: Past years' transcripts, or an Advisor Evaluation Form for graduate students who do not have transcripts
Recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship
Curriculum vitae
Any other documents that strengthen the application, such as award records, proof of outstanding performance or publications
A signed word form from the sponsoring professor
application_method: Submit the application through the International Degree Current Student System during the published application period.
Ask a professor to agree to sponsor the award and have them sign the attached word form, then submit it to the College office.
About half of applicants are awarded the scholarship.
scholarships.selection_notes: Decision on NTU scholarships is made by the professors of the department to which the applicant belongs. NTU's scholarship FAQ states that about half of applicants receive scholarships. Renewal requires passing review each year.
scholarships.program_type: University merit scholarship with a matching-fund structure (university tuition waiver plus a thesis supervisor's research-assistant salary)
scholarships.best_fit: Current international master's or PhD students at NTU who have secured, or can secure, a thesis supervisor willing to sponsor them and commit to a research-assistant salary, and who can pass the annual performance review.
scholarships.notes: This is not a standalone NTU grant: it is a matching-fund scholarship, so the tuition waiver comes from the university but the monthly income comes from the applicant's own supervisor. Applicants should approach potential supervisors before applying. Do not confuse it with NTU's other awards on the same pages, which have different amounts: the NTU Scholarship for International Degree Student (undergraduate) carries a tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend of NTD 8,000, with tuition fees waived up to NTD 65,000; the NTU Loyalty Award pays NTD 100,000 for master's and NTD 200,000 for PhD places; and the Financial Assistance Grant for International Students is a tuition waiver plus a TWD 6,000 monthly stipend. The stored official_source_url points to NTU's 'Scholarships for Current Students' hub page, whose own content is stale (footer 'Last update : 2024 / 04 / 23') and which does not list this award.

scholarships.description: The NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students awards a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 together with a tuition waiver for two years to new doctoral students at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University who have outstanding grades and hold no other scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government. Recipients must submit semester transcripts and tuition payment receipts before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible, and the stipend is in principle deposited on the 10th of each month.
