important_advice_for_students: This record could not be verified and must not be relied on for an application. No official page describing this scholarship was found, so nothing about its eligibility, money, deadlines or process is established here.

Check the operative official source yourself before spending any time on this: the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program site (https://taiwanscholarship.moe.gov.tw/) publishes the Ministry of Education's Taiwan Scholarship programmes, and its Scholarship Guidelines page carries a comparison table of the MOE Scholarship, the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and the MOFA Scholarship. No scholarship for university lecturers from South and Southeast Asia appears there.

If you were told about this scholarship by a university or an agent, ask them to name the official guideline document and the administering office. Taiwan MOE scholarship rules are published as numbered administrative rules, so a citable document should exist.

Do not assume the figures of the MOE Scholarship, MOFA Scholarship or Taiwan ICDF scholarship apply to this scheme. Those three have published rates â€” for example the MOE Scholarship pays a monthly living allowance plus up to a stated tuition and miscellaneous-expense ceiling per semester â€” but they are separate programmes and none of them is this one.
Be wary of anyone charging a fee for information about this scholarship. Taiwan MOE scholarships are applied for through Taiwan's overseas representative offices, not through paid intermediaries.

referee_tracking.role: Mission officer assessing your application (MOFA Scholarship only)
referee_tracking.instructions: For the MOFA Scholarship, representative offices publish a specific assessment form and a recommendation form as PDF attachments. That is where assessment is documented, so if you hold the MOFA route, ask your mission what the assessment form requires you to supply - it is not described on the central pages. No referee or letter of recommendation requirement is published for the MOE or Huayu Enrichment Scholarships.

post_award_requirements: Remain enrolled at the university or college you were awarded to.
Keep the award period continuous with no breaks, and stay within the five-year cumulative cap across all Taiwan Scholarship awards.
Pay any tuition and miscellaneous expenses above the NTD 40,000 per semester cap to the university or college yourself under the MOE Scholarship.

Produce the TOCFL Level 3 or above result or certificate required for your programme, and where your mission did not organise testing, sit the test at your own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival and submit it to your university or college.
Participate in TOCFL at Level 3 (Band B1) or above if your award is nine months or longer.
If working, hold a working permit within the published limits of 20 hours per week and six months per semester, obtained through the Workforce Development Agency.
Abide by the signed Terms of Agreement, and report any change of course, institution or status to your university and mission as those terms require.
Do not take on any other Taiwan government or Taiwanese institutional scholarship, except the published university subsidy for the fee excess.

application_readiness_checklist: Establish first that the programme in this record exists as named. The official comparison table and guidelines read on 1 October 2026 list three programmes - MOE Scholarship, MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and MOFA Scholarship - and no 'Elite Scholarship for University Lecturers from South & Southeast Asia'. Confirm the correct programme with your mission before investing effort.
Check your country's status: it must have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or be recognised as friendly by MOFA.

Check the seven hard screens before anything else: ROC national or overseas Chinese student; already studying or already registered in Taiwan; already studied in Taiwan at the same level; exchange or dual/joint degree under a cooperation agreement; five years of Taiwan Scholarship already held; a prior revocation; or any other scholarship or subsidy from a Taiwan government agency or a Taiwanese institution.

Note the one permitted exception to the other-scholarship bar: a Taiwanese university may subsidise the outstanding amount of your tuition and other fees where that total exceeds the maximum the scholarship pays.
Find your local Taiwan Representative Office through the MOFA overseas office list or the List of MOE Overseas Offices, and get its deadline. The central site publishes no deadline.

Choose your programme on the money, not the name: MOE Scholarship pays a tuition cap of NTD 40,000 per semester plus a living allowance; Huayu Enrichment and MOFA pay no tuition and differ mainly in allowance level, duration block and - for MOFA - one-way airfare.
Budget the tuition gap. Even under the richest programme the MOE pays only up to NTD 40,000 per semester, and the published rule is that you pay the excess to the university.

If your programme is not completely taught in English, arrange a TOCFL Level 3 or above result now; if your mission does not run the test, you must sit it at your own expense by the end of your first semester after arrival.
Get the prescribed document set ready: the relevant Guidelines, the Application Form, the Terms of Agreement, and the health certificate using Items Required for Health Certificate (Form B).
Remember the two-application problem: the scholarship goes to your mission, the admission application goes to the university, and neither replaces the other.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that does not exist under that name. The record's title is not one of the three published programmes, so the most likely failure is aiming at a scholarship stream that is not open.
Nationality screen: not a foreign national, an overseas Chinese student, or from a country without diplomatic relations with Taiwan or without MOFA friendly recognition.
Already studying, or already registered to study, in Taiwan - the published exception is only for someone completing a degree and graduating that year who is moving to a higher degree.
Having already studied in Taiwan at the same level as the degree intended - this is a separate bar and it is easy to overlook.
Being admitted as an exchange or dual/joint degree student under a cooperation agreement, which is an explicit exclusion.
Holding a Taiwan Scholarship for five years in total, or having had a Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship revoked at any point.

Holding any other scholarship or subsidy from a Taiwan government agency or a Taiwanese institution - the commonest practical trap, because Taiwanese university scholarships often come as automatic add-ons.
Missing the TOCFL requirement, or sitting the test late where the mission does not organise it: the published deadline is the end of the first semester after arrival, at your own expense.
Assuming tuition is fully covered. NTD 40,000 per semester is a cap, and the excess is your liability.
Missing the mission's own deadline, because the central site publishes none and applicants naturally look there.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses above NTD 40,000 per semester under the MOE Scholarship - the published rule puts the excess on the student
All tuition and miscellaneous expenses if you hold the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship or the MOFA Scholarship, both of which publish N/A for fees
The gap between a NTD 15,000 and NTD 33,000 monthly allowance and the actual cost of living and studying in Taiwan, which the award does not benchmark to any published cost of living
Return airfare, and any airfare at all unless you hold the MOFA Scholarship - and even then only one-way economy class on direct flights
All other expenses during your stay in Taiwan under the MOFA Scholarship, which states that recipients are responsible for them and that MOFA provides no other subsidies
TOCFL test fees, which the published rule places on the applicant where the mission does not organise testing
Books, equipment, insurance and personal costs - no published component covers them
Any cost of a second scholarship you were relying on, if the other-scholarship bar applies
document_audit: The official document set is published as attachments rather than as a checklist: MOE Scholarship Guidelines (EN and CH PDFs), MOE Scholarship Application Form (PDF), MOE Scholarship Terms of Agreement (PDF), Scholarship Application Process (PDF), Items Required for Health Certificate - Form B (PDF), List of MOE Overseas Offices (PDF), a list of universities and colleges offering degree programmes taught in English, and a list of universities and colleges giving Taiwan Scholarship recipients a tuition and/or miscellaneous-expense discount. Equivalent sets are published for the Huayu Enrichment and MOFA Scholarships, including the MOFA Plane Ticket Application Form in PDF, DOC and ODT.

Check the currency of the forms: the guidelines page records an update date of 10 February 2026, reference 臺教文（五）字第1152500420A號令, and the Guidelines and the two university lists as updated on 8 May 2026. Do not use a form from an earlier cycle.

Language evidence: a TOCFL result or certificate at Level 3 or above is required for programmes not completely taught in English, and Chinese-taught degree programmes require a photocopy of a TOCFL transcript or certificate at Level 2 or above. Where your mission does not organise testing, hold budget for sitting the test at your own expense.
Health documentation: use Items Required for Health Certificate (Form B) as the specification. Do not assume a general medical report satisfies it.
The Terms of Agreement is a signed document, not a formality. Read the continuous award-period requirement and the five-year cumulative cap before you sign, because a break ends the award period.

No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published as page text. The binding sources are the dated, numbered Guidelines themselves and the prescribed forms, so obtain the current version of both from the scholarship site or your mission rather than relying on a copy someone else sent you.

submission_workflow: 1. Confirm the correct programme name and money against the published scholarship comparison table, and confirm that the scholarship you have in mind is one of the three open programmes.
2. Self-screen against the seven published ineligible categories and the country condition.
3. Locate your local Taiwan Representative Office via the MOFA overseas office list or the List of MOE Overseas Offices, and obtain its application deadline and any local additional requirements.
4. Download the current Guidelines (EN), Application Form, Terms of Agreement and Items Required for Health Certificate (Form B) for your programme, checking the update date and reference number.

5. Obtain a TOCFL Level 3 or above result or certificate if your intended programme is not completely taught in English; use the list of universities and colleges offering English-taught degree programmes to check first.
6. Complete the prescribed application form and health certificate, and submit to the Representative Office by its deadline. Do not send the application to the central office.
7. Apply separately for admission to the Taiwanese university or college, by that institution's own deadline and process.
8. If selected, sign and return the Terms of Agreement, and note the continuous award-period rule, the five-year cumulative cap, and the tuition excess you must pay yourself.

scholarships.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under its New Southbound Policy to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's programme or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder to the student as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must currently hold a lecturer or more senior post at a university in an eligible country with that position on hold, must supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through the participating university, which submits the case for MOE review. Around 100 places are awarded per academic year across a three-year cycle.
scholarships.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme under the standard MOE terms, reviewed annually. Some participating universities extend this, and Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years.
scholarships.application_period: Tied to each participating university's admission cycle, with published Fall application windows running from around mid-December to mid-March, followed by a post-admission document submission stage with its own email-stated deadline. MOE announces recipient lists around late October for Fall and late April for the African Spring intake. The AY2026/27 Fall window closed in mid-March 2026; the next is expected to open around mid-December 2026 for 2027 Fall entry.

scholarships.selection_notes: The programme is administered under the MOE Elite Scholarship Program Action Plan and was created in accordance with the New Southbound Policy Work Plan announced by the Executive Yuan in December 2016, under the MOE New Southbound Policy Talent Development Program. Priority is given to doctoral programmes. The university evaluates the admission application by department, and the MOE then reviews and determines the scholarship award. Published quota: one hundred students per academic year over three academic years, for a total of three hundred students. MOE allocates the quota, so entry is limited to new PhD students in the relevant intakes and can involve a waitlist.

scholarships.notes: Critical money nuance: NT$25,000 per month is the TOTAL award, not the amount in the student's pocket. Participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total first and split only the remainder into a monthly stipend. Taipei Tech publishes the resulting figures as around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4. Applicants should not budget on NT$25,000 of disposable income. Duration also varies by university: the standard MOE terms are 2 years for a master's and 3 years for a doctorate with annual review, while Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years and restricts it to newly admitted PhD students. The scheme is quota-limited at 100 places per academic year, and waitlisted candidates approved by MOE must repay any previously disbursed stipends. Do not confuse this with MOE's Taiwan Scholarship Program, which pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NT$40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance of NT$15,000 or NT$20,000.

applicant_utility.summary: The Faculty publishes this as a range, CHF 10,000 to CHF 15,000 per year, with no teaching duties, so treat the top of the range as an aspiration rather than an entitlement and plan living costs independently. The unusual trap is sequencing: you cannot apply until you have begun the UNIGE enrolment procedure for your chosen Master's, because the Faculty requires a scan of your UNIGE card or the 'UNIGE-Candidature: Depot de votre dossier' confirmation e-mail as proof, and the application link itself only arrives by e-mail from the beginning of January. The renewal is genuinely valuable, since the award runs a full year and then extends across the whole three or four semester programme provided you are academically successful at the end of the first semester. Twenty-one candidates were funded in the 2026 round across nine disciplines, most supported by a private Geneva foundation plus one Werner Foundation fellowship, so think of this as a small, discipline-specific award rather than a broad faculty-wide pot.

important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this as a scholarship you can apply for. The invitation is the entry requirement, and HSG states plainly that an application without an invitation is not possible. Direct the effort into the Assessment Year instead

Understand what you are actually getting. The award equals the current Bachelor tuition fees for 6 semesters, so it is a tuition award, not a living-cost grant. Living costs, rent and travel are not mentioned anywhere in the published description
Do not expect a printed figure. HSG defines the value by reference to the current Bachelor tuition fees rather than publishing a fixed amount, so the actual cash value moves with HSG's fee levels

Do not confuse this with the HSG Best Talents Programme. That is a Master's-level scheme restricted to EU/EFTA nationals and Swiss C permit holders. The Bachelor Excellence Scholarships carry no published citizenship restriction, but you must already be enrolled at HSG

Do not confuse this with the HSG Loan and Scholarship Fund or with cantonal scholarships. Those are means-tested routes with different rules, and HSG notes Swiss citizens have a legal right to cantonal scholarships

If you need support before the invitation exists, the Advice Center for Study Funding does provide subsidiary funding, loans and emergency loans, with applications generally possible from the second semester. That is a different track with its own deadlines
Submit well before the deadline. HSG states that forms which have not been duly completed will not be processed, and that the completeness check comes first, followed by a personal interview

If you need partial or total tuition-fee remission in an urgent financial situation, that is a separate route with the same 1 October and 1 March deadlines and a means test based on your and your parents' financial and familial situation

Nomination-only access is the defining constraint of this award and is often mis-stated as an open application. The supporting network spans dsm-firmenich, Givaudan, F. Hoffmann-La Roche, Merck/Sigma-Aldrich, Novartis, Syngenta and Metrohm Stiftung on the industry side, and the Universities of Basel, Bern, Geneva, Neuchatel and Zurich plus EPFL and ETH on the academic side. The page is internally inconsistent about totals, stating 95 scholars since 2013 in the introduction, 88 between 2013 and 2024 in Facts and Figures, and 48 in a historical statement by a former president; the Facts and Figures range is the most recent. required_documents is left empty because the official page does not publish a nomination dossier list.

scholarships.description: The CERN Doctoral Student Programme is a PhD-level employment contract in which doctoral students carry out cutting-edge research at CERN in collaboration with their university, in fields spanning physics, engineering, applied physics, electronics, electrical engineering, information technologies, chemical and process engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, data science and AI, and technology transfer. The programme pays a monthly net allowance of CHF 3,907 together with CERN health insurance, a possible family supplement, possible travel to Geneva on joining, and 30 days of paid leave plus two weeks of annual closure. Contracts run six months and are renewable up to three years, with the possibility of spreading the total over a maximum of four consecutive years. Eligibility is limited to nationals of CERN Member or Associate Member States, and applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey are currently excluded because the Article II.5 ceiling has been reached.

scholarships.description: The CERN Research Fellowship Programme, part of CERN's broader Graduate Programme, is an opportunity for recent PhD graduates in physics and engineering to conduct advanced research in science, technology, engineering and mathematics at CERN. It pays a monthly net stipend of either CHF 7,004 or CHF 7,425 depending on the degree and years of post-graduation experience, together with CERN health insurance for the fellow, their partner and children, a contribution to the CERN Pension Fund, and depending on individual circumstances an installation grant, family, child and infant allowances and travel to Geneva on joining. Fellows receive 30 days of paid leave per year plus two weeks of CERN's annual closure, and on-the-job and formal training including language classes. Contracts run 6 to 24 months with the possibility of extension up to 36 months. Applicants must be nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State, must hold a PhD or obtain one within six months, must respect a research-experience cap of six years for Theoretical and Experimental Physics or three years for Applied Sciences and Engineering, and must never previously have held a CERN fellow or graduate contract.

scholarships.description: IMD Business School offers a portfolio of scholarships and need-based bursaries for candidates applying to and entering its one-year full-time MBA in Lausanne. Six named scholarships were listed as open in October 2026: the MBA5 Scholarship of CHF 50,000, the Hilti STEM Scholars Program of CHF 50,000, the Nestle Scholarship for Women of CHF 40,000, the Forté Scholarship for Women of CHF 30,000, IMD MBA Merit Scholarships of up to CHF 40,000, and the BackPack Scholarship for Women with full funding. Most run throughout 2026 on an available-until-allocated basis, while the BackPack Scholarship closes on 14 July. Scholarships are applied for through the Program section of the MBA application form and are awarded to candidates who have applied for and accepted an offer, with selection based on academic and professional excellence, GMAT/GRE scores, career progression, international exposure and Assessment Day performance. Separate need-based bursaries are awarded on proven financial need and confirmed on an ongoing basis.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are already enrolled, or will be enrolled, at the University of Basel - the page's funds are for students of the university.
Decide which of the five funds you are actually applying to; the general scholarship fund, Solifonds, Legat Grobe, Lichtenstein Foundation and Health and Accident Fund have different rules.
Check the final-degree-phase rule: the university scholarship funds are awarded primarily in the final phase of a BA or MA.
If you want the Legat Grobe, confirm you are completing a biology BA/MA with a focal area in zoology/botany.
If you want the Lichtenstein Foundation medical funds, confirm you hold Swiss citizenship - this is an absolute exclusion for everyone else.
Prepare evidence of very limited resources / low-income family background, because that is the stated basis of the fund.
Aim to send the application at least a week before 15 January (spring) or 15 June (fall) so that a missing item can still be supplied.
Email sozialberatung@unibas.ch or call +41 61 207 30 38 / 20 before submitting, to confirm which fund and which documents apply to you.
important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this as a full scholarship: the largest published figure is CHF 600 per month from the university scholarship funds. Build a full living-cost budget around that number, not around tuition being waived.
No tuition waiver is published on either page, so assume you still pay University of Basel tuition fees unless Social Services tells you otherwise in writing.

The university itself says that funding studies is essentially the responsibility of the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence, and that its awards come in addition to cantonal education contributions. Do not stop applying for cantonal or home-country aid on the strength of a Basel award.
International applicants are told by the university to check what they qualify for in their home country - the Basel funds are not a substitute for home-country or cantonal support.
If you are claiming illness or accident costs, apply before treatment and attach a cost estimate; the page states this as the expected procedure.
Because no document list or format rules are published online, ask the student welfare office for the required attachments rather than guessing.
common_rejection_risks: Non-Swiss citizens applying to the Margarete and Walter Lichtenstein Foundation medical funds - citizenship is an explicit requirement.
Applying to the Legat Grobe from a degree programme other than biology with a zoology/botany focus.
Missing the semester cut-off: 15 January for spring, 15 June for fall. Late applications are not described as accepted.
Submitting a Health and Accident Fund claim only after the treatment has already happened, or without a cost estimate.
Expecting the award to cover tuition, housing or travel - none of those cost lines are published as covered.
Assuming the award replaces cantonal education contributions - the page says the university grants scholarships in addition to them.
estimated_uncovered_costs: University of Basel tuition fees - no tuition waiver is published on this page.
The large majority of living costs: the published award is CHF 200-600 per month (university funds) or CHF 500-1000 per semester (Solifonds), against Basel living costs.
Housing, food and local transport - none listed as covered.
Travel to and from Switzerland - not listed as covered.
Health insurance premiums and any illness/accident costs not covered by insurance, unless the Health and Accident Fund is granted.
Any shortfall between the award and the parents' or cantonal contribution the university says is still expected.
document_audit: No document list, file-type, size or translation rules are published on the Scholarships, Submission Deadlines or Funding from the University of Basel pages. Treat this as an official gap.
Only two document-like requirements are published, and both come from the Health and Accident Fund: a cost estimate, and submission before treatment.
Practical consequence: confirm in writing with sozialberatung@unibas.ch which attachments are needed, in which language and format, before you assemble anything.

scholarships.deadline: Fellowship positions may be advertised through calls for expressions of interest published on WIPO's career website, or via WIPO's LinkedIn or other social media channels. No fixed central deadline is published on the programme page.
scholarships.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places professionals in specialized disciplines at the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, for 12 to 36 months. Fellows are classified into four categories: translation fellows in the PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, legal case manager fellows in the WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, visiting and research fellows in the Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, and other specialized fellows. Applicants must hold at least a first-level university degree, with additional requirements such as professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies depending on the category. Fellows receive a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience, comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance largely paid by WIPO, relocation assistance covering travel at the start and end of the fellowship, assistance with visa formalities, 10 official holidays plus 2.5 days of annual leave per full month, and access to WIPO Academy training with up to six study leave days a year. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website and LinkedIn.

applicant_utility.summary: This record is an umbrella, not one scholarship: pick a specific Erasmus Mundus consortium that includes an Austrian institution and apply to that consortium directly, because EACEA and the Commission take no applications. Deadlines sit with each consortium and typically fall between October and January for a September start, so your transcripts, references and language evidence have to be ready in early autumn. The money is one monthly allowance of EUR 1 400 for the whole programme, so compare it against the cost of living in each consortium city rather than the two-year total, and remember the allowance is trimmed if you spend long stretches in your own country of residence.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor's students and recent graduates with a strong grade record who want a genuinely two-country master's and can give one consortium application their full autumn.

Prepare an English bachelor's transcript and degree certificate, or documented proof of expected graduation
Ask referees early, as consortium letters are usually uploaded with the application rather than requested afterwards
Write the motivation letter to the consortium's published criteria instead of a generic statement
Budget visa, travel and installation costs separately, since the single allowance also has to absorb them
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the wrong body - there is no central Erasmus Mundus application form
Assuming one Europe-wide deadline and missing the consortium's own closing date
Being in the final year of a bachelor's without evidence you will graduate before the programme starts
Overlooking the compulsory mobility rule, which requires study in at least two countries and none of them your country of residence
Applying with a previous EMJM scholarship already held, which disqualifies you from a second award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Residence permits, extra health and liability insurance, and the gap between EUR 1 400 a month and living costs in the more expensive consortium cities; installation and visa costs come out of the same allowance.
document_audit: Academic records normally need certified English translations issued or verified by the degree-awarding institution
Check the consortium's scholarship document list separately from its admission list - scholarship files often add a CV, motivation letter and references
Keep proof of your last completed semester and, if asked, a residence certificate for the programme-country or partner-country classification
alerts: The 10% per-nationality cap means applicants from heavily represented countries face the tightest odds
There is one round per intake, so a missed consortium deadline usually means waiting a full year
Check each programme page for scholarship availability before investing effort, since not every catalogue entry still funds scholarships
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit online through the consortium's own portal, which handles both admission and the scholarship request; the consortium runs selection, contacts shortlisted candidates for anything extra, then issues the admission and award decision.

scholarships.name: CEU Scholarships (Central European University) — Vienna

applicant_utility.summary: If you want CEU money you must apply in Round 1 or Round 2, because institutional aid stops after the 2 February 2027 deadline and later rounds only admit self-funding students - that single rule kills more applications than academic records do. The award you are competing for depends on level: doctoral candidates are automatically considered for a scholarship that covers full tuition plus EUR 2,002 gross a month for 48 months, while master's applicants are typically looking at 50 to 80 percent of tuition plus EUR 300 to 750 a month, and full tuition at master's level is explicitly exceptional. Build the application around two recommendation letters that referees submit themselves, since a referee who never uploads leaves your file incomplete no matter how strong the rest looks.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong applicants to a full-time CEU master's or doctoral programme who can complete a full file - including both referees - by the first or second admission round.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm which of the four admission rounds applies to your citizenship and programme, and whether the programme runs its own calendar
Tick the Funding section of the application form - leaving it blank removes you from aid consideration
Ask your undergraduate institution to send transcripts and diplomas itself, or through a transcript platform, because copies sent by students are rejected
Register both referees and submit the application early enough that their letters arrive within the one-week window
Prepare an English evidence pack: test score or an official letter confirming your degree was taught exclusively in English
Have a SEPA euro account ready, since stipends are paid into one and only after you physically arrive in Vienna
common_rejection_risks: Applying in Round 3 or 4, when financial aid is already closed
Leaving the Funding section of the application form blank
A referee who never submits, or who submits after the one-week window
Uploading transcripts and diplomas yourself instead of having the issuing institution send them
Missing the ECTS floor of 180 for a two-year master's or 240 for a one-year master's
Being simultaneously enrolled elsewhere while receiving CEU aid without documented leave of absence
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: At master's level the uncovered share of tuition when the award covers 50 to 80 percent, plus the gap between the EUR 300 to 750 stipend and Vienna living costs; also a EUR 30 application fee, a EUR 500 registration fee (EUR 1,000 to 3,000 for selected MS programmes), the Austrian student union fee, and health and liability insurance.
document_audit: Diploma supplements must be accompanied by the diploma itself, and both need English versions

Recent test scores only: TOEFL and IELTS must be no older than two years, Cambridge and PTE within five, Duolingo within one
alerts: Applications cannot be edited after submission apart from contact details, so submit only when the file is final
PhD stipends are taxable self-employed income in Austria and require SVS registration and social security contributions
Late arrival does not generate retroactive stipend payments - the money starts from your arrival date on campus
Expect an interview if you are pre-selected, and write your materials without generative AI beyond light proofreading
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online per programme with the Funding section completed, pay the EUR 30 fee, let the referees upload, then track the decision in the Applicant Portal against the round's notification window.

scholarships.name: NL Scholarship (formerly known as Holland Scholarship)
scholarships.funding_period: one-off award paid in the first year of study

applicant_utility.summary: The NL Scholarship is a one-off EUR 5,000 payment in your first year, awarded by the Dutch institution you apply to rather than by a central body, so the deadline, the eligible programmes and the extra criteria all live on that institution's website. It is explicitly not a full-tuition scholarship, so treat it as a first-year top-up and prove separately that you can fund the rest. Because the participating-institution list is refreshed every year, confirm your programme is on the current list before you build your budget around the award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA students admitted to a full-time Dutch bachelor's or master's programme who can cover most costs themselves and want a modest first-year contribution.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the current participating-institutions list and your programme's eligibility for this academic year
Open the institution's own scholarship page and note its closing date; it is the only deadline that counts
Prepare whatever the institution requires (typically a motivation letter and financial plan) alongside your admission application
Confirm you hold no degree from a Dutch institution before applying
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a programme the institution does not include in its NL Scholarship round
Assuming the national 1 November opening date is also the deadline and missing the institution's earlier closing date
Budgeting as if EUR 5,000 covered tuition; the official page states it is not a full-tuition scholarship
Holding a prior degree from a Dutch institution, which disqualifies you outright
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition (which for non-EEA students is typically far above EUR 5,000), living costs, insurance and travel are all uncovered; the award is a one-year contribution only.
document_audit: Each institution decides its own document set, so never reuse another university's checklist; read your own institution's page before uploading anything
Where the institution asks for a financial plan, it must cover the full duration of the programme, not just year one
alerts: The award was renamed from Holland Scholarship to NL Scholarship; older pages under the old name may quote outdated rules
The participating list changes every academic year, so last year's list is not evidence that your programme still takes part
Nuffic's Integrity Code of Conduct excludes applicants involved in financial misconduct, money laundering, terrorist financing or related conduct
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission to an eligible programme at a participating institution, indicate or tick the NL Scholarship in that institution's own application, upload what the institution asks for, and wait for the institution's decision.

scholarships.title: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS)
scholarships.name: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS)
scholarships.funding_period: one-off award for the 2027-2028 academic year

applicant_utility.summary: For the September 2027 start the Faculty of Science has exactly one Amsterdam Merit Scholarship, worth 26,125 EUR, and the university is explicit that it is cash paid in instalments rather than a fee waiver, so you must still budget the full mandatory tuition fee and the institution contribution on top. That makes the award a living-cost subsidy, not a free ticket, and it means the faculty is looking for candidates whose alternatives are constrained by money, not just candidates with the best CV. Because the application needs a motivation letter of at most 500 words plus a CV, treat those two documents as the whole contest: the faculty selects in March and tells you in April, so you will know the outcome well before you have to arrange funds for August.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Ambitious master's applicants, including to the Artificial Intelligence programme in the Faculty of Science, with strong academic records and a genuine funding gap that the award would close.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the Faculty of Science page and the AMS portal for the exact opening date, generally mid-December to mid-January
Write a 500-word motivation letter that covers academic achievement, leadership, motivation and your actual financial situation
Apply for admission to the programme as well, since the scholarship is linked to being accepted for the 2027-2028 intake
Prepare a CV that evidences extracurricular engagement, which is an explicit selection criterion
Check whether you hold, or are applying for, other funding, because the AMS is not combined with other support for the same purpose
Have the full tuition fee and living costs covered from somewhere else, since the award alone will not cover them
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the AMS waives tuition, when the faculty states it cannot be used as a tuition fee waiver
Missing the 15 January Faculty of Science deadline, with no chance to top up an incomplete file later
Leaving the motivation letter over 500 words, which breaks an explicit requirement
Applying for funding for a second year without checking the 40 ECTS first-year condition
Being enrolled in a preparatory or foundation year at a Dutch institution, which makes you ineligible
Counting a commercial student loan as available money, which removes the financial-need criterion
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The full mandatory non-EU tuition fee and institution contribution, plus rent, food, insurance and transport in Amsterdam; the AMS is paid in two instalments in early December and January, so no early payout is available.
document_audit: Start assembling the CV and motivation letter before the portal opens, since December and January are the window
If the programme admission process already gives you an acceptance decision, include it, as the selection runs in March with notifications in April
Keep any evidence of other funding applications separate and clear, since double-funding for the same purpose is excluded
alerts: Only complete applications are considered, so a missing motivation letter or CV ends the application
There is one Faculty of Science award for the 2027-2028 intake, so the odds are a single decision, not a ranking
The Amsterdam Graduate Scholarship and other UvA funds follow their own rules and processes, so do not assume the AMS process applies to them
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to your master's programme, submit the AMS application with the 500-word motivation letter and CV through the portal by 15 January, and track the faculty's selection in March and notification in April.

scholarships.name: Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) — Holland Scholarship & Talent Programmes

applicant_utility.summary: The Holland Scholarship or NL Scholarship is a flat EUR 5,000 contribution towards studying in Rotterdam, and IHS is blunt that it is not a full-tuition scholarship, so treat it as a discount on a bill you will largely pay yourself. Because each school runs its own round and its own deadline, the practical move is to work backwards from the school: get your admission letter first, then file the scholarship documents by that school's date, which at IHS is 25 April for the programme application due 15 April. The IHS document list is exacting on money, asking for a bank statement covering twelve times EUR 1,250 plus a statement of how much you and your family will personally contribute, so start that financial evidence early because it is the part that stalls applicants.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA master's students who already have or will soon have an unconditional admission letter from an EUR school, and who can show genuine financial need alongside a strong grade list.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify which EUR faculty or school runs your programme and open its own scholarship page, not only the central list
Secure the unconditional admission letter first, since it is a mandatory attachment
Ask your university for a certified copy of the bachelor degree including the grade list rather than a photocopy
Prepare a motivation letter that clearly outlines the career path after the programme, as the school requires
Prepare the financial file: a bank statement from you, your parents or your sponsors, plus a statement of the maximum contribution you can make
Note the decision date for your school, at IHS 3 May, and plan visa and housing applications around it
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for the central EUR deadline instead of the school-level date, which varies
Missing the unconditional admission letter requirement by applying only for a conditional offer
Submitting a CV-style motivation letter without the required career path outline
Providing uncertified grade lists, which the school requires to be certified
Assuming the EUR 5,000 pays tuition, when the school states it is not a full-tuition scholarship
Overlooking the required statement of your own contribution, which is an explicit document
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Most of the non-EEA tuition fee, plus rent, food, transport, health insurance and visa costs; the bank statement requirement of twelve times EUR 1,250 gives a rough floor for the living-cost need the award does not cover.
document_audit: The degree and grade list need certification, so allow a week or two at your home institution
Bank statements from parents or sponsors are accepted, but the statement of your maximum contribution must still be explicit
If your admission letter is conditional, hold the application until it becomes unconditional rather than submitting an ineligible file
alerts: One award per school per round, so this is a single-slot competition decided once
Deadlines move per school, and IHS already publishes the 2027 dates while other faculties may not yet
Check the faculty-level pages for additional EUR funds such as the Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship, which covers tuition and support on a different scale
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the programme at your EUR school by its deadline, then submit the NL Scholarship documents with the admission letter and financial evidence to that school by its own scholarship deadline, and await the school's decision date.

That sequencing is the trap: the scholarship clock starts only when the admission letter exists, so it rewards applicants who applied for admission early. The award can be received only once in a lifetime, and the university plainly states the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat the VUFP as a tuition solution, not a study budget: the university's own wording is that it covers tuition only and gives no allowance for rent, food or insurance, so you must already be able to self-finance living costs in Amsterdam before you accept. The binding constraint is admission rather than the scholarship itself, because you need at least a conditional Master's offer before the VUFP form even becomes available, which is why VU tells you to apply for admission by 1 December 2026. The application is one-shot: resubmission is not allowed, and a single unanswered question or a missing transcript makes the file incomplete and therefore never evaluated. One VUFP place is reserved for a former Semester in Amsterdam student, so alumni of that programme should flag their application to the Semester in Amsterdam team.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of a country outside the EU/EES/Switzerland and are required to pay tuition fees; the award is void if you become a non-fee-payer

Check you meet the new minimum academic standards: GPA 3.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale, a first or high second class degree, or an equivalent average, typically 75%+ in India, 80-85%+ in China, or 8.0/10+ on a 10-point CGPA scale

Be in position to pay tuition fees. Do not plan on money you do not have, because the award is a 50% reduction rather than a full waiver and any uncovered balance must be paid by the payment deadline

Know your application window is tiny. It opens on the day of the Notification of Selection Results and closes four days later at 23:59 CET, so set a reminder for the Notification and check the page daily
Prepare no extra documents: LiU states no additional documents are needed to support the scholarship application
Plan the 75% course-pass rule from day one of the programme, because you need 45 completed credits from your programme by 1 July to keep the award the following year
Start the Swedish residence permit process early enough to have it in time for the start of studies, since failing to do so rescinds the scholarship
important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this as a scholarship you chase. Eligibility is decided for you by five fixed conditions, four of which are about your admission application rather than your qualities. Get the ranking, the deadline and the documentation right first

Rank Chalmers-free: put Linköping first. LiU states you must choose a Linköping University master's programme as first priority ranked number 1 of 4. A strong application that ranks another university first is ineligible, however good the grades

Plan for 50%, not 100%. LiU says fees are normally reduced by 50%, that the percentage is decided year by year, and that the scholarship may cover only part of the fee, in which case you must pay the remainder by the payment deadline. It also states the scholarship can be revoked

Assume your money must cover everything except half the tuition. There is no published living-cost allowance, no travel coverage and no stipend. Gothenburg or Linköping rent, food, insurance and travel are on you

Treat the 75% course-pass rule as a hard deadline, not a target. LiU assesses only results registered on 1 July of the regular academic year, and explains that studying 60 credits a year means you need 45 completed credits from your programme by 1 July or you lose the scholarship. Over-examining in a later semester does not help

Do not stack the Swedish Institute scholarship with this one. LiU states that applicants awarded a scholarship by the Swedish Institute will subsequently have their Linköping University scholarship rescinded. If the SI is your better route, take the SI

Do not skip the residence permit. LiU states applicants unable to acquire a permit from the Swedish Migration Board in time for the start of studies or the registration deadline will have the scholarship rescinded
Watch your fee-paying status. If your status changes to that of a non-fee-payer the scholarship is no longer valid, and LiU requires you to inform the University in writing

Be realistic about volume. LiU states it offers a limited number of scholarships and reserves the right to decide year by year how many are offered, what percentage, and the merit process itself where more eligible applicants than places exist
Do not overshoot 30 credits a semester without budgeting. LiU states the scholarship or fee normally covers 30 credits per semester and that additional courses beyond that carry an additional fee
Expect the result on the university page, not by email. LiU publishes the list of recipients on the scholarships page, and for 2026 the published date was 10 April

applicant_utility.summary: There is no central Erasmus Mundus application: you apply to one consortium, for one programme, through that programme's own website, which means each programme is a separate deadline, a separate document set and a separate selection panel. The money is a single published rate - EUR 1,400 per month for the full duration of the programme, up to 24 months - plus coverage of participation costs and travel, visa, installation and subsistence, so tuition cannot be charged to you if you hold the scholarship. Because the EU caps any one nationality at 10% of a consortium's scholarships, students from heavily applied countries face the hardest competition, so apply to more than one programme rather than betting on a single consortium. Read each catalogue entry carefully, since the catalogue itself warns that some listed programmes offer no scholarships because their EU funding has run out and only the name is being used temporarily.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year or recent bachelor's graduates who want a multi-country European master's and can absorb a full-time, application-heavy process between October and January.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist several programmes from the EACEA catalogue and confirm on each programme's own website whether it currently offers Erasmus Mundus scholarships, not just the Erasmus Mundus label
Diarise each consortium's deadline separately - the October-January window is a norm, not a shared cutoff
Check the mobility design: at least two study periods in two countries you have not lived in, each of at least one semester or 30 ECTS
Confirm you will hold your bachelor's degree before the programme starts, since enrolment depends on it
Open the programme's Student Agreement template on its website so you know the obligations before you accept
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the European Commission instead of the consortium, which is never the route
Assuming every catalogue programme still funds scholarships; some are in a temporary name-use period
Being over the 10% nationality cap within a consortium without realising the quota exists
Applying for a programme whose mobility design conflicts with your personal situation
Missing the individual consortium deadline because the only date you tracked was the general October-January window
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Costs beyond the monthly allowance and the participation, travel, visa, installation and subsistence coverage, including anything the consortium charges non-scholarship holders, pre-departure relocation from home, and personal spending.
document_audit: Each programme's website publishes its own document list and its own steps for applying with and without a scholarship - read both, because the scholarship route often adds an evaluation stage

scholarships.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes are master's degrees jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, plus academic and non-academic associated partners. The European Commission's Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, maintained by EACEA and updated annually, lists the master's programmes currently supported by the EU; the stored row corresponds to the catalogue's Sweden country facet. Master's-level students from all over the world may apply, and Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available for outstanding students at participating programmes. Applicants apply directly to the consortium running their chosen programme, not to the European Commission.

scholarships.name: Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship (50%)

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold international student status. Domestic students are not eligible and the University files this scholarship under the International Student category

Check the academic threshold against the qualification you are using as the basis of admission: undergraduate needs a minimum ATAR of 99 or international equivalent, or the overall GPA route of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale; postgraduate needs the 6.7 GPA or a comparable score, since the ATAR 99 route is undergraduate only
Confirm the degree is CRICOS registered

Confirm the degree length: at least 96 units / 2 years equivalent for a bachelor, at least 72 units / 1.5 years equivalent for a master, measured after credit or RPL is applied. If your credit cuts you below the threshold, you are out

Check the Excluded Programs list before you commit. It removes 11 undergraduate degrees including Dentistry, Medical Studies, Midwifery, Physiotherapy, Veterinary Bioscience and Speech Pathology, and 18 postgraduate degrees including Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, all the MBAs, all the Graduate Entry allied health degrees and the three applied Master of Psychology programs
Confirm you are not an Australia Awards recipient
Confirm you are not an International Sponsored Student with a sponsor tuition fee waiver equal to or greater than the scholarship value. If you are, the fee waiver applies instead of the scholarship
Plan for the other half. You pay 50% of tuition for the whole program, and nothing of living costs
Download the correct application form from 24 August 2026: the general form, or the SATAC form if you are applying through SATAC
Submit early. The process is rolling and allocations are limited, so the pool of places is smallest late in the cycle
After you start, know the continuation rule: a minimum Program Term GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale in every compulsory Study Period
important_advice_for_students: Check the Excluded Programs list first, before anything else. It is long, it is programme-specific, and it eliminates entire professions. Applying to a Doctor of Medicine, a Bachelor of Dental Surgery, any MBA, or any Graduate Entry physiotherapy, occupational therapy, midwifery or nursing degree makes this scholarship impossible regardless of your grades

Understand the credit trap. The minimum lengths are measured after the application of any credit or RPL. A three-year bachelor with 48 units of credit may drop below 96 units and remove your eligibility. Model this before applying

Do not assume 50% means affordable. You still pay half the international tuition fee for the full program, on top of living costs, accommodation, insurance, visa and flights. Adelaide University publishes no living-cost component for this award

Do not stack it with a sponsor waiver. The University states a student cannot receive a scholarship and a sponsor tuition fee waiver concurrently, and that where a sponsor waiver of equal or greater value applies, the waiver amount is what counts

Apply early even though no priority is published. Because review is rolling and offers stop when allocations are exhausted, a complete application in the first weeks of the cycle is strictly better than the same application in the last

For postgraduate applicants, note the ATAR 99 route does not apply to you. The undergraduate-only ATAR 99 threshold and the GPA threshold are listed separately, and only the GPA or comparable score applies to you

Get your comparable score argument in order. A minimum overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale, or a comparable score, must be demonstrated in the qualification used as the basis of admission. Prepare the evidence of that comparison rather than assuming it is self-evident

Protect the award from day one. The continuation condition is a Program Term GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale in each compulsory Study Period. A single term below can suspend the scholarship, and the suspension mechanism is not simply a make-up opportunity

Note the recovery rule, which is unusual and worth understanding. If your overall GPA falls below the minimum, the scholarship is not applied to the next invoice; if your GPA returns to the minimum or above, it recommences and is applied to the next invoice. So a dip is not necessarily permanent, but you will pay the intervening invoice
Use the free academic support. The University points to the Student Academic Learning Support team and its free academic support services, which is directly relevant to holding the 5.5 GPA
common_rejection_risks: Being a domestic rather than international student
Applying to an Excluded Program, which covers most clinical, allied health, veterinary and business degrees
A qualification length below 96 units / 2 years equivalent for a bachelor, or below 72 units / 1.5 years equivalent for a master, after credit or RPL is applied
An undergraduate result below a minimum ATAR of 99 or international equivalent, and not meeting the alternative overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale
A postgraduate result below an overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale or comparable score, and mistakenly relying on the undergraduate-only ATAR 99 route
Being an Australia Awards recipient
Being an International Sponsored Student entitled to a sponsor tuition fee waiver equal to or greater than the scholarship value
Attempting to hold this scholarship concurrently with a sponsor tuition fee waiver
Applying to a degree that is not CRICOS registered
Not being a new student, since the scholarship is for students commencing the degree
Missing the 24 August 2026 opening, or applying after allocations have been exhausted, since the process is rolling and the award is described as having limited places
Falling below the minimum Program Term GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale in a compulsory Study Period, which can suspend the scholarship

Books, equipment, course materials and field-trip costs
Any fees for credit or RPL assessment, which is relevant because credit affects your eligibility as well as your fee load

scholarships.deadline: Applications open from Monday 24 August 2026; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with scholarship offers made throughout the recruitment cycle until all allocations have been exhausted.
scholarships.description: The Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship is a merit award for international students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Adelaide University, offering a 50% tuition fee reduction over the standard full-time duration of the degree. Places are limited and allocated on merit by a selection panel reviewing applications on a rolling basis through the recruitment cycle. Applicants must be international students applying to a CRICOS-registered bachelor or master degree that is not on the Excluded Programs list, and must have an ATAR of 99 or an overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale as the basis of admission. Recipients must maintain a minimum Program Term GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale in each compulsory Study Period.

Undergraduate only: minimum ATAR of 99 (or international equivalent)
Undergraduate and postgraduate: minimum overall Grade Point Average of 6.7 (on a 7.0 scale) or comparable score in the qualification used as the basis of admission

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are an international student: not an Australian or New Zealand Citizen and not an Australian Permanent Resident
Choose a program of at least 16 units. Anything shorter is not a Relevant program

Check the excluded program list before you commit. It excludes 38 named programs, including Medicine, Nursing, Midwifery, Dentistry, Veterinary Science, Physiotherapy, Psychology majors, every Master of Psychology and Master of Clinical Psychology, Counselling, Speech Pathology, the Master of Business Administration, and all the dietetics, audiology and pharmacy pathways
Confirm the program is a full-time undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program, since research degrees are not Relevant programs
Confirm you hold no other UQ scholarship, tuition fee reduction or rebate. The only permitted exception is the UQ English Language Scholarship
Confirm you do not hold a full scholarship or sponsorship from another organisation. A partial one does not disqualify you, but it is considered at UQ's discretion
Meet the program entry rank and the English language proficiency requirements for your program
Plan to enrol full time at 8 units per semester unless your study plan requires otherwise
Do not write a scholarship application. There isn't one. Your UQ program application is the application
Be ready to accept the UQ program offer and pay the tuition deposit, because the scholarship is only confirmed once you do
Note that you will be notified at your Unconditional Offer point, or once all Conditional Offer conditions are met, and that you will be told an acceptance deadline at that point
If you need more time, prepare a written extension request with a compassionate or compelling reason, addressed to the email in the scholarship offer
important_advice_for_students: Understand this is a quarter off, not a full ride. You pay 75% of the international tuition fee for the whole program, plus all living costs, accommodation, insurance, visa and flights. UQ publishes no living-cost component for this award

Check the excluded list first. It is unusually long and it removes entire professional pathways, not individual majors. If you are heading into medicine, nursing, midwifery, dentistry, veterinary science, physiotherapy, psychology, counselling, speech pathology, dietetics, audiology, pharmacy or an MBA, this scholarship is very likely not for you
Note the 16-unit floor. Short programs and micro-credentials are not Relevant programs, so the scholarship cannot attach to them

Do not waste time on a scholarship application. UQ states you are automatically assessed when you apply to study a program. The only thing you control is the quality of your program application and how you score in the pool

Plan for the deposit. The scholarship is confirmed only once you accept the UQ program offer and make the tuition deposit payment. If you were counting on the 25% to fund the deposit, that is a real cash-flow problem, so check the deposit amount against your own money

Treat the 25% as fragile across program changes. If you change program, your eligibility is re-evaluated against the excluded list at the time of the change. A change into a clinical, psychology or business program can remove the award

Treat deferral as ending the award in practice. Deferring commencement may make you no longer eligible, and eligibility is re-evaluated for the new semester if applicable. Do not defer assuming the scholarship follows you
Do hold the GPA that UQ's Academic Progression Procedure requires. Satisfactory Academic Progress is the defined trigger, and failing it is an express ground for termination

Be honest about external funding. A full external scholarship or sponsorship disqualifies you outright. A partial one leaves you at UQ's discretion, so if you are holding one, expect it to be examined

Know your rights on timing. You can request an extension in writing to the email in the scholarship offer, with a compassionate or compelling reason, and it is considered case by case with an outcome notified within a reasonable timeframe. That is a real mechanism, but it is discretionary, so ask early

Not enrolling in a relevant program in the proposed semester of commencement
Committing serious misconduct

scholarships.description: The UQ International Excellence Scholarship is a 25% reduction in tuition fees per semester awarded to high-achieving international students commencing a full-time undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program at The University of Queensland in 2027. There is no separate application: UQ states "You don't need to apply for this scholarship. When you apply to study a program at UQ, you're automatically assessed for this scholarship." Offers are issued with the unconditional offer letter or once all conditions of a conditional offer are met, and the reduction is applied before the tuition fee due date each semester. The number of awards may vary, and the scholarship is valid only for the program and commencement semester named in the offer letter.

scholarships.name: Melbourne Research Scholarship (MRS)

applicant_utility.summary: You never apply for this scholarship - you apply for the graduate research course, and if that application lands before the course's closing date you are automatically considered and receive confirmation within seven days. What decides the outcome is panel ranking on your previous academic results and research potential, so a strong transcript plus evidence of research output such as refereed publications, a same-level degree or relevant professional experience is the lever to pull. Domestic students receive the Research Training Program fee offset with their course offer, while stipend-and-fee-offset offers are issued separately but around the same time.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving research-degree applicants, domestic or international, who want full fee remission plus a living stipend without a separate scholarship deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Find the closing date of your target graduate research course and submit well ahead - that date is your real scholarship deadline

scholarships.description: The Melbourne Research Scholarship is offered to high-achieving domestic and international students enrolling in, or already enrolled in, a graduate research degree at the University of Melbourne. It exists in three forms: a Fee Offset award, a Stipend award, and a combined Stipend and Fee Offset award. No separate application is required: applicants who apply for a graduate research course by that course's closing date are assessed automatically. Around 350 scholarships are available, and selection is by ranking on academic results for previous study and research potential.

applicant_utility.summary: Deakin has folded its country-specific international scholarships into a single Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship, so do not plan around a dedicated South Asia round - the outcome is now either 100% or 50% of tuition fees and you will not know which until you are told. This one is genuinely application-based rather than automatic: unlike most of Deakin's international scholarships, it needs the International Scholarship Program form, a 300-word personal statement and two references, emailed to Deakin International Admissions at least a month before your program starts. The academic bar is at least an 85% average with several published reference points (85% overall in CBSE, ICSE or State Board Year 12; 10 overall in GCSE/A Level; 32 in the IB Diploma; or 80% across the first four semesters of an undergraduate degree), and Deakin warns that stronger results may be needed because competition is strong. Winning also commits you to the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program, which is a requirement of the scholarship, not an optional extra.

The application is almost entirely evidence-driven: an unanswered question or an unevidenced claim is simply not assessed, so budget your time for uploads rather than prose. Because you must already hold an offer by the deadline, sequence your admission application first and treat the scholarship form as the second half of the same submission.

applicant_utility.summary: This scholarship is decided by whichever SNU college or school you apply to, not by a central committee, which means your admission documents are doing double duty as your scholarship application and there is nothing extra to submit. The two hard gates are both institutional: you must be a non-Korean applicant enrolled or graduated from one of SNU's currently listed eligible countries, and you must be applying to a college or school that is actually participating in the GSFS for that semester. Both lists change every semester, so a scheme that was open to your country and your department last intake may not be this one - check the guide SNU's Office of Global Affairs circulates each semester rather than relying on last year's information. The money is full tuition exemption for up to four semesters plus a minimum of 500,000 KRW a month for living costs, with the exact amount varying by major, but there is no published airfare or insurance component so you will need to fund your own travel. Roughly 20 people get it each semester, and if you are also selected for the SNU President Fellowship Program you must pick one and give up the other.

scholarships.english_requirement: KAIST's official language of communication and instruction for international students is English. All applicants must provide at least one English proficiency test score, and the scores must be valid as of the online application deadline. Published minimums: TOEFL iBT 83 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026); IELTS Academic 6.5 band; TOEIC 720 (Listening & Reading, TOEIC Public Testing Program); TEPS 326. TOEFL institutional code 0195, department code 99; Home Edition accepted; iBT MyBest Scores are NOT accepted; IELTS Online is accepted but IELTS One Skill Retake is NOT accepted; test scores from Institutional Testing Program (ITP) are NOT accepted. Exemption: no EPT score is required if you hold citizenship of, or have physically studied and completed a bachelor's-equivalent or higher qualification at an institution physically located in, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Malta, New Zealand, St Kitts, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad and Tobago, the U.K. or the U.S.A. A further exemption applies if you hold citizenship of one of a listed group of countries AND have physically studied and completed a qualification equivalent to a bachelor's degree or higher in English as the medium of instruction at an institution physically located in one of those countries, in which case a certificate from the school attended indicating English as the medium of instruction (e.g. English Lecture Certificate) must additionally be provided. Applicants expecting to graduate from regular KAIST degree programmes in the semester before the intended course also do not need to provide a score. Programs that do not require an EPT score: GDI-ITTP track, KINS-KAIST.

KAIST states that 94 percent of its international students benefit from the scholarship and that the scholarship rate may vary by student.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-tuition-for-four-years award attached to UIC admission, not a separate competition: submit the undergraduate application and admitted international students are considered automatically, with the offer letter arriving inside the admission packet. The waived amount equals the International Students Track tuition of 8,202,000 KRW per semester (2026), so you still need funds for miscellaneous fees (about 56,000-61,000 KRW per semester), housing, food and personal costs. The one continuing condition is your semester GPA - the scholarship is re-checked each semester and lapses in the following semester if you fall below the required level.

GED, home-schooled or cyber-schooled certificates, which UIC does not treat as a high school diploma

Un-notarized kinship or parent-relationship documents, especially for applicants with Chinese nationality

applicant_utility.summary: The KOICA Scholarship Program runs through your own government, not through a Korean university: your KOICA overseas office or Korean Embassy screens and nominates you in the first round, and only nominated candidates reach the university screening. Budget months for the full chain - an e-mail application package with a completed Document Checklist, an on-site interview at the embassy or office, university document screening and interview, original documents mailed by DHL, a local medical check-up, and a final medical check-up in Korea before enrolment. Because KOICA sets no central deadline, the only date that matters is the one your own overseas office or embassy publishes.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career government officials from KOICA partner countries on the OECD DAC list who can secure a government nomination and sixteen to seventeen months of study leave for a master's in Korea.

common_rejection_risks: Applying without the government nomination or to a university course before the embassy round closes
Having previously held a Korean government degree scholarship (a bachelor's-level Korean government scholarship is the only exception)
Failing the medical check-up or arriving without the vaccinations the institution specifies
Assuming your own country's deadline matches another office's - dates are set independently per overseas office and embassy

applicant_utility.summary: TU Graz runs a two-tier scholarship scheme for its own degree students: up to EUR 8,800 for Bachelor's and up to EUR 17,600 for Master's, paid over up to two years, funded by named industry partners. The Master's window for the 2027/28 winter semester doubles as the nearest opportunity - it opens on 15 October 2026 and closes on 15 February 2027, so the work you do this autumn determines whether you can apply at all. Selection is not purely academic: a TU Graz expert jury pre-selects, and the funding company then makes the final call, which is why the motivation letter and reference letters matter as much as the transcript.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong Bachelor's or Master's applicants to any TU Graz degree programme who can show concrete professional ambition - a clear reason for choosing engineering at Graz, technical depth in a field a named partner company works in, and evidence of independent thinking. Applicants who enjoy fieldwork, workshops and company contact will fit the mentoring and educational programme better than applicants who want a purely technical, classroom-only experience.

applicant_utility.summary: The One World Scholarship pays EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) to students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who are enrolled in a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg and pursue development-related topics. It is explicitly a partial scholarship, so treat it as a top-up on your own funds rather than a full funding package. Selection is heavily need-based: AAI looks at your income, savings, support, and your parents' profession and income, so the bank statement carries as much weight as the transcript.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funded students from the Global South studying in Salzburg who can show real financial need, steady study progress, and an academic profile shaped by sustainable development - anywhere from climate and energy policy to migration, gender equality or human rights. Because attendance at a monthly get-together and the co-organisation of an event are expected, you also need to be genuinely willing to be community-active. Joint-Master students are only accommodated by arrangement, so this works best if you are on a standard Master's or doctoral programme at the University of Salzburg, UAS Salzburg or Mozarteum.

applicant_utility.summary: ESPRIT is a job as much as a grant: the FWF employs you at the host institution for 36 months at the senior postdoc rate (EUR 97,380 per year in 2026, gross) and layers a project budget of at least EUR 45,000 on top. The two gating items are people, not paperwork - you need an Austrian mentor who signs a support declaration and mentoring plan, and an Austrian host institution willing to submit the application in PROFI mode. Because submissions are rolling with five board meetings a year, your start date depends on which meeting your file lands at, so apply as soon as your documents are complete rather than waiting.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Postdocs inside the five-year window after their doctorate, in any discipline, who have a credible Austrian mentor and host institution and want a funded PI project without applying from within Austria.

With two or more subject profiles, confirm which doctorate counts - the subject-specific degree counts, as for the START programme
Prepare the template publication record, the Statistics Austria scientific disciplines code and the ESPRIT checklist before opening elane, since the file must be uploaded in full
If you want the higher budget up to EUR 75,000, draft the cost breakdown and justification for the whole amount from the start
common_rejection_risks: No mentor named, or a mentor letter drafted as an afterthought - the plan must be specific enough to be reviewed
Applying while another ESPRIT, Erwin Schroedinger, Elise Richter or Elise Richter PEEK application is pending; the programmes cannot run in parallel
Choosing the wrong elane route (Application ad personam instead of Application PROFI), so the ESPRIT category never appears in the drop-down
Assuming you must already be in Austria - you may apply from abroad, but without an Austrian host and mentor the application cannot be submitted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The flat-rate project costs of EUR 45,000 to EUR 75,000 are the ceiling for project spending; anything the project genuinely needs beyond them (your own living setup, relocation costs beyond the salary) has to be covered by you or the host institution.
