Prepare the transcript, degree certificate or proof of final-year study, CV and motivation letter that the consortium requires
Check the English or other language requirement on that master's own website - it is not set centrally
Apply directly to the institution running the programme, applying for the scholarship within the same application
Submit in time for the consortium's own deadline, which falls in most cases between October and January for a start the following academic year
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the Commission office instead of the consortium - applications go directly to the institution running the programme
Using another university's deadline instead of the one on the chosen master's website
Missing the master's own English language requirement
Applying without proof that you will graduate before the programme starts
Having previously received an EMJM scholarship, which makes you ineligible for another
Assuming all Erasmus Mundus scholarships are the same - the award and process differ per master
Leaving applications until January when popular masters have earlier closing dates
Choosing a master without checking the list of participating universities, only to find the country mix is not what you expected
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: A full scholarship covers participation costs, travel, visa and a living allowance, but if you are ranked below the scholarship threshold you can still be admitted as a self-funded student. In that case you carry the full programme fee rate plus everything the scholarship would have covered. Even as a scholarship holder, confirm on the individual master's page whether the award is the maximum EMJM rate or a partial award.
applicant_utility.document_audit: There is no central document list. The only two things the Commission states are that you hold a bachelor's degree (or are in your last year and will graduate) and, where relevant, a recognised bachelor's-equivalent level of learning; everything else comes from the master's own website. Build a separate document pack per consortium.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no BME scholarship to apply for. The university's own pages route incoming international students to Hungarian state schemes administered by the Tempus Public Foundation, chiefly Stipendium Hungaricum, which covers tuition plus a monthly stipend of HUF 43,700 at bachelor's, master's and one-tier master level. So the decision to make first is whether you can secure Stipendium Hungaricum, which requires a sending partner nomination from your country, because your fallback is the self-funded route through BME's online application portal. That portal carries real costs of its own: a EUR 150 application fee receipt must be uploaded with your documents, and every applicant also has to pass BME's electronic e-admission exam, with BSc applicants who fall short in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or English directed into a one-year preparatory course instead.

Thinking transfer into a BME Stipendium Hungaricum place is open at any time, since the university has run it only in fixed windows

applicant_utility.summary: The Banach scholarship is one of the few international Master's awards that genuinely covers the full package: PLN 2,500 a month for up to twelve months in the academic year, free tuition at the Polish public universities that have a framework agreement with NAWA, a PLN 2,500 one-off travel sum, and a funded year of Polish language study if you take the Polish-language path. The application itself is two-tracked: you apply both through the NAWA IT system and register in your chosen university's own online system, and the university's own admission deadlines govern when you must do the latter. You must choose your path at application stage, so decide early whether you will do a year of Polish before starting, or take the English path with the Polish language and culture course.

Book a B2 certificate from NAWA's List of Recognized English or Polish Language Certificates well before the call opens, because it must be produced during admission
Arrange legalization or apostille of your prior-academic documents, since the university may require them
Conclude the scholarship agreement within 45 days of it being made available in the NAWA IT system, and submit an annual report by 31 October each year
common_rejection_risks: Missing the university's own registration deadlines, which sit before the scholarship result and govern the admission process
Failing to document B2 in the language of instruction at admission
Assuming the tuition exemption applies at private universities: it is at the university's discretion and agreed individually
Being in a country whose group deadline was moved earlier than the general date, in which case applications submitted after that deadline are not considered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Poland are above PLN 2,500 a month in Warsaw, and the travel lump sum is a one-off payment that covers arriving in Poland only; accommodation, insurance, visa and study materials are not part of the package. At a private university, tuition itself would be an out-of-pocket cost.
document_audit: The B2 language certificate must come from NAWA's published list of recognised certificates, so a local test result may not qualify
Legalization or apostille of educational documents should be started early, because universities may require them at admission

applicant_utility.summary: This is a mobility grant, not a place to study: you already need a bachelor's or master's degree, and you spend one to two semesters studying or researching at a host institution in a different eligible country, which must be at least 150 kilometres away from your home institution. The money is EUR 3,500 per semester for you and EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, which is a scholarship support amount rather than a living stipend, so you are topping up a mobility arrangement rather than funding a degree. The two dates to work from are 1 January 2027 when the round opens and 15 April 2027 at noon when it closes, with results on 31 May at noon, and the Fund explicitly gives preference to applicants who have not previously been supported. Timing is the practical problem: the file needs a letter of acceptance from your host institution, or at the very least proof that you have applied for master's-level mobility, so you have to start the conversation with your host supervisor in the autumn before.

important_advice_for_students: You apply to the university, not to Brussels. Erasmus+ publishes no central application; the institution running the programme runs its own process, and that is where your ranking is decided.

The scholarship is not automatic and is not the programme. Every joint master publishes a process 'with and without scholarship', so a self-funded place is a real option and a real cost. Decide which route you are applying on before you invest effort.
'Best-ranked' is relative. The same transcript wins in a weak cohort and loses in a strong one, so choose cohorts by the supervisor and project rather than by brand.

Timing is narrow: in most cases applications go in between October and January for the following academic year. Miss it and the programme is simply closed to you for that cycle, and a new batch of programmes is added each year rather than the same one re-opening.

Confirm the degree title carefully. You will get either a joint degree or multiple degrees, and the detail is fixed in the study agreement you sign at the start - ask what exactly is on the certificate before you accept.

Weigh the money honestly: the published benefits are participation costs plus contributions to travel, visa and a living allowance, with no rates published. Get the actual figures for the specific programme and the specific scholarship route from the institution.
If you rely on a bachelor's-equivalent level of learning, get it officially recognised under the legislation of the country where you earned it. Self-assessment will not satisfy the published rule.

referee_tracking.instructions: Erasmus+ publishes no central referee requirement for Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters. Any reference requirement belongs to the specific programme, whose website is the published authority for entry requirements and the application process. Approach referees only after reading that programme's own checklist, because a reference prepared for one Erasmus Mundus Joint Master will rarely fit another.

post_award_requirements: Sign the study agreement with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master at the beginning of your studies, which is where the joint or multiple degree structure is defined in detail.
Follow the programme's published pattern of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence across the consortium's institutions.
Meet the specific financial terms of your scholarship route, which the programme publishes rather than Erasmus+.

If on a scholarship, note that it is awarded on ranking and that the published scheme provides no renewal mechanism; there is no published route to extend an EMJM scholarship beyond the programme's own duration of 1 to 2 academic years.

Complete the requirements of the degree itself in at least two institutions, since the published award is either a joint degree on behalf of at least two higher education institutions or multiple degrees from at least two of them.
questions_to_ask_host: Is this programme a currently selected Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, and in which year's batch was it selected?
Which institutions are in the consortium, which countries, and where in the pattern does the Polish institution sit?
Will I receive a joint degree or multiple degrees, and exactly what appears on the certificate or certificates?
How many scholarships are available, how many applicants were there last cycle, and what does 'best-ranked' mean operationally here?
For the scholarship route, what are the actual amounts for participation costs, travel, visa and the living allowance, and are they paid in monthly instalments?
What is the exact application deadline, and is there a separate earlier deadline for scholarship consideration?
What is the exact breakdown of the published October-to-January application window, and are there interviews?
Are there language requirements, and does the programme waive or reduce tuition fees for self-funded students as well?
What happens to the scholarship if I defer, if I fail a module, or if the consortium changes my mobility country?

scholarships.title: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for Students from Developing Countries
scholarships.name: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for Students from Developing Countries

applicant_utility.summary: Read the published Guidelines PDF before you touch the form - the Ministry makes it binding, and it carries the conditions that decide admissibility. The gate that trips most applicants is the compulsory online tests: the application is not accepted or evaluated until both the general academic prerequisites test and, for English-medium study, the English test are complete, and they must be finished by the same 30 September cut-off. Money is tight by design - roughly 16 000 CZK a month for a master's student must cover dormitory accommodation, canteen meals and public transport out of the same pot, and travel to Czechia is never reimbursed.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nationals of the listed partner states who have completed a bachelor's (for master's) or master's (for doctoral) degree, fall inside the 1991-2008 birth window, and can commit to the standard length of full-time study at a Czech public university.
application_readiness_checklist: Download and read the binding Guidelines for Granting Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic (2026) from the Ministry's page before starting the form
Check your country appears in the 2027/2028 list and that you are not already enrolled at a Czech university, which disqualifies you outright
Check your date of birth against the published window (after 1 September 1991 and before 31 August 2008)
Choose between the English route (open to all eligible countries) and the Czech route (only Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus) before you plan your year
Book the English test and the general academic prerequisites test early in the window so a failed attempt still leaves time to retake before 30 September
Get certified copies of your diploma, diploma supplement and transcripts plus proof that your institution was authorised to award higher education
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the form but never completing both compulsory tests, which leaves the application unprocessed
Being a Czech or EU citizen, or holding permanent residence in the Czech Republic - an absolute bar with no appeals route
Missing the bachelor's degree for a master's application or the master's degree for a doctoral application
Falling outside the published age window for the call
Choosing the Czech-language route without B2 Czech, which forces the extra preparatory year
Assuming travel to Czechia is funded - the Ministry states plainly that travel expenses are not reimbursed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to and from Czechia, and anything beyond dormitory, canteen and public-transport costs - the 16 000 CZK monthly allowance has to absorb those, and installation or relocation support is not offered.
document_audit: Diplomas and supplements must be officially certified copies, not plain photocopies, and must be accompanied by confirmation that the awarding institution was authorised to provide higher education
The motivation letter is length-capped at one A4 page for master's applicants and two for doctoral applicants - going over reads as not following instructions
The statutory declaration of return to the country of origin after completing studies is mandatory and must be signed
The list of study and research stays abroad must cover exactly the last five years with year, duration, location and purpose
Doctoral applicants additionally need an outline of the professional focus and the dissertation idea
alerts: The call closes on 30 September and the next one is not announced until roughly August of the following year, so a missed round costs a full year
Each applicant may register only once and submit only one application - there is no second file
The Ministry describes the period as opening 21 August while the application register records 1 August, so treat late August as the safe assumption and do not wait for the later date
There is no legal claim to the award and no right of appeal, so embassy-stage documentation quality is decisive
Scholarship payments start only after you arrive and are admitted at the faculty - plan for the gap before the first instalment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the Ministry's portal, complete the electronic form with all documents attached, finish both compulsory tests before 30 September, then pass through the Czech embassy interview and documentation route to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT for the final decision.

scholarships.description: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for students from developing countries let nationals of designated partner states study at Czech public universities within the Czech foreign development cooperation programme. DZS states that "the Czech Republic offers scholarships to foreigners for a standard period of study in accredited university study programmes provided at public universities, and for courses in the Czech language and vocational preparation". Awards cover a master's study programme in Czech preceded by a one-year Czech language and professional training course, or study in master's and doctoral study programmes conducted in English. Applications are made through an electronic form, then the file passes through the applicant's Czech embassy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide which specific scheme you are applying for on the Charles University overview page — rectorate, faculty-level, or an external funder (MEYS, Václav Havel Bursary). The page is a directory, not an application form.

Secure or apply for admission to the relevant Charles University programme first where the scheme is tied to enrolment; several scholarships are awarded by the dean of the faculty in which you are enrolled.
Check the English-language teaching question carefully: the basic accommodation bursary is explicitly not available to students enrolled in a programme taught in a foreign language.

Check the standard length of study for your programme. More than two years over standard length in a bachelor's or master's programme blocks all scholarships and bursaries; more than one year over blocks the scholarship for outstanding academic achievement.

Collect the mandatory application content before you start: name and surname and any other names/maiden name, date of birth, address of permanent residence, a separate mail-delivery address if different, the subject matter, what is being requested, and your signature.
For an increased accommodation bursary, prepare the household social situation assessment in the form required by the Rector's directive.
Read the Faculty Internal Regulation 'Rules for Awarding Scholarships and Bursaries at the Faculty' for your faculty — the faculty sets the actual award amount and, in many cases, the deadline.
important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this page as an application portal. It carries no form, no amount and no deadline; it is a routing page.
Do not assume a full scholarship. Nothing here is published as covering tuition, living costs and required expenses together.
Do rely on the guaranteed doctoral study income as a real entitlement for full-time doctoral students: at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage for the standard length of study (4 years).

Contact the faculty Admission Office directly rather than the central rectorate for the specific amount and deadline of a faculty scheme — the University states amounts are always set by faculty internal regulations.
Note that most faculty merit scholarships are awarded retroactively for the previous unit of study, so they are awarded after your results exist, not at the start of the year.
Use the Carolina Centre route if you are in an emergency financial situation rather than waiting for a scholarship round.
common_rejection_risks: Actual length of study in a bachelor's or master's programme exceeding the standard length by more than two years — an absolute bar to any scholarship or bursary.
Actual length of study exceeding standard length by more than one year — bars the scholarship for outstanding academic achievement.
Enrolment in a programme taught in a foreign language — bars the accommodation bursary.
Not being a full-time student — bars the accommodation bursary and the doctoral bursary.
Previous studies at public higher education institutions terminated rather than successfully completed more than twice — bars the accommodation bursary.
Aggregate of completed study exceeding the standard length of the doctoral programme — bars the doctoral bursary.
Failure to fulfil the individual curriculum as judged by the Subject-Area Board — bars or withdraws the doctoral bursary.

Missing mandatory application content (identity, addresses, subject matter, request, signature) — the dean or Rector must invite you to cure deficiencies within a reasonable time, which is the most common delay cause.
Applying to a bursary to support study abroad and then not fulfilling the purpose for which it was awarded — the bursary must be returned.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond the published bursary ranges: no scheme on this page is published as covering living costs in full
Tuition fees for programmes taught in English, unless your faculty grants a waiver or reduction under its own internal regulations
Airfare, travel and relocation: no travel funding is published anywhere on this page
Health insurance: only a bursary not exceeding the premium actually paid by a full-time doctoral student is described, and only for doctoral students
Books, equipment and course-specific costs: not addressed on this page
The gap between a bursary award and actual cost of living in Prague, which the University publishes separately on its 'Costs of Living' page rather than covering here

Name and surname, other names and maiden name where appropriate, and date of birth — all mandatory identifying data points.
Address of permanent residence, plus a mail-delivery address if different and not deliverable electronically.
Subject matter of the application and a clear statement of what is being requested — both mandatory.
Submission form: electronic by default, unless the relevant Rector's directive provides otherwise. Check the directive for your bursary type.
For an increased accommodation bursary: the household social situation assessment document required by the Rector's directive.
No file-size limits, accepted file types or translation rules are published on this page; they are set in the applicable Rector's or dean's directive, which you must obtain.

referee_tracking.instructions: No referee or reference requirement is published on this overview page. The published selection route is the grade-based indicator from examinations and graded study requirements of the previous unit of study, assessed by the dean or Rector; where a faculty Internal Regulation requires references, it is set there, not here.

alerts.message: Start with the faculty, not the rectorate: faculty scholarship amounts and deadlines are set in the faculty's internal regulations, and the University explicitly directs students to the faculty Admission Office.

alerts.message: You are excluded from the basic accommodation bursary under Article 13(4)(b). Plan accommodation costs accordingly.

alerts.trigger: You are a full-time doctoral student
alerts.message: Your doctoral bursary is an entitlement during the standard length of study, but it is reduced or withdrawn if the annual Subject-Area Board assessment finds you did not fulfil your individual curriculum.

alerts.trigger: You received a bursary to support study abroad
alerts.message: You are contractually required to return it if its purpose cannot be or was not fulfilled; the deciding dean or Rector sets the return deadline, manner and procedure.

alerts.trigger: You received a decision you disagree with
alerts.message: The appeal period is 30 days from notification; an appeal against the reasoning alone is impermissible. Missing or defective notification of the right of appeal extends the outer limit to 90 days.

submission_workflow: Choose the specific scheme and identify the deciding authority: dean of the faculty where you are enrolled, or the Rector.
Obtain the applicable Faculty Internal Regulation or Rector's directive for that scheme — it fixes the amount, the deadline and the submission form.
Assemble the mandatory application content, including your signature.
Submit electronically through the University's information system unless the Rector's directive for that bursary provides otherwise.
Retain proof of submission; proceedings commence on the day the dean or Rector received the application.
If the application is deficient, cure it within the reasonable time period given, or ask the dean or Rector's office to help you correct it.
If refused or reduced, decide within 30 days of notification whether to appeal, and file with the dean or the Rector as the notice specifies.
post_award_requirements: Hold the award for its stated purpose; a bursary to support study abroad must be returned if the purpose is not fulfilled.
Accept that bursary payments are proportionate to days of eligibility if you become eligible part-way through a month.

For doctoral students, undergo the annual assessment of the doctoral student by the Subject-Area Board; failure to fulfil study requirements leads to reduction of up to 50% or withdrawal of the doctoral bursary.

Do not enrol simultaneously in programmes in a way that would duplicate bursaries: the accommodation bursary, the difficult-social-situation bursary and the doctoral bursary may each be paid only once per period.
Watch your own length of study against the standard length, since exceeding it is the most common bar to payment.
Study in the Czech Republic bursary holders must comply with Article 23 of the Constitution of the University, which the criteria must also comply with.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the exact award amount of my faculty's scholarship or bursary for this academic year, and is it set in the Faculty Internal Regulation?

Which Rector's directive governs the bursary type I want, and what does it require in terms of form, formal elements and submission dates?
For doctoral students: what does the annual Subject-Area Board assessment require of me to keep the doctoral bursary, and what happens to the CZK 2,000 post-examination increase?

scholarships.description: Charles University guarantees every full-time doctoral student a doctoral study income of at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage for the standard length of the doctorate (four years). The income may take the form of a doctoral scholarship, a salary or wage for creative work directly related to preparing the dissertation, or a combination of both, and is often supplemented by research-project awards and teaching remuneration. For bachelor's and master's students the university publishes no general scholarship: its page routes applicants to Czech Ministry of Education scholarship schemes (developing-country, general international and International Visegrad Fund), the Vaclav Havel Bursary, the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies, and faculty-level awards whose amounts are set by each faculty's own regulations.

scholarships.description: The International Visegrad Fund runs regional mobility programmes for Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Ukraine. The Visegrad Fellowship Program funds individual short-term in-person stays of 2 to 10 weeks for full-time doctoral students and PhD holders to conduct a research project, give lectures or seminars, or study archival material at an institution in a V4 country other than their country of citizenship and residence; it pays a lump-sum scholarship of EUR 500 per week in two instalments (80% and 20%). The separate Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe and its next cycle opens on 1 January 2027. Other Fund programmes include the Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships for doctoral and post-doctoral researchers, the Western Balkans-Visegrad Fellowships, research grants at the Historical Archives of the EU, and a scholarship at the Open Society Archives in Budapest.

The Visegrad Scholarship Program opens 1 January 2027.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a mobility award for one or two semesters, not a full degree, so the first job is finding a willing host and getting a letter of acceptance or at least proof of application before the window opens on 1 January. Two conditions catch applicants out: your previous university studies must have been completed in a country other than the host country, and the host must be more than 150 km from your current university or permanent residence. The Fund, not Masaryk University, awards and funds the scholarship; the university acts as host and supplies the letter of acceptance needed for the application. important_advice_for_students: You apply to the university, not to Brussels. Erasmus+ publishes no central application; the institution running the programme runs its own process, and that is where your ranking is decided.

The scholarship is not automatic and is not the programme. Every joint master publishes a process 'with and without scholarship', so a self-funded place is a real option and a real cost. Decide which route you are applying on before you invest effort.
'Best-ranked' is relative. The same transcript wins in a weak cohort and loses in a strong one, so choose cohorts by the supervisor and project rather than by brand.

Timing is narrow: in most cases applications go in between October and January for the following academic year. Miss it and the programme is simply closed to you for that cycle, and a new batch of programmes is added each year rather than the same one re-opening.

Confirm the degree title carefully. You will get either a joint degree or multiple degrees, and the detail is fixed in the study agreement you sign at the start - ask what exactly is on the certificate before you accept.

Weigh the money honestly: the published benefits are participation costs plus contributions to travel, visa and a living allowance, with no rates published. Get the actual figures for the specific programme and the specific scholarship route from the institution.
If you rely on a bachelor's-equivalent level of learning, get it officially recognised under the legislation of the country where you earned it. Self-assessment will not satisfy the published rule.

referee_tracking.instructions: Erasmus+ publishes no central referee requirement for Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters. Any reference requirement belongs to the specific programme, whose website is the published authority for entry requirements and the application process. Approach referees only after reading that programme's own checklist, because a reference prepared for one Erasmus Mundus Joint Master will rarely fit another.

post_award_requirements: Sign the study agreement with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master at the beginning of your studies, which is where the joint or multiple degree structure is defined in detail.
Follow the programme's published pattern of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence across the consortium's institutions.
Meet the specific financial terms of your scholarship route, which the programme publishes rather than Erasmus+.

If on a scholarship, note that it is awarded on ranking and that the published scheme provides no renewal mechanism; there is no published route to extend an EMJM scholarship beyond the programme's own duration of 1 to 2 academic years.

Complete the requirements of the degree itself in at least two institutions, since the published award is either a joint degree on behalf of at least two higher education institutions or multiple degrees from at least two of them.

important_advice_for_students: The scholarship decision is made in your Master's application, not after it. Interest must be shown in the designated field at the time you apply, and the page states applications cannot be considered after the Master's application has been submitted. This is the single most costly mistake available here.
Apply early - the school says so explicitly. Awards are made on a rolling basis and the budget can run out before the Master's admission cycle ends.
You will never be funded for the first instalment. Every award, including every 100% award, excludes the enrolment-fee instalment, and you must pay it to secure your place.
Know the 70% stacking ceiling before you chase the biggest number. Multiple Nova SBE awards together cannot exceed 70% of total tuition unless the whole package is a 100% social mobility scholarship.

The financial-need route is the strongest one. The Social Mobility Scholarship goes to 100%, and most partner-funded 100% awards require eligibility for a 100% Social Mobility or Continuity Scholarship - so the tax-return evidence is the gateway, not a side application.

Some of the best-funded awards are nationality-restricted. The António Serrenho, Banco Primus, Deloitte, McKinsey First Generation, McKinsey Women in Leadership and NOS awards require Portuguese nationality; the two McKinsey awards accept three years' residence in Portugal; the Explorer Excellence award is open to students of all nationalities but only in three named programmes.

Second stages are real. Banco Primus, NOS and Explorer Excellence want a three-minute video in English and add a final interview; several others want a specific document pack; André Sousa Bessa adds a family interview. Treat the email stage as part of the application.
Watch your spam folder. The page tells you twice that you are responsible for checking your email, including spam and trash, during the process.
The Portuguese-language regulations are the binding text and this English page is a summary. If a conflict matters to you, read the regulation linked for that specific award.

The McKinsey awards state that candidates 'may have a final interview with McKinsey'. These are partner interviews, not academic referees, and they are the published reason to prepare beyond the application form.

post_award_requirements: Pay the first instalment of tuition as the enrolment fee to secure your place - it is excluded from every award, including the 100% awards.
For the Nova SBE Merit Scholarship and the Explorers, McKinsey and Women in Finance awards, check the merit criteria at the end of the first year of the Master's programme to keep the award.

Stay within the stacking ceiling: funding across Nova SBE awards cannot exceed 70% of the total tuition fee unless the entire package comes from a 100% social mobility scholarship, and the Women in Finance Scholarship cannot be combined with the Merit Scholarship.
Remain enrolled in the specific programme for which the award was granted, and in the award's published intake.
Expect to be contacted by email for second stages, and to monitor spam and trash folders, throughout the process.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no single scholarship here to apply for, so do not wait for one call: ULisbao routes international and domestic students through different doors - DGES state scholarships through the national BeOn platform with credentials issued by SASULisba, university merit and PhD fellowships published individually on the scholarships page, and residences applied for online with priority for scholarship holders from outside Lisbon. Two practical points matter most. First, tuition is not waived by any of these routes: the published 2026/2027 fee is 697 EUR for bachelor's and integrated master's cycles, master's and doctoral fees vary by school, and international fees are those set by the General Council Decision and listed on each course page - the brochure only says the international fee may be reduced to the Portuguese-student value, which is a request to the school, not an entitlement. Second, residence and grant cash is modest and time-bound: DGES scholarships are paid in 10 monthly instalments, and residence supplements are capped at 17.5% of the Index of Social Support.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students already or soon enrolled at ULisba who need cash-flow help, accommodation or health support, particularly applicants from outside Lisbon with limited household resources and Erasmus students who are SASULischoa holders.
application_readiness_checklist: Request DGES BeOn access credentials through the SASULischoa website's 'Credentials Request' option as soon as you enrol
Apply for the DGES scholarship in BeOn inside the published period - 25 June to 30 September is the standard window, with the 20 working days after enrolment if you enrolled after 30 September
Apply separately for a university residence application online if you are coming from outside Lisbon, since priority goes to scholarship holders from outside Lisbon
If you are an Erasmus student holding a SASULischoa scholarship, tell your school's International Relations or Erasmus Office so the supplementary mobility grant is triggered
Check the individual award pages for PhD fellowships (Unite!, PRISC, Angola, Unite! Widening) and the Merit Scholarships, since each is published separately
Ask your intended school in writing about a reduction of the international tuition fee to the Portuguese-student value
common_rejection_risks: Assuming one university-level scholarship application covers DGES, merit, PhD and residence routes - they are separate
Missing the DGES BeOn window because you waited for enrolment, when the 20-working-day post-enrolment route only applies if you enrol after 30 September
Assuming tuition is covered: the only tuition-linked possibility is a discretionary reduction to the Portuguese-student value
Forgetting to notify the Erasmus Office, which forfeits the monthly supplementary mobility grant
Not preparing the full household financial documentation Seteple BeOn requires, including bank balances and IMI-declared properties
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition of at least 697 EUR per year for bachelor's and integrated master's cycles (higher and school-dependent for master's and doctoral cycles), plus living costs, since the awards are cash grants in 10 monthly instalments and the residence supplement is capped at 17.5% of the Index of Social Support.

scholarships.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship program encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario and has provided merit-based scholarships to Ontario's best graduate students in all disciplines since 1975. At the University of Toronto the program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, and the Province allocates OGS awards to universities specifying how many each may offer annually. The OGS is worth $5,000 per session at U of T, and the awarding graduate unit contributes one-third of the total award cost. Deadlines and application dates are set by each graduate unit, with results in mid-July.

The published range of CAD 11,000 to 15,000 means your school's own criteria decide where in that band you land.

scholarships.description: In support of the Quebec government's science policy, the Merit Scholarship for Foreign Students (PBEEE) supports the internationalization of research activities in Quebec higher education institutions, attracts top foreign researchers and students, and creates cultural links for joint research projects. It is managed by the Fonds de recherche du Quebec - secteur Nature et technologies, which was commissioned by the Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur du Quebec, which provides the funding. The programme has four component types - master's research, doctoral research, postdoctoral and short-term research or professional development - available both to students of all countries and, through five bilateral components, to students from Brazil, China, India, Israel and Wallonia. Recipients must be preselected by a Quebec university or the CCTT network, and scholarship payments begin only after FRQ receives a copy of the study permit (doctoral) or work permit (postdoctoral).
scholarships.duration: Master's: maximum 6 instalments (6 semesters). Doctoral: maximum 12 sessions (12 instalments), with $25,000 for the first 9 sessions and $12,000 for the last 3 if an extension is requested. Postdoctoral: maximum 12 months, not renewable. Short-term research or professional development: 4 months, not renewable.

scholarships.description: The Canada Postdoctoral Research Award program recognizes and empowers the next generation of highly qualified innovators, knowledge workers and creative thinkers. It supports outstanding postdoctoral researchers in developing their research skills and provides the funding and flexibility needed to support their contributions to building world-class research capacity and to Canada's prosperity and competitiveness. For the September 2026 competition SSHRC publishes a value and duration of $70,000 per year for 2 years, with an application deadline of September 10, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. eastern.

scholarships.application_period: Annual competition; September–October deadlines

scholarships.description: The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2) program is offered by Global Affairs Canada as a key initiative under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy, funded under that strategy. It expands the Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) programme to students from ASEAN Member States, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia, who conduct short-term study or research at Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas contributing to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Canadian institutions must apply on behalf of eligible candidates, must be Designated Learning Institutions, and must waive tuition fees for recipients. Four award components are offered, from $10,200 to $15,900, with durations of four to eight months.
scholarships.duration: Four to eight months: college/undergraduate 4 months or 8 months (two academic terms); graduate 4 months or 5 to 6 months. Scholarships cannot be deferred and are not renewable.
scholarships.application_period: Applications open January 2026; institutional deadline March 24, 2026

Enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country
Paying tuition fees to that institution at the time of application and for the full duration of the exchange
Not hold or have pending an application for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency
Not already participating in a scholarship program funded by the Government of Canada
Not already enrolled in a degree, diploma or certificate program at a Canadian post-secondary institution
Not have previously received a scholarship under the first phase of the program (Canada-ASEAN SEED)

scholarships.eligibility_summary: Candidates must be citizens of an ASEAN Member State (Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam), a Pacific Island Country (Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu), or Mongolia; be enrolled full-time at a post-secondary institution in an eligible country; and be paying tuition fees to that institution at the time of application and for the full duration of the exchange. Hosting Canadian institutions must be a Designated Learning Institution, must waive tuition fees for scholarship recipients, and must centralize applications through their international office.

scholarships.description: Schulich Leader Scholarships are Canada's largest undergraduate STEM scholarship programme, launched in 2012 from a CAD 200 million fund. One hundred awards are made each year across 20 partner universities, half worth CAD 120,000 for engineering and half worth CAD 100,000 for science, technology and math, and the funds are disbursed directly by the university over the degree. Every high school or cegep in Canada may nominate one graduating student per year, who then submits a separate scholarship application with two referees.

scholarships.description: The UCAS Scholarship for International Students is a University of Chinese Academy of Sciences award for non-Chinese-citizen students pursuing a Master's or doctoral degree, or attending courses, conducting research or making academic visits at UCAS colleges and CAS institutes. It has two tiers: a full scholarship covering tuition waiver, application fee waiver, monthly stipend, basic accommodation and medical insurance, and a partial scholarship covering only the tuition waiver, insurance and application fee. Awards run for no longer than 36 months, and the full tier publishes RMB 40,000/year (PhD) or RMB 30,000/year (Master's) tuition waived plus a monthly stipend of RMB 2,500 (PhD) or RMB 2,000 (Master's), with a combined total of at least RMB 3,500 or RMB 3,000 once the host assistantship is added.

scholarships.description: The CAS-ANSO Scholarship (Degree Program), previously the ANSO Scholarship for Young Talents, is the postgraduate scholarship of the Alliance of National and International Science Organizations for the Belt and Road Regions (ANSO), sponsored by the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and administered at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS) for master's and PhD study. The 2026 call opened for application on 15 October 2025 and closed for applicants and referees on 31 January 2026 Beijing Time; results were announced in June 2026 and the 2027 call was not yet published on 2026-10-04. The 2026 coverage table published on the call page lists tuition waiver, a monthly stipend of CNY 6,000 or 7,000 for PhD candidates and CNY 3,000 for master's candidates, health insurance, application fee waiver, one international travel allowance and a one-time visa/residence permit allowance. A sub-category, the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship, selects up to 40 PhD students from developing countries each year, with 10 scholarships prioritised for recipients engaged in climate-related research.
scholarships.duration: PhD: monthly stipend for up to 48 months. Master's: monthly stipend for up to 36 months. The official page states the scholarship duration explicitly in the Admission Notice.

application_readiness_checklist: Get admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty first. Without enrolment the bursary cannot be awarded, no matter how strong the persecution case.
Identify the Student Affairs Office of your faculty; that is where the application goes, not the Rectorate.
Download the official Václav Havel Bursary Application Form from the programme page.
Obtain every document required under Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, Article 2 point 3.
Check the language of every document proving persecution: English is accepted as-is; anything in a less commonly used foreign language needs a certified translation into Czech.
Aim for the earlier of the two deadlines, 31 March, if you want maximum processing time.
If you are preparing for studies in the Czech language, prepare the separate living-expenses contribution application as well.
important_advice_for_students: Do not apply before you are enrolled. The published rule is that the bursary can only be awarded to a student who has been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at one of the faculties through the standard admissions procedure.
Do not send your file to the Rectorate yourself. The faculty submits it digitally via the Dean or an authorised Vice-Dean to the Chair of the Board.

Do not rely on a generic statement of persecution. The published test is country-based: human rights and freedoms being violated according to humanitarian organisations, and discriminatory measures restricting access to education.
Do not assume this is full funding. The page describes direct financial support plus an optional living-expenses contribution, and says nothing about tuition, travel or insurance.
Budget for your own tuition and housing. Nothing on the page waives fees.
Read Rector's Directive No. 56/2025 yourself: it, not the web page, sets the document list, the award conditions and the amount.
common_rejection_risks: Applying without having been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty.
Submitting to the Rectorate instead of the faculty Student Affairs Office, so the file never reaches the Board through the required route.
Missing the 31 March or 31 October submission date — there are only two rounds per calendar year.
Documents proving persecution in a less commonly used foreign language without the certified Czech translation the directive requires.
An incomplete application: the faculty must forward the complete application including all attachments, and the required-document list is fixed by Article 2, point 3 of the directive.
Country conditions not met, i.e. not from a country where human rights and freedoms are being violated and discriminatory measures restrict access to education.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees for programmes taught in English or in a foreign language at Charles University: no waiver is described
Accommodation and general living costs beyond the optional contribution towards living expenses
Airfare and travel, and health insurance: not addressed on the programme page
Study materials, equipment and course-specific costs: not addressed
document_audit: Václav Havel Bursary Application Form — the official published form; use it rather than a free-form letter.
Documents proving persecution — required; may be submitted in English.
Translation rule — if the documents are in a less commonly used foreign language, a certified translation into Czech is required.
Documents required under Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, Article 2 point 3 — the full list sits in the directive; the programme page does not enumerate it.

Delivery — the complete application with all attachments is forwarded digitally by the faculty through the University's document management system, so check that every attachment is legible and complete before you hand it in.
No file-size limit or file-type list is published; assume nothing is accepted that cannot be sent electronically by the faculty.

referee_tracking.instructions: No referee, reference or recommendation requirement is published on the programme page. Evidence is documentary — documents proving persecution — rather than testimonial, subject to the Article 2 point 3 list in Rector's Directive No. 56/2025.

Complete the official Václav Havel Bursary Application Form.

Submit the complete application with all attachments to the Student Affairs Office of your faculty by 31 March or 31 October.
The faculty forwards the file digitally via the Dean or an authorised Vice-Dean to the Chair of the Václav Havel Bursary Board.
Track with your faculty Student Affairs Office; there is no published applicant-facing status page.
post_award_requirements: Remain enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty, since the bursary is only available to admitted and enrolled students.
Comply with Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, which governs the award conditions, and re-check it if your circumstances change.
Keep evidence of your situation current: the award rests on the country-based repression and access-to-education test at the time of assessment.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the current award amount of the Václav Havel Bursary under Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, and is it a single figure or a range?

scholarships.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports full-time Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for one to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. It is funded by the International Visegrad Fund, founded by the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia. The award is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, and it does not cover tuition. Applicants must already hold a bachelor's or master's degree, and their country of citizenship or residence must differ from the host institution's country.

scholarships.deadline: No application deadline is published on the CTU Scholarships page. Applications are submitted to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate of CTU via the faculty International Office, with no published closing date or intake calendar.
scholarships.description: CTU awards a scholarship to foreign students who wish to take a Master study programme at the Czech Technical University in Prague and display qualities that entitle them to the award, and to foreign doctoral students capable of doing scientific work who study on a doctoral programme in English at CTU in Prague. The Master's award is a contribution towards the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CZK 10,000 per month for one to two semesters; the doctoral award covers the basic doctoral-study scholarship plus living costs of up to CZK 16,000 per month for six to twelve months. Both are financed equally from the rectorate's scholarship fund and the relevant faculty's fund, and are awarded under Act No. 111/1998 Sb. on Universities, section 91(3)(b). The award is a living-cost contribution and does not cover tuition fees.

scholarships.name: Danish Government Scholarship

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form to fill in: your master's admission application is your scholarship application, and only applicants admitted to a programme are ever considered. Because awards are made purely on academic achievement, your transcript matters more than any financial statement, and at the Faculty of Science you are only in contention if your bachelor's grade point average sits above 90% - the 2025 cohort started at 98%. Budget for tuition anyway: the award may be a partial waiver, arrives only with the admission offer, and at Theology it is decided after you have already been charged.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-of-class non-EU/EEA applicants who can present a near-perfect bachelor's transcript and are applying to a September-intake master's at UCPH.
application_readiness_checklist: Rank your chosen programme first - Faculty of Science only considers your first priority application
Check where your transcript sits on the Danish 12-scale: Science requires above 90% of the bachelor's degree
Pay the DKK 1,120 application deposit fee before submitting and upload the receipt with every application
Upload all admission documentation before the 15 January cut-off; nothing can be added afterwards
Plan acceptance of the study place by 18 March, and of any scholarship offer by the deadline in the award letter
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a February-start programme, which several faculties exclude from awards
Ranking a programme lower than first at the Faculty of Science, where only first-priority applications are considered
Assuming a full waiver: the award may be partial, and Theology grants partial tuition waivers only
Letting the scholarship offer lapse, since it is revoked and given to another applicant if not accepted in time
Relying on second-year awards, which at most faculties number only about two per year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition share not waived, Copenhagen living expenses estimated by the University at EUR 1,280-1,800 per month, travel, insurance and the DKK 1,120 application deposit fee, which is not refunded even if a tuition waiver is awarded.
document_audit: The deposit fee receipt must be uploaded with each application, not just paid
Documentation must be uploaded before the deadline; late uploads leave the application unprocessed
A time-limited residence permit for study purposes is a condition of eligibility, so the permit route matters as much as the transcript
Any living-expense grant is taxable under Danish law, and the award letter states whether your nationality is exempt
alerts: The award can arrive with an admission offer that also contains a tuition invoice - accept the study place first and claim the reimbursement afterwards
At the Faculty of Theology the decision is made after applicants are charged tuition, so you must fund tuition while waiting
Second-year scholarships at HEALTH and SCIENCE require about 60 ECTS and a top grade average in the first year
The number of awards is very small and varies by faculty, so treat it as a bonus rather than a funding plan
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One master's admission application in the portal before 15 January, automatic consideration in the academic assessment, a decision on 13 March, then accept the study place and the scholarship within the stated deadlines.

applicant_utility.summary: You are entered into this scholarship the moment you submit a non-EU Master's application to Aarhus University by 15 January (August start) or 15 September (February start) - there is no separate form and nothing extra to upload. Choose your faculty deliberately: Arts and BSS awards pair the tuition waiver with a monthly living grant, while Natural Sciences and Technical Sciences awards are tuition waivers only, so budget living costs yourself if you apply to STEM. With typically only one or two awards per programme, treat any waiver as a discount on your bill, not as guaranteed funding your study plan can rely on.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU applicants with strong academic records who can fund Danish living costs even if no waiver is awarded
application_readiness_checklist: Pay the 150 EUR (1,125 DKK) application fee through the AU web shop and upload the receipt to each application - applications are not processed until the fee is paid

Prepare the official diploma and transcript, the official grading-scale description, and linkable or stamped course descriptions well before the deadline, with authorised translations if they are not in English, Danish, Norwegian or Swedish
Book IELTS or TOEFL early: the result must be under two years old on the day the portal opens, Duolingo and PTE are not accepted, and subscore thresholds (6.0 IELTS) apply
Submit by 15 January (summer) or 15 September (winter) - later applications are outside scholarship consideration entirely
If admitted without an immediate waiver, keep your offer until 1 April (summer) or 1 November (winter), since STEM waiver decisions continue into March

common_rejection_risks: Missing the 15 January / 15 September cut-off - scholarship consideration is tied to applying by those dates, so a strong late applicant gets nothing
Weak or expired English documentation (test older than two years at portal opening, unaccepted test such as Duolingo/PTE, or a subscore below the threshold) blocks admission and therefore the waiver
An unpaid or unprocessed application fee, which stops the whole application from being assessed
Applying where faculty strategy sits elsewhere - strategic focus can be placed on selected programmes or countries, and only one or two awards exist per programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: If no waiver is awarded, the full tuition of EUR 13,000-17,300 per year (2026/27, faculty-dependent); beyond any waiver, the monthly grant may not cover all living expenses, and settling-in costs (room deposit, furniture, bicycle, bus card), books and course materials, health insurance before CPR registration, and residence-permit fees come out of pocket. The application fee is not refunded if you are not admitted.

applicant_utility.description: The single most useful fact here is that you cannot apply for this scholarship separately - every non-EU applicant to a master's programme is considered automatically, so your admission application is your scholarship application. That also means you cannot influence the outcome beyond your application materials, and AAU explicitly warns not to rely on receiving one: roughly 15 awards against a full non-EU intake is a low hit rate. Because AAU cannot guarantee the decision arrives before the tuition deadline, and tuition is refundable if the scholarship is later granted, the realistic strategy is to pay and hope rather than to wait.
eligibility_tips: You must be liable for tuition fees. If you hold a permanent residence permit, a humanitarian protection permit, a Ukraine-displacement permit or one of the other listed permits, you are fee-exempt and therefore outside the scholarship scheme.
EU/EEA citizens cannot apply, and there are no bachelor's scholarships at all - this is a master's-only, September-intake-only award.
Scholarships are granted per September intake, so a February start does not enter you into the pool.
application_tips: Put your effort into the master's application itself, since that is the only material the scholarship committee sees. There is no extra form to optimise.

Pay the 150 EUR (1,150 DKK) application fee promptly and upload the receipt to every application in the portal - it is non-refundable even if you later withdraw, and it doubles as a de facto application deadline.

Arrange the Danish logistics early: AAU notes you need a CPR number, NemKonto and tax registration before the stipend can be paid, and until then it is paid retroactively from 1 September. Do not plan your first month's budget around receiving money on time.
documents: Application fee receipt uploaded to all applications - AAU is explicit that one fee covers a maximum of three applications for a specific intake.
Programme admission documents as required by the chosen master's programme.
Nothing extra for the scholarship itself.
mistakes_to_avoid: Waiting for the scholarship decision before paying tuition. AAU cannot guarantee the decision precedes the tuition deadline, and the deadline cannot be extended.
Relying on the scholarship as your funding plan. AAU states plainly that it does not advise relying solely on receiving a scholarship.
Assuming the stipend covers Danish living costs. AAU warns the scholarship may not cover all living expenses and expects you to supplement with savings, a home-country loan or a student job.
Applying as an EU/EEA citizen or to a bachelor's programme - both are excluded.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: There is no scholarship deadline to miss, which is either reassuring or a trap depending on how you plan: the binding date is the tuition payment deadline roughly 14 days after your admission information, and AAU says it cannot be extended. Scholarship decisions land by the beginning of July at the latest, so expect a long period of uncertainty. If your studies are prolonged beyond four semesters you will not receive further stipend, so the award is a two-year funding floor rather than a guarantee for your whole degree.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are actually liable to pay Aalto tuition fees - if you are exempt, this scholarship is not for you.
Apply in Studyinfo.fi during the published window and request the scholarship on the same application form; there is no separate scholarship form for the admissions-stage award.
Pay the â‚¬100 application fee within seven days if you are not an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen. Unpaid applications are not processed and no waivers exist.
Have all obligatory documents ready as separate, correctly named PDF files before the window opens, because you cannot save a draft and the form must be completed in one session.

important_advice_for_students: This is a tuition waiver, not a living-cost scholarship. Aalto states it offers no university-wide scholarships to cover living costs in Finland, so budget Helsinki/Espoo living costs entirely yourself.

Do not confuse the Excellence Scholarship with the Aalto Reserve Scholarship. The Reserve Scholarship is only for students who become liable to pay tuition fees mid-studies, and it cannot be used to waive tuition while waiting for a residence permit decision.
Do not skip the scholarship request on the application form. The award is merit-based and competitive, there are very few of them, and programmes may decide to award none at all.

If you are an Aalto bachelor's graduate in an English-medium programme heading into a master's under your 3+2 study right, apply in Sisu at the bachelor's graduation request - that is a separate route with its own grade condition of at least 3.50 and target-time condition.

Watch the clock on progression, not just enrolment. The scholarship continues automatically only if you avoid the four discontinuation triggers, and the annual enrolment in May is the hard practical cliff.
If your Finnish residence permit or tax position changes your fee liability mid-study, the Aalto Reserve Scholarship is the route - not a fresh Excellence Scholarship application.
Note the one study right rule: accepting this study right terminates your previous Finnish study rights at the same or lower level, and the right begins on 1 August.

2. Prepare all obligatory and study-option-specific documents as separate, correctly named, legible PDF files, and obtain official translations where required.
3. Open the application form in Studyinfo.fi when the period opens (7 December 2026 at 9.00 UTC +2) and complete it in a single session, ranking up to two study options.
4. Request the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship on the same application form.
5. Pay the â‚¬100 application fee within seven days if you are not an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen, or upload proof of exemption.
6. Upload and save every document to the correct section by 12 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2), clicking 'Save modifications' after any change.
7. Await study option evaluation (January to March 2027) and the results publication on 30 March 2027.
8. Accept the admission offer by 21 April 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +3), and if awarded the scholarship, agree to the scholarship terms by the given deadline.
9. Submit officially certified (attested) educational documents by the applicable certified-document deadline.
10. Enrol annually each May, maintaining 45 ECTS credits or more and following your personal study plan.
post_award_requirements: Agree to the terms of the scholarship by the given deadline.
Study full-time and follow the approved personal study plan.
Have your study progress reviewed annually, with the review done by the end of March in the spring term and any issues resolved by the end of April.
Maintain at least 45 ECTS credits per academic year, which is also the Finnish Immigration Authority's residence permit renewal threshold.
Complete the officially certified (attested) educational documents required after admission.
Cover all living and other study-related costs from your own financial resources, as no Aalto university-wide scholarship covers living costs in Finland.

What happens to the scholarship if I need to revise my study plan, and who at Student Services should I contact first?
Are there any additional grants or awards I could stack with the tuition waiver, and what is the Finnish tax threshold that applies to my combined awards?

scholarships.description: The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based, competitive tuition fee waiver awarded to non-EU/non-EEA applicants who are liable to pay Aalto tuition fees. It covers the full tuition fee for the target time of the degree programme - three years for a bachelor's degree and two years for a master's degree. Applications are made as part of the normal admission process, and only a very limited number of scholarships are awarded, with some programmes awarding none. The scholarship does not cover living costs in Finland, which students must fund themselves.

scholarships.selection_notes:
Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are merit-based and are granted on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants based on the programme's evaluation criteria.
Each study option evaluates and ranks applications that are complete and meet the general eligibility criteria, based on its own selection criteria, which may include the relevance of previous studies, academic performance, motivation and, in the fields of art, design and architecture, a portfolio.
The applications are compared to each other, and the highest-ranked applicants are admitted; since the number of study places is restricted, not all eligible applicants will receive an offer of admission, and study options are not required to fill all available places.
There is a very limited number of scholarships available, and programmes may also decide not to grant any scholarships.
For the bachelor's-to-master's continuation route: completion of the bachelor's degree within the target time period and a weighted average grade of at least 3.50, calculated from the completed degree in its entirety.

applicant_utility.summary: Read this as a prompt-payment reward, not a scholarship you win: the first-year discount is 5% to 30% of your programme's fee and is simply granted if you pay within three weeks of the results, with no application and no assessment. From year two the waiver is earned by completing at least 60 ECTS in the previous year, including the required Finnish language studies, so the Finnish courses are a funding condition rather than an optional extra. Check your programme's percentage before you commit, because the same 60 ECTS buys a 40% waiver in Architecture and only 10% in Learning, Education and Technology.

scholarships.funding_period: one-off on first academic year tuition

applicant_utility.summary: The money here is earned by paying on time and then by studying fast: 30% off the first year if you pay within 21 days of the results, another 30% in later years if you bank at least 55 ECTS in year one, plus EUR 2,500 or EUR 1,500 once for reaching Finnish language proficiency. There is no full waiver for ordinary applicants - UEF says so directly - so plan for EUR 7,000-8,400 of tuition a year plus living costs on top. The one genuine route to 100% is temporary protection granted by Migri, which UEF will even grant provisionally while your application is pending.

scholarships.title: University of Turku Merit Scholarship (50% of tuition) and Early Bird Discount
scholarships.name: University of Turku Merit Scholarship (50% of tuition) and Early Bird Discount

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a two-part deal rather than one award: the discount you can bank immediately is the EUR 2,000 Early Bird, and it requires paying the full first-year tuition within 28 days of the admission decisions, so have the funds ready before results land. The larger prize is the Merit Scholarship, but it only kicks in for year two (or years two and three on a bachelor's) and is conditional on 55-110 credits, a 3.0 average, and at least 4 credits of Finnish completed before you first apply. Because the invitation arrives by email from admissions services in spring and there is no published closing date, keep your UTU inbox monitored and do not assume there is a form to fill in autumn.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fee-paying non-EU/EEA master's and bachelor's students at Turku who are strong academically and willing to take Finnish language credits alongside a full course load.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme appears on the published tuition-fee list and note its exact annual fee, since 50% of that figure is your actual year-two value
Diarise the 28-day Early Bird window from the admission decision date and pre-arrange international payment of the full first-year fee
Track credits from day one: 55 credits in year one is the hard gate for the master's award, and 110 cumulative credits for the bachelor's third-year award
Enrol in at least 4 credits of Finnish early enough to finish before your first scholarship application; prior Finnish study or proven proficiency can substitute but is assessed case by case
Watch for the spring invitation email from admissions services and check spam folders, since missing the invitation means missing the round
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 28-day Early Bird window because the payment cleared after the deadline - the discount is forfeited, not deferred
Falling below 55 credits in year one, which removes the Merit Scholarship entirely regardless of grades
Applying for the Merit Scholarship before completing the 4 Finnish credits, or assuming prior Finnish study will definitely be counted
Assuming a first-year scholarship exists - the page states plainly that first-year tuition support is not available, so a fully funded first year is not on offer here
Letting the average drop under 3.0 on the 1-5 scale in a single strong or weak semester
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Roughly half of every tuition fee from year two onwards (and all of year one minus EUR 2,000 on master's programmes), plus living costs, flights, the mandatory Student Union membership fee of about EUR 55 per academic year and the compulsory Student Health Care fee paid to Kela.
document_audit: The scholarship page itself lists no documents for the Merit Scholarship, so do not build a file around a published checklist that does not exist - wait for the invitation and follow its instructions exactly
Evidence of prior Finnish proficiency or completed Finnish studies, if you intend to rely on either instead of the 4 Turku credits, needs to be ready at the point you first apply
For the Early Bird route the only 'document' is a payment receipt within 28 days, so confirm your bank's international transfer lead time against that window
alerts: The University corrected an earlier error on this page: the Early Bird window is 28 days, not 30 - discount any third-party listing that still says 30 days
The Early Bird discount is explicitly not available for applicants of the bachelor's degree programmes
The page states its information is for students admitted in 2026; students admitted in 2025 or before are directed to a different page, so check which version applies to you
No first-year tuition scholarship exists under this scheme, so plan funding for the whole of year one independently
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission through the Finnish joint application in January, then accept and pay within 28 days for the Early Bird, then respond to the spring admissions-services invitation to apply for the Merit Scholarship.

scholarships.title: Åbo Akademi University tuition fee scholarship - early commitment offer and second-year reduction
scholarships.name: Åbo Akademi University tuition fee scholarship - early commitment offer and second-year reduction

applicant_utility.description: This is a payment-timing scheme, not a merit competition: the money is already allocated to every fee-liable admitted student, and the only way to lose it is to miss the deadline buried in your admissions letter. That makes it a EUR 4,000 reward for having cash ready at short notice and a EUR 4,000 penalty for hesitation, since students who do not claim the offer owe the full EUR 12,000. The second-year reduction is automatic and requires nothing, so your entire practical task is to read the letter carefully and move funds quickly.
eligibility_tips: You must be liable to pay tuition fees. Åbo Akademi states that students exempted from tuition are not eligible for the scholarship, so fee-exempt status removes the award entirely.

The scheme applies only to international master's degree programmes with studies starting in autumn 2026 or later. If you were admitted in 2025 or earlier, the old 100%/80% waiver rules apply instead.
Awards run for the first two years of study only - you will still need a funding plan for any third year or for living costs throughout.
application_tips: Read the admissions letter for the payment deadline as your first action. It is not a fixed university-wide date and it is the only thing standing between you and EUR 4,000.
Arrange the funds before the letter arrives. A bank transfer that takes a week to clear can quietly cost you the discount.
Do not look for a scholarship application form for the first year - there is none. Payment is the application.
Do nothing at all for the second year. Åbo Akademi states applicants do not need to apply separately and all admitted students receive the EUR 4,000 reduction.
documents: No scholarship documents. The evidence of claim is the tuition fee payment itself, made within the deadline in the admissions letter.
mistakes_to_avoid: Treating the admissions letter as a formality. The deadline inside it is the operative date, and missing it means paying the full EUR 12,000.
Assuming you can appeal. Åbo Akademi states decisions regarding all scholarships are final and may not be appealed.
Applying as a fee-exempt student, which is explicitly out of scope.
Expecting the award to help with living costs. It is a fee reduction only, and Turku living costs are entirely on you.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: There is no published calendar deadline for either award. The first-year early commitment offer must be claimed within the deadline stated in your admissions letter, and the second-year reduction is automatic with no date attached. Because Åbo Akademi grants scholarships only for the first two years and decisions are final and unappealable, the practical advice is to secure the first payment on time and to plan independently for the remainder of your costs.
