scholarships.title: Hanken GBSN Honor Scholarship (GBSN Scholarship for students from developing countries)
scholarships.name: Hanken GBSN Honor Scholarship (GBSN Scholarship for students from developing countries)

applicant_utility.summary: This is the only scholarship Hanken awards at admission, it covers tuition completely for two years, and only two people win it - but you never apply for it separately. You simply tick the GBSN Honor Scholarship on the Hanken admission form in the 7-21 January 2027 Main Admission round, and the decision arrives with your admission result. Confirm on the GBSN membership page that your school is a current member and in one of the 21 listed countries before you spend money on GMAT/GRE and language tests. Budget for everything except tuition: living costs in Helsinki run roughly 950-1200 EUR per month, and Finnish migration rules require proof of about 9 600 EUR per year before a residence permit is granted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Degree students or recent graduates of GBSN member business schools in the 21 listed developing countries who are tuition-liable and can meet the January Main Admission deadline with a strong academic file.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your institution is a current GBSN member school located in one of the 21 eligible countries (GBSN membership page) before applying
Book GMAT/GRE/IELTS/TOEFL early - results must be valid through the application period, and TOEFL scores must be sent to Hanken under reporting code 8433
Prepare the English CV and degree transcripts as high-quality PDFs before opening the Studyinfo.fi form, because it cannot be saved as a draft
Complete and upload every attachment by 28 January 2027 at 15:00 (UTC+2) - late uploads stop the application from being processed
Pay the 100 EUR application fee if you are from a non-EU/EEA country
Use an email address you will still access until at least September 2027, since scholarship and admission news arrive there
common_rejection_risks: Applying in the Rolling Admission round or after 21 January 2027 - the scholarship is only available in the Main Admission round
Forgetting to tick the GBSN Honor Scholarship box on the admission form, since there is no separate application and no later correction
Assuming any business school in a listed country qualifies - the school itself must be a GBSN member
Missing the 28 January attachment deadline or uploading a school certificate that does not clearly state English as the language of tuition
Being tuition-exempt (EU/EEA citizen or qualifying Finnish permit), which makes you ineligible because the waiver only applies to tuition-liable students
Falling below the 3.00 minimum academic assessment score or the 25-30 ECTS relevant-studies threshold
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs (about 950-1200 EUR/month in Helsinki, 800-1000 in Vaasa), the 100 EUR application fee, aptitude and language test fees (roughly 100-300 EUR and 200-450 EUR), residence permit fee 400-750 EUR, health insurance about 450 EUR, Student Union membership 70 EUR/year and the student health care fee 70.70 EUR/academic year - the scholarship waives tuition only.
document_audit: The Studyinfo.fi form cannot be saved as a draft; answers determine which attachments are requested and cannot be changed after submission
If claiming English proficiency from a prior degree, the language of tuition must be explicitly stated on an official certificate, transcript or diploma supplement
TOEFL must be sent via reporting code 8433; IELTS One Skill Retake and TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted
If exempt from tuition fees by residence permit, upload both sides of the permit card with the application
alerts: Only 2 scholarships exist per year across all eligible countries, so treat this as a long shot alongside other funding
You cannot change study location (Helsinki/Vaasa) or programme after accepting the offer
Scholarship decisions cannot be appealed under the Universities Act, and the 25% Early Commitment discount is not available to scholarship recipients
Second-year continuation requires 60 completed ECTS and a 3.0 GPA by 31 July each year, plus a commitment to limited student recruitment activities
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the joint Studyinfo.fi application between 7-21 January 2027 with the GBSN Honor Scholarship ticked, pay the application fee, upload attachments by 28 January, then wait for the combined admission and scholarship e-mail with results by 31 May 2027 at the latest.

scholarships.title: Nokia Foundation Fellow
scholarships.name: Nokia Foundation Fellow

applicant_utility.description: This grant is aimed at professors, not students, so its usefulness to most applicants is indirect: it is the route through which a Finnish professor hires a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher onto a new ICT direction, and the EUR 75,000 is explicitly earmarked for that salary. If you are a PhD or postdoc looking for a position, the practical move is to find a professor who is applying and ask to be named in their application - the Foundation says naming a candidate is beneficial but not required at the application stage. There is no template and no page limit, which sounds liberating but actually means your proposal is judged purely on quality and persuasiveness.
eligibility_tips: The applicant must be a tenured associate or full professor applying as Principal Investigator for their own project. Doctoral and postdoctoral researchers cannot apply directly.
The project must be carried out at a Finnish university, which fixes the host institution to Finland.
One application per professor per call, so a professor cannot hedge across multiple ideas in the same round.
application_tips: Lead with the high-risk, high-reward framing. The Foundation asks applicants to clearly highlight the innovativeness and the high-risk high-reward nature of the project, and says it focuses on exceptional proposals that open genuinely new frontiers.
Budget the full EUR 75,000 explicitly against salary, overheads and other expenses. A vague financial plan weakens an otherwise strong proposal.
Treat ethics and research security as a scored component rather than boilerplate - the Foundation requires these to be comprehensively explained in the form.
Use the draft-and-return function to build the application over several weeks rather than submitting a first attempt.
documents: Project plan: there is no template and no length restriction, so the burden is on the applicant to be clear and realistic without padding.
Financial plan showing salary, overheads and other expenses against the EUR 75,000 total.
Ethics and research security explanation inside the application form.
mistakes_to_avoid: Writing a safe, incremental proposal. The Foundation is explicit that it wants genuinely new frontiers and high-risk high-reward work, so a low-risk project is structurally a poor fit.
Leaving overheads out of the financial plan. The Foundation requires a detailed breakdown including overhead costs.
Positioning it as student funding. It is a research project grant that pays for a hired researcher, not personal financial support.
Missing the extension opportunity. Successful projects can reapply for an extension via the next year's process, which is a second bite at funding for the same direction.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: The 2026 window ran 18 May to 15 September 2026 and has closed, with decisions scheduled for late October 2026. The call recurs annually, so watch the page from around May. Note the project clock: successful projects may begin in early 2027 and must conclude no later than August 2028, a fixed horizon that constrains what kind of research can realistically be proposed.

scholarships.title: Jorma Ollila Grant
scholarships.name: Jorma Ollila Grant

applicant_utility.description: What the official page actually gives you is the money, not the rules: the Jorma Ollila Grants page is an award archive, so the most reliable signal available is the range of amounts awarded. Recent single-year visits landed between roughly EUR 9,500 and EUR 25,000, with a EUR 50,000 award for a two-year visit, so a realistic ask for a one-year placement sits in the low tens of thousands rather than the hundreds. Because the criteria, deadlines and permitted costs are not published on this page, treat every figure here as an observed award rather than a promise, and use the Foundation's grant system and general pages to confirm current terms before applying.
eligibility_tips: Recipients are consistently based at Finnish universities - Oulu, Helsinki, Tampere, Aalto, Turku, Jyväskylä and Vaasa all appear - so a Finnish institutional affiliation is the visible pattern in the awardee list.

Awarded projects are ICT-centred: sparse channel estimation, AI alignment, neural network interpretation, 6G RF transmitters, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces and digital healthcare all feature, which gives a clear sense of the thematic centre of gravity.
A named host institution abroad is a feature of every award, so a concrete invitation appears to be part of a credible application.
application_tips: Use the archive to calibrate your budget request rather than inventing a number: single-year awards cluster in the EUR 9,500-25,000 range while a two-year visit was funded at EUR 50,000.
Approach a host institution first. Every entry in the archive names a specific host, and a visit without a secured host is unlikely to be competitive.
Submit through the Nokia Foundation grant system, where drafts can be saved and completed later - useful because the financial and visit details often change while you negotiate.
Check the Tutkijat maailmalle page as well, since the Foundation lists it as a related call route with its own award archive and larger awards, including EUR 41,350 and EUR 36,040.
documents: The page as read publishes no required-document list. Confirm current requirements in the Nokia Foundation grant application system before submitting.
mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming a single fixed award amount. The published awards vary by more than a factor of five in a single year, so there is no standard figure to plan around.
Relying on this page for the deadline. It publishes none, and missing an unpublished deadline is the most common way a good visit application fails.
Proposing a visit with no named host. The archive shows a host organisation for every award.
Confusing this grant with the Nokia Foundation Fellow award on the same site. That one is EUR 75,000, is led by a professor, and funds hiring a researcher - a completely different instrument.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: This page publishes no deadlines at all, which is the single most important thing to know: the award archive is the content, and the call window lives elsewhere on the Nokia Foundation site. Since the most recent cohort listed is 2025, confirm with the Foundation whether a 2026 round ran before planning a visit. For context on the size of awards, the archive records EUR 20,000, EUR 25,000 and EUR 9,500 for 2025 single-year visits and EUR 50,000 for a two-year visit in 2024.

Your Bachelor's degree must come from the published partner-institution list, or from an approved bridge or mentoring programme, or you must hold or have held UNHCR refugee status - if it comes from nowhere on those lists, this route closes regardless of your record.

scholarships.title: ANRF Ramanujan Fellowship
scholarships.name: ANRF Ramanujan Fellowship

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are Indian or Indian-origin, working abroad at the time of nomination, and aged under 40 - all three are hard eligibility conditions.
Confirm you hold no position or employment in India. A temporary Indian posting disqualifies you, and a permanent offer makes you ineligible.
Choose a host institution in India that is not where you did your doctorate, and get the head of that institution (or an autel) to agree to nominate you before you apply.
Check the institution will provide the R&D, administrative and basic infrastructural support the FAQ requires.
Prepare evidence of a proven research track record - the page makes publications and recognitions the basis of eligibility, and the Fellowship is described as very selective.
Confirm you are moving to a new area or laboratory, not the one where you did your doctorate.
Complete the application on anrfonline.in and route it to your nominator early: the nominator must verify and submit online, which adds an internal step to your timeline.
Be ready to join within six months of the Selection Intimation letter, and to have RTGS bank details in the prescribed format.
Set up annual financial reporting from day one: SE, UC and a progress work report are needed before the next year's grant is released.
important_advice_for_students: This is a research fellowship for a returning scientist, not a study scholarship. If you are a current student without a research career, you are the wrong applicant.

Understand the trade-off before you accept: you may not take any salary from the institute for the full five years, and taking a permanent, tenure-track or contractual position forces you to relinquish the fellowship entirely, with final settlement and closure.
The Rs.1,35,000 per month already includes HRA - do not budget a separate housing allowance on top, because ANRF states it gives only the consolidated figure.
Only one international travel per year is available, so plan conferences and fieldwork around that limit.
Your grant is released year by year, not upfront for five years. Without the SE, UC and progress report, the following year's money does not arrive.
Do not expect your former PhD institute or your PhD supervisors to be able to nominate you - both routes are explicitly excluded.
The award is treated as Scientist-D equivalent in the host institute for TA/DA, which is worth checking against the host's own rules.
common_rejection_risks: Being 40 or older at nomination.
Not working abroad at the time of nomination, or holding any position or employment in India, including a temporary one.
Nominations from the candidate's Ph.D. guides, or from the institute where the Ph.D. was pursued - both are excluded.
Proposing to work in the same area or laboratory where the doctorate was obtained.
Being offered a permanent position at any point - this makes the fellow ineligible.
Taking a salary from the host institute on a permanent, tenure-track or contractual basis, which requires relinquishing the fellowship in total.
Missing the six-month joining deadline after the Selection Intimation letter, which cancels the award automatically.
Failing to submit the SE, UC and progress work report, which blocks the next year's grant release.
A host institution that is the candidate's own doctorate institute.
Not having a proven or outstanding publication and recognition record, since the Fellowship is stated to be very selective on that basis.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any salary from the host institute - the awardee is not entitled to any kind of salary during the tenure.
Salary, pension and employer contributions of any kind from the host institution.
Relocation costs, shipping of personal effects and settling-in costs to India - not listed as covered.
Family costs, children's education and dependants' expenses - not listed as covered.
Health insurance, medical and dental costs - not listed as covered.
Any research cost beyond the Rs.7.00 lakh research grant, and any host-institution overhead beyond Rs.60,000.
Beyond 5 years - there is no provision for extension.
More than one international travel per year.
Funding for the remaining years if the annual SE, UC, progress report or scientific review is not satisfactory.
document_audit: Application: completed on the ANRF online portal at anrfonline.in. No file type, size or signature rules are published for the application attachments.

Joining letter: forwarded by the fellow to ANRF after joining the institute.

Statement of Expenditure (SE) and Utilization Certificate (UC): both must be in the prescribed format available on the ANRF website, and are financial-year wise (1 April to 31 March; first year from the Date of Start to 31 March).
Progress work report: required for the year, in addition to the SE and UC, before the subsequent year's grant is released.
No translation, notarisation or certification rules are published. Download the SE and UC templates from the ANRF website rather than drafting your own.

alerts.message: Rule out your own doctorate institute and your PhD supervisors as nomination routes - both are excluded by the published criteria.

alerts.trigger: On receipt of the Selection Intimation letter
alerts.message: You have six months to join the host institute; after that the award is cancelled automatically.
Submit the SE, UC and progress work report for the year, or the next year's grant will not be released.

alerts.message: A permanent, tenure-track or contractual position makes you ineligible and requires you to relinquish the fellowship in total, subject to final settlement and closure.
Only one international travel is available per year.

submission_workflow: 1. Verify the published eligibility conditions against your own situation, especially age, working-abroad status and absence of any Indian position.
2. Identify a host institution in India other than your doctorate institute, and confirm its willingness to provide R&D, administrative and basic infrastructural support.
3. Secure agreement from the head of that institution (or an autel) to act as nominator.
4. Complete your application on the ANRF online portal at anrfonline.in.
5. Submit the application to your nominator, who verifies it and submits the nomination to ANRF through the online portal only.
6. On award, note the six-month clock from the Selection Intimation letter and plan to join within it.
7. Send the Acceptance Letter with the tentative start month to the host institute, which forwards it to ANRF with RTGS bank details in the prescribed format.
8. Forward your joining letter to ANRF and await the Sanction Order.
9. Annually, submit the SE, UC and progress work report, and declare any IPR, technology, product or process developed or commercialized.
10. If you wish to change host institute, intimate ANRF and submit NOCs from both institutions with any other required documents for approval.
post_award_requirements: Do not accept any salary from the host institute for the duration of the fellowship.
Submit the annual Statement of Expenditure, Utilization Certificate and progress work report in the prescribed formats, financial-year wise.
Submit the joining letter to ANRF on joining, and the Acceptance Letter through the host institute with RTGS bank details.
Cooperate with the scientific review of the work done, on which subsequent-year grant release depends.
Make information on other research grant proposals applied for or sanctioned through the host institute available to ANRF from time to time.
Keep ANRF informed about IPR issues and any technology, product or process developed or commercialized during the tenure.
For a change of host institute, intimate ANRF and obtain approval with NOCs from both institutions.
questions_to_ask_host: Will the institution provide the R&D, administrative and basic infrastructural support the fellowship requires, and is that confirmed in writing?
Who at the institution will act as my nominator, and is that person the head of the organisation or an authorised delegate as the FAQ requires?
Can the institution take me on without a salary, given the fellowship's prohibition on salary during the tenure?
What research facilities, laboratory space and administrative support will I have from day one?
What is the internal timeline for verifying and submitting the nomination through the online portal?
How is the Rs.60,000 overhead administered, and what obligations does it carry for the department?
What is the institution's position on Scientist-D equivalence for TA/DA and on guideship for M.Phil./Ph.D. scholars?

scholarships.description: The Ramanujan Fellowship, operated by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, is a reverse brain drain scheme that brings brilliant Indian and Indian-origin scientists and engineers from abroad to take up scientific research positions in India. It is scientist-specific and highly selective, restricted to candidates below 40 years of age who hold a higher degree such as a PhD in science or engineering, a master's in engineering or technology, or an MD, with adequate professional experience and a proven track record evidenced by publications and recognition. Fellows must not already hold any permanent, tenure-track or contractual position in an Indian institution or university, and must be working abroad at the time of nomination. The fellowship pays Rs 1,35,000 per month consolidated including HRA, plus a research grant of Rs 7.00 lakh per annum and Rs 60,000 per annum in overhead charges to the host institute.

Confirm your research sits inside the Royal Society's natural-sciences remit, and identify which of the five Research Appointment Panels (Ai, Aii, Aiii, Bi, Bii) your work belongs to.
If you are applying from the Republic of Ireland, use the Research Ireland-specific scheme notes and conditions of award rather than the UK terms.
Read the scheme notes and the Royal Society Funding Guidance for the full funding details before you build your budget, because the page only lists cost heads.
Budget against the Â£1,907,400 eight-year maximum, and if you have relocation or visa costs, justify them explicitly in the application because that is the published route to exceeding the cap.
Request any adjustment from adjustments@royalsociety.org or +44 20 7451 2666 well before the close date, including a deadline extension or a Word-format application form.
Write pages 6-8 of the application form for external readers, because from the 2027 round they will be visible to reviewers at the peer-review stage.
important_advice_for_students: This is not a scholarship for study. It is a research-employment fellowship for someone three to eight years past their PhD. If you are still a student or a fresh PhD, you are not eligible yet.

A second PhD, a master's or any taught programme will not be funded by this award. The published cost heads are salary, indirect and estate costs, equipment and research expenses, staff costs, and relocation/visa.

Plan for the mid-term review. Years six to eight are not guaranteed; they depend on satisfactory progress shown at a review at the start of year four, so the first four years determine whether the last three exist.

If you are near the eight-year boundary, the counting date is the round's closing date, not the interview date. If a career break affects your count, read the scheme notes, because the page says only that career breaks are excluded.

Do not rely on the grant cap being flexible beyond relocation and visa. The page says the cap may be exceeded for those costs where well justified, and says nothing about exceeding it for other reasons.

Take up the flexibility on offer. Part-time working, sabbaticals, secondments, parental and sick leave provision and childcare support for conferences are all published entitlements, and using them is not a penalty.
If you need a visa, mention it early: the Royal Society states visa costs are coverable and that a Global Talent Visa can be endorsed through a fast-track process.
common_rejection_risks: Holding a tenure-track faculty position or a permanent academic post, including a proleptic position, in a university or not-for-profit research organisation - an explicit exclusion.
Already leading a research group with responsibility for the research programme and staff or students beyond day-to-day supervision - an explicit exclusion.
Holding an external award as 'Principal Investigator' - an explicit exclusion.
Holding, or having previously held, a nationally competitive research fellowship that meets the published five-part URF-equivalent definition - an explicit exclusion.
Being outside the three-to-eight-year research-experience window at the closing date.
Research outside the natural-sciences remit, or being assigned to the wrong Panel because the primary subject area was misidentified.
Missing the published close date of 09 September 2026 for the 2027 round.
Not requesting an adjustment in time, which can cost deadline time that is not recoverable.
Writing pages 6-8 of the form as internal notes, now that they are visible to reviewers from the peer-review stage.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the maximum of Â£1,907,400 over eight years, except relocation and visa costs where exceeding the cap is well justified in the application
Tuition fees - not a published cost head for this award
The costs of an additional qualification or a taught course, which the award does not fund
Any expense category the Royal Society does not recognise under the published cost heads; the page states the funds 'can cover' the listed items rather than guaranteeing each one
Costs of maintaining a separate, non-funded position, since the fellowship is intended to build an independent research career
document_audit: Applications are submitted in Flexi-GrantÂ®; the page does not publish a document list, file types, file size limits, translation or signature rules.
Read the University Research Fellowship scheme notes and the Royal Society Funding Guidance for the full funding details and any document requirements; both are published as downloads from this page.
Republic of Ireland applicants must also read the Republic of Ireland scheme notes and the separate Conditions of Award for Republic of Ireland applicants.
Note the assessment streamlining change: no changes to application content were made, but pages 6-8 of the application form will be visible to reviewers from the peer review stage onwards.
If you need the application form in a different format, such as a Word document, request it from the Grants team - it is published as an available adjustment, not something you can do yourself.

Practical consequence: download the scheme notes and Funding Guidance first, and confirm any institutional letter or host agreement requirement with your department, because the page does not name one.

referee_tracking.instructions: Longlisted applications are subject to independent peer review after the initial panel assessment. The peer review stage is the stage from which pages 6-8 of the application form become visible to reviewers. The Royal Society does not publish the number of referees, how they are nominated, or what they must include, so check the scheme notes.

Following eligibility checks, applications are initially assessed by a minimum of two panel members with the most appropriate scientific expertise, with additional expertise co-opted to the Panel where needed. Panel Chairs oversee the shortlist for interview, and the Panels confirm the funding recommendations at the end of the interview stage.

Count research years since your PhD as at the closing date, excluding career breaks; you must be in the three-to-eight-year window.
Work to the Â£1,907,400 eight-year maximum, and put relocation and visa costs in the application with justification if you need to exceed the cap.
Close date for the 2027 round.
Attend the in-person interview at the Royal Society; prepare to show the importance and scientific validity of your work and how the award leads to your independence.

submission_workflow: 1. Verify eligibility against the research-experience window, the natural-sciences remit and all four disqualifiers.
2. Identify your primary subject area and Panel (Ai, Aii, Aiii, Bi or Bii).
3. Read the scheme notes, the Royal Society Funding Guidance, and the Republic of Ireland variants if relevant.
4. Request any adjustment from the Grants team, including a deadline extension or a different form format.
5. Build the budget against the Â£1,907,400 cap, justifying any relocation or visa costs that would take you over it.
6. Submit the application in Flexi-GrantÂ® before the published close date, writing pages 6-8 for external readers.
7. Await eligibility checks and initial assessment by at least two panel members.
8. If longlisted, respond promptly to independent peer review.
9. If shortlisted, prepare for and attend the in-person interview at the Royal Society.
10. On award, plan for the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four and the continuation of years six to eight.
post_award_requirements: Satisfy the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four, on which years six to eight depend.
Build an independent research career at a UK university or research institution, or in the Republic of Ireland.
Comply with the relevant conditions of award - the Research Ireland-specific conditions for Republic of Ireland-based fellows.
Use the fellowship within the published cost heads, with relocation and visa costs justified in the application.
Take up the published flexibility provisions where needed - part-time working, sabbaticals, secondments, parental and sick leave, and childcare support for conferences and research visits.
questions_to_ask_host: Is there a letter of support or heads-of-department agreement required from my institution, and at what stage?
What salary or salary increment will sit under the 'contribution to the award holder's salary' head at my institution, and what indirect and estate cost rates apply?
How does the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four work internally, and what evidence of progress will my department need to provide?
Are the funds portable if I move institution during the fellowship, and what would that require?
What are the PDRA and PhD studentship salary scales my institution would use for the staff-cost head?
If I am based in the Republic of Ireland, how do the Research Ireland-specific scheme notes and conditions of award differ from the UK terms?
What institutional commitments follow if I take a sabbatical or a secondment during the fellowship?

scholarships.description: The Royal Society University Research Fellowship is an eight-year independent research fellowship for outstanding early career scientists, with a dedicated Royal Society - Research Ireland arm for fellowships hosted at a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body in the Republic of Ireland. Research Ireland meets the cost of awards based in the Republic of Ireland, while UK-based awards are funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade. Funding covers a contribution to salary, indirect and estate costs, equipment and research expenses, staff costs, and relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants. The 2027 round closed on 9 September 2026 with decisions due by 31 May 2027.

Irish and UK candidates are assessed together through the normal Royal Society peer review process. Historical success rates are 7% (2022/23), 6.4% (2023/24), 6.8% (2024/25) and 6.3% (2025/26). scholarships.name: Sapienza University of Rome Scholarships

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you graduated from Sapienza within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the call year - the post-degree scheme is for Sapienza graduates only.

Check your age against the published limits: the Q&A describes the eligible group as 'all students under 29' and the requirements section says candidates 'need to be 28 years old or younger by the announcement of the call'. If you are 28, confirm the reference date with the scholarship office rather than assuming.
Match your degree class to a CUN disciplinary area. An application to a CUN area for which you do not hold the degree is rejected outright.

Secure the host yourself - there is no list of hosting countries or institutions - and get an official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper, with the institution's official signature and stamp, stating the course name, internal structure and duration or the programme of activities.
For non-Italian citizens, confirm the host is outside your country of origin as well as outside Italy.
Prepare the application in PDF using the model attached to the call, with the self-declaration of publications and titles in the same format.
If your host document is not in English, get it translated into Italian. An English document needs no translation.
Send everything by PEC to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it only. The University says 'exclusively', so email or in-person submission will not be accepted.
If you hold a PhD scholarship, decide now whether you are willing to renounce it - that is the only route to benefit.
Prepare for the interview to test both disciplinary preparation and the language your host requires.
important_advice_for_students: Do not assume a fee waiver. No tuition payment at the host is described anywhere; treat the â‚¬1,290.00 per month as your entire benefit and budget your own costs around it.

Start the host search immediately. There is no list of hosting countries or institutions and the University expects you to approach institutions yourself, which is normally the slowest part of this application.

Watch the income cap. The published rule is that a holder cannot possess, for the major part of the calendar year of the scholarship, an income superior to 'â‚¬ 7.750,000' - the figure is printed exactly that way on the official page. Get the intended threshold clarified with the scholarship office before you rely on it, because the notation is ambiguous.

Do not stack other scholarships. Holding any other scholarship during the period abroad is prohibited, with a narrow exception for national or foreign institutional grants that integrate a foreign stay.
For PhD students, the practical cost of this award is your PhD scholarship: you must renounce it, and you need faculty board authorisation to suspend doctoral studies.

Plan the timing carefully. You can only start receiving from the day after the interview, and the activity must begin within the end of the following calendar year, so a late decision can cost you months.

The two schemes are different. If you are still enrolled, the International Thesis Scholarship (â‚¬2,821.00 gross, at least two months, via your faculty) is the relevant one, not the post-degree monthly award.
Note the payment blackout: Sapienza scholarship payments are suspended in December and January because of year-end closing procedures, so do not assume a December instalment arrives.
common_rejection_risks: Not having graduated from Sapienza University of Rome.
Being outside the published age limit at the announcement of the call.
Applying to a CUN disciplinary area that does not match your degree class - the application is rejected as incongruous or inconsistent.
Submitting more than one application, or an application covering more than one CUN area.
Missing the published deadline - 16 September 2026 for the 2026 call, under penalty of exclusion.
Sending the application by ordinary email instead of PEC, which the University says must be used exclusively.
Submitting the application in the wrong format or without the model attached to the call.
Omitting the Italian translation when the host document is not in English - the translation is required in that case only.
A host certification missing the required content (course name, internal structure, duration, or programme of activities) or not on headed and certified paper with official signature and stamp.
For non-Italian citizens, a host institution in their own country of origin.
A total selection score under 35 points, which is stated to be insufficient.
PhD students unwilling to renounce an existing PhD scholarship, or lacking faculty board authorisation.
Specialisation school students who already hold another scholarship, or who are winners of a 'Scuola di specializzazione' scholarship.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition or enrolment fees at the host institution - not a published benefit of either scheme
Flights, travel and relocation to and from the host country
Accommodation at the host location
Health, medical and travel insurance
Books, materials, equipment and research costs for the thesis placement
Any income above the published threshold, which holders are not permitted to have for the major part of the award year
Anything arising from holding a second scholarship, which is prohibited during the award period
document_audit: The application must be in PDF format, drafted according to the model attached to the call - use the model, not a free-form CV.
Submission channel: certified and accredited personal electronic mail (PEC) to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it, exclusively. Ordinary email, hand delivery and post are not accepted.

Attachment 1: official certification from the foreign institution or international university (or a certified declaration by a professor of that university) containing acceptance or possible acceptability for the chosen course of study or post-lauream specialization activity. It must be in a certified format with the institution's official signature and stamp.

Attachment 1 content check: it must state the name of the course, its internal structure and respective duration (for a course of study), or the programme of activities to be completed (for a post-lauream specialization activity).
Attachment 2: self-declaration of the candidate's publications and previously attained titles, in PDF, in the format specified in the application model.
Attachment 3: translation into Italian of the documentation in Attachment 1, required only if that document was originally released in a language other than English.

After selection: a self-declaration that you possess the compulsory requirements in the call, with the obligation to maintain them for the whole scholarship period, and a new certification from the international institution giving the starting and final date of the activity.

No file size limit, page limit, signature rule or certification/legalisation requirement for copies is published beyond the certified-format and stamp requirement for the host certification. Download the current call and model from the Amministrazione trasparente portal and check for any attachment-specific rules before sending.
Certificazione Unica, if you need it, is obtained through https://uniroma1.u-web.cineca.it/ using SPID or CIE credentials.

referee_tracking.role: Selection Committee for the CUN disciplinary area
referee_tracking.instructions: A Selection Committee is nominated for each disciplinary area and scores the application out of 100, with up to 50 points for the degree final grade, previously attained titles and publications, and up to 50 points for the interview. No external referees or letters of reference are requested in the published application requirements; the Committee formally reports the reason for excluding any candidate.

Not a referee in the academic sense, but a mandatory signatory: they must issue an official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper with the institution's official signature and stamp, containing the course name, internal structure and duration or the programme of activities. A certified declaration by a professor of the host university is accepted as an alternative.

Sapienza scholarship payments are suspended in these months because of year-end closing procedures.

submission_workflow: 1. Verify eligibility: Sapienza graduate within the last viable session of the preceding academic year, within the published age limit, with a degree class matching a CUN area.
2. Choose one CUN disciplinary area and one intended number of months, remembering the Committee decides the final number.

3. Approach a foreign host institution or supervisor yourself and obtain the official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper with official signature and stamp, containing the course name, internal structure and duration or the programme of activities.
4. Confirm the host is outside Italy and, if you are a non-Italian citizen, outside your country of origin.
5. Download the call and the application model from the Amministrazione trasparente portal.
6. Complete the application in PDF using the model, and prepare the self-declaration of publications and titles in the same format.
7. Obtain an Italian translation of the host document if it is not in English.
8. Send the application and all three attachments by PEC to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it before the deadline.
9. Monitor the published interview list and your PEC inbox, then attend the interview.
10. If selected, submit the self-declaration of compulsory requirements and obtain the new host certification with the start and final dates.
post_award_requirements: Maintain the compulsory requirements stated in the call for the entire period of the scholarship, as confirmed by self-declaration.
Do not hold any other scholarship during the period of the activity abroad, except national or foreign institutional grants that integrate a foreign stay.
Keep income at or below the published threshold for the major part of the calendar year of the scholarship.
Ensure the host institution issues a new certification giving the starting and final date of the specialization activity.
Begin the activity from the day after the interview and no later than the end of the calendar year following the year in which the contest was promulgated.
For PhD students, maintain faculty board authorisation for the suspension of doctoral studies and remain without a PhD scholarship.
If you decide to renounce, notify the offices as soon as possible so the next candidates can be contacted, and return any first instalment already received.
questions_to_ask_host: Will the institution issue the acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper with its official signature and stamp, and does it state the course name, internal structure and duration?
Is the activity arranged as a course of study or as a post-lauream specialization activity, and does the host document reflect that distinction?
What are the start and end dates of the activity, and can the host confirm them in writing at the end so I can obtain the required post-selection certification?
What language will the activity be conducted in, so I can prepare for the interview on that language?
What additional costs will I face at the host - fees, accommodation, insurance - that the â‚¬1,290.00 per month will not cover?
For the International Thesis Scholarship, what is my faculty's Call deadline and which faculty presidency do I apply to?
What is the intended interpretation of the published income threshold, given the notation on the official page?

scholarships.description: The Padua International Excellence Scholarship Programme awards up to 76 scholarships to high-achieving international students entering an English-taught first-cycle or master's degree at the University of Padua. Each award is worth €8,000.00 gross per academic year plus exemption from student fees, with beneficiaries paying only the regional fee and the revenue stamp. Scholarships run for a maximum of two years on master's courses and three years on bachelor's or single-cycle courses, paid in two instalments and conditional on earning at least 20 CFU by 30 November each year. Eligibility follows automatically from the degree course application.

applicant_utility.summary: A ministry-funded MAECI scholarship of €8,000 for one academic year, paid in 12 monthly instalments, to study the ItAS master's in Italian for Teaching to Foreigners at the University for Foreigners of Perugia. It is a cultural diplomacy instrument of the Mattei Plan for Africa, designed explicitly to produce Italian teachers in the graduates' home countries, so the intended career path of teaching Italian abroad should be visible in your motivation. Selection is run by Perugia with its partner institutions and designated representatives of the Italian diplomatic mission in your country, which means the route to an application is local and personal rather than a portal you can simply download.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Young graduates from Algeria, Cameroon, Egypt, Ethiopia, Libya, Morocco, Senegal, Somalia, South Africa or Tunisia who want to teach Italian and can commit to the ItAS master's in Perugia.

Missing the locally communicated closing date, since the Ministry does not publish one on the ITALYOU page
Failing to secure a place on the ItAS master's, without which the scholarship cannot be used
For 3rd-edition holders, not reaching 40 CFU, which blocks renewal

applicant_utility.summary: MEXT's undergraduate award covers the full package a student in Japan needs: JPY 117,000 a month, no tuition or entrance fees, paid economy flights both ways, and a preparatory year of Japanese before your degree starts. Two routes exist - embassy recommendation through your own Japanese diplomatic mission, or university recommendation through a quota-holding Japanese university - and the route you pick changes who screens you first. Whichever you choose, the fixed 1-7 April 2027 arrival window and the embassy's own document deadline are the two dates to build your year around.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School leavers under 25 who want a fully funded undergraduate degree in Japan and can demonstrate strong Japanese, English, mathematics and science examination results.

Book the physician-signed medical certificate on MEXT's prescribed form well in advance
Confirm you can be in Japan between 1 and 7 April 2027 before applying
common_rejection_risks: Missing the embassy's own deadline while looking for a central MEXT date that does not exist
Weak written examination results; every applicant sits all subjects, including science-faculty candidates taking two sciences
Submitting files with untranslated documents or missing the second copy packet
Being unable to arrive in the fixed early-April window, which cancels travel support
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel to the nearest international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel insurance, baggage costs, and personal spending during the first weeks before the allowance starts.

Medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and six-year pharmacy stretch the scholarship to seven years

applicant_utility.summary: If you are already an undergraduate majoring in Japanese language or culture outside Japan, this scholarship sends you to a designated Japanese university for one fully funded year: JPY 117,000 per month, no tuition, round-trip airfare, and your home-university enrolment preserved for your return. The screening leans heavily on Japanese - the written examination at the embassy is in Japanese, and you need enough Japanese to be taught at a Japanese university. Applications run December to February for an October arrival, so the practical window opens right after the autumn term starts.

Insufficient Japanese to receive education at a Japanese university or to pass the Japanese written examination
Losing home-university enrolment status, which ends eligibility

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are enrolled full-time in one of the six published categories of Japanese institution and hold 'Student' residence status.
Confirm you are privately financed - no Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship and no Foreign Government Scholarship.

Add up your own income from other sources. The total allowance excluding enrolment fee and tuition must average 90,000 yen or less per month, and if anyone supports you while you are in Japan their annual income must be under 5 million yen.

Check the language condition now: JLPT N2 or above, EJU Japanese 200 points or more, a JASSO-recognised level, or CEFR B2 or above - unless you are at a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course or a Japanese language institute.
Make sure you are not on JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program and are not holding a scholarship that cannot be combined with the Honors Scholarships.

Ask your institution's international office immediately whether it can recommend you. JASSO states the number an institution can recommend depends on its enrolled international students, and that you may not be able to apply.
Ask for the application guidelines, because the grading criteria and the document list are set there and are not published on the JASSO page.
Note the enrolment month: the award runs April to March for a 12-month period, or October to March for 6 months.
important_advice_for_students: Do not apply to JASSO. The official instruction is to ask the staff at your educational institution, and there is no JASSO application portal for this scholarship.
Do not treat this as tuition funding. JASSO's own allowance rule is defined as 'excluding enrollment fee, tuition fee, etc.', so you still pay enrolment fee and tuition in full.
Budget on 48,000 yen per month (30,000 if you are at a Japanese language institute). That is the whole award, and it is capped at 12 or 6 months - there is no published renewal route.
Check your institution before you invest effort. JASSO explicitly warns that some institutions may not be able to recommend anyone, so your school's willingness is the first gate, not your grades.
Watch the 90,000 yen allowance ceiling. Family support, part-time work and small awards can push you over it, and the rule is an average per month across the year.
The monthly signing is not a formality. Failing to sign the JASSO-designated sheet each month at the international students' office is a breach of the published grant conditions.
Selection results are published in Japanese only on the JASSO page, so ask your institution how they will tell you.
common_rejection_risks: Holding a Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship or any Foreign Government Scholarship, which makes the student not privately financed.
Not holding 'Student' residence status.
An allowance above 90,000 yen per month on average, excluding enrolment fee and tuition fee.
A financial supporter in Japan with annual income of 5 million yen or more.
Holding JASSO Student Exchange Support Program support, or a scholarship that cannot be combined with the Honors Scholarships.
Failing the published grading criteria in the application guidelines.
Failing the Japanese or English language condition, unless at a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course or a Japanese language institute.
Being at an institution that does not nominate candidates - JASSO states this may be your situation.
Not signing the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees at your institution - the allowance cap is defined as excluding tuition fee, and no waiver is published
The enrolment/admission fee - also excluded from the allowance definition and not covered
Housing, food and local transport - the fixed monthly stipend is not described as a living-cost payment
Books, materials and course-related costs
Medical insurance premiums and health costs not covered by insurance
Flight, visa and relocation costs - travel coverage is not published
Everything after 12 months from an April enrolment, or after 6 months from an October enrolment
document_audit: The official JASSO page publishes no application document list and no file type, size, translation or signature rules, so there is nothing on the page to audit against.
The one document the page names is the JASSO-designated sheet that the holder must sign every month at the international students' office - a post-award obligation, not an application attachment.
The application guidelines, which contain the grading criteria the candidate must meet, are not published on this page; obtain them from your institution.
The 2026 selection results are published in Japanese only, so no English result document is available from JASSO.
Practical consequence: get the document list, language, format and any certification rules from your institution's international office in writing, because JASSO publishes none.

alerts.message: Ask your institution's staff whether it can recommend candidates for this scholarship - JASSO says the number depends on the institution's enrolled international students.

Sign the JASSO-designated sheet at your institution's international students' office - this is a published condition of the grant.

submission_workflow: 1. Verify the six published enrolment categories and that you are full-time with 'Student' residence status.
2. Verify you are privately financed and are not on JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program.
3. Check the allowance cap of 90,000 yen per month and the 5 million yen supporter income limit.
4. Check the language condition, unless you are at a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course or a Japanese language institute.
5. Ask the staff at your educational institution how to apply and obtain the application guidelines, which set the grading criteria.
6. Have your institution recommend you to JASSO.
7. On award, sign the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office and cooperate with the JASSO career path survey.

scholarships.description: The JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a stipend for privately financed international students in Japan with excellent academic and character records who face financial difficulties. It is not open for direct application: each educational institution nominates candidates to JASSO, and the number of candidates depends on the institution's international enrolment. The stipend is JPY 48,000 per month at graduate and undergraduate level and JPY 30,000 per month at Japanese language institutes, for 12 or 6 months.

eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.

scholarships.description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.
scholarships.duration: One-off payment of EUR 5,000, received in the first year of studies. The scholarship is not described as multi-year or recurring.

applicant_utility.summary: This scholarship is won in the MSc application, not alongside it: the form, the reference letter and the English certificate all have to be inside your admission application by 1 December 2026, and TU Delft states outright that a missed scholarship deadline means the application is never reviewed. With only two awards per faculty, your odds depend heavily on which faculty you apply through, so the choice of programme is also a choice of competition level. Think of the top-10% guideline as a filter rather than a hurdle: no ranking proof is requested, but a borderline transcript in a competitive faculty will simply be outranked.

Check your CGPA against 75% of the scale maximum and any country-specific requirement, since the minimum must be met at the time of application with no rounding

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition-only award, so budget for roughly EUR 16,500 of first-year costs yourself (living allowance, health and liability insurance, residence permit fee), payable to WUR before 1 July 2027. Two hard gates sit before the money: you must hold one of 21 listed nationalities and no EU/EFTA nationality, and you need a GPA of 80% or higher with unconditional admission. Even after clearing those, entry to the final stage is by invitation in March-April 2027 and a lottery then picks the winners, so treat this as one line in a funding plan rather than a certainty. Everything, including your bachelor's diploma and English test result, must be complete before 1 December 2026.

The decisive factor is mission fit: forty percent of the score is the match between you and the mission's own project description, so read the Call for Proposals annexes before choosing a position. applicant_utility.summary: The two-deadline structure is the main trap: submitting in OSIRIS by 31 January only starts the process, and Student Admissions may send the application back for the handling fee or for missing documents, which means the real deadline for you is well before 14 February. Your faculty quota is the other thing to understand, because 26 awards are split unevenly across six faculties, so applying to the Faculty of Science, with nine places, is a materially different bet from a faculty with one or two. Since admission and the scholarship are decided as separate processes, full admission does not imply selection, and the award's value depends on the programme's actual tuition fee.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/non-EEA applicants with outstanding grades and a degree from outside the Netherlands, who are admitted to an English-taught Radboud Master's starting 1 September 2027 and can fund their own living costs in Nijmegen.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify your faculty's quota for 2027/2028 (Arts 2, Law 2, Nijmegen School of Management 5, Philosophy Theology and Religious Studies 1, Science 9, Social Sciences 7) and weigh it in your programme choice
Confirm your programme is not an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree Master's, which are excluded
Get the English proficiency result in hand before 14 February rather than leaving it as a later upload
Prepare two academic reference letters in advance, or written permission to reuse the ones already filed with your Master's application
Treat the motivation letter as part of the scholarship case, since its quality and relevance are scored under ambition
Budget for roughly EUR 12,000 a year of living costs in Nijmegen, since the scholarship covers none of them
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 14 February completion deadline after submitting in OSIRIS on 31 January, because incomplete applications are excluded from selection outright
Holding any prior education in the Netherlands, which breaches the eligibility rule unless it is an exchange that formed part of the foreign bachelor's degree
Assuming admission to the Master's programme implies selection for the scholarship, when the two processes are separate
Applying to an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree Master's programme, which is not eligible
Leaving the handling fee unpaid or a document illegible, which triggers a resubmission cycle inside the two-week window
Passing fewer than all first-year courses in a two-year programme, which forfeits the grant for the second year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living and study costs in the Netherlands are explicitly not covered, so rent, food, local transport, course materials and the remaining tuition of EUR 2,771 must be funded from your own resources or from the NL Scholarship, with which the Radboud Scholarship can be combined.
document_audit: Documents already uploaded for the Master's application can be re-uploaded for the scholarship, so there is no need to duplicate effort, but the scholarship file must still be complete
Follow Radboud's published reference letter guidelines, since the quality of the two references is an explicit scoring criterion
A curriculum vitae is required alongside the two letters; a CV-only file without both reference letters will not satisfy the upload requirement
Applications are read individually by the faculty selection committee and some programmes hold interviews, so check whether your programme interviews before assuming a paper-only process
The scholarship's requirements follow the Profiling Fund's regulations, so any change in those regulations can affect the terms
alerts: The EUR 2,771 tuition figure is published as an amount to be confirmed and the EUR 19,000 is only illustrative depending on your programme, so do not fix your budget to either number
For a two-year Master's you must pass all courses in the first year to qualify for the grant again in year two
Only 26 scholarships exist for 2027/2028 across six faculties, with the distribution published on the page
Radboud University holds scholarship Q&A sessions, and questions should go to the Student Life and International Mobility team rather than to the application email
The final decision date of before mid-April 2027 is marked as subject to change, so do not treat it as a fixed commitment for visa and housing planning
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission and scholarship in one OSIRIS submission, then a Student Admissions completeness check with resubmission if needed, faculty committee review for academic excellence, ambition and references, and a decision from Student Life and International Mobility before mid-April 2027.

Final decisions are notified before mid-April 2027.
scholarships.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a highly selective Radboud University scheme for talented, highly motivated non-EU/non-EEA students with outstanding study results, covering English-taught Master's programmes. A scholarship reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 (the university notes the amount is to be confirmed) instead of an illustrative EUR 19,000, and additionally covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs. Costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028, allocated across six faculties, and selection is based on academic excellence, ambition and the quality of two reference letters.

applicant_utility.summary: The flagship route into a funded master's at EUR is the Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship, where the school pages publish a €17.500 package that waives tuition in full and pays €1.200 a month plus a €249 one-off allowance and an immigration-fee waiver, so your file has to prove two things at once: academic excellence and genuine financial need. The decision is taken school by school, so the amount is only the starting point - your deadline, portal and document list are set by the faculty you apply to, not by the university-wide listing. Start the paperwork early, because certified transcripts with wet signatures and a certified GPA statement routinely take weeks to obtain and incomplete applications are not reviewed. If you are a first-generation, refugee, disabled or otherwise underrepresented applicant, the parallel Erasmus Trustfonds and TSH Changemaker Scholarship (€9.895 plus a year of Social Hub housing) may be the stronger route.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving EEA and non-EEA applicants who cannot self-fund a Dutch master's and can document real financial need; the Changemaker variant specifically suits underrepresented and first-generation applicants.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a family of faculty-run awards rather than one central scholarship: the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship is decided by each faculty or Graduate School, so only your target programme's page carries the binding amount, criteria and document list. The money works as a tuition reimbursement, not a waiver, which means you must be able to front the full fee and fund Amsterdam living costs before any payout arrives. Competition is steep - Economics and Business alone received about 150 applications for 12 awards last year - so pair this with external funding from the start rather than treating it as a plan A.

scholarships.description: The University of Amsterdam runs several scholarship programmes for talented and motivated international students, published from one official Fees and funding hub. Each faculty also runs its own scholarships for international Master's students, covering Economics and Business, Humanities, Law, Science and Social and Behavioural Sciences, and a separate set of Bachelor's scholarships exists. The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship equals the tuition fee but the UvA states it cannot be used as a partial tuition waiver, so the recipient still pays the full tuition, payable in monthly instalments. Amounts are set annually and are published by each faculty.

scholarships.description: Tulī Takes Flight scholarships are funded by the New Zealand Ministry of Education and administered by the Pacific Education Foundation to reduce financial barriers to tertiary study and vocational training for Pacific people. They form part of the government's gesture of goodwill and reconciliation to Aotearoa Pacific communities following its 2021 apology for the Dawn Raids. Awards can be made for either vocational or academic study and can run for one, two or three years. For the 2027 round the Ministry states applications are closed and outcomes will be notified by 18 March 2027; a new annual round is expected to open in the same late-summer window each year.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a three-month paid internship placement at NASA JPL, not a degree scholarship, so the value arrives as flights, accommodation and a daily living allowance rather than a single bursary figure - budget for the gap between the allowance and Southern California living costs yourself. Because MBIE shortlists and then hands its shortlist to JPL for the final decision, the strength of your match to a specific JPL project area matters more than your GPA once you clear the 3.0 threshold. Start your enrolment proof and visa paperwork early: the Ministry requires evidence that you will be or already are enrolled in postgraduate STEM study at a New Zealand institution before the award is made.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New Zealand citizen postgraduate STEM students with a 3.0+ GPA on the US 4.0 scale who can be in Southern California in person for the whole of July to September 2027.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold New Zealand citizenship only - check your status against NASA's Designated Countries List, since holding or having held citizenship of a listed country disqualifies you outright
Convert your New Zealand grades to the US 4.0 GPA scale and confirm you are at or above 3.0 before you start the form
Pick your two research areas from the Ministry's published list and write them so they map onto a plausible JPL project rather than your thesis title
If you will finish your current qualification before 2027, secure a written offer or enrolment pathway from a New Zealand tertiary institution now
Budget for travel and medical insurance, visa costs and any additional expenses the allowance will not reach
common_rejection_risks: Failing the NASA Designated Countries List exclusion through dual or former citizenship - this is checked before anything else and is not waivable
Nominating research areas that do not line up with JPL's current mission priorities, so the shortlist never reaches a JPL reviewer who wants you
Being under the 3.0 GPA threshold once grades are converted to the US scale, which is stricter than it looks for New Zealand B/B+ averages
Being unable to prove postgraduate enrolment at a New Zealand institution before the award is made, which stalls the application at the last step
Not being able to commit to the full in-person July to September 2027 window because of teaching, fieldwork or another placement
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any expense beyond the internship itself: MBIE states the scholarship only covers costs associated with participating in the internship and that additional expenses remain the recipient's responsibility, so visa fees, insurance excesses, personal spending and anything outside the published categories sit with you.
document_audit: The only document the Ministry names is proof of postgraduate enrolment at a New Zealand tertiary institution - and it must exist before the award, not before the deadline
Your academic record will be read on the US GPA scale, so supply the conversion rather than leaving JPL to guess
No closing date is published, so do not assume the round stays open until an advertised finish; contact the New Zealand Space Agency if you need certainty
alerts: The 2027 round opened on 1 October 2026 and the Ministry publishes no closing date - treat the window as short
MBIE assessment is not the final word: final shortlisted candidates are submitted to JPL for final selection
Applicants who hold or have held citizenship of a country on NASA's Designated Countries List are not eligible at all
Recipients take on participant code of conduct, insurance and outreach obligations - these are conditions, not suggestions
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online through the MBIE recruitment link, nominate your two research areas, then MBIE assesses and forwards its shortlist to JPL, which makes the final selection.

scholarships.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students a fully supported three-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, working alongside scientists and engineers on space missions and research. Applications for the 2027 scholarship opened on 1 October 2026 and the internship runs from July to September 2027. The scholarship covers return economy flights to the United States, accommodation, a daily living allowance and reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, and hold at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.

scholarships.description: The Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship is the early-career scheme within the Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships, administered by Royal Society Te Apārangi on behalf of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. important_advice_for_students: Do not apply if you are an overseas candidate; the page states overseas candidates may contact advisers for information, but eligibility requires New Zealand citizenship or a Permanent Resident Visa plus five of the previous ten years in New Zealand

It supports outstanding all-round students to undertake postgraduate study at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom. Up to three scholars are elected from New Zealand each year, and the Scholarship covers fees, accommodation and living costs for up to three years. scholarships.description: The Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships are annual awards funded by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board, established in 1945, and administered through the Ministry of Education. They are awarded to exceptional Māori students for vocational or tertiary study who demonstrate values aligned with those of the 28th (Māori) Battalion. Following a $100,000 per year increase from the 2026-27 Budget, 14 scholarships are awarded each year across five schemes: 5 VET, 4 undergraduate, 3 master's, 1 Master of Education research and 1 doctoral. Do not confuse this with a degree scholarship; it funds research employment and didactic activity for 6 to 24 months and confers no academic credential
Do note that age, discipline and country of origin are all expressly not barriers - 'regardless of their age, discipline or country of origin', including Polish scientists permanently abroad

Do exploit the Special Track if you hold a Seal of Excellence or MSCA4Ukraine Accolade of Excellence, because NAWA treats those European certificates as binding verification of application quality and exempts such applications from the remaining Principal Investigator requirements
Do make sure your institution has both a Principal Investigator and an Inviting Person identified, since funding includes remuneration for both roles
Do not delay on the institution side; because the institution is the applicant, their internal deadline comes before NAWA's and is not published
Do read the Regulations of Institutional Programmes for Researchers (Appendix 1) and the Beneficiary Agreement template (Appendix 2), which govern the funding relationship

applicant_utility.summary: This is a job, not a grant: NAWA funds a call budget of PLN 17 million in total and the host institution gives you a full-time employment contract, so your actual salary is negotiated with the host rather than set by NAWA. That makes finding the right host the real work - NAWA itself points applicants at researchinpoland.org for exactly that reason. Because the pilot round closed on 27 February 2026 with results due by 31 July 2026, there is currently nothing to apply for; treat this as background for the next call and use the interval to build a host relationship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers (doctorate within the last seven years) and established team leaders currently at a top-200 global university who want a funded research group in Poland.
application_readiness_checklist: Work out which track you fit - Junior Fellow if your doctorate is no more than seven years old at the deadline, Senior Fellow if you have led research teams - because the evidence you prepare differs sharply
Confirm your current institution appears in the Shanghai, QS or THE top 200 in a current edition, since NAWA names all three rankings as qualifying
Start conversations with prospective Polish hosts early and use researchinpoland.org, NAWA's recommended platform, to find a supervisor
Negotiate the employment package with the host directly: NAWA publishes a call budget, not a salary scale
Register for the NAWA applicant portal at programs.nawa.gov.pl and check the Call for applications and Documents pages when a new round opens
common_rejection_risks: Assuming NAWA pays you directly - the money flows through the host's employment contract, so a weak host commitment sinks the application
Applying to the wrong track for your career stage, particularly Senior Fellow applicants without documented team-leadership experience
Relying on a ranking position from an older edition when your institution has dropped out of the top 200
Looking for a salary figure on NAWA's site and finding only the PLN 17 million total call budget, then misjudging the offer
Missing that the published pilot round has already closed and waiting for a portal that has no open call
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published. NAWA publishes only the total call budget of PLN 17 million, so relocation, family and any costs outside the host employment contract must be negotiated case by case with the host institution.
document_audit: NAWA's 'Call for applications' sub-page carries no published content, so the document list must come from the 'Dokumenty do pobrania' (Documents to download) section when a round opens

Evidence of research-team leadership is needed for Senior Fellow and is not something you can assemble at the last minute

scholarships.selection_notes:
Applications are subject to formal and merit-based assessment in accordance with the Regulations for Institutional Programmes for Researchers
Merit-based assessment is conducted in three stages: initial assessment by the Team of Experts (applications without the Team's recommendation are not submitted further), assessment by two External Reviewers, and final assessment by the Team of Experts
The final stage of the assessment process may include interviews with candidates for Principal Investigators to discuss research plans and clarify concerns raised
Criterion 1: The Principal Investigator's scientific or academic career and scientific achievements to date - to what extent achievements are internationally recognizable and outstanding for the discipline and career stage (Team of Experts 15 points, External Reviewers 10 points)
Criterion 2: Justification for the selection of the Host institution as the place of project implementation, including the proposed support for the PI and the benefits the Host institution gains (External Reviewers 10 points, Team of Experts 15 points)
Criterion 3: Scientific or technological quality of the Project - originality, innovative nature of the research hypothesis, research tools and methods, planned results, potential risks and contingency plan, and plans for applying for grants (External Reviewers 10 points, Team of Experts 15 points)
Criterion 4: Impact of the Project on the development of science (External Reviewers 10 points, Team of Experts 15 points)
Maximum total score 100 points (Team of Experts 15, External Reviewers 40, Team of Experts 45)
An application may be left without consideration for formal reasons also at a later stage of assessment
