scholarships.description: The Bekker NAWA Programme supports the international mobility of PhD students, scientists and academic teachers from Polish scientific and academic units by funding research fellowships of 3 to 24 months at recognised research centres abroad. It covers the scholarship holder's living expenses during the stay together with a mobility allowance, and the amount may be increased for a spouse, underage children, or an assistant with a severe or moderate disability. The 2026 call closed on 29 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Polish time, for projects starting between 1 March and 1 October 2027, with applications in English through NAWA's ICT system.

applicant_utility.summary: Walczak is an outbound mobility award, not a degree scholarship: you keep your post and travel to a foreign medical centre for one to six months, choosing between a teaching, research or clinical track, with up to PLN 32,000 per month of stay covering a stipend, living and accommodation costs and travel. If you are a doctoral student or researcher on the scientific path and can stay longer than three months, you can also claim a one-off PLN 20,000. Eligibility is specifically for medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences, so a social science or humanities applicant will not fit. There is currently no open call: the only announcement on NAWA's pages is no. 41/2024 of 5 December 2024, and the programme page's reference to a call running until 31 January 2024 is out of date, so watch NAWA's Walczak pages rather than assuming a fixed annual round.

Relying on the programme page's 31 January 2024 deadline, which is out of date on NAWA's own site
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Costs above PLN 32,000 per month of stay, any tuition element, which the programme does not describe, and any part of a trip outside the chosen one-to-six month window.

scholarships.description: The Walczak NAWA Programme funds international mobility for researchers in medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences connected with Polish institutions, letting them carry out research and work alongside leading specialists in the best medical centres worldwide. Participants choose a teaching, research or clinical track for a stay of one to six months. Eligible applicants are PhD students and doctoral-school participants, doctors with at least a doctorate working in hospitals and other medical institutions, and academic teachers in the medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences. The support, described by NAWA as covering a stipend, living and accommodation costs and travel expenses, amounts to up to PLN 32,000 for each month of stay, with a one-off PLN 20,000 for doctoral students and researchers on the scientific path whose stay exceeds three months. NAWA's call page still shows the December 2024 edition as the most recent announcement.

applicant_utility.summary: The Visegrad Scholarship pays EUR 3,500 per semester directly to the scholar, plus EUR 2,000 per semester to the host institution, for one or two semesters of full-time master's or post-master's study or research across more than 190 institutions in Central and Eastern Europe. The eligibility geography is the part applicants underestimate: your host country must differ from your citizenship country, your previous studies must have been completed in yet another country, and the host must sit more than 150 km from your current university or permanent residence. The call opens 1 January 2027 and shuts hard at noon on 15 April 2027, with results at the end of May, so mobility realistically starts in September or October.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's, doctoral and postdoctoral students and researchers from the Visegrad Four or EaP/WB countries planning a 1-2 semester exchange with a V4-relevant topic.

Measure the distance between your permanent residence or current university and the host: it must exceed 150 km
If not yet accepted at application, secure a letter of acceptance from the host university or documented proof of applying
For post-master's level, arrange the letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan
Prepare certified translations early - sworn-translator or university-official certification is required for non-English documents
Diarise the 15 April 12:00 PM (noon) cut-off; the My Visegrad system will not wait
common_rejection_risks: Host institution in the same country as your citizenship, which is an automatic fail
Previous university studies completed in the country of application
The 150 km distance rule disqualifying a host close to home
Uploading documents separately or after the deadline instead of one complete submission
Applying as a previously supported scholar without a strong justification, since preference favours first-time applicants
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and fees beyond what the host institution's EUR 2,000 per semester covers, plus any travel, insurance and living costs beyond the EUR 3,500 per-semester stipend.

Your topic's relevance to the V4 region is a stated selection preference, so make it explicit in the application
alerts: Results come at the end of May, so a funded stay cannot begin before September/October - plan any academic-year commitments around that
The 2027/28 call only opens on 1 January 2027 at 12:00 PM; earlier submissions are impossible
Separate Visegrad instruments (Visegrad Fellowship, Visegrad Postdoc, Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships) run on their own calendars and are not covered by this application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Assemble ID, transcripts and the host acceptance (or proof of applying) with certified translations, submit everything in one upload through My Visegrad before noon on 15 April, and await the end-of-May results.

scholarships.description: The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program is a nine-month non-degree professional development scholarship for graduates from Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan who already have at least two years of professional experience. Grantees attend two semesters of classes at one of about fifteen affiliated Polish universities, take part in an introductory course, trainings and grantees' conventions, and complete at least two weeks of professional internship. The programme provides support valued at PLN 6,000 per month, free access to university classes, accommodation, health insurance and a return ticket to Poland. It was founded by the Polish-American Freedom Foundation and is financially supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA).

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are registered at a higher education institution that participates in the Erasmus+ programme, and check the Commission's published ECHE 2021-2027 list for your institution
Confirm you are enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification
Find a receiving institution connected to yours by an inter-institutional agreement, since mobility without one cannot proceed

Confirm the Erasmus Charter position on both sides: both institutions must hold the Charter if in EU Member States or associated third countries, and a non-associated third-country institution must commit to the Charter principles when signing
Frame the mobility so it is part of your study programme and relevant to your degree-related learning and personal development needs, because both are stated requirements
Contact the international or Erasmus+ office of your own institution for the internal route and deadline, because there is no central Erasmus+ application or deadline
Choose your mobility length deliberately: 2 to 12 months long-term, or 5 to 30 days short-term blended, or up to 24 months for one-cycle courses such as medicine and architecture
If you are not a doctoral candidate, plan a blended short-term mobility with a virtual component, since only doctoral candidates can omit it
Budget on the assumption that the grant is only a contribution to travel and daily living costs, and that small insurance or student union fees may still apply
If you have a physical, mental or health-related condition, ask the Erasmus+ coordinator at your sending institution about additional funding before you apply
important_advice_for_students: Do not look for a central Erasmus+ application form; there isn't one, so your first action is your own university's Erasmus+ or international office
Do not assume a fixed grant amount; the Commission publishes no scale, and the amount depends on living-cost differences, how many students apply, distance and other available grants
Do not treat the grant as full funding - it is 'a contribution to your travel and daily living costs'

Do not forget the fee exemption is broad: tuition, registration, examinations and laboratory or library access charges are all exempt, but small insurance or student union membership fees may still apply
Do secure the learning agreement for studies before you travel; it defines how your work will be recognised and sets everyone's rights and responsibilities
Do rely on the recognition guarantee: your sending institution must count your credits towards your degree 'without any other requirements'
Do plan your mobility duration against the 12-month-per-study-cycle cap, remembering you may do more than one exchange within it and up to 24 months for one-cycle courses
Do check that your mobility sits inside your own study programme, since relevance to your degree-related learning and personal development needs is a stated eligibility condition
Do use Erasmus+ Online Language Support and read the Erasmus+ Student Charter once you are accepted

Do remember that doctoral candidates have options the others do not, including short-term mobility without a virtual component, and should also consider the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions for research periods abroad
common_rejection_risks: Not being registered at an institution participating in the Erasmus+ programme
Not being enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification
No inter-institutional agreement between the sending and receiving institution
Erasmus Charter non-compliance, or an unwilling non-associated third-country partner
A mobility proposal that is not part of the applicant's study programme or not relevant to their degree-related learning and personal development needs
Missing the sending institution's internal deadline, which is the only real deadline in the system
Planning a short-term mobility without a virtual component while not being a doctoral candidate
Exceeding the 12-month-per-cycle cap, or the 24-month limit for one-cycle courses
Underestimating costs because the grant was treated as full funding
Assuming insurance or student union fees are covered when small such fees may still apply
estimated_uncovered_costs: The majority of travel and daily living costs beyond the grant contribution
Small insurance and student union membership fees that may still apply at the receiving institution
Additional funding for students with physical, mental or health-related conditions, which must be applied for separately
Visa, residence permit and immigration costs
Study materials, equipment and course-related costs
Family accommodation and dependants' costs
Costs of a traineeship combined with the study mobility, beyond the extra support that is stated to exist
Any additional top-up, since applicants may be eligible for further grants from their institution, government or other sources
document_audit: Learning agreement for studies - signed with your sending and receiving institutions before the mobility; this is the single most important document for securing recognition
Participant grant agreement - signed with your sending or receiving institution if you are accepted for a grant
Erasmus+ Student Charter - explains your rights and obligations; read it rather than treating it as boilerplate
Transcript of records from the receiving institution after the mobility, confirming completion and results achieved
Diploma Supplement record of the mobility period, where your institution is based in a system that uses it
Proof of enrolment in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification, as required by your institution
Additional funding application through the Erasmus+ coordinator at your sending institution if you have a physical, mental or health-related condition
Erasmus+ publishes no file size limits, accepted file types, translation rules or document date rules for these documents; the formats are set by your sending and receiving institutions

referee_tracking.instructions: The Commission publishes no referee or reference-letter requirement for Erasmus+ student mobility, because selection is internal to the sending institution. Your institution's selection process may use academic references, transcripts or interviews; that is governed by your own institution's Erasmus+ or international office, not by the Commission.

questions_to_ask_host: Does my institution participate in the Erasmus+ programme, and does my specific department have outgoing agreements?
Which partner institutions are available to me under inter-institutional agreements?
What is my institution's internal application deadline for Erasmus+ outgoing mobility?
How does my institution select applicants, and is selection fair and transparent as required?
What grant amount would I receive, given living-cost differences, applicant numbers and distance?
What is the maximum mobility duration my programme allows, and how does that interact with the 12-month per-cycle cap?
What recognition arrangements exist for my credits, and how is the learning agreement for studies set up?
What additional funding is available for students with physical, mental or health-related conditions?
What top-up grants from my institution, government or other sources could I claim on top?
What are the fee and insurance implications at my receiving institution, given small insurance or student union fees may still apply?
Can I combine a study mobility with a traineeship, and what extra support does that bring?

scholarships.description: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting projects, partnerships, events and mobility in education, training, youth and sport. Its higher education strand is mainly a student exchange programme that also covers placements in companies abroad and academic staff mobility. Students can spend part of their studies in another country without additional tuition, registration or examination costs and receive a scholarship covering living costs, with the period and courses recognised by their home institution. In Poland the programme is implemented by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System, appointed as the Polish National Agency.

scholarships.description: CEEPUS is a multilateral exchange programme with Central and Eastern Europe, organised as a transnational university network of subject-specific networks, each containing at least three higher education institutions from at least two different CEEPUS contractual countries. Exchanges last 3 to 10 months. Within a network, incoming students are exempted from paying tuition fees and receive a comprehensive grant from the host country sized according to local living costs. Eligibility requires CEEPUS-country nationality and participation through a member institution.

applicant_utility.summary: The Master's route is narrow by design: it is for Citizen final-year undergraduates or fresh graduates whose experience sits entirely in the private or non-government sector, and it must lead to a Master's that PSC approves, with MBAs explicitly ruled out. The Sustainability variant is the same package with a sustainability-and-circularity first posting, so the choice you make at application shapes where you land afterwards. Study is capped at two years in any country and carries a three-year bond.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year Singapore Citizen undergraduates or fresh graduates with under three years of private or non-government sector experience who want a Public Service leadership career rather than a technical or MBA track.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your work history against the 'private or non-government sector only' rule; three years including part-time and contract work is the ceiling.
Pick between the standard and Sustainability variants before you start, and make sure your intended Master's subject lines up with that choice.
Verify your intended programme is not an MBA and is one PSC can approve as relevant to the Public Service.
Confirm you can matriculate in the academic year immediately after the offer, since that is a stated condition.
Gather the same Secondary 4 and pre-tertiary document set as the undergraduate PSC route, plus university transcripts and university CCA records.
common_rejection_risks: Holding more than three years of qualifying experience, or having spent it in the public sector.
Proposing an MBA or a course PSC judges outside the Public Service relevance test.
Being unable to start in the immediate next academic year, which is an explicit condition.
Applying for the Sustainability variant without a genuine sustainability-and-circularity subject.
Leaving the essay or one document set unsubmitted, which stops the application being counted as complete.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: No allowance amount is published, so living costs beyond the stated maintenance allowance cannot be sized from the official page; anything outside the approved course is self-funded.
document_audit: The document set blends school-level records (Secondary 4 / Year 4 reports, CCA and CIP records) with university transcripts and university CCA records, so pre-university paper has to be dug out years later.
Employment testimonials are required if applicable, and Public Service internship testimonials are listed for those who have done them.
The NS Certificate of Service and Testimonial applies to those who have served National Service and takes time to obtain.
Preliminary examination results are explicitly not required.
alerts: The 3-year bond starts on graduation and holders are emplaced on the Public Service Leadership Programme, so the commitment is a leadership career rather than a single job.
Outcomes are not all issued until June, and assessments and interviews run from August to June, so plan around a long resolution window.
The Gap Year Programme is available after studies and National Service but before joining the Service, which can shift your start date by six to twelve months.
Sustainability variant holders take a first posting in a sustainability and circularity role, which narrows later mobility at the outset.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Singpass login, then form plus essay plus uploads, then a video interview link within 7 days, then assessments and a PSSB panel interview, with an outcome by June.

You must apply for NTU admission first, because the scholarship form only opens behind the application number that admission gives you, and your school teacher has to file the online appraisal within 7 days of your submission. Keeping the award depends on a CGPA of 3.5 out of 5.0 reviewed every semester, on not holding another award without permission, and on doing ambassador duties when asked.

Tuition is not waived, so the MOE Tuition Grant (plus a three-year work bond for anyone who is not a Singapore Citizen) is what actually reduces your fees. You cannot open the scholarship form until your admission application is submitted, and the scholarship window shuts on the same day as your qualification's admission deadline, so the date that matters is whichever of 20 January, 21 February or 19 March 2027 applies to you.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a Singapore Citizen - this is the first eligibility criterion and international applicants are not eligible for this award.
Apply to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU; the scholarship is not available to other levels or to part-time study.

Tick the SMU Merit Scholarship in the Scholarship section of the online admission application. There is no separate scholarship form, so an application that omits this is not considered for the scholarship.
Write the scholarship personal essay as a distinct piece of work - it is completed and submitted online with the admission application and is the only scholarship-specific written component.
Nominate a tutor or principal as referee if you want a letter of recommendation, and give them enough time to submit it online. The letters are optional but SMU strongly encourages them.

Gather evidence of outstanding academic results and of strong co-curricular and community activity records, because shortlisting is on academic qualifications plus the strength of non-academic records.
Be ready for a panel interview at SMU if shortlisted.
Note the application closing date and the separate standardised test score deadline, and submit the score by the earlier of the two.
important_advice_for_students: Do not assume this pays your living costs. The published package is a subsidised tuition fee waiver plus a S$12,000 activity allowance, so budget accommodation, food, transport and travel to Singapore yourself.

The waiver is described as subsidised tuition fees for regular terms (semesters 1 and 2). If your programme has compulsory ancillary or laboratory fees, ask SMU whether those are inside or outside the waiver before you compare offers.
The 'up to 4 years' wording matters. The waiver is not described as unconditional for four years, so ask what happens if you need a repeat year, a leave of absence, or a change of programme.
Scholarship timing lags the admission cycle. The package is stated to start from Academic Year 2027-28, so check carefully which intake's closing date applies to you.

Do not skip the referee. The letters are optional on paper, but SMU says applicants are strongly encouraged to obtain them, and shortlisting weighs the strength of non-academic records, so a tutor or principal letter is the cheapest way to strengthen that part.
Give referees real time. SMU specifically asks you to ensure your referee has sufficient time to submit the recommendation online, and a late nomination is a common self-inflicted loss.

The S$12,000 is a growth opportunities allowance, not a cash stipend. Plan it for the listed activities - overseas community service projects, exchanges, summer programmes and study missions - rather than treating it as spendable money.
common_rejection_risks: Not being a Singapore Citizen.
Failing to indicate interest in the Scholarship section of the admission application form, which is the only route to consideration.
Not submitting the scholarship personal essay.
Weak co-curricular and community records - shortlisting is explicitly on academic qualifications plus the strength of non-academic records.
A referee who does not submit the online recommendation in time.
Missing the standardised test score deadline where a test score is required.
Self-declared predicted results - SMU states these are not accepted; predicted scores must be attested by a school teacher or counsellor.
Not being ready for the panel interview at SMU.
Submitting final examination results late; SMU requires them within 3 working days of their release.

submission_workflow: 1. Confirm Singapore citizenship and that you are applying to a full-time SMU undergraduate degree programme.
2. Prepare strong evidence for both the academic and the non-academic side of your record.
3. Draft the scholarship personal essay as a standalone document.
4. Nominate a tutor or principal as referee in the Scholarship section and brief them on the online submission route.
5. Complete the SMU online admission application and indicate interest in the SMU Merit Scholarship in the Scholarship section.
6. Submit the personal essay online with the application, before the closing date.
7. Submit any required standardised test score, or school-attested predicted results, by the test-score deadline.
8. Submit your actual final results within 3 working days of their release.
9. Attend the panel interview at SMU if shortlisted.
10. On award, plan the S$12,000 growth opportunities allowance against the listed overseas activities and engage with Student Success Centre development opportunities.
post_award_requirements: Study full-time in an SMU undergraduate degree programme, for which the subsidised tuition fee waiver applies in regular terms.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form to fill in: you indicate your interest in the admission application and SUTD assesses admission and scholarship together, telling you which award you received alongside the offer. That also means you cannot negotiate which SUTD scholarship you get, and the selection committee's decision is final with no disputes entertained. What you get here is the subsidised tuition fee after the Tuition Grant for up to four years, with no living stipend, so treat it as a fee waiver rather than full funding.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizen school leavers with outstanding GCE A-Level, local polytechnic, NUS High School, IB or Year 12 results and a design-and-technology bent applying to SUTD.
application_readiness_checklist: Indicate scholarship interest inside the admission application itself; there is no separate scholarship submission to make.
Take up the Tuition Grant Scheme when you matriculate, because subsidised fees only exist with it.
Also flag donor scholarships in the same application, since SUTD says you may apply for both to improve your chances.
Plan for the 20 hours of service to the University each year, which can mean publicity talks and receiving guests.
Track your GPA against the every-term academic standing review rather than only first-year results.
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for a separate scholarship window that does not exist, and missing the admissions deadline instead.
Expecting a specific SUTD scholarship rather than accepting whichever the committee assigns.
Declining the Tuition Grant Scheme, which removes the subsidised fee the waiver is based on.
Letting academic progress or conduct slip after the award, since withdrawal is at the University's opinion.
Holding another scholarship or grant concurrently without University approval.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Only subsidised tuition after the Tuition Grant is covered; accommodation, living costs, miscellaneous fees, and equipment or project costs are the student's own.
document_audit: No scholarship-specific document list is published; the evidence sits inside the admission application.
For PR or international concession awards, the fee cap is the Singapore Citizen fee level, so confirm what that means for your own fee band before relying on the waiver.
Donor scholarship applications are made as part of the financial aid application, which is a different submission from the admission application.
As SUTD scholarships are made possible with donor support, recipients may be asked to write appreciation notes and attend university or donor events.
alerts: SUTD reserves the right not to award any scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit, and the selection committee's decision is final.
The 20-hour service requirement and possible donor obligations continue for the duration of the award.
If you terminate the scholarship prematurely, SUTD reserves the right to impose a repayment on a case-by-case basis.
Academic performance is reviewed every term, so renewal is not automatic at the year level.
Many other SUTD-administered and donor scholarships on the same page carry richer packages, so check whether another one on the list fits better.

applicant_utility.summary: Only one KTH India Scholarship is on offer for 2027 entry, so treat it as one shot among several: Indian citizens may also apply for the general KTH Scholarship in the same round. Your first move is the programme application at universityadmissions.se with a two-year KTH master's as your single first priority, since a second-to-fourth priority choice disqualifies you entirely. The small scholarship form on KTH's page opens 1 December 2026 and shuts 15 January 2027, and it reuses the documents already in your University Admissions file, so there is no extra paperwork, only a hard timing window. If you win, the two-year tuition bill (SEK 385,000 for most KTH two-year programmes) disappears and you receive a living allowance for the 10 academic-year months; second-year coverage still depends on passing your first year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Indian nationals holding a completed Indian bachelor's degree with a strong GPA from a highly ranked Indian university, targeting a two-year KTH master's programme; Mumbai and Pune applicants receive statutory priority.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the universityadmissions.se application for a two-year, KTH-based master's programme as your FIRST priority before 15 January 2027 (opens 16 October 2026).
Pay the SEK 900 application fee and upload every degree document and transcript by the document deadline; there are no fee waivers and a late or incomplete file is not assessed.
Confirm your chosen programme is not a joint programme and has no obligatory exchange term, which would void scholarship eligibility.
Between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027, submit the scholarship application form on the KTH India Scholarship page.
Add the general KTH Scholarship in the same round, since Indian citizens can apply for both, and keep a self-funded fallback budget in case neither lands.
common_rejection_risks: Listing the target programme as priority 2, 3 or 4 at University Admissions, which makes a scholarship award impossible.
Targeting a joint master's programme or a programme with obligatory exchange studies (e.g. Railway Engineering), which the foundation excludes.
Missing the scholarship form window (1 Dec 2026 to 15 Jan 2027) even after being admitted, because the form must be filed separately.
Weak motivation, work-experience or extra-curricular evidence in the assessed file, since grades and university ranking alone do not win it.
Unsatisfactory first-year study results, which void the second-year tuition coverage.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The SEK 900 application fee, flights to Sweden and initial installation costs, residence-permit and insurance expenses, and living costs for the summer period outside the 10-month allowance; if the target programme's tuition differs from the standard SEK 385,000, only the programme's own fee is covered.
document_audit: Your bachelor's degree must have been completed at an Indian institution; a degree earned elsewhere does not satisfy the foundation's India rule even if you hold Indian citizenship.
Conditional eligibility (final-year students) is accepted, but final documents must reach University Admissions by the deadline or the whole application, scholarship included, is not assessed.
Do not upload anything extra for the scholarship itself; the assessment reads only the documents already filed at University Admissions, so anything missing there counts against you.
Programme-specific entry documents are listed per programme on KTH's entry requirements pages and vary by subject, especially portfolio or prerequisite-course documentation.
alerts: The scholarship form is open for a narrow window only, 1 December 2026 to 15 January 2027, and it cannot be filed before the programme application exists.
It is a single award for 2027 against a pool of all admitted eligible Indian applicants, so plan as if the odds are very long.
Mumbai Metropolitan Area and Pune applicants are prioritized under the foundation's statutes.
Second-year tuition coverage is conditional on satisfactory first-year results, so the award is not fully front-loaded.
Scholarship results are announced 1 April 2027, the same date as admission results, leaving little time to rearrange funding before the autumn term.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a means-tested top-up, not a scholarship you compete for on merit, so the whole file is a financial audit: your parents' tax assessment, your own bank statements and a subsidiary test that asks whether every other source has been exhausted. The gates are sharp - first degree programmes only, no PhD, and international master's students are only fundable with a Swiss bachelor's degree, which rules out most overseas master applicants by design. Plan a month ahead of the 1 February spring deadline, because incomplete files are what actually stall decisions, and expect roughly eight to ten weeks before you hear.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled UZH students in a first degree programme whose family income sits near or below CHF 86,000 and who can produce complete Swiss tax documentation.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are in a first degree programme - a completed apprenticeship, vocational bachelor's or master's degree ends initial education and ends eligibility
Request the latest final tax assessments for you and your parents early, since final assessments lag returns
If you do not file in Switzerland, gather six months of statements for every bank account you hold
For international bachelor students, track the 55 ECTS threshold, or aim at a first-semester application only if your grades are genuinely strong
Apply for the cantonal scholarship in parallel; UZH treats its own award as supplementary and a pending cantonal decision can be added to the calculation later
Clear your browser cache before starting the portal form, as UZH specifically warns about this
common_rejection_risks: Parental income above CHF 86,000 or net worth above CHF 300,000, with no allowance for children beyond the CHF 6,000-per-child uplift
Personal assets exceeding the CHF 5,000 exemption without explanation
Applying as an international master's student without a Swiss bachelor's degree, which the office states outright it cannot support
Submitting an incomplete file, which the office says you can speed up only by being meticulous
Assuming the award replaces a cantonal scholarship rather than supplementing it
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: UZH asks students to budget at least CHF 2,200 per month (about CHF 26,400 a year for international bachelor students), of which tuition and materials are only around CHF 250. Zurich accommodation at roughly CHF 910 a month is the largest single line, and dual-degree additional costs are explicitly not covered.
document_audit: Documents must be PDF and uploaded one per upload process - a single batch upload will silently drop files
If you do not file a Swiss tax return, the six-month bank statements substitute for tax assessments and are not optional
Your UZH email address is a precondition for the form; if it has not arrived two weeks before the deadline, contact the office immediately
Scholarship holders wanting the UZH/ETH Language Center fee waiver must obtain the acceptance letter before registering, otherwise the fee is not refunded after the enrolment deadline
alerts: Two hard dates: 15 August for autumn and 1 February for spring, and files open only two months before each
Part-time work does not reduce the scholarship unless you earn more than CHF 6,000 a year
Loan products are gated separately - hardship loans up to CHF 6,000 and the one-off Pecunia loan of CHF 1,000 to 4,000 both require Swiss citizenship or a C permit
Decisions arrive about eight to ten weeks after the deadline, with payment credited roughly one week after approval, so the bridge months need separate funding
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Portal application with UZH login, PDF uploads one at a time, office review making documents visible, decision in the portal about eight to ten weeks after the deadline, payment for the semester credited about a week after approval.

scholarships.title: UZH Hardship Loan
scholarships.name: UZH Hardship Loan

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are enrolled at UZH. That is the published precondition, and it is checked before anything else.
Be clear that this is a loan, not a grant: decide in advance how you will repay up to CHF 6,000 within six months, because the University requires a plausible guarantee to that effect.
Check you have no existing debt. If you have debt, this is the wrong product - the University says these loans are not meant for paying off debts.
Time it to a genuine acute emergency. The loan exists to bridge a gap, for example while waiting for cantonal scholarship funds, not as routine funding.
Apply for no more than CHF 6,000 and only once per semester.

If you are an international student, check your level: at Master's level you need a Swiss Bachelor's degree to be eligible for support, and at Bachelor's level support ends once you have successfully completed the first year.
Complete the portal application form thoroughly and correctly - the University explicitly warns about this for all of its financial support applications.
Use the office's published hours: telephone and email contact is Monday and Thursday, 14.00-15.00h.
important_advice_for_students: Do not confuse this with a scholarship. It is repayable within six months and going to a debt collector immediately if you miss it. The University is unusually direct about that.
Do not use it to clear existing debt. You must be in an acute financial emergency and have no debt for eligibility.
Do not wait for a deadline, because there isn't one. There is no annual round; apply as soon as the crisis arises, because processing usually takes only a few working days.
Apply for the maximum only if you can actually repay it. Six months is short, and the guarantee is a condition of the award, not a formality.

If you are waiting on a cantonal scholarship, this loan is explicitly designed for that gap. If you are waiting on anything else, check whether one of the other UZH products fits better - the Â«PecuniaÂ» one-time loan (CHF 1,000-4,000, one time only, parents' finances not assessed) is restricted to Swiss students and C-permit holders.
If you are an international Master's student without a Swiss Bachelor's degree, you are not eligible for support at all, so do not apply.
If you are an international Bachelor's student who has already passed the first year, support is no longer available to you at that level.
common_rejection_risks: Not being enrolled at the University of Zurich.
Already having debt - the published test is an acute financial emergency without any debt.
Not being able to plausibly guarantee repayment within six months.
Applying more than once in the same semester.
Applying for more than CHF 6,000.
Prospective international Master's students who do not hold a Swiss Bachelor's degree.
Prospective international Bachelor's students who have already successfully completed the first year, or who are not entitled to financial aid in principle.
An incomplete or incorrectly completed portal application form - the University specifically warns applicants about this.
Missing the six-month repayment date, which leads to immediate referral to a debt collector.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything above CHF 6,000 in a single crisis
A second crisis in the same semester - only one application per semester is permitted
All ordinary study and living costs - this is an emergency bridge, not a cost-of-living loan
Tuition fees, accommodation and study materials - no such coverage is published for this product
The remainder of your studies once a second emergency arises in a later semester, since each semester allows only one application and each loan must be repaid within six months
document_audit: The University publishes no document list for the hardship loan. The only published instruction is to fill out the relevant application form in the portal thoroughly and correctly.
No file type, file size, translation, signature or date rules are published for this loan.

Do not assume the Â«PecuniaÂ» requirements apply here: the University states that for the Â«PecuniaÂ» one-time loan it needs only the application form and a certificate from the debt collection register, and that the parents' financial situation is not assessed. That is a different product with its own eligibility (Swiss students and C-permit holders).

Practical consequence: ask the Student Financial Aid Office, at studienfinanzierung@sib.uzh.ch during the published Monday/Thursday hours, what evidence of your emergency and your six-month repayment plan they need, since none is published.

applicant_utility.summary: JJ/WBGSP is a full package for mid-career development professionals: tuition, basic medical insurance, a monthly living stipend whose size the World Bank does not publish, economy flights and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip, at one of only 44 participating master's programmes. The scholarship is strictly second in line to admission - you must first hold an unconditional (except funding) offer from a participating programme outside your home country, and only then does the university hand you the application link. Scoring weights your development track record heavily: professional experience, recommendations and commitment to your home country are 30% each, so a strong CV matters more than academic pedigree.

scholarships.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.

scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.

scholarships.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. It is congressionally funded, established by the U.S. Congress in 2001, and administered by the Institute of International Education since its inception. Applicants must be receiving a Federal Pell Grant during the time of application or be able to prove they will receive one during their term abroad. The programme has funded American students to study and intern abroad in more than 170 countries, with recipients from all 50 U.S. states and D.C.

scholarships.name: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
scholarships.funding_period: one-off award, tiered by programme duration

applicant_utility.summary: Boren pays a fixed tiered grant ($8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on programme length) that the programme itself says is not all-inclusive, so budget for the gap between the tier and your real costs. The two deadlines are separate and early: Fellowships January 20, Scholarships January 27, 2027, both 5pm Eastern. There is no interview stage - the essays are the entire audition - so tie your chosen language and country to a concrete U.S. national security and federal service story rather than generic study-abroad motivation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. citizen undergraduates and graduate students who can commit a full year to immersive language study in a preferred destination and genuinely intend a federal national-security career.

For Arabic, Mandarin or Russian, or any asterisked destination, line up a viable alternate programme now
Confirm you can remain matriculated and delay graduation until the funded programme ends
Ask your campus representative about any earlier campus deadline
Model the shortfall between your award tier and your programme's actual cost before committing
common_rejection_risks: Programmes shorter than 12 weeks (8 weeks only for undergraduate STEM summer programmes) are ineligible
A language plan with fewer than 15-20 weekly classroom contact hours
Essays that never connect the language and region to U.S. national security and public service
Graduating before the funded period ends - Scholars and Fellows may not graduate until complete
Proposing study in a country of which you are a citizen
Study tours such as a semester at sea, which are not eligible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is explicitly not all-inclusive; you fund the difference between the tier and your actual programme cost, plus anything outside eligible costs such as non-approved travel.
document_audit: Unofficial transcripts must show your name, institution, course titles and grades - the unofficial transcript is required to submit
The study-programme description is capped at 5 pages
Recommenders submit their own letters through the system; even the optional third letter needs lead time
For asterisked destinations the alternate programme must be a real, viable plan, not a placeholder
alerts: Funding for programme expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent on availability and cannot be guaranteed at award
2027-cycle funding may be applied to programmes starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028

Internships during the funded period may not be remunerated or conducted with any government; Fellows may not work as journalists abroad, even freelance or unpaid
Financial aid from other sources must be reported and may affect the grant (student loans do not)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online application at apply.iie.org with unofficial transcripts and letters by the national deadline, then await regional panel review with notifications in mid-to-late April.

scholarships.deadline: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027 - both 5pm Eastern time.
scholarships.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.
scholarships.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes).
scholarships.application_period: The 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycle is open as of 2026-10-01. National deadlines are January 20, 2027 (Fellowships) and January 27, 2027 (Scholarships), 5pm Eastern time. Selected applicants are notified in mid-to-late April. Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that applicants are asked to respect.
scholarships.official_source: Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO), National Security Education Program; administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE)
eligibility: U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline
A high school graduate, or have earned a GED
At least 18 years of age or older by the time the application is submitted
Planning an overseas program in an overseas destination outside of Western Europe, Canada, Australia, or New Zealand
Planning to study in an overseas destination of which they are not a citizen

Matriculated for the duration of their Boren Awards-funded program in an undergraduate or graduate degree program located within the United States and accredited by a body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education

Boren Scholarships applicants must be matriculated in an associate's or bachelor's degree program at the time of application and must remain matriculated in an undergraduate degree program; they may not graduate until the scholarship is complete

Boren Fellowships applicants may be matriculated in or applying to a graduate degree program, but Boren Fellows must be matriculated in a graduate degree program by the start date of the fellowship and may not graduate until the fellowship is complete

Eligible graduate degree programs include master's (MA, MS, MBA, LLM and others), juris doctor (JD), or doctoral (PhD, MD and others) programs; non-degree certificate programs are not eligible by themselves

Access to the NSEP Alumni Association

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know must be stated in the essays and other application materials. Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: U.S. citizens aged 18 or over who are matriculated at an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate degree programme, can commit 8-52 weeks to overseas study of a Boren-preferred language in a Boren-preferred region, and intend to pursue a federal national-security career.
scholarships.notes: Non-deferrable in practice: recipients must remain matriculated at their U.S. institution for the whole funded period and may not graduate until the award is complete, and overseas programmes must be approved by a Boren Program Advisor before travel. Not renewable as published - the award is a fixed one-time grant tier set by overseas duration, and requests to increase awards above the published maximums are contingent upon availability of funds. No return-home obligation is published; instead recipients must complete at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation, with preference given to a longer-term commitment. Internships conducted during a Boren-funded period may not be remunerated nor conducted with the U.S. or a foreign government, and Boren Fellows may not work as journalists while abroad, even freelance or unpaid. Funding for programme expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent upon availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award.

scholarships.description: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi awards 40 Fellowships of $8,500 each, six at $15,000 each, and two at $35,000 each to members entering the first year of graduate or professional study. Established in 1932, the Fellowship Program annually provides funding to first-year graduate students pursuing post-baccalaureate degrees across all academic disciplines. Each active chapter may select one candidate from among its local applicants to compete for the Society-wide awards, and endorsed Phi Kappa Phi Fellows go on to study at some of the nation's top graduate schools. The 2027 cycle opens its application portal on December 15, 2026 and closes at the national deadline of April 15, 2027.

scholarships.deadline: Reference letters due October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time. Application deadlines: October 19, 2026 (Life Sciences); October 20, 2026 (Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social Sciences); October 22, 2026 (Engineering); October 23, 2026 (Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy). All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date for the Major Field of Study selected. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application without it counting towards the number of times an individual may apply.
scholarships.description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. There is no post-graduate study service requirement, and fellows may transfer to a different institution after completion of the first fellowship year. Estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation (NSF 26-526), pending availability of funds.
scholarships.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
scholarships.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. The module opened in time for the 2026 application cycle; the 2027 application deadlines were published August 25, 2026.

scholarships.image_alt_text: United States National Science Foundation logo

Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Fellowships may only be used for an eligible graduate degree program at a nonprofit academic institution accredited in, and having a campus located in, the U.S., its territories, possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. application_readiness_checklist: Start with the classification test, not the paperwork: if you are not eligible for federal student financial aid under the FAFSA, you follow the international instructions regardless of where you live.
Note the deadline for your cycle: November 30 for Early Action, February 15 for Regular Action and transfers, or February 15 if you are a current student.
File the CSS Profile with MIT's CSS Code 3514 and complete every MIT supplemental question - consideration is automatic but only if the CSS Profile is filed.
Collect the CSS inputs now: parents' income tax returns or wage statements from two years ago, other money earned, current bank balances, investments and untaxed income.
If your parents are separated or divorced, arrange two CSS Profiles and two sets of income documentation.
Plan the IDOC step separately and submit through IDOC, never to MIT directly, and allow up to two weeks for MIT to receive it.

If your parents live outside the U.S., gather the tax return from that country and translate it into English if it is not already - a professional translation is not required, so you, your family or anyone you know can do it.
Track everything in the MIT Application Portal and allow 10 business days for documents to appear in the Online Financial Aid System.
Do not miss mid-May. Aid applications must be received by the end of the academic year, or mid-December if you attend only in the fall, or you lose eligibility for that year.
Once awarded, put the 1 May to 1 July window in your diary for the annual Student Information Review Form.
important_advice_for_students: MIT's need-blind, full-need commitment applies to international students exactly as to domestic students, and MIT says so explicitly. If you are admitted and your family cannot pay, that is not a reason to withdraw - it is what the aid package is for.

Expect to contribute something yourself. The median annual price paid by an undergraduate who received an MIT Scholarship was $10,268, and students are expected to contribute from summer savings and term-time work. Full need means MIT meets what it calculates to be your need, not that your family pays nothing.

Understand that tuition coverage is income-dependent. From 2025-2026 families under $200,000 typically attend tuition-free, but for families over $200,000 the published median MIT Scholarship is $37,750 and covers 59% of tuition. If your family income is above that band, start budgeting early.

Do not send anything to MIT. Parental tax documents go to the College Board's IDOC service, and MIT says it cannot accept documents sent directly to it. This is the single most common procedural failure point.
Budget two weeks for IDOC and 10 business days for the portal. MIT publishes both timings, and they are the reason late-feeling applications slip.

A professional translation is not required. Documents may be translated by you, your family or someone you know, which removes a real cost barrier - but they must be in English if the original is not.

There is no penalty for a late application, but there is a hard cut-off. MIT says just submit as soon as possible; the risk is not a penalty, it is missing mid-May (or mid-December for fall-only attendance) and losing the aid for the year entirely.

Do the Student Information Review Form between 1 May and 1 July. MIT uses it to match you to the right scholarship fund, and because donors often specify the kind of student they support, this is what connects you to the fund - and sometimes to an MIT alum donor.
Travel, visa and immigration costs are not addressed on these pages. They are not listed as covered expenses, so plan for flights and visa fees separately.
common_rejection_risks: Not filing the CSS Profile, which is the basis of automatic consideration for an MIT Scholarship.
Missing the MIT supplemental questions in the CSS Profile, or failing to use CSS Code 3514.
Sending parental tax returns or income documentation directly to MIT instead of through IDOC.
Allowing the two-week IDOC receipt time and the 10 business-day portal processing time to eat into the deadline.
Not submitting by mid-May, or mid-December if attending only in the fall, which results in no MIT or federal aid for that academic year.
Failing to translate non-English parental tax documents into English, where applicable.
Having only one parent complete the CSS Profile where the parents are separated or divorced.
Assuming full-need means a zero payment and being unprepared for the student contribution and net price.
Missing the 1 May to 1 July Student Information Review Form window after being awarded, which affects the scholarship fund MIT matches you to.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The family financial responsibility calculated after the MIT Scholarship - MIT publishes a median MIT Scholarship of $73,666 for 2025-2026 and a median net price of $0 for families in the $0-$100,000 income band, rising to $19,734 for $100,000-$200,000 and $49,083 above $200,000
The student's expected contribution from summer savings and term-time employment during the school year
Air travel to the United States, visa and immigration costs, and relocation - not listed as covered expenses on the pages read
Any gap for families whose income exceeds the tuition-free threshold, where the published median MIT Scholarship covers 59% of tuition
Student loans, where a family chooses them despite MIT's position that students should not need loans and that 88% of MIT students graduate debt-free

scholarships.description: The University of Texas at Austin's International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS) states that "Certain scholarship opportunities are open to international students who meet eligibility criteria", and that "Scholarship applications are open twice a year: once in the Fall for the spring and summer terms and once in the Spring for the upcoming fall term and academic year." Applications for Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 scholarships are accepted 1 October 2026 to 1 November 2026, and applications for Fall 2027 and the 2027-2028 academic year are accepted 1 February 2027 to 1 March 2027. Applications are submitted through LASSO, the university-wide scholarship system. ISSS states plainly that "scholarships are one-time awards, and recipients are not guaranteed to receive the scholarship in subsequent years." The portfolio runs from fixed-value tuition scholarships (for example the $3,500 SIAWE and $4,800 STEM awards) to competitive need-based cash aid (General ISSS Financial Aid), a nonresident tuition waiver (TAMS), a fee scholarship established by student referendum (IEFS), and a Western Hemisphere tuition exemption (Good Neighbor Scholarship).

scholarships.description: The University of Chicago states that "Nearly $20 million in need-based financial aid has been offered to international students at UChicago over the past four years, and a recent gift of $35 million for international financial aid has strengthened the University's commitment to enrolling a diverse and talented student body from around the world." Its commitment is explicit: "We are committed to meeting 100% of your demonstrated need with a loan-free financial aid package if you are admitted and applied for funding." Packages "are based on an estimate of the full costs of enrolling at the University of Chicago, including tuition, housing, health insurance, a meal plan, and estimates for additional costs like books and personal expenses." International students must apply for funding during the admissions process; they are not eligible afterwards or during their four years in the College. Separately, UChicago offers partial-tuition merit scholarships - single lump-sum or renewable annual - which are considered independently of financial situation and for which all first-year applicants are automatically considered.

applicant_utility.summary: Two gates matter here: you must first be admitted to MSIT, MS ECE or MS EAI, and only admitted applicants of African nationality can access CMU-Africa financial aid including the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. Apply by December 15 to have the competency-test and DET fees covered - applications after the early deadline are considered only with valid English scores already in hand. The award itself is genuinely comprehensive (tuition, fees, health insurance, travel, basic living expenses, laptop and textbooks), so the real work is the admission: essays including a video essay, a one-hour technical test and three recommenders.

If you want need-based aid you must decide before you submit, because Trinity is need-aware and tells you that applying for aid puts you in its most competitive pool, with applicants contributing at least $45,000 per year the most competitive for admission. Deadlines are the standing decision-plan dates - November 1 for Early Decision I and Early Action, February 1 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision - and aid materials are due with the matching round, not later.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International first-year applicants with strong secondary school records who can either self-fund a meaningful share of costs or commit to the need-aware aid route early, and who are applying straight from secondary school rather than as transfers.

scholarships.funding_period: one-off honorarium on delivery of a working paper

applicant_utility.summary: This is commissioned research, not a scholarship: you are paid an honorarium of US$3,000-10,000 for delivering an acceptable working paper, and the money is explicitly expected to absorb every research cost, so there is no tuition, living stipend or fee support attached. The call closes at 23:59 UTC+2 on 15 October 2026 - five days from the verification date - and submission is only through one of three online forms (individual, group, or non-profit), so pick the right form type before you start typing. Scope tightly to the two workstreams and to South African tax administrative data, because relevance to the project is the first of the three published selection criteria and only the final decision is ever communicated - expect no feedback if you are not selected.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Economists and social scientists - especially early-career, female and South Africa-based researchers - who can deliver a publishable 10,000-word policy paper using tax administrative data within the June-September 2027 draft cycle.
application_readiness_checklist: Choose the correct submission form first: individual, group of individuals, or non-profit organization
Download and use the published proposal template - off-template proposals risk screening problems
Cast the proposal explicitly against the WS2 revenue-mobilization or WS3 poverty/inequality/labour-market questions and the tax-data angle
Prepare a five-page-or-less CV for every researcher on the team, plus the cover page, before opening the form
Enter each researcher's address, gender, nationality and date of birth accurately - the form demands these details
Submit before 23:59 UTC+2 on 15 October 2026; no budget document is needed
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that reads as general development economics rather than the two named workstreams - relevance is criterion one

Using the wrong form type for your team structure (individual vs group vs non-profit)
Submitting after 23:59 UTC+2 on 15 October 2026, or expecting feedback - only the accept/decline decision is communicated
A weak CV trail relative to the honorarium band sought, since qualifications of the lead researcher drive the amount offered
Proposing data access plans that ignore the confidentiality restrictions National Treasury attaches to tax administrative datasets
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The honorarium is expected to cover all research expenses including data collection and research assistance; there is no living-cost, tuition or salary support in this award, and only non-Gauteng researchers using the tax data can receive the small travel stipend.
document_audit: Short CVs must be five pages or less per researcher - trim before uploading rather than hoping for leniency
All researchers' personal details (address, gender, nationality, date of birth) must be on the form, so collect them from co-authors before you start
No budget document is required - spending time on one is wasted effort

Successful teams will later sign a consultant contract or institutional contractual agreement under UNU conditions of service, and copyright transfers to UNU-WIDER unless no further publication is expected

applicant_utility.summary: This is a stipended eleven-month policy fellowship, not a degree or a salaried job: you trade your classroom for a federal agency or congressional office in Washington, DC and draw a monthly living stipend. For the 2027-2028 cycle the window runs from August 3, 2026 to 8:00pm ET on November 5, 2026, and nothing counts unless the entire file, including all three recommendation letters, shows complete in the online system by that moment. Treat the $8,200 as gross pay: the programme withholds no tax and stipends are IRS-reportable, so plan quarterly estimated payments and DC-area housing costs, which the programme does not arrange.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Veteran U.S. public or private school STEM teachers with five-plus years of full-time classroom experience who can secure an eleven-month leave of absence and want a foothold in national education policy.
application_readiness_checklist: Create your online account early and confirm you actually meet the five-complete-years full-time teaching rule, excluding student teaching.
Line up a qualifying district-official recommender (principal, superintendent or board member level) well before November.
Draft and spell-check the five essays offline, since the system times out after 60 minutes of inactivity.
Send all three recommendation requests as soon as you have account access; they do not need to wait for your essay drafts.
Check the 'Check Your Status' page weekly and resend reminders until all three letters show submitted.
Block February 27 - March 1, 2027 now in case you are called to DC for semi-finalist interviews.
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete file at 8:00pm ET on November 5, 2026 because one recommendation letter never arrived through the system.
Choosing a district official who does not qualify: assistant, associate and vice-principals and department chairs are explicitly excluded.
Counting student teaching or assistant teaching toward the five-year classroom requirement.
Being currently employed outside a U.S. school or district, including teaching abroad.
Reapplying as a current or former AEF Fellow, or exceeding three applications in a six-year period.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Washington, DC housing (the programme provides resources but no housing), federal and state income tax with no withholding, health insurance above the $550/$1,300 monthly stipend amounts, and any family relocation costs beyond the $3,500 allowance.
document_audit: Recommendation letters are valid only if submitted through the online Recommender form; mailed or emailed letters are refused and a submitted letter cannot be removed.
Citizenship proof is required only when you accept an offer, so applicants in naturalisation should note the FAQ bar on applying before citizenship.
The five essays must be pasted into the online application fields; there is no separate document upload route for them.
alerts: U.S. citizenship must already be held at the time of applying, not by the fellowship start date.
The deadline is 8:00pm Eastern, not midnight Pacific; build in recommenders' time zones.
If selected for a congressional placement you must return to DC for a week of interviews in mid-June 2027.
Stipends are paid semi-monthly by the sponsoring agency and are reportable to the IRS with no withholding.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account, complete all fields and five essays, trigger the three online recommendation requests, monitor 'Check Your Status' until every letter is received, then submit before the 8:00pm ET deadline.

scholarships.description: The AEF Programme places accomplished K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, working on national education programmes and policy. Each fellow receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200, a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency, an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses, relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for fellows relocating from outside the Washington, DC area, and a health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month on an individual plan or $1,300 per month on a family plan. The DOE sponsors up to five congressional office placements. The programme is a single eleven-month appointment; it is not a degree award and involves no tuition.
scholarships.duration: Eleven months, mid-August through mid-July; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial programme Orientation
scholarships.application_period: Online application opens August 3, 2026 and closes 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026 for the 2027-2028 programme. Semi-finalist notifications with travel arrangements are made by February 24, 2027; interviews in Washington, DC February 27 - March 1, 2027; finalist notifications March 9, 2027; congressional fellows placement interviews mid-June 2027; fellows arrive in Washington, DC mid-August 2027.

eligibility: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).

Have a minimum of five complete years of full-time classroom teaching experience prior to submitting the application; student teaching does not count toward this minimum full-time teaching requirement.

Have been teaching full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school for at least five of the last seven years in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) discipline; current employment may be as an educator or district official.
Be currently employed full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school or school district in the U.S.
Be able to provide a letter of recommendation from a school district official as one of their three required letters of recommendation.
Be able to obtain a leave of absence from teaching in order to participate in the program for the full eleven months.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens who have completed five years of full-time STEM classroom teaching, have taught full-time in a U.S. public or private elementary or secondary school or school district for at least five of the last seven years, are currently so employed, can obtain an eleven-month leave of absence, and can obtain a recommendation letter from a school district official.
benefits: Develops a professional development plan to guide individual professional development objectives outside host office responsibilities, with ongoing mentoring provided by the AEF Programme.
Access to a national network of education leaders and programmes.
Placement in a federal agency or U.S. Congressional office, with the DOE sponsoring up to five placements in congressional offices.
Up to ten personal days off per year and up to ten sick days off without reduction in the Fellow's stipend.
Fellows are connected with outgoing Fellows to help identify available housing in the Washington, DC area.
coverage: Monthly living stipend of $8,200.
Travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency; limitations on foreign travel vary by agency.
Education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved expenses aligned with the Fellow's individual professional development plan, including courses, conferences and professional books.
Relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for Fellows relocating from outside of the Washington, DC area (home-to-Washington distance more than 50 miles one way).
Stipend of up to $550 per month (individual plan) or $1,300 per month (family plan) to offset the cost of health insurance.
Designated office space and agency/office-specific orientation and training.
Official twice monthly professional development meetings, conferences and field trips organised for Fellows by the AEF Programme.
requirements: All applications must be completed online through the online application system.
Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements.

Submit the requested written reports, presentations and surveys related to the Fellowship experience before the published deadlines.
Represent themselves as educators in a responsible and professional manner.
Only use the AEF Programme name or the Fellow's affiliation with the AEF Programme in an authorised manner.
In managing their responsibilities throughout the fellowship, give priority to the duties assigned to them by their host office.

Request recommendations from three individuals familiar with the applicant's professional and education background and their experience, aptitude or promise relevant to the AEF Programme, entering their names and email addresses on the Request Recommendations page; requests can be made as soon as the application system is accessed, without waiting for the application to be complete.
