Finalists selected for a Congressional office placement return to Washington, DC in mid-June 2027 for a week of placement interviews.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.
scholarships.program_type: Government fellowship
scholarships.best_fit: Experienced, currently employed U.S. K-12 STEM teachers or district officials who have at least five complete years of full-time classroom STEM teaching, can secure an eleven-month leave of absence, and can relocate to the Washington, DC area.
scholarships.notes: Not deferrable and not renewable: the fellowship is for a single eleven-month period from mid-August with initial programme Orientation, and there is no flexibility in start and end dates. There is no return-home requirement, but relocation to the Washington, DC area is a programme requirement if the Fellow does not already live there. The Fellow cannot maintain a teaching position while serving; a leave of absence must be secured or employment terminated. The AEF Programme does not arrange housing. Fellows receive a monthly stipend and are not considered employees of the hosting office, so they do not earn sick or annual leave, although up to ten personal days and ten sick days are allowed without stipend reduction. All stipends are reportable to the Internal Revenue Service and the AEF Programme does not withhold taxes; fellows may need to file Form 1040-ES and pay estimated income tax. Current and former AEF Fellows are not eligible to apply for a second fellowship. No clinical restriction is published.

important_advice_for_students: Budget realistically: EUR 500 per month does not cover Latvia. VIAA states plainly that tuition components, living costs and other expenses must be covered personally, and average tuition alone ranges from EUR 2,800 to EUR 15,000 per year

Arrange insurance yourself; it is not part of the scholarship
You will lose the stipend for any period in which you are in Latvia for less than 15 calendar days, so plan travel and remote periods carefully
You cannot hold this scholarship together with another grant, so if you have other funding, check the exclusivity rule before applying
The scholarship covers at most two terms within one study cycle - it is not a full-degree funding package
Work backwards from 1 April: the HEI confirmation letter has to be in your hands before you submit, and HEIs need time to issue it

scholarships.description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution. The award does not pay tuition or fees, does not cover supplies and materials, and does not cover travel during the project; the student must remain enrolled full-time at their home institution and keep paying their own tuition. Successful applicants are considered guest scientists at the host laboratory, not employees.
scholarships.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates

eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.

The opportunity, after receiving the award, to apply for further funding to conduct a brief (6 weeks maximum) research visit to select research institutions abroad, such as CERN or RIKEN.

Consult your primary graduate thesis advisor and confirm Ph.D. candidacy, an approved thesis topic, and that the proposed laboratory work is part of your thesis project.
Obtain official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as a signed letter from the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, including the date of thesis committee approval of your topic.
Obtain your official graduate transcript stamped with the university seal, and redact Social Security numbers and dates of birth while keeping your name visible.

Co-develop the research proposal with the collaborating scientist, in consultation with your thesis advisor, addressing the stated aims of at least one priority research area and identifying how the laboratory's capabilities and assets will be used; keep it to three pages plus a one-page reference list.

Ensure both your thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist review and approve the final proposal PDF before uploading it, because they receive an automatic notification when you upload or update it.

Enter your thesis advisor's contact information under 'Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor Information' and the collaborating scientist's contact information under 'Host DOE Laboratory', then use 'Send Email' on the Request Letters of Support tab to send both requests.
Monitor the receipt of both letters of support through the online system and send reminder emails where needed.
Review and print or export your application as a PDF using the 'Print your Application' option before submitting.

Submit the complete application, including transcripts, proof of candidacy, research proposal and both letters of support, by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026, and confirm the Status page shows 'Submitted'.
If selected, respond to the DOE Office of Science notification promptly; you will be given about a week to decide whether to accept.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.
scholarships.program_type: Government research fellowship
scholarships.best_fit: Full-time U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents who have already obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, are enrolled in a thesis-based research Ph.D. in a DOE-supported STEM field at an accredited U.S. institution, and can arrange a 3 to 12 month in-person research residency with a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist at a participating laboratory.
scholarships.notes: Not deferrable in the ordinary sense, but the award period may be changed under exceptional circumstances, such as unexpected schedule changes at scientific user facilities, with the support of both the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist and the primary graduate thesis advisor; such requests must reach the SCGSR Program Manager at least 20 business days in advance with signed consent letters from both, and the overall project period must remain the same length as proposed. Cumulative SCGSR award periods across all awards may not exceed 12 months. The award is not an internship and not a full graduate fellowship: the SCGF programme, which provided a stipend and tuition support for up to three years, is no longer accepting applications. Awardees are not employees of the host laboratory or DOE and are not entitled to employee benefits. Regular travel between the host laboratory and the university during the award period violates the terms and conditions, because a full-time schedule at the host is required during normal laboratory business hours; awardees may observe the host's holidays but must report any expected interruption to the collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager. Awardees become ineligible if, after applying, they accept a separate non-SCGSR appointment from the host laboratory, such as an hourly paid intern or a full-time or temporary position. Medical research, or biological research on model systems for the purpose of understanding disease or pathogens, is not eligible, which excludes clinical and medical-degree routes; joint MD/PhD, joint JD/PhD, DVM, MBA, MD, JD and joint BS/MS programmes are all ineligible. Published work based on the research should carry the SCGSR acknowledgement statement, including contract number DE-SC0014664.

eligibility: In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.
If you live in a European overseas territory, you may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which you are a citizen.
Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field).
Have at least five years' relevant professional experience.

Be a mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, and employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation.
Be working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness within their organisation and/or country.

Be able to demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to applying the knowledge and networks gained through the fellowship within their organisation and/or country on completion of the programme.

General Chevening Fellowship criteria: be a citizen of a fellowship-eligible country or territory; demonstrate the potential to rise to a position of leadership and influence; demonstrate the personal, intellectual, and interpersonal attributes reflecting this potential; return to your country of citizenship (country of award) for at least one year after your fellowship ends; and meet all programme-specific fellowship eligibility requirements.

General work-experience rule for Chevening Fellowships: a minimum of five years' work experience in a relevant related field, which equals 7,200 hours, calculated by multiplying weeks worked by hours per week (a working week comprises 35-60 hours and a working year comprises 40-50 weeks). 'If you do not already have the level of work experience required for your chosen fellowship programme, you will be unable to submit your application.'
You do not need to meet the work experience requirement in one period of employment; applicants can submit up to fifteen different employment periods.

scholarships.selection_notes: Chevening publishes the four general Fellowship objectives - supporting mid-career professionals in positions of leadership and influence, offering dynamic training/professional development/research relevant to professional interests and UK international strategic priorities, increasing the breadth and diversity of Chevening awards, and supporting FCDO foreign policy priorities by creating lasting relationships with future leaders, influencers and decision-makers. For this programme the assessment is against the general Chevening Fellowship criteria plus the published programme-specific requirements, and against the needs of a cohort drawn from the listed European countries. Chevening Fellowships are 'an important element of Britain's public diplomacy effort', and fellows are active in their field or subject. Chevening does not publish a separate scoring framework or interview format for this programme; applications for Chevening Scholarships follow the published sifting, reading committee, embassy shortlist and interview stages, while Chevening states that 'Application timelines for Chevening Fellowships vary.'

scholarships.notes: Deferral: 'Applications to defer awards will only be granted in the case of pregnancy.' Extensions: 'Extensions to the original fellowship duration may be permitted in exceptional circumstances, but the total duration must not exceed 12 months. All extensions are subject to the availability of funds and assessed on a case-by-case basis. Extensions are not automatic and should not be assumed.' Return home: 'You are expected to return to your home country for at least one year on completion of your fellowship.' Dependants: 'All Chevening Awards are calculated to support fellow costs only. There are no financial or welfare provisions for dependants of Chevening Fellows. It is strongly advised that Fellows do not bring dependants to the UK', and 'The Chevening Programme will not endorse the visa applications of, nor provide travel for, dependants.' Other conditions: no transfer to any course other than that confirmed in the Final Award Letter; no other publicly funded award during the fellowship period; approval required before any part-time employment or internship outside the approved programme; cannot serve as an official government representative during the fellowship; must not be outside the UK for more than 30 days in total (pro-rata: 3-month tenure up to 7 days outside the UK), and absences without prior notice may suspend the stipend or end the award; must cite Chevening Fellowships in publications; breach may result in withdrawal of the award. Stipend suspension may occur if fellowship terms and conditions are not complied with, if compulsory documentation is not returned, or if the Fellow elects to return home early and submit work from overseas.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on academic excellence, the clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes, the rigour of the research proposal, and the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society. Only applications meeting the programme's eligibility criteria are assessed. Applicants who pass review are notified by email; all other applicants are informed at the end of the application review period. Applicants shortlisted in the selection process are invited to group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference. Final decisions are approved by the Board of Directors. The application form is removed from the portal once the competition ends; the confirmation email is the only proof of receipt.

scholarships.best_fit: First- or second-year PhD students in the humanities and social sciences whose research maps onto one of the Foundation's four themes (Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment), who already have an outstanding academic record and who want mentorship and a non-academic network alongside funding.
scholarships.notes: The Scholarship is a three-year program. It is not deferrable in the sense that the value is adjusted: Scholars may accept other awards, but the value of the Trudeau Scholarship is adjusted based on amounts received from other organizations, institutions or universities, and all additional sources of income must be declared annually. Regardless of other funding, every Scholar receives the full annual $20,000 research, travel and networking allowance and a minimum of $25,000 from the annual stipend. For Scholars studying outside Canada who receive external funding in foreign currency, the Foundation converts that amount into Canadian dollars; the location of study does not affect the Scholarship amount. Scholars may work part-time (up to 20 hours per week) while continuing to receive full benefits, including university or campus-based roles such as research assistant, teaching assistant or lecturer. Scholars may suspend the Scholarship for up to one year for parental, medical, personal or professional leave; the Foundation states Scholars are not employees of the Foundation and it does not provide paid parental leave, and payments are paused until the Scholar re-enrols full-time. Funds begin only after Board of Directors approval, signature of the funding agreement and submission of required documentation. The annual Scholarship is disbursed in three instalments per year. There is no return-home requirement for Canadian students studying abroad or for international students.

scholarships.deadline: No single calendar deadline is published. The Alberta Innovates programme page gives the due date as "Continuous" and states "This program is accepting applications on a seasonal basis. Intake Open Date is specific to each individual university; please contact your university of choice for deadline information." At the University of Calgary, "The Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 of each year" and "Deadlines vary by program"; the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
scholarships.description: This is a programme information page rather than an open scholarship, published by the Czech Development Agency (Důzm zahraniční spolupráce, DZS). It states: "The fourth programme period of the EEA Grants (2021-2028) builds on previous cooperation in the field of education while responding to the current challenges of the Czech education system and to the priorities arising from the Memorandum of Understanding between the Czech Republic and the donor states (Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein), approved by the Government of the Czech Republic in November 2025." The total allocation is "EUR 24.117 million (EUR 20.5 million from the EEA Grants and EUR 3.617 million from national co-financing)", and "Mandatory cooperation with a partner from a donor state is a key element of the programme." The 'Projects and grants' sub-page adds that the programme "will focus on supporting and developing civic and pedagogical competences and on strengthening the quality of initial teacher education as well as teachers' continuing professional development", and that DZS is "currently preparing" it. "The Programme Agreement is expected to be signed in 2026, followed by the launch of the first calls for proposals at the turn of 2026/2027."
scholarships.duration: Terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the program. At the University of Calgary the published terms are $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years.
scholarships.application_period: Continuous at the funder level, with a seasonal intake at each institution. Alberta Innovates publishes the due date as "Continuous". At the University of Calgary the Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year, program deadlines vary and must be confirmed with Graduate Program Staff, and results for the Alberta Innovates competition are announced September to December. Awards are paid in the following academic year, with the majority starting in September.

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is institution-specific. Each of the participating Alberta institutions has its own scholarship application and evaluation processes for students in full-time programmes, and Alberta Innovates directs students to their faculty of graduate studies for that information. At the University of Calgary the competition is merit-based and the applicant must be able to clearly articulate alignment with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and the potential impacts of the work for Alberta. For the Killam and Open Doctoral categories a first-class average is required, which at the University of Calgary is a grade point average of 3.5 or higher in the last two years of study, though that published indicator is stated for those categories rather than for the Alberta Innovates category. Successful students may normally hold one GAC scholarship per year across the Open Doctoral and Special Awards categories and will be awarded the highest-value scholarship for which they are eligible.

Promotion funding ends in the month of the last examination or defence of the dissertation, and is initially granted for three years, with a six-month extension possible on justified application and up to a maximum of four years in exceptional cases such as illness or pregnancy. The online application form for Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen is published and open.
scholarships.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung funds doctoral candidates from abroad who are admitted to a German university, paying 1,500 euros a month plus a supplement for statutory health insurance, together with an extensive political education programme. Applicants must have very good German skills (B2 accepted, also without a certificate, and required even when the dissertation is written in English), socio-political engagement, identification with the values of social democracy, an above-average and fast degree result, and a research project that makes a significant contribution to research. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
scholarships.duration: As a rule three and a half years; in justified exceptional cases it can be granted for longer, but at the latest until the final examination
scholarships.application_period: Continuous/rolling: applications are accepted while the doctoral thesis can still be completed within the funding period, in principle from about two years before submission of the dissertation. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the relevant meeting.

scholarships.selection_notes: The FES checks the online application for formal and content criteria. In selecting, it particularly considers applications from people who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as from women and from students at universities of applied sciences and in MINT subjects. Suitable applicants are passed to a trust lecturer for a specialist interview that produces an opinion; shortlisted applicants then have a second interview with a member of the selection committee, whose opinion goes to the committee's meeting. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and decides on admission; the applicant is informed at the latest one week after the meeting. All applicants are informed by email at each stage. 'Above average' refers to the average grade in the subject at the university location or in the training occupation.

scholarships.notes: The scholarship does not have to be repaid. scholarships.title: France 2030 - PEPR GFM "Grands Fonds Marins" - Appel à projets - 2026
scholarships.name: France 2030 - PEPR GFM "Grands Fonds Marins" - Appel à projets - 2026
scholarships.funding_period: one-off grant per project (36-54 month projects)

applicant_utility.summary: This is consortium funding for institutions, not a personal scholarship: the money goes to a coordinating French higher education or research institution, companies and foreign partners join without funding, and any doctoral or post-doctoral positions are salaried jobs on the project budget rather than scholarships. The design constraints are strict - 36 to 54 months, 800 kEUR to 3 M EUR requested, English scientific document on the mandatory template capped at 15 pages - and the evaluation rewards genuinely wide interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary breadth, so a consortium that merely adds one humanities partner to a geology project will read thin. Build in the required maturation phase with its roadmap, ethics analysis and internal ethics charter, name your data and ethics referents at submission, and collect every partner's signed and stamped commitment letter well before 17 November 2026 at 11:00 Paris time, because only the complete file sitting on the submission site at closing counts.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A permanent researcher or teacher-researcher at a French higher education or research institution who can coordinate a 36-54 month, wide-interdisciplinary deep-sea consortium and needs ANR funding of 800 kEUR - 3 M EUR including doctoral and post-doctoral positions.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the project maps onto at least one of the five PEPR GFM challenges and can defend its interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary claim under section 2.2 of the AAP
Size the budget inside 800 kEUR - 3 M EUR with an explicit justification - no level inside the range is favoured, but the sizing must match the consortium and its staffing
Register on the ANR submission site early and test the upload sections before the final week
Draft the scientific document on the published template, in English, within 15 pages, including the three-year publication list appendix
Collect signed and stamped commitment letters from every partner for the administrative and financial document
Budget for the compulsory in-person meetings (two every 18 months in metropolitan France) and the 3-4 travels every two years for workpackage leaders and staff in training
common_rejection_risks: A file that is incomplete at the closing time - only the electronic version present at closing is evaluated
Exceeding the 15-page scientific limit or departing from the template
A consortium that claims interdisciplinarity without a shared scientific question integrating conceptual frameworks
Missing the maturation phase, ethics analysis, internal ethics charter or Data Management Plan design, all of which are evaluation criteria
No named referent donnees, referent des enjeux ethiques or equity-and-inclusion monitor at submission
Requesting aid outside the 800 kEUR - 3 M EUR range or proposing a project shorter than 36 or longer than 54 months
Sea campaigns on unprogrammed fleet means without the upstream feasibility study and CNFH/CNFC commission minutes
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The grant pays the project's eligible costs (equipment, assigned personnel, running costs) to the coordinating institution; anything outside the eligible-expenditure framework - and any participation by companies or foreign institutions - is not funded by this call.
document_audit: The administrative and financial document must contain every partner's commitment letter signed and stamped by the legal representative - chase these early, they are the classic last-minute failure
The scientific document must be an unprotected PDF in English on the published template, with the publications appendix
If a sea campaign is planned, the ad hoc commission minutes (CNFH or CNFC) are part of the file
A consortium agreement is needed only in defined cases, but where required it must reach the ANR within 12 months of the aid contract - its absence can stop funding and trigger repayment
alerts: This is a one-off exceptional grant distinct from recurrent institutional funding, intended for new actions

Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript in HAL, deliver a first PGD within six months, and deposit data in a thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv
Communications must mention France 2030 support and use its logos, and annual indicator reporting to the State and ANR is mandatory

The aid may constitute State aid and is subject to the French research State-aid framework, the RDI exemption regime, the de-minimis Regulation and the 2011/20/EU decision - check your institution's cumulative aid position before sizing the request

The call is a single phase, with projects of 36 to 54 months requesting 800 kEUR to 3 M EUR of ANR funding within a total envelope of approximately 17.5 M EUR, awarded to French higher education and research institutions.

scholarships.selection_notes: Only proposals satisfying the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are assessed by an independent international-dimension committee convened by the ANR, which may call on external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after sending questions in advance. The committee produces (1) a list of projects it recommends for funding on the published criteria and (2) a list it proposes not to fund because quality is insufficient on at least one criterion, with a written justification for each project, and may give an opinion on the amount requested. Uninvolved PEPR GFM programme directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after opinion of the CPMo and the SGPI, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (a) scientific ambition and excellence (research question going beyond the documented state of the art, discipline combination justified by the question, dialogue of conceptual frameworks, ethical questions treated as integral to ambition); (b) quality of the consortium, resources mobilised and governance (recognised complementary expertise, adequacy of staff with objectives including a precise role and career benefit for each contractual worker, structured maturation phase, mechanisms for shared appropriation of questions, inventory/acquisition/management strategy for data and samples, recurrent ethical monitoring mechanisms, explicit choices to minimise the environmental footprint, coherent sizing with an argued 0.8-3 M€ budget); (c) fit with the PEPR GFM challenges and impact (clear fit with at least one challenge and the programme's strategic priorities, described scientific/economic/environmental/societal impacts, described sharing of data and results, open-access data strategy with FAIR and CARE and Opidor PGD links, dissemination to academic and non-academic audiences).

scholarships.best_fit: A permanent staff member (enseignant-chercheur or chercheur) at a French higher education or research institution who can lead a 36-54 month consortium and needs to build a genuinely new, wide-interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary deep-sea research consortium, typically with 800 k€-3 M€ of ANR money and with doctoral students to hire on the project budget.
scholarships.notes: Aid is awarded as a one-off exceptional grant, distinct from recurrent institutional funding, intended for new actions. It is a grant to an institution, not a personal scholarship: no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is paid to individual students, and the individuals hired on a project are salaried employees of the host institution. Consortiums without companies are not obliged to conclude and transmit a consortium agreement; where required, the coordinating institution must supply it to the ANR within a maximum of 12 months from signature of the aid contract, and its absence can lead to cessation of funding and repayment under article 6.6 of the Financial Regulation. Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, deliver a first PGD within 6 months of project start, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and must mention the France 2030 support and logos in communications. Annual indicator reporting to the State and the ANR is mandatory for ex-post evaluation. Financial aid may constitute State aid under TFEU Article 107(1) and is subject to the French research State-aid framework 2022/C 414/01, the RDI exemption regime SA.111723, the de-minimis Regulation 2023/2831 and the 2011/20/EU decision.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an institutional call, not a personal scholarship: a French coordinating organisation submits and receives the money, so an individual doctoral candidate cannot apply in their own name. Budget between EUR 500k and EUR 2M depending on the axis you pick, and note that the closing date has already been extended once from 15 October to 10 November 2026. If your project is clinical or mixed you must have a second French research structure committed before you can file, so consortium-building time is the real constraint, not the writing.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your coordinating institution falls into one of the three published beneficiary categories before anything else.
Fix the axis first, because it sets both your duration window and your aid band.
Line up a second, different French research structure identified by an RNSR number if you are on the clinical or mixed axis.
Identify and document every cohort, database or health-data warehouse record you will mobilise, including SNDS or French Minds data, before writing the proposal.
Collect each partner's signed commitment letter and the administrative/financial signature early - the scan is part of the complete file.
Open the ANR submission account well before 10 November and read the FAQ published after the 26 August 2026 webinar.
common_rejection_risks: A project that reads as mainly addiction research - only secondary or comorbid addiction questions inside the four target disorders stay in scope.

Clinical or mixed projects assembled around a single French research structure.
A scientific document that overruns 15 pages, is not on the ANR template, or is deposited as a protected PDF.
Leaving the mobilised data sets vague, which makes feasibility inside 24-48 months impossible to verify.
Scientific objectives that duplicate a project already funded by, or currently under evaluation at, the ANR.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The grant covers eligible research expenditure under the PEPR financial regulation only. Anything outside those eligible costs - and every individual's tuition, living costs or personal travel - must be met from other sources.

Submission documents and signed documents have distinct upload sections on the submission site; a file placed in the wrong section counts as missing.
A consortium agreement is mandatory only when companies are involved, otherwise within 12 months of signature when required - its absence can stop funding and trigger repayment.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot join this call cold: step 1 closed in May 2026, so you must already hold a M-ERA.NET invitation from at least three funding agencies in three different countries before the 18 November 2026 step-2 deadline. The ANR only funds four of the six call topics, and your final TRL must stay at or below 5, so an industry-facing project aimed at demonstration is not eligible here. Budget your ANR request at 15 000 EUR minimum and remember that the amount cannot be increased between the two steps.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A French materials, energy-storage, energy-conversion, functional-materials or electronics team whose pre-proposal cleared step 1 and which needs ANR co-funding inside a three-country consortium.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your consortium still has at least three funded partners from three countries, with two EU or Horizon Europe associated countries, after any step-1 withdrawals.
Check the person-month balance: no single partner above 60% and no single country above 70% of total effort.
Confirm your topic is one of 1, 2, 4 or 6 and that the justification is already visible from the pre-proposal - it cannot be invented at step 2.
Re-check that the TRL of every French task stays in fundamental or the first applied research segment and that the final TRL is 5 or lower.
Keep the requested ANR aid inside the caps; do not plan on increasing it, because increases between steps are not authorised.
Have your hierarchy sign off formally, since the scientific lead must commit that the managing institution approved the submission.
common_rejection_risks: One or more invited partners dropping out and pushing the remaining effort above the 60% or 70% thresholds, or above 15% of total effort, which discards the whole proposal.
Applying under topic 3 or 5, which makes a French partner ineligible for ANR funding even though the consortium is otherwise strong.
A final TRL above 5 or work positioned in later applied-research segments, which is an automatic ineligibility for ANR-funded partners.
Modifying the scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal.
Adding a partner from a country that was not in the pre-proposal - only partners from already-involved countries may be added at step 2.
Exceeding the page limit on the mandatory template, which ANR treats as an ineligible modification.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Aid covers only the eligible costs of partners that requested ANR funding, at the rate set by the ANR Financial Regulation. Any partner not funded by ANR, any non-eligible cost category and any individual's tuition or living costs must be carried by the partner's own institution or other funders.
document_audit: The M-ERA.NET template is compulsory - any unauthorised change, including a page-limit overrun, can make the proposal ineligible.
Annexe 1 with the CVs of all consortium participants is mandatory and must also be in English; a missing CV set is a completeness failure.
Partners requesting ANR aid must file the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site as well - the link and deadline arrive by email, so watch the coordinator's inbox.
If genetic resources are used the Nagoya due diligence declaration receipt must reach the ANR by the date of final payment.
alerts: Step 1 is closed; only M-ERA.NET-invited coordinators can submit in step 2 by 18 November 2026 at 12:00 CET.
The requested aid cannot be increased between step 1 and step 2, so set the figure correctly at pre-proposal stage.

The optional 20 000 EUR European-preparation supplement requires a dedicated work package and budget, an FP10-targeted proposal coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner, and is subject to final assessment.

Applications must be approached through your institution's defence and security officer or PPST services, and projects with foreign partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion - a negative opinion prevents selection.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The coordinator files the detailed proposal on the M-ERA.NET submission site by 18 November 2026 at 12:00 CET, ANR-requesting partners file the identical proposal on the ANR submission site via the emailed link, M-ERA.NET's independent experts evaluate centrally, the funder group draws up the recommended list, and each funder - including the ANR - takes its own final funding decision.

scholarships.deadline: Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET. The two-step schedule is: "Étape 1 : 12/05/2026, 12 h 00 (CEST)" (pre-proposals, closed) and "Étape 2 : 18/11/2026, 12 h 00 (CET)" (detailed proposals). Only coordinators whose pre-proposal was recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries and who received the M-ERA.NET invitation may deposit a detailed proposal in step 2. Partners requesting ANR aid must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with the exact link and deadline communicated later by email.
scholarships.description: The M-ERA.NET Call 2026, the 2027 edition for the ANR, brings together more than 30 funding agencies to fund ambitious transnational research and innovation projects in advanced materials and battery technology supporting the European Green Deal and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Partners of selected projects are funded directly by their own national or regional organisations, so national and regional eligibility rules apply in addition to those of the call.
scholarships.duration: Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).
scholarships.application_period: Ouverture : 31/03/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Limite de dépôt des pré-dossiers : 12/05/2026 à 12:00 CEST (step 1, closed). Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET (step 2, open on 2026-10-01). An information webinar was held on 18 March 2026, 12:00-14:00 CET, with presentations and the recording available on the M-ERA.NET call site.
scholarships.official_source: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR), pour le compte du consortium M-ERA.NET
eligibility: The pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one (and only one) scientific collaboration theme defined in the call.
Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).

Minimum consortium composition of 3 Partners requesting funding from a funding agency listed in Annex 3 of the call text and eligible for that funding, from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026. Partners not requesting funding may participate if this minimum is met.
The coordinator must request funding from one of the agencies participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026 and be eligible there.
The involvement of a single Partner must not exceed 60% of the total involvement (measured in person-months) of the proposal.
The involvement of Partners from a single country must not exceed 70% of the total involvement (measured in person-months).

If one or more Partners are not eligible (or not invited to step 2) and their total effort is equal to or greater than 15% of the total project effort (in person-months), the entire pre-proposal or detailed proposal is discarded from the selection process.
To be invited to submit a detailed proposal in step 2, the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different countries participating in the Call 2026.

A pre-proposal containing one or more Partners requesting ANR aid must clearly indicate the topic studied and the TRL levels of the tasks of each French partner in the consortium, and must be deposited on the ANR submission site in step 2, in addition to the deposit on the call site, providing all the information requested on the site.

A pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one of the ANR-eligible topics: 1. Materials for energy storage and distribution systems; 2. Materials for energy conversion; 4. Innovative functional materials with designed architectures; 6. Next-generation materials for electronics. The relevance of the proposal to the chosen topic must be clearly justified from step 1; proposals not matching these topics are rendered ineligible for ANR funding.

The final TRL of the project must not exceed 5 for an ANR-funded partner, on pain of ineligibility, and the work carried out by partners requesting ANR aid must necessarily be positioned either in the "fundamental research" segment or in the first "applied research" segment.

Partners, legal or natural persons, subject to European Union sanctions are excluded from the call; the ANR declares ineligible any partner requesting its aid who is associated within the submitted project with partners covered by a sanction measure. As of publication this concerns in particular partners from Russia and Belarus, and partners from territories of Ukraine escaping the control of the Ukrainian government. The list is non-exhaustive and may change with new EU sanctions.

A project proposal may not be similar in whole or in part to another proposal submitted to any ANR call under evaluation (all calls and all evaluation stages) or funded by the ANR. Similarity is established when the projects describe identical main objectives or result from a simple adaptation.
A researcher may request ANR aid (whether as partner, coordinator or co-coordinator) for only one proposal in the 2026/27 M-ERA.NET call.
Each project Partner must meet its own funding agency's national or regional criteria, including its TRL requirements, and must be selected by that agency to receive funding.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: A French partner may request ANR aid if the consortium has at least three funded partners from three different countries with at least two EU member states or Horizon Europe associated countries, the project matches exactly one ANR-eligible topic, the final TRL for the ANR-funded partner does not exceed 5, no single partner exceeds 60% and no single country exceeds 70% of person-months, and the aid requested stays within the ANR caps.
benefits: ANR aid of at least 15 000 € per partner, with the requested amount not exceeding 180 000 € for a non-coordinating partner and 250 000 € for a coordinating partner.
A total ANR aid cap of 350 000 € for a project with several ANR partners.

An optional additional 20 000 € per project for network-development activities, on a commitment to draft and submit, after the M-ERA.NET project, a collaborative international research proposal to calls of the next EU Framework Programme (FP10), coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner. This raises the caps to 200 000 €, 270 000 € and 370 000 € respectively.

Only the eligible costs of the Partners that have requested ANR aid are financed; the applicable funding rate and cost types are set by the ANR Financial Regulation (eligible cost sheet no. 3) and can be determined by completing the "Déclaration relative aux activités économiques des Partenaires d'un projet ANR" form.
Project duration up to 36 months.

This raises the caps to 200 000 €, 270 000 € and 370 000 € respectively.

Project duration up to 36 months.
requirements: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, written in English, must be deposited by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site.
Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification, in particular exceeding the page limit, may render the proposal ineligible.
The pre-proposal must be the duly completed pre-proposal form, in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions.

The detailed proposal must be the duly completed detailed-proposal form in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions, and must include Annex 1 describing the Partner profiles together with the CVs of all consortium participants, also in English.

Partners requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated later by email.
National and regional eligibility, selection and funding rules apply at both steps, and for some countries/regions restrictions on topics, TRL levels and the type of eligible partners apply.
The scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal cannot be modified at step 2.

It is not possible to add Partners from new countries to the consortium in step 2; only new Partners from countries already involved in the pre-proposal via a funding request to one of their funding agencies may be added.

Any change must be communicated to and accepted by the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date, with the consortium coordinator ensuring acceptance.

The scientific lead (Responsable scientifique) formally commits that their hierarchy (administrative and financial services and persons legally entitled to represent the managing institution, or their representatives) has approved the submission and that the information has been communicated to them.

French project leaders (requesting funding or not) ensure compliance with the national research professions deontology charter and the ANR deontology and scientific-integrity charter within the research activities carried out under their responsibility.

Where genetic resources are used, all participants (requesting funding or not) must respect the Nagoya Protocol obligations, and beneficiaries under the access-and-benefit-sharing regulation must provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the date of the final payment.
Where relevant, take into account the sex and/or gender dimension in the research and give equitable visibility to the work produced.

Before any ANR project deposit, applicants should approach their institution's defence and security officer or PPST services to verify their project's eligibility conditions; projects with foreign public or private partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion, and a negative opinion prevents selection.

scholarships.english_requirement: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, and Annexe 1, must be written in English (rédigées en langue anglaise). The ANR also states that, on request, a translation of the evaluation criteria may be provided.
application_method: Register the intended project with the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site before the step 1 pre-proposal deadline of 12/05/2026 at 12:00 CEST (this step is closed).
Submit the pre-proposal form in English on the M-ERA.NET site, clearly stating the topic and, where ANR aid is sought, the TRL levels of each French partner's tasks.
Wait for the M-ERA.NET invitation: the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries.
Prepare the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory template, with Annexe 1 and the CVs of all consortium participants.
For ANR aid, await the email from the ANR with the exact ANR submission link and deadline, then deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site.
Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET; the ANR does not require a deposit on its site at step 1.
Communicate and obtain acceptance of any change from the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
scholarships.selection_notes: Evaluation and selection are centralised at M-ERA.NET level and take place in two steps: step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations to step 2 issued in ranking order and taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by independent international experts convened by the same secretariat. Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection follows the ranking. The list of projects recommended for funding is drawn up by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is then taken individually by the funders concerned. Results are sent by the call secretariat to the project coordinators. Evaluation modalities and criteria are those of the call text (Guide for proposers) available on the ANR call page and the M-ERA.NET call site; the ANR adds its own horizontal objectives, which are that projects show significant French participation (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the work), generate significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and are ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration. During discussions to separate projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, projects involving a wider and/or more diverse consortium may be favoured.
scholarships.program_type: Research grant
scholarships.best_fit: A researcher or institution in France leading or joining a materials or battery-technology consortium of at least three funded partners from at least three different countries, whose pre-proposal was recommended in step 1 and who need French ANR co-funding for a maximum 36-month project in one of the four ANR-eligible topics.
scholarships.notes: This is institutional research funding, not a personal scholarship: nothing is paid to individual students and no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is established for individuals. The aid is paid to each partner's own national or regional organisation, not centrally. Amounts may not be increased between the two steps: increases are not authorised, and projects that do not respect the aid limits or that do not conform to any budgetary adjustments requested by the ANR are declared ineligible. The 20 000 € European-preparation supplement is conditional on adequate planning and activities within the M-ERA.NET project (a dedicated Work Package and budget under the responsibility of an ANR-funded partner), on the activities actually leading to a research proposal involving consortium members in continuity with the M-ERA.NET work, and on the follow-up proposal targeting clearly identified FP10 calls (not co-funded by the ANR) coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner; it is a subject of a final assessment and a supplementary deliverable to the ANR. Beneficiaries commit to immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, a FAIR approach to research data, a PGD within 6 months of the scientific start, deposit of data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and free-licence release and Software Heritage archiving of software. Any change affecting the whole project (extensions, consortium modifications) must be approved by all partners, their funding agencies and M-ERA.NET. Proposals may be transmitted to other administrations, control bodies and partner funders, and certain national funders are obliged to publish submitted pre-proposals/proposals, which may disclose intellectual-property or business-secret content; applicants are warned to be careful with what they include. The ANR applies the PPST protection of the scientific and technical potential of the nation to projects with foreign public or private partners, and a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion prevents selection without reasons being given.

scholarships.title: AFdoc – Aides à la formation doctorale (FNR PhD funding scheme)
scholarships.name: AFdoc – Aides à la formation doctorale (FNR PhD funding scheme)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a salary, not a stipend: the FNR gives the money to your host institution, which then employs you, so you will be on an employment contract rather than receiving a bursary. The ceiling is EUR 54,574 a year including employer charges, but the actual figure is set per project, so the published maximum is not a promise. Tuition and research costs are explicitly excluded, so if your host charges doctoral fees you need a second source of money. The very first call closes on 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET, and from 2027 the scheme moves to two calls a year with April and November deadlines.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A Master's graduate with a demonstrated link to Luxembourg who wants a funded, employed PhD at a public university abroad or with a Luxembourg R&D company partnered to a PhD-awarding institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the AFdoc guidelines to check whether your personal link to Luxembourg meets the FNR's definition - the instrument page only summarises it.
Secure your host and supervisor early: the Host Institution must be a public PhD-awarding institution abroad or an accredited Luxembourg R&D company.
For company-based projects, confirm the collaboration with a public PhD-awarding institution is documented before you submit.
Make sure you will be enrolled in the PhD programme by the project start date, not just admitted.
Build the budget around the EUR 54,574 employer-inclusive ceiling and be explicit that tuition and research costs sit outside it.
Work on the AFdoc project description template and the COMMITMENT LETTER, then submit in English through grants.fnr.lu well before 14:00 CET on deadline day.
common_rejection_risks: Not being able to evidence a link to Luxembourg as the FNR defines it in the guidelines.
Not yet holding a PhD but already receiving an old-age pension, which is an explicit exclusion.
A host that is neither a public PhD-awarding institution abroad nor an accredited Luxembourg R&D company.
A company-based project without a documented collaboration with a public PhD-awarding institution.
Budgeting tuition or research costs into the award, which the FNR states are not eligible.
Submitting more than one proposal in the same call.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees and related research costs are not eligible and must be funded elsewhere. The salary contribution is also a ceiling: if the host institution's employment cost model exceeds EUR 54,574 a year, the difference between the indexed salary and the FNR contribution has to be met by the host.
document_audit: The call documents sit in an FNR SharePoint folder rather than on the instrument page, so download the application guidelines, selection guidelines, project description template and commitment letter from there before starting.
The COMMITMENT LETTER is a separate required piece from the host, not a line you write yourself.
The application must be in English; French or German drafts will not do for the submission system.
Only one proposal per applicant per call is allowed, so choose the host carefully.
alerts: The first-ever call closes on Wednesday 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET - this is a brand-new scheme, so there is no past-round precedent to calibrate against.

From 2027 the scheme runs two calls a year: decisions in July for the February call and in March for the September call, with funded projects starting no later than 1 February and 1 October respectively.
The 2026 call is a pilot for a self-assessment on potential research security aspects, so expect that topic in the application.
A webinar hosted by ACEL and FNR took place on 10 September 2026; its materials are the quickest way to pick up the 'link to Luxembourg' definition.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You prepare the proposal on the AFdoc templates with your host's commitment letter, submit it in English through the FNR Grant Management System by the 14:00 CET deadline, and the FNR assesses project quality, applicant potential, host quality and impact before communicating its funding decision - March for the September call, July for the February call.

scholarships.deadline: First call: 'a deadline on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET'. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first call launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, and the second call launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET.
scholarships.description: Following the entry into force of the new FNR law on 1 August 2026, the Luxembourg National Research Fund is launching AFdoc - Aides a la formation doctorale, a PhD funding scheme supporting talented doctoral candidates with a clear link to Luxembourg who undertake PhD projects in established research environments abroad or through collaborations involving Luxembourg-based R&D companies.
scholarships.duration: Funding may cover up to four years of doctoral training.
scholarships.application_period: The very first call was launched mid-September 2026 with a deadline on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET, so the scheme is open on 2026-10-01. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first call launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, funding decisions are communicated in July and funded projects must start no later than 1 February of the following year; the second call launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET, decisions are communicated in March of the following year and funded projects must start no later than 1 October.

scholarships.selection_notes: Eligible proposals are assessed on the scientific quality and potential of the project, the applicant's profile and potential, the quality of the Host Institution, supervision and training environment, and the expected impact of the project. AFdoc follows a bottom-up approach: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible, and projects do not need to align with Luxembourg's National Research Priorities provided they fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner. The 2026 call is a pilot for a self-assessment on potential research security aspects.
scholarships.program_type: Government research funding
scholarships.best_fit: Doctoral candidates who already hold a Master's degree, can demonstrate a clear link to Luxembourg, and want to do a funded PhD at a public university abroad or at a Luxembourg R&D company working with a public PhD-awarding institution.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold citizenship of Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines or Vietnam - the country list is closed and not extendable
Check your age at the time you apply: 35 for undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate applicants, 45 for postdocs

Match yourself to the right published category: undergraduate; graduate of an artistic field for a music practice study visit; postgraduate at an ASEA-UNINET member university; postgraduate admitted to a doctoral/PhD programme in Austria; or postdoc teaching and researching at an ASEA-UNINET member university
If you want to do a doctorate in Austria, secure proof that you fulfil the admission requirements before applying
If you are a postdoc, confirm you are involved in teaching and research at an ASEA-UNINET member university in one of the five eligible countries
Read the Ernst Mach grant guidelines, available in German as 'Sonderrichtlinie Incoming' - this is the binding rulebook
Read the 'Information on travel costs subsidy' before you cost your travel
Plan to apply through the OeAD grants database at grants.at before 1 March
If you only need a short research stay of 1-2 months, consider the Short-term Research Grant instead, where applications are ongoing
important_advice_for_students: Do not confuse this with the Ernst Mach Grant Ukraine strand, which ended on 30 June 2026 and had a published stipend of 715 euros per month - that figure does not apply to ASEA-UNINET
Do not expect a published award amount here; OeAD publishes no figure for the ASEA-UNINET strand, and the only amount on the page belongs to a different, closed strand
Be ready to work in German for the guidelines: the operative Sonderrichtlinie is published in German only
Apply well before 1 March; the closing date is the only date OeAD publishes and the opening date is not stated
If you are a Southeast Asian postdoc or lecturer, the Short-term Research Grant is easier: ongoing applications, 1-2 months, eight eligible countries including Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar
Your stay length is fixed by category, so choose the category before you plan the research period
common_rejection_risks: Applying from a country outside the five eligible ones, including Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar, which are eligible only for the Short-term Research Grant
Being over the age limit at the time of application
Applying as a postgraduate who cannot evidence admission to an Austrian doctoral programme
Applying as a postdoc who is not teaching and researching at an ASEA-UNINET member university
Assuming the sibling strands' windows apply - worldwide opens in September, the Fachhochschule strand in October, but this strand has only a 1 March closing date
Missing 1 March, the single published deadline for this strand
Missing documents required by the German-language Sonderrichtlinie Incoming
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond whatever the grant provides - OeAD publishes no stipend or allowance figure for this strand, so the gap cannot be quantified from the official source
Costs above any travel subsidy cap, which is set in the German-language travel information document
Fees and living costs at the Austrian host institution, which are not described as covered
document_audit: The binding rulebook is 'Sonderrichtlinie Incoming' (Ernst Mach scholarship guidelines), published in German only

No document list is published on the pages read; the document set comes from the German-language guideline

Applications are submitted through grants.at, so verify format rules in that system before submitting
Expect to supply proof of nationality, age, institutional affiliation and, for Austrian doctorates, admission requirements

scholarships.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme gives young people who hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant is made up of a one-off travel allowance and a monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, both set in advance; the monthly amount depends on the host city. Nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant, and the programme targets people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights. The 2026 budget is exhausted; a budget is available again for 2027, with applications reopenable from January 2027.
scholarships.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months. The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2026 are closed. The 2027 budget reopens for applications in January 2027 for internships taking place in 2027, and new internship vacancies will be published on the programme's internships page from late 2026 onwards. Inside a funded budget year the published rule is that you may apply at any time of the year until one day before your internship starts, up to six months in advance, but a grant is only granted while budget remains.
scholarships.official_source: Government of Flanders — Flanders Trainee Programme (Departement Buitenlandse Zaken)
eligibility: You are younger than 35 on the start date of your internship.
You have obtained a secondary or higher education diploma in Flanders. So your nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant.
You have secured an internship with a multilateral organisation from the published qualifying list.
The internship lasts at least two and up to six months.
The internship must take place at the headquarters or a field office of the organisation, within the areas of jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: You must be under 35 when the internship starts, hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders, and have secured an internship of at least two months with an organisation on the published list of qualifying multilateral organisations.
benefits: The grant is not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, so it is not an obstacle to the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit you may still be entitled to for 12 months after finishing your studies

scholarships.selection_notes: No competitive jury or published ranking is described for this programme. The published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: in principle you can apply at any time of the year, but you only get a grant if budget is still available, and if a budget is no longer available for the current year that is announced clearly on the programme website; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available. The average administrative turnaround time is three weeks. The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Anyone under 35 with a secondary or higher education diploma earned at a Flemish institution, of any nationality, who has already secured or is about to secure an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation such as the UN, NATO-adjacent bodies, the OECD, the WHO family, the Council of Europe, the Benelux Union or an EU institution.
scholarships.notes: The grant is explicitly not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, made up of a one-off travel allowance and an expense allowance for accommodation and living expenses. Coverage is partial: it does not pay tuition or course fees, there is no travel payment for an internship in Belgium, and the amounts are capped at a fixed 200 or 500 EUR travel payment plus a city-based monthly living amount. The internship can be extended to a total of six months, or nine months for internships linked to a project funded by the Government of Flanders. If you end the internship early you must inform the programme and may have to repay part of the grant, the amount being determined by the number of days you actually worked. There is no clinical or professional restriction published beyond the requirement that the host be a qualifying multilateral organisation.

scholarships.title: Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff — Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia
scholarships.name: Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff — Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia

applicant_utility.summary: Only 15 awards exist in the 2026 round and historically about 10% of applicants win, so treat this as a top-up rather than a funding plan. Nothing is paid toward tuition - the Board repeats that other costs are not covered - so you need an Estonian admission letter plus independent money for fees, housing, insurance and travel. The critical-path item is the host institution's confirmation letter, which must name your 2026/27 degree or exchange status, level of study, curriculum and exact study dates; PhD applicants additionally need written proof they hold no junior researcher contract. Everything goes in a single email to rvo.dokumendid@harno.ee by 23:59 Estonian time on 31 October 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's or PhD applicants from the 39 listed countries who already hold (or can obtain before 31 October 2026) a 2026/27 admission confirmation from an Estonian HEI and can cover tuition and living costs from other sources.
application_readiness_checklist: Email your Estonian HEI admissions office in September 2026 and request a confirmation letter naming 2026/27 degree or exchange student status, level of study, curriculum, and study start and end dates
Download the fixed 'Degree_exhange study APPLCIATION FORM 2026.docx' from harno.ee and fill it in without altering its structure
Prepare a clean scan of your passport or ID card as a PDF
If applying at PhD level, ask the HEI to add a line confirming you have no active (junior) researcher employment contract; if you enrolled before 2025/26, add proof of full-time study in 2025/26
Get any non-English/non-Estonian document translated into English or Estonian and attach the translation with it
Draft the motivation letter first, since motivation and overall application quality are the two equally weighted criteria, then submit the whole package in one email before the deadline
common_rejection_risks: No admission confirmation letter attached by the deadline - such applications are not processed at all, which is the most common outright knock-out
Sending an incomplete file, or splitting the three annexes across several emails; the address accepts complete applications only
Documents in another language without an English or Estonian translation
Missing the 23:59 Estonian time cut-off, including submissions that are still 31 October in your own time zone
Being a citizen of the Russian Federation or Belarus, whose applications are excluded from the 2026/2027 round entirely
PhD applicants holding an active junior researcher employment contract with the Estonian HEI, which makes them ineligible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, health insurance, residence-permit fees, travel to Estonia, accommodation and day-to-day living costs, since the official page states other costs are not covered. The Board's own guide puts average student living costs at roughly 300-500 EUR per month, with dormitory places around EUR 150-350 and private flats EUR 350-750 per month, against a stipend of 350 EUR (BA/master's) or 660 EUR (doctoral) per month.
document_audit: The Word form must go in as an unmodified .docx - do not convert it to PDF or restructure the layout
A generic admission offer email is usually not enough: the letter must state 2026/27 status, level of study, curriculum and exact start/end dates
PhD applicants need a separate statement in the letter about having no junior researcher employment contract
Scans must match the originals, because the Board reserves the right to check conformity with submitted documents
Send questions to liis.uulman@harno.ee, not to the application address, which is for complete applications only
alerts: The window is one month long and closes at 23:59 Estonian time on 31 October 2026, so applicants outside Europe must convert the deadline to their own time zone
Winning does not guarantee admission: you must separately satisfy the host HEI's own admission requirements, and the final scholarship decision is made only after admission is confirmed
If you do not start or continue studying in Estonia you lose the scholarship, and changes to the scholarship period after results need the Board's written consent and cannot increase the total
The award covers one academic year only and no automatic renewal is published for this strand, so year two onwards needs a new funding plan
The summer school and researcher strands of the same Estonian Scholarship Programme use an April-May window, so do not confuse those deadlines with the October round
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure the HEI confirmation letter, complete the unmodified Word form, assemble the passport/ID scan plus any translations, then send one email with all three annexes to rvo.dokumendid@harno.ee titled 'Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia'; the committee weighs motivation against overall application quality and announces results personally by email.

The rate is EUR 350 per month for first-cycle (BA) and master's studies and EUR 660 per month for doctoral studies. The Board pays the scholarship to the host university, which then disburses it. The scheme is funded under bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements and is run through the Estonian Scholarship Programme.
