This application round is for students who intend to start their doctoral studies before the 1 July 2027.

With the exception of the UC Doctoral Scholarship for Students with Disabilities and the UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships, students can apply for all other Core UC Doctoral Scholarships on the single 'UC Doctoral Scholarship' application form.
You must also have submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications.
These scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year.

Most UC scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports; some require an interview with the selection panel, and the Scholarships Office will notify you if one is required.
UC states that late applications are not accepted and that the closing date is not flexible.
documents: The UC application guidance lists the types of item you may be asked to provide: proof of citizenship or residency status (for example a birth certificate or passport).
Evidence of community involvement, financial hardship or ethnic background, where relevant.
List of referees; referees' reports are a written statement about your abilities from people you nominate.
Transcripts or records of learning, including Scholaro reports if your previous learning was at an overseas institution.
If necessary, an academic or language test.
Privacy provisions that you must sign and date as part of the application.
A CV only if it is specifically requested.
UC advises that if the scholarship entails a particular project, you should find out the full objectives and intended methodology of the project.

application_method: Search the UC scholarships database and read the scholarship's Regulations to confirm you meet every eligibility criterion.
Check the closing date for your round; UC states late applications are not accepted and scholarship applications are generally open approximately eight weeks before closing.
Create a myUC account if you do not already have one; UC states you need a myUC account before you can apply for any scholarship.
Submit your separate admission application for the research doctoral degree programme at UC in your myUC account, before the scholarship closing date (point 2.2 of the Regulations).
In your myUC account, click the 'Apply for a Scholarship' link and use the 'Search' function to find the scholarship.
Click 'Apply here' on the scholarship, which brings the application into your myUC account under 'My Applications'.
Complete the application. You can save and return to it. Attach every requested document and sign and date the privacy provisions.

Nominate your referees and make sure they know which scholarships you are applying for, the closing date, and what they must include; UC says it is your responsibility to ensure referees' reports arrive by the due date and the Scholarships Office will not follow up missing referee reports.

Submit the application before the closing date, then check that the status in 'My Applications' has changed to 'Submitted' and that you received an email confirming receipt. 'Request Pending' means the application was submitted but at least one reference is outstanding.
Await the outcome; UC states the selection process typically takes six to eight weeks but may take longer, and you will receive notification of the outcome in writing once the selection is final.
scholarships.selection_notes: UC states that most scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports, that some require an interview with the selection panel, and that selection committees vary according to the scholarship. It states the selection process typically takes six to eight weeks but may take longer, and the outcome is notified in writing once selection is final. The scholarship's own selection criteria sit in the Regulations document, which is not published on the pages read here. Prestige awards are awarded from the applicants who applied for a Core scholarship in a given academic year, with no separate application, and are awarded at the end of each academic year.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: International and domestic applicants who intend to enter their first research doctoral degree at the University of Canterbury, can start before 1 July 2027, and hold academic results equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0 over the last two years of relevant academic study.
scholarships.notes: Not deferrable, not renewable, and no must-return-home or clinical restrictions are published on the pages read; treat all four as unconfirmed rather than as published terms. It is a university award, not an Australian or New Zealand Government scholarship, and UC states these scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year. The published value is $32,650 per 120 points plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment up to 360 points; UC does not publish on these pages a statement that living costs, travel, or compulsory course fees outside thesis-only enrolment are covered, so this must not be budgeted as full funding. If you intend to start your doctoral study on or after 1 July 2027 you are in the wrong round and must apply in the next round, which opens 20 March and closes 15 May.

scholarships.deadline: Applications close 31 January 2027 for Semester 1, 2027 intake, and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2, 2027 intake.
scholarships.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship is a Charles Darwin University award for international students with a record of academic excellence. CDU publishes that it covers 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course, and that it is neither transferable for cash nor refundable and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. Applicants must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, must be paying international student fees, and must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency. Results are announced during Orientation Week.
scholarships.duration: The minimum time in which the course can be completed, or until the maximum scholarship value is exhausted, the course is completed, or the recipient no longer meets the ongoing eligibility of the scholarship.
scholarships.application_period: Applications are open at the time of checking on 1 October 2026. CDU publishes closing dates of 31 January 2027 for Semester 1 2027 and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2 2027, but does not publish a separate opening date for the scholarship.
eligibility: Applicant must apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027, in the intake they are first offered.
Applicant must meet the University's academic and English language entry requirements for their chosen course.
Applicant must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification.
Applicant must be an international student paying international student fees.
Applicant must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency.
Applicants must be able to pay their portion of the tuition fees on or before the payment due date, which CDU states is the first day of teaching of each semester.
The scholarship applies to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be international students paying international student fees who apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027, meet CDU's academic and English language entry requirements for their course, hold a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, and not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency.
benefits: Results are announced during Orientation Week, earlier than the start of teaching.

CDU's international student scholarships page also lists automatic, no-application-required awards that can sit alongside a study offer, including the CDU Global Merit Scholarship (30% of the tuition fee for select courses, for new international TAFE, undergraduate, postgraduate coursework and higher degree by research students commencing in 2026 and 2027, automatically assessed after submitting a course application) and the CDU Bachelor of Nursing Scholarship (up to 20% of the tuition fee for the Bachelor of Nursing, for new international students commencing in 2027, automatically assessed).
coverage: 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course.
requirements: Step 1: apply to study at CDU.
Step 2: submit your application for the VCIHAS.
The application form requires an application intake, an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC) and an email address that matches the one provided in the Studylink application.
The form requires an average overall score in your highest completed qualification, expressed as a percentage.

The applicant statement is mandatory and answers why you should be selected, how you will become an outstanding ambassador of CDU, your extracurricular activities with a focus on community engagement, work experience, creative arts and sport, and how you will use your CDU qualification to make a difference in your community.

A declaration must be ticked confirming the information is true and correct, that you have read and understood the conditions of application, that the decision of the University selection panel is final, that you cannot hold more than one tuition fee scholarship from CDU at a time, that you do not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsorship agency, and that you accept you may be asked to provide a student story or testimonial as a scholarship recipient.
The form must be signed and dated.

Ongoing eligibility: continue to be an international student liable for international student fees, pay your portion of tuition fees on or before the first day of teaching of each semester, maintain satisfactory academic progress each semester with a minimum GPA of 5.3 and no fail grade in any unit, and maintain a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless you have approval to reduce your study load or take a leave of absence for the semester.

scholarships.english_requirement: CDU requires all higher education applicants to satisfy the English Language Proficiency Requirements for their chosen course and to supply evidence of this at the time of application. CDU's published minimum English test scores are: IELTS Academic overall minimum 6.5 with no band below 6.0 for postgraduate and overall minimum 6.0 with no band below 6.0 for undergraduate; PTE Academic overall minimum 58 with no score below 50 for postgraduate and overall minimum 50 with no score below 50 for undergraduate; TOEFL overall minimum 79 with a minimum writing score of 21 for postgraduate and overall minimum 60 with a minimum writing score of 21 for undergraduate; Cambridge English Advanced overall minimum 176 with no skill below 169 for postgraduate and overall minimum 169 with no skill below 169 for undergraduate; CDU ELICOS EAP004 for postgraduate and EAP003 for undergraduate; and an approved English test completed within two years of commencement. IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted, allowing a single skill to be retaken within 60 days. Alternative evidence routes published on the same page include Year 12 in an approved English-speaking country, 0.5 FTE of higher education study in an approved country completed within the past five years where relevant, an enabling course, a TAFE qualification at Certificate III or higher, current AHPRA registration, two years of full-time equivalent employment in English-medium roles within the last five years in a recognised English-speaking country, or a primary language pathway declaration.
application_method: Apply to study at CDU and obtain an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC).
Use the same email address in the scholarship form as in your Studylink application.

Complete the Vice-Chancellor's High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS) Application form on CDU's website, including your intended intake, your average overall score as a percentage, and the four applicant statement questions.
Tick the declaration, sign the form and enter the date.
Submit the form before the closing date for your intake: 31 January 2027 for Semester 1 2027 or 4 July 2027 for Semester 2 2027.
Await the outcome; CDU states results will be announced during Orientation Week.
scholarships.selection_notes: CDU publishes the selection criteria as the overall score in your highest completed qualification plus a supporting statement. The application form adds that the decision of the University selection panel is final, and the declaration confirms the process is competitive. CDU publishes no interview requirement, no weighting for the two criteria, no offer round structure and no appeal process for VCIHAS; other CDU International College scholarships on the same page do publish an interview requirement, so confirm whether an interview applies to VCIHAS.

scholarships.notes: This is not full funding: it covers 50% of the tuition fee only, and the recipient must pay their portion of tuition on or before the first day of teaching of each semester. The scholarship is neither transferable for cash nor refundable, and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. It is conditional rather than open-ended: it ends at the earliest of course completion, exhaustion of the maximum scholarship value, or loss of ongoing eligibility, and retaining it requires a minimum GPA of 5.3 with no fail grade in any unit and a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless a reduced load or leave of absence is approved. Only one CDU tuition fee scholarship may be held at a time, and holding another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency disqualifies the applicant. Official pages disagree on the statement length: the scholarship page says up to 600 words, the application form says 500 words or less.

scholarships.funding_period: percent off first-year tuition fees (one year)

applicant_utility.summary: There is nothing to apply for here: you are considered automatically through your admissions application, so the only thing you control is making your admissions application as strong as possible and accepting the academic and scholarship offers separately when they arrive. It is worth 20% of first-year tuition only, not a full scholarship, and it ends after one year, so plan for years two onwards from your own funds. It is also restricted to residents of China, Japan, Mongolia and the two Koreas, and it is void if any external sponsorship covers even part of your ANU tuition.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving applicants resident in China, Japan, Mongolia or Korea applying for an eligible ANU undergraduate, honours, graduate certificate or postgraduate coursework program with no external tuition sponsorship.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your residential status is one of the listed countries or regions before relying on this award.
Check your target program is not the MChD or the MDTE - both are excluded outright.
Aim above the thresholds rather than at them: Selection Rank 85 or equivalent for undergraduate, GPA 5.5 or equivalent for postgraduate.
Make sure no external sponsor is paying any part of your ANU tuition, which would disqualify you.
Treat the admissions application as the scholarship application and submit it early enough to be considered for the intake.
When the two offers arrive, accept the academic offer and the scholarship offer separately, and keep the scholarship offer letter - it states the value.
common_rejection_risks: Holding external sponsorship that covers all or part of your ANU tuition fees.
Applying for the MChD or MDTE, which are excluded programs.
Just missing the Selection Rank 85 or GPA 5.5 thresholds - selection is purely on academic merit with no interview or additional statement to offset a weaker transcript.
Assuming the award applies at every level: it can be offered only once at each level of study, apart from the Honours and packaged-offer exceptions.
Being a resident of a country outside the published list, for which the separate ANU International Achievement Award applies instead.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: 80% of first-year tuition and the whole of second year onwards, plus books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study. ANU states explicitly that recipients are responsible for these.
document_audit: There is no scholarship document to prepare, so the risk sits entirely in the admissions application and its evidence.
The value is not published as a figure - it is stated in the letter of offer, so read that letter carefully rather than budgeting from the web page.
Two acceptances are required: the academic offer and the scholarship offer, and they are separate steps.
The governing document is the Conditions of Award (63/2026) PDF linked from the scholarship page, which contains the conditions the web page only summarises.
alerts: The award lasts one year only, so fee relief stops after your first year.

It can be offered only once at each level of study, except for progression from an undergraduate degree to a one-year Honours program or a packaged offer such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's.
No closing date is published, which reflects the automatic-consideration route rather than an open-ended opportunity - your admissions timing is effectively your deadline.

If your residential status is outside the listed countries, the separate ANU International Achievement Award is the right target, with published values of 20% undergraduate, 20% postgraduate, 25% South East Asia and 50% Pacific.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit an admissions application through the ANU admissions process, ANU assesses eligibility automatically against residential status, academic thresholds and program eligibility, issues an academic offer and, if selected, a separate scholarship offer stating the value, which you accept independently of the academic offer.

scholarships.deadline: Application period: Open for applications. ANU publishes no closing date for this award; consideration is automatic with the admissions application.
scholarships.description: The ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award is an Australian National University award whose stated objective is to attract a diverse range of academically capable overseas students to enrol in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs at ANU, funded by the University. ANU publishes the value as 20% off first-year tuition fees, with the tuition scholarship applied towards tuition at the start of each semester for the one year of the award. It is restricted to residents of China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and excludes the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE). Recipients are responsible for the costs of books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study.
scholarships.duration: Payment made for 1 year (payments are made for a fixed number of years; for this award that is one year)
scholarships.application_period: Continuous. ANU's scholarship page shows the application period as 'Open for applications' with no closing date, because no separate scholarship application is required: all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the University are considered automatically.
eligibility: You are an international student.
You are a new commencing student, or a continuing student who has received an offer of admission to a higher AQF level of studies.

You hold residential status in one of the following Countries or Regions: China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, Republic of Korea, or The Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

You meet the minimum academic entry requirements: undergraduate applicants a Selection Rank of 85 (or equivalent as determined by the University) or above, or postgraduate applicants a minimum GPA of 5.5 (or equivalent).
You are not the recipient of an external sponsorship that covers all or part of your tuition fees at the University.

You acknowledge that the award can be offered only once at each level of study, except where you progress from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8), or accept a packaged offer such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's degree.
Your program is an eligible program, excluding the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE).
Study level: Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters and Graduate certificate. Selection basis: academic merit.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: The award is available to an international student who is a new commencing student, or a continuing student with an offer of admission to a higher AQF level, who holds residential status in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, meets the minimum academic entry requirements (Selection Rank of 85 or equivalent for undergraduate, minimum GPA of 5.5 or equivalent for postgraduate), is not the recipient of an external sponsorship covering all or part of their tuition fees at ANU, and accepts that the award can be offered only once at each level of study.
benefits: No separate scholarship application: all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the University are considered automatically.
You accept the academic offer and the scholarship offer separately; more information is provided with the scholarship offer letter.

ANU publishes a separate ANU International Achievement Award for applicants resident outside this award's country list, with published values of 20% for Undergraduate, 20% for Postgraduate, 25% for South East Asia and 50% for Pacific.
coverage: 20% off your first-year tuition fees, with the tuition scholarship applied towards tuition at the start of each semester.
One year of payments; ANU states the duration of the Award is one year.
requirements: There is no need to apply for the scholarship; all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the university will be automatically considered.
Press the 'Apply now' button to start the Admissions application process.
You will need to accept both your academic offer and your scholarship offer separately; more information is provided with your scholarship offer letter.
The recipient is responsible for making payment of all tuition fees by the prescribed date as set out by the University each session.
The value of the Award is stated in the letter of offer.
Only applicants who meet all the eligibility criteria will be considered.
ANU publishes a Conditions of Award document numbered 63/2026, linked from the scholarship page.
documents: No separate scholarship application or scholarship document is required; consideration is automatic with the admissions application.
The ANU admission application itself, submitted through the 'Apply now' button on the scholarship page.
The scholarship offer letter, which states the value of the Award and must be accepted separately from the academic offer.
required_documents: No separate scholarship application or scholarship document is required; consideration is automatic with the admissions application.
The ANU admission application itself, submitted through the 'Apply now' button on the scholarship page.
The scholarship offer letter, which states the value of the Award and must be accepted separately from the academic offer.
application_method: Choose an eligible ANU program; the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE) are excluded.
Press the 'Apply now' button on the scholarship page to start the ANU Admissions application process.
Submit the admission application; there is no separate scholarship application, and eligibility is assessed automatically.
Receive the academic offer and, if selected, a separate scholarship offer stating the value of the Award.
Accept the academic offer and the scholarship offer separately.
Pay your share of the tuition fees by the prescribed date set out by the University each session; the tuition scholarship is applied towards tuition at the start of each semester of the award year.
scholarships.selection_notes: ANU states that selection is based on academic merit, that only applicants who meet all the eligibility criteria will be considered, that qualifications submitted for admission will be converted to the common scale which determines whether an applicant is eligible, and that eligible applicants with multiple qualifications will be ranked according to the qualification used as the basis of admission. The value of the Award is stated in the letter of offer. ANU publishes no interview, no referee requirement, no offer rounds and no appeal process for this award.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: International students resident in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the Democratic People's Republic of Korea who are applying for admission to an eligible ANU undergraduate, honours, graduate certificate or postgraduate coursework program, meet a Selection Rank of 85 or equivalent (undergraduate) or a GPA of 5.5 or equivalent (postgraduate), and are not already covered by external sponsorship of their tuition fees.
scholarships.notes: This is not full funding and should not be budgeted as such: the published value is 20% off first-year tuition fees for one year only, and recipients pay the balance of all tuition fees by the prescribed date each session. ANU states recipients are responsible for the costs of books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study. The award can be offered only once at each level of study, with two published exceptions: progression from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8), and packaged offers such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's degree. Eligibility is by residential status, not citizenship, and is restricted to China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea; residents of all other countries apply to the separate ANU International Achievement Award. Holding external sponsorship covering all or part of your ANU tuition fees disqualifies you. Deferral, renewal, return-home obligations, clinical restrictions and tax treatment are not published on the page read; the Conditions of Award (63/2026) PDF is the document that governs them and could not be read.

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)

applicant_utility.summary: This is genuinely full funding: entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees are waived, you get an economy-class air ticket and a monthly allowance of 143,000 yen rising to 144,000 or 145,000 yen once you are a regular master's or doctoral student, with 2,000 or 3,000 yen extra if you are placed in one of the specially designated regions. The single most important practical point is that there is no central deadline - each Japanese embassy or consulate sets its own, so your embassy's website is your only reliable source for the closing date and document list. Start by securing provisional acceptance from a Japanese university once you pass the first screening, because MEXT does the placement itself from November.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates under 35 who want a funded master's or doctoral research degree at a Japanese university and are prepared to learn Japanese and adapt to living in Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the age rule: in principle you must have been born on or after April 2, 1992.
Go to the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality and note its own deadline, since MEXT sets none centrally.
Confirm your chosen field of study is not traditional entertainment arts such as Kabuki or classical Japanese dance, and is not restricted by your mission.
Decide between the April term and the October term before you submit, because in principle the choice cannot be changed afterwards.

Assemble the required documents on the 2027 forms: physician-signed health certificate, transcripts for every university year, graduation certificate, and a free-format recommendation letter from your dean or advisor.
After passing first screening, contact Japanese universities directly to request provisional acceptance, then submit the Placement Preference Application Form to your mission.
common_rejection_risks: Being already enrolled, or planning to enrol, in a Japanese university as a privately-financed international student from the time of application until the scholarship payment period starts.
Being a previous grantee of any MEXT scholarship program, which is an automatic bar unless the three-year exception applies.
Planning to receive another scholarship from the Japanese government or a government-related organisation, or simultaneously applying under another MEXT program.
Failing to arrive in Japan within the specified April or October window, in which case travel expenses are not paid and the scholarship is withdrawn.
Changing residence status away from Student after arrival, which suspends payment.
Cheating during the first screening written examination, or having no intention of obtaining a degree in Japan, both disqualify you outright.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel within Japan, airport taxes, special taxes, travel insurance, carry-on luggage or unaccompanied baggage expenses, and travel costs beyond the economy-class ticket MEXT provides. You also bear the entrance examination fee if you cannot proceed to the master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted to the university.
document_audit: The Application Form, Placement Preference Application Form, Field of Study and Research Plan and Medical certificate must all be the 2027 forms - last year's version is a common mistake.
The transcript must cover all academic years of university attended and be issued by the university attended or your national government.
The language proficiency certificate only counts if issued no earlier than two years before application, and is optional.
Abstracts of theses are submitted in three copies and only if you have written theses; the medical certificate requires a physician's signature.
The recommendation letter is free format, so do not wait for a prescribed template.
alerts: There is no central deadline: the guidelines state the deadline for submission of application documents varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission.
Military personnel and military civilian employees are ineligible both at arrival and throughout the payment period.
Applications cannot be made simultaneously with another program under the Japanese Government Scholarship system, including programs whose payments begin in FY2026.
The scholarship is suspended if a grantee is absent from the university for an extended period, and may be reduced or repaid after false statements or other violations.
Arrival choice between the April and October terms is fixed at application in principle; changing it is not permitted.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You apply with all documents to the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality by its own deadline, pass the first screening there, request provisional acceptance directly from Japanese universities, submit the Placement Preference Application Form to your mission by around mid-September to early October, and MEXT then conducts second screening and university placement from November with results notified January to March 2027.

scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
scholarships.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
scholarships.duration: Embassy Recommendation: irregular course within 2 years; regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)
scholarships.application_period: Applications for the 2027 cycle are handled at embassy/consulate level. MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under "募集中のプログラム" (programmes currently being recruited). No central opening or closing date is published; embassies set and publish their own deadlines and sit their own qualifying examinations.

scholarships.english_requirement: No English requirement is published; applicants must be willing to learn Japanese, and Japanese language proficiency certificates only qualify as optional supporting documents.
application_method: Confirm with the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your own country whether the Research Student type and the field you wish to apply for are open this year.
Sit the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations for research students (Japanese and English).

Complete the MEXT application forms: Application Form, Configuration Preference for University of Placement, Field of Specialization and Research Plan, Certificate of Health, and the University Acceptance Consent format.
Submit all required documents and attend the interview conducted by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country.
The embassy/consulate screens applicants and forwards its recommendations to MEXT.
MEXT makes the scholarship offer and the receiving graduate school is identified for placement.
Receive round-trip airfare funded by MEXT and begin study in Japan.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are recruited and initially screened by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country, which sits its own qualifying examinations (Japanese and English for research students), conducts the interview and collects all required documents; MEXT then selects the scholarship students and allocates them to host graduate schools, subject to the host university's acceptance.

scholarships.best_fit: Applicants who already hold (or are close to) a bachelor's degree and can enter a Japanese graduate school's master's or doctoral programme, who are under 35, who sit the embassy/consulate's Japanese and English examinations, and whose country runs the Research Student track.
scholarships.notes: No published deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction terms were readable on the official pages read. MEXT publishes rules on extending the scholarship period (applications for extension from newly admitted students in April 2026 and from early-completers are handled by notice), rules on combining the scholarship with other awards, and rules on part-time work by scholarship students, but these notices are in Japanese and were not readable in the English sources used for this record. Application is free of charge.

scholarships.title: Young Leaders' Program (YLP) - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship, GRIPS School of Government and School of Local Governance
scholarships.name: Young Leaders' Program (YLP) - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship, GRIPS School of Government and School of Local Governance

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-year Master of Public Policy at GRIPS in Tokyo taught entirely in English, running October enrolment to September graduation, and every admitted YLP student receives the MEXT scholarship - you are not competing against a separate funding pool or mixing scholarship types. The money is set by the Japanese government rather than negotiated per applicant: JPY 242,000 a month (FY 2026 figure), waivered application, admission and tuition fees, economy-class round-trip airfare and required field trip costs, plus Tokyo International Exchange Center housing. The catch is not academic merit but the route: there is no direct GRIPS application, so your real deadline is whatever your own ministry or embassy sets, and GRIPS only publishes 'Varies' with the Japanese Embassy as contact. Your genuine out-of-pocket exposure is Tokyo living costs beyond the stipend, visa and medical costs, and moving-in expenses; if you cannot secure a full year's release from your post, this is not the right programme.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Serving civil servants from one of the 29 School of Government or 20 School of Local Governance countries who already have three to five years of public-administration work and can secure a nomination from the authority GRIPS lists for their country.
application_readiness_checklist: Find your country on GRIPS's List of Recommending Authorities and check both the School of Government and School of Local Governance columns - the two schools are sometimes nominated by different bodies, and a country on one list may be absent from the other.

Request the application form from your Japanese embassy or recommending authority rather than from GRIPS; the brochure states applicants obtain the form there, and GRIPS publishes no YLP application pack of its own.
Secure the recommending authority's own recommendation letter as a separate step, because it is a distinct document from your two work/university letters of recommendation.

Book TOEFL iBT (aim for 79+) or IELTS Academic 6.0 early enough that the official report arrives inside the July-October window GRIPS publishes; this is a published eligibility threshold, not a preference.
Order certified English-language transcripts, degree certificates and a certificate of health now, since the whole file goes in hard copy and medical appointments are slow to schedule.

Confirm with your HR or personnel directorate that your organisation will release you for a full year away and will re-employ you afterwards - GRIPS expects graduates to return to their former governmental organisations.
Verify you have not applied to any other GRIPS programme (including MEP) in the same academic year, which would void the application.
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to GRIPS: GRIPS explicitly lists YLP under applications that 'should be made through the sponsoring organization', and only accepts the nominating body's submission as an application.
Applying to more than one GRIPS programme in one academic year - the FAQ rules this out in any circumstances, including external applications such as YLP and MEP.
Missing the three-year full-time public-administration experience requirement, or being 40 or over as of 1 October 2027.
Submitting a recycled file: GRIPS states no supporting document submitted in a previous year can be reused for a later application.
Being unable to travel to Japan by the last date of the period GRIPS specifies, which the brochure names as a ground of ineligibility.

Serving military status - active military members or civilians employed by the military at any point in the scholarship period are ineligible, as are applicants already enrolled or planning to enrol at a Japanese university under Student status.
Assuming the YLP brochure is optional: it is the only published source of the eligibility thresholds, the English score and the document list.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Covered: monthly stipend of JPY 242,000, application/admission fees and tuition, economy-class round-trip airfare and required field trip costs; housing is offered at the MEXT-built Tokyo International Exchange Center residence halls run by JASSO. Still on you: Tokyo living costs above the stipend, visa application and residence-card costs, the medical examination, and initial relocation, moving-in and furnishing costs. For scale, GRIPS's self-financed charges are 30,000 yen application, 282,000 yen admission and 642,960 yen yearly tuition, so the waiver is a large share of the award's value. Accommodation is offered rather than free, and family rooms cost more than singles.
document_audit: Three separate letters are involved: the recommending authority's recommendation letter plus two letters from an immediate superior at work or your supervising professor - applicants routinely supply only two and then cannot complete the file.
'Official evidence of English ability' means the official score document, not a printout of a self-service online result; request the score report from ETS or IELTS directly.
Official transcripts of academic record and graduation/degree certificates are required, so local-language documents need certified English translations - build this in before the window opens.
The file goes in hard copy, so courier time to the recommending authority counts against the deadline; there is no online submission portal for YLP.
A certificate of health is on the mandatory list and visa processing depends on it, so book the medical examination before the window opens rather than after nomination.
Essays are required but no length, prompt or template is published, and GRIPS publishes no YLP-specific form - ask the recommending authority what it expects rather than guessing.
alerts: GRIPS publishes no YLP deadline at all: its 2027-2028 deadline table lists YLP with 'Japanese Embassy' as contact organization and 'Varies' as the deadline, so do not diarise the November 20, 2026 / November 27, 2026 dates shown elsewhere on that page - those are for MEXT University Recommendation and other GRIPS-administered programmes.
The JPY 242,000 stipend is the FY 2026 figure and GRIPS notes the amount is subject to change, so treat it as indicative for the 2027 intake.
You must keep your status as a public administrator or government official: losing it before completion makes you ineligible, which constrains any career move during the year.
Grantees who are absent from the university for long periods stop receiving the scholarship, so plan the year as continuous residence in Tokyo.
The School of Government and School of Local Governance have different country lists and, in many countries, different recommending authorities - confirm both before choosing which to apply for.
GRIPS also admits Japanese students to YLP through a separate Japanese-language route, so the international quota is not the entire cohort.
Country eligibility is explicitly 'subject to change without notice'-style wording; check the current GRIPS chart rather than relying on the brochure's older list.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Request the form from your Japanese embassy or recommending authority, build the hard-copy file including the authority's own recommendation letter, and submit to that authority by its deadline - GRIPS treats that submission as your application to GRIPS, then runs admission screening and passes successful candidates into the MEXT/YLP scholarship route.

scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all application procedures for Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan, and candidates should ask their own embassy/consulate. GRIPS publishes the application window as a historical reference only: application acceptance period (last year's result) July to October, with results announced the following April.
scholarships.description: The Young Leaders Program (YLP) at GRIPS is a special one-year master's degree program in Public Policy, taught entirely in English, for exceptionally promising young government officials. It was introduced by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology in 2001 to foster future national leaders in designated countries, build comprehensive human networks among the leaders of nations, establish friendly relationships among the countries involved, and improve the quality of policymaking in the participating countries. It is fully supported, including full scholarships for all students, by the Japanese government.
scholarships.duration: Within 1 year and 6 months including Japanese language education (MEXT table); GRIPS states a 1-year programme, October enrolment to September graduation
scholarships.application_period: GRIPS publishes that for the cycle it runs, application acceptance runs July to October (last year's result), enrolment is in October and graduation the following September, with results announced the following April. GRIPS has published the YLP Brochure for 2027-2028. The nominating authority in the applicant's own country sets the operative date; no central deadline exists.

Study in Japan: 'Young Leaders Program (YLP) students' - Embassy recommendation: No; University recommendation: No. Recommendations come from official overseas recommending organizations (footnote 2).

GRIPS target group: 'This program is open to exceptionally promising young government officials with considerable working experiences in the area of public administration. In principle, a minimum of three years working experience in the field in the applicant's home country is a prerequisite for admission to the program.'

GRIPS: 'Students will be admitted on the basis of an appraisal of their potential to become future leaders at home, to play important roles in their countries' development, and to maintain the lasting friendship and trust of Japan and other countries around the world.'

MEXT's published table shows no preliminary training block for YLP and a one-year duration including Japanese language education. No deferral, renewal or clinical-restriction term is published on the pages read, so those fields are null.

scholarships.title: GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) Program - Undergraduate Degree Programs
scholarships.name: GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) Program - Undergraduate Degree Programs

applicant_utility.summary: GKS Undergraduate is a two-route Korean government scholarship: the Embassy Track applies through the Korean embassy in your country during September, while the University Track (UIC and Associate Degree) is a direct application to a designated GKS university in a September-November window, and both feed into NIIED selection with results in December. Every awardee does a compulsory one-year Korean language course before the degree starts. NIIED publishes no monetary value for the monthly allowance on this page, so the actual stipend figure only becomes available in the annual GKS announcement guidelines, and the department-level detail lives in the downloadable University Information File rather than the overview page.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent high-school graduates under 25 who are non-Korean citizens (both parents included) with an 80%-or-top-20% academic record and who want a government-funded degree in Korea including a language year.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm that you and both of your parents hold non-Korean citizenship before anything else
Check you will still be under 25 in the intake year and gather transcripts showing 80% or higher, top-20% class rank, or the equivalent CGPA

Decide your track early: Embassy Track (online through Study in Korea) or University Track (direct to a listed GKS university), including at least one Type B university for Embassy General and Overseas Korean applicants
Download the University Information File from the GKS announcement for department-level detail before choosing your universities
Plan for a compulsory one-year Korean language training programme before your degree begins
common_rejection_risks: Applying only to Type A universities when the Embassy Track rules require at least one Type B choice
Missing a University Track window that is set by each university individually, not by a single NIIED deadline
Falling below the published academic-performance threshold (80% cumulative, top 20% of class, or required CGPA)
Assuming the online Study in Korea application also covers the University Track, when that route is a direct application to the university
document_audit: The page publishes no document checklist; the required document set appears only in the annual GKS announcement guidelines and the University Information File, so do not rely on last year's list
Embassy Track applicants apply online through Study in Korea and must follow the announcement's document rules exactly
alerts: By mid-October the Embassy Track submission month (September) has passed for this cycle; the University Track September-November window is the live one

The undergraduate quota is fixed at 286 places (156 Embassy Track: General 88, Overseas Koreans 7, R-GKS 61; 130 University Track: UIC 100, Associate Degree 30), so adding more universities does not create more places
Final results come from NIIED in December, so keep any parallel university admissions compatible with that timeline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Embassy Track: submit online on studyinkorea.go.kr in September, then embassy screening, NIIED review and the university decision; University Track: apply directly to the GKS university during September-November, then university screening and NIIED review, with NIIED announcing final results in December.

scholarships.deadline: 30 September 2026, 18:00 KST (Embassy Track online application)
scholarships.description: The Korean government-invited scholarship degree programme that funds a year of Korean language training followed by an associate degree (2-3 years) or bachelor's degree (4-6 years) at a designated GKS university in Korea. The published benefits list is airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances. Selection runs through two routes: an Embassy Track that applies through the Korean embassy/consulate, and a University Track in which the student applies directly to a GKS-designated university (UIC specialisation and Associate Degree).
scholarships.duration: Korean language training (1 year) + associate degree programs (2-3 years), bachelor's degree programs (4-6 years)
scholarships.application_period: Embassy Track: applications accepted in September. University Track: applications accepted September to November. On 2026-10-01 the University Track falls inside the published September-November window; the Embassy Track submission month published is September.
scholarships.official_source: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Ministry of Education, Republic of Korea
eligibility: Nationality: Applicants and both of their parents must hold non-Korean citizenship
Age: Applicants must be under 25 years of age as of the applicable year
Education: Associate Degree Program - High school graduate or expected to graduate; Bachelor's Degree Program - High school or associate degree graduate or expected to graduate

Academic Performance: Applicants must meet the academic performance requirements, such as a cumulative score of 80% or higher, ranking within the top 20% of their class, or meeting the required CGPA threshold
Embassy Track General and Overseas Korean applicants may apply to up to three universities, including at least one Type B university
Embassy Track R-GKS applicants may apply to up to two Type B universities
The UIC Program under University Track provides customized curriculum and field experience through industry-university cooperation focused on the fields of natural science and engineering
Specialization (UIC) is available only for associate and bachelor's degree programs

scholarships.selection_notes: Two-stage selection. Embassy Track: the applicant's embassy/consulate screens and selects first, then NIIED, then the university. University Track: the university screens and selects first, then NIIED. Final results are announced by NIIED in December. Selection quota for the undergraduate programme is 286 places in total: Embassy Track 156 (General 88, Overseas Koreans 7, R-GKS 61) and University Track 130 (UIC 100, Associate Degree 30).

application_readiness_checklist: Check the single hardest gate first: take the SAT (minimum 1100 points, equivalent to percentile 63) or the SCIO Mathematics and General Academic Prerequisites tests (minimum average percentile 63). The test result is the only selection criterion
Sit the SAT within the accepted window - between 1 January 2021 and the application submission deadline - or obtain an official SCIO-issued certificate; there is no alternative to these two tests
Verify you have never had permanent residence in Slovakia since 1 January 2021 and sign the solemn declaration
Verify you never studied at a secondary school in Slovakia, and that you have never studied at a Slovak HEI if you are applying at Bachelor's level
Pick a selected public or state HEI offering a programme on the SK RIS 3 2021+ list - a private university such as UMB is not eligible for this scheme
Apply to that HEI for admission; you only need to have applied, not been admitted, when you submit the scholarship application

Prepare your documents: notarised copy of your passport or ID, the hand-signed Solemn Declaration of Permanent Residence, the SAT/SCIO certificate, the CV on the provided template in English, the Motivation Letter on the provided template in English, and the guardian consent if you are under 18
Submit electronically on the scholarship website only - e-mail applications are explicitly refused
Be ready to enrol officially in autumn of the scholarship year, because evaluation happens after enrolment
Keep every original document: originals must be handed to the HEI after award
important_advice_for_students: If your record is tied to Applied Informatics at FPV UMB, note that this scheme does not fund private institutions; UMB is outside its eligibility
Do not assume your tuition is free: the waiver exists only under legislation and only "exclusively on HEIs decision"
Do not rely on the tuition waiver or on any living-cost figure when budgeting; the only published payment is EUR 500 per month for ten months

Do not rely on the CV or motivation letter to win the award - the test score is "the only criterion for the selection of successful applicants", though both documents are described as essential for evaluation
Because evaluation happens after enrolment, make sure you actually start the programme; not starting means no award
Watch out for the page's stale sections: the site simultaneously shows an extended deadline notice and says registration is not yet open. Rely on the site's top banner and announcements
Do not plan to switch institution or to switch to part-time study - either ends the entitlement
common_rejection_risks: SAT below 1100 points or SCIO average percentile below 63, which means "will not be considered"
Trying to substitute another standardised test, which is expressly disallowed
Permanent residence in Slovakia at any time since 1 January 2021
Prior study at a Slovak secondary school, or at a Slovak HEI for Bachelor's applicants
Applying to a private HEI rather than a selected public or state HEI
Choosing a study programme not on the SK RIS 3 2021+ selected list
A study programme not taught full-time and in person
Applying by e-mail rather than through the website
Missing the SAT/SCIO certificate upload, or uploading it after the deadline
Unsigned solemn declarations
Failing to enrol officially in autumn of the scholarship year, because evaluation occurs after enrolment
Changing HEI, or switching from full-time to part-time, after award
Providing false or altered documents, which triggers withdrawal and repayment
estimated_uncovered_costs: Most living costs - EUR 500 per month is the only published payment and no living-cost calculation is published
Tuition fees unless the chosen public HEI grants a discretionary waiver
Visa and travel costs; the site publishes no travel subsidy
Any cost above the public health insurance the Act provides for qualifying non-residents
Deposit or ancillary fees charged by the HEI
document_audit: Certified copy of a valid passport or ID; citizenship must be evidenced by a notarised copy. EU, EEA and Swiss applicants may use a national ID card
Hand-signed Solemn Declaration of Permanent Residence, using the template downloadable during the application process

SAT certificate with a minimum of 1100 points, or SCIO certificate with an average percentile of 63 - essential and non-substitutable
Acceptance Letter from the HEI, if available
Structured CV in English on the provided template - marked an essential document for evaluation
Motivation Letter in English on the provided template, explaining the motivation for studying in Slovakia and demonstrating talent characteristics - also marked essential

Format rules: electronic submission only via the website; notarised copy for citizenship proof; all declarations hand-signed; SAT only from tests taken 1 January 2021 to the submission deadline; SCIO certificate must be issued by SCIO; original documents required from successful holders at the HEI
No published file size limit or accepted file type; verify in the upload control

alerts.message: Take the SAT or SCIO test. The test result is the only selection criterion, and the minimum threshold is SAT 1100 or SCIO average percentile 63.
Only selected public or state HEIs on the SK RIS 3 2021+ programme list are eligible - private institutions such as UMB are not.

scholarships.description: This scheme gives partial financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who have been formally invited to present a paper at an international conference abroad. Assistance covers air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance for the stay, and registration fee up to US$200. Regular faculty receive up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit, while SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability, and postgraduate/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection may be considered for the full cost of the visit.

eligibility: Faculties with regular service in public funded Universities/Deemed-to-be-Universities/Colleges, Institutes of National Importance as defined by MoE / UGC, and ICSSR Research Institutes/Recognized Institutes having a PhD degree are eligible to apply.
Post-Graduate (Regular)/PhD/PDF scholars in Social Science disciplines who are in the advanced stage of their studies/research are eligible to apply.

Independent scholars having served as Civil servants, officers from Defence services, and other professionals with a social science perspective having not less than 20 years of regular service and demonstrable research experience through publications of books/research papers/reports/policy documents, etc. may also apply.

benefits: Preference is given to younger scholars, scholars attending a conference or seminar for the first time, and scholars from remote and backward areas.

Invitations from global subject associations, reputed international organisations, universities or institutions are given preference, and due consideration is given to the peer review process used by the conference organisers.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a reimbursement-style research travel grant rather than a scholarship: ICSSR pays the actual cost of one research visit of up to two weeks abroad - economy airfare, visa, insurance, local transport and daily maintenance - at Government of India notification rates, and publishes no fixed amount, so the sanction sanction is what sets the payable value. Applications roll in year-round through app.icssr.org, but approval needs an Expert Committee and then Research Committee/Council sign-off, so a realistic applicant starts several months before the intended travel dates. The decisive part of the file is documentary proof that the data simply does not exist in India and exists, with access permission, abroad.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Indian faculty with a PhD and Indian Ph.D/PDF scholars in social sciences whose approved or planned research genuinely requires a short overseas fieldwork or archive consultation trip.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the two archive letters early: one from an Indian library/archive stating the desired data is not available there, and one from the foreign institution confirming availability plus permission to access - these are mandatory screens, not optional extras.
Attach a finalized schedule of the primary/secondary data to be collected with confirmed appointments with the faculty or experts you intend to meet.
Write an explicit academic justification for travelling in person, especially if any of the primary sources could be reached online - the guidelines specifically call this out.
Keep the itinerary within two weeks; a longer proposed visit falls outside the scheme.
Prepare the application and later the reports in English or Hindi only.

Register on app.icssr.org, submit online, then dispatch the hard copy with all enclosures to the In-charge, IC Division, ICSSR, Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, New Delhi 110067 - use a trackable courier, since ICSSR disclaims responsibility for postal delay or loss.
common_rejection_risks: Missing or informal archive correspondence - without the Indian non-availability letter and the foreign availability/permission letter the application will not be considered at all.
No convincing academic justification for a physical visit when the primary data is available online.
Incomplete applications, or institutional applications not duly forwarded by the institution (independent scholars are the only ones exempt from the forwarding rule).
Proposing fieldwork longer than two weeks, or work that was never part of the approved fellowship or project.
Reapplying too soon - a second application is considered only after a gap of three years, and the award can be availed only twice in a lifetime.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the prescribed Government norms: extra days beyond the two-week cap, anything above economy class, personal incidentals, and any expense without a valid receipt; unspent balance must be refunded to ICSSR.
document_audit: Economy air tickets must be booked only through the three authorized travel agents - M/s Ashoka Travels and Tours (ATT), M/s Balmer Lawrie & Company Ltd (BLCL) or IRCTC - tickets bought elsewhere risk non-reimbursement.
Keep the original boarding pass, the immigration-stamped passport pages and the foreign-currency purchase bill; settlement is documentary, so a missing paper means an unpaid cost.
If airfare comes from any other source, only 75% of the maintenance grant is advanced and the remaining 25% is released only after a satisfactory Statement of Expenditure.
For students, the post-visit report must be duly forwarded by the Supervisor and a copy of the collected data must accompany it.
The claim pack needs an attendance certificate plus copies of the air ticket and visa alongside the expenditure statement.
alerts: No published figure: ICSSR funds actual expenditure within Government notification norms, so you cannot budget a fixed stipend in advance - the sanction order determines what is payable.
Applications that were not approved will not be reconsidered, and the Council reserves the right to reject any application without assigning any reason.
Preference is given to applicants having proficiency in the native language of the country of visit.
ICSSR may ask for copies of the tickets booked and visa obtained before departure as a monitoring step - do not travel first and inform later.
Any monograph or book brought out from the material collected under the scheme must acknowledge ICSSR funding, with a copy sent to ICSSR.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online at app.icssr.org at any point in the year, post the hard copy with enclosures to the IC Division in New Delhi, then wait for Secretariat scrutiny, Expert Committee shortlisting and Research Committee/Council sanction; the maintenance grant is released before departure and the balance is settled as reimbursement after the visit on the statement of expenditure.

scholarships.name: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students

applicant_utility.summary: This is a work-based assistantship rather than a cash award: the University of Sharjah funds eligible master's students who commit 20 hours per week to Research or Teaching Assistant duties and give up any outside employment. No stipend amount, tuition waiver, or expense coverage is published anywhere on the official pages, so treat the financial value as unknown until the department confirms it in writing. Apply through the regular master's admission route inside the 5 October to 12 November 2026 window and check your programme against the exclusion list before building any plans around the award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-CGPA master's applicants (3.60/4.00 if non-national, 3.20/4.00 if Emirati) who want to study at Sharjah, can give 20 hours a week to university work, and have no outside job.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target programme is not on the published exclusion list (all five Master of Dental Surgery programs, MSc Leadership in Health Professions Education, Master of Leadership in Higher Education, Executive MBA, PharmD) - and note MSc Molecular Medicine and Translational Research is RA-only, not TA.
Verify your bachelor's CGPA clears the higher bar for your nationality track: 3.60/4.00 for non-nationals, 3.20/4.00 for UAE nationals.
Book TOEFL iBT (79), IELTS Academic (6.0), or PTE Academic early - Home Edition and online home-based tests are rejected, and results are only valid for two years.
Line up certified coloured copies of your bachelor's degree and transcript, plus two recommendation letters from professors who taught or supervised you.
Budget the AED 500 non-refundable application fee and, if admitted, the AED 10,000 seat reservation (AED 5,000 lost if you withdraw or do not enrol).
If your degree is from outside the UAE, start the MoHESR equivalency process before you apply, since it is required documentation.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme on the exclusion list, or assuming TA is available in Molecular Medicine and Translational Research when only RA is.
CGPA below the nationality-specific scholarship threshold even though general master's admission only needs 3.00/4.00.
Submitting a Home Edition TOEFL/IELTS or a test older than two years, which the University states it will not accept.
Missing the 12 November 2026 application window - the University publishes no separate RA/TA application round.
Being currently employed elsewhere: holders may not work outside the University, and an employer letter is required if you are employed at application time.
Assuming the scholarship is guaranteed on meeting minimums - the department awards it only where it has academic/research need and budget.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The official pages attach no payment to the scholarship, so applicants should expect to fund the AED 500 application fee, the AED 10,000 seat reservation, tuition, and living costs themselves. The University's published fee structure for master's students admitted from 2022/2023 lists fees per credit hour (AED 3,200 for most master's programmes, AED 4,200 for the MBA and Executive MBA-related business programmes, AED 3,500 for Biomedical Engineering) plus programme-specific annual fees such as AED 68,250 for the PharmD. Housing, meals, insurance and travel are not addressed by the scholarship at all, and remediation classes are explicitly not covered.
document_audit: Certificates and transcripts must be certified copies and colour copies are requested on the Graduate admissions page - plain black-and-white scans are a routine rejection reason.
Recommendation letters must come from professors who taught or supervised you at bachelor's level, not employers or referees from later roles.
An Emirates ID and/or Family Book copy is requested; non-Emirati applicants typically hold a residence visa instead, and the document list explicitly allows Family Book or Residence Visa.

Employed applicants must attach a letter from their employer confirming current employment - this clashes with the 'no outside work' rule only after award, so read it as a disclosure requirement, not a bar.
Kuwaiti applicants need a Kuwait Embassy Cultural Office approval letter, and male Emirati applicants aged 18-30 need the National and Reserve Service No Objection Certificate.
alerts: The two official pages disagree on timing: the Master's Degree page sets 5 October - 12 November 2026, while the Graduate admissions page shows an extended deadline of 1 July 2026 for selected graduate programs. Verify the current MASTER's intake deadline with the admissions office before relying on either date.
The scholarship is awarded by the concerned academic department based on its own needs and available positions - numbers are limited and not published, so a strong CGPA does not secure it.
The award locks you into university-only employment for the whole period; turning down or leaving outside work is a real career cost.
Remedial or prerequisite courses (up to 24 credit hours for applicants from a different field) are not covered by the scholarship.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account on the University of Sharjah Online Admission Portal, complete the master's application, upload documents and pay the AED 500 fee within the published window, then wait for the admission decision (the University states an email on admission status within 7 working days) - RA/TA nomination and any benefit terms then come from the concerned department.

scholarships.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan that offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate study at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. AfDB states it covers tuition for the 24-month study programme, a monthly living stipend, air travel between the scholar's home country and the host university at the start and end of the scholarship period, and health insurance usually obtained through the university, plus an additional six months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation. It is not complete funding in AfDB's own terms: the Bank publishes an explicit exclusion list covering visa application costs, family members, extra-curricular courses, additional travel during the study programme, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers. AfDB publishes no stipend figure and no central call date, so the amount and the closing date must both be confirmed with the chosen partner university and the JADS Secretariat.
scholarships.duration: Two-year scholarship; "the scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less"
scholarships.application_period: Annual partner-university admissions cycle. AfDB states there is no separate application to the Bank and no central JADS window.

scholarships.selection_notes: All eligible applications are comparatively evaluated by the Program Implementation Unit hired by the African Development Bank, and the final selection is approved by the JADS Secretariat. Evaluation focuses on educational and professional excellence, commitment to home country development priorities, the quality of the statement of purpose, financial status and geographic diversity of awardees. The Bank's management decision and approval of the finalist also takes into consideration geographical diversity, gender balance, equity and inclusiveness (unusual circumstances or hardships when assessing employment experience), financial needs (applicants are financially constrained), and special consideration for applicants with special needs.

scholarships.best_fit: Citizens of an African Development Bank regional member country who are 35 or younger and in good health, hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering or a related field with an excellent academic record, and have at least one year of paid employment in their home country or another African country obtained within the past three years of completing that degree. Applicants must already be able to apply to an approved master's course at a JADS partner university, must not be enrolled in another graduate degree programme, and cannot be AfDB Group staff or a close relative of AfDB Group staff.
scholarships.notes: There is no separate application to the African Development Bank - "Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program", and a university admission offer alone is not a scholarship award. The scholarship "may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support/fellowship you might have"; finalists and awardees must inform the JADS Secretariat of other funding, and "The JADS stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if during the scholarship period the program has evidence of additional sources of support." Deferral and renewal are not addressed on the AfDB pages. Scholars "are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development, using the newly acquired knowledge and skills." No clinical or field-of-practice restriction is published, but the approved master's courses are limited to energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering and related areas. "The scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less."

Selection rewards a concrete, multi-year record in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance or security, a stated interest in building U.S. partnerships, and a credible plan to keep contributing from Sub-Saharan Africa; a university degree is not required. Draft the four essays and the 200-word track-fit essay offline in English first, then paste them into the system; save often in case of connectivity drops.
Read the 2027 Application Instructions PDF end to end before writing, especially the institute track descriptions, so your track ranking and track-fit essay are coherent.
Pre-select resume facts to fit the section's entry caps, and check your passport expiry now - finalists need validity through at least 28 February 2028 (31 March 2028 for the PDE).
Use a permanent personal email address (not a work account you may lose) and add an alternate email in the application.
Decide before submitting whether you want the Professional Development Experience: interest must be indicated in this application and cannot be added later.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the hard 16:00 GMT cut-off on 13 October 2026 - the deadline is published in GMT and no extension mechanism exists.
Plagiarism, including borrowed phrasing from sample applications, other applicants, or alumni essays; originality is checked and copied content disqualifies.
Undisclosed AI assistance in essay drafting, when the Technology Use Disclosure is a required application section.
Age 36 or older by 13 October 2026 (or under 21): age is fixed at the deadline and the official FAQs state no exceptions will be made.

Technical-eligibility failures that never reach reviewers: U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, residence outside an eligible country, prior Fellowship participation, or an immediate family member employed by the U.S. Government.
Plans to live, work, or study outside Sub-Saharan Africa in early 2027, which breaks the residency requirement for 1 February 2027.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Salary or self-employment income for the six-week (roughly ten-week for PDE Fellows) absence, personal purchases, and support for your home organization are explicitly not funded; you should also budget for a passport, travel to any embassy interview, and incidental personal spending beyond the provided housing and meals.
document_audit: Enter your name, date of birth, and biological sex exactly as printed on your passport or government ID; mismatches create verification problems at the interview stage.
A passport is not needed to apply, but start any renewal now if yours expires before 28 February 2028 (31 March 2028 if you may pursue the PDE).
Log in after submitting and use the 'Generate PDF' function to keep a personal copy, since no edits or additions are possible after you submit.
Keep the resume entries within the system's caps (five positions, five institutions, five trainings, five community roles, ten awards, eight languages, ten software skills) to avoid rework.
Ensure the email address you register with is one you will still control in mid-2027, since all Fellowship correspondence flows through it.
alerts: The 2027 cycle closes at 16:00 GMT on Tuesday, 13 October 2026 - three days after this record was verified - so treat the deadline as immediate.
Submitted applications are final and only one application per applicant is allowed; duplicate submissions may disqualify you.
Dependents, including spouses and children, cannot accompany Fellows to the United States, so arrange caregiving and work cover before applying.

Selected finalists must attend mandatory pre-departure orientation and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa, and must depart for the United States from their country of residence in an eligible African country.
