scholarships.description: The Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders is the exchange component of the U.S. Government's Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI), a program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government and administered by IREX. It brings up to 550 accomplished young African leaders to the United States for a comprehensive executive-style program: a six-week institute at a U.S. college or university combining academic coursework, professional site visits, structured networking, community service, and cultural activities in one of three tracks (Business and Trade, Emerging Technologies, or Governance and Security), plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience for up to 50 Fellows and ongoing alumni opportunities.

scholarships.selection_notes: "The Fellowship selection process is a merit-based open competition." After the deadline, all eligible applications are reviewed and scored against the published criteria: proficiency speaking, reading and writing in English; a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security; a demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals; a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents; the ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others; strong social and communication skills; and demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments. Applicants who do not meet the technical eligibility requirements "will not be forwarded to the selection committee." Semi-finalists are then interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country between October 2026 and January 2027. Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa. The U.S. Department of State and IREX "reserve the right to verify all information included in the application", requiring documentation of age, citizenship and residency at the interview stage; any discrepancy or false information means "the application will be immediately declared invalid and the applicant ineligible." PDE applicants are assessed separately on the ability to work professionally in a U.S. organization, articulation of clear and specific learning goals, flexibility, alignment between professional background, institute track and potential U.S. organizations, interest in sustaining engagement with U.S. professionals, and strong English proficiency.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (U.S. Department of State educational and cultural exchange programme, administered by IREX)
scholarships.best_fit: Citizens and permanent residents of any of the 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries, aged 25 to 35 on the application deadline of 13 October 2026 (exceptional applicants aged 21-24 may be considered), proficient in reading, writing and speaking English, with a proven record of accomplishment in business and trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security, and with a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants must not be U.S. citizens or permanent residents, must be eligible for a U.S. J-1 visa, must not be U.S. Government employees or their immediate family, and must not be alumni or prior participants of the Fellowship.
scholarships.notes: This is a non-degree exchange programme, so no tuition is charged or funded and no degree is awarded. It is not deferrable, not renewable, and a Fellow cannot re-apply: the technical eligibility rules exclude "alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship". The programme requires a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa, and applicants must be residents of an eligible country as of February 1, 2027 and at the start of the Fellowship in June 2027. "Fellows are not allowed to have dependents, including spouses and children, accompany them during the Fellowship." There is no clinical or field-of-practice restriction. Selected Fellows must complete a detailed Medical History Form and, if applicable, an Accommodations Form, and the programme "strongly encourages all eligible applicants to apply regardless of your medical history or accommodations you may require." Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions receive reasonable accommodations and support at no cost. Fellows must attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities, and housing may be shared: "Every effort will be made to provide single-occupancy housing; however, Fellows may share a double-occupancy bedroom with another Fellow of the same sex and a bathroom with one or more Fellows of the same sex." The U.S. Department of State and IREX reserve the right to alter or suspend Fellowship activities at any time, and selection of finalists may be reviewed case by case for nationals of countries subject to a U.S. entry or visa suspension.

scholarships.description: DAFI is UNHCR's dedicated tertiary scholarship programme for refugees and returnees, founded in 1992 and funded principally by the Government of Germany. The published scholarship package covers a range of costs including tuition and study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, and depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner may also cover academic preparatory, language and ICT courses as well as psychosocial support. It funds ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent programmes and ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary and TVET programmes of two years or more, and it explicitly does not cover master's studies. Applications are made through the DAFI Programme Management Platform, which was live and accepting registrations and submissions on 2026-10-01.
scholarships.duration: Duration follows the degree programme enrolled in: ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent, or ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary / TVET of two years or more
scholarships.application_period: Country-specific. The 2026/2027 cycle ran on country-published windows in July-August 2026 (Rwanda 15 July-7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 7 July-21 August 2026; Slovakia 1 July-31 August 2026). New country calls for the next cycle are announced on the relevant UNHCR country help page and applications are submitted through the DAFI Programme Management Platform.

It also states that only qualified candidates duly registered with UNHCR are invited to interviews, that names of shortlisted candidates are posted at the respective offices, and that academic documents are verified with the relevant authorities (the last two statements are published in the Windle International Kenya DAFI scholarship instructions, not on the UNHCR Rwanda call). scholarships.notes: The scholarship does not cover master's degree programmes (published: 'DAFI does NOT cover Masters studies.' / 'Please note that the scholarship does not cover master's degree programs.'). Awards are not deferrable, renewable or multi-year by default: funding follows admission to an ISCED 5 or ISCED 6 programme in the cycle applied for. No return-home obligation is published, and because studies take place in the country of asylum or home country no relocation is required. No clinical or field-of-study restriction is published beyond the general rule that the programme targets undergraduate and short-cycle tertiary/TVET study. The 2024 cycle was the first since 2020 with a decrease in the number of scholars supported, reflecting reduced global funding. As this is a multi-country programme with no published global deadline, the applicable deadline is the one published by the applicant's own UNHCR country operation; the published 2026/2027 country windows had all closed by 31 August 2026 at the time of verification, and the platform itself remained live and accepting registrations on 2026-10-01.

scholarships.description: The Staff Exchanges action of the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions "funds short-term international and inter-sectoral exchanges of staff members involved in research and innovation activities of participating organisations", with the aim of developing "sustainable collaborative projects between different organisations from the academic and non-academic sectors (in particular SMEs), based in Europe and beyond." Exchanged staff benefit from new knowledge, skills and career development perspectives while participating organisations increase their research and innovation capacities. Grants are awarded to international consortia, not to individuals: a consortium "needs to include at least three organisations in three different countries, two of which need to be located in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country", must include both academic and non-academic sectors, and "participation of organisations from non-associated third countries is strongly encouraged". Projects can last up to four years and fund secondments of one month to one year. Seconded staff receive "a top-up allowance (for travel, accommodation, subsistence costs), which is on top of the salary paid by their organisation", plus a special needs allowance where applicable, alongside funding for research, training and networking activities and for management and indirect costs. The current call is closed; the 2027 call opens on 15 December 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: The Ernst Mach Grant worldwide buys you a research stay of one to nine months at any Austrian university, without needing to enrol there, and it is explicitly aimed at people who finished or pursued their studies outside Austria. The OeAD has not published the monthly rate for this grant on its own pages, so do not budget against a figure you have not confirmed. The hard gate is the written confirmation of supervision from an Austrian university lecturer, using the mandatory OeAD template, before you can even open a strong application.

The published grant benefit is a supplementary monthly grant of EUR 1,300, together with assistance in arranging accommodation and health insurance, but scholarship holders pay the costs of accommodation and insurance themselves and must show own funds. Tuition fees at Austrian public universities and universities of applied sciences do not have to be paid by grant holders, and may be waived upon request to the rectorate, but this does not apply to private universities and private colleges. Holders from listed non-European developing countries also receive a travel costs subsidy of up to EUR 1,200 upon submission of original travel invoices.

scholarships.selection_notes: The selection follows a multistage process: 1. Examination of the formal requirements; 2. Examination of the application's general plausibility; 3. Assessment and evaluation of the application by experts; 4. Final decision by the BMFWF. Incomplete applications and applications not complying with the application criteria will not be accepted for the further selection process. All formally valid applications are then evaluated by experts from the respective field and the selection committee awards the best applicants. The selection is competitive, i.e. there is no legal claim to a grant even if all application requirements are fulfilled; the number of grants awarded during one call depends on the quota and/or the available budget.

The earliest possible start is September 2027 (the Austrian academic year 2027/28). Stay dates must consist of full months only, starting on the first of a month and ending on the last; short-term grants of 1 month should be consumed in February or September. Applicants must have interrupted any stay in Austria for at least six months before taking up the grant. Gainful employment is not allowed, with a marginal employment exemption of EUR 551.10 per month in 2026. A final report is obligatory at the end of the stay. The grant contract (Letter of Award and Letter of Acceptance) defines start and end date, grant amount, payment modalities, compulsory attendance at the guest institution, performance report and final report, data protection and repayment obligations. The grant cannot be used to enrol in a Master or PhD programme in Austria. Without written proof of accommodation in Austria, a residence permit is not granted. Applicants from non-EU/EEA countries planning a stay of more than 6 months whose accommodation costs exceed EUR 386.43/month may need to prove additional funds to the Austrian residence authority.

scholarships.name: Programa Portugal-Berkeley (Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley)

applicant_utility.summary: This call does not pay you a scholarship: it buys the UC Berkeley side of the stay - CPS pays the Visiting Student Researcher service, visa-processing and Institute of European Studies fees - while you personally finance travel, accommodation and health insurance for up to six months. The decisive work happens before you apply, because a UC Berkeley professor must agree in writing to supervise you and arrival cannot happen until at least six months after selection, so sequence the stay around your doctoral timeline. If you already hold an FCT doctoral fellowship, the complementary supports (maintenance abroad, travel and installation allowances) exist but must be requested separately in myFCT. With only about 8 slots per calendar year, rolling quarterly windows and an early close once the quota fills, treating this as a last-minute December option is the main way to lose it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral candidates enrolled at a Portuguese institution who can secure a UC Berkeley supervisor quickly and can self-fund a Bay Area stay for up to six months.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the UC Berkeley faculty member's agreement to supervise the stay before anything else - use the model letter published on the call page
Obtain UC Berkeley's proof of acceptance in English; it is a required attachment, so start the CPS/VSR request process early
Draft the motivation letter with a concrete planned arrival date that respects the six-month post-selection rule and ties the stay to your doctoral work plan's scientific ambition
Cut the CV to two pages in English and request proof of current doctoral enrolment from your institution
If you hold an FCT PhD fellowship, file the complementary-support request in myFCT as a separate step - selection alone does not trigger it
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a confirmed Berkeley supervisor or without the English-language proof of UC Berkeley acceptance - the dossier is incomplete
A motivation letter that reads as a generic mobility wish-list; criterion C (30%) rewards a direct link to your doctoral work plan and career impact
A work plan that is ambitious but not feasible - criterion B explicitly weighs feasibility, not just innovation
Thin track record against criterion A (40%), which counts publications, conferences, prizes and project participation
Withdrawing after selection because the real cost of roughly six months in the Bay Area was never budgeted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel, accommodation in the Berkeley area and US health insurance are explicitly the selected candidate's own cost, and the call provides no monthly stipend; existing FCT doctoral fellowship holders can offset this via the complementary supports claimed in myFCT (maintenance abroad, single travel allowance, single installation allowance).
document_audit: The proof of UC Berkeley acceptance must be in English - a Portuguese-language confirmation does not satisfy the rule
The CV is hard-capped at two pages, in English, so leave no room for annexes
The motivation letter must state a planned arrival date consistent with the six-month post-selection waiting rule
Proof of doctoral enrolment must evidence current enrolment at a Portuguese higher education institution
Everything travels with the single electronic form submission - there is no separate document portal, so assemble the package before opening the form
alerts: The call can close before 30 December 2027 once the annual quota of up to 8 Visiting Student Researchers is filled
Arrival at UC Berkeley cannot occur earlier than six months after selection - do not promise a supervisor or supervisor a start date inside that window
Assessment runs in quarterly windows by submission date, so a submission sent just after a window close can wait months for a verdict
No IELTS/TOEFL threshold is published, but the CV, motivation letter and acceptance proof must all be in English - get them drafted and checked well before the window you are targeting
Complementary FCT supports for existing doctoral fellows are requested separately through myFCT and are not automatic with selection
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One-shot submission of the electronic form with the four English attachments; the academic committee appointed by FCT and FLAD scores the application in the next quarterly window and issues a positive or negative opinion.

scholarships.description: The Programa Portugal-Berkeley is an FCT call, run with FLAD and UC Berkeley, that supports doctoral students to spend a research stay as Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley for up to six months. FCT launches the call to promote the internationalisation of Portuguese science and to foster research exchange between Portuguese universities and UC Berkeley in areas of mutual scientific interest. The selected candidate's home institution (CPS) is responsible for the administrative procedures to acquire the Visiting Student Researcher status and pays the University Services Fee, the DS-2019 visa processing fee and the Institute of European Studies administrative fees at UC Berkeley. The selected candidate must arrange and financially cover their own travel, accommodation and health insurance, and the call publishes no direct stipend or award figure.

scholarships.selection_notes: Assessment is carried out by an academic committee appointed by FCT and FLAD. Criterion A: candidate's curriculum, considering academic grades, track record and scientific achievements including peer-reviewed publications, scholarships, prizes, conferences and project participation (40%). Criterion B: scientific quality, innovative character of the work plan and feasibility of the research activities to be developed (30%). Criterion C: motivation letter explaining the relevance of the stay and the work to be developed for the scientific ambition of the doctoral work plan, and the expected impact of the stay on the candidate's career (30%). Selection is based on the analysis of these criteria, producing a positive or negative opinion, with final classification CF = 0.4 A + 0.3 B + 0.3 C.

scholarships.funding_period: per project, up to 18 months of project development

applicant_utility.summary: RESTART is not a scholarship and pays no stipend: it is a project grant of up to EUR 50,000 for up to 18 months, awarded to your host R&D unit rather than to you personally, so budget for salaries and consumables inside the proposal instead of expecting a monthly payment. You must clear three cumulative tests - a doctorate, integrated doctoral membership of an FCT-funded R&D unit or a State laboratory contract, and a qualifying parental leave of at least 120 days (72 if shared) taken between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 - and you need your host institution's written commitment before you can submit anything. scholarships.funding_period: one-off grant; follow-on stages up to £8k/£12k/£18k

applicant_utility.summary: Rufford money buys fieldwork, not a degree: it pays for conservation work on the ground in roughly 150 developing and emerging countries, with caps rising from £7,000 to £18,000 as you progress through four stages. Because funds are paid to an NGO or university rather than to you, the most common blocker is having no organisation ready to accept and manage the grant before you apply. The programme never closes, so your real enemies are the 12-month reapply lockout after a rejection and the 12-week reference deadline - if all three references have not arrived by then, the application is rejected and you wait a year to try again.
applicant_utility.best_fit: MSc/PhD conservationists (or within 3 years of graduating) in an eligible country who need their first £7,000 of field budget for threatened species or habitat work.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a named organisation (NGO or university) that agrees to receive and manage the grant before you open the form - money is never paid to personal accounts, and an overhead request above 10% forces you to find another organisation.

Line up three referees with the exact required mix: one from a well-established institution (major conservation NGO, university or government body), one based in your project country, one from outside it; if you are an MSc/PhD student one must be your supervisor, and no two referees from the same institution.
Brief referees so they can write independently - references go straight to Rufford and are confidential; drafting or ghost-writing your own reference gets the application rejected.
Draft answers offline from the published form-questions document and respect the strict word limits, because anything over the limit cannot be pasted into the online form.

Build the budget from fieldwork items only - subsistence, local travel and accommodation, field assistants such as drivers/porters/guides - and leave out tuition, your salary, publication charges and international flights.
Confirm before investing effort that your project country is on the eligible list and any target species is not globally Least Concern on the IUCN Red List.
common_rejection_risks: Missing references: the application is not processed without three, and if they have not all arrived 12 weeks after submission it is rejected and you cannot reapply for at least 12 months.
Applying for a project that has already started - Rufford will not fund work already begun, and review can take up to 4 months.
No organisation in place to receive and manage the funds, or a host organisation charging more than a 10% management fee.
A target species listed as globally Least Concern on the IUCN Red List, or a project located in an ineligible (advanced-economy or currently sanctioned) country.
Framing the work as pure research with no obvious conservation benefit, or including conferences, participation expeditions or publishing costs.
Assuming a submitted application can be edited - it is final once submitted, and unsubmitted applications are deleted after 3 months.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and academic fees (explicitly not funded), your own salary (salaries generally not funded), publication charges, international travel to the project country, and any organisational overhead above 10%; at the Booster and Completion stages you must also raise matching co-funding from other donors yourself.
document_audit: The three references are confidential documents sent by referees directly to Rufford - you may only give background project information, never text for a referee to sign.

Referee composition must include an established institution, someone in your project country and someone outside it; MSc/PhD applicants must include their supervisor and cannot use two referees from the same institution.
Co-funding evidence is required whenever Rufford is not the sole funder, and at Completion Grant stage the Foundation expects matching funds from other sources.
The final evaluation report must use the Foundation's template; without it you cannot apply for further funding.
The application form imposes strict word limits and cannot be edited after final submission, so prepare offline using the published Word question list.
alerts: There is no deadline, but only one application is allowed in any 12 months - a rejection locks you out for 12 months, and being funded locks you out for at least 12 months before the next stage.
Applications reaching external review can take up to 4 months to decide, so do not begin the project or commit dates before a decision arrives.
Chase your three referees immediately after submitting: the 12-week reference rule rejects the whole application if they lag.
Keep gaps between Rufford applications under 5 years; longer gaps count against follow-up applications.

Money is paid only to an organisation (NGO or university), never to you personally, and that organisation may be based outside your project country but must have any permissions needed to receive foreign funds.
Any material change to project design or budget after the award must be agreed with the Foundation first, or the full grant may have to be returned.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account at apply.ruffordsmallgrants.org, submit the finalised English form online (no edits afterwards), then track progress while three referee-submitted references arrive - office screening can reject within days, and external-reviewed applications get a decision within 4 months.

scholarships.deadline: There are no deadlines - applications can be submitted at any time of year. You can only make one funding application in any 12-month period; if an application is rejected you must wait 12 months before you can reapply; if you are funded you cannot apply for further support for at least 12 months.
scholarships.description: The Rufford Small Grants Programme funds fieldwork costs for small-scale, pilot nature conservation projects run by early-career conservationists in developing and emerging economy countries. Funding is staged across four levels - 1st Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 8,000, Booster Grant up to GBP 12,000 and Completion Grant up to GBP 18,000 - and the Foundation aims to provide between 50% and 100% of project costs, requiring evidence of co-funding where it is not the only funder. Only fieldwork costs are considered, and award holders must provide project updates and a final report that are posted on their Rufford webpage. There are no deadlines, so the programme was open on the verification date.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a salaried 12-month executive placement, not a scholarship: three African nationals with a master's degree and at least seven years' experience are placed in the AfDB, ECA or ITC offices with a $100,000 stipend and mentorship from the head of the institution. Because you apply through the host's own system, the host you choose effectively determines your closing date and extra rules, so open all three host pages before drafting anything. Treat the age limit strictly: 40, or 45 for women with children, at the start of the fellowship.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a US$5,000 one-off business grant, not a scholarship - no tuition, living costs or travel are paid, so you need your own funds to keep the business and yourself running between the 1 January application opening and the 22 March participation confirmation. The portal is only open for two months a year and applications cannot be edited once submitted, so the exact-match of your name, your business age under five years and your ID document all have to be settled before you click submit. Eligibility is decided automatically and immediately after submission by a minimum score in the online business assessment test, which is why treating that test as the real gate matters more than polishing the pitch.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Africans aged 18 and above living in Africa, with a business idea or a business under five years old, who have never received funding from any TEF programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you have never benefited from any TEF programme and have not applied in this same annual application window - either is an automatic disqualifier.
Check your business is no older than five years at the time of application; registration date, not launch date, is what counts.
Obtain a government-issued ID showing both date of birth and a clear photo - student IDs are explicitly rejected and void the application.
Reconcile the exact name and personal details on your TEFConnect profile with the ID character for character before submitting.
If the business is already operational, get the Business Registration Certificate in the business name and tax registration also in the business name.
Prepare a Jpeg/png headshot under 1mb and use a phone number you control that is reachable on WhatsApp.
common_rejection_risks: Falling below the minimum score in the business assessment test, which is the first and largest filter and is applied automatically right after submission.
Any mismatch between the TEFConnect profile and the government-issued ID, which the Foundation says makes the application null and void.
Documents found inauthentic, containing discrepancies, or matching the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries - immediate disqualification.
Duplicate applications using two email addresses, or submitting two business ideas, or applying to more than one TEF programme.
Failing the LSEG World-Check global compliance screening or the physical verification exercise that follows shortlisting.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the US$5,000. You fund your own living costs through the entire cycle, plus business and tax registration, opening the business bank account, producing the 2-3 minute pitch video, and any travel to an onboarding session or a physical verification visit.
document_audit: Tax registration must be in the business name, not the founder's personal name - this is a distinct requirement from the business registration certificate.
The bank reference letter must capture your name, the business name and the business bank details; a plain account statement does not satisfy it.
The accepted ID set is National Driver's Licence, International Passport, or Permanent Voter's Card - and the PVC option applies to Nigerian participants only.
A Partner Consent form is required only if you are a co-owner, and a medical report from a reputable hospital only if you live with a disability.
Uploaded files must be Jpeg/png and no more than 1mb, so scan or compress identity documents before the window opens.
alerts: The portal is closed from 2 March until the following 1 January - there is no rolling intake, so a missed window costs a full year.
Seed capital arrives only after training, mentorship and an independent investment-readiness review, so the money is not paid at the point of selection on 22 March.
The application is free; the Foundation states that anyone asking for money in exchange for application support is running a scam and should be reported to whistleblower@tonyelumelufoundation.org.
Seed capital payment requires a business bank account and signing the seed capital undertaking before funds are processed.
If you are found ineligible you are encouraged to reapply the following year, but participants disqualified from a previous programme may not reapply to any TEF programme.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit free online on TEFConnect during the January window, receive an immediate on-screen and email eligibility verdict, then pass due diligence and World-Check screening, await the 22 March shortlist decision, complete onboarding, training, mentorship and the investment-readiness submission, and receive the US$5,000 once the Audit and Finance team endorses your documents.

Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. scholarships.selection_notes: Independent third-party experts review eligible applications. A minimum score in the business assessment test is required or the applicant is notified as ineligible and encouraged to reapply the following year. Eligible applicants undergo LSEG World-Check global compliance screening and a physical verification exercise by authorised enumerators, which may be in person or virtual. Shortlisting is evaluated on business feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability, and leadership and entrepreneurial skills. In the investment readiness phase an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video and ranks participants for investment readiness. Shortlisted participants are notified of participation on the 22nd of March each year.

scholarships.notes: The seed capital is non-refundable and is not a scholarship: it does not pay tuition or living costs, and applicants must fund their own living expenses throughout the cycle. The portal is only open for two months a year, 1 January to midnight 1 March; there is no rolling intake, so missing the window means waiting a full year. You cannot have previously benefited from any TEF programme, and you cannot reapply within the same application window of the same year, which the Foundation states explicitly. Programme participants whose documents are found inauthentic, contain discrepancies, or match the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries are immediately disqualified. Seed capital payment requires signing the seed capital undertaking and is processed into the business account you provide.

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
scholarships.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

applicant_utility.summary: There is no single application to this scholarship: you must shortlist an affiliated partner institution and apply through its own admissions process, on its deadline, with its document list. The Foundation publishes no fixed award amount because support is defined institution by institution, but it confirms that tuition fees, accommodation, books and other scholastic materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development and, if necessary, a return air ticket home are covered. Selection rests on academic excellence, leadership, financial need and a credible plan to give back to society, and admission to a partner does not by itself guarantee the scholarship. PhD and doctoral candidates are not currently eligible, so this route fits secondary, undergraduate and master's applicants.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Service-oriented young people from underrepresented backgrounds - especially young women, persons with disabilities, and forcibly displaced young people - who can win a place through an affiliated partner at secondary, undergraduate or master's level.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist two or three affiliated partners whose eligible majors, location and admission route genuinely fit you, starting only from the Foundation's Where To Apply listings.
Open each partner's own admissions page and record its exact deadline, required documents and application fee before drafting anything.
Build evidence for the published selection pillars - academic excellence, leadership, financial need and giving back to society - into your essays and references, not just your grades.

If your target partner is in North America, budget and book TOEFL/SAT months ahead; the Foundation notes these costs are a barrier for many applicants and points to Education USA as a possible source of test-cost support.
Do not let an admission application fee stop you where it is genuinely unaffordable - the Foundation states the fee is reimbursed if the candidate is selected.
common_rejection_risks: Sending an application to the Foundation itself - there is no central portal, and packages are not considered through the Foundation.
Assuming admission equals funding: gaining admission to a partner institution does not guarantee selection, which the Foundation calls highly competitive.
Tracking the Foundation's news page instead of the partner's own admissions calendar and missing the partner's deadline.
A grade-only application that does not evidence leadership, community contribution and financial need, which partners explicitly assess.
Submitting without the TOEFL and/or SAT scores a North American partner requires for international candidates.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Admission application fees (reimbursed only if you are selected) and TOEFL/SAT test costs where a partner requires them; the Foundation publishes no coverage for visas, initial travel to the partner institution or day-to-day personal expenses.
document_audit: Every partner defines its own document list, so transcript formats, reference letters and essay requirements differ from institution to institution - never reuse one partner's package unchanged for another.
TOEFL/SAT scores must be booked early where a North American partner requires them for international candidates; late scores arrive after the decision.
Keep proof of payment for any admission application fee, since reimbursement depends on being selected.

Applicants without conventional academic records, including displaced applicants, should contact their chosen partner directly and early - the Foundation states exceptions cannot be made outside the partner-led process.
alerts: The Foundation warns of Facebook posts and groups advertising recruitment for this programme and requesting an application fee; it states these groups are not associated with it, that it never solicits funding or requests payments from individuals, and asks that suspected fraud be reported to local law enforcement and to ethics@mastercardfdn.org.
There is no central deadline and no central status tracker - application status questions must go to the partner institution directly.
PhD/doctoral candidates are not currently eligible, and the Foundation does not sponsor or financially support candidates who are not awarded a scholarship through the programme.
The Foundation is not accepting unsolicited partnership proposals, so new partners are announced only through its own news channels.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Choose an affiliated partner, follow its published admissions process and deadline, submit the full partner application package including any fee, then wait for the partner's decision - the partner, not the Foundation, selects scholars.

scholarships.deadline: Each partner in the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program sets their own deadline. Please check the Program website of the partner institution(s) of your choice for the specific deadline.
scholarships.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a global initiative designed to develop the next generation of transformative leaders by enabling highly talented, service-oriented young people to pursue higher education and cultivate their leadership potential. The Foundation describes it as the largest scholarship initiative of its kind in Africa, focused on enabling talented and diverse young people, particularly young women, to lead, pursue their aspirations and enrich their communities. It provides financial, social and academic support delivered through a pan-African and global network of partner universities and NGOs.

scholarships.application_period: No central application window. The programme is published as active and ongoing from August 2012, and applications are accepted on each partner institution's own admissions schedule.

scholarships.title: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement
scholarships.name: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement
scholarships.degree: Not a degree programme (open to Indian bachelor's-degree holders and early to mid-career professionals)
scholarships.degree_levels: Not a degree programme (open to Indian bachelor's-degree holders and early to mid-career professionals)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a two-year personal stipend for self-directed social-impact work in India, not a study award, so there are no tuition fees to offset and none are covered. The only published financial support is a monthly stipend of INR 25,000-45,000 set by the X/Y/Z category of the area where you live and work, so project costs, travel, equipment, insurance and any living costs above the stipend must come from your own pocket. Applications for the 2027 cohort close on 15 November 2026 (11:59pm IST) and your mentor and referee must upload their letters by the same date, so line both up weeks in advance. Shortlisting is announced by late February 2027 with an online interview within a fortnight, final fellows by late March 2027, and work begins on 1 May 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Indian citizens living in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, holding a bachelor's degree from a recognised Indian institution (or three-plus years of relevant work experience), who want two years of mentored, self-directed work in fields such as cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, public health, ecological or community-rights work.
application_readiness_checklist: Download the Foundation's statement of purpose and work plan template (linked on the fellowship page) early and draft both to under 1,000 words, with a realistic two-year timeline and clear expected outcomes in the work plan.

Secure a mentor who will endorse your work plan, agree to supervise you for the fellowship, review quarterly and annual progress reports, and meet the Foundation periodically - and request their letter well before the deadline.

Line up a separate referee who has supervised your work for at least six months (an academic referee is acceptable for fresh graduates) and confirm neither the mentor nor referee is a current Inlaks Fellow or otherwise supported by Inlaks.
Enter both the mentor's and referee's email addresses in the Online Application System early so the upload links go out, and confirm both letters are in before 15 November 2026, 11:59pm IST.

Check your project against the stated forms (action-oriented research, cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, ecological efforts, community rights, public health, archiving, dying arts/culture/language) and confirm it is individual learning rather than organisational work with no art-installation or photo-book component.
Type your date of birth exactly as it appears on the proof of age and citizenship you upload.
common_rejection_risks: A project framed as organisational or institutional work rather than individual learning, which the Foundation explicitly excludes.
An art-installation, photo-book or similar art-practice project, which is not eligible for this fellowship (apply for the Inlaks Fine Arts Award instead).
Being enrolled in academic studies or a PhD during the fellowship period.
Naming the same person as both mentor and referee, or naming a current Inlaks Fellow / someone currently supported by Inlaks in either role.
A mentor or referee letter that misses the 15 November 2026 deadline because the applicant waited to trigger the upload links.
A vague 'Topic of your project' entry, or a work plan without a credible two-year timeline and stated expected outcomes.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the monthly stipend (INR 25,000-45,000 depending on the X/Y/Z area category), applicants must self-fund project costs, travel, equipment, health insurance and any living costs above the stipend; the published pages list no other coverage.
document_audit: The statement of purpose and work plan must use the Foundation's own template (download link on the fellowship page) and be uploaded as a PDF only.
Both documents are capped at 1,000 words each; the work plan needs a title, description, expected outcomes and a detailed two-year timeline.

The mentor letter must contain specific statements: endorsement of your work plan, agreement to supervise, willingness to review quarterly and annual progress reports, and willingness to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation.
The referee letter must state the capacity in which they engaged with you; both letters are uploaded by the mentor and referee themselves through emailed links, not by you.
Your date of birth must be typed exactly as on the proof of age and citizenship you upload.
alerts: The 15 November 2026, 11:59pm IST deadline applies to the mentor and referee letters too - send the upload requests as soon as you submit, ideally days before the deadline.
The Foundation states it will be unable to respond to individual queries regarding the status of your application.
Your stipend tier depends on the X/Y/Z category of the area where you live and work (per the linked government HRA classification), and the final amount is at the Foundation's discretion.
The fellowship carries a six-month probation period plus quarterly and annual reviews, and requires attendance at three Foundation-hosted workshops.

2027 cohort timeline: shortlisted candidates announced by the last week of February 2027, final interview within a fortnight, final fellows announced by the last week of March 2027, and fellows expected to begin work from 1 May 2027.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Online Application System form on Submittable via 'Apply Now', trigger the mentor and referee upload links by entering their email addresses, wait for both letters to land before the deadline, then await desk-review and, if shortlisted, an online interview with the selection committee.

scholarships.description: The Fellowship gives young people the opportunity to build a diverse worldview and establish long-lasting connections to issues of public importance, encouraging them to challenge the status quo while building the confidence and security to explore alternatives and make independent choices about their lives. It gives graduates and early to mid-career professionals the chance to learn from a mentor of their choice and contribute to social change through self-directed work in India.
scholarships.duration: Two years, with a six-month probation period and quarterly and annual review of the Fellow's work
scholarships.application_period: Applications open for the 2027 cohort (opening date not published on the page); closing 15 November 2026, 11:59pm IST. Shortlisted candidates announced by the last week of February 2027, final interview within a fortnight, final fellows announced by the last week of March, fellows expected to begin work from 1 May 2027

The applicant must be a graduate (hold a Bachelor's degree) from a recognised institute/university in India.
In the absence of a Bachelor's degree, they must carry at least three years of relevant work experience.
Those enrolled in academic studies/PhD for the duration of the fellowship are NOT eligible to apply.
Applicants proposing to work on art installations, photo books etc. are not eligible to apply for this fellowship.

scholarships.name: RISE Germany - Research Internships in Science and Engineering

applicant_utility.summary: This is an internship stipend, not a degree scholarship: 992 euros a month plus health, accident and liability insurance, an international travel subsidy and a 160-euro travel stipend for the July meeting in Heidelberg, with no tuition involved. The award is a matching system rather than an exam - providers rank applicants in January and DAAD alternates between student GPA and project demand, so a tailored motivation letter for each project and an early referee upload matter more than applying to the maximum number of offers. You must still hold undergraduate status when the internship runs, so anyone graduating before summer 2027 is excluded and belongs in RISE Professional instead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Second- or third-year undergraduates in biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, earth sciences or engineering at North American, British or Irish universities who want a funded summer research internship in Germany.
application_readiness_checklist: Register for a DAAD ID early and browse offers across several fields rather than only your exact major
Write a separate motivation letter for each project, explaining how your experience prepared you for that specific position
Produce a one-page list of courses you will have completed by the internship start date
Request a transcript and a certificate of enrollment showing your expected graduation date
Ask a PhD-holding academic referee early and send them the generated upload link (deadline 15 December 2026)
Open a European (IBAN) bank account soon after arriving in Germany so stipend and travel payments can be made
common_rejection_risks: Graduating before the internship, which breaks the undergraduate status that German work-permit rules require
An incomplete application - if everything is not online by 30 November 2026, the application cannot be considered
A reference letter from a company, or from a referee without a PhD, which is not accepted
Applying to both RISE Germany and RISE Professional in the same year, which is not allowed
Restricting the project search to one field and missing relevant interdisciplinary offers
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing and daily living costs beyond the 992 euro monthly stipend; hosts assist with finding housing but DAAD publishes no housing grant, and Canadians receive their 7,000 CAD directly from Mitacs rather than DAAD.
document_audit: The transcript may be a digital version with university name, logo, student name and print date, or a copy of a certified hard copy - an 'issued to student' stamp is acceptable

The certificate of enrollment must show the university stamp, an authorized signature and the expected graduation date, because the German Federal Employment Agency needs proof of continuing student status
The reference letter must be on university letterhead, signed, and uploaded online by the referee through your generated link
alerts: The application closes 30 November 2026 at 11:59 pm CET but references run to 15 December - do not apply late and assume your referee still has time
Virtual internships exist but carry different scholarship rates, so check the project description
Stays are capped at a minimum of ten weeks and a maximum of 90 days, starting between 15 May and 15 July 2027
DAAD provides no individual feedback on unsuccessful applications, by email or phone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply entirely online in the RISE Germany internship database by 30 November 2026; your referee uploads the letter via your generated link by 15 December; providers rank candidates in January and DAAD announces positions around February/March 2027.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a monthly living stipend, not a tuition award: budget for the roughly 992 Euro per month to replace income while health insurance is handled for you. The binding constraint for most applicants is German at B2 or better plus documented socio-political engagement, not grades alone. Apply as early as possible in the degree stage window - a Master's applicant starting in the winter semester must be in by 30 November 2026 - because the whole process, from form to committee decision, runs three to seven months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International students already enrolled at a German university with strong German, above-average grades and a record of voluntary or political engagement.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are inside the degree-stage window: Master's applicants at the very start of the programme, Bachelor's applicants after semester one and no later than three semesters before the standard study period ends
Assemble first graded transcripts before anything else - without them the application cannot be considered
Document engagement concretely (organisation, role, hours, dates), including any volunteering from your home country if you only recently arrived
Line up two university teachers willing to write references, and give them the FES reference guidance early
Write the motivation letter in German and tie it explicitly to social-democratic values
Diarise travel-cost reimbursement forms for the selection interviews and keep all tickets
common_rejection_risks: Applying before first graded performance records exist, which is an automatic formal barrier for Bachelor's applicants
Treating the German requirement as optional because the degree programme is in English - FES states sufficient German must be proven regardless
Leaving socio-political engagement vague or undocumented, which undercuts the ideelle side of the assessment
Submitting part-time, dual, short (under three semester) or second-degree programmes, which FES explicitly does not fund
Lateness in the degree stage: past the window the application is not considered even with strong grades
Letting references arrive late - FES will not chase them and late documents cannot be considered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester contributions and any tuition charged by your university, rent above what the 992 Euro monthly stipend covers, and living costs for family members beyond the 255 Euro child supplement.
document_audit: Transcripts, matriculation certificate and certificates need to be at hand in the second stage only - the online form comes first and a rejection can arrive before you prepare them
References must come from university teachers; for school-leaver programmes from teachers, so check which category your programme falls into
The CV must explicitly cover socio-political engagement, not just academic history
If you are invited to interviews, travel costs are reimbursable only on the official FES form
alerts: The German programme page and the English summary page publish different family-allowance figures (255 vs 276 Euro) - verify with the FES contact staff before budgeting
Master's summer-semester applicants face a 31 May cut-off, much earlier than most students expect
A 403-style rejection at the online-form stage costs you the whole window, because degree-stage timing cannot be repeated
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online form first, then an e-mail request for documents and references, then two interviews, then a committee decision communicated by e-mail.

scholarships.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung's basic funding programme for international students supports Bachelor's, Master's, Diplom and Staatsexamen degree programmes at German public or state-recognised universities. The published financial support is 992 Euro, with health insurance costs covered and an additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children. The scholarship does not have to be repaid and is awarded independently of need.
scholarships.application_period: Rolling within the published degree-stage windows; for Master's programmes starting in the winter semester, applications are due by 30 November.
eligibility: You are a foreign national
You are already studying at a German public or state-recognised university or university of applied sciences
You have very good German language skills
You have above-average grades in your studies
You are socially and politically engaged
You identify with the values of Social Democracy
The programme covers Bachelor's, Master's and Diplom degree programmes as well as programmes leading to the Staatsexamen

scholarships.title: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
scholarships.name: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)

applicant_utility.summary: Do not send anything to the DAAD - the application goes straight to the postgraduate course you choose, by that course's own deadline, and the DAAD will not forward materials sent to it. You may apply for up to three listed courses, but you must send one identical motivation letter to each, explaining why you chose those specific courses and that priority order. Shortlisted candidates are contacted by the DAAD to upload into the DAAD portal, and shortlisting normally involves a telephone interview with university staff that you personally have to attend. Since funding depends on the BMZ budget provision, treat the award as conditional until the DAAD confirms it in writing.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from a DAAD-listed developing or newly industrialised country who hold a relevant four-year bachelor's degree with top-third results, two or more years of development-related work experience after that degree, and a degree no older than six years.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the current EPOS list of courses for intake 2027/2028 and open each course's own website for its deadline, procedure and any extra documents it requires.
Assemble the employer recommendation letter early: official letterhead, signature and stamp, current date, unsealed - a stale or sealed letter is a classic miss.
Obtain certified translations of degrees and transcripts where they are not in German or English, and add an explanation of your grading system if the transcript lacks one.
Book IELTS or TOEFL well ahead (institutional TOEFL is not accepted); for German-taught courses, hold a B1 certificate at application and plan DSH 2/TestDaF 4 before the course starts.
Keep PDF copies of every submitted document, because you must upload them to the DAAD portal if the course suggests you for a scholarship.
If you are applying from the People's Republic of China, request the APS certificate in parallel with your application pack.
common_rejection_risks: Motivation letter that does not explain the specific courses chosen and the priority order - the application cannot be considered, or an awarded scholarship may be withdrawn.
Applying to a course that is not on the current EPOS list; the scholarship is only granted for the entire duration of listed courses.
Degree completed more than six years ago, or residence in Germany longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
Incomplete applications or applications not submitted in English or German.
Waiting for the course deadline that has already passed - the official FAQ states a late application is not possible.
Switching the priority order between the different course applications.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Registration or enrolment fees at the university (the FAQ says these may still be payable); the rent subsidy and family allowance are additional benefits only under certain circumstances, and the travel allowance is not paid where travel is covered by the home country or another funding source.
document_audit: The employer letter must be of current date, on letterhead, signed, stamped and not sealed - old letters are routinely accepted by employers and rejected in practice.
CV must follow the europass template in reverse chronological order with no unexplained gaps.
Certified copies may or may not be required depending on the university - check each course's rules before sending.
The same signed checklist and DAAD application form are needed for each course you apply to, and the motivation letter must be identical across them.
alerts: Every course has its own deadline and the list only says 'see website of the course' - assume deadlines are earlier than the intake year suggests and check each course individually.
Funding is announced subject to BMZ budget provision, so a nomination is not a guarantee of payment.
The DAAD cannot give status information; only the course you applied to can update you, and most of the selection process is finished in March.
If you apply to several courses you must apply to each university directly - one application does not cover the others.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Send the complete pack directly to the course by its deadline; the course's selection committee screens and nominates; the DAAD contacts nominees to upload into the DAAD portal; the selection process is finalised and nominees are informed.

scholarships.deadline: Depending on chosen study programme; please check the DAAD list of application deadlines or the website of the chosen study programme. Applications are sent directly to the course, not to the DAAD.
scholarships.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
scholarships.duration: 12 to 42 months (dependent on study programme)
scholarships.application_period: Cycle-based: applicants apply directly to a listed EPOS postgraduate course for the published intake year (the current DAAD programme list is headed 'List of Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028'); the course's own committee then nominates candidates, who are invited to upload to the DAAD portal for the final selection.

application_method: Step 1: Send your complete application directly to the postgraduate course you have chosen.

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is by independent, voluntary selection committees. Candidates must fulfil the academic requirements and be expected to complete the study programme successfully (above-average first academic exam, top performance in the third, language skills), hold a relevant Bachelor degree, have at least two years' professional experience, and prove a development-related motivation. Special circumstances such as a disability may be taken into account.

scholarships.best_fit: Graduates from DAC-listed developing and newly industrialised countries who hold a Bachelor (normally a four-year course) with above-average results (upper third), have at least two years of professional experience after that degree, and can prove a development-related motivation tied to their work in a public authority or company.
scholarships.notes: The scholarship call is made subject to the provision of funds by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), so funding is not guaranteed by the DAAD itself. Applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded and will not be considered - the course must be applied to directly. Applicants resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline are excluded. Degrees should normally not be more than six years old. Some courses require additional documents. DAAD scholarships do not have to be paid back.

scholarships.title: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers
scholarships.name: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers

applicant_utility.summary: MOPGA 2027 pays EUR 2,500 a month for exactly 12 months plus a one-off EUR 500 settling-in allowance, but it is a living-costs-only award: no tuition, no flight, no research budget, and no renewal. The real bottleneck is not the application form but the host laboratory - the supervisor's support letter must be co-signed by the laboratory director, which typically takes weeks of negotiation, so start contacting labs now rather than in December. Applications run only through the Campus France SMApply portal (email submissions are rejected), can be written in English or French, and every project section is character-capped, so draft offline first. Check the hard eligibility gates before anything else: French nationals, anyone already living and working in France, and PhDs defended outside December 2021-December 2026 are excluded.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Researchers who defended a PhD between December 2021 and December 2026, hold a non-French nationality, are based outside France, and have already secured a willing French host laboratory on a climate or environment topic.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your PhD defence date falls between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive; if the diploma has not been issued, obtain an official certificate of defence or proof of thesis submission instead
Contact candidate laboratories early and secure both the supervisor's support letter and the laboratory director's co-signature or commitment letter - this is the longest-lead item
Draft the eight project sections offline and map each explicitly onto one of the five MOPGA research themes; respect the character caps (2,000 for most sections, 4,500 for methodology and timeline)
Trim the CV to 4 pages including the publication list and ask the supervisor for a 2-page CV
Line up 1-3 referees early and upload their letters plus the passport/ID copy before the deadline
Submit through SMApply before 15 December 2026 and keep the confirmation; email applications are not considered
common_rejection_risks: Applying while resident and professionally active in France, or holding French nationality - both are absolute exclusions
Host-laboratory letter missing the laboratory director's co-signature or separate commitment letter
A One Health-themed project framed purely as medicine or human health without a genuine animal-health or ecosystem dimension
PhD defended outside the December 2021-December 2026 window without the maternity-leave extension documented in the application file
Already holding another French government fellowship or a French employment contract, which is incompatible with MOPGA
Submitting by email or after the 15 December 2026 deadline
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel to France (explicitly not covered, though the host laboratory may help), visa and residence-permit costs, housing deposit and setup, and any laboratory or research costs, since host laboratories receive no funding under the programme.

The supervisor's letter is incomplete without the laboratory director's co-signature or accompanying commitment letter
Page limits are published: CV 4 pages max., supervisor CV 2 pages max. - over-length files signal non-compliance
Recommendation letters are capped at 3: choose referees who can speak to the project, not just to coursework
Applications must be in English or French; anything else needs translation before upload
alerts: The eligibility window closes with a defence in December 2026: a later defence makes you ineligible for this cycle regardless of the rest of the file
Results only arrive May-June 2027 and the stay starts between September and December 2027 - plan your funding and employment for the long gap after the deadline
The maternity-leave extension (18 months per child, or the actual duration of leave) must be documented inside the application file, not claimed afterwards
Incompatibility rule: you cannot hold a French employment contract or any other individual French government funding during the fellowship
The fellowship is not renewable, so treat the 12 months as a single, fully-planned project rather than a start that can be extended
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One-shot online submission on the Campus France SMApply portal: complete the form, upload all documents and the project description in the window between 15 September and 15 December 2026; there is no separate institutional nomination step.

scholarships.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.

scholarships.application_period: Applications open 15 September 2026 and close 15 December 2026. Results are notified May-June 2027, and successful applicants arrive in France between September and December 2027.

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection takes place in two stages: scientific experts appointed by the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space in the relevant fields assess the applications received, then a scientific committee makes the final selection. Innovative approaches involving advanced technologies within the eligible research areas are given particular consideration during the selection process.
scholarships.program_type: Government research fellowship
scholarships.best_fit: Researchers who defended a PhD between December 2021 and December 2026, hold a nationality other than French, are not resident and professionally active in France, and have already lined up a French host laboratory willing to sign a research stay agreement.
scholarships.notes: The fellowship is not renewable and lasts exactly 12 months. International travel costs to France are not covered by the programme; the host laboratory may be able to help but is not funded to do so. The award cannot be combined with a French employment contract (research contract or postdoctoral contract) or any other individual funding from a French government entity. A PhD defended after December 2026 is not eligible. If the doctoral degree certificate has not yet been issued, an official certificate confirming the defence, proof of thesis submission, or another official institutional document is accepted. For researchers who obtained their PhD more than five years ago, the eligibility window may be extended by 18 months per child, or by the actual duration of maternity leave, on submission of supporting documents noted in the application file. Only projects with a genuine integrated 'One Health' approach qualify under the human, animal and environmental health theme; projects focused solely on medicine or human health are not eligible.

scholarships.name: AAPG - Appel à projets générique 2027 (ANR Generic Call for Proposals 2027)

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a job, not a scholarship: Inria hires you as a fixed-term doctoral employee on a gross EUR 2,300 a month for three years from 1 December 2026, with 7 weeks of leave plus RTT days, subsidised meals and partial transport reimbursement. The research topic is already set - 3D change detection and large-scale spatio-temporal analysis of LidarHD and satellite surface-model data for the JUNN Digital Twin - so the application is about proving you can execute it, not pitching an idea of your own. Everything runs through the Inria portal, and the deadline of 30 November 2026 is barely seven weeks away. The structural risk to weigh before applying is the restricted-zone (ZRR) warning: even after selection, an unfavourable Ministerial decision would cancel the appointment.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's-level graduates in 3D geometry, computer vision or machine learning who code in C/C++ and Python and want a salaried three-year PhD inside a French national research institute rather than a stipend-based university position.

Read the full TITANE topic description linked from the offer before writing anything, so your text addresses the two stated objectives

Email the PhD supervisor Florent Lafarge (TITANE) to introduce yourself, confirm fit and check the timeline before the portal close
Diarise 30 November 2026 as a hard deadline - the contract clock starts 1 December 2026, so there is no rolling window
common_rejection_risks: Thin evidence of C/C++ or Python ability: the posting names both languages explicitly and the field is specialised
Sending a CV by email or through another channel, which is not guaranteed to be processed at all
Applying with no exposure to 3D geometry or remote sensing when the reference list (planar primitives, point clouds, LOD trees, building datasets) is highly specific
ZRR clearance: an unfavourable Ministerial decision cancels the appointment even after a candidate is selected
Waiting until the deadline week - the posting gives no grace period and the start date is fixed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing in the Sophia Antipolis/Nice area, relocation and travel to France, visa-related costs, and anything beyond the published benefits package (subsidised meals, partial transport reimbursement, mutual insurance contribution).

Mirror the posting's keywords (geometry processing, 3D computer vision, machine learning, statistical analysis, urban reconstruction, planar shape detection) so screening sees the match at a glance
Expect the team's own subject PDF to be the benchmark for your motivation - make your profile map onto it explicitly

scholarships.name: Institut Pascal (IPa) Call for Proposals 2026

applicant_utility.summary: This is a call for programme organizers, not a personal scholarship: you assemble a scientific team, write a 5-page proposal plus the Annex 1 summary sheet, and Institut Pascal pays for your participants' accommodation, catering and up to EUR 4,000 of travel. Aim for a two-to-three week programme of 30-40 people, since the call explicitly favours groups under 30 or above 40 and requires a minimum 15 and maximum 60 participants. Send a draft to institut-pascal@universite-paris-saclay.fr before 28 October 2026 if you want board feedback that materially improves your odds before the 20 November 2026 deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and senior researchers who can convene an international community in a Paris-Saclay field and need a venue plus a modest travel budget rather than a salary.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your local organizing committee includes at least one Paris-Saclay scientist before you write anything
Fix your dates inside 2028 or 2029 and check they do not clash with major conferences in your field
Draft the week-by-week schedule showing genuine brainstorming slots rather than a lecture series
List additional funding requested or obtained, because co-financing is not mandatory but scarce budgets reward it
Name two or three referees the Scientific Council can ask about your leadership of the topic
Prepare the Annex 1 summary sheet with participant-per-week and accommodation estimates that are internally consistent
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that reads like a conventional conference with back-to-back talks instead of small-group interaction time
A topic with weak or no overlap with what is actually researched at Paris-Saclay labs
An all-male organizing committee or speaker list, since gender balance is a named selection criterion
Ignoring the two-week minimum on-site expectation without flagging the exception and rationale in the proposal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond accommodation, catering and the travel cap: flights above EUR 4,000, co-funding for extra participants, personal per-diem and publication or dissemination costs.
document_audit: The proposal and the summary sheet must arrive as ONE PDF, so convert and merge before uploading rather than assuming separate uploads work
Page limit is strict: a 5-page maximum means references and figures compete with the actual programme design
If your discipline cannot keep participants on site for two weeks, you must say so in the proposal and explain why
alerts: The 28 October 2026 draft-review window closes roughly three weeks before the real deadline and is the cheapest way to improve your chances
This round funds programmes for 2028 and 2029, so do not budget a grant that has to run next semester
Individual students cannot apply to Institut Pascal: if you are looking for personal funding, look instead at the host programme's own schemes
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single online PDF submission, then a Scientific Council interview at the end of February / beginning of March 2027, after which the board and organizers implement the programme together.
