scholarships.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)
scholarships.name: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply directly: a full-time, KAKENHI-eligible host researcher in Japan must submit the application for you through their institution by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027 (FY2027 2nd recruitment; the 1st round closed 28 August 2026). The package is a JPY 362,000 monthly maintenance allowance for 12-24 months plus a round-trip air ticket, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance. Host institutions often set internal deadlines more than a month before the JSPS date, so contact your prospective host's research office no later than February 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers who earned their PhD on or after 2 April 2021 and can secure a willing Japanese host researcher with lab space before the institution's internal deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up a host researcher at a university or other KAKENHI-eligible institution early - JSPS does not match candidates with hosts
Confirm the host institution's internal deadline, which can be more than one month before 23 April 2027
Prepare Form 2 (CV, achievements, research plan, career plans) jointly with your host, in English or Japanese
Ask your doctoral supervisor - not your host researcher - for the one-page, signed letter of recommendation
Check your PhD date against the six-year window; if you took maternity or parental leave, consult JSPS through the host institution in advance because extra documents are required
Ensure your doctoral degree certificate can reach JSPS before the fellowship start date
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to JSPS instead of through a Japanese host institution - individual applications are not accepted
Missing the host institution's internal deadline while watching only the JSPS date
A recommendation letter written by the host researcher, longer than one page, or signed with a typed handwriting-style font
Duplicate applications submitted through both the open call and an overseas nominating authority
The doctoral degree certificate not arriving at JSPS before the fellowship start date, which cancels the fellowship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing deposits and furnishings, living costs beyond the JPY 362,000 monthly allowance, Japanese taxes and insurance contributions, and visa costs; airfare and the settling-in allowance are withheld if you already live in Japan.
document_audit: The recommendation letter must come from your doctoral supervisor or a similar person - not the host researcher - and must carry a real or self-signed electronic signature
Name spelling and details entered on the system are printed on the fellowship certificate, and JSPS will neither confirm nor correct them
Unsuccessful candidates are not notified directly; your host researcher must relay the result, though the approximate ranking (Non-selected A/B/C) is visible to host researchers on the system
alerts: If you have been living in Japan with a mailing address before the fellowship start date, the outbound airfare and the JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance are not paid
Fellows must reside in Japan continuously for the whole tenure; the period cannot be divided into multiple stays
The number of fellowships (about 120 per round) and the support amounts are subject to change for budgetary reasons
A selected person who cannot start within the arrival window (1 April - 30 September 2027 for the 1st round; 1 September - 30 November 2027 for the 2nd) loses the fellowship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Host researcher enters Form 1 and uploads your Form 2 and recommendation letter on the JSPS Electronic Application System; the institution head approves and the institution transmits the application to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the deadline.

A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.

Secihti adds its monthly support under the Secihti 2026 National Scholarship Scale plus ISSSTE medical service. scholarships.name: Convocatoria de Becas OEA - UNIR, EP NEWMAN y UNIR Mexico (Curso Academico 2026, 2a convocatoria)

applicant_utility.summary: Get admitted first and the scholarship follows: there is no separate OEA application form, so your only real task is completing UNIR, EP NEWMAN or UNIR Mexico's own admission process, paying their admission fee, and waiting for their application letter. Budget for the share you still owe, which is 40% of total tuition for official master's and degree programmes and 50% for UNIR Formacion Permanente, plus every administrative fee from translation and notarisation to certificates and graduation. Watch the institution-specific deadlines, because UNIR and EP NEWMAN close on 19 October 2026, eight days before UNIR Mexico and eleven before UNIR Formacion Permanente.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Professionals from an OAS Member State (not Nicaragua) who want a Spanish-language online master's and can fund roughly half the tuition themselves without studying in their home country.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target programme is one of those named in the call before paying any admission fee
Check you are not studying in your country of origin, a rule that disqualifies otherwise strong candidates
Get the programme cost in writing from an advisor, since the document warns the printed costs are orientative and may be lower in your country
Prepare proof of financial capacity for the uncovered share before the programme starts
Line up certified translations and notarisation of your documents early, as they are explicitly not covered
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the scholarship application is separate, missing the admission deadline, and arriving with no application letter at all
Being a Nicaraguan national or resident, which is excluded outright
Applying to study in your own country of origin
Having held another OAS scholarship at the same level
Dropping below a 5/10 average or being reported academically dropped, which can trigger repayment of the scholarship value
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: 40% of total tuition for official master's and degree programmes (50% for Formacion Permanente), plus admission fee, translation and notarisation, study materials, titulation and degree procedures, certificates, and any other unlisted expense.
document_audit: The application letter from the institution is the trigger for your candidacy, so chase it if admission confirmation is slow

The call refers to a 'Responsabilidades del Becario' section on page 27, but the published PDF has only 10 pages, so request the current obligations directly from the institution or Scholarships@oas.org
The SG/OAS reserves the right to cancel the announcement at any point in the process, so do not resign from a job or pay non-refundable costs on the strength of the award
alerts: UNIR Maestrias/Grados and EP NEWMAN close 19 October 2026; UNIR Mexico 26 October; UNIR Formacion Permanente 30 October
Selected candidates are published from November 2026 and only they are contacted, so silence is not a soft rejection you can query
You must commit to working in your country of origin or residence, in an OAS member country, or in an international organisation for at least the length of the scholarship, or repay the funds
Neither the OAS nor the institutions take responsibility for recognition, legalisation, homologation or convalidacion of the resulting title in your country
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission at the institution, automatic candidacy via the application letter, specialised committee selection, results at www.oea.org/becas from November 2026, email offer to selected candidates only, then acceptance and payment procedures.

scholarships.deadline: 2a convocatoria: 19 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Maestrías Oficiales y Grados Oficiales, and EP NEWMAN); 26 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Mexico); 30 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Formacion Permanente)
scholarships.description: The SG/OAS awards tuition discounts for online postgraduate study with UNIR (Spain), the Escuela de Posgrado Peruana de NEWMAN (Peru) and UNIR Mexico. Up to 885 places are offered, with a 60% discount on total tuition for official master's programmes and official degrees, and a 50% discount for UNIR Formación Permanente programmes, applicable only to the value of the study programme. Admission fees, translation and notarisation, study materials, titulation and degree-awarding procedures, and any other cost not listed are explicitly excluded, and recipients must personally demonstrate the financial capacity to cover the uncovered programme costs, so this is not full funding.
scholarships.duration: UNIR Maestrías Oficiales 12 months; UNIR Grados Oficiales 4 years, with the scholarship applying only to the first teaching year of the degree scholarship; UNIR Formación Permanente 21 to 34 weeks; EP NEWMAN maestrías 12 months; UNIR México maestrías 18 or 24 months
scholarships.application_period: Two calls in the 2026 academic course. 1a convocatoria (Primavera 2026) deadlines ran 16 March to 10 April 2026 and are closed. 2a convocatoria (Otono 2026) is open with deadlines of 19, 26 and 30 October 2026 depending on the institution and programme; selected candidates are announced in November 2026 and programmes start in October/November 2026 depending on the programme.
scholarships.official_source: Secretaria General de la Organizacion de los Estados Americanos (SG/OAS) with UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico
eligibility: Seran elegibles los interesados con nacionalidad y/o residencia legal permanente de cualquiera de los Estados Miembros de la SG/OEA, excepto Nicaragua.
No se puede estudiar en su propio pais de origen.
Para ser beneficiario de la beca, el candidato debera haber finalizado el proceso de admision y haber sido admitido en uno de los programas de estudios en una de las instituciones.
No haber recibido otras becas academicas de la OEA, en el mismo nivel de estudios propuesto a esta convocatoria.
Antes de iniciar cualquier Programa, todo Becario debera demostrar su capacidad financiera para solventar los costos del Programa no cubierto por la Beca dentro de un plazo establecido.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be nationals or permanent legal residents of an OAS Member State except Nicaragua, must not study in their own country of origin, must already have completed admission to a participating programme, must not have held another OAS scholarship at the same level, and must prove they can fund the costs not covered.
benefits: Up to 885 places available across the three institutions for the 2026 academic course.
coverage: 60% discount on the total tuition (colegiatura) for UNIR official master's programmes and official degrees, and for EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico official master's programmes.
50% discount on the total tuition for UNIR Formación Permanente programmes.
The discount applies only to the value of the study programme.
requirements: Have been admitted to one of the programmes listed in the call, evidenced by an application letter issued by the institution.
Pay the admission fee (cuota de admision) required by the institution in order to be admitted to the study programme.
Before starting the programme, demonstrate financial capacity to cover the programme costs not covered by the scholarship within the established period.
Maintain an average of 5/10 or higher to keep the scholarship for the duration of the programme.
Not be reported with baja academica through absences from the programme and/or failure of subjects.
documents: Institution's application letter (carta de aplicacion) issued once the applicant is admitted
Admission documentation required by the institution for the chosen programme
required_documents: Institution's application letter (carta de aplicacion) issued once the applicant is admitted
Admission documentation required by the institution for the chosen programme
application_method: Step 1: Follow the admission process for the chosen programme directly with the institution, submitting all documentation the institution requires, and pay the admission fee.

Step 2: Once admitted and in receipt of the institution's application letter (carta de aplicacion), the applicant is automatically considered a candidate for the OAS-UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico scholarship; there is no separate scholarship application form.
Step 3: UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS form a specialised committee to select the scholarship holders.
Step 4: Await publication of results at www.oea.org/becas, announced from November 2026 for the 2a convocatoria.

Step 5: Only selected candidates are contacted by email by UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions; after accepting, the scholarship holder starts the corresponding payment procedures with the chosen institution.
scholarships.selection_notes: A specialised committee of UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS selects the scholarship holders, considering the geographic distribution of candidates according to the needs of Member States as reflected in the UNDP Human Development Index, the academic profile and merit and academic credentials, the applicant's potential impact on completing the programme, and gender distribution.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Citizens or permanent legal residents of OAS Member States other than Nicaragua, from a country other than the one they plan to study in, who have already been admitted to a participating online programme and can fund the non-discounted portion of the tuition themselves.
scholarships.notes: This is a tuition discount only and it does not cover the whole fee, so applicants must not treat it as full funding. The 2a convocatoria deadlines fall between 19 and 30 October 2026, so the UNIR and EP NEWMAN lines close first on 19 October 2026. Excluded from eligibility: SG/OAS officials, persons under contract by results with the SG/OAS, Permanent Mission staff, and relatives of all of the above. Nicaraguan nationals and permanent legal residents are excluded. Applicants cannot study in their own country of origin. The call states programme costs shown in the document are orientative and may be lower in some countries, and it repeatedly warns that neither the OAS nor the institutions take responsibility for recognition, legalisation, homologation or convalidacion of the resulting title in the applicant's country of country of origin. The scholarship is conditional on academic performance, and it applies only to the value of the study programme. The SG/OAS reserves the right to cancel this announcement at any point in the process. The document's benefits section refers to a 'Responsabilidades del Becario' section on page 27, but the official PDF available at this URL contains only 10 pages, so that section could not be read.

scholarships.title: KAUST Fellowship (Master's, Ph.D. and M.S./Ph.D. Pathway)
scholarships.name: KAUST Fellowship (Master's, Ph.D. and M.S./Ph.D. Pathway)

applicant_utility.summary: The KAUST Fellowship is automatic once you are admitted, so the only application that matters is the admissions application and it closes on 3 January 2027 for Fall 2027 Round 2 with decisions on 14 February 2027. Build the file around a 750-word statement of purpose and three referees with institutional email addresses, because KAUST rejects personal email addresses and expects references within seven calendar days of the deadline. Secure a valid IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL 5.0 / PTE 71 / Cambridge 185 score, or qualify for the in-person degree exemption from the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, since Medium of Instruction certificates and the Duolingo test are not accepted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong science, engineering and mathematics graduates with a relevant degree, a GPA comfortably above 3.0 and a clearly articulated research direction.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your three referees before entering their details, since reference requests fire immediately and late references delay the application
Book an English test early enough that the score date is within two years at the time you apply
Chase a complete transcript that shows the grading scale, not just grades
Declare any Professional Master's degree explicitly if you are applying for a Ph.D.
Scan the passport page unobscured, with picture and personal details readable
Plan finances for a housing upgrade if you want one, since base accommodation is shared for single students
common_rejection_risks: Referees submitting after the seven-day window, which stalls the whole application
Submitting a Medium of Instruction certificate, a Duolingo score, a TOEFL MyBest superscore or an IELTS One Skill Retake, all of which KAUST will not accept
GPA near the 3.0 floor, when 90% of admitted applicants sit above 3.3
A statement of purpose that reads as generic rather than tied to a KAUST programme and faculty
Assuming a GRE score will compensate for weak academics, since KAUST is explicit that admission decisions are final and no feedback is given
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any housing upgrade fee, and costs for dependents or family members not covered as eligible dependents living on campus; relocation support covers only the initial move and the return home on graduation.
document_audit: A non-English transcript needs both the original and a certified translation uploaded together
If your degree is not finished you may submit a partial or unofficial transcript, but an official final transcript must come directly from the awarding institution before arrival
Saudi applicants should use a national ID card rather than a passport
alerts: Students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship
You can submit without an English score, but you must meet the minimum before enrolment and a competitive applicant should include it
Saudi nationals and Ph.D. students with IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in the first year
There is a limited time to respond to an offer or the decision may be withdrawn
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online portal submission, document review, faculty ranking and shortlisting, online interview if invited, then an emailed decision within the round's notification window.

scholarships.deadline: Fall 2027 Round 2 application deadline 3 January 2027 (Round 2 opened 28 September 2026); decisions released 14 February 2027
scholarships.description: The KAUST Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted graduate students at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. The published package covers full tuition and bench fees (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year), a monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress), base on-campus accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs. KAUST states the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's situation.
scholarships.duration: M.S. is a 36-credit program expected to be completed in three semesters and one summer session; the M.S./Ph.D. pathway typically takes five to six years
scholarships.application_period: Fall 2027 Round 2 applications open 28 September 2026 and close 3 January 2027; Spring 2027 entry (PhD only) had a Round 1 deadline of 27 September 2026 with decisions on 8 November 2026
scholarships.official_source: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
eligibility: Bachelors degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Master's programs

Masters degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Ph.D. programs; Professional Master's degrees are not regarded as directly equivalent and must be declared
At least 18 years of age on entry
Minimum permitted GPA of 3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent); typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3 and 75% above 3.5
Evidence of proficiency in the English language
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Applicants need a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject for Master's entry or a relevant master's degree for Ph.D. entry, be at least 18 years old on entry, hold a minimum 3.0/4.0 GPA, and demonstrate English proficiency.
benefits: Eligible students can request a housing upgrade, which will be subject to an additional fee
Relocation assistance covers each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation
Over 90% of admitted students receive full tuition support, a monthly stipend, housing, medical coverage and relocation assistance
coverage: Full tuition and bench fee coverage (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year)
Monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 for Ph.D. students)
Base accommodation (shared accommodation for single students; 2-bed accommodation for married students)
Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus
Relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs
requirements: Submit an application through the KAUST online application portal before the published round deadline
Provide contact details of 3 referees with academic or professional email addresses; personal email addresses are not accepted
Provide an official English language test score if available
Provide a clear, unobscured copy of the passport page showing picture and personal details (Saudi applicants may provide a national ID card)
All supporting documents, including academic transcripts, must be in English
If your official transcript is not in English, upload both the original transcript in the native language and a certified English translation
A statement of purpose of approximately 750 words
GRE or PGAT scores may be submitted but are not a compulsory requirement
documents: Official university transcripts (complete academic record showing courses, credits where applicable, grades, final grade or award, and the grading scale used)
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Statement of purpose (approximately 750 words)
Contact details of 3 referees
Official English language test score (if available)
Clear, unobscured copy of the passport page (or national ID card for Saudi applicants)
Certified English translation of non-English transcripts
Final official transcript sent directly by the awarding institution before arrival, if admitted
required_documents: Official university transcripts (complete academic record showing courses, credits where applicable, grades, final grade or award, and the grading scale used)
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Statement of purpose (approximately 750 words)
Contact details of 3 referees
Official English language test score (if available)
Clear, unobscured copy of the passport page (or national ID card for Saudi applicants)
Certified English translation of non-English transcripts
Final official transcript sent directly by the awarding institution before arrival, if admitted
scholarships.english_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in all individual sections (IELTS Online accepted), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 overall with at least 4.5 in all individual sections (KAUST Admissions code 4107; TOEFL Home Edition accepted), or PTE Academic 71 overall with at least 67 in all individual sections, or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185 overall with at least 176 in all individual sections. Scores valid for two years from the test date.
application_method: Log into the KAUST application portal and submit the application before the published round deadline
Upload transcripts, CV, statement of purpose, English test score and passport page as part of the online application
Enter 3 referees' contact details, which sends reference requests to them automatically
Respond to any invitation for an online interview with KAUST faculty from your subject area
Await the decision notification by email within the published notification window for the round
scholarships.selection_notes: Five-stage process: submission, Admissions team document review, faculty review committee evaluation and ranking against other applicants with shortlisting for interviews, academic interview and/or test, then decision. Admission review is holistic, considering academic achievements and personal qualities such as motivation and potential impact in the scientific community. All admission decisions are final and will not be reconsidered, and KAUST states it cannot provide individual feedback on specific applications.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Graduate students in science, engineering, mathematics and related fields who hold a relevant bachelor's (Master's entry) or relevant master's (Ph.D. entry) degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0 and clear research interests.
scholarships.notes: Relocation assistance is only for each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation. Some students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship. Eligible students who request a housing upgrade pay an additional fee. An English proficiency score is not required if the applicant's degree was completed by in-person study at an accredited institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, or if the applicant previously completed a degree taken at KAUST's campus in Thuwal; distance learning, satellite campuses, joint programs and branch institutions outside those countries do not qualify for the exemption. Applicants may submit without an English score but must meet the minimum before enrolment. Saudi nationals and PhD students scoring IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in their first year. KAUST does not accept Medium of Instruction certificates, the Duolingo English Test (except for Visiting Student applicants), TOEFL MyBest superscores, or IELTS One Skill Retake results. If accepted, there is a limited time to respond to secure the place or the decision may be withdrawn.

scholarships.title: MBZUAI Graduate Funding for M.Sc. and Ph.D. Students
scholarships.name: MBZUAI Graduate Funding for M.Sc. and Ph.D. Students

applicant_utility.summary: Apply once and apply well, because MBZUAI processes only one submission per admission cycle and the Fall 2027 portal closes at 5 p.m. GST on 15 December 2026 with decisions on 31 March 2027 and an offer response deadline of 15 April 2027. Do not assume funding comes with admission: M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and are funded only through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship or, for UAE nationals, an approved government scholarship, so your research statement and referee recommendations are doing the real work. Keep the Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence out of your plan if you need funding, since it is fee-based at AED 5,000 per credit for a total of AED 170,000 and is excluded from University and faculty-sponsored funding.
applicant_utility.best_fit: STEM graduates with a strong CGPA (3.0-3.5 or above on a 4.0 scale depending on programme) applying to M.Sc. or Ph.D. programmes in AI who can secure or attract a faculty advisor's research sponsorship.
application_readiness_checklist: Write the research statement against the specific work of the faculty group you hope to join, not against AI in general
Arrange referee recommendations from people who can speak to research potential, since funding depends on advisor sponsorship
Check your degree qualifies for attestation (UAE) or a Certificate of Recognition (outside the UAE) and start that process early
Budget for the AED 200 application fee, which must be paid for the application to proceed to review
Plan around the 31 March 2027 decision date and the 15 April 2027 offer response deadline before committing to competing offers
common_rejection_risks: Submitting multiple applications in the same cycle, which are simply not processed
Applying to M.Sc. expecting automatic funding when funding depends on a faculty advisor-sponsored assistantship
Choosing the Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence and discovering it is excluded from University and faculty-sponsored funding
Leaving degree attestation or the Certificate of Recognition past the first semester
A statement of purpose and research statement that do not name a concrete research direction
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: For unfunded M.Sc. students, tuition and fees apply; full Cost of Attendance figures for Fall 2027 were still being finalized at the time of verification. Funded students should expect to fund any off-campus or family accommodation themselves.
document_audit: Senior-level applicants may apply with a transcript copy but must submit the official complete degree certificate and transcript upon admission
Degree attestation (UAE degrees) or a Certificate of Recognition (degrees from outside the UAE) must be furnished within the first semester
Students receiving external scholarships or fellowships must disclose the funding, which normally replaces rather than tops up the University stipend
alerts: Funded students must maintain an in-person on-campus presence throughout the funded period and need approval before being away
Ph.D. Year 1 funding is centrally funded by the University while a faculty advisor match is arranged, and moves to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2
M.Sc. and Ph.D. Computational Biology opened a month later than other graduate programmes, on 30 September 2026

Admission is highly competitive with limited places in each incoming cohort, and MBZUAI states that 43% of its incoming graduate students for 2026-2027 came from the world's top computer science universities
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One portal application with CV, statement of purpose, research statement and referees, then a screening exam and technical interview if invited, with the decision published on 31 March 2027.

scholarships.deadline: Final application deadline 15 December 2026, 5p.m. GST for all graduate programs except the Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence (28 February 2027 for MAAI); decision notification 31 March 2027; offer response deadline 15 April 2027
scholarships.description: MBZUAI's graduate funding is not a single named scholarship but a University-and-faculty funding model under which funded M.Sc. and Ph.D. students receive free tuition fees, a monthly stipend, one return airfare each year to their home country, health insurance for the approved funding period, and a University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID where eligible. Ph.D. Year 1 funding is centrally funded by the University while the student is matched with a faculty advisor, and funding moves to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is secured through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship, or an approved government scholarship for UAE nationals, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence is a fee-based programme and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding.
scholarships.duration: M.Sc.: full-time, on campus, 36 credits (coursework in the first year, thesis research in the second year, plus a master's internship of up to six weeks). Ph.D.: full-time, on campus, 60 credits, with thesis research pursued for a period of three (3) to four (4) years.
scholarships.application_period: Application portal opened 7 September 2026, 8a.m. GST for all graduate programs except M.Sc. and Ph.D. Computational Biology, which opened 30 September 2026, 8a.m. GST. Portal closes 15 December 2026, 5p.m. GST (MAAI: 28 February 2027).

University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID (where eligible)

coverage: Free tuition fees for funded students
A monthly stipend

scholarships.english_requirement: IELTS Academic 6.5; TOEFL iBT 90; PTE Academic 60; Cambridge C1 Advanced 180; Cambridge C2 Proficiency 200; Duolingo English Test 120 (accepted only when IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/Cambridge access is limited). Exams must be administered at an approved physical test centre - Home Edition exams are not accepted - and results are valid for 2 years from the test date. Full exemption applies for a degree entirely taught and assessed in English at a university in a listed country where English is an official language (including the UK, US, Canada excluding Quebec, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa and others); conditional exemption can be requested with an official medium-of-instruction letter on university letterhead, provisionally accepted at application and verified later. Applications without English proficiency documentation remain incomplete and do not progress.
application_method: Choose your admission pathway on the MBZUAI admissions page (undergraduate, graduate master's, or graduate Ph.D.)

scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are evaluated on academic excellence, technical preparation, research potential, and alignment with their chosen program. Admission to MBZUAI is highly competitive with limited places available in each incoming cohort; MBZUAI states that forty-three percent of its incoming graduate students for the 2026-2027 academic year came from the world's top computer science universities. Funding decisions for M.Sc. students depend on whether a faculty advisor sponsors a research or teaching assistantship or, for UAE nationals, an approved government scholarship, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Graduate applicants to MBZUAI's M.Sc. or Ph.D. programmes in computer science, electrical or computer engineering, mathematics, physics or another relevant science or engineering major who hold a STEM degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 on a 4.0 scale depending on the programme.
scholarships.notes: M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is NOT guaranteed for all admitted students; students without a funding source are classified as fee-paying. Ph.D. funding is subject to a confirmed advisor match and satisfactory progress, and transitions to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. Funded students are expected to maintain an in-person presence on campus throughout their funded period and to obtain approval before being away. Students receiving external scholarships or fellowships must disclose this funding to the University; external funding normally replaces the University stipend rather than being paid in addition to it. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence (MAAI) is fee-based at AED 5,000 per credit, 34 credit hours, total tuition AED 170,000 (approx. USD 46,291), and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding. Cost of Attendance figures for Fall 2027 for unfunded M.Sc. students are currently being finalized and were not published on the page at the time of verification. An English language waiver exists and is described on the MBZUAI admissions FAQ, but the minimum score thresholds are published only on programme-specific pages, so no score is recorded here.

scholarships.title: HBKU Graduate Tuition Waiver and Stipend
scholarships.name: HBKU Graduate Tuition Waiver and Stipend

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate scholarship form: HBKU considers you for a tuition waiver and stipend inside the graduate admissions process, so the admission file itself is the scholarship application and must be complete by the deadline. An international master's student on the published rates receives 7,000 QAR per month for 21 months plus a programme-specific tuition waiver (up to 75% for STEM MS, 60% for SHAPE MS/MA) and a single round-trip airfare, while PhD students receive higher rates over 45 months. The stipend is conditional on working 10 hours a week as a research assistant for your supervisor, caps total work at 20 hours per week, and must cover your housing and meals because HBKU pays no housing benefit. Treat the award as renewable rather than guaranteed: it is reviewed annually against academic progress and the availability of funds.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International students targeting a funded, full-time research master's or PhD at HBKU who can commit to weekly RA/TA service and want a Qatar-based research environment.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit through the Apply Now portal and upload every document in PDF only - non-PDF files are not accepted
Ensure each transcript includes an explanation of the grading system and an official translation if it is not in English or Arabic
Request two reference letters early, at least one from an academic referee, and enter their contact details after submitting
Write the 300-500 word personal statement well before the deadline and check the word count - incomplete or short statements are not accepted
Book IELTS/TOEFL early enough that scores are valid on 1 February 2027 and arrange for official score reports to reach HBKU
For CSE PhD programmes that require GRE/GMAT (Sustainable Energy, Sustainable Environment), schedule the test and send official scores directly to HBKU

Being a full-time professional or working more than 40% of full-time hours, which rules out the stipend entirely
Missing the 1 February 2027 international deadline - the 15 March 2027 date applies only to Qatari and resident applicants seeking funding
Assuming admission guarantees money - awards are merit or need based, depend on available funds and are reviewed annually

Holding external funding or sponsorship without checking the scholarship agreement first, since external funding may affect eligibility
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing in Qatar Foundation dorms or external accommodation, meals and general living costs (all paid from the 7,000 QAR/month stipend or personal funds), the QAR 250 non-refundable application fee, visa and residency costs, and any costs for dependants - the stipend does not vary with marital status or number of dependants.

Do not attach anything beyond the required list - additional materials are automatically discarded

External funding may affect scholarship eligibility, and deferring admission may also affect it - contact your college before deferring
Stipends for local students are limited, and stipend exceptions beyond the published rates need dean and provost approval
The award is reviewed annually: keep academic standing strong and expect re-confirmation against available funds each year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account in the Apply Now portal, submit up to two programme applications with all required documents, then upload supplementary documents and reference contacts via the confirmation email while the admissions team and the college assess the file.

scholarships.deadline: Online graduate admission application opens to the public 1 October 2026; admission application deadline for international graduate applicants 1 February 2027; admission application deadline for Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding 15 March 2027
scholarships.description: HBKU graduate scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs and a stipend paid directly to the student, and HBKU states that graduate students receiving a stipend would generally also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU and range from 100% for PhD STEM and PhD SHAPE and S.J.D. programmes down to 0% for LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, with published monthly and annual rates for Qatari, international and local PhD and Master's students, over durations of 45 months for PhD and 21 months for Master's. Awards depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are made on a merit or need basis only.
scholarships.duration: Stipend duration of 45 months for PhD programmes and 21 months for Master's programmes
scholarships.application_period: Online applications open to the public on 1 October 2026 and close on 1 February 2027 for international graduate applicants. Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding have a later deadline of 15 March 2027. No separate scholarship application is needed; candidates are considered during the admissions process.
scholarships.official_source: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU), a member of Qatar Foundation for Education, Science, and Community Development
eligibility: Admitted or applying HBKU graduate student, considered for scholarships during the admissions process
Awards depend on the availability of funds and are made on a merit or need basis only
For stipends: full-time graduate students serving at the university as research assistants and/or teaching assistants, depending on the availability of funds
Full-time working professionals and part-time workers who exceed 40% of full-time hours are not eligible for stipends
Students must maintain good academic standing as specified in the scholarship agreement
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Tuition waivers and stipend awards at HBKU depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are awarded only on a merit or need basis; stipends are awarded to full-time graduate students serving as research assistants and/or teaching assistants.

Stipend holders are eligible for paid employment through the Student Employment Program for up to 10 additional hours per week
coverage: Tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs, at a programme-specific percentage
Monthly stipend paid directly to the student
Single round-trip airfare for international students during their candidature, consisting of one inbound ticket upon starting the academic program and one outbound ticket upon graduation

Serve as a research assistant with the primary supervisor for 10 hours per week while receiving a stipend
Observe a maximum of 20 hours per week of work in total, i.e. 10 hours beyond the RA commitment
Maintain good academic standing as specified in the scholarship agreement, since scholarships are reviewed annually and depend on academic progress and available funds

required_documents: HBKU graduate admission application and supporting documents as required by the admissions process
scholarships.english_requirement: Valid IELTS score of 6.5 or TOEFL score of 79 to demonstrate proficiency in English (published graduate admission requirement; further details about the language proficiency requirement and the process to seek exemption are available from HBKU admissions)
application_method: Create a user account through the HBKU Apply Now portal
Submit an application by choosing the desired college and program, with up to two applications permitted per academic year
After submission, log back into the account using the confirmation email instructions to submit supplementary documents and provide contact details for references
The HBKU admissions team checks the application for completion and eligibility before forwarding it to the relevant college for assessment
Await the college's decision and offer letter
Scholarships are considered as part of the admissions process; no separate scholarship application is required
scholarships.selection_notes: There is a preliminary application review by the HBKU admissions team for completeness and eligibility, followed by assessment by the relevant college. scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Graduate applicants to HBKU colleges (College of Science and Engineering, College of Health and Life Sciences, College of Islamic Studies, College of Humanities and Social Sciences, College of Law, College of Public Policy and the School of Economics and Management) who are seeking a tuition waiver and stipend, including international students who can serve as research assistants.
scholarships.notes: Students are responsible for covering the cost of their housing, whether in Qatar Foundation dormitory facilities or external accommodation; this expense is paid from the monthly stipend or personal funds, and HBKU does not provide direct payment for student housing. Meal plans are not separately included; the stipend is a fixed amount meant to cover general living expenses including meals. Stipend awards do not depend on the student's marital status or the number of family dependents. Stipends for local students are limited. Stipends funded from external sources, including research grants, are excluded from the published rates. Self-sponsored graduate students are only eligible for a discounted tuition rate of 2,000 QAR per credit hour based on financial need, and these scholarship guidelines do not apply to students funded by external sources. Receipt of external funding may affect eligibility. Deferral of admission may affect scholarship eligibility. LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes carry a 0% tuition waiver.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a career pipeline into the UAE diplomatic corps, not a study-abroad grant: you must already hold an unconditional offer from a university on MOFA's own approved list, be willing to serve in the Ministry for as many years as the scholarship covers, and join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy after graduation. There is no published deadline, so work backwards from your own timeline and expect the review and final approval process to take three to five months. The mandatory interview is the make-or-break stage, and an offer from a university not on the MOFA list cannot be used at all.

The programme is not a general study-abroad scholarship: it carries a service obligation, requiring the holder to join the MOFA diplomatic corps for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship and to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation.

scholarships.title: Career Development Fellowship
scholarships.name: Career Development Fellowship

applicant_utility.summary: This is a four-year, GBP 703,800-capped postdoctoral fellowship for researchers who self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, with fewer than 24 months of postdoctoral experience and a UK connection through nationality, prior UK study or a UK postdoc. It funds salary at 80%, so your prospective host institution must be willing to cover the remaining 20% and directly allocated costs, which makes the host conversation as decisive as the science. Treat it as a high-risk, high-reward application: the published success rate was 3% in 2024/25 and 7% in 2025/26, so apply knowing the numbers and do not rely on it as your only route.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early postdoctoral researchers from Black heritage backgrounds in natural sciences who already have a UK host department willing to co-fund 20% of salary and directly allocated costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Count your postdoctoral months precisely, since more than 24 months of postdoctoral experience at the funding start date ends your eligibility
Line up a UK host institution early and confirm in writing that it will cover the 20% shortfall on salary and directly allocated costs
Register on Flexi-Grant well before 18 November 2026 and check the scheme notes for the full attachment list
Attend the scheme information session linked from the scheme page if it is still open for the 2027 round
Request relocation and visa costs for dependants explicitly, since these sit outside the grant cap
Plan for an in-person interview at the Royal Society in London, including travel and any accessibility needs
common_rejection_risks: Exceeding the 24-month postdoctoral experience threshold by the time funding would start
Having no UK connection through nationality, UK study or a UK postdoctoral position
Research that falls outside the Royal Society's natural sciences remit
A host institution that cannot absorb the 20% of salary and directly allocated costs it must cover
A proposal that cannot be defended on the importance and scientific validity of the work, which is exactly what the interview tests
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The 20% of salary, associated on-costs and directly allocated costs that the host institution must fund, plus anything outside research expenses and the dependant relocation and visa provision.
document_audit: The scheme notes PDF is the authoritative source for the required attachments, so read it rather than relying on the summary page
If you need an adjustment for the application, the interview or any other part of the process, email adjustments@royalsociety.org or call +44 20 7451 2666, and requests are handled confidentially
Applicants requiring a visa should confirm eligibility for the Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement before committing to a UK move
alerts: The scheme is a pilot restricted to researchers from Black heritage backgrounds; if it is not broadened, later cohorts may not exist
Undergraduate, Master's and PhD students cannot apply for Royal Society funding, so this is not a route into a PhD
The 18 November 2026 close date is fixed for the 2027 round and decisions are not due until 30 June 2027, leaving a long gap to plan around
The scheme is funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) and Royal Society charitable funds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Flexi-Grant application with research proposal, panel assessment and shortlisting, in-person interview at the Royal Society for shortlisted applicants, then a decision by 30 June 2027.

scholarships.description: The Career Development Fellowship provides the most talented early career scientists from underrepresented groups in STEM with research funding and high-quality training opportunities to build a strong base for a successful research career. It is currently offered as a pilot with researchers from Black heritage backgrounds and, if successful, may be broadened to researchers from other underrepresented groups.

scholarships.application_period: 2027 round opens 22 September 2026 and closes 18 November 2026; decision by 30 June 2027.
eligibility: You self-identify as being from a Black heritage, including mixed Black background.

You are a UK national or you have completed a part of your education in the UK through your Undergraduate, Master's or PhD degree studies or you hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK.
You have a PhD, or will have one by the time the funding starts, but have less than 24 months post-doctoral experience.

Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to, biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
Both UK and non-UK domiciled researchers who wish to conduct their research in the UK are eligible.
Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.

scholarships.title: Wellcome Early-Career Award
scholarships.name: Wellcome Early-Career Award
scholarships.funding_period: up to, over the award duration (usually 5 years)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a salaried research grant, not a studentship: Wellcome pays the total cost of your salary for the whole grant plus up to GBP 400,000 for research expenses, and you must be able to give at least 80% of your research time to the project. There are no deadlines - applications go year-round to the next shortlisting meeting - but the location rules tighten on 29 October 2026, after which only lead applicants based in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia are eligible. Your institution rather than you submits the application, so research-office lead time matters far more than any deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A researcher with a passed PhD viva and no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, at an eligible UK, Irish or LMIC institution, with a bold Discovery Research question they want to make their own.
application_readiness_checklist: Run Wellcome's self-assessment tool before drafting anything - Wellcome states that applications are often withdrawn before shortlisting because the researcher does not meet eligibility requirements.
Test the proposal against the Discovery Research remit; insufficient relation to human health is the most common reason applications are withdrawn.
Confirm your administering organisation is eligible and secure a sponsor who holds an established post for the full duration of the award.
Line up a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship - your sponsor can double as your mentor, and neither is paid for their input.
Cost the application at 1.0 full-time equivalent on your host organisation's own pay scales, even if you intend to hold the award part-time.
Request the Finance Director overhead letter early if you want overheads, since they sit outside the GBP 400,000 cap and are capped at 20% of direct research costs.
common_rejection_risks: Withdrawal before shortlisting for ineligibility, most often on career stage, postdoctoral years or the time-commitment rule.
Withdrawal because the proposal does not fit what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research, usually because it is not sufficiently related to human health.
Scoring in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting, which blocks any resubmission of that project.
Budgeting beyond the GBP 400,000 research expenses limit, or requesting excluded items such as PhD stipends, contingency funds, office furniture or indemnity insurance.
A proposal that reads as incremental rather than bold and creative - the proposal alone carries 50% of the interview weighting.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: PhD stipends and studentships are not provided on this award, and overheads are not paid to UK research organisations that already receive core funding for overheads. Relocation up to GBP 1,000, conference travel (GBP 2,000 a year for you), caring costs at conferences up to GBP 1,000 per conference and training up to GBP 500 a year per person are claimable within the award.
document_audit: The sponsor statement must come from someone holding an established post for the entire award; a sponsor on a fixed-term contract is a common structural failure.
If you plan to work for more than three months outside your administering organisation you need an additional sponsor at that location to guarantee space and resources.
An overhead request needs a Finance Director letter that either confirms an externally validated rate, who provided it and when it was last reviewed, or breaks down the actual costs requested.
Coapplicants are not accepted, so collaborators cannot lead a component of the research and cannot receive salary or compensation for their time.
If your organisation has never applied to Wellcome before, you must request an organisation account in the 'Add your administering organisation' section, which adds lead time.
alerts: Location eligibility changes on 29 October 2026: applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current rules, after which only UK and Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia LMIC-based lead applicants qualify.
Shortlisting and interview committees each meet only three times a year, and an application can be pushed to the following meeting if one is full - apply well in advance of any planned start date.
The same project may be submitted a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, so a resubmission must include significant changes.
You can only hold one Early-Career Award and Wellcome does not offer renewals; you also cannot apply if you hold, have held or have accepted an equivalent award at this career stage.
You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You build the application on the Wellcome Funding platform and submit it to your institution's approver, who sends it to Wellcome; it then goes to a Career Advisory Group for shortlisting, external written expert review, an interview in London or remotely at which you present, and a Discovery Research Decision Board decision.

scholarships.deadline: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. Apply anytime - Applications are accepted year-round.
scholarships.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
scholarships.duration: Usually 5 years, but may be less for some disciplines, and may only be longer if held on a part-time basis
scholarships.application_period: Rolling, applications accepted year-round. Location eligibility changes on 29 October 2026: from that date applications are only accepted from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia. Applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current location eligibility requirements.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
Coapplicants are not accepted.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Early-career researcher with a passed PhD viva or at least four years' equivalent research experience, no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, at least 80% of research time on the project, based at an eligible administering organisation.
benefits: If, after two or more years from the activation date, your organisation awards you a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract that includes your salary, you can keep the salary element of the award to use towards your remaining research costs
Award holders who need a visa to work in the UK may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa
The award may be held on a part-time basis, with the duration extended to reflect this; the application must still be costed at 1.0 (100%) full-time equivalent
Access to Wellcome's global talent, mentoring and community networks
coverage: Total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire period of the grant, determined by the administering organisation, including basic salary, employer contributions, pension scheme costs, incremental salary progression and locally recognised allowances
Up to £400,000 for research expenses
Overheads, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit; total overhead cost should not be more than 20% of direct research costs
Overseas allowances and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit
Adjustment support including assistive technology and support staff, which does not count towards the £400,000 limit
Visa and work permit costs for the grantholder, their partner and dependent children, plus Immigration Health Surcharge costs if in the UK six months or more
Relocation allowance of up to £1,000 to cover personal removal costs
Staff salaries up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post
Conference attendance contributions: £2,000 a year for the grantholder and £1,000 each a year for research and technical staff, plus accredited carbon credits to mitigate emissions
Caring responsibility costs at conferences up to £1,000 per person per conference, subject to the stated conditions

Continuing professional development and professional skills training up to £500 a year per person, and research skills training, for staff in posts of 12 months or more working on the grant at 50% FTE or more
Materials and consumables, animals, equipment purchase and maintenance, computer equipment, and access charges for shared equipment, facilities or services

Obtain a sponsor statement from an individual at your administering organisation who holds an established post for the duration of the award
Identify a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship
If requesting overheads, provide a letter from your Finance Director stating how overhead costs were calculated, including confirmation of any externally validated rate and when it was last reviewed
You must check that your type of research project is within what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research before applying

Sponsor statement from an individual at the administering organisation holding an established post
Mentor details
Finance Director letter on overhead calculation, if overheads are requested

Confirm your research fits what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research
Agree your administering organisation and secure a sponsor and a mentor

Complete the application in Wellcome Funding and submit

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.
scholarships.program_type: Foundation research grant
scholarships.best_fit: Researchers with a completed PhD (or equivalent) and no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, from any discipline, based at an eligible UK, Republic of Ireland or eligible LMIC organisation, whose work has potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
scholarships.notes: Location eligibility is changing on 29 October 2026: from that date Wellcome will only accept applications from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia, so an application submitted in October 2026 from a Republic of Ireland or a Latin American organisation would not be accepted under the new rule. You can only hold one of these awards and Wellcome does not offer renewals. No studentships are provided on this award. You cannot apply if you hold or have accepted an equivalent award at this career stage, or if you have an existing tenured salaried post for the duration of the award (unless based in a low- or middle-income country). You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China. Total resubmission of the same project is capped at two times across all Wellcome schemes. Overheads are not paid to UK research organisations that already receive core funding for overheads.

scholarships.title: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) - Cycle 2026
scholarships.name: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) - Cycle 2026
scholarships.funding_period: one-time lump sum, up to the published ceiling

applicant_utility.summary: Only applications routed through your National Commission for UNESCO count, and the Commission needs your file at least two weeks before the 15 October 2026 deadline, which puts the real cut-off around 1 October 2026, so you are already inside the final window. Ten fellowships are on offer, each a lump sum of up to US$10,000 from which the cost of the mandatory UNESCO-arranged medical insurance is deducted before you receive any money. Tuition, equipment, publication costs and conference attendance are explicitly excluded, so treat this as a mobility and subsistence grant rather than a degree scholarship, and assume the supervisor acceptance letter, the Annex 4 proposal and the Annex 5 language certificate are the three items most likely to stall you. The stay must start from February 2027 and be completed no later than December 2027, which constrains visa timing.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Researchers aged 40 or under from an invited African, Small Island Developing State, Ukrainian or Turkish institution who already hold a Japanese supervisor's acceptance and have a proposal squarely inside one of the five AI and heritage research areas.
application_readiness_checklist: Email your National Commission for UNESCO immediately to confirm it is still accepting files for the 15 October 2026 UNESCO deadline
Check that your country appears in Annex 1 and that you are 40 or younger on the application date
Map your proposal against Annex 2 and lock in exactly one primary research area plus one matching sub-area
Collect the supervisor's acceptance letter, degree and academic documents, recommendation letter and language certificate in the formats the Commission requires
Draft the research proposal directly on the Annex 4 template rather than as a free-form document
Prepare both your language certificate and the Annex 5 UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge
common_rejection_risks: Missing the National Commission's own cut-off, since a Commission cannot nominate you late and UNESCO will not consider a late online file
A proposal that straddles two research areas or matches no listed sub-area in Annex 2
No acceptance letter from a supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution
An incomplete dossier, which UNESCO states will not be considered
Age above 40 at the time of application
Nationality outside the Annex 1 list, or a home country where the National Commission route is not functioning in time for this cycle
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and any enrolment or research registration fees, a computer or other equipment, publication costs, conference participation (unless clearly justified as integral to the research), and any travel, accommodation or subsistence beyond the lump sum after the insurance deduction.
document_audit: Use the Annex 3 application form and the Annex 4 proposal template exactly; free-format documents risk the file being treated as incomplete
The host institution acceptance letter must name the academic supervisor who will oversee the research in Japan
Both the language certificate and the Annex 5 UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge are listed, so a missing Annex 5 is a completeness trap
Academic documents must evidence at least a Master's degree or equivalent in a field relevant to the proposal
The recommendation letter should support both your research potential and your ability to work with a Japanese supervisor for a 3-9 month stay
alerts: The deadline was already extended once to 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time, so assume no further extension
National Commission nomination is the binding gate: contacting it late is the single most common way a strong file dies
Insurance is deducted from the US$10,000 before disbursement, so the amount you actually receive is lower than the ceiling
The research stay must begin from February 2027 and finish by December 2027, leaving a narrow window for visa and supervisor scheduling
Only 10 fellowships are awarded, so national shortlists are competitive even where many applicants are invited
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file with your National Commission for UNESCO, which nominates you and sends the letter of nomination plus your documents to UNESCO by 15 October 2026, and you then email the online application form and supporting documents to keizoobuchi.fellowships@unesco.org.

scholarships.deadline: Deadline for candidate submission is now extended to 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time. Letters of nomination and all application documents must reach UNESCO from the National Commissions no later than 15 October 2026, and candidates must submit to their own National Commission at least 2 weeks before the required deadline.
scholarships.description: Under the 2026 cycle UNESCO and the Government of Japan award 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye to carry out postgraduate research in a Japanese university or research institution. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence in Japan including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses, and other research-related expenses where applicable. It is a research fellowship, not a degree programme: the grant does not cover tuition fees, and the page publishes no award figures beyond the US$10,000 ceiling.
scholarships.duration: No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months
scholarships.application_period: Cycle 2026 call is open (page last updated 28 September 2026, stating the application for the Cycle 2026 is open and the deadline is now extended to 15 October 2026). Because the National Commission needs at least two weeks, the practical national deadline falls around 1 October 2026. Fellowship period in Japan from February 2027 onwards, to be completed no later than December 2027.

Research stays in Japanese universities and research institutions, from February 2027 onwards and to be completed no later than December 2027

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by a Selection Committee composed of experts from UNESCO and the Government of Japan in the relevant fields, taking into account the merits of the candidates and the quality, relevance and originality of their proposed research. The final selection decision is made by the Japanese authorities based on the recommendation of the Committee, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity.

scholarships.best_fit: Researchers aged 40 or under who hold at least a Master's degree (or equivalent) in a field relevant to the proposed research, come from an invited Member State or Associate Member, already have acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, and are applying in one of the five listed research areas on heritage conservation, AI for natural resources and climate action, ethical and human-centred AI, AI for sustainable cities and infrastructure, or AI and education.
scholarships.notes: Only 10 fellowships are awarded in the 2026 cycle, and only applications nominated by your National Commission are accepted, so the national shortlist is the binding gate. The fellowship grant is a lump sum capped at US$10,000, not a line-itemed scholarship, and the cost of the mandatory medical insurance is deducted from the total before disbursement, so the amount actually received is below the ceiling. The grant does NOT cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs, or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. Candidates who submit incomplete applications, or who submit the online applications beyond the deadline, will not be considered. The practical deadline is at least two weeks earlier than 15 October 2026 because your National Commission must forward the file.

scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals
scholarships.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals
scholarships.funding_period: per trip, paid twice (start and end of scholarship period)

applicant_utility.summary: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the World Bank's JJ/WBGSP, aimed at mid-career Japanese professionals holding or about to hold an unconditional offer for a development-related master's or PhD outside Japan. The only published cash figure is the $600 travel allowance paid at each end of the scholarship; tuition, university-arranged basic medical insurance and a host-country-dependent monthly subsistence allowance make up the rest, so the total value depends on where you study. The 2027 round opens February 15, 2027 and closes in mid-to-late April depending on which official document you read, with winners informed by mid-July. You cannot submit anything until the unconditional admission letter is in hand, so your university applications have to come first.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Japanese mid-career professionals with at least 3 years of paid development-related work earned in the past six years who already hold, or are about to hold, an unconditional (financing excepted) offer for a development-related master's or PhD outside Japan.

Check your degree field against the exclusions (online-only degrees, Foreign Service, Diplomacy, Business/MBA, Law/LLM, Medicine/MD, or joint programs with a Japanese university)

Line up exactly two professional recommenders who supervised paid development work and one academic recommender from a research collaboration, then send the Recommendation Request Form weeks before the deadline
Prepare diploma scans (diplomas, not transcripts), proof of paid development work years, and the Annex 2 CV with unpaid work under a Volunteer Work category
Apply on a computer, not a phone, and submit at least a week early as the Secretariat recommends
Email scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org from February 15, 2027 to register interest in the cycle

Holding other funding without declaring it; the stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially where undeclared external funding is found
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa application and resident permit fees, any cost of bringing or supporting family, a computer, language training outside the programme, additional travel during the study period, research costs, supplementary materials, field trips, workshops/seminars and internships, plus any gap between the host-country subsistence allowance and local rents.
