applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register interest by email from February 15, 2027, complete the online portal application with three online recommendations, then wait through two-assessor scoring, Secretariat shortlisting and Steering Committee approval, with winners informed by mid-July.

scholarships.deadline: The 2027 application window for Japanese nationals will open from February 15 to April 16, 2027. As from February 15, 2027, prospective candidates are invited to express their interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat with an email to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org. Winners are informed by mid-July, after the JJ/WBGSC approval. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026.
scholarships.description: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program, which the World Bank states is fully funded by the Government of Japan. It funds up to two years for a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD programme outside Japan in a development-related field. Benefits include one economy class air travel to the host university and a $600 travel allowance at the start, one economy class return travel and a $600 travel allowance at the end, tuition, basic medical insurance obtainable through the university, and a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies by host country and is not published on the page.
scholarships.duration: Up to two years; all JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: A single application window for the 2027 cycle for Japanese nationals, from February 15 to April 16, 2027. From the opening date, prospective candidates are invited to register interest with the Secretariat by email. Results are communicated by mid-July 2027.
scholarships.official_source: World Bank, Development Economics Vice Presidency, JJ/WBGSP Secretariat (scholarship fully funded by the Government of Japan)
eligibility: Be a Japanese national

On or after the date the call for scholarship applications opens, not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment (including temporary and consultant) of the World Bank Group (The World Bank, International Development Association, International Finance Corporation, Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and International Center for Settlements of Investment Disputes), and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) earned at least three years before the date of the Application Deadline

On or after the date the JJ/WBGSP scholarship application process opens, not be employed (as a staff or any type of employment) by the Government of Japan or its related agencies, including JICA, local governments and the Central Bank

Have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past six years from the date of the Application Deadline

At the time of the application submission, be either admitted unconditionally (except for financing) or currently enrolled full-time in a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Be a Japanese national; hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) earned at least three years before the Application Deadline; have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years from the deadline; and be admitted unconditionally except for financing to, or currently enrolled full-time in, a development-related graduate programme outside Japan.
benefits: The scholarship is fully funded by the Government of Japan
All JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
Two separate $600 travel allowances are payable, one at the start of the programme and one at the end
coverage: One economy class air travel from the scholar's home country to the host university at the start of the graduate degree program, if the scholar is not already attending the graduate program, plus a $600 travel allowance

One economy class air travel from the host university to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment at the end of the scholarship period, if the scholar has completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree, plus a $600 travel allowance
Tuition for the graduate program for the duration of the scholarship period
Cost of basic medical insurance that can be obtained through the university

Monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus during the scholarship period, including accommodations, food and books; the amount varies depending on the host country and is not published

Inform and document to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat any other sources of scholarship funds if notified of being a semi-finalist or awarded a scholarship

The applicant's bachelor's degree diploma, and if applicable the diploma of the most advanced graduate degree (a transcript may not be substituted for a diploma).

C.V. using the format provided in Annex 2 of the Application Guidelines, written in English or the language of the master's degree program for which JJ/WBGSP funding is sought; unpaid work must be listed under a 'Volunteer Work' category and not as employment.

Unconditional (except for financing) Letter of Admission for the upcoming academic year to a master or doctorate program for which the applicant is seeking JJ/WBGSP funding, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence.
Translations of any documents not in English or the language of the degree program; both the original and the translated document must be uploaded, and a certified translation is not required.

For finalists: a scanned copy of the identification page of the passport (or birth/marriage certificate) with the name identical to the application form, within three business days of the scholarship offer; and a medical doctor's certificate less than three months old, submitted at least 21 days before traveling to the host university.
required_documents: Scanned documentation that proves the applicant meets the eligibility requirement regarding the number of years of recent development-related work.
The applicant's bachelor's degree diploma, and if applicable the diploma of the most advanced graduate degree (a transcript may not be substituted for a diploma).

C.V. using the format provided in Annex 2 of the Application Guidelines, written in English or the language of the master's degree program for which JJ/WBGSP funding is sought; unpaid work must be listed under a 'Volunteer Work' category and not as employment.

Unconditional (except for financing) Letter of Admission for the upcoming academic year to a master or doctorate program for which the applicant is seeking JJ/WBGSP funding, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence.
Translations of any documents not in English or the language of the degree program; both the original and the translated document must be uploaded, and a certified translation is not required.

For finalists: a scanned copy of the identification page of the passport (or birth/marriage certificate) with the name identical to the application form, within three business days of the scholarship offer; and a medical doctor's certificate less than three months old, submitted at least 21 days before traveling to the host university.
application_method: From February 15, 2027, express interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat by emailing scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org
Be admitted unconditionally (except for financing) to, or already be enrolled full-time in, a development-related master's or PhD programme outside Japan
Gather the documents required by the 2027 Application Guidelines for Japanese Nationals
Submit the application within the window closing April 16, 2027
Await the JJ/WBGSC decision; winners are informed by mid-July
scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10 on four factors: Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight), Quality of Professional Recommendations (20% weight), Quality of Professional Experience (20%), and Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight). The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
scholarships.program_type: Development bank scholarship (bilateral government-funded graduate scholarship)
scholarships.best_fit: Japanese nationals with a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline and at least three years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years, who are admitted unconditionally (except financing) to, or already enrolled full-time in, a development-related master's or PhD programme outside Japan.
scholarships.notes: The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you are notified of being a semi-finalist or are awarded, you must inform and document other scholarship funds to the Secretariat. After earning their degree, Japanese national scholars are expected to advance their professional career with a keen focus on the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries. The air travel benefit at the end of the scholarship period is conditional on having completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree, and the return ticket is to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment. The published US$600 is a per-trip travel allowance, not the award total. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 window is live.

scholarships.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)
scholarships.name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)

applicant_utility.summary: ESKAS pays CHF 2,450 a month - basic living expenses for one person, explicitly not a salary - and deliberately does not cover tuition, so you must budget semester fees (CHF 600-2,000) and, for ETH/EPFL-type hosts, possibly reduced tuition yourself. Your single hardest task is not the paperwork but finding a Swiss academic supervisor who writes a genuine letter of support: applications without one are not considered at all, and professors can take weeks to reply. Timing is country-specific: applications open 20 August 2026 and go through your country's Swiss diplomatic representation, with decisions by end of May for a 1 September 2027 start.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers under 35 (born after 31 December 1991) who hold a Master's, have a concrete Swiss-hosted project in mind, and are not already living or studying in Switzerland.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your country's deadline and available scholarship types in the official A-Z/regional country lists (published each August)
Find a supervisor early - a professor or lab group leader at a Swiss university, UAS or ETH Domain institute - and secure a substantive letter plus their 2-page CV

Line up two professors in your field to upload recommendation letters through the system when contacted
If you already live in Switzerland, verify you entered no earlier than 1 August 2026 and have under 13 months' residence
For graduate-school PhD scholarships, obtain the doctoral school's confirmation of admission in time to submit it with the application

Being over the age line (born on or before 31 December 1991) for the 2027-2028 cycle
Having lived, studied or worked in Switzerland for more than 13 months before the start
A fourth application after three unsuccessful attempts (excluded)
Informal errors or incompleteness in the file

Field research outside Switzerland is not permitted during research fellowships; PhD holders may request up to six months without additional funding

scholarships.deadline: Applications are open from 20 August 2026. Applications are submitted to the applicant's Swiss diplomatic representation, and the deadline is set country by country: information on application deadlines and scholarship opportunities by country of origin is published by the Federal Commission in August each year.
scholarships.description: The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are awarded annually by the Swiss Confederation to encourage international exchange and research cooperation between Switzerland and more than 180 other countries. Recipients are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS, also known as ESKAS), an independent decentralised federal body that is not bound by directives. The programme has two components: research scholarships for talented early career researchers from abroad who have already completed a Master's degree, and art scholarships for students from a limited number of countries wishing to pursue an initial Master's degree in an artistic field in Switzerland. Applicants are aged 35 or less and the scholarship pays CHF 2,450 per month.
scholarships.duration: Research fellowships: maximum 12 months (minimum 6 months), no extension possible, start 1 September 2027. PhD scholarships: 12 months, renewable twice for up to 36 months subject to academic progress, start 1 September 2027.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Applications open on 20 August 2026, country-specific deadlines apply between August and December 2026, and the Federal Commission announces its award decisions by the end of May at the latest for the following academic year.

Official phishing warning: the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation warns against fake Swiss Government scholarship offers sent by e-mail or published on social media, and the application for a Swiss Government Scholarship is free of charge.

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)

applicant_utility.summary: There is no SEMP application you file yourself: your route runs through your home institution's International Relations Office, which nominates you, sets its own deadline and often its own restrictions, so the first step is asking that office what agreements and criteria it actually has. A SEMP grant is partial by design, so plan a semester budget around CHF 1,430 to CHF 3,900 for European outgoing mobility, CHF 1,750 to CHF 5,000 worldwide, or CHF 1,430 to CHF 4,500 if you are coming into Switzerland, and remember that study fees at the host institution are waived rather than reimbursed. Time your planning around the 60-day minimum and 12-month maximum stay, and get the learning agreement validated before you leave.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled bachelor's, master's or PhD students at a Swiss or partner institution who already have, or can create, an interinstitutional agreement with a host where credits will transfer.
application_readiness_checklist: Email your home institution's International Relations Office first and ask for its SEMP deadlines, partner list and internal restrictions
Confirm your home and host institutions have a current interinstitutional agreement covering your destination
Get the learning agreement signed by the sending institution, the receiving institution and yourself before departure
Book travel by train, bus or car sharing if you want the extra CHF 100 sustainable-mobility contribution, which is only paid if you actually travel that way
Check whether your institution restricts SEMP grants to mobilities within Europe or blocks mobility to your country of origin
If you have a disability or a physical, mental or chronic illness, start the special-needs application about two months before departure
common_rejection_risks: No interinstitutional agreement between your home and host institutions, which is a hard eligibility condition
Courses at the host that will not count towards your degree, since ECTS or equivalent recognition is required
A stay under 60 days or over 12 months
Missing your home institution's internal deadline, which is the only deadline that governs your application
Applying to a destination your institution has no partnership with, or to your own country of origin where that restriction is applied
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The gap between the grant and your real cost of living abroad, since the grant contributes to travel and accommodation but does not cover full living costs; insurance and any costs above the CHF 12,000 special-needs ceiling are also yours.
document_audit: The learning agreement must be validated in advance by both institutions, so do not travel on the assumption it can be signed later
The Declaration of Honour for student mobility is prepared and finalised by the Swiss institution before the mobility period, so confirm who is drafting it
Special-needs grants need actual documented costs, so keep receipts and requirements notes
alerts: Switzerland is planned to join Erasmus+ from 2027, so the next call is likely to be launched under Erasmus+ and the current SEMP rules may change
Grants are always paid by the institution, never to you, so payment timing depends on your institution's administration
Some institutions only fund mobilities within Europe, so worldwide destinations are not universally available
For institutions the funding period starts on 1 June, which shapes when institutional money is available for your stay
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Home institution's International Relations Office nominates and selects you, validates the learning agreement, then the Swiss home or host institution applies for and pays out the grant.

scholarships.deadline: There is no central student deadline. Participants apply through their home institution's International Relations Office and the deadline is set by that institution. For institutions, accreditation and funding applications can be submitted annually at the beginning of March and the funding period starts on 1 June of the year of application. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
scholarships.description: The Swiss-European Mobility Programme is Switzerland's national mobility programme for higher education and forms part of the Swiss solution to the EU's Erasmus+ programme. Funded by SERI and implemented by the Swiss agency Movetia, it enables officially accredited Swiss higher education institutions and colleges of higher education to send their students and staff abroad (outgoing) and to host students and staff from abroad (incoming). Students, including PhD students, spend one or two semesters at a partner higher education institution and keep their enrolment at home, earning ECTS credits; they do not pay study fees abroad and receive financial support for travelling and accommodation.
scholarships.duration: 2 to 12 months per mobility (a stay must last between 60 days and 12 months); one or two semesters for study mobility
scholarships.application_period: Annual institutional cycle: applications from accredited institutions each March, funding period from 1 June. Student-level applications run year-round through the home institution's own deadlines. Movetia expects the next call to be launched under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned association from 2027.
scholarships.official_source: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI), Switzerland - implemented by Movetia
eligibility: Enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or college of higher education in Switzerland or abroad; PhD students included
Stay lasting between 60 days and 12 months
Interinstitutional agreement between the home and host institutions

Funding applicants are officially recognised Swiss higher education institutions, or colleges of higher education with federally recognised courses, holding a SEMP Charter or an ECHE.

scholarships.selection_notes: Participants are selected by their home institution through fair and transparent selection procedures and criteria; each institution sets its own participation criteria, and some award SEMP grants only for mobilities within Europe. Institutions may also apply internal restrictions, for example no mobility to the applicant's country of origin for foreign nationals, language skills, or mobility duration.
scholarships.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+
scholarships.notes: SEMP funds four mobility types under one annual application: semesters abroad for students (Student Mobility for Studies), traineeships abroad for students (Student Mobility for Traineeships), training activities for staff in higher education, and teaching assignments for staff in higher education. Grants are always paid out by the Swiss home or host institution, never directly to the participant. In 2024 the Swiss solution enabled more than 17,000 participants from Switzerland and Europe to supplement their education or training with a stay abroad.

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland

applicant_utility.summary: There is no application you can send to Movetia: for incoming mobility your first email must go to the International Relations Office of the Swiss institution you want to attend, because only that office can submit the SEMP grant and pay it out. Check before anything else that your home university already has an interinstitutional agreement with that Swiss institution, since no agreement means no funding regardless of your grades. Expect the grant to sit somewhere between CHF 1,430 and CHF 4,500 for a European stay, or up to CHF 5,000 for worldwide mobility, and note that your tuition at the Swiss host is waived.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students already enrolled at a university abroad whose institution has a Swiss partner and who can spare one or two semesters without paying Swiss tuition.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the International Relations Office of your target Swiss institution and ask whether they participate in SEMP, hold an agreement with your home university, and what their internal deadline is
Confirm with your home institution's international office that they will nominate you and that the planned courses will be credited towards your degree
Plan a stay of at least 60 days and no more than 12 months, and check the maximum number of students your destination accepts
Ask the Swiss office whether they restrict SEMP grants to European destinations only, since that internal rule varies by institution
If you qualify for the special-needs grant, start the note of requirements with the Swiss office well before departure
common_rejection_risks: No interinstitutional agreement between your home and the Swiss host institution, which disqualifies the mobility outright
Choosing a Swiss institution that is not SEMP-accredited or simply does not pay out incoming grants
Missing the Swiss host institution's own internal deadline, which is set locally and is not published by Movetia
Planning a stay shorter than 60 days or longer than 12 months
Assuming the grant covers your whole budget: it is travel and accommodation support, not a living allowance for a full Swiss semester
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Swiss cost of living beyond the travel and accommodation contribution, health insurance and any visa fees, plus the CHF 100 sustainable-travel element only arrives if you actually travel by train, bus or car sharing.
document_audit: The note of requirements for a special-needs grant must reflect actual costs and is handled through the Swiss international office, not through Movetia directly
Do not send documents to Movetia at all; the Swiss host institution holds the file
Keep proof that the courses you plan to take will be credited towards your home degree, as this is a published condition

The SEMP Call 2026 is shortened to 1 June 2026 - 31 August 2027, which compresses the window in which mobilities can be funded
Each Swiss institution sets its own criteria and deadlines, and some fund only European destinations
Insurance and visa fees are at your own expense
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You approach the Swiss host institution's International Relations Office; your home institution nominates you; the Swiss office submits and pays the grant.

scholarships.deadline: There is no central deadline for individual students: applications are handled by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which sets its own dates. At institutional level, accreditation and funding applications go to Movetia annually in early March for a funding period starting 1 June. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
scholarships.description: Incoming mobility to Switzerland is funded under the Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP), the higher education part of the Swiss Programme for Erasmus+ that Switzerland operates in place of Erasmus+ association. Students from abroad, including PhD students, can spend one or two semesters at a Swiss university or college of higher education, or do a traineeship in Switzerland, while remaining enrolled at their home institution and earning ECTS credits. They do not pay study fees at the Swiss host institution and receive a financial contribution towards travel and accommodation. Applications are coordinated by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which is the only party that can receive and pay out the grant.
scholarships.duration: 2 to 12 months per mobility (minimum 60 days); one or two semesters for study mobility; traineeships of at least 60 days
scholarships.application_period: Annual institutional cycle with applications each March and a funding period from 1 June; student-level applications run through the Swiss host institution's own deadlines. Movetia expects the next call to be launched under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned participation from 2027.

Swiss SEMP institutions apply their own transparent selection criteria and may restrict SEMP grants to certain destinations.

scholarships.notes: Switzerland is not associated to the Erasmus+ 2021-2027 programme; the funding for incoming mobility comes from the Swiss solution to Erasmus+, administered by Movetia on behalf of SERI. scholarships.title: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) - Turkish Government Scholarship
scholarships.name: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) - Turkish Government Scholarship

applicant_utility.summary: This is a placement scholarship, not a pick-your-university fellowship: you rank up to 12 university and department options in TBBS and YTB decides where you go, so read the programme descriptions of every option before you rank them. Budget your effort around three gates - the file screening in March-April, a 30-question quantitative test and a face-to-face interview between April and June, and results only in early August, which leaves barely a month before the September transfer to Turkiye. The stipend differs sharply by level (6,500 TL undergraduate, 9,500 TL master's, 13,000 TL PhD), so the same award is worth very different things depending on which programme you land in.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong all-round applicants with community or social activity track records who are comfortable being placed at a university they did not choose, including those who want a free Turkish year.
application_readiness_checklist: Open TBBS and check which universities and departments the system actually offers for your educational background before drafting anything
Verify that the field you want is recognised and equivalent in your own country, as YTB explicitly warns about this
Prepare the research proposal and a written sample of prior research if you are applying at PhD level
Rank your 12 choices honestly - the system only lets you choose what is offered, and placement, not preference, decides your university
Book interview availability for April-June and be ready to bring original certificates to the interview
common_rejection_risks: Missing or unreadable uploads: the preliminary assessment screens on minimum academic achievement, age limits and required documents before anyone reads your motivation
Choosing health sciences, which the programme explicitly does not fund
Weak consistency between your ranked choices, your letter of intent and your career goals, which the Expert Committee scores directly
Failing the 30-question quantitative test or the interview, which are held in person by the Presidential Delegations
Assuming an English-medium placement without the language certificate the chosen university requires
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond tuition, dormitory accommodation, the monthly stipend, insurance and the two flights: personal spending, transport within Turkiye, additional travel home, and any costs tied to the university you are placed at.
document_audit: The photograph must have been taken within the last year, and the identity document must be valid at application time
A temporary graduation certificate is accepted in place of a diploma, but it must be uploaded - not promised later
National exam results are only required 'if any', but international exam results become mandatory when the chosen university or programme demands them
PhD files need two separate items: a proposal for the research topic and a written example of research already carried out
alerts: The application window is short and fixed (10 January - 20 February); there is no rolling entry for the full-time programmes
Results arrive in early August and grantees transfer to Turkiye in September, so visa and travel planning must start before the award letter
The Merit Scholarship Program doubles the monthly stipend but is judged on GPA plus ALES/GRE/SAT and TOEFL/IELTS thresholds, which must already exist at application time
Research Scholarships and the Success Scholarship run entirely separate calendars, including a Success window in October-November
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online only, through TBBS: register, upload documents, rank up to 12 offered options, then sit the test and in-person interview if shortlisted.

scholarships.deadline: 10 January - 20 February each year for the full-time programmes (associate, bachelor's, master's, PhD and art scholarships); the 2026 window ran 10 January - 20 February 2026 and the 2027 dates have not been separately announced
scholarships.description: Türkiye Bursları is the Republic of Türkiye's government-funded, competitive scholarship programme for international students, run under the coordination of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Relatives of Overseas Citizens (YTB). It funds associate, bachelor's, master's, PhD and research places at the most prestigious Turkish universities and is distinctive in providing university and department placement rather than a fellowship to be spent at a chosen institution. The package covers tuition, a monthly stipend, health insurance, accommodation, a one-year Turkish language course, a once-off return flight ticket and free academic and cultural programmes. Applications are submitted online, free of charge, through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS).
scholarships.duration: One year of free Turkish language education before or alongside the degree programme; associate degree is a two-year programme, with bachelor's, master's and PhD programmes of standard length. Research Scholarships have their own application periods.
scholarships.application_period: One annual period each year: 10 January to 20 February for international applicants, for associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral scholarships. Research Scholarships run on separate, individually announced periods.

scholarships.eligibility_summary: The programme is competitive and merit-based with a strong emphasis on academic excellence. scholarships.name: Global Scholars Program Scholarship (Clark University)

applicant_utility.summary: Everything hinges on the extra essay: the other three international first-year merit scholarships are automatic, but the Global Scholars Program Scholarship is invisible to the committee unless that essay is in, so treat it as a second mini-application rather than an afterthought. Apply by 1 November rather than 15 January if you can, because Clark gives Early Decision applicants more scholarship funding and a higher admission rate. Be realistic about the gap: Clark publishes a total cost of attendance of about $85,000 and says international students typically pay around $40,000 a year after aid, and it will deny an application outright if the need you declare is larger than what it can fund.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants from outside the U.S. with a documented record of community leadership who can either self-fund a substantial share or qualify for significant need-based aid.

Book the optional interview; it doubles as supplementary proof of English proficiency
Open the applicant status portal as soon as you have applied and complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form
Confirm which need-based application Clark wants from you this cycle (CSS Profile or the international certification form), because Clark's own pages disagree
Check that your transcripts cover three complete years, adding a middle school transcript if your country uses a 6-3-3 system
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the application without the Global Scholars essay, which removes you from this award entirely

Incomplete transcripts - Clark states it cannot review an application with only two years of credentials
Leaving the certification of finances form late, since it only appears in the portal after you apply
Assuming a U.S. mailbox or an interview replaces the required English test evidence
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Against a published total cost of attendance of about $85,000 per year, international students typically still pay around $40,000 a year after scholarships and aid; on-campus work is limited and cannot cover a significant share, and U.S. rules bar off-campus employment.

alerts: Need-aware admission means your funding request can decide the admission outcome, not just the award size
Early Decision is binding and Early Action is not - only Early Decision guarantees a decision and award before Thanksgiving

Clark also runs a Presidential Scholarship covering tuition, room and board for 3-5 students a year with no separate application, so your file is competing on two essay-optional and essay-required tracks at once

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One Common App submission by the round deadline, plus the Global Scholars essay and the portal certification form; the scholarship committee then reviews the whole file and no separate award application exists.

scholarships.name: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT) — MAECI / ICE / Uni-Italia scholarship programme
scholarships.funding_period: per academic year (9 months of study), paid quarterly

applicant_utility.summary: This MAECI-run scholarship pays EUR 10,800 across nine months for an English-taught Master's or postgraduate course in Italy, but it only works if you have already applied and been admitted to a course on the official IYT list. Flights, accommodation, health insurance, the regional right-to-education tax and stamp duty stay on your own budget, and you cannot switch courses after applying. With 211 scholarships against 1,634 applications in the 11th edition, the university pre-admission step is the real bottleneck to plan around.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates aged 25 or under from the 22 partner countries who hold a completed bachelor's and are applying for an English-taught Italian Master's in engineering, economics/management or architecture/design.

Shoot and edit a 59-second MP4 video under 10 MB, ideally in Italian for extra evaluation points
Get official translations stamped if your diploma and transcripts are not in English, French or Spanish, and keep every other PDF under 1 MB
Register on My-App with your exact passport names and complete the upload well before the 6:00 pm Italian-time cutoff
common_rejection_risks: Applying while still finishing your degree - students about to graduate are explicitly excluded
Name mismatch between the portal registration and the passport machine-readable line
Submitting multiple applications from different email addresses, which are strictly prohibited
Any missing document at the deadline - incomplete files are simply ineligible and documents cannot be emailed afterwards
Choosing a course outside the IYT list, or a second course when your first choice is not limited-enrolment
Holding another Italian government scholarship such as Erasmus+ or a regional scholarship, which is incompatible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Return flights to Italy, accommodation for the full stay, private health and accident insurance, regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, visa costs and everyday living expenses beyond the EUR 10,800.

The second preference on limited-enrolment courses is binding - you cannot choose between the two courses after admission
If you switch to the self-study Italian route, attach an online placement test result showing your CEFR level

scholarships.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy is a MAECI scholarship programme run with the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia that pays a nine-month scholarship to foreign students from 22 partner countries to attend a Master's or Postgraduate course at a participating Italian university, combined with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association. Courses are taught entirely in English, and the programme includes study of Italian language and culture plus a mandatory gender-equality and anti-gender-violence seminar or module. The winner receives an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800, paid quarterly into an Italian bank account in the holder's name, and is exempt from enrolment fees and university contributions, but must still pay the regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, accident and civil liability insurance and health insurance. The scholarship explicitly does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance.

scholarships.title: ARES Scholarships - Bourses de formations internationales (scholarships for study in Belgium)
scholarships.name: ARES Scholarships - Bourses de formations internationales (scholarships for study in Belgium)

applicant_utility.summary: The decisive filter here is not academic but professional: ARES wants someone who already holds a relevant higher education diploma no older than 20 years and has at least two years of relevant work in one of the 32 partner countries, so recent graduates with no work history are excluded before anyone reads a transcript. Applications run through GIRAF, the form opens only once, and once you press submit the file is frozen, so assemble everything - including evidence of your professional experience - before you start typing. Only ten programmes were on offer for 2027-2028, so the choice of programme is effectively the choice of scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from an ARES partner country who already hold a relevant diploma and want a one-year specialised degree in Belgium with a development focus.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is one of the 32 partner countries and that you hold permanent residency and work there
Count the years since your diploma: it must be no more than 20 years at the start of the training, with one extra year per childbirth or adoption
Document at least two years of relevant professional experience in an eligible country, after your last diploma and before the call closes
Request or check your GIRAF account early, since ARES must validate it before you can open the form
Download the reference document of the call and the applicant's guide, and read the admission conditions of the specific programme before committing
common_rejection_risks: Applying straight after graduation: the two-year professional experience requirement is the most discriminating condition
A diploma older than the 20-year limit with no childbirth or adoption adjustment
Residence or work outside the 32 eligible countries (the only exception is Palestinian nationality)
Submitting an incomplete or imperfect file, since the application cannot be modified after submission
Choosing a programme whose own admission conditions you do not meet
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: ARES does not publish the amount of the subsistence allowance, so the personal share is unknown in advance; only travel, insurance, tuition (for degree tracks) and small capped extras are covered, and the visa allowance is capped at EUR 200 inside the subsistence allowance.
document_audit: Visa costs above EUR 200 are reimbursed only on actual costs with supporting documents, so keep every receipt

Professional experience must be evidenced for a period after the last diploma, not merely claimed in the form
The application form can be opened only once - do not click the button to explore it
alerts: The 2027-2028 call closed on 18 September 2026; the next one opens in August 2027, so a missed window costs a full year
Applying is free: ARES warns that anyone asking for payment by email while claiming to act for ARES should be reported to scholarships-cooperation@ares-ac.be
Award holders commit to returning to their country or another country and using the training for development purposes, with a multiplier effect
Appeals against the selection decision can be lodged with the Belgian Council of State
The continuing-education track works differently: no tuition coverage, a monthly allowance for the course duration and a fixed EUR 200 travel costs allowance instead
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: GIRAF account validated by ARES, then one submission of the International Training application form during the August-September window; selection follows per programme.

scholarships.description: ARES, the Walloon agency for international cooperation and education, awards scholarships so that professionals from its partner countries can study in Wallonia, in institutions of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. The 'bourses de formations internationales' cover a one-year bachelor of specialisation (bachelier de spécialisation), a specialised master's degree (master de spécialisation) or a short continuing-education course of up to six months, with study programmes that address development-related issues. The scholarship is aimed at people who are permanent residents and working in one of ARES's partner countries and who already hold a higher education diploma. For the 2026-2027 call 200 scholarships were available; for 2027-2028 the call offered one bachelor of specialisation, eight specialised master's degrees and one continuing-education certificate. Applications are submitted through the GIRAF platform and the selection is run by a jury for each programme.
scholarships.duration: Specialised bachelor's and specialised master's degrees: 12 months maximum (one academic year). Continuing training: 6 months maximum.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle: the call opens in early August and applications close in mid-September, with preselection and selection running from October to May and results in June

Insurance costs paid directly by ARES

scholarships.name: Boren Scholarships and Fellowships (National Security Education Program)
scholarships.funding_period: maximum award determined by duration abroad

applicant_utility.summary: Boren is a service-linked study-abroad grant rather than a general scholarship, so everything hinges on a credible national-security argument for your language and destination plus a concrete plan for the one-year federal service obligation. Target the $25,000 tier by designing a programme of at least 25 weeks that keeps 15-20 weekly classroom language hours at its core; shorter stays pay strictly less and duration bands are never rounded up. Budget against the eligible-cost list: the grant covers approved tuition, housing and food, Fly America airfare, insurance and visa costs, while passports, medical costs, a personal laptop, dependents and personal travel stay on you. Engage your campus representative early, because many campuses run internal deadlines that fall weeks before the January national deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. citizen undergraduates and graduate students who are certain about a federal national-security career and can accept a one-year federal service obligation after graduation.
application_readiness_checklist: Find out whether your institution has a Boren campus representative and an internal deadline, and plan around the earlier of the two dates.
Map your proposed programme against the preferred language, destination and duration lists (25+ weeks) before locking in a provider.
Line up referees early and share essay drafts with them before the January deadline.
Check the French/Spanish proficiency rules if either is your target language, and keep testing verification in mind.
Prepare a signed matriculation form or a dean/registrar letter proving you will still be enrolled when the programme ends.
If you are a Fellow proposing research or internships abroad, request host affiliation letters now rather than later.
common_rejection_risks: A weak or generic national-security rationale for the chosen language and destination.
Proposing a programme shorter than the preferred 25 weeks without a compelling justification.
Letting English-taught coursework dominate a programme that must keep 15-20 weekly language hours at its core.
Failing to show a realistic, specific path to the one-year federal service requirement.
Missing a campus internal deadline while focused on the national one.
Ignoring destination restrictions (Western Europe, Canada, Australia, New Zealand) or an approved-destination asterisk without naming a viable backup.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Passport fees, medical expenses including inoculations, copays, treatment, prescriptions and COVID testing, a personal laptop, dependent expenses, personal travel and entertainment, and U.S.-side personal costs such as car payments, student loan payments, personal taxes or U.S. housing.
document_audit: Programme selections made in the application can only be adjusted within the same language and country at roughly the same weekly language intensity.
Recommendations must come from referees named in your application, so brief them before your essays are final.
Fellows attaching research, internship or extra coursework need host affiliation letters to make the plan credible.
Arabic, Mandarin or Russian proposals in starred destinations must include a viable alternate programme in an unrestricted destination.
Home-institution matriculation fees are capped at $2,500 per semester ($5,000 overall) - check whether your programme charges more.
Keep proof of any other aid you receive; overlapping support reduces your Boren award dollar for dollar.
alerts: Duration bands are firm: 24 weeks plus a few days does not round up to the 25-week/$25,000 award.
Funding for programme expenses after 31 May 2028 is contingent on availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award.
Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand are permanently ineligible destinations.
Study tours of several countries, such as a semester at sea, are not eligible for funding.
Other financial aid applied to the same costs must be reported and may reduce the grant; student loans will not.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online application at apply.iie.org, submit by the national deadline (Fellowships 20 January 2027; Scholarships 27 January 2027, 5pm Eastern) plus any earlier campus deadline, and expect selection news in mid-to-late April.

Applicants are notified of selection in mid-to-late April.
scholarships.description: The National Security Education Program awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service. Boren Scholarships fund study abroad by U.S. undergraduates and Boren Fellowships fund research and language study proposals by U.S. graduate students, in world regions critical to U.S. interests. Maximum awards are determined by duration abroad: $25,000 for 25-52 weeks (preferred), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, and $8,000 for 8-11 weeks for STEM majors under the Scholarships programme. There are no minimum language requirements except French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America. The Boren Awards are an initiative of the Defense Language and National Security Education Office.

applicant_utility.summary: Kyushu University's Friendship Scholarship pays JPY 80,000 a month to non-Japanese students from overseas universities who come to Kyushu U as special auditing, special research or double-degree students and cannot fund the stay themselves. There is no central application: your prospective host department applies on your behalf during one of two annual recruitment rounds, around February for April-September starts and around May for October-March starts. The published central rules cap your combined scholarship income at JPY 80,000 a month, so this award generally cannot be stacked with JASSO for the same months. Treat tuition and flights as your own cost unless your host department confirms a fee waiver under your exchange agreement.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Japanese students at overseas universities, with or without an exchange agreement with Kyushu U, heading to Kyushu for a 3, 5 or 11-month special auditing, special research or double-degree stay, with strong grades (coefficient 2.30 or higher) and genuine financial need.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your prospective Kyushu U host department months ahead of the round; the department, not the International Student Center, runs the application
Confirm in writing which description of the Friendship Scholarship applies in your department (monthly amount, stay length, any fee waiver) before relying on it
Verify your stay is 3, 5 or 11 months and starts within the Japanese academic year
Obtain written confirmation from your home university that you will return to complete your degree or graduate
Check your previous-year grade evaluation coefficient (JASSO calculation method) is at least 2.30 on the 3-point scale
Declare any other scholarships you hold; the combined monthly total may not exceed JPY 80,000
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to the International Student Center instead of through the prospective host department
A previous-year grade evaluation coefficient below 2.30
A stay shorter than 3 months, longer than 11 months, or beginning outside the academic year
Holding another scholarship that pushes the combined monthly total over JPY 80,000
Being on track to complete a regular course of study at Kyushu U rather than returning to the home university, or being scheduled to withdraw or be expelled
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International flights to and from Fukuoka, Kyushu University tuition, examination and matriculation fees unless waived under your exchange agreement, housing deposits and initial setup, and national health insurance enrolment; none of these are covered by the central published rules.
document_audit: The university publishes no central document list, so ask your host department for the exact checklist in writing (request English wording if you need it)
Expect to evidence the financial-hardship claim, your eligibility for Student status of residence, your home-university enrolment and your return commitment
Home-university transcripts and certificates may need Japanese or English preparation depending on what the department requires
Keep the Kyushu U acceptance or exchange-eligibility letter together with your home university's return confirmation, as the two are checked against each other
alerts: Kyushu University publishes more than one description of a scholarship with this name across its sites; do not rely on any faculty-level amount, stay length or fee-waiver wording until your host department confirms it applies to you
The combined-scholarship cap means this award usually cannot run alongside JASSO for the same months, which matters if you were counting on both

Students who finish a regular course of study at Kyushu U, or who are scheduled to withdraw or be expelled, are excluded; the award is meant for students who return home
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You never submit centrally: your prospective host department collects and submits the application during Period I (around February) or Period II (around May), and the university then decides.

It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 80,000, and the total of all scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed that amount. Applicants apply through their prospective host department at Kyushu University, not directly to the university centre. There are two recruitment periods per fiscal year: Period I around February for students who will study from April to September, and Period II around May for students who will study from October to March. The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters).

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this scholarship until you hold a Leeds offer, and you must submit a separate scholarship application for each course you hold an offer for - applicants with multiple offers who file once quietly lose consideration on the others. The award is a first-year tuition discount of £3,000, £6,000 or £16,000 with the final value decided by the University, so treat £16,000 as the ceiling rather than the expectation. Round one on 28 February 2027 is the better target since unsuccessful round-one applicants roll into later rounds anyway, and note that the money cannot touch maintenance or accommodation - you still need a full living-cost plan.

Being UK fee-status classified, which excludes you from this international scheme

applicant_utility.summary: The Max Weber Fellowship is a residential one- to two-year postdoc at the EUI near Florence paying EUR 2,500 a month plus health insurance, EUR 1,500 of research funds and travel reimbursement, so living costs are covered but Florence rent on top of the grant remains your own. Only about 2% of applicants receive an offer while another 5-10% sit on the reserve list, so a rejected application is not a verdict on your profile and reapplying next cycle is common. The 16 October 2026, 14:00 CEST deadline applies to your referees' letters too, which is where otherwise strong applications fail.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fresh PhDs in history, law, economics, political and social sciences or transnational governance who want a residential European research post and an academic career.
application_readiness_checklist: Register on the OSIRIS portal (MWP-APPLY) as soon as the call opens, since referees can only upload after you register
Line up two or three academic referees, exclude current EUI professors, and confirm in person that they received the automated request
Write the two-page research proposal with realistic 12- and 24-month phasing plus the required gender-and-diversity reflection
Draft the one-page academic career statement against the programme's Academic Practice activities, and tighten the CV around the publication list
Check your PhD date against the five-year window and, for a 2027-28 start, ensure the defence falls by 31/12/2027
common_rejection_risks: Reference letters arriving after the deadline, which are never accepted
A research proposal whose goals cannot realistically fit a 12-month fellowship
Weak mentor fit with the hosting unit, since mentorship capacity is a formal selection criterion
Applying while still enrolled in or employed by the EUI without a full year away
Letting generative AI write substantial parts of the statements, against the EUI's GenAI guidelines
Disclosing other grants or salary late, which triggers a grant reduction to a minimum of 1,750 EUR per month
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Florence rent and daily living costs beyond the EUR 2,500 grant, removal or installation expenses (explicitly not provided), travel for family members, and any personal tax obligations the Institute does not cover.
document_audit: Passport copy must be JPEG while the CV, career statement and research proposal must be standard-font PDFs without macros, special characters or password protection

scholarships.title: EASL Mobility / Research Fellowship Programme
scholarships.name: EASL Mobility / Research Fellowship Programme

applicant_utility.summary: EASL funds up to EUR 25,000 for a six-month liver-disease project, with just 3 awards per round, and the money is budgeted as salary or living costs, travel and accommodation (mobility route only), lab consumables and equipment, other logistics including childcare, plus attendance at a future EASL Congress. Because the review is a 100-point grid where scientific/clinical merit alone carries 35% and the host-institution environment carries another 15%, the strongest applications are genuinely two-way partnerships: a sharply feasible hepatology question that a named lab has agreed to host. Only active EASL members can open the portal, so treat the membership payment as a precondition, not an afterthought - trainee and postdoc membership is EUR 50, regular is EUR 250, and membership runs for 12 months from the date of payment. The 2026 window ran 15 July to 1 September 2026 and has closed, so plan for the same mid-summer opening next year rather than waiting for the call to appear.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early- to mid-career hepatology researchers and clinicians at a European institution who want a six-month placement in another European lab (mobility) or funding for a focused project at their own (research).
application_readiness_checklist: Create or renew the EASL membership first and keep the payment confirmation date in mind - membership is valid for 12 months from payment, so a lapsed renewal blocks portal access on deadline day
Secure the host lab agreement in writing before drafting: mobility applicants need a signed host-institute letter confirming the ability to host, capped at 1 page
Build the budget in the four published cost lines (travel/accommodation, salary/living, lab supplies and equipment, other logistics including childcare) and reserve money for EASL Congress attendance
Record and cut the 3-minute motivation video well before the closing week - it carries 20% of the score and is the only criterion a panel judges on your behalf if motivation scores weakly elsewhere
Ask the supervisor or mentor for the 1-page recommendation letter early, since it must be attached to the same submission
Rehearse a one-sentence liver-disease relevance statement; alignment with EASL's mission and impact on liver disease research is 15% of the score
common_rejection_risks: Proposing work that is only tangentially about liver disease - relevance to hepatology is a scored 15% block and the programme exists expressly to advance liver research
A weak or absent host-institution fit: the environment criterion is 15% and the panel judges whether the host can actually supply the training and resources the proposal assumes
Requesting costs outside the published budget categories, or asking for the full EUR 25,000 without a defensible line-by-line justification - the award is capped, not guaranteed

A route mismatch: research-fellowship motivation claims are only scored for that route, and mobility-only documents such as the host letter will be missing or misapplied if the wrong fellowship type is chosen
Over-length submissions: 5 pages for the proposal, 4 for the CV, 1 for the recommendation and 1 for the host letter are hard ceilings, not targets
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything not in the four budget lines: tuition or course fees are not covered, institutional overheads and bench fees outside the negotiated budget are not covered, visa and insurance costs are not itemised, and the grant only funds attendance at a future EASL Congress rather than other conferences. With only three awards per round, most applicants receive nothing regardless of quality.
document_audit: The budget template is described as 'download budget template' on the public page but the link is not live there - locate the current template through the Memberzone or the EASL office (easloffice@easloffice.eu) before the window closes, because a submission with an ad-hoc budget sheet instead of the template risks being discounted
The motivation video is an elevator pitch, not a research summary; a 3-minute file is easy to overrun, so time the final cut rather than assuming the recorder kept it to length
The 1-page host letter and the 1-page recommendation letter are separate documents - a single combined letter does not satisfy either requirement
The CV cap of 4 pages is strict; tailor it to hepatology research experience rather than pasting a complete publication list
alerts: Only 3 awards are made per round, so treat this as a competitive small-grant prize rather than a broadly available funding line
The award is 'up to EUR 25,000' and varies with host location, travel costs and research needs - do not plan the budget against the maximum
The window is short and seasonal (15 July - 1 September), roughly six weeks, which is tight for securing a host letter and editing a video
Mobility applications are scored with a preference for moves that create institutional collaboration and knowledge exchange, and preference may be given to Inclusiveness Target Countries
EASL membership is a hard gate, and the membership fee is paid by the applicant and is non-refundable
Award notifications land roughly two to three months after the deadline (November 2026 for the last round), so have a fallback funding plan for the start of the year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Log into the EASL Memberzone while the window is open, complete the online fellowship form, and upload the proposal, motivation video, CV, recommendation letter, host letter (mobility only) and budget template as attachments before the 1 September cut-off.

scholarships.title: Doctoral Scholarships — Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German Academic Scholarship Foundation)
scholarships.name: Doctoral Scholarships — Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German Academic Scholarship Foundation)

applicant_utility.summary: The call is open only from 1 to 14 October 2026 and there is no online route - the complete pack must arrive by post inside those 14 days, and an incomplete or late pack is simply not considered. The published funding is EUR 1,750 per month plus a research cost allowance of up to EUR 100 per month paid at year end, with a health insurance contribution of up to EUR 170 per month where your insurance is not covered by employment. Plan around the fixed calendar: the October call feeds a selection meeting in May 2027 with the earliest scholarship start on 1 July 2027, so avoid any career or relocation commitments before the award letter. Remember that a rejection is final and you cannot resubmit or send updated documents during the process.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral candidates at German universities whose last degree is no older than four years and three months, who can evidence top-15-percent performance and sustained social engagement, and who have a full-time project completable within three years.
application_readiness_checklist: Ask your formal first reviewer - not your day-to-day supervisor - to complete the supervisor questionnaire early; the English version is available on the website and a supplementary questionnaire from the second reviewer is welcome.
Request an ECTS ranking or grade classification table from your university for the qualifying degree; without it, reviewers cannot judge the cohort position.

Draft the exposé to the prescribed structure (working title, abstract, key terms, introduction, research question, research status, methods and provisional structure, schedule, references) in German or English within the 20-page limit.
Name four or more eligible reviewers on the official proposal form and do not contact them yourself - the foundation does that.
Print the pack single-sided without staples, clips or folders and post it well inside the 14-day window, since only complete applications received during the call count.
If you hold EU plus non-EU citizenship, complete the declaration on security-relevant aspects anyway; the selection cannot proceed without it.
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete pack or documents arriving after the 14-day window - only complete applications received during a call are included.
Exposé missing, in another language, or over the 20-page limit; the pre-selection does not assess it, but the academic review stage does.
Supervisor questionnaire completed by the wrong person - it must be the first reviewer assessing the thesis.
Application at an advanced stage of the doctorate, since funding for completion is not the primary focus and such applications are generally not considered.
Most recent degree older than four years and three months without documented grounds; professional qualification periods such as legal or teacher training do not extend the deadline.
Part-time doctoral study, or a parallel taught degree/professional training, which is incompatible with the funding.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: There is no institutional insurance cover - only the 50 percent contribution capped at EUR 170 per month where insurance is not covered by employment; no thesis printing or publishing allowance is paid; travel to any in-person interview is at your own cost (interviews are usually video calls).
document_audit: The CV is required in both chronological and narrative format - one format alone is incomplete.

If you have not yet graduated, submit the transcript of all completed degree courses plus a ranking of performance to date; the final certificate and full transcript must follow before final consideration.
The thesis summary of the last qualifying thesis must stay within two or three pages.
Dual nationals must still submit the security-relevant declaration, and the selection process cannot proceed without the completed and signed form.
alerts: Funding must start within the period specified in the award letter, otherwise the offer expires - and any other doctoral scholarship must be terminated before the Studienstiftung funding begins.
Periods of other doctoral funding are credited in full against the maximum funding period, which is 42 months (54 with children).
Documents of unsuccessful candidates are not returned, and no individual feedback is given on the decision.
A second application after rejection is only possible with a different supervisor and a different subject; withdrawing during a selection procedure counts as a rejection.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Post the complete pack inside the 14-day call; a formal pre-selection follows after about six weeks; admitted applications receive two written academic reviews plus an interview (usually by video); the selection board decides within the call's schedule.

scholarships.name: HFA Research and Training Grants Programme (Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology)
scholarships.funding_period: per month, maximum EUR 10,000 per award

applicant_utility.summary: Membership is the gate, not the science: you must already be an HFA Member or Fellow when you apply, so join before September rather than planning to join alongside the application. The scoring is unusually transparent - half the marks sit on the project's feasibility and its sustained benefit for cardiovascular disease reduction, a further 20% on World Bank low- or middle-income country citizenship or residence, and only 10% on the host centre - so a modest centre with a strong heart failure question beats a famous centre with a vague one. Build the file around your supervisor: two of the five required uploads are documents they must complete themselves, and they cannot be chased on the last day.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Cardiologists and heart failure researchers under 40 who already hold HFA membership and want a three-month-plus research or clinical training stint in another ESC country.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your HFA membership or Fellowship is active before the window opens in April
Check your age against the deadline date, not the project start date
Choose an ICARe-HF Accredited Centre if you can, or otherwise a centre with a visible track record in your exact topic
Draft the project description with your future supervisor so the three-month minimum is realistic and the feasibility argument is explicit
Ask your current head of department or supervisor for their document early, since it is a required upload
common_rejection_risks: Applying without active HFA membership or Fellowship, which is a hard eligibility condition
Being 40 or older at the application deadline
A project shorter than the three-month minimum
A vague feasibility or impact argument, which carries half the selection score
Holding a permanent, senior staff or consultant post if you apply on the MD route
Choosing a host centre with no track record in the specific topic of the application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The page does not state what the EUR 2,500 monthly payment covers or whether travel and relocation are reimbursed, so assume relocation, flights and any institutional fees come from your own funds.
document_audit: The CV must itemise publications in refereed journals with journal titles, page numbers and co-author names - a bare list of papers is not what the form asks for
The project description must be prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor, so allow time for genuine collaboration
Two separate supervisor documents are required: one from your current head of department or supervisor, one from the future supervisor

applicant_utility.summary: Mobility is the hard filter, not publication count: EMBO will not fund you going back to the country where you did your PhD, to a lab you already worked in for more than six months, or to your PhD supervisor's lab, and the project cannot be a continuation of your doctorate. The money is country-dependent and paid either as an employment contract through your host institution or as a stipend, so a Swiss or Icelandic postdoc is worth roughly double a Bulgarian or Polish one. From Autumn 2027 you only get one shot - re-applications are banned - and from Autumn 2026 each host lab can back only one candidate per round, so agree with your prospective host before you file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A recently graduated life-science PhD with a first-author paper who needs to change both country and research direction and wants a two-year funded postdoc abroad.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the mobility rules first: different country from your PhD, and not your PhD lab, institute, department or supervisor.
Confirm your PhD date: if you already hold it, it must have been awarded within the two years before you submit.
Make sure the project is framed as a new direction, not an extension of your doctoral work.
Agree with your host lab that they will issue an employment contract if you are awarded, and confirm they are not supporting another candidate in the same round.
Have your first-author paper accepted or your preprint with public in-depth peer reviews ready - this is an eligibility criterion, not a nice-to-have.
Submit before the hard cutoff of 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET and plan to start within one calendar year of it.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to return to the country where the PhD was obtained.
Applying to a lab where you already spent more than six months, or to your former PhD supervisor.
A project that reviewers read as a direct continuation of the doctoral work.
Holding the PhD for more than two years at the time of application.
No first-author publication and no preprint with public in-depth peer reviews from an independent service.
Your host laboratory supporting a second candidate in the same round, which forces a withdrawal.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Bench fees, overheads, consumables and any other financial benefit to the host supervisor or receiving institute are explicitly not covered, so the host lab must find its own money for your experiments. Income from the stipend may also be taxable in certain countries, and fellows are responsible for national tax arrangements and their own social security where applicable.
document_audit: The application goes through the EMBO portal, but the host supervisor and host institution confirmation is a separate piece your prospective lab must stand behind.
Your first-author output must be verified as accepted or published - a preprint only counts if it has public in-depth peer reviews from an independent peer review service.
Hosts must agree that the EMBO grant is used to fund an employment contract, which requires their institutional sign-off, not just the supervisor's enthusiasm.
Child daycare and dependent child allowances apply only to non-EMBC fellows, so do not budget on them if your host is in an EMBC Member State.
alerts: From the Autumn 2027 round (applications after 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET) re-applications will no longer be permitted - researchers may submit only one EMBO Fellowship Proposal.
From the Autumn 2026 selection round a host laboratory may support a maximum of one candidate per round, and excess applications will be withdrawn.
Part-time work at 50% or 75% is possible, but total full-time plus part-time duration may not exceed 36 months.
EMBO cannot advise on national tax regulations; contact the tax authorities in your host country.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file one application for one project at one host laboratory through the EMBO portal before the round's hard cutoff, EMBO evaluates project excellence, track record and mobility, and on award EMBO transfers a country-rate grant to the host institution, which issues you an employment contract, or pays you a stipend in non-EMBC countries.
