scholarships.name: Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships

applicant_utility.summary: Both you and your placement must sit inside an EMBC Member State, so this is a European scheme in both directions and cannot be used for a newsroom or lab outside Europe. The money is a daily subsistence rate scaled to the country you are going to - roughly 68 EUR a day in Prague or Warsaw against 140 in Switzerland - plus a travel allowance, so the same fellowship is worth more than twice as much depending on destination. Applications can be filed at any point but must be fully registered in the portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October, and the fellowship cannot be extended, so get the length right the first time.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Working science journalists based in EMBC Member States who want an in-person research sabbatical, and mid-career life scientists with a master's or doctorate who have already begun reporting and want to move into full-time science journalism.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you live in an EMBC Member State and that your proposed host is also in one.
Talk to the proposed host before you apply - formal written acceptance is not needed yet, but prior discussion is.
Pick your length deliberately: three to six months as a journalist, three to twelve as a researcher, with no extension possible.
Write the three-page proposal around concrete learning and knowledge outcomes rather than story ideas you hope to publish.
Assemble three to five published or broadcast samples; blog posts, social posts and academic commentary pieces do not count.
For a researcher-to-journalism switch, secure written confirmation that the placement is a full-time internship in a mainstream media newsroom.
Register the completed application in the EMBO portal well before 23:59 CEST on 30 October.
common_rejection_risks: A placement that is fully virtual rather than in person.
Two or more placements all in the same EMBC Member State, when at least one must be in a different one.
Evidence of journalism consisting of personal blog posts, social media postings, or commentary and review articles in academic journals.
A researcher applicant who cannot show prior reporting on the life sciences or a genuine intention to enter journalism as a profession.
An incomplete application - only fully completed applications are considered.
A proposal that reads as a route to immediate publication opportunities rather than as a sabbatical for learning.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is a daily subsistence rate scaled to the host country plus a travel allowance. Fellows are responsible for their own social security contributions, taxes and any other costs incurred, and there is no tuition or course-fee element.
document_audit: The CV must be in English and must carry a permanent residential address, email and mobile number - a standard academic CV will not do.
Journalist applicants need an explicit statement that the sabbatical is focused on individual learning and that they will not report from the host institution.
Researcher applicants need a separate written confirmation that the placement is a full-time internship in a mainstream media newsroom.
Journalists are additionally expected to attend a two-day workshop at EMBO in Heidelberg, for which travel and accommodation are provided - diarise it.
alerts: Only one selection round a year: registration closes 30 October at 23:59 CEST and outcomes arrive by email by mid-November.
The fellowship cannot be extended, so plan the length of your sabbatical inside the three-to-six or three-to-twelve month bands.
Fellows must not undertake other work during the fellowship and must not report on their host research institution during the term.
The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin, which is worth knowing if you look for prior awardee profiles.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file a complete application through the EMBO portal, it must be registered by 23:59 CEST on 30 October, the EMBO advisory board judges the motivation, proposal quality and learning outcomes, and successful applicants are notified by email by mid-November before organising their own placement on a conditional offer.

applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship is won or lost on the proposal, not on your CV - the Center says explicitly that fellows are chosen on the strength of the project and its supporting documents rather than past achievements. Your project must already be well into the writing stage, with most of the research done, and you must say so in the proposal: proposals that do not address project status and projected timeline are deemed ineligible. It is also a half-salary salary-replacement award, not full funding, and you must be physically resident in Durham for the whole term, so field-work-heavy projects are a poor match. Applications for the 2028-29 year open on 1 July 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and senior humanities scholars with a published monograph or substantial peer-reviewed record and a book project already in draft who can spend a full semester or year in residence.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the five-year clock: your terminal degree must have been awarded no later than 30 September 2022 for the 2028-29 cycle, unless you qualify for the Geiss-Hsu or Quinn fellowships.
Confirm the project is beyond the dissertation and is not creative writing, an edited volume, a primary-source collection or a textbook.
Make sure the project is at an advanced stage with most research complete before you invest in an application.
Draft the 1,000-word proposal so its final paragraph states plainly how much research is done and what you intend to accomplish at the Center.
Cut the CV to four pages focusing on the publication record that positions you for this specific project.
Choose referees who know your work well rather than famous names, and ideally at least one who is outside your own institution.
Confirm you can be continuously in residence in Durham for the full term you request.
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that does not explicitly address project status and projected timeline - the Center deems such proposals ineligible.
A project still in the research phase rather than in the writing phase.
A dissertation derivative, an edited volume, a primary-source collection, a textbook, or fiction or poetry.
A CV longer than four pages, which reviewers may rank lower.

Bibliography is capped at two pages, CV at four pages and the outline at one page; overshooting any of them signals poor self-editing.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a monthly stipend tied to the UMA and to your study level, so the number you should budget with is 16,047.99 MXN a month for a master's and 21,397.32 MXN for a doctorate, not a single figure - and it is refreshed against the February UMA each year for the life of the award. It does not pay tuition, so if your programme charges colegiatura you need another source. The application itself is fully administrative: what sinks applications is an out-of-date CVU, an unsigned CURP e-signature or a missing SNP registration record, not a weak research idea. The window closes on 28 November 2026 at 23:59 local time.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mexican citizens, or foreign nationals legally resident in Mexico, already enrolled in a full-time master's or doctoral programme registered in the Sistema Nacional de Posgrados.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme is registered in the Sistema Nacional de Posgrados and appears on the eligible-programme list for this call.
Update your CVU in the Perfil Unico at rizoma.secihti.mx and validate it before the window closes.
If you held a previous CONAHCyT or SECIHTI scholarship, complete its conclusion formalities first and obtain the Carta de Reconocimiento or Carta de No Adeudo.
Check that your CURP is valid; foreign nationals must keep the CURP on their temporary resident card valid.
Have your SNP registration record and official photo identification ready as separate files.
Sign the application electronically with your CURP e-signature - an unsigned file is not a submission.
After an award is assigned, work through the formalisation guides and register your bank account in Apeiron.
common_rejection_risks: Applying while a previous SECIHTI or CONAHCyT scholarship is still not formally concluded.
A programme that is not registered in the SNP or is not on the eligible list for this call.
An invalid or outdated CURP, especially for foreign nationals whose temporary resident card has expired.
An application left unsigned with the CURP e-signature.
Missing the inconsistency window if you did not meet every requirement during the ordinary period.
For non-schooled (no escolarizado) programmes, applying under the escolarizado rules instead of the parallel Terminos de Referencia B.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees are not covered, and no travel allowance is published. The award is a monthly stipend plus ISSSTE medical service, so enrolment fees, materials and any study-related travel must be met from other income.
document_audit: The CVU lives in the Perfil Unico at rizoma.secihti.mx and must be created, updated or validated - an abandoned draft CVU is the most common silent failure.
Evidence of registration must be the SNP registry record, not a general enrolment letter from the university.
The Carta de Reconocimiento or Carta de No Adeudo is needed from your previous institution or funder, and it takes time to obtain.
The ISSSTE letter is generated through its own guide (Guia para Descarga Carta del ISSSTE) rather than issued automatically.
Bank account registration happens in Apeiron after the award, guided by the Guia para el Registro de Cuenta Bancaria BNP.
alerts: Applications close on 28 November 2026 at 23:59 local Mexico City time; the window opened on 23 February 2026 at 20:00.
The monthly amount is recalculated each February against the UMA in force, so a figure fixed at application time will drift over the life of the scholarship.
The first payment includes retroactivity to the start of the scholarship, and payments continue through intermediate periods that include holidays.
The call, the guides and both the Rizoma and Apeiron systems are Spanish-only, so budget time for that if Spanish is not your working language.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You build and validate your CVU in Rizoma, submit the request with your CURP e-signature before 28 November 2026, SECIHTI assesses eligibility over two periods, and if you are awarded you then complete formalisation, electronic signature and bank account registration in Apeiron.

applicant_utility.summary: The threshold is family income, not GPA: USD 55,000 or less for the household, plus a full-time high-school junior year, so if your family earns above that line this is not your award. Only 105 students win nationally, and the essay on overcoming adversity plus community service carries as much weight as your transcript. What makes this one distinctive is the wrap-around money: 25,000 USD from the Rural America Initiative plus 25,000 USD through the Successful Turns support programme, which matters because the core award alone is unlikely to cover a four-year bill. Applications for the next cycle open on 1 December 2026 and close on 1 March 2027, and notification arrives within 90 days.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Full-time US high-school juniors from low-income families who can evidence hardship overcome, sustained community service and solid academics, and who intend to enrol straight into a US bachelor's degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the family income ceiling first: USD 55,000 or less is a hard gate.
Confirm you will be a full-time high-school junior during the cycle you are applying in.
Confirm US citizenship and that you intend to enrol straight into a bachelor's degree at an accredited non-profit US institution.
Line up evidence of perseverance in overcoming adversity and of community service rather than a list of activities.
Ask for transcripts and the school official's certification well before 1 March - it is a third-party sign-off.
Gather family financial documentation early; income limits are documented, not asserted.
Answer your phone around the notification period, since shortlisted applicants are contacted by telephone for a brief interview.
common_rejection_risks: Family income above the USD 55,000 threshold.
Not enrolled full time as a high-school junior in the cycle applied for.
Being a green-card holder or other non-US citizen.
A statement of adversity that reads as routine hardship rather than perseverance in overcoming it.
Community service that looks last-minute or is done only for the application.
Missing the 1 March cutoff - technically no applications are accepted after 25 March, but the published window closes on 1 March.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published award is 105 scholarships at 25,000 USD each. Because tuition_coverage is inferred rather than stated, treat the full cost of attendance - fees, room, board and travel - as largely your own responsibility unless you are also awarded the Rural America Initiative or Successful Turns support.
document_audit: The application is submitted online, but the transcripts and school official's certification have to come from your school, so start the request early.
Financial documentation must substantiate the USD 55,000 figure, not just assert it.
The essay on adversity is the differentiator and the piece most applicants underprepare.
A telephone interview is part of the process for shortlisted applicants, so keep a phone monitored.
alerts: Applications open 1 December and close 1 March each year; the next cycle runs 1 December 2026 to 1 March 2027.
Applicants are notified within 90 days of the application deadline.

State-level awards exist through State Scholarship and the county and state programmes, so check the state directory page for your state's specific criteria and window - the effective date can run as late as 1 March with no applications accepted after 25 March.
Programme availability varies by year and by state, and criteria are adjusted if no one applies from a given state in a cycle.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You check eligibility, prepare supporting documents and the essay, submit the online application between 1 December and 1 March, and the Association notifies applicants within 90 days of the deadline, with shortlisted applicants contacted by telephone for a short interview before selection.

scholarships.name: Building Brighter Futures: Bursaries and Scholarships (Indspire)

applicant_utility.summary: One application gets you considered for everything - bursaries, scholarships and awards - so there is nothing to gain from filing multiple times, and re-applying each academic year is mandatory. You must prove financial need, so an application from a well-off household will not be awarded, but the flip side is that the money is unrestricted: it can go to tuition, childcare, food, rent or travel, whichever is actually pressing for you. The three documents are all third-party - Status Card or Metis or Inuit Enrolment card, official enrolment proof and last year's final marks - and a fee statement or an acceptance letter will not be accepted as enrolment proof. Apply before 1 November 2026 to catch that consideration date.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Registered First Nations, Metis or Inuit students enrolled at accredited Canadian institutions, including skilled-trades programmes, who can demonstrate financial need and community participation.
application_readiness_checklist: Locate or request your Status Card, Metis card or Inuit Enrolment card well before you apply, since you need the front and back copied.
Request official proof of enrolment from your Registrar's Office - not a fee statement, acceptance letter or intent-to-enrol letter.
Pull your final marks from the most recent completed academic year or programme.
Check your course load: you need 60%, or 40% with a disability-related accommodation.
Log your community participation honestly, including school and community volunteering, since it is scored and a zero score lowers your chances.
Make sure every document shows your name, your school's name and the academic term or terms.
Apply before the 1 November 2026 consideration date rather than waiting for the 1 February 2027 cycle close.
common_rejection_risks: Not demonstrating financial need - all students are required to show it, with only a very limited set of merit-only scholarships exempt.
Using a letter of acceptance as proof of enrolment, or a fee statement, intent-to-enrol letter or student contract.
Documents missing the school name, the academic term or terms, or the student's name.
Enrolment in a fellowship or residency programme, which is not eligible.
Studying outside Canada at a non-graduate level.
A course load below 60%, or below 40% without a disability-related accommodation.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Indspire does not publish a maximum award value, and the award is calculated to assessed financial need, so you cannot assume the full cost of attendance is covered. Because the funds are unrestricted, treat the award as a contribution to your overall budget rather than a full-fee scholarship.
document_audit: Enrolment proof must come from the Registrar's Office or be a class schedule showing your name, the school and the term; acceptance letters, fee statements, intent-to-enrol letters and student contracts are all rejected.
If your official enrolment documentation is not yet available, an acceptance letter may be held as a placeholder, but the application is not complete until active course registration is documented.
All three documents must contain your name, the school's name and the academic term or terms.
If you did not sit a 2025-2026 academic year, you must supply final marks from your most recent completed programme instead.
alerts: Applications are accepted continuously from 1 May to 1 February, with consideration dates of 1 August, 1 November and 1 February - the earlier you apply, the more funding opportunities you are considered for.
Your application stays active for the whole academic year and is carried forward automatically until the cycle closes on 1 February 2027.
Only successful students are notified, so silence is not a rejection and you should keep the application current.

Awards cannot be deferred, must be applied to the programme of study and academic year on the application form, and are paid by EFT to your personal bank account within four to six weeks of your banking details.
Indspire issues a T4A because awards are treated as income, so plan for a tax slip.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit one online application per academic year with the three mandatory documents, Indspire calculates your assessed financial need and living expenses, the application is reviewed at 1 August, 1 November or 1 February consideration dates until the cycle closes on 1 February 2027, and successful students are notified at the end of the month with funds transferred by EFT within four to six weeks.

The single most time-critical step is filing the Expression of Interest within one week of your university application, so prepare both in parallel rather than waiting for offers. Perimeter will not confirm residency until your university offer exists, so supervisor contact before you apply is effectively part of the application.

Check each partner university's own deadline first (Waterloo Physics and IQC routes are common) and diarise a one-week-later date for the Expression of Interest
Draft the 2-page Statement of Purpose around the named researchers' work, not a generic physics CV essay
Line up 3-4 referees who will upload letters directly on AcademicJobsOnline, and warn them the deadline is early in the cycle
Prepare transcripts and CV in advance so the Expression of Interest submission is never the bottleneck
common_rejection_risks: Treating the Expression of Interest as the PhD application itself - Perimeter's posting states explicitly it is NOT a PhD programme application
Missing the one-week window after the university application, or using a later date when applying to several universities instead of the earliest
Naming a researcher who has left Perimeter or whose group is full, with no prior email contact to confirm availability
A Statement of Purpose over the 2-page limit or unfocused across too many research areas
Reference letters that referees never submit on the portal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Relocation to Waterloo and any costs above the combined university-plus-top-up support are not covered; no travel, moving or installation allowance is published, and amounts beyond the $30,000 per year top-up (after fees and tuition) depend on the home department's standard package.
document_audit: Statement of Purpose is capped at 2 pages - Perimeter's portal will not rescue an overwritten essay

The acceptance letter can be uploaded after the Expression of Interest is submitted, but the Expression of Interest itself cannot wait for the offer
English test scores are optional - only include them if they strengthen an otherwise thin file
alerts: A formal residency offer is impossible before the partner university issues its PhD offer, so never decline a university place on the assumption Perimeter will fund you later
Only one Expression of Interest is needed even if you apply to several partner universities - but it must land within one week of your earliest university application

Term-12 cap means the top-up stops at Term 12 - plan around a four-year completion horizon

scholarships.description: Perimeter Institute awards a PhD Residency Program Award to doctoral students admitted to a partner Canadian university and supervised by a Perimeter faculty member, associate faculty member or senior researcher. The official page states that resident PhD students are financially supported through their home university, typically for four years or twelve academic terms, and that the Residency Award adds top-up funding up to $30,000 per year, calculated after fees and tuition, on a September to August academic year, until Term 12. Benefits also include a dedicated desk in a shared workspace, access to Perimeter facilities, a 50% discount at the on-site Black Hole Bistro, and a technology grant of up to $2,000.

scholarships.application_period: Expression of Interest submitted November to January, within one week of the partner-university application; partner universities issue offers February to March; Perimeter contacts selected students April to May; arrival in Waterloo August to September.

scholarships.title: OAS-AUWCL Scholarship Program (American University Washington College of Law LL.M.)
scholarships.name: OAS-AUWCL Scholarship Program (American University Washington College of Law LL.M.)
scholarships.funding_period: one-off, 50% of total tuition for the degree

applicant_utility.summary: This is a 50% tuition waiver, not a full ride, so you must fund the remaining USD 30,972 of tuition plus mandatory fees, health insurance, books, visa costs, flights and DC living costs yourself; secure that money before you invest in an application. Admission comes first: the scholarship letter of consideration is only issued after AUWCL admits you, which makes the AUWCL admission deadline the real gate, and it differs by modality (residential 1 November, hybrid/online 30 November for Spring 2027). The award carries a return-home commitment for at least the length of the scholarship and a 3.0/4.0 GPA floor, and breaching either can trigger repayment of the full award value. If funding is the barrier, the announcement itself points to the separate OAS Rowe Fund interest-free loans of up to USD 15,000.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Law graduates and practising lawyers from OAS member states (outside the US) who need an American LL.M. in human rights, humanitarian law or international arbitration and can cover the other half of tuition plus living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for AUWCL admission first - scholarship consideration only starts once the Admissions Letter is issued.
Prepare law-degree credentials and, for English programmes, English proficiency evidence well before 1 or 30 November 2026.
Build a full budget: remaining 50% tuition, mandatory fees, health insurance, books, visa, flights and Washington, D.C. living costs.
Shape your essay around concrete impact on return to your country of origin - it is an explicit selection criterion.
Argentine applicants: file the required form with the National Liaison Office (ONE) in Argentina without waiting for the deadline.
Decide the modality early: residential, hybrid and online tracks have different deadlines, and only the English programmes can be taken onsite.
common_rejection_risks: Treating the scholarship as a separate application instead of an automatic consequence of AUWCL admission.
Missing the modality-specific deadline (residential 1 November versus hybrid/online 30 November 2026).
An essay that fails to make a credible, specific case for impact on return to the country of origin.
Being a current OAS scholarship holder, a US citizen or permanent resident, GS/OAS staff, consultant or relative, or an OAS Permanent official or relative.
Dropping below a 3.0/4.0 GPA, which forfeits the scholarship.
Declining the award after the programme start date without proof of force majeure, which can force full reimbursement.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 50% of tuition (USD 30,972), mandatory university fees, round-trip travel, books and study materials, health insurance, graduation expenses, visa expenses, and all other living and study costs.
document_audit: The Admissions Letter is issued only after admission, so assemble AUWCL's requested documents before you apply rather than after.
Only the documents AUWCL requests go with the admission application; the scholarship decision rides on that admission file.
The Spanish-language LL.M. needs no English proficiency evidence - do not pay for tests you do not need.
Signing the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form is mandatory for the award to be formally granted.
The published tuition is the 2026-2027 price (USD 2,581 per credit, expected to rise 3-5% annually), so re-check the current total before budgeting.
The GS/OAS reserves the right to cancel the announcement at any point during the process.
alerts: Tuition is expected to increase 3-5% each academic year, so the USD 61,944 total and USD 30,972 balance are 2026-2027 figures only.
The return-to-country commitment lasts at least as long as the scholarship; failure to comply can trigger reimbursement of the total scholarship value.
Scholarship benefits are conditional on academic performance and availability of funds.
Unsuccessful applicants are not contacted; results are published in August and December at www.oas.org/scholarships.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for AUWCL admission by the modality deadline (residential 1 November 2026; hybrid/online 30 November 2026 for Spring 2027), receive the Admissions Letter, then await the joint AUWCL-OAS selection with results published in August and December.

scholarships.description: The OAS-AUWCL Scholarship Program awards a 50% tuition waiver for the LL.M. programmes of American University Washington College of Law in Washington, D.C., under the OAS Partnerships Program for Education and Training (PAEC). It is open to citizens and permanent legal residents of any active OAS member state other than the United States who hold a JD from an ABA-accredited US law school or an equivalent foreign law degree and are admitted to an AUWCL LL.M. programme. Applicants apply for admission through AUWCL, which then issues the Admissions Letter used for scholarship consideration; the Spring 2027 deadlines are 1 November 2026 for residential study and 30 November 2026 for hybrid and online study. The award covers 50% of published tuition; recipients pay the remaining tuition, mandatory fees, health insurance, books, graduation and visa costs, travel, and all other living and study costs, and must commit to return to work in their sponsoring country for the duration of the scholarship.
scholarships.duration: 2-3 semesters (LL.M. in International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law); 2-10 semesters (LL.M. en Derechos Humanos y Derecho Humanitario); 9-18 months (LL.M. in International Arbitration and Business Law)
scholarships.application_period: Spring 2027 intake: admission through AUWCL and scholarship application deadlines of 1 November 2026 (residential) and 30 November 2026 (hybrid/online); classes begin January 2027

scholarships.title: Bolsas Doutorado Sanduiche no Exterior - Edital Comite Gestor Fiocruz no 01/2026 (CAPES-Global.Edu)
scholarships.name: Bolsas Doutorado Sanduiche no Exterior - Edital Comite Gestor Fiocruz no 01/2026 (CAPES-Global.Edu)

applicant_utility.summary: This is an internal Fiocruz call, not an open international competition: you must already be a doctoral student registered on Sucupira inside a Fiocruz programme that belongs to the CAPES Global network and is tied to one of its five Strategic Themes. Ten scholarships are on offer, seven for six months and three for nine months, with the overseas stay starting in September or October 2027, which means the real deadline pressure is the 16:00 Brasilia cut-off on 23 October 2026. Merit is scored out of 100 points, so your work plan and the strength of the host institution carry most of the weight, while an extra 9 equity points can be claimed only if the supporting documents are uploaded at application time.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A Fiocruz doctoral student in a CAPES Global network programme who has passed qualification, has a foreign host already lined up and can still defend the thesis after returning.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme appears in Annex I and pick your main Strategic Theme plus two alternatives before drafting anything else
Count backwards from your thesis defence date: the stay you choose must leave at least six full months in Brazil for credits and defence
Ask the host co-supervisor for the Annex V letter on institutional letterhead with exact start and end month/year matching the 6- or 9-month duration
Get both fluency declarations (Annexes VI and VII) signed and dated, even if the host country is Portuguese-speaking
Check that your ORCID is live and linked inside your Lattes CV, then paste the Lattes link into the form
Verify you are not in default with CAPES and that you hold no other same-level federal scholarship, or get the supervisor's formal authorisation for any accumulation
common_rejection_risks: Registering in more than one of the five Fiocruz calls, which voids every registration with no exception
The stay not leaving six months in Brazil for credit completion and thesis defence
A missing or unjustified qualifying examination, since only the programme coordinator's Annex IV statement can cover it
Dates that disagree between the acceptance letter, the research plan and the chosen duration
Already holding a Doutorado Sanduiche no Exterior scholarship, in this or any earlier doctorate
A late or unfinished submission, since the call warns the 23 October 16:00 deadline will not be extended for technical problems
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees and bench fees at the host institution, visa and passport issuance costs, any costs of companions or dependants, and every expense outside the five financed items listed in item 2.4; any extension of the stay beyond the granted period is authorised with no cost to CAPES, so it must be self-funded.
document_audit: Letters from the host institution must be on letterhead and carry the full institution name including campus or institute, complete address, institutional website, contact phone, date, signature and the signatory's email and phone
The Brazilian advisor's letter is capped at one page and must justify the stay and show technical-scientific interaction with the co-supervisor abroad

The research plan is capped at 5 pages in Times New Roman 12 and needs both a Portuguese and an English summary of the activities, plus a timetable, expected results and the host institution's infrastructure
The co-supervisor's CV must be no longer than 5 pages, with production from 2022 to 2026 and at least a doctoral title
Foreign applicants must supply photo ID with CPF, or CRNM plus CPF together with the permanent residence authorisation
Equity documentation for the 9 extra points must be attached at application, and only proof of admission through affirmative action or a PPG statement is accepted for the ethnic-racial criterion
alerts: Applications close at 16:00 Brasilia on 23 October 2026 with no extension, and the platform header shows a later 15/12/2026 date that belongs to the results and implementation window, not to the application deadline
The same student cannot compete in more than one of the five Fiocruz calls, and earlier applications under other calls void all but the first submission
Priority goes to Global South and BRICS+ destinations, so a proposal aimed at Europe, the United States, Japan or Australia scores lower on Block 3
Results and appeals are published exclusively on the call page, so monitor the daily list rather than email
After implementation the file leaves Fiocruz hands: doubts go through CAPES Linha Direta and approvals by silence are treated as withdrawal, so watch the inbox, including spam
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One electronic form upload, then Fiocruz technical homologation, a merit analysis scored out of 100 plus 9 equity points, and results published on the same call page with the award implemented by CAPES in the SCBA system in April 2027.

The scholarship funds a research stay at a foreign higher education institution for doctoral students of Fundacao Oswaldo Cruz, who return to Brazil within the CAPES deadline to complete and defend their thesis. scholarships.title: Dos becas de investigacion: sedes Costa Rica y Ecuador (Fellowships CALAS 2027)
scholarships.name: Dos becas de investigacion: sedes Costa Rica y Ecuador (Fellowships CALAS 2027)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a short, senior-level residency rather than a degree scholarship: you must already hold a doctorate and be able to relocate to San Jose or Quito for two to three months in 2027. The money side is deliberately thin on detail, so budget as if only the airfare is guaranteed - CALAS states plainly that it cannot house fellows. Your competitive edge is a project that visibly speaks to CALAS's crisis-and-horizons agenda and a publication record that a reviewer can check.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctorate-holding social science and humanities researchers with publications and working Spanish who can spend a spring or summer 2027 residency in Costa Rica or Ecuador.
application_readiness_checklist: Trim the CV to exactly 2 pages and list only publications related to the project
Build the proposal to the hard limits: 4 pages / 2000 words, work plan, calendar, max 10 bibliographic sources
Write the cover letter against this specific seat (Costa Rica vs Ecuador) and name what you expect from the residency
Scan the doctorate certificate as PDF and keep every file in Spanish or English
Line up a rental contact in San Jose or Quito early, since accommodation is yours to solve
common_rejection_risks: Proposal drifts off the CALAS 'Creando horizontes' research questions into a generic Latin American topic
Over-length documents: the 2-page CV, 4-page/2000-word proposal and 10-source cap are explicit
No doctoral certificate attached, or certificates not as PDF
Applying without working Spanish, which the call lists as a requirement
Assuming housing is included and later withdrawing when it is not
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Rent, food, local transport and daily living costs in San Jose or Quito for 2-3 months - only the remuneration (unquantified) and the round-trip flight are covered; nothing is published about insurance or visa support.
document_audit: The proposal must read as a proposal, not a thesis chapter: objectives, methodology and expected results inside 4 pages
The doctorate certificate must be a copy of the actual doctoral degree (título de doctorado), not a master's degree
Cover letter must justify fit to this specific fellowship and seat, not to CALAS in general
alerts: Applications close 12 October 2026 and results are only notified on 30 November 2026, for a stay starting March-June 2027 - plan visa and rental timelines around that lag
CALAS warns that, given the expected volume of applications, rejections will not be justified
Cultural and literary studies proposals are expressly encouraged this round
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill the CALAS online form, upload the four PDFs (cover letter, 2-page CV, doctorate certificate copy, proposal), and wait for the 30 November 2026 notification; the fellowship itself is arranged directly with the chosen seat.

Fellows sit within the transdisciplinary research programme "Creando horizontes: aceleraciones, transformaciones, emergencias". applicant_utility.summary: One single place is on offer, so this is effectively a national final: your project must sit squarely in geosciences, energy, environment or a related engineering field, and you need a French co-director linked to an IRD joint unit before you apply, because co-tutela or co-dirección is part of the application itself. Money-wise the package is complete - stipend, PUCP tuition/degree fees, airfare, insurance and French fee/visa exemptions - but it is structured around a three-year Peru-France-Peru rhythm you must genuinely commit to. Watch the under-40 age limit at the closing date.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Peruvian master's graduates under 40 in geosciences, energy, environmental or related engineering fields who can secure a French co-director at an IRD-linked university and commit to a three-year split doctorate.

Decide between co-tutela (double degree, PUCP-France convention) and co-dirección (PUCP matriculation only) before drafting
Use only the official Formato-Postulacion-EDFPCIG-2026-VF Excel and the Carta-de-Compromiso template from the page
Build the documentation per numeral 3.2 of the bases, including the SUNEDU-registered master's degree
Confirm you will still be under 40 on 15 October 2026
Email becas-posgrado@pucp.pe with any doubt well before the closing date
common_rejection_risks: A project that does not map onto geociencias, energía, medioambiente or ciencias afines
No French co-director identified, or a French university outside the IRD joint unit's partners
Non-official application formats or a missing commitment letter
Turning 40 before the close of applications
Master's degree not registered with SUNEDU
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal expenses beyond the stipend during the three years, and any cost not listed in the non-monetary benefits; the stipend amounts are labelled 'sujeto a modificación', so do not budget to the last euro on the published figure.

During the three funded years, other academic activity is exceptional and capped at teaching one course
Past winner lists (2017-2025) are published on the same page - useful for calibrating the expected profile
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Download the bases, Excel format and commitment letter, assemble the numeral-3.2 documentation, and submit through the PUCP School of Postgraduate Studies by 15 October 2026; results are published on the page on 4 December 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: This grant pays for your thesis research, not your degree: the fund says outright it will not pay tuition, so treat the COP 3.5 million ceiling as your research budget, with the total project budget allowed to exceed it if other sources cover the rest. The file is document-heavy - supervisor letter, faculty letter on letterhead, enrolment certificate, recommendation letter from a professor who is not your director - so start collecting signatures weeks before 20 October 2026. If your fieldwork is in the Orinoquía, the AKAE Conservación reserve convention can also open a field station to one II-2026 grantee.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Colombian undergraduate or master's students with a faculty-approved biodiversity thesis at the start of execution, especially field or sampling work in the Orinoquía.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your thesis is faculty-approved and under 50% executed at the close of the call
Get the supervisor letter and the faculty letter on letterhead early - both must name every member of a collective proposal
Build the five-page proposal exactly to format: Times New Roman 12, 1.5 cm margins, with all required sections
Prepare the justified budget showing which lines the grant covers and which come from other sources
Secure the recommendation letter from a professor other than your thesis director
Declare any AI tool use in the proposal and any wild-species collection permits needed
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that is already finished or in an advanced execution stage
Requesting more than COP 3'500.000 from the fund
Missing either the supervisor letter or the faculty letter - both are mandatory and must address the Colombia Biodiversa Fund
Applying with a project that is not a degree thesis, or not a research proposal
Leaving the enrolment certificate or identity document out of the uploads
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and study fees, health-risk insurance for field or laboratory work (the fund disclaims responsibility), and any budget line beyond the COP 3'500,000 grant.
document_audit: Collective proposals need every member's enrolment certificate and identity documents unified into single files

AI-use and collection-permit declarations are explicit checkboxes in the form - do not leave them blank

FAAE, not the student, activates the definitive registration after verifying the form and uploads - check inbox and spam for the number

Winners commit to progress reports, the approved thesis, a manuscript submitted for publication, a web abstract and FAAE seminars, signed by contract and a pagaré with a co-signer; failure means returning the full grant
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill the three-stage online pre-registration (data, category/abstract/motivation, uploads/survey); FAAE verifies and emails the definitive registration number; awarded students then work within their one-year (undergraduate) or two-year (master's) window.

applicant_utility.summary: Timing is everything here: the postdoctoral window (18 February to 5 March 2027) opens only after the 2026 call's doctoral rounds have closed, and the fellowship itself starts 1 August 2027, so plan your postdoc start around that date. You must have already defended the thesis or made the final delivery of copies before you apply - an in-progress doctorate does not qualify. Because 70% of each Advisory Commission's places are reserved for the priority themes and regions, framing your plan against the CONICET priority list is the single highest-leverage move you can make.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Newly defended PhDs who want three years of funded research in Argentina and can align their plan with CONICET's priority themes or priority regions.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the thesis defence or final delivery of copies is complete before the window opens
Read the priority themes PDF and the priority regions/thematic areas matrix and map your plan onto them
Identify the correct Advisory Commission for your discipline before registering
Follow the 2026 presentation instructivo exactly and upload the endorsement letters it requires
If you hold a CONICET doctoral or completion scholarship (cohorts 2021/2027, 2022/2027, 2025/2027), check how the automatic extension interacts with your application
common_rejection_risks: Applying before the thesis is defended or the final copies are delivered
A research plan with no link to the priority themes or regions, which forfeits the 70% quota
Applying to the wrong Advisory Commission for your discipline
Not following the electronic instructivo (missing endorsement letters or fields)
Counting on cross-Commission reassignment of leftover places - CONICET does not reassign
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is the only published monetary support; relocation to the host locality in Argentina and any international travel are not part of the published benefits.
document_audit: The instructivo governs the file - document names and formats must match it
Digital letters of endorsement are part of the submission, not an optional extra
Evidence of thesis defence or final delivery must match the dates the bases require
alerts: The window is short (18 February to 5 March 2027) - the system does not wait for late uploads
Published stipend values are for September-December 2026 and will be updated before the 01/08/2027 start
The overall 2026 call is for 1,000 doctoral, 300 completion and 800 postdoctoral places - those doctoral windows already closed in July-August 2026
CONICET pays no pension contributions on the stipend
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the electronic system per the instructivo, submit the plan and endorsements to your Advisory Commission between 18 February and 5 March 2027; selection follows the 70/30 priority-then-merit allocation within each Commission.

applicant_utility.summary: There are exactly 100 BUCH places, so this is effectively a top-100 ranking race decided by PAES: 25% Competencia Lectora, 25% your better maths paper, 20% your better elective, 20% ranking and 10% your school average. The BUCH application does not admit you to the university - you must separately apply through SAES, be summoned to enrol and formalise the matricula, or the award cannot be finalised. If MINEDUC grants you gratuidad or Beca Vocacion de Profesor instead, the ministerial benefit prevails over BUCH.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving Chilean secondary-school leavers from low and middle socioeconomic households (Registro Social de Hogares up to the 90% band) who have not won MINEDUC gratuidad and want tuition fully covered at the Universidad de Chile.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fully funded overseas scholarship for Pakistani nationals studying for a Master's, M.Phil or Ph.D abroad, and it is one of the rare overseas awards that combines a maintenance allowance with explicit tuition support up to USD 3,840 a year plus a books and replication allowance. The critical eligibility trap is that you cannot hold any other scholarship, stipend, loan, allowance or subsidy from a government or other institution while you study, so accepting this award ends any other funded obligation. The second constraint is duration: the degree must be finished within the officially allowed period, and HEC states no extension is permitted in any case, which means choosing a programme whose length fits the scheme matters as much as your research proposal. Because this record could not be verified against HEC's live pages on 10 October 2026, treat every figure in it as provisional and re-check the HEC Phase-III page before committing to a plan built on these numbers.

The money is generous but structured - full tuition paid directly, a living allowance that differs for accompanied scholars (FJD 32,472 vs 21,450 for Masters), a one-off books allowance of FJD 750, an establishment allowance of FJD 1,900 where applicable, and a research grant capped at FJD 17,500 (Masters) or FJD 40,000 (PhD). applicant_utility.summary: This is a 50% tuition waiver, not a living scholarship, so budget for the other half of your fees plus rent, food and insurance out of pocket. The scholarship cannot be applied for until you already hold a Griffith Letter of Offer, which means your application to study must be submitted well before 28 November 2026 if you are targeting Trimester 1 2027. If your grades come through a 7-point scale, the 6.0 GPA threshold is materially higher than the 4.5 threshold on Griffith's automatic merit scholarship, so check your transcript conversion before deciding which to rely on.

Diary the acceptance deadline stated in your Scholarship Letter, since failing to accept by that date withdraws the award

Choosing an excluded program, most often the MBA (5158), a Diploma, an online or partner-delivered program, or any Higher Degree Research degree
Dropping below a 5.5 cumulative GPA or failing a course, which ends the fee deductions for later years
Late acceptance of the scholarship offer, which Griffith treats as a withdrawal

applicant_utility.summary: The $25,000 figure is a ceiling, not a guaranteed payment, so treat it as the maximum and check the offer letter for what you will actually receive each year. Money arrives in two equal instalments and the second one is conditional on passing every first-semester course, so a single failed paper can stop the second half of the year's funding. The programme prioritises applicants in in-demand health disciplines with a short runway to employment, so being close to finishing your qualification is a real advantage rather than a neutral factor.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Former refugees and their children living in New Zealand who have already completed at least a year of tertiary study and have at least a year left on a level 7 or above health qualification.

Gather transcripts for every prior programme including English language and foundation studies, not just your current institution's records
Secure both a personal reference and an academic reference early, since you need one of each and referees are the usual bottleneck
Write the financial statement carefully, covering how you are currently supported, how you would spend the award, and the impact on your family
Time your application so you still have at least one full-time year of study remaining at the moment of the award, not at the moment you apply
common_rejection_risks: Having less than one year of full-time study remaining when the award decision is made
Applying at a qualification below level 7 or with a provider that is not NZQA-accredited
Failing any first-semester course, which blocks the second semester instalment
Not having refugee background status documented through an INZ Certificate of Identity or INZ letter
Submitting a statement that only covers financial need without addressing workforce and health-outcome impact
Holding another scholarship without prior approval from the Chair of the Selection Committee
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any gap between the actual award and your true costs, since the $25,000 is a cap rather than a guaranteed amount, plus anything the cap does not absorb such as travel, equipment and dependants' costs.
document_audit: Refugee status must be evidenced by an INZ Certificate of Identity or INZ letter that confirms date of birth, refugee status and permanent residency all together
Transcripts are required for all previous study, including incomplete and non-degree programmes such as English language and foundation study

The scholarship cannot be deferred, so your enrolment plan must match the award year exactly
alerts: The application window is only three months (1 July to 1 October), and it has now closed for the 2027 intake, so plan for a July 2027 opening

Priority goes to in-demand disciplines with a short lead time to workforce entry, so late-stage students are favoured over early-stage ones

applicant_utility.summary: There is no central application form, so your real deadline is whichever university you target, and that window can differ by months between institutions. The headline benefit is tuition-free study plus an arrival payment, housing and annual tickets, but the Ministry splits awards into type A full scholarships, type B partial scholarships offering only a seat or a seat plus housing, and type C paid grants, so confirm which level your institution is actually offering before you decline other funding. Health and medical specialties are excluded at the postgraduate stage, which eliminates a large share of the programmes most international applicants would otherwise target.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Saudi applicants aged 17 to 35 who want a tuition-free degree at a Saudi public university and can navigate a university-specific admission window rather than a central portal.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the specific Saudi public university and programme first, then find that university's own admission window and deadline, since the Ministry does not set one
Have your academic certificates and supporting papers attested by the competent authorities named by the institution before you apply
Request the certificate of absence of precedents from your own country's security services early, since it is a required document and often slow to obtain
Book the medical examination required by the regulations and keep the result with your file
Confirm with the university or Cultural Attaché which benefit level (A, B or C) is on offer for your programme, since it determines whether housing is included
If your own government must approve study in the Kingdom, obtain that approval before submitting
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a health or medical specialty at the post-secondary stage, which is excluded
Falling outside the age limits: 25 for undergraduate or the Arabic language institute, 30 for master's, 35 for doctoral
Submitting unattested certificates or supporting papers, which the institution will not accept
Missing the individual university's own admission window while waiting for a central deadline that does not exist
Holding another scholarship from a Saudi educational institution, or having previously been dismissed from one
Assuming a type B seat-only award will include housing, when it may not
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Under a type B partial scholarship or type C paid grant, part or all of your tuition, plus living costs beyond the arrival reward and any housing provided. Even under a type A award, personal expenses, travel beyond the annual ticket and family costs beyond the regulated health care are not covered.
document_audit: Certificates and supporting papers must be attested by the competent authorities specified by the educational institution, so check which authorities that institution accepts before paying for attestation
The certificate of absence of precedents must come from your own country's security services, not a local police station equivalent
You need a scholarship from a Saudi university before you can obtain a study visa, so the admission decision is the gating step for travel
Female students covered by a scholarship or regular residence must comply with the mahram rules as set by the governing instructions
alerts: Because each university sets its own opening date, the practical deadline varies and can be unknown until the university publishes it
The three benefit levels are decided by the institution council, so the same programme can be full, partial or paid at different universities
The free residence permit is issued only after arrival, with a letter from the admitting university's passport department, so build that step into your travel planning
Health and medical specialisations are excluded at the post-secondary stage, so check the exclusion before choosing a field
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to a Saudi public university during its own admission window, or lodge the application through the Saudi Cultural Attaché or the Saudi Embassy where no Attaché exists, then use the university's admission decision to obtain a study visa and, after arrival, a free residence permit.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply directly: your application has to be endorsed by your ECOWAS member state's nominating agency, and each member state only gets three nominees, so the real competition is at national level rather than in Accra. The first practical step is a Ghanaian university admission, because the Authority requires either a conditional offer or a paid-application acknowledgement before your file moves forward. Since the funding notice never says whether tuition, living costs or travel are covered, budget as if you may be funding much of the award yourself until you receive an offer letter that itemises it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: ECOWAS nationals who already hold or are close to securing admission to a participating Ghanaian public university in a listed priority field, and whose home ministry will actually nominate them.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm which of your country's bodies is the official nominating agency, since a nomination from the wrong organisation is discarded
Apply early to a participating Ghanaian public university and pay the application fee so you can produce the acknowledgement notice the Authority requires
Check the institution table in the notice for your chosen university's own opening and closing dates, since they differ materially between institutions
Prepare attested academic credentials and a passport with enough validity for a Ghanaian student visa
Contact your nominating agency well before 30 August so the National Endorsement Form is returned and couriered in time
Align your field of study with the section 3.0 priority list, since nominating agencies are told to use it
common_rejection_risks: Assuming you can apply directly and missing the nomination step entirely
Submitting after your member state's three-per-country quota has been filled by earlier nominees
Applying without a Ghanaian admission offer or a paid-application acknowledgement, which fails step 1
An incomplete supporting document set, which the notice says will not be considered
Studying a field outside the published priority areas, which weakens a nomination decision
Choosing a public tertiary institution that is not on the participating list in the notice
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Unknown from the notice, which is itself the risk: since the award does not state whether tuition, living costs or travel are covered, you may need to fund some or all of these yourself. Ghanaian university application fees, attestation, passports, visas and travel to Ghana are always yours to pay.
document_audit: Either a conditional offer letter or an acknowledgement notice proving the application fee was paid is mandatory, not optional
The National Endorsement Form is completed and submitted by the nominating agency, so confirm they have your details rather than uploading it yourself
Scanned endorsement forms must be emailed and the complete paper application couriered to the Director-General via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, so build in courier time
Academic credentials must support the admission you are claiming, so inconsistencies between the two are a fast rejection
alerts: The 2026 cycle is closed: the nominating-agency deadline of 30 August 2026 has passed and the notice was published on 3 June 2026 for the 2026/2027 year
Each participating institution has its own admission window, some opening as early as January and others as late as September 2026
The quota of three nominees per member state means a strong application can still fail purely on national-level timing
The notice gives no award value or itemised coverage, so do not treat the scholarship as fully funded on the basis of this page alone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to a participating Ghanaian public university, upload your credentials and admission evidence to the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal, then wait for the Authority's review and your country's nominating agency to return the National Endorsement Form through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

applicant_utility.summary: This is one tight annual window, historically 15 November to 15 December, and the announcement is explicit that late applications will not be considered, so the practical deadline is the day the window closes rather than whenever you finish gathering documents. Your three reference lecturers must be listed with both an email address and a WhatsApp number, which is an unusual data requirement that routinely delays applications. The age limits are strict and gendered, with PhD applicants capped at 28 for men and 30 for women, so eligibility should be checked against the exact cut-off before investing in the full document set.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Young African graduates and postgraduates within the published age limits who want master's or PhD study at one of the four Pan African University institutes.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your age against the exact caps: 25 male / 28 female for master's, and 28 male / 30 female for PhD
Line up three reference lecturers early and collect both an email address and a WhatsApp number for each, since all three are mandatory
Have certificates and transcripts certified as true copies, including high school records, not just university ones
Prepare a 2cm x 2cm clear coloured passport photograph to the exact stated dimensions
PhD applicants: draft the 3 to 4 page concept note with tentative title, research questions, objectives and significance before opening the portal
Register on the portal early and immediately check spam for the confirmation email, since registration must be confirmed before you can log in
common_rejection_risks: Submitting after the 15 December close, which the announcement says will not be considered at any point
Exceeding the age limits, which are published per gender and are not waived
Failing to confirm the registration email, which blocks login and therefore submission
Omitting one of the three mandatory reference lecturers, or providing an email without a WhatsApp number
Leaving the application saved rather than clicking FINISH, which means it is never submitted
A bachelor's degree below a second-class upper division or equivalent, since academic competence must be evidenced at that level
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published: because the announcement does not itemise the scholarship, any shortfall in fees, living costs, travel or family support cannot be quantified from the official page.
document_audit: Both university and high school transcripts are required, so applicants who discarded school records early will need to obtain certified replacements
Certified true copies are required rather than plain photocopies or uncertified scans
The photograph must be 2cm x 2cm, coloured and clear, which is stricter than the usual generic passport photo
Reference lecturers must be listed with email and WhatsApp contact details, so referees need to be briefed on this before submission
PhD applicants need two professor recommendation letters plus the concept note, a heavier set than the master's single lecturer letter
alerts: The 2026-2027 call closed on 15 December 2025 and late applications are explicitly not considered, so the next realistic opportunity is the following November window
Registration must be confirmed by clicking the link sent to your email, so use an address you actively check and look in the spam folder

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of the few government scholarship programmes that assigns your university and department for you, so research effort is better spent on making the strongest possible TBBS application than on cold-emailing admissions offices. The stipend scales sharply by level (6,500 TL undergraduate, 9,500 TL master's, 13,000 TL PhD), so doctoral applicants get the strongest package; every scholar without C1 Turkish must still complete the one-year language course before degree study begins. Applications are free, but the window is a narrow 10 January - 20 February each year and the interview round does not start until April-June, so plan a gap of roughly six months between submission and a decision.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students from any country (except Turkish citizens) with 70-90%+ academic records who want a fully funded degree in Türkiye and are comfortable with YTB choosing the university and department.
application_readiness_checklist: Prepare passport, diploma or temporary graduation certificate, transcript and a photograph taken within the last year before the window opens on 10 January
Check your age against your level's cut-off (under 21 for bachelor's, under 30 master's, under 35 PhD) using your age on the application date
Masters and PhD applicants: line up GRE/GMAT/SAT or ALES results early if your intended host programme may require them
PhD applicants: draft the research topic proposal and written research example before December - these cannot be improvised in the final week
Choose your 12 TBBS programme options deliberately, remembering you can only pick from programmes the system offers you
common_rejection_risks: Being a Turkish citizen or having lost Turkish citizenship - an absolute bar that no strength of record overcomes
Already being enrolled at a Turkish university at the level applied for
Missing the age cut-off (the rule is applied by level, and PhD applicants turning 36 lose eligibility entirely)
Weak academic average below the 70%/75%/90% thresholds for your level
Incomplete uploads - the TBBS form is documentary, so a missing transcript or expired photo stalls evaluation before it starts
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The programme covers tuition, dormitory or housing allowance, health insurance and flights, but the TL stipend is modest against personal spending, visa fees, and the cost of settling in before the first payment; graduate students who leave the dormitory after year one may find the 5,000-6,000 TL housing allowance tight in Istanbul or Ankara.
document_audit: The photograph must have been taken within the last year - older passport-style photos are a common rejection
Graduating students must graduate before August of the application year; a delayed certificate invalidates the application
Any document not issued in Turkish or English needs a certified translation before upload
alerts: The 2026 window closed on 20 February 2026; the next cycle is expected to open 10 January 2027 - there is no rolling or late entry
Turkish language study is compulsory for anyone without C1, which effectively adds a year before degree coursework
Research Scholarships and Success Scholarships (October-November window) are separate programmes with their own deadlines - do not wait for the general round if you are a researcher
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on TBBS during the 10 January - 20 February window, complete the form, upload all documents, select up to 12 offered programmes, then await documentary evaluation (March-April), interviews (April-June) and results in early August.

scholarships.title: World in Serbia Project Scholarships of the Government of the Republic of Serbia
scholarships.name: World in Serbia Project Scholarships of the Government of the Republic of Serbia

applicant_utility.summary: World in Serbia is run as a government-to-government nomination scholarship, so the decisive step happens in your home country: your national authority must endorse and forward your file, and that nomination deadline sits only days after the online application closes. The award covers tuition, student-centre accommodation and meals, a RSD 18,000 monthly allowance and health insurance (mandatory under 26), but explicitly excludes flights, textbooks, exam-registration fees and roughly RSD 4,300 in residence-permit charges, so budget for those yourself. Because every degree is taught in Serbian, treat the free preparatory year as a real academic hurdle rather than a bonus: passing the Serbian-language examination is what keeps both your enrolment and your funding alive.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School-leavers and bachelor's or master's graduates from Non-Aligned Movement member and observer states whose government will nominate them and who accept a degree taught entirely in Serbian after a one-year language course.
application_readiness_checklist: Approach your country's competent authority (ministry of education, foreign affairs or the body that announced the local competition) months before the June deadline, because official nomination - not the online form - is what makes you eligible
Check passport validity immediately: it must be valid for at least another six years at the date of your visa application
Gather certified copies of every secondary or higher-education certificate, diploma, transcript and diploma supplement, and have them translated into Serbian or English by an authorized certifier

Build the health dossier early: official vaccination record covering tuberculosis, hepatitis B, polio, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, measles, mumps, rubella, S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae, plus a QuantiFERON-TB test or chest X-ray and HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and malaria laboratory results, all signed and stamped by a physician with diagnoses written in Latin and ICD-coded
Obtain a certificate proving conversational-level English or Serbian (A1 minimum), and for doctoral applicants a certificate of your average grade from the previous level of studies

Submit the Google Form, email the document set to worldinserbia@prosveta.gov.rs with your name, surname and country in the subject line, then deliver certified paper copies to your national authority in time for the consular list deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing the state endorsement: candidates not proposed by the competent authority of their country are not considered regardless of academic strength
Documentation that is uncertified or not translated into Serbian or English - the call explicitly warns such files will not be taken into consideration

Health documentation the Student Health Care Institute of Belgrade cannot verify, or that lacks the physician's signature and stamp, uses local-language diagnoses instead of Latin ICD codes, or lacks the required infectious-disease test results
A passport with less than six years of validity remaining at the visa application date
Losing the scholarship after arrival by failing the Serbian-language examination or earning fewer than 37 ECTS credits in an academic year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights to and from Serbia, local city transport, textbooks and study materials, exam-registration and diploma-issuance fees, meal fob cards, and residence-permit charges of RSD 420 (application), RSD 2,120 (temporary residence permit) and RSD 1,788 (biometric card) - about RSD 4,328 in Ministry of Interior fees alone
document_audit: The passport must stay valid at least six years from the visa application date, so renewing it mid-study is a compliance risk the call specifically flags
Every educational document needs a certifier's stamp plus a Serbian or English translation; an uncertified photocopy of a foreign-language transcript is ignored
The email subject line must contain your name, surname and the country you apply for, or the Ministry may fail to match your documents to your form

Health tests (QuantiFERON-TB or chest X-ray, HIV, hepatitis B and C, malaria) must be issued by a recognised institution in your own country and carry a physician's signature and stamp - book these appointments well before the deadline
Bring originals of everything on arrival; the original health certificate must be no older than six months at that point
alerts: The 2026 call closed on 26 June 2026 with consular lists due 3 July 2026; the competition is re-issued annually, so watch prosveta.gov.rs and your national authority from spring 2027 for the next cycle
Your national endorsement is the real deadline: only days separate the online close from the mission's submission to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, so slow local processing can eliminate you
Scholarship holders must arrive in Belgrade inside the published arrival window (15 October to 15 November for the 2026 cohort) and sign a formal Scholarship Contract with the Ministry
One programme per cycle and no transfers after admission: enrolling in Serbian-language classes and then not taking up a degree place for 2027/2028 forfeits the scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Google Form first, then the scanned document package by email to worldinserbia@prosveta.gov.rs, then certified paper copies to your national authority, whose endorsed list travels through Serbia's diplomatic-consular mission and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to the Ministry of Education for inter-ministerial selection

scholarships.name: PTDF Overseas Postgraduate Scholarship Scheme (MSc/PhD)

applicant_utility.summary: This scheme pays for everything it lists - flights, health insurance, tuition and bench fees, accommodation and living allowances - but it is tightly gated: only Nigerian citizens who have completed NYSC and hold at least a 2:1 (or 2:2 with industry experience) can compete, and only for courses on PTDF's approved partner list. The application route rewards early administrative work: NIN verification, WAEC/NECO PINs ready for online checking, and a 500-word Statement of Purpose (MSc) or five-page proposal (PhD) that ties your study explicitly to the oil and gas industry. Because the Fund deliberately limits awards to fields relevant to its mandate, a persuasive relevance argument in your proposal matters as much as your grades.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nigerian graduates with strong oil-and-gas-aligned degrees, completed NYSC, and clean documentation who want a funded MSc or PhD at a PTDF partner university in the UK, Germany, France or Malaysia.

DAAD-track PhD applicants: identify and secure a German research supervisor before the final interview stage
common_rejection_risks: Submitting more than one application - this results in automatic disqualification
Proposing a programme PTDF judges not relevant to the oil and gas industry, or outside your prior academic background
Illegible or falsified documents - both are automatic disqualification grounds
Having been previously sponsored by the Fund at the same or a lower category
Applying for a UK PhD outside the CPESK split-site route, which was the only UK PhD structure for 2026

applicant_utility.summary: Two facts decide most applications: Catholic Church membership is effectively a hard gate, and foreign applicants must already hold admission to doctoral study at a German university with German at C1, so start the admission procedure months before 1 November. The money is a stipend, not a fee award: 1,750 Euro per month plus 100 Euro research allowance, with tuition support of up to 10,000 Euro per year only on individual application. Budget for a long, staged process - internal review alone takes four to six weeks, then two interviews, then a panel.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Catholic doctoral candidates (or Cusanuswerk alumni) with an excellent degree, an interdisciplinary project and a concrete record of voluntary engagement.

applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition above the EUR 10,000 per year that can be applied for, conference travel not approved on application, and any shortfall between the stipend and actual living and health-insurance costs (the insurance subsidy is capped at EUR 170 per month).

Because the application needs both a host invitation form and a home supervisor support form, the real deadline for you is several weeks before 31 October 2026 - that is when your chosen host must have agreed in writing. ERS also warns that clinical training and research projects are out of scope, so frame the visit as knowledge exchange and network building, not as a research stay.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fully self-directed residency rather than a funded degree: you propose your own project, spend 3-8 continuous months in Lisbon, and receive travel, insurance, a monthly stipend and a partial housing allowance whose size is only fixed after you are selected. The window closes 15 October 2026 at 15:00 Lisbon time, and only the CV, a short proposal and two referee names are needed to apply. With up to 15 places worldwide and no nationality, language or degree prerequisites, the decisive factor is the strength and originality of the written project.

common_rejection_risks: A proposal that reads as applied, practical or creative production rather than inquiry - the Institute explicitly excludes primarily practice- or application-oriented work

scholarships.name: Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholarship Program (UNCF)

applicant_utility.summary: Only two students win each year - one female and one male - making this a high-prestige, low-probability award for full-time seniors at accredited four-year HBCUs with a 3.5+ GPA and verified unmet need. The 2026-2027 round is open and closes 10/29/2026 at 7:00 PM EST, earlier in the day than most UNCF deadlines. You need two faculty recommendation letters and two prescribed essays, one of them explicitly about Frederick Douglass's legacy, so line up recommenders and draft months ahead, not weeks.

Draft essay 2 (500-700 words) on Frederick Douglass's impact and legacy
Register on the UNCF portal and submit everything before 10/29/2026 7:00 PM EST

Unmet need not verified by the college or university
Applying as a junior or at a two-year or non-HBCU institution

scholarships.description: The Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholarship Program was established by Tony Signore and funded by the Signore Family to support students attending accredited historically black colleges and universities nationwide. UNCF administers and manages the programme for 20 years, through academic year 2038-39. Each year the programme awards two USD 10,000 scholarships to exceptional HBCU seniors who have demonstrated high academic achievement, strong leadership skills, a commitment to community service and unmet financial need. Applicants must hold a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale and must complete a Free Application for Federal Student Aid.
