scholarships.title: HHMI Janelia Joint Graduate Program in Neuroscience (with Johns Hopkins University)
scholarships.name: HHMI Janelia Joint Graduate Program in Neuroscience (with Johns Hopkins University)

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate Janelia application - everything hinges on the Johns Hopkins neuroscience application and on naming one to four Janelia Group Leaders in your Statement of Interest and Career Objectives, which is the single mechanism that routes you into this programme. Funding is genuinely complete for admitted students (stipend, health insurance, programmatic travel, free housing during rotations), so the competition is about fit rather than finance. Contacting a group leader before you apply - politely, with a specific read of their work - is effectively the interview head start, and students who enter JHU without signalling Janelia interest can still join after a summer rotation, so this route is not a one-shot door.
applicant_utility.best_fit: B.S./B.A. graduates with laboratory research experience who want a fully funded neuroscience PhD and can see themselves doing thesis work in a specific Janelia lab.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply directly to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience programme; do not look for a Janelia form - none exists
Read the Janelia group leader list and name one to four labs in your Statement of Interest, describing why each fits your goals
Quantify your research experience in the Personal Statement, including months of full-time work as the guidance requests
Confirm the recommended coursework (calculus, physics, biology, general and organic chemistry) on your transcript, or address gaps in your statement
Have TOEFL or IELTS scores sent (institution code 5316) unless you qualify for the US/UK degree waiver
Secure three letters of recommendation early so the file is complete by the December 3 deadline - incomplete files are not considered
common_rejection_risks: Applying to JHU neuroscience without naming any Janelia group leaders, which removes you from this programme's pool
Naming labs whose research you clearly have not read - the statement must describe interest grounded in those labs' actual work
Letters of recommendation arriving after December 3 - the deadline explicitly includes them
A Personal Statement with no research narrative, when laboratory experience is 'desirable' and expected of competitive applicants
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Admitted students are fully supported (stipend, health insurance, programmatic travel, free housing during rotations), so the main out-of-pocket costs are application fees, test fees, relocation to Baltimore before the first stipend payment, and any personal travel beyond the funded programme and conference travel.
document_audit: The Statement of Interest and Career Objectives is a distinct document within the JHU application - it must both declare Janelia interest and list the named group leaders
TOEFL waivers apply only to applicants with a completed or in-progress degree from a US or UK university; other international applicants need scores
Graduate visas are sponsored by Johns Hopkins, not Janelia - coordinate with JHU, not the campus
alerts: The official page states the deadline as December 3 with no year, and notification by April 15 - plan around the JHU admissions calendar for the current cycle
Acceptance into the joint programme is communicated by Johns Hopkins, not Janelia, and interviews happen during the JHU recruitment visit at Janelia
Students admitted to JHU neuroscience without early Janelia interest can still transfer in after a summer rotation by agreement of the student, advisors and programme directors
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience programme with Janelia interest and named group leaders in the Statement of Interest, submit the complete file (including three letters) by December 3, interview at Janelia during the JHU recruitment visit, receive the admission decision from JHU by early March, then spend year one at JHU with a summer rotation at Janelia before thesis research.

scholarships.description: The Janelia Research Campus of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute runs two fully-funded graduate training programmes with Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, in neuroscience and in cross-disciplinary biology (XDBio). Students apply directly to the Johns Hopkins Neuroscience programme in the autumn, naming one to four Janelia group leaders in the Statement of Interest; the published deadline for completed applications including letters of recommendation is December 3, and decisions are communicated by April 15. Janelia states that graduate scholars are fully supported financially by their labs and the graduate programme during their research, with a first-year Johns Hopkins stipend plus health insurance while in Baltimore, and a Janelia Graduate Scholar stipend, health insurance and travel support while at Janelia.
scholarships.duration: Multi-year PhD; one year in residence at Johns Hopkins followed by research years at Janelia
scholarships.application_period: Applications to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience PhD programme are submitted in the autumn each year; the deadline for completed applications including letters of recommendation is December 3 and candidates are notified by April 15.

scholarships.name: Organization of American States (OAS) Scholarship at Colorado State University

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition discount, not a living scholarship: you must first win admission to a Fort Collins degree programme for Fall 2027, then file the short CSU form with two 2-3 paragraph essays. Because the discount only touches non-resident tuition, budget for living costs in Fort Collins yourself, and note that holding a full departmental assistantship disqualifies you from this award.

Locate your CSU ID from RamWeb (issued when you created your CSU application account)

Holding dual US citizenship or US permanent residence alongside OAS member-state citizenship - an automatic exclusion
Being admitted to the SPUR campus programme, whose discounted tuition already excludes the award
Holding a full departmental assistantship, which makes you ineligible outright
Expecting the award to cover living costs - it reduces tuition only, so visa funding proofs still rest on you

scholarships.name: Bolsas Capacitacao de Curta Duracao no Exterior - Edital Comite Gestor Fiocruz no 02/2026 (CAPES-Global.Edu)

applicant_utility.summary: This call funds a short technical, scientific or pedagogical training stint abroad for people formally tied to Fiocruz, with overseas activity starting September or October 2027 - and language courses are explicitly excluded. The hard filter is administrative: you may register in only one of the five Comite Gestor editais, and a duplicate registration voids all of them automatically. Nothing on the page states a stipend value, so treat the financial side as whatever CAPES Edital 13/2025 sets and verify it with the programme before budgeting.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fiocruz staff with a formal CLT or statutory contract, and Fiocruz master's or doctoral students on Sucupira, whose graduate programme sits in the CAPES Global strategic themes and who need a short training period at a foreign institution.

If you are entering an earlier Fiocruz edital too, submit this one first, since only the first submission stays valid
Secure the foreign host institution's acceptance letter (Anexo VII) early - it is the long-lead document
Line up the supporting letters (orientador; PPG and chefia) that match your profile (discente vs profissional)
Register on the Fiocruz site in advance if this is your first access, so login issues cannot eat the deadline
common_rejection_risks: Registering in more than one of the five editais - an automatic, exception-free annulment
Applying with a programme that is not linked to the CAPES Global strategic themes in Annex I
Proposing a language course, which the modality expressly excludes
Submitting outside the electronic form or after 16:00 Brasilia time on 23 October 2026 - no extension is promised
Being mid-selection in an earlier edital and assuming both candidacies survive - only the first does
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published on the call page; the page reproduces no stipend, travel or tuition figures, so assume the CAPES Edital 13/2025 rules govern what is and is not paid and confirm with rede.capesglobal@fiocruz.br before committing.
document_audit: The annex set differs by profile: discentes use Anexo V and the supervisor's fluency declaration (Anexo IX), while profissionais use Anexo VI and their own (Anexo VIII)
The host institution's acceptance letter (Anexo VII) must come from a higher-education institution abroad, not a course provider's informal email
Anexo X (equity self-declaration) and Anexo XI (appeal form) are separate files - do not assume the form bundles them
alerts: Applications close at 16:00 Brasilia time on 23 October 2026 and the page warns there will be no prorogation - do not leave submission to the final hour
Overseas activities only start in September or October 2027, roughly a year after the deadline - plan work and leave around that window
All results and appeals appear exclusively on the call page; nothing is sent individually, so monitor the page
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One electronic form on the Fiocruz Campus Virtual platform; the proposal is valid only if submitted there within the window, and every result or appeal is then published on the same page.

scholarships.description: The second of the five editais opened by the Managing Committee of Fiocruz for the 2027 activity year. This call covers the CAPES-Global.Edu modality Capacitacao de curta duracao no Exterior, short-term training abroad. Unlike the sandwich-doctorate call, it is open not only to Fiocruz master's and doctoral students registered on Sucupira but also to Fiocruz teaching staff, researchers and technical staff who hold a formal employment relationship (CLT or statutory) with the institution and are involved in graduate-programme activities. The purpose is individual qualification and institutional strengthening through technical, scientific or pedagogical training courses abroad, expressly excluding language training. Each candidate may register for only one of the five Fiocruz editais, and multiple registrations are automatically voided.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a training bursary, not cash: you receive a one-year DataCamp licence (expected 1 November 2026 - 1 November 2027) plus a four-session live course on 28-29 October and 4-5 November 2026. Applications close 20 October 2026, with internal selection from 21-27 October and winners announced by email and on social networks before 28 October. There is no nationality, residence, degree or employment restriction - the form explicitly welcomes Ecuadorians and foreigners - so the published gatekeepers are economic need, time and motivation for independent study, the social-media like-and-follow step, and consent in the form to LIDE using your answers anonymously for research. After the award, monthly XP and activity checks mean the licence has to actually be used.
applicant_utility.best_fit: People anywhere - Ecuadorian or foreign - with genuine financial need who want to break into Excel, Power BI, Tableau, R, Python or SQL without paying for commercial training, and can sustain independent monthly study for a year.
application_readiness_checklist: Like the official call post and follow El Quantificador on at least one of Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Bluesky or Threads before submitting - the call makes this an eligibility requirement
Prepare to answer the form's consent question ('Si') agreeing that your responses are recorded, kept confidential and used anonymously for research purposes
Use an email address you monitor: winners are contacted by email before 28 October 2026, so check spam folders; announcements also appear on social networks
Reserve the four course dates (28-29 October and 4-5 November 2026) immediately - they begin within a week of selection
Plan realistic monthly study hours, because reminders arrive from the 25th and XP and activity dates are reviewed between the 3rd and 5th of the following month
Email becas@laboratoriolide.org with questions or form problems before the 20 October 2026 cut-off
common_rejection_risks: Skipping the social-media gate (like the call post and follow El Quantificador), which the call lists as a requirement
Submitting after 20 October 2026 - the Google Form simply stops accepting responses
Vague or inconsistent economic-situation answers: with no published selection criteria, need is the primary published signal
Going inactive after selection, since monthly reminders and XP/activity audits begin straight away
Missing the winner email because it landed in an unchecked inbox before 28 October
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except the platform: internet access, a suitable device and your study time - the award is a licence plus training, with no stipend, tuition, travel or living support.
document_audit: The published call and form request no CV, transcripts, certificates or motivation letter - the Google Form alone is the application
The form asks for a valid email address and includes a research-consent question you must answer 'Si' to continue; data is kept confidential but reused anonymously for academic purposes
The 2026-2027 call names no university-enrolment proof as a required upload, even though the form frames applicants as third-level students
alerts: Applications close 20 October 2026 - about a month after launch, with selection running immediately afterwards (21-27 October)
Licence activation depends on DataCamp's renewal and activation; LIDE states it will promptly inform fellows of any operational delays
The form opens the call to Ecuadorians and foreigners alike but frames them as third-level (university) students of any major - read the form's own wording if you are not currently enrolled
Former LIDE-DataCamp fellows may reapply, so the applicant pool includes returning candidates
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the single Google Form from the call page; LIDE selects internally between 21 and 27 October 2026 and announces winners by email and social networks before 28 October 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: At S/. 10 000 for an individual project and S/. 20 000 for a group, this is a competitive internal grant at PUCP, and the gatekeeping is membership of the Instituto Riva-Aguero, so an outside applicant cannot simply apply. The money pays honorarios, that is, fees for the researcher and for a mandatory PUCP undergraduate assistant, and it arrives in two halves: the first only after the award contract is signed, the second only once the research is published in a Scopus or Web of Science journal, or in a book with an academic publisher, carrying an explicit Riva-Aguero affiliation. Be aware that PUCP members receive the amount through the payroll, which means pension contributions and fifth-category income tax are deducted, so the net figure in your hand will be materially below the headline number. The window closes on 16 October 2026 with results at the end of November, which is an unusually fast turnaround.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Ordinary members of the Instituto Riva-Aguero, and associate or affiliated members holding a doctorate with a contracted PUCP teaching position, as well as registered and council-approved Instituto research groups, working within the Instituto's five research lines.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your Instituto membership category (ordinario, asociado, afiliado, honorario) and that your group is registered and approved by the Instituto's council
If you are an associate member, count your taught courses: at least one course worth a minimum of two credits in each of the last four regular semesters 2025-1, 2025-2, 2026-1 and 2026-2
If you are an affiliated or honorary member, check you have no academic activity, article or research pending delivery to the Instituto
Recruit a PUCP undergraduate student as project assistant before you write the project, since this is indispensable in both modalities
Frame the project inside one of the five Instituto research lines and state it clearly
Build the presupuesto into the project document, along with the brief updated CVs of all participants
Complete the modality-specific online form and submit before 16 October 2026
common_rejection_risks: Not being an Instituto member, or having an unregistered research group, since the convocatoria is closed to them
Failing to commit a PUCP undergraduate assistant to the project
A project that does not inscribe within one of the five research lines

Missing the instalment conditions: the second 50% depends on publication in an indexed journal or academic book, so a project longer than the 31 December 2027 article deadline risks losing half the money
Forgetting that the Instituto retains the right to publish the research for two years
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Salary, living expenses and anything outside the researchers' honorarios. The convocatoria also warns that amounts paid to PUCP community members are remuneration subject to pension contributions and fifth-category income tax, so the net amount is lower than the gross award.
document_audit: The convocatoria specifies an exact project format including the bibliografia, cronograma and presupuesto; an application missing any of these elements is incomplete on its face
Brief updated CVs of all participants are part of the required package, not an optional attachment
alerts: The Instituto may revoke any decision it has made as guarantor, declaring the assignment null and void, and it does not accept any responsibility for decisions incorrectly taken

There is a separate track: the winner may not publish other works in the period covered by this call, since the Instituto retains publication rights for two years from delivery of the publishable document
Results are announced at the end of November 2026, with the project running from 2 November 2026 to 3 September 2027
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online form published in the convocatoria, one for the individual scholarship and one for the group scholarship, with the project document in the specified format attached; queries to evelyn.sotomayor@pucp.pe.

scholarships.description: The Directorate of the Instituto Riva-Aguero, a research institute of the Pontificia Universidad Catolica del Peru, has published its 2027 research support call. Two modalities are offered: an individual research grant of PEN 10,000 and a group research grant of PEN 20,000, each for a maximum of ten months between 2 November 2026 and 3 September 2027. Project topics must fall within the institute's five research lines, covering Peruvian and Latin American history, the state and social processes, literature, art and cultural practices, tangible and intangible heritage, and philosophy, science and education in Peru. Winners must publish their results in a Scopus or Web of Science indexed journal or in an academic-press book, with their affiliation to the Instituto Riva-Aguero stated explicitly, and the individual modality requires the holder to supervise an undergraduate student assistant, which the institute presents as a way of promoting young researchers.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate scholarship form: registering in the PUCP 2027-1 doctoral admission process by 4 November 2026 IS the application, so you must first be admitted and have a PUCP thesis adviser committed before the grant can pay out. The package covers academic and registration fees and adds a S/ 4,000 monthly stipend for 12 months, renew-able twice, paid as a scholarship so it carries no withholdings. Scoring by the doctoral programme's Directing Committee runs 0-20 on your five-page research project, academic/research experience, two-page motivation essay and reference letters, and only scores of 18 or higher reach the VRI merit ranking, where each programme can end up with at most two grantees.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A master's graduate with a publishable doctoral research agenda who can relocate to Lima and commit to exclusive full-time study with no other full-time job.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure an ADMITIDO place in a PUCP doctorate and a named PUCP professor as thesis adviser before relying on the grant
Prepare the two-page statement of purpose and five-page research project early - page limits are hard
Ask your two referees well in advance because they must upload the letters themselves via Kissflow
Obtain the B2 English certificate before the 4 November 2026 registration deadline
Pay admission fees by 5 November 2026 (S/550 regular, S/150 PUCP graduates; non-PUCP applicants get better discounts before 18 September and 12 October)
Check whether the doctoral programme is Centrum PUCP or the Consorcio's Gestión Estratégica - both are excluded
common_rejection_risks: Failing the doctoral programme's own admission (no ADMITIDO status means no scholarship regardless of project quality)
Scoring below 18/20 on the rubric, which keeps the candidate out of selection entirely
Being second or lower in a programme that already has two stronger eligible candidates
Applying without a committed thesis adviser or a project unrelated to PUCP research groups and lines
Missing the page limits or the essay/letter content expected by part 4 of the rubric
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The admission registration fee (S/550 regular, S/150 PUCP graduates), relocation to Lima, visa, housing and transport above the S/ 4,000 monthly allowance, conference travel, and any thesis publication charges are not covered.
document_audit: Letters of recommendation must come from the referees themselves through Kissflow - an applicant-uploaded letter can invalidate the file
The essay may not exceed two pages and the project five pages; oversized files are a common self-inflicted wound
All data entered in the application form is declared under sworn statement (declaración jurada)
The English certificate must evidence B2 or its equivalent, not just coursework or informal proficiency
Everything travels through Kissflow, so give yourself time for platform account issues and upload confirmations
alerts: Registration for the 2027-1 cycle closes 4 November 2026 and the whole selection concluding 11 December 2026, so a late start cannot be recovered
The grant demands exclusive dedication: PUCP full-time teachers and anyone holding a full-time executive, research or administrative post inside or outside PUCP are excluded
Grantees cannot teach at any institution other than PUCP and may only lecture up to 3 credits per semester
Renewal is not automatic - it depends on the VRI's annual evaluation against monitoring milestones, and failing commitments can mean suspension and repayment of funds received
Expected results are binding: at least one first-author publication and one refereed oral conference presentation, plus thesis defence within 12 months of the grant ending
Results of the beneficiary list are final and inappealable
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register and upload the seven documents in the 2027-1 admission process on the Escuela de Posgrado portal with Kissflow as the document platform, then wait for eligibility review, programme evaluation and the VRI merit selection.

scholarships.name: Programa de Cooperacion Internacional del Gobierno de Chile para Policias Extranjeras Uniformadas (CECIPU)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a police-training award, not a university scholarship: selection is centralised in Santiago, results go to your Commander General in the second half of December, and unsuccessful applicants are simply never notified. The money covers your board and lodging in Chile - international airfare, complementary insurance and personal spending stay with you, and life insurance must already be in place before you apply. Two administrative points sink most files: every document must be merged into one PDF, and the authorisation letter must come from your institution's highest authority.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Serving officers, NCOs and enlisted personnel of uniformed (not civilian) police forces in participating countries who can work in Spanish at a medium-high level and want Chilean police training.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your life insurance and passport are both current and valid well beyond the course dates - both are mandatory
Obtain the authorisation letter from your National Director or Commander General early; it is the hardest signature to get in time
Complete the official medical and psychological certificates using the programme's own ficha medica and seleccion psicologica forms
Apostille or legalise your police clearance certificate well in advance - this is the slowest document for most applicants
Check the specific requirements and health conditions of the exact course you want in the current prospectus, since they vary
Merge every document into a single PDF before the 30 October 2026, 23:59 deadline and keep the automatic confirmation email with its registration number
common_rejection_risks: Applying through a civilian police institution, which the programme does not accept
Lacking medium/medium-high Spanish as a non-Spanish speaker - comprehension in speech and writing is required, not just survival Spanish
Uploading documents as separate files instead of one merged PDF, which blocks the portal submission
Missing the apostille or legalisation on the police clearance certificate
Assuming silence means pending: unsuccessful applicants are never notified, so only a call from your command confirms an award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International air tickets, complementary insurance and all personal expenses outside the scholarship; life insurance must be arranged and paid by the applicant.
document_audit: The photograph spec is strict - 9 x 12 cm, 300 dpi, full body, front view, in uniform, without headgear
The institutional CV has an official model on the postulacion page; free-format CVs risk rejection
The authorisation letter must be addressed to the CECIPU Executive Secretariat and signed by the highest police authority, not a local commander
alerts: The Secretariat's decision is explicitly unappealable and depends on available places - an eligible file can still be closed out
Formalising the application is legally taken as accepting the Requisitos, the Instructivo and everything on the CECIPU site, so read them before clicking submit
The window closes at 23:59 on 30 October 2026; the portal, not your command, is the only route
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Electronic form on the CECIPU portal with a single merged PDF of all documents; the Secretariat then reports selections directly to each applicant's police command in the second half of December.

What you can prepare now is the document set - notarised translations, health and HIV/AIDS certificates issued by your country's official health authority, recommendation letters, and a motivational essay in Kazakh, Russian or English. Master's and PhD applicants need IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 46 / TOEFL PBT 453 or an equivalent unless their previous degree was already taught in the language of the programme.

applicant_utility.summary: UPM's IGSS waives only 30-50% of PhD tuition and nothing else, so you must fund the remaining tuition plus all living costs in Malaysia yourself. Eligibility is strict: you must already hold a master's degree, hold no other scholarship or financial assistance, and be unemployed at the time of application. Start the supervisor support letter and the embassy letter early, because both must be in place before the August window closes. Academic staff at institutions with an MoU/MoA with UPM receive priority, so independent applicants compete for a limited pool of awards.

Ensure your supervisor and Dean/Director can complete the online endorsement before the closing date

scholarships.description: The School of Graduate Studies of Universiti Putra Malaysia awards the International Graduate Student Scholarship (IGSS) as a 30-50% tuition fee waiver for PhD students from Southeast Asia, South Asia, Central Asia, the Middle East and Africa. Funding covers up to three years (to the sixth semester) and is subject to an annual review of the student's academic progress. Priority is given to applicants from developing countries where UPM holds strategic importance and to staff of institutions with an MoU or MoA with UPM. Applicants must hold a master's degree, must not hold any other scholarship or financial assistance, must not be employed at the time of application, and must supply a supervisor support letter and an embassy letter confirming they receive no government or agency financial assistance.

applicant_utility.description: This is a school-run award, not a government one, so it does not compete with the CSC Type B route - but ZJU still routes every doctoral applicant through its own application system, and the International School of Medicine must be named as both your preferred college and your preferred programme or the dossier is not even considered. Expect the tier decision to be made at the video interview rather than in advance, and budget for a Yiwu address rather than Hangzhou, since the teaching base is in Yiwu. The monthly allowance stops the moment you are suspended or absent without leave for more than two weeks, so treat the attendance rules as part of the funding terms.
eligibility_tips: In the ZJU application system the preferred college must be 医学院 (Medical School) and the preferred programme must carry the 国际医学院 (International School of Medicine) suffix. Picking a different ZJU medical programme excludes you from this scholarship entirely.
You cannot hold any other scholarship simultaneously - this is stated twice on the page and is checked.

The English requirement depends on the programme language: English-taught programmes need IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 90 / Duolingo 120 or a Certificate of Instruction in English, while Chinese-taught programmes need HSK 5 (180 points).
application_tips: Send the scholarship form by email AND upload it in the ZJU system - the page states both must be completed before the deadline, and the email is the only emailed document that gets reviewed.
Use the exact email subject format: application number + passport name + programme name. Anything else risks the form being missed.

Pay the RMB 800 non-refundable application fee through the online system before the deadline; ZJU states applications without the fee are invalid, and that rule applies to scholarship applications too.
Time the physical examination carefully: it is only valid for six months, so an examination done in August is useless by a February deadline.
documents: Foreigner Physical Examination Record - a missing photo, cross-page seal, doctor's signature or hospital seal each individually invalidate the form, and the six-month validity window is tight against a February deadline.
Police clearance certificate - also six-month validity, so obtain it close to the deadline rather than early.
Personal statement in Chinese or English of not less than 1,500 words, plus two recommendation letters from full or associate professors with signature, phone and email on the letter.
mistakes_to_avoid: Mailing paper documents or emailing additional documents beyond the scholarship form. ZJU states posted hard copies and emailed documents will not be reviewed.
Applying to another ZJU college by mistake. The scholarship is exclusive to the International School of Medicine.
Assuming the scholarship follows you if you change institutions, programmes or study length after arriving in China - the terms state recipients may not change any of the three.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: Deadline is 28 February and results land in the ZJU system at the end of July or beginning of August, so there is a five-month gap in which you have no funding certainty and must not commit elsewhere. Keep in mind the scholarship can be retained for at most one year if you suspend for serious illness at university approval, but the living allowance stops during the suspension and return travel is at your own cost.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an employment-first scholarship: you must already be a regular employee of an academic, research, or government institution in a SEAMEO member country, and you enter through your national ministry, not directly through SEARCA. Your documents must reach your Ministry of (Higher) Education by 31 October 2026; only ministry-endorsed shortlisted applicants get iSCHO portal access in December. SEARCA publishes its entitlement categories (tuition, travel, thesis support, books, insurance, stipend for food/lodging/incidentals) but no peso or dollar figures, so build your budget around your study post's actual cost of living and confirm current allowance rates with ECL-GSID before resigning from other income sources.

scholarships.title: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (JSP)
scholarships.name: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (JSP)

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to ADB directly: you apply for admission to one of the 27 designated institutions, tell that institution you want ADB-JSP consideration, and submit at least six months before you intend to start. Check the hard barriers before investing time: you need at least two years of full-time professional experience after your bachelor's degree, you must be 35 or under, and you must commit to returning home for at least two years after graduating. Note what the award excludes: family expenses, extra-curricular courses or training, additional travel, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and computers are not covered, and admission by itself is not a scholarship award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career professionals under 35 from ADB borrowing/ODA-eligible countries with a strong bachelor's record, two years of work experience and a development-focused master's at a designated institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your nationality against ADB's published eligible-country list and confirm no developed-country dual citizenship
Confirm you meet the 35-year age limit and have two years of full-time post-degree professional experience
Choose a designated institution and programme, then request its application forms
Prepare income documents: latest income tax return or salary certification, plus certification of parents' income
Submit the institution application plus the ADB-JSP application sheet at least six months before your intended start
Do not resign from your job until the institution confirms you have been awarded the scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to ADB instead of through an academic institution
Missing the six-month lead time before the intake
Lacking the required two years of full-time professional working experience
Being over 35 without an exceptional Government of Japan endorsement
Incomplete or inaccurate documentation, which ADB warns can void an award even after selection
Assuming admission by the institution equals a scholarship award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Expenses for the scholar's family; extra-curricular courses or training; additional travel during the study program; supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships; and purchase of educational equipment such as computers
document_audit: Both the institution's own application and the ADB-JSP information sheet must reach the institution

The institution must formally endorse and rank you before ADB will consider your application

Only about 130 awards exist across 27 institutions, so institutional ranking is the effective competition
The two-year return-home service obligation is a condition of the award
ADB's main page states about 130 scholarships a year while its procedures page states about 135
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the designated institution with the ADB-JSP application sheet; the institution screens and ranks and sends its list to ADB; ADB recommends awardees to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval; the institution then informs all applicants of the outcome.

scholarships.description: The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program awards about 135 graduate scholarships a year for study in economics, business and management, science and technology and other development-related fields at 27 designated institutions in Asia and the Pacific, 17 of which are in Japan. The Japanese Government finances the programme and ADB administers it, including selecting awardees. Applicants apply directly to a designated institution, which screens and ranks them before ADB reviews the list and recommends awardees to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval.

scholarships.title: AICTE - Pragati Scholarship Scheme For Girl Students (Technical Degree)
scholarships.name: AICTE - Pragati Scholarship Scheme For Girl Students (Technical Degree)

applicant_utility.summary: Everything hinges on three numbers: two girls per family, Rs. 8 lakh per year maximum family income, and your 10+2 percentage, because selection is purely on that exam with 10th-standard marks and age only as tie-breakers. Apply on the National Scholarship Portal by 31 October 2026 and then make sure your institution actually verifies it - an unverified application is not considered even if perfect. Since payment is a single annual lump sum of Rs. 50,000 that also covers books, computer and stationery, treat it as a one-off yearly top-up rather than monthly support.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-year or lateral-entry girl students in AICTE-approved technical degree institutions from families with all-source income below Rs. 8 lakh per annum.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your year of admission qualifies: first-year or second-year through lateral entry only, and that the gap since passing 10+2 is within two years
Check that no more than one sister in your family is already drawing the scholarship, since two girls per family is the cap
Get the State or UT government income certificate issued for the current financial year, below Rs. 8 lakh from all sources
Complete NSP one-time registration and apply for AY 2026-27 before 31 October 2026
Follow up with the institute office for NSP verification, then the State/UT DTE second-level scrutiny
Diarise 15 November 2026 for defective and institute verification and 30 November 2026 for the DNO/SNO/MNO stage
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete applications, which are summarily rejected regardless of merit
An institute that never verifies the online application, so only verified applications are considered
A third girl sibling in the family qualifying, breaching the two-per-family cap
Family income above Rs. 8 lakh from any source during the current financial year
Holding any other scholarship, stipend, salary or emolument, which discontinues the award and requires full refund
Failing to get promoted, which forfeits the scholarship, or a CGPA being used incorrectly - conversion is CGPA x 9.5
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Hostel charges and medical charges, which carry no additional grant, and any living or travel expenses.
document_audit: The income certificate must be a State/UT government document for the current financial year, not a self-declaration
Merit is computed from the 10+2 or equivalent percentage, so keep that mark sheet exact
For renewal you must upload the passing certificate or mark sheet plus a letter from the Head of the Institution through NSP
Provisional merit-list queries must be raised within one month of publication; payment queries within six months
alerts: Awarding of this scholarship does not entitle the student to any other scholarship; if you win another, refund to AICTE via demand draft payable to the Member Secretary, AICTE at New Delhi
The quota is distributed State and UT-wise, with an additional open pool for 13 UTs and North-Eastern states, so competition varies sharply by domicile
There is a separate Pragati scheme for technical diploma students with the same pattern, so confirm which version your course falls under
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on NSP, apply for AY 2026-27 before 31 October 2026 with income certificate and 10+2 marks, then institute and DTE verification, then DBT payment.

scholarships.description: The Pragati Scholarship Scheme is implemented by the All India Council for Technical Education for girl students taking admission to AICTE-approved technical institutions at degree level. Each award is a lump sum of Rs 50,000 per year of study, given for up to four years for students admitted to the first year of a degree course and up to three years for degree students admitted through lateral entry. Eligibility is limited to female students from families with an annual income below Rs 8 lakh, with up to two girls per family eligible. The scheme is applied for through the National Scholarship Portal, which lists the award as open for academic year 2026-27 with student applications closing on 31 October 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an automatic tuition discount, not a competitive scholarship: apply for admission to one of the 15 listed Bachelor's degrees for any 2027 intake and, if you meet the entry requirements, the NZ$15,000 appears as a fee reduction on your offer of place. The money touches tuition only for the first year, so living costs, accommodation, insurance and travel stay entirely on you and later years of the degree are unfunded. Two eligibility traps decide most outcomes: Australian and New Zealand citizens and permanent residents are excluded, and students arriving through a partner institution's TNE or articulation pathway or with recognition of prior learning are not eligible. Apply by the international admission due date for your intake (31 October 2026 for Semester 1 2027; 1 May 2027 for Semester 2), because later applications are only considered if spaces remain.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School leavers and direct-entry students from outside Australia and New Zealand targeting one of the 15 listed 2027 Bachelor's degrees who want a tuition contribution without writing a scholarship application.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your chosen degree is on the 15-degree eligible list before applying; if it is not, look at the Toroa International Undergraduate Fee Scholarship instead

Check the 2027 admission due date for your exact intake and qualification - selected-entry degrees such as Bachelor of Nursing (31 January 2027) and Bachelor of Aviation Management (30 October 2026, international) close well before the standard date
Prepare officially verified identity documents (passport or birth certificate), academic transcripts translated into English with the grading scale shown, and your high school certificate
Book an English test early if you need one - undergraduate admission requires IELTS (Academic) 6.0 overall with no band below 5.5 or an accepted equivalent, and results are valid for 2 years
Decide upfront not to combine this grant with any other Massey scholarship or fee reduction, because the terms and conditions prohibit stacking
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a degree that is not on the eligible list - the grant simply never appears on the offer of place
Holding Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency, which excludes you regardless of where you actually live
Entering via a Massey partner institution's TNE or articulation programme, or with recognition of prior learning
Already being enrolled at Massey - the grant is only available at the offer stage
Dropping below full-time (120 credits) or withdrawing before the census date, which can cancel, prorate or withdraw the grant
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, accommodation, insurance and travel are not covered at all, and the grant funds only the first year of the degree - years two onwards carry full international tuition plus all personal costs.
document_audit: Overseas transcripts must include the grading scale and be translated into English - an untranslated transcript stalls the application
Massey may request verified hard copies or an Educational Credentials Evaluators report to establish New Zealand equivalency, so start verification early
A driver licence cannot be used to confirm identity and citizenship - use passport, birth certificate or citizenship certificate
If you already hold any scholarship, supply evidence of it with your admission application, as Massey's document list requires
alerts: The grant cannot be used in conjunction with any other Massey scholarship or fee reduction - compare it against the Toroa scholarship before committing
If you start in Semester 2 2027, the grant spans Semester 2 2027 and Semester 1 2028 and you must stay full-time in the same eligible programme across both
There is no cash value - the grant cannot be transferred, exchanged, deferred or refunded if unused
The University reserves the right to amend, suspend or withdraw the study grant where necessary
Status shows Open, but places in listed degrees can fill before the due date, so early application is the real deadline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit a single online admission application for an eligible degree; the grant needs no separate form and is decided at the offer stage, appearing on the offer of place as a tuition reduction.

applicant_utility.summary: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander postgraduates can apply for up to AUD 75,000 in top-up support for full-time study at a recognised overseas university, released semester by semester as long as academic progress holds. Because the award is explicitly supplementary, expect to self-fund or win additional funding for tuition and most living costs - the application itself forces you to disclose every other income source. The paperwork is the real filter: a sealed confirmation of Aboriginality and an Elder reference take weeks to arrange, so start both well before the 29 January 2027 close.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students with strong academic records and visible community engagement who hold, or are close to, a full-time place at a leading overseas university and need supplementary support rather than full-cost coverage.
application_readiness_checklist: Begin the sealed Confirmation of Aboriginality now - the Land Council chairperson or incorporated-organisation delegate signature is the slowest item in the checklist
Ask an Elder or senior community member early for the community reference, and brief your academic referees so their emails arrive before the deadline
Confirm each referee will send their reference directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au - applicant-forwarded references are a common failure point
Map the two-page personal statement to the three published prompts: motivation for the course, community identification and contributions, and tangible community benefit on return
Complete the budget template downloaded inside the application form, listing scholarships, wages, savings and any partner-institution funding
Request written enrolment confirmation from your overseas university, or written confirmation of your submitted application if the offer has not landed yet
common_rejection_risks: No sealed Confirmation of Aboriginality - Aurora states such applications are marked incomplete and will not be assessed
Any single required document missing at the 29 January close, which blocks the shortlisting process
References that never arrive from the referee's own email address
Academic references written by professional staff such as student success officers, which Aurora explicitly does not accept in place of lecturers, tutors or course coordinators
A community-benefit narrative that stays generic instead of showing concrete, applied outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Overseas tuition, flights, insurance and most day-to-day living costs. Aurora publishes no statement that the award covers tuition, travel or living expenses, so budget to fund the bulk of an overseas postgraduate course from other sources and treat the AUD 75,000 as a total cap, not an annual sum.
document_audit: The identity letter needs a common seal plus either a Land Council chairperson signature or an authorised delegate of an incorporated Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander organisation
The personal statement is capped at two pages and must answer all three published prompts, not just one
The budget template lives inside the application form and must disclose additional funding and income, not only planned spending
Transcripts must be official and current, and the headshot must be a high-resolution jpeg
Enrolment confirmation can be evidence of a submitted application at the time of applying, but some form of written university confirmation is mandatory
alerts: The round opened 5 October 2026 and shuts 29 January 2027 - the sealed identity letter is the usual bottleneck, so treat mid-December as the practical deadline for paperwork

Four different Roberta Sykes awards exist - the Scholarship (up to AUD 75,000), Fellowships (up to AUD 30,000), the Executive Scholarship (up to AUD 20,000, with the employer often asked to contribute up to 50%) and the Chief Executive Women Harvard Kennedy School scholarship - apply to the right one
The value is a cap, not a guarantee: 'up to' AUD 75,000, paid per semester or term and conditional on maintaining academic progress
Any recognised overseas university can qualify via the portal's 'Other' option, not only the named institutions such as Cambridge, Harvard, NYU, Oxford and UCL
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register or log in on Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal, open the Roberta Sykes Scholarship listing, click 'More & apply', upload the statement, CV, transcript, headshot, identity letter and budget template, and have referees email their references before the 29 January 2027 close.

applicant_utility.summary: PASS funds Pacific Island nationals to undertake agriculture, forestry and related research degrees at Fiji National University without leaving the region, pairing each scholar with an ACIAR project leader or co-supervisor so the research plugs into a live ACIAR project. The package is concrete: full tuition, a FJD 21,450 yearly living allowance (FJD 32,472 if accompanied), one-off book and establishment allowances, medical insurance, and a research grant of up to FJD 17,500 for Masters or FJD 40,000 for PhD. The application is more than a form: you must settle a research topic with both FNU and ACIAR supervisors and submit before 5pm FJT on 21 October 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Pacific Island nationals aged 35 or under (45 for PhD) with a relevant bachelor's or postgraduate degree who want a research degree in agriculture or forestry at home in the region.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the ACIAR Graduate Officer (aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj) to check eligibility before doing any paperwork

Draft the research intent with both supervisors and obtain their signatures
Assemble transcripts, certificates and citizenship evidence into one complete package before deadline day
common_rejection_risks: Applying without first checking eligibility with the ACIAR Graduate Officer
A research topic not agreed with both the FNU supervisor and the ACIAR project leader or co-supervisor
GPA shortfalls against the stated thresholds (3.0 for MSc Agriculture/Forestry; 3.5 for a coursework bachelor's; 4.0 for coursework master's or Honours routes)
Submission after 5pm FJT on 21 October 2026
Age over the 35/45 limit without an exceptional-case argument

Applications are submitted only by email, unlike the sibling schemes that use an online form, and the page requires a valid passport where the virology scheme accepts an expired copy. If you qualify, the work is compressed into a very short electronic window - the 2026/27 round was extended by only about two days - so have your national ID and secondary certificate in hand before it opens.

Prepare the student and parent/guardian undertaking signature in advance
Be ready to sit the admission test shortly after the mark-based preliminary shortlisting

Applying for a faculty outside the nine designated specialisms
Failing the admission test that follows the preliminary shortlisting on secondary-school totals

Because the allowance follows admission to a catalogue programme, your first task is securing a place in a FOAD programme run by an AUF member institution; the award is decided on merit or limited resources and is paid as partial reimbursement rather than up front. The 2026/27 window closed on 14 September 2026, so track the AUF calls platform and the catalogue for the next call instead of waiting for an invitation.

scholarships.title: Qatar University International Students Scholarship
scholarships.name: Qatar University International Students Scholarship

applicant_utility.summary: This is Qatar University's fully funded route for non-Qatari school leavers averaging 95% or above in high school: full tuition, textbook fees, shared housing with campus transport, a 500 QAR monthly salary, an annual round-trip ticket and a QU-sponsored residence permit. Everything hinges on two synchronized steps during the short March window - the online application in the 'Scholarship Application' section and the original high school transcript physically reaching QU's Admissions Department in Doha. As of 10 October 2026 the official timeline still shows the Fall 2026 dates (applications closed 25 March 2026) and marks the next round TBA, so re-check the timeline page from late February. Note that transfer, visiting, non-degree and second-degree applicants are excluded, so this route only suits first-time undergraduates.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-percentage international high school graduates (95%+ average) who have never enrolled at a university and want a fully funded QU bachelor's degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify early that your school grading converts to at least a 95% average under QU's evaluation - it is a hard cutoff, not a guideline

Complete the QU online admission application with the 'Scholarship Application' section filled in during the announced window (1-25 March for Fall 2026) and pay the QR 200 non-refundable application fee

Obtain a final, original, certified high school transcript and courier it to the Admissions Department, Qatar University, P.O. Box 2713, Doha, Qatar, allowing international transit time before the document deadline (26 March 2026 for Fall 2026)
Upload a passport copy through the online application and submit official IELTS/TOEFL and SAT/ACT or QU Math Placer reports if you have them, since the committee may weigh them
Prepare Foundation Program competency test reports if you want an exemption from the Foundation Program
common_rejection_risks: High school average below 95%, or a grading scale that cannot evidence 95% equivalency
Original transcript arriving at QU after the deadline - the application is not considered without it
Applying as a transfer, visiting, non-degree or second bachelor's degree applicant, all of which are excluded
Holding any other sponsorship or scholarship at the same time
Failing the first semester after the award, which cancels the scholarship outright
Dropping below a 3.0 cumulative GPA, below 12 credit hours in a semester, or breaking continuous Fall-Spring registration
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The QR 200 non-refundable admission application fee, plus personal spending beyond the 500 QAR monthly salary and provided housing (day-to-day personal items and any travel beyond the annual round-trip ticket).
document_audit: The transcript must be the original, final, official and certified copy - a photocopy or unofficial printout is not accepted
Non-Qatari applicants upload a passport copy; the Qatar ID route applies only to residents
A health certificate must be issued inside Qatar and be no more than six months old at examination
No scholarship essay, portfolio or recommendation letters are used for this award - only admission documents count, so extra material neither helps nor substitutes
alerts: The window lasts roughly three and a half weeks and opens only once a year for Fall entry; missing it means waiting a full academic year
Nominees first receive a conditional acceptance letter, and only after QU applies for the student visa does the final decision arrive by email
The 500 QAR monthly salary is modest on its own - the real value is the tuition exemption plus free housing, so weigh Doha living costs accordingly
Next-cycle dates were TBA at verification time; do not assume the March window repeats without checking the official timeline page
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online admission and scholarship application in March, original transcript couriered to Doha, competitive committee review after the deadline, conditional acceptance email, then final decision and QU-processed student visa.

scholarships.name: Government of Brunei Darussalam Scholarship to Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam (BDGS)

applicant_utility.summary: Brunei's BDGS is a genuinely complete package: full tuition fees, two economy air tickets, BND$500 a month personal allowance, BND$150 a month meals allowance, BND$600 a year for books, residential college accommodation, baggage allowance and comprehensive insurance for the whole programme. It is open to Diploma, Bachelor's and Master's students at five Brunei institutions, but the eligibility list is strict and unusually long: anyone who has previously studied or graduated in Brunei, Bruneians and Brunei Permanent Residents, dual citizens, and candidates currently employed by the Government of Brunei Darussalam are all excluded. The published 2026/2027 closing date was 15 February 2026, so the next round should open around December 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Genuinely incoming international students aged 25 or under for Diploma and Bachelor's programmes (35 or under for Master's) who have never studied or graduated in Brunei, and whose English proof is in place. Because the Ministry screens for study level, programme and institution as well as application completeness, this suits applicants who can pick their programme strictly from Brunei's published eligible list rather than trying to study anything they like.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme and study level (Diploma, Undergraduate Degree or Postgraduate Master's Degree) appear on the current eligible list
Confirm your age as at 1 July of the year the course starts: 25 or under for Diploma/Undergraduate, 35 or under for Master's
Confirm your English proof: Credit 6 at GCE 'O' Level, Grade 'C' in IGCSE English as second language, IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 550
Confirm you have never studied or graduated in Brunei, are not a Brunei Permanent Resident or citizen, and are not employed by the Government of Brunei Darussalam
Obtain certified true copies of your birth certificate, passport, certificates, testimonials and transcripts
Arrange certified English translations of anything not already in English
Identify referees C1 and C2 and request their references and recommendations
For Master's, prepare your Master's degree certificate, transcript and an outline of your proposed research topic
Complete the official BDGS Application Form and upload every document
If applying to UDB or UTB, complete the additional university portal application
common_rejection_risks: Submitting after the closing date, or an incomplete application - both are explicit ineligibility conditions
Having previously studied or graduated in Brunei, whether through your own studies or any prior programme
Being a Brunei Permanent Resident, a Brunei citizen or a dual Bruneian citizen
Being 26 or over at the start of the academic year for a Diploma or Bachelor's programme, or 36 or over for a Master's
Choosing a programme, study level or institution that is not on the eligible list
Applying for a Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' Level, Brunei Darussalam GCE 'A' Level, Polytechnic Diploma or Higher National Diploma to enter a Master's programme
Submitting transcripts that are incomplete, unofficial or inaccessible
Applying to UDB or UTB without completing the separate university portal application
Failing to certify translations of non-English documents
Missing the supplementary instructions that the Ministry attaches to the announcement

scholarships.name: Nazarbayev University Financial Aid and Scholarships for International Applicants — Foundation Year and Undergraduate programmes (2027–2028 cycle)

applicant_utility.summary: At Nazarbayev University the scholarship is a second competition you enter only after an admission offer exists: log into the Personal Account, click 'Submit Financial Support Application', and pick exactly one of six categories, because a below-minimum result in that category means the application is not considered at all. International applicants normally compete through the SAT/ACT category, and the official page fixes both the scores and the last acceptable test dates, so book an in-person SAT (by 5 December 2026) or ACT (by 28 November 2026) early. The prize is tuition coverage toward published fees of USD 12,000 (Foundation Year) or USD 15,000 (undergraduate), with the university separately estimating about USD 400 a month for living expenses that you must fund yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-scoring international school-leavers with strong in-person SAT/ACT, IB or A-Level results who can separately cover roughly USD 400 a month of living costs in Astana.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your category and that your result clears its minimum (SAT 1140/ACT 24 for NUFYP; SAT 1240/ACT 26 for undergraduate; IB 30 with 4,4,5 at HL; A-Level ABB)
Sit an in-person IELTS or TOEFL and have the electronic result sent to code NU (TOEFL iBT 6762) before applying - home editions are not accepted
Score the SAT/ACT in person before the published last dates (SAT 5 December 2026, ACT 28 November 2026) and have College Board send results to codes 7915/5521
Hold the admission offer first - financial support cannot be applied for before it
If choosing NUET, pay the 7,000 KZT fee inside the deadline or the application is not processed
common_rejection_risks: Submitting a financial support application without an admission offer, or paying the guarantee fee and accepting regular admission instead
Missing the category minimum by a small margin - there is no partial credit and the application is simply not considered
Remote or home-edition English tests, or results that expire before 1 August 2027
Changing documents after submission - the form and uploads are locked once submitted
Test-rules violations during NUET, which cancel results and block the financial support application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition share beyond the coverage granted, plus living costs of roughly USD 400 a month (dining about USD 300, dormitory about USD 55, transport, laundry, sports and additional medical insurance) and flights to Astana; the university publishes no stipend or travel allowance on these pages.
document_audit: Electronic test results must travel through the official channels (Testing Center for IELTS/TOEFL, College Board for SAT/ACT) and a scanned copy must also sit in the Personal Account - a scan alone is not enough
A-Level/NIS Grade 12 certificates must be final certificates issued in 2025 or 2026; provisional or earlier documents are not accepted
Results are read without superscoring, so do not assume best-section combining will lift you over the threshold
alerts: Only one financial support application is allowed per person, and the chosen category cannot be switched after submission
Accepting a regular fee-paying offer and paying the guarantee fee forfeits consideration for financial support
The deadline is published only as 'October 2026 - To be announced later', so check the page and your email regularly, including the Spam folder
NUET results have no appeal procedure and are released roughly six weeks after the test
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission offer first, then a single locked-in financial support application in the Personal Account under one category, with category documents uploaded; corrections, if any, are notified by email within a stated deadline.

scholarships.title: Brunei Darussalam Government Scholarship for Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam (BDGS)
scholarships.name: Brunei Darussalam Government Scholarship for Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam (BDGS)

applicant_utility.summary: BDGS (IS) is one of the few genuinely full awards in the region - government-borne tuition plus bursaries for accommodation, books, food and personal spending, government-hospital medical treatment and mission-arranged travel - but it is administered by annual announcement through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs portal rather than an open rolling form. The 2026/2027 portal now reads 'This application is now closed', so the practical move is to register interest with your country's Brunei Darussalam mission and watch the MFA page for the next announcement rather than applying on a fixed calendar. Note the level ceiling: PhD places at UBD run through the separate UBD Graduate Research Scholarship, so BDGS fits Bachelor's and Master's plans.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International students from any country who want a fully funded Bachelor's or Master's degree in Brunei Darussalam and can work through their Brunei Darussalam mission.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the Brunei Darussalam mission covering your country of origin and confirm it handles BDGS applications and travel
Research eligible Brunei institutions (UBD is the listed example) and your target programme's entry requirements and intake dates before the announcement
Prepare certified academic certificates, transcripts, identity/nationality proof and English proficiency evidence expected by the institution
Watch mfa.gov.bn/Pages/scholarship.aspx and apps.katalyst.gov.bn for the next session to open, and apply inside that window
common_rejection_risks: Being a Bruneian citizen and applying to the foreign-student scheme instead of BDGS (LS)
Aiming at PhD level, which sits under the UBD Graduate Research Scholarship rather than BDGS (IS)
Waiting for a publicised deadline - dates are not published in advance, they arrive with the annual announcement
Missing the institution's own entry requirements, since the award presupposes a place at an eligible Brunei institution
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: No amount figures are published, so budget for anything beyond the listed bursaries - personal extras, dependants' costs, and any expenses the mission-arranged travel does not include.
document_audit: The itemised document list is not published on the MFA or portal pages; the annual announcement and your mission define it - ask early
Nationality evidence matters: the scheme hinges on not being a Bruneian citizen
alerts: The 2026/2027 session is closed; the next window is expected to follow the same annual announcement pattern but carries no published date
The English proficiency thresholds published on MOE/UBD pages (for example IELTS 6.5) belong to the Bruneian-citizens scheme; BDGS (IS) applicants follow the institution's requirements
Travel is arranged through the mission, so build lead time for mission processing into any relocation plan
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Annual Ministry of Education / Ministry of Foreign Affairs announcement, then application through the MFA Katalyst portal with mission coordination; the award is tied to admission at the chosen Brunei institution.

scholarships.description: The Brunei Darussalam Government Scholarship for Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam, known as BDGS, is the Government of Brunei Darussalam's scholarship scheme for international applicants, administered by the Ministry of Education with applications handled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs through its Katalyst applicant portal. It covers undergraduate and postgraduate study at institutions in Brunei Darussalam, with tuition paid by the government plus bursaries for accommodation, books, food and personal spending, complementary medical treatment in Brunei government hospitals and travel arranged through Brunei's diplomatic missions. The applicant portal for the 2026/2027 session now displays that applications are closed, and the scheme is announced annually.

scholarships.title: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS)
scholarships.name: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS)

applicant_utility.summary: MASS is Mauritius's government scholarship for African students: tuition covered up to MUR 100,000 (SADC) or MUR 160,000 (non-SADC) a year, a MUR 16,500 monthly living allowance paid against attendance, and return airfare - but the caps mean you should expect to top up fees and living costs yourself. The application only exists through your own country's nominating agency, and you must already be applying to a listed Mauritian public institution, so the real work happens in parallel at home and in Mauritius. Once on island, original certificates within two weeks and a medical check within one month are hard post-arrival conditions.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African Union and African Commonwealth citizens aged 18-26 (or under 40 for postgraduate study) who hold or are applying for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution and can secure agency endorsement at home.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the nominating agency in your country (typically the Ministry of Education) and ask for its internal shortlist deadline, which falls before the Ministry's 27 March-style cut-off
Apply to a listed Mauritian public higher education institution in the same window and obtain a conditional offer or the application-fee receipt
Get birth certificate, passport biodata page, certificates and transcripts certified in advance
Have the medical certificate completed and stamped by a registered medical practitioner before submission
If your qualifying examination was not in English, book TOEFL (550/213/79) or IELTS 5.5 early
common_rejection_risks: Submitting directly to the Ministry instead of through the nominating agency, which disqualifies the file outright
Failing the age test measured at 1 January of the intake year (26 for undergraduate, 40 for postgraduate)
Missing the agency's shortlist round - each agency can endorse a maximum of fifteen candidates
Having no conditional offer and no application-fee receipt from a Mauritian institution
Assuming silence after six months means pending; the Ministry says treat it as not selected
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Fees above the MUR 100,000/160,000 annual cap, books, examination re-sits or repeats, and the gap between the MUR 16,500 monthly allowance and actual living costs; awardees are expected to arrive with funds for the one-way air ticket (refunded later on receipts) and at least USD 1,000 for the first three months.
document_audit: The application form must be completed electronically before printing - handwritten or altered forms risk rejection
Section 5 endorsement by the nominating agency is mandatory and must be complete
Original certificates must be produced in Mauritius within two weeks of arrival, so carry them, not just certified copies
Air ticket costs are refunded on arrival against original receipts, so keep every receipt from the journey
alerts: Taking up employment during the scholarship terminates the award and triggers refund of the whole amount paid
Any travel out of Mauritius needs at least two weeks' notice to the institution and the Ministry
The Ministry does not answer individual queries about selection outcomes
The Government reserves the right to offer no scholarship at all following a call
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the form, apply to a Mauritian institution, get the agency to endorse and transmit everything to the Ministry by its deadline, then await merit selection and the host institution's visa and entry-permit processing.

scholarships.deadline: No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline and communicates it to prospective applicants. For the 2026 edition the Mauritian public universities opened their own application windows from October 2025 and closed them between February and March 2026, so the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
scholarships.description: The Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme is the Government of Mauritius scholarship for African students, run by the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research and open to resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries. The 2026 edition funds Diploma, Bachelor's, MPhil and PhD study at public higher education institutions in Mauritius, paying tuition and course-related costs up to a published cap, a monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 and a return airfare, while requiring awardees to have already secured or applied for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution. Applications are routed through a nominating agency in the applicant's own country, so the Ministry does not accept direct applications.
scholarships.duration: Diploma up to three years, Bachelor's up to four years, MPhil up to two years plus six months for thesis defence, MPhil/PhD up to three years plus six months for the transfer report plus one year plus six months for the thesis defence, PhD up to three years plus six months
scholarships.application_period: Annual edition published by the Ministry, with applications made through the nominating agency in the applicant's country and in parallel with the chosen Mauritian public university's admission window

applicant_utility.summary: There is nothing to apply for here: the University assesses this scholarship automatically when you apply for admission, and the value shows up in your Letter of Offer, so your only real task is making sure your programme and circumstances stay inside the eligibility rules. The discount is 20% of the gross annual international tuition fee applied term by term after Census date - not a cash payment - and the page warns that the waiver may not appear on your tuition account until after census, so keep paying the expected amount minus the scholarship by each due date rather than waiting to see it. Because it is awarded on eligibility at the University's discretion, meeting every criterion still does not guarantee an offer, and the indicative 500 places vary with the eligible cohort.

Check you are not holding another University scholarship or external sponsorship, which would disqualify the automatic offer
Meet the Australian Government's financial-obligation requirements for full fee-paying international students and keep evidence ready if requested
common_rejection_risks: Enrolling in a quota-limited programme, which removes eligibility
Being sponsored by an external entity or holding an Australia Award, both excluded

Holding a separate University scholarship without prior special dispensation
Assuming automatic assessment guarantees an award - the University reserves the right not to award
