scholarships.funding_period: per school year (master's up to 18 months)

applicant_utility.summary: This Fulbright-García Robles regional call is geography-locked: you must originate from and live in Mexico's interior outside CDMX, Guadalajara and Monterrey, and any US residence or nationality, including dual status, disqualifies you. The money is an unlabelled pot of up to USD 37,000 per school year (master's, up to 18 months) or USD 25,000 (doctorate, up to three years) that you allocate yourself across tuition, fees, books and living costs, so your budget discipline matters more than any stipend label. You cannot arrive with a US admission in hand: existing admission or a conditional offer tied to an English course both exclude you, because COMEXUS pays and tracks applications at up to five universities on your behalf. Mind the long runway: applications close 15 January 2027, but studies cannot start before August 2028 without exception.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mexican nationals from interior states outside the three big metros, in STEM fields with strong grades (average 9/10) and an intermediate English level, who want the Commission to handle the US admission process.
application_readiness_checklist: Document origin and current residence in a state outside CDMX, Guadalajara and Monterrey (temporary moves there for postgraduate study still count as eligible).
Book TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo early so results are inside the published score bands and less than two years old when you apply.
Request the English graduation commitment letter from your university, stating completion no later than March 2028.
Alert your three recommenders in advance; letters are completed online and Spanish is accepted for this programme.
Compile tiras de materias for every degree; if studied outside Mexico, obtain official conversion of the average to the Mexican scale.
Keep the automatic confirmation email after clicking 'enviar solicitud' as proof that the application was received.
common_rejection_risks: Originating from or living in CDMX, Monterrey or Guadalajara and their conurbation areas.
Already holding a US university admission, or an offer conditioned on taking an English course.
US residence, US nationality or dual Mexican-US nationality; living, working or studying in the US; over one year of US residence in the past five years; a US bachelor's or master's.
English scores outside the bands (TOEFL iBT 61-79, IELTS Academic 5.0-6.5, Duolingo 95-110) or older than two years.
Being a former Fulbright-García Robles master's or PhD recipient.
Leaving the application incomplete and never clicking 'enviar solicitud', since COMEXUS disclaims responsibility for that step.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the unlabelled award, which may only be spent on maintenance per the State Department tabulator, tuition, fees and books: relocation beyond the transfers included in the English course, dependent expenses, and personal costs not covered by Fulbright ASPE insurance.
document_audit: Registrations from previous calls are deleted from the system, so create a new account at solicitudes.comexus.org.mx.
Recommendation letters are completed inside the online form, so give recommenders stable email access and advance notice.
If your tira de materias omits the average, add a separate average letter; foreign degrees need official conversion to the Mexican scale.
The graduation commitment letter must be in English and commit to a degree date no later than March 2028.
Applying in a field different from your previous degree requires an explicit justification in the essays.
Doctoral applicants must include a Spanish writing sample of up to 10,000 words.
alerts: Studies must begin in August 2028 without exception; if your timeline does not fit, this call is not for you.
Interview slots are fixed and cannot be changed, and the selection results are final (inapelables).
This award is mutually exclusive with the EducationUSA Opportunity Funds - if you are notified of both, you must choose one.
The intensive English course (3-9 months, starting January-March 2027) is subject to State Department approval and budget.
Employees and immediate relatives of the US Department of State, Mexico's SEP and SRE, and related agencies of both countries are ineligible.
First-stage results are sent to the registered email only; a dead inbox means a missed interview stage.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register at solicitudes.comexus.org.mx, complete the form with all documents and click 'enviar solicitud'; COMEXUS then pays and tracks admission applications at up to five universities, followed by expert-panel interviews (March-May 2027) and notifications in June 2027.

It funds a master's or doctorate in science, technology, engineering and mathematics at a US university for students starting in August 2028, with up to USD 37,000 per academic year for master's study lasting up to 18 months and up to USD 25,000 per academic year for doctoral study lasting up to three years, plus help with admission applications at up to five universities. The call is open from 2 September 2026 to 15 January 2027 and requires an intermediate level of English; applicants holding a US nationality or residence, or already admitted to a US university, are excluded.

applicant_utility.summary: This is three different programmes behind one page, and your route depends entirely on which track fits you: Mexican women heading a household apply for the Track A bachelor's scholarship (MXN 4,500 a month, MXN 2,000 a year for materials, a one-off MXN 20,000, plus ISSSTE medical cover), while Tracks B and C top up scholars who already hold a SECIHTI national postgraduate scholarship with one-off payments of MXN 20,000, MXN 15,000 and up to MXN 15,000 (plus MXN 15,000 for assistive devices under Track C). The 2026 windows have all closed and the page's 'Abierta' label is stale, so use the current cycle to assemble the awkward papers - community or disability certifications, registered research projects and family-status proofs - because those, not the form, are what slow applicants down. Banking registration and formalisation through the BECAS platform are mandatory steps before any payment lands.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mexican single mothers who are their family's main earners and are starting or finishing a public-university bachelor's degree (Track A), and current SECIHTI postgraduate scholars who identify as indigenous (Track B) or have a disability (Track C).
application_readiness_checklist: Identify your track first and download its Termino de Referencia PDF from the convocatoria page - the amounts, requirements and calendars differ per track
Track A: gather children's birth certificates, SNDIF disability ID for adult children with disabilities, marital-status proof and the sworn provider statement in the official format
Tracks B/C: request the indigenous-community constancia or SNDIF disability ID early, plus the signed and sealed institutional certificate of your registered research project or titulacion procedures
Register your bank account through the SECIHTI procedure and complete formalisation (CAB and Anexo Uno) inside the published window
Diarise the report deadline: the FAC-MMJF, FAC-PI or FAC-PDISC format is due to becasinclusion@secihti.mx by 31 January 2027
common_rejection_risks: Filing under the wrong track - Tracks B and C require an active SECIHTI beca de posgrado nacional, and Track A requires a presencial programme at a public IES
Community or disability certifications that lack the required signatories or institutional seal
Applying for the research (Apoyo 2) and titulacion (Apoyo 3) supports at the same time - the Terminos de Referencia forbid simultaneous requests
Missing the formalisation window or leaving bank-account registration unpaid/unregistered, which blocks payment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition is not covered by these tracks (Track A's one-off MXN 20,000 covers inscription, materials and transport as operating expenses), and living costs beyond Track A's MXN 4,500 monthly support, research costs beyond the published rubros, and travel are self-funded.
document_audit: Track B's community constancia must come from recognised indigenous traditional authorities, community representatives or municipal authorities and state origin, self-identification, ethnicity, community, municipality and state
Track C requires a current SNDIF disability ID, both sides
Research-project certificates must be on institutional letterhead with the programme coordinator's signature and institutional seal, and include the registration date and activity schedule
Once the inconsistency window closes, no changes or additions to a submitted application are accepted
alerts: The official page's 'Abierta' status is stale: all 2026 reception windows closed by 25 September 2026 at the latest
Three Avisos (18 August and two on 17 September 2026) moved track calendars - always read the Aviso PDFs before relying on dates
Track A validity runs 6 to 48 months and cannot be extended; only the remaining study time is funded if you started before the window

scholarships.title: Apoyo Complementario de Maternidad y Paternidad Nacional, en el Extranjero y de Consolidación 2026
scholarships.name: Apoyo Complementario de Maternidad y Paternidad Nacional, en el Extranjero y de Consolidación 2026

applicant_utility.summary: If you already hold a SECIHTI postgraduate or consolidation scholarship and your child was born, adopted or recognised between 1 December 2025 and 30 November 2026, this is a one-off MXN 43,876.35 top-up paid in a single exhibition - not a monthly scheme, and not a study scholarship - and the window stays open until 3 December 2026 at 23:59 Mexico City time. The application only works if your Perfil Unico CV is current, because you must attach to it, sign with your CURP and then chase any inconsistency inside Apeiron within five business days or the file is dismissed. Payment only starts after you formalise the CAB and Anexo Uno with a bank account in your own name, and it lands within 20 business days - except for December and January, which follow Hacienda's spending rules, so a late-2026 formalisation can mean a slower transfer.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Current SECIHTI postgraduate or consolidation scholarship holders (in Mexico or abroad) who became parents between December 2025 and November 2026.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your child's date of birth, adoption or recognition falls between 1 December 2025 and 30 November 2026 - outside that window the application does not qualify
Update or validate your CV in the Perfil Unico at rizoma.conahcyt.mx before starting
Obtain the certified Registro Civil birth/adoption certificate, the certified consular foreign-birth registration, or the guardianship judgment, showing the scholar parent's name
File through the SECIHTI BECAS platform per your track's Guia de Postulacion and sign electronically with your CURP
Monitor Apeiron daily: you get one five-business-day chance to fix any notified inconsistency
Register your bank account in your own name and sign the CAB and Anexo Uno promptly - payment follows formalisation
common_rejection_risks: Children born outside the 1 December 2025 - 30 November 2026 window
Any non-compliance report or arrears under the S190 programme, which bars processing
Receiving an equivalent state support for the same purpose - an explicit incompatibility
Letting the five-business-day inconsistency window lapse
Missing bank-account registration or CAB signature, which leaves the support unformalised and unpaid
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: This is a single MXN 43,876.35 payment for childcare - it does not replace your scholarship, and any costs beyond childcare (tuition, living, travel) remain covered only by your underlying beca.
document_audit: The birth or adoption certificate must be a certified copy from the Registro Civil and must show the scholar parent's name
Children born abroad need the certified registration before a Mexican consular office, not a local foreign certificate
Guardianship cases need the final judgment decreeing tutela
If both parents hold SECIHTI scholarships the support is assigned per child to each of them - check your household situation fits the per-child rule
alerts: The closing date is 3 December 2026 at 23:59 Mexico City time; days run 09:00-23:59 CDMX
December and January payments are subject to Hacienda spending rules, so formalise as early as possible
Results are published by bimestre (31 July 2026 and 30 September 2026 lists already out), so later bimestres can still deliver outcomes after the call closes
The two June 2026 Avisos moved the calendar for the consolidacion track only - confirm which calendar governs you
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Perfil Unico CV, then the BECAS-platform application signed with your CURP, one inconsistency-correction round in Apeiron, results by bimestre, then CAB/Anexo Uno formalisation with a registered bank account and payment within 20 business days.

scholarships.title: DOST-SEI Foreign Graduate Scholarships in Specialized Priority Fields in Science and Technology (Philippines)
scholarships.name: DOST-SEI Foreign Graduate Scholarships in Specialized Priority Fields in Science and Technology (Philippines)

applicant_utility.summary: This award is built for Filipino professionals who already hold a permanent or regular post: you need your head of office's endorsement and a research topic that maps onto DOST's Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda, so start with your employer rather than with the university. Treat the PHP 3,000,000 per academic year ceiling as a cap, not a promise - the Budgetary Requirements document has to justify every rate you claim with real quotes. File to the intake calendar: 15 August for a January-July start and 15 March for an August-December start, with results roughly two to four months after the panel interview.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Filipino researchers and engineers in the early years of their career who are permanently employed in the Philippines and want an MS or PhD abroad in a priority S&T field without severing their institutional ties.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the written recommendation of the Head of your Sending Institution before drafting anything else, since it is a hard requirement
Obtain the Letter of Admission from your foreign university first - the application is incomplete without it
Line up the two professor endorsements early (former college professors for MS, MS-programme professors for PhD) because they are independent of your employer
Build the Budgetary Requirements document from actual quotations from the host university so the ceiling is defensible
Book the PRC-licensed medical certificate and a valid NBI Clearance close to filing, since both are dated documents
Write the re-entry plan as a narrative tied to your current institution's needs, because the DOST Council scores it explicitly
common_rejection_risks: Lateral entry: applicants who already hold a graduate degree at the level applied for are excluded outright
Research topics that do not map onto HNRDA priority areas, which fail at the second-level DOST Council screening
A thin or generic re-entry plan, even when the research topic is strong
Missing employer recommendation or permission to take a leave of absence, which signals the sending institution is not committed
Availing of another scholarship at the same time, which is expressly prohibited
Missing the filing deadline: the advance copy must reach fgs@sei.dost.gov.ph before 15 March or 15 August, and originals must follow
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything above the maximum allotted budget of PHP 3,000,000 per academic year, plus costs the published privileges do not list such as visa fees, dependants' expenses and personal travel beyond the round-trip economy airfare.
document_audit: The Transcript of Records must be a certified true copy, not a plain photocopy or a scan of one
The medical certificate must show the physician's PRC license number; a signed letter without it is routinely rejected
The NBI Clearance must be valid on the day you file, so do not obtain it months in advance
The two professor endorsements must come from the right people for your level: college professors for MS applicants, MS-programme professors for PhD applicants
The Program of Study must be consistent with the admission letter from your foreign university
Original documents must physically reach DOST-SEI in Bicutan, Taguig City, so allow courier time after emailing the advance copy
alerts: Two hard filing dates govern the whole year: 15 March for the August-December intake and 15 August for the January-July intake - miss one and you wait roughly six months
You must not engage in any form of employment during the scholarship period, which rules out consulting or remote work on the side
Results follow the panel interview by months: December for the January-July intake and July for the August-December intake
No lateral entrants are considered, so a second graduate degree in the same field is not fundable here
Placement must be at a foreign university with a good track record in the specialized field, not simply any accredited institution
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the advance copy to fgs@sei.dost.gov.ph before the filing deadline, courier the originals to the Science Heritage Building in Bicutan, Taguig City, then pass documentary screening, DOST Council evaluation of the research topic and re-entry plan, and a panel interview.

scholarships.title: Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.name: Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation Scholarship

applicant_utility.summary: This is a small, need-weighted top-up of up to NZD 1,000 a year for South Pacific-born tertiary students, so treat it as part of a wider funding package rather than a main award. Eligibility turns on where you were born, not where you now live or study, so a student born in Samoa, Tonga, Niue, Fiji, Australia or New Zealand who is enrolling anywhere in New Zealand or the wider South Pacific qualifies on that test. Because the trustees size the grant to the need and cost of your course, a cheap certificate course and an expensive nursing degree will not be treated alike. Recipients can reapply every year, so a first success is a renewable relationship rather than a one-off.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A South Pacific-born tertiary student, at any level from certificate to bachelor's, whose course fees and living costs exceed their other support.
application_readiness_checklist: Download and read the Conditions for Application first, because the Federation refuses incomplete submissions outright
Gather proof of place of birth (birth certificate or passport) before you start the form
Request your 2027 course cost breakdown and any evidence of financial need early, since the trustees weigh both
Have the completed form and every required paper physically in the Federation's hands before 1 February 2027, not merely posted on that date
common_rejection_risks: Sending the form without the full set of papers listed in the Conditions for Application, which the Federation says means the application is not accepted at all
Submitting after 1 February 2027 or assuming a late posting date is enough
Assuming the award follows a set schedule: the trustees exercise discretion, so a strong financial-need case still needs to be evidenced
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, travel, and most or all of tuition: NZD 1,000 a year is a modest contribution against a New Zealand tertiary tuition bill, so the bulk of fees, accommodation and day-to-day costs must be met from other sources.
document_audit: The Conditions for Application is a separate download from the application form, and applicants routinely submit one without the other
Place-of-birth evidence must be documentary, not a statement in the form
alerts: The 2026 round is already closed; the live round is for the 2027 academic year and closes 1 February 2027
Recipients may reapply in later years, so keep the enrolment and cost evidence from this year for a future application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Download the form and conditions, assemble the papers, and post a complete paper application to the Federation so that it arrives before the 1 February 2027 closing date.

scholarships.deadline: 1 February 2027
scholarships.description: The Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation provides financial assistance to tertiary students born in the South Pacific region who want to study in New Zealand or elsewhere in the South Pacific. Scholarships of up to NZD 1,000 a year are granted according to the need and cost of the course, at the discretion of the Foundation's trustees. Successful recipients may apply again in any subsequent year. The Foundation was established in memory of Barbara Wood MBE, a former Dominion President of the New Zealand Federation of Country Women's Institutes who died in the Mt Erebus air disaster, and the programme is administered by the New Zealand Federation of Women's Institutes.
scholarships.duration: Annual award; recipients successful in one year may apply again in any subsequent year
scholarships.application_period: Applications for the 2027 academic year are open, with an application form published for that year. Applications close on 1 February 2027. Applications for the 2026 academic year have closed.

scholarships.title: Türkiye Scholarships - IsDB Joint Scholarship Program
scholarships.name: Türkiye Scholarships - IsDB Joint Scholarship Program
scholarships.funding: Fully Funded with Repayment Obligation at Associate and Bachelor's Level
scholarships.funding_type: Fully Funded with Repayment Obligation at Associate and Bachelor's Level

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate IsDB application: you file one ordinary Türkiye Scholarships application and switch on the joint programme by answering 'Yes' in the Joint Scholarship Programs section, so the ordinary academic and age bars apply. Your choices are confined to the departments, universities and countries on the IsDB list, published as a separate PDF per level, so check that list before you build your preferences. At associate and bachelor's level the support is repayable to the IsDB Education Trust after graduation and employment, so treat the master's and PhD routes as the grant-funded ones.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving students from IsDB member countries, or from Muslim communities in other countries, who want a fully serviced package (tuition, accommodation, stipend, insurance, a Turkish year and flights) at a Turkish university and who are under the age cap for their level.
application_readiness_checklist: Download the IsDB list of eligible departments, universities and countries for your level and shortlist only from that list
Check your age against the cap for your level - under 21 for associate and bachelor's, under 30 for master's, under 35 for PhD - as these are measured at application
Confirm your percentage meets the threshold for your level, including the 90% bar for Health Sciences (Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy)
Prepare documents in advance: diploma or temporary graduation certificate, transcript, identity document, and a photograph taken within the last year
For PhD, draft the research topic proposal and a written example of research you have carried out before the window opens
Check the language of instruction for your chosen programme, because English-medium programmes require an internationally accepted language certificate
common_rejection_risks: Being a Turkish citizen or having lost Turkish citizenship - an absolute bar
Already being enrolled at a Turkish university at the level of education you are applying for
Forgetting to answer 'Yes' under Joint Scholarship Programs, which silently removes you from the IsDB pool
Choosing a department, university or country that is not on the IsDB list for your level
Falling below the level-specific percentage, especially the 90% bar for Health Sciences
Submitting after 20 February - the window does not reopen mid-year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa and residence permit costs, personal travel beyond the single round-trip ticket, and any living costs above the stipend, since the programme's own pages do not quantify the stipend.
document_audit: National exam results are only needed if you have them; international qualifications such as SAT must meet the secondary-school completion minimums the awarding body lists
GRE, GMAT or SAT results are only required where the chosen university or programme demands them, so check the department page first
TOEFL or equivalent language results are only required where the chosen programme is taught in English or another language - confirm the language of instruction in the application system
Only PhD applicants need the research proposal and written research example; preparing them at other levels wastes effort

Every awardee without a C1 Turkish proficiency certificate, including those placed in English-medium programmes, must complete the one-year Turkish language course and reach C1 by the end of the first academic year
alerts: The 2026 round closed on 20 February 2026 - the window reopens around 10 January each year, so do not plan around a rolling deadline
At associate and bachelor's level the support is a loan repaid to the IsDB Education Trust in easy instalments after graduation and employment
It is a single Türkiye Scholarships application, so you compete inside one system for both the general and the joint programme
Only the departments and countries on the IsDB list are open to you - a strong CV for an unlisted department does not help
The programme's stipend is not published on its own pages, so model your budget on cost of living in Türkiye rather than on an advertised figure
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on TBBS, complete one application, answer 'Yes' under Joint Scholarship Programs, choose from the IsDB list, upload documents and submit before 20 February; results follow the Türkiye Scholarships selection calendar.

scholarships.deadline: 10 January - 20 February (annual window; the 2026 round closed on 20 February 2026)
scholarships.description: A Türkiye Scholarships programme co-funded by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities and the Islamic Development Bank, enabling high-achieving students from IsDB member countries and Muslim communities in other countries to study at internationally recognised universities in Türkiye. Scholarships are offered at associate, bachelor's, master's and PhD level and cover a monthly stipend, accommodation support, tuition fees, health insurance, a one-year Turkish language course and a one-time round-trip airfare. Associate and bachelor degree holders are required to repay the loan to the IsDB Education Trust after graduation and employment.
scholarships.duration: Associate degree programmes are two years as published; durations for bachelor's, master's and PhD programmes follow the length of the chosen programme and are not published on the official pages
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 application period ran 10 January to 20 February 2026. Türkiye Scholarships publishes a General Application Period of 10 January to 20 February in its Application Calendar, so the next window falls in January and February 2027.

scholarships.title: Perimeter Scholars International (PSI) Master's Program - Full Scholarship
scholarships.name: Perimeter Scholars International (PSI) Master's Program - Full Scholarship

applicant_utility.summary: Funding is not a separate competition here: if you are admitted you receive the full scholarship package, so put your effort into the application rather than into parallel fellowship applications before admission. The field is genuinely selective - several hundred applications for about 25 places - but the file itself is compact, so the referees and the statement of purpose do most of the work. Apply by 24 January 2027; the programme accepts late applications until positions are filled and even allows ELP scores to follow later, so a missing English test date is not automatically fatal.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Physics and mathematics undergraduates, and strong candidates from related fields, who want one intensive year of theoretical physics inside a research institute and a route into a Perimeter PhD.
application_readiness_checklist: Ask three referees early and brief them on your physics preparation, since letters arrive through an automated AJO email and late letters stall your file
Write the statement of purpose to the 5000-character limit, covering your reasons for applying, your preparation and your career goals
Check your background against the five named topics (classical mechanics, electromagnetism, special relativity, quantum mechanics, statistical physics) and evidence it in your CV
Book an ELP test if one is offered in your country, even though scores are optional at application
Do not mail hard-copy transcripts or anything else unless requested - the programme states it will not view unrequested hard copies
If you are Canadian, apply for the NSERC Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's before 1 December and discuss the outcome with Perimeter
common_rejection_risks: Referees who never receive or never act on the automated AJO email, leaving the application incomplete
A statement of purpose that describes ambition but not preparation - the committee reads it for evidence of ability and motivation
Applying from a non-physics degree without demonstrating the five required undergraduate topics anywhere in the file
Assuming the one-year format is lighter than a two-year master's: the assessment is continuous, with oral interviews for core courses
Leaving the ELP test until after the deadline on the assumption that scores can always follow
Confusing the PSI master's with PSI Start: you may apply to both but cannot hold both in the same year, and you cannot choose between them
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal expenses, travel to Waterloo beyond the published travel supplement, and any costs of additional English language training if your ELP scores fall below the University of Waterloo minimums.
document_audit: Transcripts may be unofficial at application, but if you cannot upload one at all you may substitute a 300-word summary of how you acquired the prerequisite background
A transcript in a language other than English needs an English translation - uncertified is acceptable at application, but a certified translation is required after acceptance
The Graduate School page refers to official transcripts while the How to Apply page says unofficial: follow the application portal and be ready to send sealed copies on request
Referees cannot see your application or your private information, so nothing in your uploads will prompt them - you must brief them yourself
The MSc itself is awarded by the University of Waterloo at its convocation; Perimeter cannot issue documentation of your UW degree completion
alerts: Late applications are considered until all positions are filled, so a missed deadline is a disadvantage rather than an absolute bar - but it is not guaranteed
ELP scores may be submitted after the deadline if the test was unavailable to you in time
Canadian applicants are expected to seek NSERC CGS-M funding first; if successful, part of it is applied to the PSI programme cost and the remainder is yours to use
Grades are credit/no-credit, which removes grade competition but also means external funders will read your referee letters
Perimeter cannot confirm completion of the University of Waterloo MSc - any official proof must come from Waterloo, around the end of August
PSI is presented as a pathway into a Perimeter PhD, so use the year to build relationships with potential supervisors
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online application with transcripts, CV, statement of purpose and three referees before 24 January 2027; shortlisted candidates attend a short oral interview, and admission carries the full scholarship automatically.

scholarships.name: Killam Fellowships Program (Fulbright Canada)

applicant_utility.summary: Budget for tuition yourself: as a direct-exchange student you keep paying your home university fees, and as a self-placed visiting student you pay host tuition, so the US$12,000 is a living-cost stipend rather than a scholarship. If your U.S. university is a Killam partner, the direct-exchange route runs on your home institution's internal deadline, which is almost always earlier than the 31 January open-competition cut-off, so confirm your campus calendar in September. The prize is genuinely competitive and document-heavy, with strict page limits and an advisor-signed cover form, so the application quality bar is in the paperwork as much as the transcript.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong sophomore or junior U.S. undergraduates who want a fully supported semester or year at a Canadian partner university and whose home campus exchange office is a Killam nominating institution.

Request the two references inside the online form and monitor whether referees have submitted, since unsubmitted references stall the file

Fellows receive a cash award of US$6,000 per semester, or US$12,000 for a full academic year, plus a health benefit plan for American Fellows, a three-day orientation in Ottawa and a three-day spring seminar in Washington. All Fellows may apply for a mobility grant of up to CAD 800 for an educational field trip. Fellows either pay their home university fees as direct exchange students or pay host tuition as self-placed visiting students, so the award is a stipend rather than a tuition scholarship.

scholarships.name: CSHL School of Biological Sciences Ph.D. Program (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)

applicant_utility.summary: Funding here is not a scholarship you compete for separately - admission carries it, with the School paying all tuition and associated study fees and a stipend currently $50,000 per year - so the entire effort belongs in the application itself. The file is unusually short: transcripts, a personal statement and three letters, with no GRE and no minimum GPA, and roughly nine places a year from a worldwide pool. Apply by 1 December for the following autumn; if you later win an external fellowship such as NSF or NIH your stipend rises to $55,000 or the fellowship amount, whichever is higher.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year students and recent graduates in any area of biology, or in computer science, engineering, mathematics, chemistry and physics, who want a small, mentorship-intensive biosciences PhD without writing a separate funding case.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up three recommenders early and brief them on your laboratory work, because letters are highly valued in the holistic review
Write the personal statement around concrete research experience and the challenges you have faced, since those are read explicitly
Check that your degree will actually be conferred before enrolment, as the School requires a bachelor's degree or equivalent by then
Only book TOEFL or IELTS if your previous university was not English-medium; the GRE is not required
Treat 1 December as a hard date and submit well before it, since review is tied to the annual cycle
Read the brochure and catalog as well as the How to Apply page, because the School points to them for process detail
common_rejection_risks: Weak or generic letters of recommendation, which the School says it values highly
A personal statement with no evidence of hands-on research or of obstacles overcome
Assuming a non-biology background is a barrier - it is not - while also failing to show genuine research engagement
Leaving English test scores until January if you come from a non-English-language university
Expecting a large cohort: with roughly nine students per entering class, admission is highly selective even though funding is automatic
Relying on grades alone: review is holistic and includes the types of courses you chose, so a non-linear path needs explaining, not hiding
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa and relocation costs beyond the published relocation support, and personal living expenses above the stipend; the School does not publish dependent or childcare costs.

TOEFL or IELTS is only needed if your previous university was not English-medium, and no minimum score is published
alerts: Funding is automatic on admission, so there is no second application to win money - but equally no partial award to fall back on
1 December is the submission deadline for the current cycle and the application portal is labelled for the following year's intake
Holding an external fellowship raises the stipend to $55,000, or the fellowship amount if higher, so keep fellowship applications alive after admission

The School also runs a separate BioAI PhD programme with its own rolling timeline, so check which programme fits your interests before applying

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to Posse yourself: a registered high school or community-based organisation in a Posse recruitment city has to nominate you, so the first move is to ask your counsellor whether your school is in Posse's nominating network and, if not, whether a local community organisation is. The award covers full tuition only at a Posse partner college, so housing, meals, books and travel remain yours to fund, and because Posse states it is neither minority nor need-based you should not expect the award to be scaled to your finances. Timelines are city-specific and nominations run in the spring and summer before senior year, so contact your local Posse office at the start of the calendar year rather than in the autumn of your senior year.

Living in a city with no active Posse programme, or with no registered nominating school or organisation

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a stand-alone scholarship but a set of 750 reserved places inside three existing Mineduc tuition scholarships, so the value you receive depends entirely on where you enrol: a Council of Rectors university pays your full reference tuition, accredited private institutions are capped at CLP 1,150,000 a year, and technical degrees at institutes run CLP 600,000-860,000. There is no separate portal or interview - you apply through the same FUAS form used for every Chilean student benefit, and assignment is decided against state records rather than a published score. Because results only arrive on 10 March 2027, plan to matriculate and cover early costs while you wait, and keep the 10-25 March 2027 appeal window free in case of a negative result.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Chilean first-year undergraduate students registered in the Registro Nacional de Discapacidad, in the lowest 70% income bracket, with a secondary-school average of 5.0 or above.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your entry in the Registro Nacional de Discapacidad (RND) is active before 31 December 2026 - registration after that date excludes you from the 2027 cycle
Check your Registro Social de Hogares tramo in Mi ChileAtiende with your RUN and ClaveÚnica, and activate ClaveÚnica if you do not have it
Complete the FUAS between 1 and 22 October 2026, entering household data accurately because the grant is decided against state records
Shortlist accredited institutions and verify their accreditation status as at 31 December 2026 on the Mineduc access site before enrolling
Diary the milestone dates: socioeconomic information 17 December 2026, preselection 15 January 2027, assignment 10 March 2027
common_rejection_risks: Not being inscribed in the RND by 31 December 2026, or a registration that does not match the name and RUN used in the FUAS
A secondary-school average below 5.0, or a prior technical or professional degree of higher-education level (including a terminal licenciatura)
Having previously received Mineduc tuition scholarships twice, including two first-year tuition scholarships, which bars a new arancel benefit
Applying for the same degree previously studied with Gratuidad - the benefit is only granted in a different degree
Matriculating at an institution that is not accredited as at 31 December 2026, or in a non-presencial programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The enrolment fee (matrícula) itself, living costs, transport, materials and any tuition above the applicable cap - at private institutions the arancel above CLP 1,150,000, and at technical institutes the arancel above CLP 860,000, remains the student's responsibility.
document_audit: The official pages publish no document checklist for this ficha - eligibility is verified against state databases (RND, RSH) rather than uploaded certificates, so any mismatch between those records and your FUAS entry is the real trap
If you have used Gratuidad before, be ready to evidence that the degree you now apply for is different
Keep your enrolment proof showing the 2027 arancel of the degree, since the amount is set against it
alerts: The 1-22 October 2026 window is the first application period only; late FUAS filers must wait for the second period, and results for that route are later in the cycle
Only 250 places exist for each of the three underlying scholarships, so meeting the requirements does not guarantee assignment
Quotas are explicitly subject to the annual budget law, so the number of places for the assignment year can change
If your result is negative, the only remedy published is the 10-25 March 2027 appeal period
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the FUAS online in October, Mineduc pulls your RND/RSH data, preselection results follow in January, you matriculate and accredit socioeconomic status, and the final assignment is published in March.

applicant_utility.summary: The Valech benefit is a statutory entitlement rather than a competition - there is no income test and no admissions score, so the real work is proving your connection to the Valech report and getting the paperwork variants right. A named holder receives the enrolment fee plus the full annual tuition, while a transferee at a private university is capped at CLP 1,150,000 and a technical-degree transferee at CLP 600,000. The transfer route splits into four documented variants depending on whether the holder is alive and whether posesión efectiva was granted, and choosing the wrong anexo stalls the file, so decide your exact route before the October window opens. Completing the general FUAS as well costs nothing extra and additionally opens the Junaeb food scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: People named in the Informe de la Comisión Valech who never used the benefit, and their children or grandchildren entering an in-person undergraduate degree.

Have the transfer form legalised before a notary - a plain signature is not accepted
Obtain the birth certificate, cédula de identidad on both sides, legalised licencia de enseñanza media and an enrolment proof that states the degree and the 2027 annual tuition

If the holder is deceased, obtain the death certificate and, where applicable, the posesión efectiva resolution; check whether the holder executed a notarial transfer while alive, since descendants of holders who died after 10 December 2009 without one cannot access the transfer route
Complete both the benefit-specific FUAS form and the general FUAS between 1 and 22 October 2026
common_rejection_risks: A family member having already drawn the benefit before you apply - the transfer is void once used
Filing under the wrong anexo variant, for example using the living-holder form when the holder is deceased
Missing notarial legalisation of the transfer form, which invalidates the document
An enrolment proof that does not state the degree and the annual tuition, leaving the grant unquantifiable
Enrolling at a non-accredited institution on a transfer or continuing-student route, or in Medicine, Pedagogy or Dentistry where the degree is not accredited or in process as at 31 January 2027
A holder who died after 10 December 2009 without executing the transfer while alive, which blocks descendants from the transfer route
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, transport and materials are not covered in any route; on the transfer route the annual tuition above CLP 1,150,000 (private universities and professional degrees) or above CLP 600,000 (technical degrees) is also the student's responsibility.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a capped state tuition discount rather than a living award: up to CLP 750,000 off your annual arancel, granted for the whole regulatory length of the degree, and aimed precisely at people who finished a higher technical programme in 2025 or 2026 and now want the professional title. You apply once through the FUAS in October, with no essay, interview or document upload, because Mineduc works from your form plus State databases. Treat it as a reduction you stack on top of gratuidad or a state credit, not as your complete funding plan, since the enrolment fee and everything above the cap stay on you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: 2025-2026 graduates of a Chilean higher technical programme in the 70% most vulnerable RSH tramo with a secondary-school average of at least 5.0 who want a related professional degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Before the FUAS closes on 22 October 2026, verify your household's Registro Social de Hogares tramo and refresh the RSH if household income or composition changed, because the socioeconomic determination lands on 17 December 2026 from State data.

Choose the professional degree and confirm both conditions: it is in a field related to your technical degree, and the institution was accredited as at 31 December 2026 (check Mineduc's accreditation lists before enrolling).
Confirm with the institution that the programme is presencial pregrado and is not offered as distance/semi-presential, special titulacion, postgraduate/postitulo or a 'plan especial de estudios'.
Make sure your ClaveUnica or FUAS password works before October; a locked account on the closing day costs you a full cycle.
Check your history of Mineduc first-year tuition scholarships: two prior awards as a first-year student disqualify you regardless of need.
common_rejection_risks: Enrolling in a programme the institution labels a special study plan, or in a distance or semi-presential modality, where the benefit simply does not apply.
Picking a professional degree in an unrelated field, which breaches the 'area del conocimiento afin' condition.
Enrolling at an institution that does not hold accreditation as at 31 December 2026, or in Medicine, Dentistry or Pedagogy where the degree itself must also be accredited.
The household falling outside the 70% most vulnerable tramo once the December socioeconomic determination runs on State records.
Having twice previously held a Mineduc arancel scholarship as a first-year student.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The matricula (enrolment fee) is explicitly outside the arancel, so you still pay it in full, plus any part of the annual arancel above CLP 750,000, plus all living costs, transport and study materials, none of which this benefit touches.
document_audit: There is no document upload at all, so an error in your RUT or household data inside the FUAS is a silent failure rather than a fixable rejection.
Your technical degree must have been completed during 2025 or 2026; keep the titulacion or egreso evidence at hand in case the institution asks when you accredit your situation.
Your secondary-school average (minimum 5.0) is verified against State records, not uploaded, so address any discrepancy in your school record early.
Save your FUAS submission reference after applying; it is what you cite during the narrow 10-25 March 2027 appeal window.
alerts: Timing trap: FUAS closes 22 October 2026 but assignment results only appear on 10 March 2027, months after you must enrol and pay, so arrange a bridge (gratuidad, a state credit or savings) before committing to an institution.
If you are an existing beneficiary rather than a new applicant, the 2026-cycle assignment, appeal and renewal results are published from 15 October 2026.
The appeal window runs only from 10 to 25 March 2027, with no later opportunity to fix a socioeconomic mismatch.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the FUAS online once between 1 and 22 October 2026; Mineduc then pulls State data, publishes socioeconomic levels on 17 December 2026 and preselection on 15 January 2027, you enrol and accredit your socioeconomic situation at the institution, and the final assignment is published on 10 March 2027.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a government-to-government route into Pakistani public and private universities for Bangladeshi nationals at Bachelor's, Master's and PhD level, and it is only worth preparing for if you accept a post-study service obligation to Bangladesh, because that obligation is a condition of the award. HEC publishes no stipend figure, so you should plan on the assumption that the monthly allowance may not cover your full living costs in Pakistan and keep a personal buffer. Because no closing date is published on the HEC pages, the window can open and shut at short notice, so check the Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor pages on the HEC site rather than relying on third-party listings. If any part of your education was completed outside Bangladesh, start your IBCC and HEC equivalence applications now, since they routinely take longer than the application window itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bangladeshi students with strong HSC, Bachelor's or Master's results who want a state-supported place at a Pakistani university and are willing to return home to serve afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your aggregate or CGP against the threshold for your level (60% for BS, 65% for Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy and Engineering, 3.00 CGP or 65% for Master's and PhD) and confirm your age is inside the 17-23 window for BS or under 35 for doctoral study
Start IBCC and HEC equivalence applications early if any qualification was obtained outside Bangladesh
Assemble mark sheets, transcripts and proof of Bangladeshi citizenship as clear scanned copies before the portal opens
Watch the HEC Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor pages weekly for the opening of the application window
Decide in advance whether you can accept the requirement to serve Bangladesh after graduation, and get the undertaking in writing if required
common_rejection_risks: Falling just below a level-specific threshold, particularly the 65% bar for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and engineering
Missing the IBCC or HEC equivalence certificate for a qualification obtained outside Bangladesh
Being outside the age window (17-23 for BS, 35 maximum for doctoral programmes)
Completing the qualifying examination after the closing date, which the published rules exclude
Submitting an incomplete portal application, since HEC routes everything through the scholarship portal with no paper fallback
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: HEC does not publish a stipend value, so the adequacy of the stipend against living costs in Pakistan cannot be checked. On the recorded package of tuition, stipend, hostel and mess charges, settlement allowance, air ticket and books, applicants should still expect to fund personal spending, visa and documentation fees, and any travel beyond the single provided ticket themselves.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form to fill in: your HKUST undergraduate admission application is the application, and applicants from nationalities HKUST treats as underrepresented are considered automatically, with the decision normally arriving alongside your offer. The award waives the full non-local tuition of HKD 260,000 per academic year for 2027/28 entry and is renewable across the degree as long as your academic performance stays satisfactory, but it pays nothing towards living costs, so you still need to fund roughly HKD 65,000 a year of personal expenses plus accommodation on your own. Because the top-up a School or Programme Office can add is capped at full tuition plus HK$65,000, the realistic ceiling on total support is about HKD 325,000 a year, and it is discretionary rather than promised. Apply by the 25 November 2026 Priority Round if you can, since later applicants are handled on a rolling basis from 26 November.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-local applicants to HKUST undergraduate programmes who hold a nationality HKUST treats as underrepresented and want a renewable full tuition waiver without a separate scholarship application.

common_rejection_risks: Assuming a separate scholarship application exists and therefore never having the admission application assessed properly - the admission application is the scholarship application
Holding a nationality that is not on HKUST's underrepresented list, in which case this particular award will not apply even though other admissions scholarships may
Missing the English Language Admissions Requirements, which are assessed at admission alongside the scholarship decision
Letting academic performance slip after enrolment, since the waiver is only renewable subject to satisfactory performance

applicant_utility.summary: This is a 40% tuition discount rather than a living grant, so treat it as a fee reduction and fund your own flights, accommodation and day-to-day costs. You do not apply for it separately: apply to Curtin through a registered agent or directly to Curtin online, and Global Admissions automatically assesses qualifying applications, confirming success by supplementary letter with your Letter of Offer. The bar is a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in your most recent eligible study, and Curtin decides equivalence itself, so a strong but slightly lower average is unlikely to qualify. Check the excluded course list before you commit to a programme, because medicine, nursing, paramedicine, oral health therapy, dietetics, occupational therapy, social work and the psychology and taxation masters are all carved out.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international fee-paying students, not sponsored, with a 95% CWA or equivalent, entering a non-excluded Curtin undergraduate or coursework Master's at a Western Australian campus in 2027 or 2028.

Deferring studies beyond the study period and year offered, which forfeits the award
Failing to pay the full Deposit or to accept and enrol by the date specified in the Letter of Offer
Dropping below Good Standing or a 70% CWA from the second study period onwards, or withdrawing/going AWOL, all of which can trigger revocation and leave you liable for outstanding tuition

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-off grant of $1,000 to $3,000 whose size is fixed entirely by the NZQCF level you are studying at, so the single biggest thing you control is how your qualification is levelled on the NZQF. The panel says plainly that it is not looking for perfect grades and instead weighs why you returned to study, where you are heading, and what the money will let you do. Because applicants can hold only one award per level of study, a certificate graduate who later enrols in a degree can apply again at the higher level. Applications for the 2026 round closed at 11.59 pm on 25 August 2026 and every applicant hears back by email in October 2026, with no next opening date published yet.

scholarships.name: Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund

applicant_utility.summary: With $4,000 as the ceiling and an 18-day window, this award rewards applicants who have already thought their project through. The selection panel is looking for three things: your track record on the issue, a clear account of how the initiative advances peace in New Zealand, and a timeline and budget that show the money will actually be spent. Unlike the Trust's education awards, entry is open to unincorporated groups, individuals enrolled at a tertiary institution, and formal organisations, so you do not need legal entity status to apply, but if a group applies the project leader must be a woman. Note that prior Trust recipients are excluded entirely, so this is a once-per-person opportunity within the Trust's portfolio.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A woman or female-led group with a concrete, near-ready peace-building project － mediation, conflict resolution, inter-community work, or eliminating family violence － that can be delivered with up to $4,000.

Confirm no one on the leadership team has previously received a New Horizons for Women award

common_rejection_risks: Applying after 30 October 2026: the window is fixed and short, and no extension is published

A group application whose project leader is not a woman, which is not eligible
Applying as a previous Trust award recipient, which the Trust excludes outright

Other Trust awards cannot be held simultaneously with this one

scholarships.title: ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship
scholarships.name: ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship

applicant_utility.summary: This award exists to break the English barrier that blocks newly arrived refugees from tertiary study or work in Australia, and it covers tuition, materials and administrative fees for 11-12 weeks of classes with no cash value attached. Only two scholarships per campus are released every three sessions, so competition is tight at each campus even though applications are accepted all year. You will be placed by placement test, not by prior qualification, and the practical trap is the 48-hour window: once an offer email arrives you must accept it within two days or the place goes to someone else. If you cannot travel to a campus, ask about the online ILSC Hello option, since the page now explicitly extends scholarships to those courses.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Refugees aged 18 or over living near Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Sydney or Perth, or able to study online, who need funded English to unlock further study or employment.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your visa is one of the listed humanitarian subclasses (200, 201, 202, 203, 204, 785, 790, 851, 866) or the relevant bridging visa, and have the evidence ready
Confirm you have never held the ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship before and have not received a Centrelink Relocation Grant
Submit the online application, then watch for the placement test link email and complete it before the stated deadline
Keep your inbox free around the offer stage so you can accept within 48 hours
Check that you can commit to 80% attendance across the three sessions and to a start date that cannot be deferred
common_rejection_risks: Holding a visa subclass that is not on the published list, which rules out eligibility entirely
Having previously received the ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship, or a Centrelink Relocation Grant, both of which are disqualifying
Missing the placement test deadline buried in the notification email, which stalls the application
Missing the 48-hour offer acceptance window and losing the place to another candidate
Being under 18 at the commencement of studies
document_audit: Visa evidence is the gatekeeper: the grant letter, ImmiCard or bridging visa notice must clearly match the subclass numbers ILSC lists, so keep it current and legible
There is no academic transcript requirement, so do not delay applying while chasing overseas documents
The placement test link arrives by email with its own deadline, so use an email address you check daily
alerts: Two scholarships per campus every three sessions means a campus can run out of places for months at a time
The offer must be accepted within 48 hours or it is withdrawn and offered to another candidate
Confirmed start dates cannot be deferred, and course selections and timetables depend on availability at enrolment
Attendance below 80% breaches the terms, and the scholarship cannot be exchanged for cash
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online application on ILSC's Humanitarian Scholarship page, complete the placement test from the emailed link before its deadline, then wait for committee selection and accept any offer within 48 hours.

scholarships.name: Joint Algeria/Ghana Government Scholarship Awards 2026/2027 (tenable in Algeria)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a paper-plus-portal application: you register on the Ghana Scholarships Authority website under the Algerian Government Scholarship, print the form, and physically submit it with your WASSCE result slips, birth certificate and transcript to the Authority in North Ridge, Accra, so an online-only submission is not enough. The gates are numeric and unforgiving - a WASSCE aggregate of 13 or better from the 2025 result and an age of 23 or below - and they are applied as published conditions rather than guidelines. Be aware that the published deadline of 21 September 2026 has already passed, so treat the Open label on the page with caution and confirm with the Authority whether a further round will be advertised. If you are admitted to the Islamic Studies or religious studies streams, build a year of French language training into your plans before your main course begins.

With a deadline of 28 October 2026 and publication on 28 September 2026, you have about a month, so open the Study in Saudi platform today and read the terms and conditions for the specific university and programme you want before you start. Start your passport immediately if you do not hold one, because it is a stated requirement.

scholarships.name: Heydar Aliyev International Education Grant (Study in Azerbaijan project)
scholarships.funding_period: per month for 10 months a year, excluding July and August

applicant_utility.summary: The decisive step happens in your own country: your file only enters evaluation once your education ministry or the Azerbaijani embassy nominates you, so open that conversation by February-March, well before April. The package is comprehensive - tuition, 800 AZN per month for 10 months, 200 AZN yearly medical allowance, an annual economy flight, visa and residence permit - but the call states any expense outside the published list is not reimbursed, so budget for the two unpaid summer months and personal costs. With only 100 grants across all eligible countries and all study levels, nomination alone does not guarantee selection.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants aged under 35 (bachelor), 40 (master) or 45 (PhD) from OIC, Non-Aligned Movement, small-island or culturally-linked countries with strong grades (GPA 70+) who want a fully funded degree in Baku and can clear a modest IELTS 5.0-5.5 bar.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the eligible country list (Annex 2 of the official call) before preparing anything else
Contact your education ministry or the Azerbaijani embassy in your country early - their review and nomination step runs before your own deadline
Have diplomas and transcripts notarized, with notarized English translation if they are not in Azerbaijani, Turkish, English or Russian
Time the medical certificate within 3 months of submission and ensure HIV/AIDS and Hepatitis B/C results are included
Draft the CV and motivation letter in an accepted language and keep everything as clean PDFs ready for the SIACAS upload
common_rejection_risks: No government nomination: applications sent directly to universities or to the Study in Azerbaijan office do not enter the evaluation process
GPA below the hard 70/100 (or 7/10) threshold in any previous degree
Age ceiling passed as of 15 September of the intake year (35 / 40 / 45 by level)
Medical certificate older than 3 months or missing the HIV/AIDS and Hepatitis B/C tests
Documents not notarized, in a non-accepted language without certified translation, or uploaded after the SIACAS deadline
Failing to confirm acceptance in SIACAS within the given window after selection - the award is then reassigned to another applicant
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The call states that any expense not specified will not be covered or reimbursed by the Government of Azerbaijan: practically, July and August living costs (the monthly allowance is paid for 10 months only), personal spending, and any costs incurred before the scholarship grant is formalized.
document_audit: The first-stage nomination form (Annex 1 of the call) goes to your home authority and is separate from the SIACAS upload
Diplomas and transcripts must be notarized copies in Azerbaijani, Turkish, English or Russian, otherwise accompanied by a notarized translation into English
The medical certificate must be issued by a clinic in your country of residence, dated no more than 3 months before submission, and include HIV/AIDS and Hepatitis B/C results
Passport must be valid and clearly show your identification information
Motivation letter and CV are mandatory uploads; local and international awards are requested if available
alerts: The 'Apply' form on the Study in Azerbaijan website explicitly states it is not a registration form for any scholarship programme - the real route is government nomination plus SIACAS registration

The 2026/2027 cycle is fully closed (nomination ended 15 April 2026, SIACAS registration 10 June 2026, academic year began 15 September 2026); the next call is expected around February 2027 on the same schedule
The flight benefit covers one round trip per year only - additional trips home are at your own expense
Citizens of China, Romania, Kazakhstan, Hungary, Kyrgyzstan, Somalia and Uzbekistan follow separate intergovernmental scholarship schemes rather than this grant

scholarships.title: Government of Guyana Scholarships
scholarships.name: Government of Guyana Scholarships

applicant_utility.summary: This is not one scholarship but a rolling series of separately advertised awards, so the practical task is monitoring the Ministry's scholarship page and the newspapers for an advertisement that matches your qualification. Nothing here is a form you can fill in on a fixed annual date: each award opens and closes on its own schedule, and the last several rounds closed between March and September 2026. Budget your preparation around having a valid Guyanese passport and an unconditional acceptance letter in hand before an advert appears, because most awards ask for both at the point of application. Remember that accepting an award means signing a bond that commits you to public sector service afterwards, so treat it as a career decision and not just a funding decision.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Guyanese nationals who already hold, or can realistically secure, an unconditional offer from the named institution and who are willing to serve in the Guyanese public sector on a contract after graduating.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the Ministry's Government of Guyana scholarships page at least weekly and set a standing alert on mps.gov.gy, since awards appear and close with only weeks of notice
Confirm your Guyanese passport is valid well beyond the expected programme start date, and renew it now if it is not
Line up your transcripts and certificates as clean scans so you can attach them the day an advert opens
Register on the online scholarship portal and verify you can log in before the round you want opens

Read each advert for its own age cap, GPA floor and language rule - the Japan, Indonesia and China postgraduate offers all set 35 years or under and a 3.0 GPA, while the Chile offers add Spanish fluency
Read the bond terms and be certain you accept a public sector service obligation before you submit
common_rejection_risks: Applying to an award whose age cap you have already passed - the caps differ by award (25, 35, or below 40 as of a stated date for Azerbaijan) and are set at the time of application
Supplying a conditional or provisional acceptance letter where the advert requires an unconditional one
Missing a language condition, most obviously the requirement to speak, read and write Spanish for the Guyana-Chile awards
Falling short of the 3.0 GPA floor on a 4-point-style transcript where your grading scale does not translate straightforwardly
Waiting for an advert in your field instead of applying to the nearest eligible discipline - the fields are fixed and narrow
Not being registered on the portal when a short window opens, so losing days to account setup
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is published as fully funded, covering full tuition plus allowances for books, outfit and travelling and compensation for any other programme cost, so no specific uncovered cost is identified. Donor-funded awards, however, are published as full or partial depending on the award, so confirm in writing which cover applies and what the 'other cost' compensation reaches - insurance, relocation and visa costs for overseas awards are not named in the published wording.
document_audit: Your passport must be valid, not merely present - an expired or soon-expiring passport will not satisfy the advert condition
The acceptance letter must be unconditional; an offer conditional on funding or on results will not meet the requirement
Transcripts must evidence the GPA named in the advert, so obtain a grading scale explanation if your institution does not report a 4.0-style GPA
CSEC and CAPE results are needed for the undergraduate offers, including the minimum five CSEC subjects inclusive of English Language and Mathematics with Grades I or II
For continuing technical institute students, evidence of passes in all completed courses is required
alerts: Every award listed on the Ministry page is currently marked Closed, so treat any plan built on this scheme as dependent on a new advertisement appearing
Closing dates in recent rounds fell as early as March and as late as September, so there is no predictable annual window to plan around
The bond and the guaranteed public sector job are contractual - check what service period and terms are attached before you accept
Donor-funded awards under the same umbrella can be partial, so do not assume the fully funded wording applies to every advertisement you see
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Spot an advertisement, register or log in on the online scholarship portal, complete the online application for that specific award, upload the named documents, and wait for the Ministry's published outcome; there is no single annual intake.

scholarships.name: National Scholarship Programme of the Slovak Republic (Národný štipendijný program SR, NŠP)
scholarships.degree: Not applicable (mobility scholarship for study, research or artistic stays; no degree is awarded)
scholarships.degree_levels: Not applicable (mobility scholarship for study, research or artistic stays; no degree is awarded)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a living-cost stipend, not a full scholarship: incoming master's students receive a fixed 620 EUR per month and incoming doctoral candidates and teachers/researchers 1 025.50-1 470 EUR per month, while outgoing Slovak-based applicants receive country-based rates ranging from 350 EUR (Ukraine) to 2 200 EUR (Switzerland, Liechtenstein, USA postdocs). Two deadlines operate each year, 30 April and 31 October at 16:00 CET, and a distance-based travel grant of up to 1 500 EUR can be requested together with the scholarship. Money is paid monthly, so budget for tuition, visa and insurance costs yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Slovak-resident students, doctoral candidates and postdocs planning a 1-10 month stay abroad, and foreign students, researchers, teachers and artists who already have or can obtain a genuine invitation from a Slovak host institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the acceptance/invitation letter early and check its date: letters, recommendations and enrolment confirmations must be under 3 months old on deadline day
For the incoming track, allow postal time: the original letter must physically reach SAIA in Bratislava by 12:00 on the 3rd working day after the deadline, not just be uploaded
Watch the online system opening (at least 6 weeks before each deadline) and do not leave submission to the final hours, when system load has caused missed deadlines
Plan the stay within the published window: for the current round, starts between 1 February and 1 April 2027 (students) or 31 August 2027 (others), ending by 31 August / 30 November 2027
Confirm you are not double-funded: concurrent publicly funded mobility such as Erasmus+ or CEEPUS is excluded, and previous NSP holders must wait 2 years before reapplying
common_rejection_risks: Missing or late mandatory attachments: the application is assessed exactly as submitted with no chance to correct, so an incomplete file fails on formal grounds regardless of quality
Recommendation, acceptance or enrolment documents older than 3 months on the deadline day
Incoming applicants whose original acceptance letter never arrives at SAIA within the 3-working-day window
Applicants who spent 15 or more of the previous 36 months in Slovakia, or who were admitted to a full degree programme, and are therefore ineligible
Stay plans shorter than a whole calendar month or inconsistent with the acceptance letter dates
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, visa and residence-permit costs, health insurance, flights and relocation beyond the travel-grant lump sum, and any gap between the stipend and local rents, which the applicant must cover personally.
document_audit: Recommendations must be on institutional letterhead (or clearly identify the institution), signed by hand or with a verifiable electronic signature, and carry the referee's role and contact details
Enrolment and employment confirmations must be issued by the institution, signed, and include year, form of study, standard duration and expected completion date

Documents in languages other than Slovak, Czech or English (outgoing) or Slovak or English (incoming) need official or institution-confirmed translations; only a working translation is accepted for the acceptance letter under force-majeure exceptions
Incoming applicants must upload a scan of the acceptance letter even when the host institution posts the original, otherwise the application cannot be submitted
alerts: Deadlines are 16:00 Central European Time, not midnight, and awards to stays in the Russian Federation remain suspended

After the award, changing the country of stay or host institution is not allowed and extending the approved support is impossible; only shortening or moving dates is possible with the administrator's consent
Stays longer than 6 months require an interim stay report, and part of the final instalment can be withheld until the final report and stay-completion confirmation are submitted
Results are normally announced within 8 weeks of the deadline, and a reserve list may be used if funds free up
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the online form on stipendia.sk (Slovak-based applicants) or scholarships.sk (foreign applicants), upload every mandatory attachment, press Send before 16:00 CET on deadline day; foreign applicants then post the original acceptance letter to SAIA, and decisions follow about 8 weeks later.
