scholarships.title: GETFund Postgraduate Foreign Scholarship (Ghana Education Trust Fund)
scholarships.name: GETFund Postgraduate Foreign Scholarship (Ghana Education Trust Fund)

applicant_utility.summary: This award is aimed at Ghanaian first-degree holders who already have, or can secure, admission to a Master's programme abroad, and the evidence is weighted towards STEM and towards women. The application is entirely portal-based and the documents are vetted before shortlisting, so the practical bottleneck is document quality rather than essays. Note that GETFund leaves the money deliberately vague: coverage is described as tuition, accommodation and scholastic materials, with a stipend only 'sometimes' and the exact partial-or-full position given only on award. Because the 2026/2027 foreign window closed on 30 April 2026, your immediate action is to watch the news page for the 2027/2028 announcement rather than to prepare a late submission.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Ghanaian graduates with at least a second-class first degree and an unconditional or financial-condition offer from an accredited overseas university, ideally in STEM or as a woman, who need tuition and living support to take it up.
application_readiness_checklist: Create and verify your GETFund scholarship portal profile now, so the account is ready when the next foreign round opens
Obtain an admission letter from an accredited university - only unconditional and financial condition letters are accepted, so request this format explicitly from your university
Request the official fee schedule from the university at the same time as the admission letter; both are needed
Draft the project or research proposal to a strict five-page maximum and check that it fits the priority areas
Line up an occupational letter of recommendation and confirm your referees are willing and reachable
Check that your Ghana Card, passport bio page and National Service certificate are current and legible as scans
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an admission letter in the wrong format - only unconditional and financial condition letters are accepted, so provisional or conditional-on-funding letters are rejected
Omitting the fee schedule, which GETFund lists alongside the admission letter as academic documentation
Uploading invisible or unclear scans, which GETFund names explicitly as a disqualifying factor
Exceeding the five-page research proposal limit
Submitting multiple applications, which GETFund describes as instant disqualification
Applying again in the same category if you were already a GETFund Foreign Scholarship beneficiary
Being unable to start by the beginning of the academic year, or already pursuing another Master's or PhD when you apply
Missing the closing date - late and incomplete applications are not considered for assessment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: GETFund states that the foreign scholarship typically covers tuition, accommodation and sometimes a stipend for living expenses, with the exact partial or full position provided only on award. Travel costs, visas and personal expenses are not named anywhere in the published coverage, so plan to fund airfare and visa costs yourself until you have the award terms in writing. Local scholarships under the same programme are explicitly tuition fees only, so do not assume the foreign award behaves identically.
document_audit: Your admission letter must be unconditional or a financial condition letter; anything weaker will not pass vetting
The fee schedule must accompany the admission letter - universities often issue it separately, so chase it early
Certificates and transcripts are required 'where applicable', but omit them only where genuinely not applicable, since missing documentation is a named disqualifier
The research proposal has a hard five-page ceiling, and it is required even at Master's level
The occupational letter of recommendation and the employer's academic leave support letter must come from the right sources; the leave letter is only required where applicable
Every upload must be legible - GETFund specifically disqualifies invisible or unclear documents
alerts: The 2026/2027 foreign round closed on 30 April 2026, so the scheme is not currently accepting applications; the next foreign call is expected in the first half of 2027
Deferment is not permitted - the scholarship must be used for the academic year awarded, so align your offer's start date with the award year
GETFund has separately opened 2026/27 undergraduate and postgraduate LOCAL scholarships, which are tuition-only and are not the same award - do not confuse the two when applying
All correspondence is through official channels only, so treat any approach outside the portal and the Fund's official addresses as suspicious
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create a profile and verify your account on the GETFund portal, complete the form and upload the vetting documents, review the summary and submit, then wait for portal, email and SMS updates through shortlisting; outcomes are only communicated by GETFund through those official channels.

scholarships.title: Pacific Scholarship for Excellence in Research & Innovation (PSERI)
scholarships.name: Pacific Scholarship for Excellence in Research & Innovation (PSERI)

applicant_utility.summary: PSERI is USP's flagship internally funded research degree scholarship, and the money is genuinely substantial: tuition and the compulsory fees are paid directly, a living allowance of FJD 21,600 per year for Master's or FJD 24,000 for PhD is paid monthly, and there is a book allowance, a dependants allowance and an establishment allowance on top. The catch is that the scholarship only buys the money, not the place - you must separately enrol in one of USP's academic units, and the award does not guarantee admission there. The other real constraint is the workload: full-time study, no paid employment for the whole tenure, a minimum 40 hours a week on research, and up to eight hours a week of teaching during semester. If you are a final year undergraduate, you can apply, but your letter must state your expected completion date or your file will not be assessable.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Citizens of a USP member country with a 3.5-plus undergraduate GPA who want a fully funded research Master's or PhD at USP and can commit to full-time, unpaid, 40-hour weeks on a Pacific-relevant research topic.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure certified true copies of your transcripts and certificates early - certified copies take days to obtain and are mandatory
Draft the research outline against one of USP's five Strategic Research Themes and against the specific unit you want to join, then check that unit's own website for what it supports this round
Contact a potential supervisor informally before you submit; the page explicitly allows applicants to discuss their application with one
Prepare the Applicant Detail Form and the Applicant Checklist, and complete every field rather than leaving blanks
Identify three referees and confirm their current contact details before you name them
Email everything in one message with the exact subject line format, rather than sending documents in several emails
If you are a final year undergraduate, state your expected completion date explicitly in the application letter
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the scholarship guarantees enrolment - you must enrol in the academic unit yourself, and a weak unit match sinks the application
A research outline that does not sit inside one of the Strategic Research Themes or inside what your target unit is funding this round
Missing the 3.5 undergraduate GPA threshold at Master's level; note the page also expects 3.5 or above in both undergraduate and postgraduate levels for applicants applying for a Masters award
PhD applicants without a completed Master's degree by thesis, which is an explicit requirement
Planning to work part-time alongside the award, which is prohibited for the whole tenure
Final year applicants who omit the expected completion date from their letter
Applying with a proposal that is not a research degree - PSERI covers Masters or PhD by research only
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, General Services fees, Health Services fees, the living allowance and the book allowance are covered, and one return airfare is provided when you have to travel to a USP campus in another country. The research grant is not guaranteed - it is only released once the research plan and budget are approved by the Academic Unit Research Committee - so fieldwork and data collection costs may initially sit with you. The dependants and establishment allowances are also conditional: the dependants allowance applies only to primary dependants who reside with you during the scholarship, and the establishment allowance requires relocating to a USP campus.
document_audit: Transcripts and certificates must be certified true copies, not plain photocopies or scans you print yourself

All eight documents travel in a single email - the Applicant Detail Form, the Applicant Checklist, the cover letter, the research outline, the CV, the three referees, the certified copies and proof of citizenship
Use the exact subject line format including your own name, because applications are triaged by subject line

If you claim a dependants allowance, you must document proof of marriage and the spouse's employment status, and for children prove the relationship, residence with you, age under 18 and your main and continuing support

If you claim an establishment allowance, you must show you are relocating from outside the greater Suva area, that neither you nor your partner is receiving a relocation package from another organisation, and that the award will run at least 12 months
alerts: The 2026 round closed at midnight on Monday 5 January 2026 and the page is marked CLOSED; USP publishes a new year-dated call each year, so watch the same page from late 2026
Enrolment in the academic unit is separate from the scholarship and is not guaranteed by it, so line up your academic admission in parallel

applicant_utility.summary: At up to $10,000 for a single year of full-time STEM study, Toloa Tertiary is one of the larger Pacific-targeted awards in New Zealand, but the eligibility gates are narrow and unforgiving. You must be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident of Pacific Islands descent, you must be in second year or beyond, and you must still be full-time － final-year and Year 3 students are excluded because the Government fees-free scheme is meant to cover them. applicant_utility.summary: PRSRS is a small, sport-focused research scholarship jointly funded by the Oceania National Olympic Committee and USP, and only three awards were made for 2026, so the field is narrow but the package is strong. You need a research Master's idea that sits in the economics, social impact or physical education of sport, a GPA of 3 or above, and citizenship of a USP member country; a postgraduate diploma helps but is not required. Two features distinguish it from PSERI: the age preference is relaxed to 40 rather than 35, and the award builds in an industry placement for one semester alongside a semester of teaching, so this is a scholarship for someone who wants their research connected to the sports sector rather than purely academic. As with the other USP Research Office awards, the scholarship pays nothing towards getting you into an academic unit - you must enrol separately.

scholarships.title: Cost Sharing Overseas PhD Scholarships Scheme with Australian Universities (TSLS, Government of Fiji)
scholarships.name: Cost Sharing Overseas PhD Scholarships Scheme with Australian Universities (TSLS, Government of Fiji)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a five-award scheme for the 2026-2027 financial year, so it is one of the most competitive overseas routes TSLS runs, and its defining feature is the cost-sharing model. TSLS pays you - a minimum living allowance of AUD/NZD 32,000 a year, economy return airfare, visa fees up to FJD 3,000, overseas student health cover, an establishment allowance of up to AUD/NZD 3,500 and a field grant of up to AUD/NZD 3,000 for approved primary data collection - while the partner university bears the tuition fee. That division of labour is the single most important thing to understand before you apply: your financial future depends on a university tuition arrangement that sits outside the TSLS award. You also need to be under 50, a Fiji citizen with three years ordinary residence, and hold an offer or candidature from one of only ten named Australian universities, with research framed around Fiji's workforce and development needs.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fiji citizens under 50 with a full-time PhD offer or candidature from one of the ten listed Australian universities, whose research demonstrably serves Fiji's workforce or development needs in a priority discipline.
application_readiness_checklist: Get the candidature or offer letter first - the scheme requires an offer letter or candidature confirmation letter from an eligible institution, and there are only ten eligible universities
Before applying, get written confirmation from the university of exactly what tuition support it will provide, since the cost-sharing model puts tuition with the university rather than with TSLS
Frame your research explicitly around Fiji's workforce needs and development, naming the discipline gap it fills and how you will return that capacity to Fiji
Check your age against the under-50 rule at the time of application, and confirm your three years ordinary residence in Fiji before the award commencement date

Assemble the standard TSLS document set as pdf, png or jpg scans: offer letter, highest qualification result, Tax Identification Number, digital passport photo, birth certificate, and bank or mobile wallet statement where applicable
Register on the TSLS Apply portal with your own Gmail, Yahoo or Hotmail address and verify the account before you start the form
common_rejection_risks: Assuming TSLS pays the tuition fee, then discovering the university's share is less than expected or not formalised

Applying with only five available awards against a field that includes all twelve priority disciplines, so a research proposal that does not clearly serve Fiji's workforce needs will not survive the cut
Holding an offer from a university outside the ten eligible Australian institutions, or from a New Zealand institution when the handbook and scheme page name Australian universities
Being 50 or older at the time of application
Being an existing TSLS sponsored student, a graduate on active bond service, or already sponsored through another agency
Arranging part-time study or employer-based study without the Service's determination, since the eligibility requires full-time studies unless determined otherwise
Submitting late or incomplete applications, which TSLS states will not be considered for assessment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: TSLS's published privileges are generous, but they are minima rather than guarantees: the living allowance is a minimum of AUD/NZD 32,000 or at a local market rate, the establishment allowance is capped at AUD/NZD 3,500, the field grant is capped at AUD/NZD 3,000 and only paid if field surveys for primary data collection are required and approved, and the excess baggage allowance is capped at AUD/NZD 300. Your tuition is wholly dependent on the partner university's own arrangement, which TSLS does not quantify. Anything beyond those caps, and any living cost above the local market rate, is yours to cover.
document_audit: The offer letter or candidature confirmation letter must come from one of the ten eligible universities; check the list before you apply anywhere else

TSLS asks for final results rather than annual results, and uploads must be pdf, png or jpg - the Know How To Apply page states file size should not exceed 5MB, while the handbook states 20MB, so keep files small and test the upload
A Tax Identification Number and birth certificate are part of the standard document set and are easy to overlook if you have never needed them

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at The American University in Cairo
scholarships.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at The American University in Cairo

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of the few genuinely comprehensive graduate fellowships for African students, covering tuition, accommodation, a stipend, a laptop, health insurance, local transport and even roundtrip airfare if you are not already living in Egypt - but it is not automatic on admission. You must submit two separate applications: the AUC graduate application first, then the Mastercard Foundation Scholars application, and the second only becomes available five working days after your AUC ID number is issued. For the Spring 2027 cohort the window is 7 October to 2 November 2026, so if you have not already started the graduate application the clock is already running. Two conditions deserve attention before you commit: fellows are assigned 12 hours per week of related academic work on top of full-time study, and tuition is published as covering nine credits per semester, so any heavier credit load is on you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically strong African citizens under 35 with a 3.2-plus GPA and demonstrated financial need who want a fully funded AUC graduate degree in Cairo and can carry 12 hours per week of academic work alongside full-time study.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the AUC online graduate application at applyweb.com/auc first, because the fellowship application stays locked until an AUC ID number is issued
Diarise five working days after your AUC ID number arrives, then complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars application at aucbanner.aucegypt.edu before 2 November 2026 for Spring 2027
Prepare a statement of purpose of about 500 words per program selected, and apply for no more than two graduate programs so both are properly argued
Ask two recommenders to submit their letters online directly - AUC only accepts online letters, and letters are valid for two consecutive semesters only from the date the recommender submits them
Book an English test early enough that results are still valid on your first day of classes, remembering AUC only accepts iBT TOEFL, academic IELTS or Cambridge CPE/CAE
Keep the fellowship deadlines page open alongside the graduate admissions deadlines, since the two schedules are not identical
common_rejection_risks: Completing only the AUC graduate application and never submitting the separate Mastercard Foundation Scholars application, since funding is not automatic on admission
Applying as a transfer student, who is explicitly not eligible for this fellowship
Falling below the 3.2 minimum GPA, or failing to evidence financial need convincingly
Being over 35 at the time of application, or not currently residing in an African country
Recommendation letters arriving late, because only online letters are accepted and it is the applicant's responsibility to track them
English test results that expire before the first day of registered classes, which AUC refuses to consider
Programs that require higher English cut-off scores than the general minimum, so check your specific program's threshold
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published award is unusually complete - tuition for nine credits per semester, a stipend during fall and spring semesters, a laptop, student services and activities fees, medical service and health insurance fees, university accommodation, the AUC bus subscription or a travel allowance, and roundtrip airfare if you are not already residing in Egypt. The gaps are specific: credits beyond nine per semester are not named as covered, the stipend is only paid during the fall and spring semesters so summer living costs are yours, and airfare is not provided to fellows who already live in Egypt. Additional research, publication and conference funding is described as available to some candidates only, so do not budget for it.
document_audit: Proof of bachelor's degree completion must show official stamps and signatures, and originals are only required from those who are offered admission - but plan for that later request
Statement of purpose is about 500 words for each of the up to two programs you select, so budget writing time per program rather than one generic essay
Recommendations must be submitted electronically by the recommenders themselves; you cannot supply AUC with the letters directly
English results must be from an acceptable test - AUC will not accept the IELTS indicator, and combining band scores from different tests is not possible
International applicants must upload the information pages of their passport and one recent passport-size photograph
You may be asked to submit additional paperwork to be considered for the fellowship, so respond promptly to any AUC request

Final admission decisions should be expected within three to four months of the application submission deadline, so plan funding and visas around that timeline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the AUC online graduate application, wait five working days for your AUC ID number, then complete the separate Mastercard Foundation Scholars online application by the fellowship cycle deadline; AUC and the programme may request additional paperwork, with queries directed to mastercardfdn@aucegypt.edu.

It targets academically talented young Africans with leadership potential who face the highest economic and social barriers. The award is granted for the total study period of the degree on full-time enrolment, subject to review every semester for satisfactory academic performance, and it covers tuition, a stipend, a laptop, health insurance, university accommodation, local transport and, for fellows who do not already reside in Egypt, roundtrip airfare. applicant_utility.summary: The decisive step here happens before any form exists: a professor at a Swiss institution must agree to supervise your project and sign the letter of support, because applications without a supervisor are not considered at all. After that, plan on one to two days to build the dossier - CV, a two-page motivation letter, a five-page research plan on the FCS/ESKAS form, the supervisor's letter and two-page CV, two referee contacts who will upload letters, and certified translations where needed. Submit only through GO ESKAS inside your own country's window, and remember the CHF 2,450 monthly stipend is explicitly not a salary and covers one person only.

Find your country's exact deadline in the A-Z country list - it is not a single shared date

Submitting more than one research project proposal, or simultaneous applications to several host universities or scholarship types
Having lived, studied or worked in Switzerland more than 13 months before the scholarship start
Applying a fourth time after three unsuccessful attempts
Incomplete or formally defective applications
